**Prerequisites.** [Effective analytic divisors over the coefficient field](#target-rd-0-analytic-effective-divisors) (`RD.0/analytic-effective-divisors`), [Compact Laurent preparation over arbitrary complete coefficients](#target-rd-0-compact-laurent-preparation) (`RD.0/compact-laurent-preparation`), [Laurent Fréchet charts and the Robba inductive limit](#target-rd-0-laurent-topology-interface) (`RD.0/laurent-topology-interface`).

**Sources.**

- [S43](#source-43), Lemme 3 and Proposition 5, §4, p.59. On the open disc: correcting factors (Lemme 3) make an infinite product converge to a nonzero function whose divisor is at least the given one; equality is not asserted. On an annulus the construction is applied separately to the zeros escaping each boundary circle, inverting the variable for the inner one.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Separate the divisor into finite polynomial packets escaping every compact window. For disc packets use Lazard’s high-degree correcting factors; for an annulus use positive and negative Laurent directions for packets escaping its two boundaries.
2. For each packet choose a correction polynomial or Laurent polynomial which retains its required zeros and makes the modified factor approach 1 on the compact windows already exhausted. Finite division and complete ultrametric summability control the product.
3. Its nonzero convergent product has at least the prescribed factor orders. Additional zeros are the price of this construction; demanding their absence is exactly the stronger spherical-completeness theorem.

**Checks.**

- D=0 admits f=1.
- The output can have extra zeros; the acceptance test must not silently strengthen ≥ to =.

<a id="target-rd-0-analytic-jet-interpolation"></a>

### Analytic principal parts and jet interpolation

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/analytic-jet-interpolation` · theorem

For a locally finite effective divisor D on U over any complete nonarchimedean K, arbitrary finite jet data at its closed points are realised by a global analytic g∈A_K(U): for every point P with D(P)>0, the image of g in K[T]/(P^{D(P)}) equals the specified residue class. Equivalently meromorphic principal parts with locally finite poles admit a global meromorphic realisation. This interpolation implies that every finitely generated ideal of A_K(U) is closed, whether or not K is spherically complete.

**Hypotheses.**

- No uniform bound on the jets is imposed. This is interpolation without a growth bound, unlike spherical prescribed-divisor realization.
- For inseparable P use the polynomial jet quotient, not derivative data at distinct roots.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Foundations`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [A nonzero function dominating a locally finite divisor](#target-rd-0-analytic-divisor-majorant) (`RD.0/analytic-divisor-majorant`), [Compact Laurent preparation over arbitrary complete coefficients](#target-rd-0-compact-laurent-preparation) (`RD.0/compact-laurent-preparation`), [Effective analytic divisors over the coefficient field](#target-rd-0-analytic-effective-divisors) (`RD.0/analytic-effective-divisors`), [Laurent Fréchet charts and the Robba inductive limit](#target-rd-0-laurent-topology-interface) (`RD.0/laurent-topology-interface`).

**Sources.**

- [S43](#source-43), §8, (8.9) and Théorème 3, pp.69–70; (8.11) and Proposition 11, p.71. On the open disc: Mittag–Leffler principal parts, their analytic interpolation consequence, and closedness of finitely generated ideals. The annulus version applies the same compact-window correction in both Laurent directions.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Group the poles by packets escaping every compact subdomain. Each rational principal part whose poles lie outside a fixed compact window has a convergent power or inverse-power expansion there. Subtract a finite Laurent-polynomial truncation to make its norm arbitrarily small on that window. Summing the corrected packets converges on every compact window and retains all principal parts.
2. Choose the nonzero divisor majorant f. Extend the requested jets to orders div(f), including arbitrary zero data at the additional zeros of f. Apply the principal-parts construction to their local quotients by f; multiply the resulting meromorphic function by f to obtain a global analytic function with the required jets (Lazard (8.11)).
3. For generators f_0,…,f_m and g vanishing along their common divisor, compact division gives local coefficients on each circle. Interpolate the coefficients for i>0 modulo the zero divisor of f_0. The remaining difference is globally divisible by f_0, so g is in the generated ideal. This identifies the ideal with its closed divisor ideal.

**Checks.**

- For two distinct closed points finite interpolation agrees with polynomial CRT.
- Arbitrarily large jets escaping the boundary are allowed; no boundedness hypothesis is introduced.
- The argument shows principal ideals are closed over any complete K, but not that every closed ideal is principal.

<a id="target-rd-0-closed-ideal-divisor-correspondence"></a>

### Closed ideals and effective analytic divisors

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/closed-ideal-divisor-correspondence` · theorem

For any complete nonarchimedean K, the nonzero closed ideals of A_K(U) correspond order-reversingly to effective locally finite divisors on U. For a nonzero ideal I define D_I(P)=min_{0≠f∈I}div(f)(P); for a divisor D put I_D={0}∪{f≠0:D≤div(f)}. Then I_D is nonzero and closed, D_{I_D}=D, and closure(I)=I_{D_I}. The zero ideal is an additional closed ideal, with no finite-multiplicity divisor. The unit ideal corresponds to D=0. On compact U every such ideal is principal; on noncompact U principality requires the separate spherical-completeness theorem.

**Hypotheses.**

- Divisors and closure use the exact carrier and topology specified above.
- No spherical completeness is needed for this classification alone.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Foundations`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Effective analytic divisors over the coefficient field](#target-rd-0-analytic-effective-divisors) (`RD.0/analytic-effective-divisors`), [A nonzero function dominating a locally finite divisor](#target-rd-0-analytic-divisor-majorant) (`RD.0/analytic-divisor-majorant`), [Analytic principal parts and jet interpolation](#target-rd-0-analytic-jet-interpolation) (`RD.0/analytic-jet-interpolation`), [Compact Laurent preparation over arbitrary complete coefficients](#target-rd-0-compact-laurent-preparation) (`RD.0/compact-laurent-preparation`).

**Sources.**

- [S43](#source-43), Proposition 10 and proof, §7, pp.68–69. On the open disc over an arbitrary complete field: integral divisors correspond bijectively to nonzero closed ideals, a divisor giving the functions with at least that divisor and an ideal the infimum of its members’ divisors, and the closure of an ideal is the ideal of its divisor. The annulus case runs the same proof over a compact exhaustion.
- [S44](#source-44), Théorème 2.30(ii), p.24. The geometric formulation, with the zero ideal excluded from the finite-divisor bijection.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Choose a nonzero member of I; its divisor bounds D_I, proving local finiteness. Vanishing to a given order is a closed condition on every compact chart, so I_D is closed. The divisor-majorant theorem supplies a nonzero member.
2. On a compact window, select finitely many members of I which attain the minimum at each of its finitely many relevant points. Compact PID theory produces their gcd on that window. Laurent-polynomial approximation to the local coefficients makes I dense in every function vanishing along D_I.
3. Use jet interpolation to make each minimum multiplicity sharp for I_D. Passing over the compact exhaustion proves the inverse correspondence and the closure formula.
4. Treat I=0 separately. Over characteristic zero transport the polynomial divisor to the Galois-invariant geometric form, correcting the omission of the zero-ideal exception in Colmez’s statement.

**Checks.**

- I_D=the unit ideal exactly when D=0.
- The zero ideal is closed but is outside the displayed bijection.
- At a point a in the disc, the ideal (T−a)^m has divisor multiplicity m at a.

<a id="target-rd-0-spherical-prescribed-divisors"></a>

### Prescribing exact zeros under spherical completeness

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/spherical-prescribed-divisors` · theorem

If K is spherically complete, every locally finite effective divisor D on a connected annulus or disc U is div(f) for some nonzero analytic f. The stronger construction includes Lazard’s norm-controlled finite-zero interpolation on increasing compact windows. Conversely, exact realization of every divisor on an open disc detects spherical completeness; completeness alone does not imply it. Spherical completeness means that every nested family of nonempty closed balls in K has nonempty intersection.

**Hypotheses.**

- K is complete, nontrivially nonarchimedean and spherically complete for the forward statement.
- The inverse implication concerns all effective locally finite divisors, not just finite polynomial divisors.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Foundations`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Effective analytic divisors over the coefficient field](#target-rd-0-analytic-effective-divisors) (`RD.0/analytic-effective-divisors`), [Compact Laurent preparation over arbitrary complete coefficients](#target-rd-0-compact-laurent-preparation) (`RD.0/compact-laurent-preparation`), [Laurent Fréchet charts and the Robba inductive limit](#target-rd-0-laurent-topology-interface) (`RD.0/laurent-topology-interface`).

**Sources.**

- [S43](#source-43), Proposition 6, §5, pp.61–62; Lemmas 4–5 and Proposition 8, §§6–7, pp.62–67; Théorème 2, p.67. On the open disc: the norm-controlled construction and the equivalence between exact realisation of divisors and maximal (spherical) completeness. Lazard states maximal completeness for decreasing sequences of discs, which is equivalent to the nested-family form for a rank-one valuation.
- [S44](#source-44), Remarque 2.31(ii), p.24. The noncompact exact-zero/principality conclusions require spherical completeness.
- [S42](#source-42), Theorem 3.4.3 and Remark 3.4.4, pp.14–15. Over a spherically complete field every coherent locally free sheaf on an annulus or disc with aligned closed endpoints is free; in rank one this realises a locally finite divisor exactly, which gives the annulus case. The remark recalls that Lazard’s disc theorem fails without spherical completeness.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Finite-zero interpolation with specified norm inequalities constrains successive coefficient choices to nested closed balls (Lazard Lemmas 4–5 and Proposition 8). Spherical completeness supplies compatible choices when their radii need not tend to zero.
2. Pass along an exhaustion with the controlled corrections, preserving the exact polynomial divisor rather than allowing extra zeros. Apply the disc argument in both Laurent directions for an annulus.
3. An empty nested family of balls gives the obstruction divisor of Lazard Proposition 6. Its realization would provide an element in their intersection; this is the necessity argument in Theorem 2.

**Checks.**

- Complete discretely valued K is spherically complete, so the theorem applies to the coefficient fields of the parent Γ theory.
- C_p is complete but not spherically complete: exclude it from the unconditional noncompact exact-divisor claim.
- Finite divisors on compact windows are already realised without this hypothesis.

<a id="target-rd-0-noncompact-analytic-bezout"></a>

### Bézout and principal closed ideals on open annuli and discs

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/noncompact-analytic-bezout` · theorem

If K is spherically complete, A_K(U) is a Bézout domain for any connected nonempty open or half-open annulus or disc U. An ideal is closed iff it is principal. Its nonzero closed ideals are generated by functions realizing their effective divisors. On compact U the stronger PID conclusion holds for any complete K. Principal and finitely generated ideals are closed over any complete K; the spherical hypothesis is needed to turn every divisor ideal into a principal ideal on a noncompact domain.

**Hypotheses.**

- Use IsBezout, the existing Mathlib class, for the finite-generation conclusion.
- The domain U and the chart topology are fixed; the LF Robba germ topology is a different case.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Foundations`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Analytic principal parts and jet interpolation](#target-rd-0-analytic-jet-interpolation) (`RD.0/analytic-jet-interpolation`), [Closed ideals and effective analytic divisors](#target-rd-0-closed-ideal-divisor-correspondence) (`RD.0/closed-ideal-divisor-correspondence`), [Prescribing exact zeros under spherical completeness](#target-rd-0-spherical-prescribed-divisors) (`RD.0/spherical-prescribed-divisors`), `mathlib:IsBezout`.

**Sources.**

- [S43](#source-43), Propositions 10–11 and (7.3), pp.68–71; Théorème 2, p.67. On the open disc: closed divisor ideals, closedness of finitely generated ideals, exact realisation of divisors, and the reformulation (7.3) of spherical completeness as principality of every closed ideal.
- [S44](#source-44), Théorème 2.30(i) and Remarque 2.31(ii), p.24. Annulus and disc statement with the compact/noncompact coefficient-field distinction.
- [S42](#source-42), Theorem 3.4.3 and Remark 3.4.4, pp.14–15. Freeness of line bundles on annuli over a spherically complete field, which makes divisor ideals principal on open and half-open annuli.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Analytic-jet-interpolation identifies every finitely generated ideal with its closed common-divisor ideal.
2. Spherical-prescribed-divisors realises the common divisor by f. The divisor divisibility criterion shows I_D=(f). Thus every finitely generated ideal is principal.
3. For an arbitrary nonzero closed ideal use closed-ideal-divisor-correspondence and the same generator. Conversely principal ideals are finitely generated and closed by interpolation. The zero ideal is separately principal and closed.

**Checks.**

- For Q_p on the open unit disc, the ideal generated by two nonzero functions is generated by a function with their pointwise minimum zero divisor.
- Do not assert this spherical version for C_p using completeness alone.
- This theorem does not imply that every algebraic ideal is closed.

<a id="target-rd-0-robba-ring"></a>

### The Robba ring R_K is Kedlaya's analytic ring Γ^{k((t))}_an,con: naive and true partial valuations agree

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/robba-ring` · comparison

Let R = R_K be the Robba ring over K (germs of Laurent series Σ_{i∈Z} c_i t^i, c_i ∈ K, converging on some annulus r < |t| < 1; constructed in RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring with its Gauss norms |·|_ρ, Fréchet topology on each annulus ring and limit-of-Fréchet (LF) topology on R), R^int, R^bd = R^int[1/π], O_E and E = O_E[1/π] as in the Frobenius-lift node. Let σ be a Frobenius lift with u = σ(t), and let ℓ = k((t)), Γ = O_E, so that the analytic-ring construction applies. Choose r > 0 with u/t^q a unit of the ring of bounded functions on |π|^r ≤ |t| < 1. Then for s ∈ (0, qr] and all n: min_{j≤n} v_{j,s} = min_{j≤n} v^naive_{j,s}, where v^naive_n(Σ c_i t^i) = min{i : w(c_i) ≤ n}; consequently Γ_s = bounded functions on |π|^s ≤ |t| < 1 with integral coefficients, w_s(f) = log_{|π|} |f|_{|π|^s} (sup norm on the circle |t| = |π|^s), Γ has enough qr-units, and Γ_con = R^int, Γ_con[π^{-1}] = R^bd, Γ[π^{-1}] = E, Γ_{(0,s]} = functions on |π|^s ≤ |t| < 1, Γ_an,con = R. The identification is independent of σ as topological rings; only the auxiliary partial valuations v_n, and the embedding into W(k((t))^perf, O^perf), depend on σ.

**Hypotheses.**

- K discretely valued with uniformiser π; O = O_K is finite totally ramified over a Cohen ring of k.
- Radius convention: Kedlaya's parameter s corresponds to the radius ρ = |π|^s; an interval I ⊆ (0, r_0) corresponds to the annulus {|π|^{max I} ≤ |t| ≤ |π|^{min I}} and (0, r] to |π|^r ≤ |t| < 1.
- The Frobenius lift is used only to transport Kedlaya's machinery; statements about the underlying topological ring (Bézout property, units, free vector bundles) hold for any choice (Remark 2.3.9).

**Prerequisites.** [Weakly continuous Frobenius lifts on the integral Amice ring](#target-rd-0-frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring) (`RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring`), [Partial valuations v_n, w_r on Witt vectors and the overconvergent Witt vectors W_con](#target-rd-0-witt-partial-valuations) (`RD.0/witt-partial-valuations`), [Kedlaya's analytic rings Γ^ℓ_I, Γ^ℓ_an,r and Γ^ℓ_an,con](#target-rd-0-analytic-ring) (`RD.0/analytic-ring`), [Laurent Fréchet charts and the Robba inductive limit](#target-rd-0-laurent-topology-interface) (`RD.0/laurent-topology-interface`).

**Sources.**

- [S2](#source-2), Lemma 2.3.5, pp. 12-13. Equality of naive and true valuations.
- [S2](#source-2), Corollary 2.3.7, p. 13. Enough units and Γ_con = R^int.
- [S2](#source-2), Remark 2.3.9, p. 13. The identification with the Robba ring.
- [S2](#source-2), Example 2.4.9, p. 15. Explicit coefficient description.
- [S8](#source-8), Definition 3.5.1, p. 15. The Robba ring as a direct limit of rings of functions on annuli (P7's description).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Lemma 2.3.3: for s ∈ (0, qr], min_{j≤n} v^naive_{j,s}(x) = min_{j≤n} v^naive_{j,s/q}(x^σ), checked on monomials u^i and then termwise with a unique minimising index.
2. Lemma 2.3.5: write x via Teichmüller coordinates, raise to a large q-power by σ and compare with naive valuations of lifts of the coordinates; with Lemma 2.3.3 this gives equality of the true and naive partial valuations.
3. Corollary 2.3.7: Γ has enough qr-units and Γ_con = Γ_con^naive = R^int.
4. Remark 2.3.8 and Example 2.4.9: Γ^naive_r[π^{-1}] is the ring of bounded analytic functions on |π|^r ≤ |t| < 1, w^naive_s is the sup norm on |t| = |π|^s, and Γ_an,con consists of the Laurent series over O[π^{-1}] with lim inf_{n→−∞} w(c_n)/(−n) > 0 and lim inf_{n→∞} w(c_n)/n ≥ 0, which is the Laurent-series Robba ring.
5. Independence of σ as topological rings: both sides are described by coefficient conditions that do not mention σ (Remark 2.3.9).

**Checks.**

- The Laurent polynomial t − p (K = Q_p, standard lift) has v^naive_0 = 1 and v^naive_n = 0 for n ≥ 1, one slope 1, and its zero is on |t| = p^{-1} = |π|^1.
- For the cyclotomic lift σ(t) = (1+t)^p − 1 the naive and true valuations agree on Γ_s for s ≤ pr with r chosen as in the statement.

<a id="target-rd-0-bounded-robba-ring"></a>

### The bounded Robba ring R^bd is a henselian discretely valued field with residue field k((t)); R^bd = R ∩ E

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/bounded-robba-ring` · theorem

(a) R^int is a local ring with maximal ideal m_R = {Σ c_i t^i : all c_i ∈ m_K} and residue field k((t)); since K is discretely valued, R^int is a discrete valuation ring with uniformiser π and valuation w(Σ c_i t^i) = min_i w(c_i); it is henselian and not π-adically complete, its π-adic completion being O_E. (b) R^bd = R^int[1/π] is the fraction field of R^int, hence a henselian discretely valued field, with residue field k((t)) and completion E. (c) Inside the space of coefficient families Z → K: R^bd = R ∩ E = {f ∈ R : sup_i |c_i| < ∞} (the functions analytic and bounded on some annulus r < |t| < 1) and R^int = R ∩ O_E. (d) R^bd is dense in R for the LF topology and in E for the π-adic topology. No perfectness of k is needed.

**Hypotheses.**

- K complete discretely valued of characteristic 0; k arbitrary of characteristic p.
- If K is not discretely valued, R^int is local but not a valuation ring in this way (overview Remark 3.5.3); this layer assumes K discretely valued.

**Prerequisites.** [The Robba ring R_K is Kedlaya's analytic ring Γ^{k((t))}_an,con: naive and true partial valuations agree](#target-rd-0-robba-ring) (`RD.0/robba-ring`), [W_con(ℓ, O) is a henselian discrete valuation ring](#target-rd-0-overconvergent-witt-vectors-henselian) (`RD.0/overconvergent-witt-vectors-henselian`), [Weakly continuous Frobenius lifts on the integral Amice ring](#target-rd-0-frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring) (`RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring`), `mathlib:HenselianLocalRing`, `mathlib:IsDiscreteValuationRing`, `mathlib:HenselianRing`.

**Sources.**

- [S8](#source-8), Lemma 3.5.2, p. 15. Part (a), local ring and residue field.
- [S8](#source-8), Remark 3.5.3, p. 15. Part (a), DVR.
- [S1](#source-1), Section 2.3, p. 12. Γ_con (= R^int) is a noncomplete DVR (Kedlaya's K = k((t))).
- [S1](#source-1), Section 2.3, p. 13. Part (c).

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a) Local with residue field k((t)): for x ∈ m_R, |x|_ρ < 1 for ρ close to 1, so 1 + x is invertible in R^int (overview Lemma 3.5.2). DVR: R^int = Γ_con by the Robba-ring comparison, and Γ_con is a henselian DVR (analytic-ring construction, from Lemma 2.1.12). π-adic completion O_E: monodromy paper Section 2.3.
2. (b) A DVR localised at its uniformiser is its fraction field; henselianity is a property of the valuation ring.
3. (c) A Laurent series converging on r < |t| < 1 satisfies |c_i|ρ^i → 0 as i → −∞ for some ρ < 1, hence c_i → 0 as i → −∞; if moreover sup_i |c_i| < ∞ it is bounded on r' ≤ |t| < 1 for r' ∈ (r,1), and conversely boundedness on an annulus forces sup_i |c_i| ≤ sup of the function by letting ρ → 1. Scaling by a power of π lands in R^int.
4. (d) Laurent polynomials are dense in each annulus ring for its radius-wise Fréchet topology. For π-adic density in O_E, retain the entire nonnegative power-series tail and truncate only the negative tail modulo each π^N; these truncations lie in R^int. Invert π to obtain density in E.

**Checks.**

- t is a unit of R^int; π is not a unit of R^int but is a unit of R^bd; t − p = t(1 − p t^{-1}) is a unit of R^int because p t^{-1} ∈ m_R.
- Σ_{n≥0} p^n t^{-p^n} lies in O_E but not in R^int (completion versus overconvergence node).
- The residue field of R^int is k((t)), not k: the reduction of Σ c_i t^i is Σ c̄_i t^i.
- For perfect k, K=W(k)[1/p], q=p and standard σ(t)=t^p, identify this target with FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory §§R07.4.7–R07.4.8, including its coefficient carriers, degree convention, standard blocks and increasing slope filtration where applicable. This roadmap supplies the stated general coefficient/Frobenius version and its compatibility with that imported special case, rather than a second implementation of the special case.

<a id="target-rd-0-units-of-robba-ring"></a>

### Units of the Robba ring are exactly the nonzero elements of R^bd (Lazard, Kedlaya)

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/units-of-robba-ring` · theorem

R^× = R^bd − {0}. More generally, for any complete valued ℓ of characteristic p with Γ^ℓ having enough units, (Γ^ℓ_an,con)^× = (Γ^ℓ_con[π^{-1}])^×; for ℓ = k((t)) and for ℓ the completed algebraic closure of k((t)) (the extended Robba ring R^alg) this is the set of nonzero elements of the field Γ^ℓ_con[π^{-1}]. Equivalently, f ∈ R is a unit iff f is bounded on some annulus r < |t| < 1 and has no zeros there (its Newton polygon has no slopes near the boundary).

**Hypotheses.**

- K discretely valued (so that Γ^ℓ_con is a DVR and Γ^ℓ_con[π^{-1}] a field).

**Prerequisites.** [Units of Γ_I are the elements without slopes; units of Γ_an,r lie in Γ_r[π^{-1}]](#target-rd-0-units-of-analytic-ring) (`RD.0/units-of-analytic-ring`), [The Robba ring R_K is Kedlaya's analytic ring Γ^{k((t))}_an,con: naive and true partial valuations agree](#target-rd-0-robba-ring) (`RD.0/robba-ring`), [The bounded Robba ring R^bd is a henselian discretely valued field with residue field k((t)); R^bd = R ∩ E](#target-rd-0-bounded-robba-ring) (`RD.0/bounded-robba-ring`).

**Sources.**

- [S2](#source-2), Corollary 2.5.12, p. 19. Units of Γ_an,r lie in Γ_r[π^{-1}].
- [S1](#source-1), Corollary 3.23, p. 36. The monodromy paper's form (for ℓ = k((t)), v_n(x) = ∞ for n ≪ 0 means x ∈ Γ_con[1/p]).
- [S2](#source-2), Proof of Proposition 3.3.2, p. 33. The use made downstream: the Frobenius of a rank-one σ-module has a well-defined valuation.

**Construction or proof.**

1. A unit of Γ_an,con is a unit of some Γ_an,r; by the units-of-analytic-ring theorem it is a unit of Γ_r[π^{-1}] ⊆ Γ_con[π^{-1}].
2. Conversely Γ_con[π^{-1}] = R^bd is a field (bounded-Robba-ring theorem), so its nonzero elements are invertible in R^bd ⊆ R.
3. The Newton-polygon form: no slopes in (0, r] iff unit of Γ_an,r (Corollary 2.5.12).

**Checks.**

- Π_{i≥1}(1 − t^{p^i}/p^i) ∈ R has infinitely many slopes accumulating at the boundary and is not a unit.
- t is a unit; 1 + p t^{-1} is a unit; log(1+t) is not a unit of R (it vanishes at the points ζ − 1, ζ a p-power root of unity, which approach the boundary).
- For perfect k, K=W(k)[1/p], q=p and standard σ(t)=t^p, identify this target with FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory §§R07.4.7–R07.4.8, including its coefficient carriers, degree convention, standard blocks and increasing slope filtration where applicable. This roadmap supplies the stated general coefficient/Frobenius version and its compatibility with that imported special case, rather than a second implementation of the special case.

<a id="target-rd-0-robba-closed-ideals"></a>

### Closed ideals of the Robba germ ring

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/robba-closed-ideals` · theorem

For the parent Robba ring R_K with the final seminorm topology, the only closed ideals are 0 and R_K. This closed-ideal assertion holds over any complete nontrivially nonarchimedean K by the compact-window argument. For spherically complete K the ring is also Bézout by noncompact-analytic-bezout and taking a common chart. Neither assertion says R_K is a field: over Q_p, log(1+t) is nonzero with infinitely many zeros tending to |t|=1, is not a unit, and generates a proper dense ideal.

**Hypotheses.**

- Closed means closed for the Robba LF topology, not for a single chart or for the Amice norm topology.
- The additional Bézout assertion retains spherical completeness; the parent DVR coefficient result is an instance.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Foundations`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Compact Laurent preparation over arbitrary complete coefficients](#target-rd-0-compact-laurent-preparation) (`RD.0/compact-laurent-preparation`), [Laurent Fréchet charts and the Robba inductive limit](#target-rd-0-laurent-topology-interface) (`RD.0/laurent-topology-interface`), [Bézout and principal closed ideals on open annuli and discs](#target-rd-0-noncompact-analytic-bezout) (`RD.0/noncompact-analytic-bezout`), [Units of the Robba ring are exactly the nonzero elements of R^bd (Lazard, Kedlaya)](#target-rd-0-units-of-robba-ring) (`RD.0/units-of-robba-ring`).

**Sources.**

- [S44](#source-44), Préface §2.5.1, last paragraph, p.24. The Robba ring is Bézout and has only the trivial closed ideals; the wider coefficient closedness assertion here is proved by compact preparation and density.
- [S43](#source-43), §2, pp.50–53 and Proposition 4, pp.55–56. Compact Laurent approximation and finite zero-factor removal used in the germ proof.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Take nonzero f∈I and a chart A_K((r,1)) containing it. On each compact window J_n of an exhaustion, compact preparation gives the finite polynomial zero factor P_n of f. P_n is a unit in the Robba germ ring: each irreducible factor has all its roots at one radius below 1, beyond which its leading term dominates, so it is invertible there by Lazard Proposition 4(1); raising the inner radius past the largest root radius inverts P_n. Over discretely valued K this is also an instance of the parent unit theorem. Thus h_n=f/P_n still lies in I and in the original analytic chart, and has no zeros on J_n.
2. The inverse of h_n on J_n can be approximated arbitrarily well by a Laurent polynomial Q_n. Choose the error so that h_n Q_n→1 on every compact window. Every h_n Q_n lies in I∩A_K((r,1)); continuity of the chart inclusion shows 1 belongs to closure(I) in R_K. This proof uses no spherical completeness.
3. For finite generators choose a common chart and apply noncompact-analytic-bezout when K is spherically complete, then pass its gcd to the union.
4. For log(1+t), the zeros ζ_{p^n}−1 have radii tending to 1, so no Robba chart removes all of them. An inverse cannot exist, yet the preceding density result applies to its principal ideal.

**Checks.**

- For f=t−a with 0<|a|<1, increase the inner radius above |a|; f becomes a unit of R_K.
- For log(1+t) over Q_p, the principal ideal is proper but dense, demonstrating why closed ideals do not classify all ideals.
- The ideal zero is closed because the chart coefficient functionals separate points and remain continuous for the final seminorm topology.

<a id="target-rd-0-analytic-ring-bezout"></a>

### Γ_an,r and Γ_an,con (in particular the Robba ring) are Bézout domains

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/analytic-ring-bezout` · theorem

For r ∈ (0, r_0) and an ideal J of Γ_an,r, the conditions (a) J is closed, (b) J is finitely generated, (c) J is principal, are equivalent. Hence Γ_an,r and Γ_an,con are Bézout domains; for ℓ = k((t)) the Robba ring R is a Bézout domain (Lazard's theorem for annuli).

**Hypotheses.**

- Enough r_0-units; O is complete discretely valued. The annular residue valuation v_ℓ is allowed to be nondiscrete.

**Prerequisites.** [Vector bundles over Γ_an,r are free; closed submodules and closed ideals](#target-rd-0-vector-bundles-on-half-open-intervals-free) (`RD.0/vector-bundles-on-half-open-intervals-free`), [Γ_r and Γ_I for closed I are principal ideal domains (Lazard)](#target-rd-0-closed-interval-analytic-ring-pid) (`RD.0/closed-interval-analytic-ring-pid`), [Units of Γ_I are the elements without slopes; units of Γ_an,r lie in Γ_r[π^{-1}]](#target-rd-0-units-of-analytic-ring) (`RD.0/units-of-analytic-ring`), [Numerical membership criterion, intersections and Mayer-Vietoris splitting for Γ_I](#target-rd-0-analytic-ring-membership-and-intersections) (`RD.0/analytic-ring-membership-and-intersections`), `mathlib:IsBezout`, [Bézout and principal closed ideals on open annuli and discs](#target-rd-0-noncompact-analytic-bezout) (`RD.0/noncompact-analytic-bezout`), [Closed ideals of the Robba germ ring](#target-rd-0-robba-closed-ideals) (`RD.0/robba-closed-ideals`).

**Sources.**

- [S2](#source-2), Theorem 2.9.6, pp. 29-30. The statement.
- [S1](#source-1), Section 2.3, p. 14. The Robba ring case and its attribution to Lazard.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (c) ⇒ (a),(b) is clear; (a) ⇒ (c) is the closed-ideal corollary of the vector bundle theorem.
2. (b) ⇒ (a): reduce to J = (x, y) with 1 in the closure. Lemma 2.9.1 (refined factorisation: g ∈ Γ_r[π^{-1}] with slopes in [s,r] generating the same ideal as f on Γ_[s,r]), Lemma 2.9.2 (approximation modulo x with prescribed decay) and Lemma 2.9.3 (principal parts: compatible residues modulo f on an exhausting chain of closed intervals come from a global g) give b ∈ Γ_an,r with by − 1 divisible by x on each Γ_{I_i}, hence in Γ_an,r by the membership criterion.
3. Γ_an,con is the union of the Γ_an,r, so finitely generated ideals come from some Γ_an,r.

**Checks.**

- Non-noetherian but Bézout: the ideal (x_1, x_2, …) with x_j = Π_{i≥j}(1 − u^{p^i}/p^i) is not finitely generated, while any two elements generate a principal ideal.

<a id="target-rd-0-modules-over-bezout-domains"></a>

### Finite modules over Bézout domains: unimodular rows, saturated spans, freeness, Galois descent of saturated submodules

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/modules-over-bezout-domains` · lemma

Let R be a Bézout domain. (a) If n ≥ 2 and x_1, …, x_n generate the unit ideal there is A ∈ SL_n(R) with first row (x_1, …, x_n). (b) For a finite free R-module M and any subset S ⊆ M, the saturated span SatSpan(S) = M ∩ Frac(R)·S is free and a direct summand of M; every finite torsion-free R-module is free. (c) Every finite locally free (equivalently finite projective) R-module is free. (d) If R_1/R_2 is an extension of Bézout domains, G a group of automorphisms of R_1 over R_2 with fixed ring R_2 such that every NONZERO G-stable finitely generated ideal of R_1 meets R_2 − {0} (automatic for G finite), M_2 finite free over R_2 and N_1 ⊆ M_2 ⊗ R_1 a saturated G-stable submodule, then N_1 = N_2 ⊗ R_1 for a unique saturated N_2 ⊆ M_2. (e) An R-module is flat iff torsion-free (Mathlib).

**Hypotheses.**

- R a Bézout domain (for example the Robba ring, Γ_an,con, Γ_con[π^{-1}], a DVR).

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:IsBezout`, `mathlib:Module.Free`, `mathlib:Module.Projective`, `mathlib:Module.Flat.flat_iff_torsion_eq_bot_of_isBezout`.

**Sources.**

- [S1](#source-1), Proposition 2.5, p. 15. Part (c).
- [S1](#source-1), Lemma 2.4, p. 15. Part (b).
- [S1](#source-1), Lemma 2.6, pp. 15-16. Part (d).
- [S2](#source-2), Definition 2.9.5, p. 29. The same facts as used in slope filtrations revisited.
- [S1](#source-1), Lemma 2.3, p. 14. Row completion, with n ≥ 2; the omitted n = 1 boundary is recorded among the source issues.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a) Monodromy paper Lemma 2.3: induction on n via the generator d of (x_1, …, x_{n−1}).
2. (b) Lemma 2.4: induction on rank using (a) to split off a primitive vector.
3. (c) Proposition 2.5: F → M surjective, N = SatSpan(ker), F/N free of the right rank, and M → F/N is locally a surjection of free modules of equal rank.
4. (d) Lemma 2.6: induction on rank, descending one vector y using G-invariance.
5. (e) is Module.Flat.flat_iff_torsion_eq_bot_of_isBezout.

**Checks.**

- Over a DVR (a PID) (b)-(c) reduce to the structure theorem; for the Robba ring they give that σ-modules and ∇-modules may be taken free.
- Rank-one negative control: over Q the unimodular row (2) cannot be the row of an SL_1 matrix; GL_1 completion works. For n = 0 there is no first row.
- For a finite group G and a nonzero G-stable ideal, the product of the G-translates of a chosen nonzero element is a nonzero invariant element of the ideal. The zero ideal has no such element.

<a id="target-rd-0-finite-separable-extensions-of-analytic-rings"></a>

### Finite separable extensions: Γ^L_con finite étale over Γ^ℓ_con and Γ^L_an,con = Γ^ℓ_an,con ⊗ Γ^L_con

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/finite-separable-extensions-of-analytic-rings` · theorem

Let L/ℓ be finite separable. Then Γ^L is a finite unramified extension of Γ^ℓ, σ extends uniquely to Γ^L (and Gal(L/ℓ) acts when L/ℓ is Galois), Γ^L has enough units if Γ^ℓ does, Γ^L_con is finite étale over Γ^ℓ_con with Γ^L_con ≅ Γ^ℓ_con[x]/(P(x)) for any x ∈ Γ^L_con whose reduction generates L over ℓ (P the minimal polynomial), and the multiplication map Γ^ℓ_an,con ⊗_{Γ^ℓ_con} Γ^L_con → Γ^L_an,con is an isomorphism, Γ^L_an,con ≅ Γ^ℓ_an,con[x]/(P(x)). If L/ℓ is Galois with group G, the G-invariants of Frac Γ^L_an,con are Frac Γ^ℓ_an,con. For ℓ = k((t)) this gives, for every finite separable extension L of k((t)), the rings R^int_L, R^bd_L, R_L; the pair (R^int, m_R) is henselian, so finite étale covers of the boundary annulus correspond to finite separable extensions of k((t)) (formally étale covers).

**Hypotheses.**

- Enough units for Γ^ℓ; pseudo-finite separable extensions L = M^{q^{-n}} are handled by Frobenius twisting (Definition 2.2.8).

**Prerequisites.** [Kedlaya's analytic rings Γ^ℓ_I, Γ^ℓ_an,r and Γ^ℓ_an,con](#target-rd-0-analytic-ring) (`RD.0/analytic-ring`), [W_con(ℓ, O) is a henselian discrete valuation ring](#target-rd-0-overconvergent-witt-vectors-henselian) (`RD.0/overconvergent-witt-vectors-henselian`), [Numerical membership criterion, intersections and Mayer-Vietoris splitting for Γ_I](#target-rd-0-analytic-ring-membership-and-intersections) (`RD.0/analytic-ring-membership-and-intersections`).

**Sources.**

- [S2](#source-2), Proposition 2.4.10, p. 15. The base-change isomorphism.
- [S2](#source-2), Corollary 2.4.11, p. 15. Galois invariants.
- [S2](#source-2), Lemma 2.2.12, p. 9. Enough units pass to extensions.
- [S8](#source-8), Proposition 3.5.5, p. 15. Henselian pair for the Robba ring.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Unramified extension and extension of σ: Definition 2.2.8 (Γ^L is the unique unramified lift; σ extends uniquely by henselian lifting of the q-power map).
2. Enough units: Lemma 2.2.12 (primitive element x lifted by henselianity, equivalence of norms on L over ℓ, estimate of v_{n,s} of lifts).
3. Γ^L_con = Γ^ℓ_con[x]/(P): Proposition 2.2.15; Γ^L_s ≅ Γ^ℓ_s[x]/(P) for small s by Lemma 2.1.12, hence Proposition 2.4.10.
4. Galois invariants of fraction fields: Corollary 2.4.11 (norm trick).
5. Henselian pair (R^int, m_R): overview Proposition 3.5.5 (Newton iteration with control on |·|_r), giving Definition 3.5.6 of formally étale covers.

**Checks.**

- For L = k'((t)) with k'/k finite separable, Γ^L_an,con is the Robba ring over the unramified extension K' of K.
- Artin-Schreier: L = k((t))[u]/(u^p − u − t^{-1}) gives R_L = R[u']/((1+πu')^p − (1 + pπ t^{-1})) with π^{p−1} = −p (overview Lemma 5.3.3).

<a id="target-rd-0-robba-ring-flat-base-change"></a>

### Flatness, faithful flatness and base change for R^bd → R, R^bd → E and finite separable extensions

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/robba-ring-flat-base-change` · lemma

(a) R and E are free, hence faithfully flat, modules over the field R^bd; for a map f of finite R^bd-modules, f is injective (surjective, bijective) iff f ⊗ R is, iff f ⊗ E is. (b) For L/k((t)) finite separable of degree d: R^int_L is finite étale of rank d over R^int, R^bd_L = R^bd ⊗_{R^int} R^int_L, R_L = R ⊗_{R^bd} R^bd_L and E_L = E ⊗_{R^bd} R^bd_L are finite free of rank d, hence faithfully flat; if L/k((t)) is Galois with group G then (R_L)^G = R, (R^bd_L)^G = R^bd, (E_L)^G = E. (c) Every torsion-free module over R (for example R^alg, R_L, or any domain containing R) is flat over R; every finitely generated submodule of a finite free R-module is free. (d) For a finite free R^bd-module M: M = (M ⊗ E) ∩ (M ⊗ R^alg_con[π^{-1}]) inside M ⊗ W(ℓ^alg, O)[π^{-1}], via Γ[π^{-1}] ∩ Γ^alg_con[π^{-1}] = Γ_con[π^{-1}].

**Hypotheses.**

- K discretely valued; L/k((t)) finite separable; in (d) a Frobenius lift is fixed to embed R^bd and E into W(ℓ^alg, O)[π^{-1}].

**Prerequisites.** [The bounded Robba ring R^bd is a henselian discretely valued field with residue field k((t)); R^bd = R ∩ E](#target-rd-0-bounded-robba-ring) (`RD.0/bounded-robba-ring`), [Finite separable extensions: Γ^L_con finite étale over Γ^ℓ_con and Γ^L_an,con = Γ^ℓ_an,con ⊗ Γ^L_con](#target-rd-0-finite-separable-extensions-of-analytic-rings) (`RD.0/finite-separable-extensions-of-analytic-rings`), [Γ_an,r and Γ_an,con (in particular the Robba ring) are Bézout domains](#target-rd-0-analytic-ring-bezout) (`RD.0/analytic-ring-bezout`), [Finite modules over Bézout domains: unimodular rows, saturated spans, freeness, Galois descent of saturated submodules](#target-rd-0-modules-over-bezout-domains) (`RD.0/modules-over-bezout-domains`), [Numerical membership criterion, intersections and Mayer-Vietoris splitting for Γ_I](#target-rd-0-analytic-ring-membership-and-intersections) (`RD.0/analytic-ring-membership-and-intersections`), `mathlib:Module.FaithfullyFlat`.

**Sources.**

- [S2](#source-2), Proposition 2.4.10, p. 15. Part (b).
- [S2](#source-2), Proof of Theorem 5.5.2, p. 59. Part (d) in the form used for descent.
- [S1](#source-1), Section 1.1, p. 3. The base change the local monodromy theorem uses (Theorem 1.1).

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a) Vector spaces over a field are free, and a nonzero free module is faithfully flat; exactness can be tested after faithfully flat base change.
2. (b) Finite-separable-extension theorem (Propositions 2.2.15, 2.4.10) for the isomorphisms and freeness; Galois invariants on the rings follow from Corollary 2.4.11 and the analogous statement on Γ^L_con (Galois theory of the finite étale extension).
3. (c) R is a Bézout domain; apply the Mathlib criterion flat ⇔ torsion-free over a Bézout domain and the saturated-span lemma.
4. (d) Coordinatewise application of the intersection statement (c) of the membership-and-intersections lemma.

**Checks.**

- For L = k((t^{1/n})) with p ∤ n: R_L = R[t^{1/n}] is free with basis 1, t^{1/n}, …, t^{(n−1)/n}.
- An R^bd-linear endomorphism of (R^bd)^n with nonzero determinant stays injective on R^n.

<a id="target-rd-0-completed-algebraic-closure-is-algebraically-closed"></a>

### The completion of an algebraically closed nonarchimedean field is algebraically closed, in every characteristic

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/completed-algebraic-closure-is-algebraically-closed` · lemma

Let F be a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value, F̄ an algebraic closure with the unique extension of the absolute value, and C_F the completion of F̄. Then C_F is algebraically closed. More generally, if L is a complete nonarchimedean field containing a dense algebraically closed subfield, then L is algebraically closed. In particular, for F = k((t)) (characteristic p) the completed algebraic closure ℓ^alg used for the extended Robba ring (RD.0/extended-robba-ring) is algebraically closed, hence perfect.

**Hypotheses.**

- No hypothesis on the characteristic: Mathlib's IsAlgClosed.of_denseRange is proved only for complete fields of characteristic 0 (it uses Krasner's lemma, which needs separability); the argument below uses continuity of roots instead.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/Analysis/Normed/Field/CompletionAlgClosed`, `TauCeti`

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:IsAlgClosed.of_exists_root`, `mathlib:Polynomial.exists_monic_and_natDegree_eq_and_norm_map_algebraMap_coeff_sub_lt`, `mathlib:Polynomial.exists_aroots_norm_sub_lt_of_norm_coeff_sub_lt`, `mathlib:spectralNorm.normedField`, `mathlib:spectralNorm_extends`, `mathlib:UniformSpace.Completion`, `mathlib:IsAlgClosed.of_denseRange`, `mathlib:IsAlgClosed.exists_pow_nat_eq`, `mathlib:PerfectField`.

**Sources.**

- [S59](#source-59), Theorem 1.1, §2 (proof), pp. 1-2; Lemma 3.1, p. 3. The completion of an algebraic closure of a complete nonarchimedean field is algebraically closed, proved by approximating a monic polynomial by ones over the algebraic closure and extracting a Cauchy subsequence of their roots, with no characteristic assumption.
- [S2](#source-2), Convention 2.2.16, p. 9 (arXiv v4). Kedlaya works with Γ^alg over the completed algebraic closure of k((t)) (as opposed to the uncompleted one of the monodromy paper), using that this complete field is algebraically closed without giving a reference.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Let f ∈ C_F[X] be monic of degree n ≥ 1. Approximate f by monic polynomials f_j ∈ F̄[X] of degree n with coefficients converging to those of f (Mathlib Polynomial.exists_monic_and_natDegree_eq_and_norm_map_algebraMap_coeff_sub_lt, using density of F̄).
2. Each f_j has a root r_j ∈ F̄; the r_j are bounded by C = max |a_i|^{1/(n−i)} and |f(r_j)| ≤ max_i |a_i − a_{ij}|·max(1, C^{n−1}) → 0 (Conrad, Math 248A handout, §2).
3. In a splitting field L of f over C_F (with the spectral norm extending the absolute value, Mathlib spectralNorm.normedField and spectralNorm_extends), f = Π (X − ρ_k), so Π_k |r_j − ρ_k| → 0; by pigeonhole a subsequence of the r_j converges to one root ρ_k (compare Mathlib Polynomial.exists_aroots_norm_sub_lt_of_norm_coeff_sub_lt, which needs no separability).
4. That subsequence is Cauchy in the complete field C_F, so its limit lies in C_F and is a root of f; hence C_F is algebraically closed (Mathlib IsAlgClosed.of_exists_root).
5. Perfectness: in an algebraically closed field every element has a p-th root (Mathlib IsAlgClosed.exists_pow_nat_eq), so it is perfect (Mathlib PerfectField; the instance IsAlgClosed.perfectField at the pin).

**Checks.**

- Characteristic 0: C_p = completion of Q̄_p is algebraically closed (Mathlib PadicComplex.isAlgClosed), recovered by this argument.
- Characteristic p: the completion of the algebraic closure of F_p((t)) is algebraically closed although F_p((t))^alg is not complete and has infinite degree over F_p((t)) (Conrad, §1).
- Non-example: F̄ itself is not complete when [F̄ : F] is infinite (Conrad, §1, citing Bosch-Güntzer-Remmert 3.4.3/1), so completing is necessary; and a complete discretely valued field such as k((t)) is never algebraically closed (Eisenstein polynomials X^e − t).

<a id="target-rd-0-extended-robba-ring"></a>

### The extended Robba ring R^alg = Γ^alg_an,con over the completed algebraic closure of k((t))

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/extended-robba-ring` · construction

Let ℓ^alg be the completion of an algebraic closure of k((t)) with v(t) = 1 (a perfect, algebraically closed, complete valued field), Γ^alg = W(ℓ^alg, O) with the Witt vector Frobenius σ (bijective), and let Γ^alg_r, Γ^alg_con, Γ^alg_I, Γ^alg_an,r and R^alg := Γ^alg_an,con be the analytic rings of the analytic-ring construction for ℓ^alg (with enough r-units for every r, Teichmüller lifts being units). R^alg is a Bézout domain; its units are the nonzero elements of the field Γ^alg_con[π^{-1}]; the residue field of the henselian DVR Γ^alg_con is ℓ^alg (algebraically closed); for every closed interval I the ring Γ^alg_I is a PID; the union of the Γ^L_I over pseudo-finite separable extensions L of k((t)) is dense in Γ^alg_I when 0 ∉ I. A Frobenius lift σ on R^int determines a σ-equivariant embedding R ↪ R^alg (next node). Also Γ^alg[π^{-1}] = W(ℓ^alg, O)[π^{-1}] is a complete discretely valued field with algebraically closed residue field (the ring over which generic slopes are read).

**Hypotheses.**

- ℓ^alg is complete (Kedlaya's convention 2.2.16; the monodromy paper uses the uncompleted algebraic closure, which gives the same Γ^alg_an,con, Remark 2.4.13).
- O is fixed; Kedlaya assumes π fixed by σ when working over R^alg (Convention 4.0.1), which is harmless after enlarging O.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Robba/ExtendedRobba`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Kedlaya's analytic rings Γ^ℓ_I, Γ^ℓ_an,r and Γ^ℓ_an,con](#target-rd-0-analytic-ring) (`RD.0/analytic-ring`), [Γ_an,r and Γ_an,con (in particular the Robba ring) are Bézout domains](#target-rd-0-analytic-ring-bezout) (`RD.0/analytic-ring-bezout`), [Units of Γ_I are the elements without slopes; units of Γ_an,r lie in Γ_r[π^{-1}]](#target-rd-0-units-of-analytic-ring) (`RD.0/units-of-analytic-ring`), [Γ_r and Γ_I for closed I are principal ideal domains (Lazard)](#target-rd-0-closed-interval-analytic-ring-pid) (`RD.0/closed-interval-analytic-ring-pid`), [Finite separable extensions: Γ^L_con finite étale over Γ^ℓ_con and Γ^L_an,con = Γ^ℓ_an,con ⊗ Γ^L_con](#target-rd-0-finite-separable-extensions-of-analytic-rings) (`RD.0/finite-separable-extensions-of-analytic-rings`), [The completion of an algebraically closed nonarchimedean field is algebraically closed, in every characteristic](#target-rd-0-completed-algebraic-closure-is-algebraically-closed) (`RD.0/completed-algebraic-closure-is-algebraically-closed`).

**Sources.**

- [S2](#source-2), Convention 2.2.16, p. 9. The rings Γ^alg, Γ^alg_an,con.
- [S2](#source-2), Convention 4.0.1, p. 39. R^alg is the ring of Chapter 4.
- [S2](#source-2), Lemma 2.4.12, p. 15. Density.
- [S3](#source-3), Remark 4.10, p. 10. The name and the role of the extended Robba ring.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- Kedlaya, slope filtrations revisited, Chapter 4: every σ-module over R^alg is a direct sum of standard modules (Theorem 4.5.7); absolute slopes of σ-modules over R are read over R^alg
- Kedlaya, slope filtrations revisited, Chapter 5: generic and special polygons of σ-modules over R^bd are compared inside Γ^alg_con[π^{-1}], Γ^alg[π^{-1}] and R^alg
- RD.1 Frobenius slopes and Dieudonné-Manin: definition of special (absolute) slopes
- RD.2 slope filtration descent: descent from R^alg to R via Galois and Frobenius (Theorem 6.4.1)

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ExtendedRobba.ring` |  | R^alg = Γ^alg_an,con with its limit-of-Fréchet topology and bijective Frobenius σ. |
| `ExtendedRobba.boundedSubring` |  | Γ^alg_con, a henselian DVR with algebraically closed residue field ℓ^alg, and the field Γ^alg_con[π^{-1}]. |
| `ExtendedRobba.isBezout` |  | R^alg is a Bézout domain. |
| `ExtendedRobba.units` |  | (R^alg)^× = Γ^alg_con[π^{-1}] − {0}. |
| `ExtendedRobba.frobenius_bijective` |  | σ is an automorphism of R^alg (Witt Frobenius on a perfect field). |
| `ExtendedRobba.dense_union` |  | ∪_L Γ^L_I is dense in Γ^alg_I for 0 ∉ I. |

**Unit tests.**

- `extendedRobba_trivial_residue` (degenerate): For the trivially valued perfect field ℓ = k^alg the same construction gives W(k^alg, O)[π^{-1}], a field.
- `extendedRobba_H0_twist` (computation): The map y ↦ Σ_{i∈Z} [y^{q^{-i}}] π^i is a bijection from {y ∈ ℓ^alg : v(y) > 0} onto H^0(R^alg(−1)) = {x ∈ R^alg : σ(x) = π x} (Lemma 4.3.1, with π fixed by σ).
- `extendedRobba_units` (characterisation): An element of R^alg is a unit iff it is a nonzero element of Γ^alg_con[π^{-1}].
- `extendedRobba_not_over_bounded` (non-example): H^0(R^alg(−1)) ≠ 0 while H^0(Γ^alg_con[π^{-1}](−1)) = 0: the eigenvector Σ [y^{q^{-i}}]π^i is not bounded.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Instantiate the analytic-ring construction with ℓ = ℓ^alg (perfect, so Γ^ℓ = W(ℓ, O) and Definition 2.1.5 applies directly).
2. Bézout, units and PID: the corresponding theorems for analytic rings (enough units holds by Remark 2.2.11(a); v on ℓ^alg is not discrete, but its value group is Q; Kedlaya's Chapter 2 hypotheses are met because the valuation used for w_r is the π-adic one, which is discrete).
3. Density: Lemma 2.4.12.

**Checks.**

- For the trivially valued perfect field ℓ = k^alg one gets W(k^alg, O)[π^{-1}], the base of classical Dieudonné-Manin theory.
- H^0 of the rank-one σ-module R^alg(−1) is in bijection with the maximal ideal of ℓ^alg (Lemma 4.3.1): nonzero Frobenius eigenvectors of negative slope exist over R^alg but not over O[π^{-1}].
- For perfect k, K=W(k)[1/p], q=p and standard σ(t)=t^p, identify this target with FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory §§R07.4.7–R07.4.8, including its coefficient carriers, degree convention, standard blocks and increasing slope filtration where applicable. This roadmap supplies the stated general coefficient/Frobenius version and its compatibility with that imported special case, rather than a second implementation of the special case.

<a id="target-rd-0-frobenius-equivariant-embedding"></a>

### The σ-equivariant embedding of R^int, R^bd, E, R into Γ^alg_con, Γ^alg_con[π^{-1}], Γ^alg[π^{-1}], R^alg

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/frobenius-equivariant-embedding` · construction

Given a Frobenius lift σ on O_E carrying O_K into itself, the completed direct limit of O_E →σ O_E →σ ⋯ is identified with W(k((t))^perf, O^perf), and composing with W(k((t))^perf) → W(ℓ^alg) gives an injective ring map ι_σ: O_E → W(ℓ^alg, O^perf) with ι_σ∘σ = σ_Witt∘ι_σ, reducing to the inclusion k((t)) ⊆ ℓ^alg. It maps R^int into Γ^alg_con, R^bd into Γ^alg_con[π^{-1}], E into Γ^alg[π^{-1}], and extends by continuity to R → R^alg, carrying functions on |π|^s ≤ |t| < 1 into Γ^alg_an,s for s small; it is compatible with w_s by the equality of naive and true valuations. For the standard lift σ(t) = t^q (O = W(k), k perfect), ι_σ(t) is the Teichmüller lift [t]. Different Frobenius lifts give different embeddings (ι_σ(t) is determined by σ).

**Hypotheses.**

- σ carries O into itself (Convention 2.2.6); after replacing O by O^perf the embedding lands in W(ℓ^alg, O^perf) (= W(ℓ^alg, O) when σ is bijective on O, e.g. O = W(k) with k perfect).

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Robba/ExtendedRobba`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Weakly continuous Frobenius lifts on the integral Amice ring](#target-rd-0-frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring) (`RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring`), [The Robba ring R_K is Kedlaya's analytic ring Γ^{k((t))}_an,con: naive and true partial valuations agree](#target-rd-0-robba-ring) (`RD.0/robba-ring`), [The extended Robba ring R^alg = Γ^alg_an,con over the completed algebraic closure of k((t))](#target-rd-0-extended-robba-ring) (`RD.0/extended-robba-ring`).

**Sources.**

- [S2](#source-2), Definition 2.2.3, p. 8. The construction of the embedding.
- [S3](#source-3), Remark 4.7, p. 9. The standard-lift case.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- Kedlaya, slope filtrations revisited, Definition 4.6.1: absolute HN slopes of a σ-module M over Γ_an,con are the HN slopes of M ⊗ R^alg
- Kedlaya, slope filtrations revisited, Chapter 5: generic slopes of M over Γ_con[π^{-1}] are read over Γ^alg[π^{-1}] via this embedding
- RD.1 Frobenius slopes: special and generic slope polygons

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `RobbaRing.toExtended` |  | ι_σ: R → R^alg, the σ-equivariant injective ring map, together with its restrictions to R^int, R^bd and E → Γ^alg[π^{-1}]. |
| `RobbaRing.toExtended_frobenius` |  | ι_σ(σ(f)) = σ_Witt(ι_σ(f)). |
| `RobbaRing.toExtended_injective` |  | ι_σ is injective on R and on E. |
| `RobbaRing.toExtended_residue` |  | On residue fields ι_σ induces the inclusion k((t)) ⊆ ℓ^alg. |
| `RobbaRing.toExtended_standard` |  | For the standard lift and O = W(k): ι_σ(t) = [t]. |

**Unit tests.**

- `toExtended_standard_t` (computation): For K = W(k)[1/p], k perfect, and the standard lift: ι_σ(t) = [t] and ι_σ(Σ a_i t^i) = Σ a_i [t]^i.
- `toExtended_frobenius_commutes` (characterisation): ι_σ∘σ = σ∘ι_σ on R.
- `toExtended_depends_on_lift` (non-example): For the cyclotomic lift over Q_p, ι_σ(t) = [1 + t̄] − 1 ≠ [t̄]: the embedding depends on σ.
- `toExtended_residue_inclusion` (compatibility): Reduction modulo π of ι_σ on R^int is the inclusion k((t)) ⊆ ℓ^alg.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Definition 2.2.3 (completed direct limit ≅ W(ℓ^perf, O^perf)) and Convention 2.2.16 (embedding into W(ℓ^alg, ·)).
2. Images of R^int and R: the Robba-ring comparison identifies R^int with Γ_con and the w_s with the naive ones, so ι_σ(Γ_s) ⊆ Γ^alg_s and ι_σ extends to the Fréchet completions.
3. Standard lift: [t] is the unique lift of t with σ([t]) = [t]^q, and σ-equivariance forces ι_σ(t) = [t] (Notes on isocrystals, Remark 4.7).

**Checks.**

- The composite R^bd → Γ^alg_con[π^{-1}] → ℓ^alg on residue fields is k((t)) ⊆ ℓ^alg.
- For the cyclotomic lift σ(t) = (1+t)^p − 1, ι_σ(1+t) = [1 + t̄] (the Teichmüller lift of the image of 1 + t).

<a id="target-rd-0-derivation-on-robba-ring"></a>

### The derivation d/dt on annulus rings, R, R^bd, R^int, O_E and E, its norm bounds and Ω^1 = R dt

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/derivation-on-robba-ring` · construction

d = d/dt, Σ c_i t^i ↦ Σ i c_i t^{i−1}, is a K-linear derivation of the ring of functions on each annulus A(I) and of R, R^bd, E (O_K-linear on R^int and O_E). For every ρ in the relevant interval, |df/dt|_ρ ≤ ρ^{-1}|f|_ρ, with equality for f = t^i and p ∤ i; the operator norm of d/dt on (functions on A(I), |·|_ρ) is ρ^{-1} and its spectral norm is p^{-1/(p−1)}ρ^{-1}. d commutes with the restriction maps between annuli of different radii and is continuous for the Fréchet topology of each annulus ring and the LF topology of R. The module of continuous differentials of R over K (resp. of R^int over O_K) is free of rank one on dt, with df = (df/dt) dt; connections on modules over these rings are automatically integrable. ker(d/dt on R) = K and R/(d/dt)R = K·t^{-1}. For a Frobenius lift σ: d(σ(f))/dt = (dσ(t)/dt)·σ(df/dt), and dσ(t)/dt ∈ π R^int (so dσ ≡ 0 modulo π).

**Hypotheses.**

- Characteristic 0 is used for ker d = K and for the cokernel computation; the norm bounds use only |i| ≤ 1 for integers i.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Robba/Derivative`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [The bounded Robba ring R^bd is a henselian discretely valued field with residue field k((t)); R^bd = R ∩ E](#target-rd-0-bounded-robba-ring) (`RD.0/bounded-robba-ring`), [Weakly continuous Frobenius lifts on the integral Amice ring](#target-rd-0-frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring) (`RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring`), `mathlib:Derivation`, `mathlib:PowerSeries.derivative`.

**Sources.**

- [S8](#source-8), Definition 5.1.1, p. 27. Operator norm.
- [S8](#source-8), Definition 5.1.2, p. 28. Spectral norm p^{-1/(p-1)} r^{-1}.
- [S2](#source-2), Example 7.1.3, p. 66. Ω^1 free on dt.
- [S8](#source-8), Example 4.1.11, p. 18. Kernel and cokernel.
- [S2](#source-2), Remark 7.1.4, p. 67. dσ vanishes modulo π.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- RD.1 differential modules: a connection on a finite free R-module is determined by the action of d/dt
- RD.1 generic radius: the spectral norm p^{-1/(p-1)}ρ^{-1} of d/dt normalises the generic radius
- Kedlaya, slope filtrations revisited, Definition 7.1.5 and Remark 7.1.4: (σ,∇)-modules use Ω^1 = R dt and dσ ≡ 0 mod π
- RD.3-RD.4: local calculations of overconvergent de Rham complexes on annuli near the boundary

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `RobbaRing.derivative` |  | d/dt as a Derivation K R R, restricting to derivations of R^bd, E and O_K-derivations of R^int, O_E. |
| `RobbaRing.derivative_monomial` |  | d(t^n)/dt = n t^{n−1} for n ∈ Z. |
| `RobbaRing.gaussNorm_derivative_le` |  | \|df/dt\|_ρ ≤ ρ^{-1}\|f\|_ρ. |
| `RobbaRing.derivative_restrict` |  | d/dt commutes with restriction from functions on r < \|t\| < 1 to functions on r' < \|t\| < 1. |
| `RobbaRing.continuous_derivative` |  | d/dt is continuous for the Fréchet topology of each annulus ring and the LF topology of R. |
| `RobbaRing.kaehler_free` |  | The continuous differentials of R over K form the free module R·dt with universal derivation f ↦ (df/dt) dt. |
| `RobbaRing.ker_derivative` |  | ker(d/dt) = K and R = K·t^{-1} ⊕ image(d/dt). |
| `RobbaRing.derivative_frobenius` |  | d(σf)/dt = (dσ(t)/dt)·σ(df/dt), with dσ(t)/dt ∈ π R^int. |

**Unit tests.**

- `derivative_t_pow` (computation): d(t^{-3})/dt = −3 t^{-4} in R.
- `derivative_ker` (degenerate): If df/dt = 0 for f ∈ R then f ∈ K.
- `derivative_compat_powerSeries` (compatibility): On power series converging on the open unit disc, d/dt agrees with PowerSeries.derivative under the coefficient map.
- `derivative_not_surjective` (non-example): t^{-1} is not in the image of d/dt on R (it spans the cokernel); a residue-free Laurent series is.
- `gaussNorm_derivative_strict` (computation): |d(t^p)/dt|_ρ = p^{-1}ρ^{p−1} < ρ^{-1}|t^p|_ρ for every ρ.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Termwise differentiation preserves each convergence condition since |i c_i| ρ^{i−1} ≤ ρ^{-1}|c_i|ρ^i; equality at t^i with p ∤ i gives the operator norm; |(d/dt)^s f|_ρ ≤ |s!| ρ^{-s}|f|_ρ with equality at f = t^s (the coefficients s!·C(i,s) have C(i,s) ∈ Z), and lim_s (|s!| ρ^{-s})^{1/s} = p^{-1/(p−1)}ρ^{-1} (overview Definitions 5.1.1-5.1.2).
2. Compatibility with restriction and continuity follow from the uniform bound on each circle.
3. Continuous differentials: slope filtrations revisited Example 7.1.3 and the monodromy paper Section 2.5 (Ω^1_R free on du with d(Σ x_i u^i) = Σ i x_i u^{i−1} du).
4. Kernel and cokernel: a Laurent series with Σ i c_i t^{i−1} = 0 has c_i = 0 for i ≠ 0; Σ_{i ≠ −1} c_i t^i has the primitive Σ c_i t^{i+1}/(i+1), which converges at every interior radius after choosing a slightly larger closed subannulus: the p-adic norm |1/(i+1)| is at most the ordinary integer absolute value of i+1, and polynomial growth is absorbed by the exponential decay from the larger subannulus (overview Example 4.1.11).
5. Chain rule for σ and dσ(t)/dt ∈ π R^int: σ(t) = t^q + πh with h ∈ R^int and q ∈ pZ ⊆ πO_K.

**Checks.**

- Change of annulus radius: for r < r' < 1 and f a function on r < |t| < 1, (df/dt) restricted to r' < |t| < 1 equals d/dt of the restriction, and sup_{ρ ∈ [r'', 1)} ρ|df/dt|_ρ/|f|_ρ ≤ 1 for any r'' > r.
- |d(t^p)/dt|_ρ = |p| ρ^{p−1} < ρ^{-1}|t^p|_ρ: the bound is strict when p divides the exponent.
- d/dt(log(1+t)) = 1/(1+t) with log(1+t) ∈ R: the derivative of an unbounded element can be bounded.

<a id="target-rd-0-change-of-frobenius-lift-taylor-formula"></a>

### Two Frobenius lifts differ by a convergent Taylor series; dependence on the coordinate

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/change-of-frobenius-lift-taylor-formula` · lemma

Let σ_1, σ_2 be Frobenius lifts on R^int with the same σ_K. Then δ = σ_2(t) − σ_1(t) ∈ π R^int and for every f ∈ R: σ_2(f) = Σ_{n≥0} δ^n · σ_1((1/n!) d^n f/dt^n), the series converging in R (in R^int, R^bd, E for f in these rings). More generally, for t' ∈ R^int with t' − t ∈ π R^int, the substitution t ↦ t' is given by the convergent Taylor series f ↦ Σ_n (t' − t)^n (1/n!) d^n f/dt^n. Hence the standard lift for the coordinate t' (t' ↦ t'^q) and the standard lift for t (t ↦ t^q) are related by this formula; ring-level Frobenius invariants such as H^0 of the rank-one σ-module R(n) for n < 0 depend on the choice of σ when k((t)) is imperfect.

**Hypotheses.**

- σ_1 and σ_2 agree on K; the coordinate change is required to reduce to t modulo (π, t^2).

**Prerequisites.** [Weakly continuous Frobenius lifts on the integral Amice ring](#target-rd-0-frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring) (`RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring`), [The derivation d/dt on annulus rings, R, R^bd, R^int, O_E and E, its norm bounds and Ω^1 = R dt](#target-rd-0-derivation-on-robba-ring) (`RD.0/derivation-on-robba-ring`), [The Robba ring R_K is Kedlaya's analytic ring Γ^{k((t))}_an,con: naive and true partial valuations agree](#target-rd-0-robba-ring) (`RD.0/robba-ring`).

**Sources.**

- [S9](#source-9), Definition 2.6.2, p. 10. The ring-level Taylor map for a change of coordinates reducing to the identity.
- [S8](#source-8), Remark 4.1.9, pp. 17-18. The Taylor comparison of two maps with the same reduction.
- [S2](#source-2), Remark 3.3.6, p. 34. Dependence of Frobenius invariants on the lift.

**Construction or proof.**

1. δ ∈ π R^int because σ_i(t) ≡ t^q mod π.
2. Convergence: |(1/n!) d^n f/dt^n|_ρ ≤ ρ^{-n}|f|_ρ (binomial coefficients are integers), |σ_1(f)|_ρ = |f|_{ρ^q} near the boundary (σ_K is isometric), and |δ|_ρ ≤ |π| near the boundary; so the n-th term is bounded by (|π|ρ^{-1})^n |f| on a thin annulus.
3. Both sides are continuous σ_K-semilinear ring endomorphisms (the right side is multiplicative by the Leibniz rule for divided derivatives) agreeing on K and on t, hence equal by the uniqueness part of the Frobenius-lift node.
4. The same argument with σ_1 replaced by the identity gives the coordinate-change formula; this is the ring case of the Taylor map of Kedlaya's Swan conductors I, Definition 2.6.2, and of the Taylor isomorphism of the overview, Remark 4.1.9.
5. Dependence of H^0(R(n)) on σ: slope filtrations revisited Remark 3.3.6 (for O = Z_p and q = p the standard lift gives H^0(R(−1)) = 0, while the cyclotomic lift gives log(1+t) ∈ H^0(R(−1)), since σ(log(1+t)) = p·log(1+t)).

**Checks.**

- For σ_1 standard and σ_2 cyclotomic over Q_p: δ = (1+t)^p − 1 − t^p = Σ_{0<i<p} C(p,i) t^i ∈ pR^int, and σ_2(t^{-1}) = Σ_n δ^n (−1)^n t^{-p(n+1)}.
- Coordinate change t' = t + p: the Taylor series of f(t + p) around t converges on R since |p| < ρ.

<a id="target-rd-0-completion-versus-overconvergence"></a>

### A function converging only on the closed unit disc separates completion from overconvergence

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/completion-versus-overconvergence` · lemma

(a) g = Σ_{n≥0} p^n x^{p^n} lies in the Tate algebra K⟨x⟩ (its coefficients tend to 0) but not in the dagger algebra K⟨x⟩† = ∪_{ρ>1} K⟨x/ρ⟩: for every ρ > 1, |p^n|ρ^{p^n} → ∞. (b) ω = Σ_{n≥0} p^n x^{p^n−1} dx is a 1-form on K⟨x⟩ (in fact on O_K⟨x⟩, the π-adic completion of O_K[x]) which is a π-adic limit of exact forms d(Σ_{n≤N} x^{p^n}) but is not exact there, since its only formal primitives Σ x^{p^n} + c have coefficients not tending to 0; so H^1_dR(K⟨x⟩/K) ≠ 0, whereas every 1-form on K⟨x⟩† is exact (termwise primitives preserve overconvergence), so H^1(Ω^•_{K⟨x⟩†}) = 0. Also ω ∉ K⟨x⟩† dx. (c) On the boundary side, f = Σ_{n≥0} p^n t^{-p^n} lies in O_E ⊆ E but not in R^bd: for every ρ < 1, |p^n|ρ^{-p^n} → ∞. So E ≠ R^bd, and the π-adic completion of R^bd is E.

**Hypotheses.**

- K a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with residue characteristic p (normalised |p| = p^{-1}).

**Prerequisites.** [The bounded Robba ring R^bd is a henselian discretely valued field with residue field k((t)); R^bd = R ∩ E](#target-rd-0-bounded-robba-ring) (`RD.0/bounded-robba-ring`), [The derivation d/dt on annulus rings, R, R^bd, R^int, O_E and E, its norm bounds and Ω^1 = R dt](#target-rd-0-derivation-on-robba-ring) (`RD.0/derivation-on-robba-ring`), `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-algebra`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/fringe-presentation`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/fringe-topology`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-differentials`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-tensor-product`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-rational-localisation`, [Weakly continuous Frobenius lifts on the integral Amice ring](#target-rd-0-frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring) (`RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring`).

**Sources.**

- [S6](#source-6), Section 2, p. 2. Part (b).
- [S6](#source-6), Section 2, p. 2. Why completion must be replaced by weak completion.
- [S1](#source-1), Section 2.3, p. 13. The Robba ring and the completed ring E are incomparable; part (c).

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a) v_p(p^n)/p^n = n/p^n → 0, so the coefficients tend to 0 but log_p ρ · p^n − n → ∞ for ρ > 1.
2. (b) Formal primitives are unique up to constants; the primitive Σ x^{p^n} is not in O_K⟨x⟩ ⊗ K. For η = Σ a_i x^i dx overconvergent, Σ a_i x^{i+1}/(i+1) is overconvergent because |1/(i+1)| ≤ i+1 grows polynomially (van der Put, Section 2.3: the de Rham complex of the weak completion).
3. (c) As in (a) with t^{-1} in place of x; f ∈ O_E because p^n → 0; the completion statement is part of the bounded-Robba-ring theorem.

**Checks.**

- Numerical check (PARI/GP, p = 3): v_3(a_m)/m at m = 3^n equals n/3^n = 0.333, 0.222, 0.111, 0.049, 0.021, 0.008 for n = 1..6 (tending to 0), and for ρ = 3^{-1/10} the exponent 3^n/10 − n equals −0.7, −1.1, −0.3, 4.1, 19.3, 66.9, 211.7, 648.1 for n = 1..8, so |p^n|ρ^{-p^n} → ∞.
- Kedlaya's Monsky-Washnitzer example: for A = R[x] the sum Σ p^n x^{p^n −1} dx is a limit of exact differentials but not exact over the completion A^∞.

<a id="target-rd-0-controlled-weak-smooth-lifting"></a>

### Controlled lifting from a smooth weak completion

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/controlled-weak-smooth-lifting` · theorem

Let O be a complete DVR, S a smooth finitely presented O-algebra, and B,C weakly complete finitely generated O-algebras in the F1 sense. Given a surjection p:B→C, a map φ:S†→C, and a reduction map h̄:S/πS→B/πB with p̄h̄=φ̄, there exists h:S†→B reducing to h̄ and satisfying ph=φ. In particular every reduction map S/πS→B/πB lifts, by taking C=0. No uniqueness is asserted, and ordinary formal smoothness alone is insufficient for a nonnilpotent kernel.

**Hypotheses.**

- O may have either characteristic for this algebraic weak-lifting result. Rational de Rham integration below requires mixed characteristic.
- S† and the weakly complete algebra carriers are imported from F1.
- The general controlled étale-neighbourhood theorem and weak-completion invariance are the exact SF.0 and F1 requests here.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Foundations`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/weak-completion`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/weak-completion-universal-property`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/weak-completion-presentation`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1`, `mathlib:Algebra.Smooth`, `mathlib:Algebra.FormallySmooth.exists_lift`.

**Sources.**

- [S12](#source-12), Théorème 2.1.2(b), pp.625–632; Corollaire 2.1.3, pp.632–633; Proposition 3.2.5 and Théorème 3.3.2(b), pp.635–637. Controlled smooth lifting through an étale neighbourhood, then weak completion.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Restrict φ and h̄ to S. Apply the requested Arabia 2.1.2(b) controlled lifting theorem: a complete-intersection étale neighbourhood B→B_ε of (πB)·ker p has a genuine S-map satisfying both conditions.
2. This neighbourhood is canonically unchanged modulo π, because its defining neighbourhood ideal is contained in πB. It is flat and finitely presented over B. The requested F1 extension of weak completion identifies (B_ε)† with B and keeps the maps to C compatible.
3. Use F1 weak-completion functoriality to extend the S-map to S†. Check the two equations by their restrictions and reduction. The C=0 specialization is precisely the requested 2.1.3 reduction-lifting case.
4. For the parent semilinear Frobenius target, apply this linear result to the coefficient-twisted source over σ_O; then use the parent finiteness/flatness input. No assumption that σ_O is an automorphism is inserted.

**Checks.**

- For S=O[X], independently chosen compatible images of X give the required lift.
- For C=0 recover every reduction map; do not require B smooth over O.
- The construction must retain ph=φ exactly, not only modulo π.

<a id="target-rd-0-frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra"></a>

### Existence of Frobenius lifts on the weak completion of a smooth O_K-algebra (van der Put; Arabia)

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra` · theorem

Let O_K be a complete discrete valuation ring of characteristic 0 with uniformiser π and residue field k containing F_q, and σ_K a Frobenius lift on K (continuous, σ_K(O_K) ⊆ O_K, reducing to x ↦ x^q). Let S be a smooth finitely generated O_K-algebra and S† its weak completion (Monsky-Washnitzer; AdicSpacesPartII:F1), so that S†/πS† = S/πS =: S̄ is smooth over k. Then there is a ring endomorphism φ of S†, σ_K-semilinear over O_K, with φ(x) − x^q ∈ πS† for all x ∈ S†. It extends to a K-(semi)linear endomorphism of S† ⊗ K preserving S†, and its relative linearisation S† ⊗_{O_K,σ_K} O_K → S† (with weak completion of the tensor product) is finite flat. If σ_K is an automorphism, the semilinear ring map may also be viewed as finite flat. When k = F_q and σ_K = id (for instance K finite over Q_p with residue field F_q), φ is an O_K-algebra endomorphism with φ(x) − x^q ∈ πS†, i.e. AlgHom.IsArithFrobAt φ (πS†) holds. Lifts are not unique; two of them are homotopic (next node).

**Hypotheses.**

- S smooth and of finite type over O_K; S† is the Monsky-Washnitzer weak completion (the subring of the π-adic completion of elements Σ_j p_j(x_1, …, x_n) with p_j ∈ π^j O_K[X] of degree ≤ λ(j+1)).
- k need not be finite; for k ⊋ F_q the lift is σ_K-semilinear (a K-linear map S†^{σ_K} → S† lifting the relative Frobenius).

**Prerequisites.** `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-algebra`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/fringe-presentation`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/fringe-topology`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-differentials`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-tensor-product`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-rational-localisation`, `mathlib:AlgHom.IsArithFrobAt`, `mathlib:Algebra.Smooth`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/weak-completion`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/weak-completion-universal-property`, [Controlled lifting from a smooth weak completion](#target-rd-0-controlled-weak-smooth-lifting) (`RD.0/controlled-weak-smooth-lifting`).

**Sources.**

- [S12](#source-12), Théorème 3.3.2(b), pp. 636-637. The weak completion of a smooth lift is very smooth.
- [S12](#source-12), Théorème 3.3.4(a), p. 637. Lifting of morphisms out of a very smooth algebra, applied to the Frobenius of the reduction.
- [S7](#source-7), (2.4.4) Theorem (ii), p. 37. Van der Put's lifting theorem.
- [S4](#source-4), Definition 3.2.3, p. 21. The statement in Kedlaya's finiteness paper.
- [S6](#source-6), Section 3, p. 4. An explicit lift for hyperelliptic curves.

**Construction or proof.**

1. S† is a very smooth lift of S̄ in the category of weakly complete O_K-algebras: given a surjection B → C of weakly complete O_K-algebras, a map S† → C, and a compatible lifting of its reduction modulo the ideal of definition to B/πB, the map lifts to B (Arabia, Theorem 3.3.2(b), deduced from his Theorem 2.1.2(b); no Artin approximation is needed).
2. The q-power map on S̄ is a morphism of k-algebras S̄ ⊗_{k,σ} k → S̄ (for k = F_q, an F_q-algebra endomorphism of S̄). Base-changing S† along σ_K gives a very smooth weakly complete algebra S†^{σ_K} with reduction S̄ ⊗_{k,σ} k.
3. Arabia, Theorem 3.3.4(a): a morphism of reductions out of a very smooth algebra lifts; applied with target B = S† and C = S̄ this gives φ. (Alternatively van der Put, Theorem 2.4.4(ii), via the Artin approximation property of O_K⟨t⟩†.)
4. Finite flatness: the relative q-power Frobenius of the smooth k-scheme Spec S̄ is finite flat; lift the finite module and flatness statements to the weakly completed relative linearisation (Kedlaya, finiteness paper, Remark 3.2.4 and Lemma 2.2.3).
5. Explicit examples: S = O_K[x] with φ(x) = x^q; for a hyperelliptic curve y^2 = Q(x) with the points y = 0 and ∞ removed, Kedlaya's formula y^σ = y^p (1 + (Q(x)^σ − Q(x)^p)/Q(x)^p)^{1/2}.

**Checks.**

- S = O_K[x, x^{-1}]: φ(x) = x^q defines a lift, and φ(x) = x^q(1 + πx) does too; they differ.
- Coleman's use: for a good-reduction pair (X, D) over O_K with residue field F_q, the dagger algebra of the complement of D admits an O_K-linear lift of the q-power Frobenius (ColemanIntegration L1/frobenius-lift).
- The completion O_K⟨x⟩ also has Frobenius lifts, but its de Rham cohomology is wrong (completion-versus-overconvergence node); the theorem is about the weak completion.

<a id="target-rd-0-endpoint-preserving-weak-homotopy"></a>

### Lifting a reduction homotopy with fixed endpoints

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/endpoint-preserving-weak-homotopy` · theorem

Let O,S,B be as in controlled-weak-smooth-lifting. Given u_0,u_1:S†→B and a polynomial reduction homotopy h̄:S/πS→(B/πB)[T] with evaluations ū_0,ū_1, there is h:S†→B⟨T⟩† reducing to h̄ and evaluating exactly to u_0,u_1. Here B⟨T⟩† is the F1 weak polynomial extension, not B[[T]] or B⟨T⟩. If the reductions are equal, a constant reduction homotopy recovers the parent equal-reduction result; general homotopic reductions are the additional interface here.

**Hypotheses.**

- S is smooth finitely presented over the complete DVR O; B is weakly complete finitely generated.
- A polynomial homotopy of the reductions is part of the input; arbitrary reduction maps need not be homotopic.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Foundations`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Controlled lifting from a smooth weak completion](#target-rd-0-controlled-weak-smooth-lifting) (`RD.0/controlled-weak-smooth-lifting`), `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/weak-completion-universal-property`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/integral-overconvergent-tate-algebra`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1`, `mathlib:Polynomial.evalRingHom`, `mathlib:Polynomial.dvd_iff_isRoot`.

**Sources.**

- [S12](#source-12), Théorème 2.2.2, pp.633–634; Théorème 3.3.4(b), p.637. Endpoint-controlled lifting of polynomial reduction homotopies and its weak-completion application.
- [S46](#source-46), (2.4.4)(iii), pp.37–38. Endpoint preservation in the weak homotopy used for Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology.

**Construction or proof.**

1. On B[T], the joint endpoint map to B×B is surjective with kernel T(T−1). This follows from the coprimality of T and T−1 over every commutative ring; zero divisors in B do not invalidate it.
2. Apply the requested SF.0 controlled endpoint theorem (Arabia 2.2.2), whose étale-neighbourhood ideal is πT(T−1), keeping both endpoint maps and the reduction homotopy.
3. Pass to the weak polynomial extension using the requested F1 invariance. It is unchanged modulo π, and its endpoint maps are the F1 evaluations at 0 and 1. The resulting map therefore preserves both endpoints exactly.
4. For rational de Rham cohomology, compose h with rational-dagger-interval-integration; this gives the parent chain homotopy and identifies the induced cohomology maps.

**Checks.**

- Linear interpolation of algebra maps is not assumed multiplicative: with u_0(X)=0,u_1(X)=1, interpolate X and X² and check that T²≠T.
- For u_0=u_1 use the constant homotopy.
- If u_0≡u_1 modulo π, choose constant h̄ and verify both exact endpoints.

<a id="target-rd-0-rational-dagger-interval-integration"></a>

### Rational integration in a dagger interval

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.0/rational-dagger-interval-integration` · construction

Let O be a complete DVR of mixed characteristic (0,p), K its fraction field, and B a weakly complete finitely generated O-algebra. On the rational dagger de Rham complex of B⟨T⟩†[1/π], write forms with dT on the left as α(T)+dT∧β(T). Define the degree −1 K-linear operator H by integrating β(T) coefficientwise from 0 to 1; H(Σ_n b_n T^n dT)=Σ_n b_n/(n+1). It lands in the de Rham complex of B[1/π] and satisfies dH+Hd=ev_1−ev_0. For any fringe radius R>1 in T and the coefficient variables, choose a strictly smaller radius R′>1: integer denominators grow at most polynomially, so integration remains overconvergent on this smaller fringe. This is rational integration, not an O-linear integral-valued operator.

**Hypotheses.**

- Use F1 dagger differentials and dagger de Rham complex on the rational generic fibre; a chosen finite weak presentation supplies the coefficient fringe.
- For integers n≥1, |n⁻¹|≤n^c where c=−log_p|p|>0; this follows from |n|=|p|^{v_p(n)}.
- Shrink the joint fringe when needed; do not demand bounded integration on the same fringe.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Foundations`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/integral-overconvergent-tate-algebra`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/weak-completion-presentation`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-differentials`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-de-rham-complex`, [Lifting a reduction homotopy with fixed endpoints](#target-rd-0-endpoint-preserving-weak-homotopy) (`RD.0/endpoint-preserving-weak-homotopy`).

**Sources.**

- [S46](#source-46), (2.4.4)(iii), pp.37–38. Coefficientwise integration defines the rational de Rham homotopy.
- [S12](#source-12), §3.4, pp.638–639, concluding MW homotopy statement. The algebraic homotopy induces equality on rational Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- Parent frobenius-lifts-induce-homotopic-maps: Turn the endpoint-preserving weak homotopy into an explicit rational chain homotopy.
- RD.3 Monsky–Washnitzer realization: Independence of a chosen smooth lift and its Frobenius action.

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DaggerInterval.integrate` |  | Degree −1 K-linear map to the base de Rham complex, given by the dT component. |
| `DaggerInterval.integrate_monomial` |  | For a base form ω, H(dT∧T^nω)=ω/(n+1). |
| `DaggerInterval.integrate_no_dT` |  | H(α(T))=0 when the form has no dT component. |
| `DaggerInterval.integrate_fringe_bound` |  | For 1<R′<R, the factor (R′/R)^n\|n+1\|⁻¹ is bounded and tends to zero; the integration map is bounded after the corresponding fringe shrink. |
| `DaggerInterval.chain_homotopy` |  | dH+Hd=ev_1−ev_0 with the specified exterior-order convention. |
