- F is a perfect complete nontrivially valued characteristic-p field; q is a power of p; σ raises residue coefficients to q-th powers and fixes π.
- E† is the bounded overconvergent Teichmüller coefficient field and E its π-adic completion, in the Fargues–Fontaine §11.2.5 convention; the coefficient-ring identification is requested from RD.0.
- Frobenius modules have invertible linearisation; this does not imply Frobenius is bijective on an arbitrary integral lattice.
- Both source and target are isoclinic of the same λ; essential surjectivity adds algebraic closedness.

**Prerequisites.** [Bijective integral-lattice invariant descent](#target-rd-1-bijective-lattice-invariants) (`RD.1/bijective-lattice-invariants`), [Calculus of slopes: direct sums, tensor products, exterior powers, restriction of Frobenius, twists, Hom vanishing](#target-rd-1-calculus-of-slopes) (`RD.1/calculus-of-slopes`), [F-stable lattices: nonnegative generic slopes versus integral models](#target-rd-1-frobenius-stable-lattices) (`RD.1/frobenius-stable-lattices`), [Standard σ-modules M_{c,d} and their tensor products, twists, duals, H^0, H^1, Hom and Ext](#target-rd-1-standard-frobenius-modules) (`RD.1/standard-frobenius-modules`), [Dieudonné-Manin classification over a complete discretely valued field with algebraically closed residue field](#target-rd-1-dieudonne-manin-classical) (`RD.1/dieudonne-manin-classical`).

**Sources.**

- [S39](#source-39), Proposition 6.3.2, Theorem 6.3.3(a) and Remark 6.3.4, preprint pp. 64–65. The H⁰ comparison applies to unit-root modules, hence to Homs between pure modules of one slope; Remark 6.3.4 shows that completion is not essentially surjective in general (its example has the imperfect K=k((t))), so for general perfect F only full faithfulness is claimed.

**Construction or proof.**

1. The internal Hom has slope zero by the imported slope calculus. Twist/iterate to a unit-root lattice and apply the H⁰ comparison of SFR Proposition 6.3.2 or the bijective-lattice invariant estimate.
2. Over algebraically closed F classify the completed object into standard blocks. Each block is already defined over E†, giving essential surjectivity.
3. SFR Remark 6.3.4 shows that essential surjectivity fails in general; it is asserted here only for algebraically closed F. Mixed-slope Homs do not reduce to unit root.

**Checks.**

- Test λ=0 by ordinary fixed vectors.
- Do not export an all-slope completion equivalence or a general-perfect-field equivalence.

<a id="target-rd-1-descending-generic-filtration"></a>

### Descending bounded generic slope filtration

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/descending-generic-filtration` · theorem

Every finite-dimensional Frobenius module M over E† has a unique filtration by saturated Frobenius submodules whose completed graded pieces are isoclinic of strictly decreasing arithmetic slopes. The filtration completes to the decreasing generic slope filtration over E. If F is algebraically closed, every graded piece is a direct sum of standard E† blocks of its one slope; M itself need not be their direct sum.

**Hypotheses.**

- F is a perfect complete nontrivially valued characteristic-p field; q is a power of p; σ raises residue coefficients to q-th powers and fixes π.
- E† is the bounded overconvergent Teichmüller coefficient field and E its π-adic completion, in the Fargues–Fontaine §11.2.5 convention; the coefficient-ring identification is requested from RD.0.
- Frobenius modules have invertible linearisation; this does not imply Frobenius is bijective on an arbitrary integral lattice.
- The argument is Kedlaya's, proved in the monodromy paper for a perfect algebraic extension of k((t)) (a 'valued field' there, §2.2, p. 102); for FF's complete perfect F the Galois-descent step uses FF Proposition 11.2.15 and the extended-ring step is SFR Proposition 5.4.3 (any K). This extension of Kedlaya's setting is part of the coefficient-ring comparison G3.

**Prerequisites.** [Descent of a saturated subobject through its determinant line](#target-rd-1-saturated-subobject-descent-via-exterior-power) (`RD.1/saturated-subobject-descent-via-exterior-power`), [Dieudonné-Manin classification over a complete discretely valued field with algebraically closed residue field](#target-rd-1-dieudonne-manin-classical) (`RD.1/dieudonne-manin-classical`), [A function converging only on the closed unit disc separates completion from overconvergence](#target-rd-0-completion-versus-overconvergence) (`RD.0/completion-versus-overconvergence`), [Isoclinic completion comparison](#target-rd-1-isoclinic-completion-comparison) (`RD.1/isoclinic-completion-comparison`).

**Sources.**

- [S14](#source-14), Proposition 5.11 and proof, pp. 164–165; §2.2, p. 102; arXiv v4 pp. 66–67. Kedlaya descends the highest generic slope first, giving decreasing bounded slopes, for a perfect algebraic extension of k((t)); the printed proof has the slips E308 and E309.
- [S27](#source-27), Proposition 11.2.24 p. 378, with accepted main source issues E218/E219. The corrected statement is filtration descent and fixed-slope comparison, not equivalence on all objects.
- [S39](#source-39), Lemma 5.4.1, Definition 5.4.2 and Proposition 5.4.3, preprint pp. 57–58. Kedlaya's later version: the reverse filtration descends from Γ^alg[π⁻¹] to Γ^alg_con[π⁻¹] for any K, by descending slope-zero eigenvectors.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Take the highest completed slope submodule. Its determinant is a rank-one Frobenius line in an exterior power.
2. In rank one choose λ with the highest slope and a completed eigenbasis vᵢ. Approximate it by bounded overconvergent wᵢ so λwᵢ=ΣⱼBᵢⱼF(wⱼ), with B mod π=diag(1,0,…,0). For v₁=Σcᵢwᵢ use σ(cᵢ)=ΣⱼBⱼᵢcⱼ. Choose r with w_r(B)≥0; induction in the π-index gives rv_h(cᵢ)+h≥0. At h=0 the coordinates reduce to δᵢ₁, not all to zero. Thus the determinant line has overconvergent coordinates. Apply the imported saturated exterior-power descent and the RD.0 intersection statement to descend from the algebraic extension.
3. Pass to the quotient and induct on rank. Completed uniqueness and injectivity give uniqueness over E†. For the graded standard forms when F is algebraically closed, apply the fixed-slope completion comparison (isoclinic-completion-comparison) to each isoclinic graded piece; the source instead repeats the eigenvector descent on each piece and applies its Proposition 5.3. Full faithfulness on mixed slopes is never used.

**Checks.**

- For slopes 0,1 the first submodule has slope 1.
- A nonsplit bounded extension can split after completion; no unconditional E† direct-sum conclusion.

<a id="target-rd-1-negative-frobenius-cokernel"></a>

### Negative-slope Frobenius cokernel comparison

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/negative-frobenius-cokernel` · comparison

For d>0 and h≥1 the additive map 1−π^(−d)σ^h:E†→E† is surjective. A solution to (1−π^(−d)σ^h)y=x is y=−Σₘ≥1 π^(dm)σ^(−hm)(x); the same formula is valid on the completion and is compatible with inclusion.

**Hypotheses.**

- F is a perfect complete nontrivially valued characteristic-p field; q is a power of p; σ raises residue coefficients to q-th powers and fixes π.
- E† is the bounded overconvergent Teichmüller coefficient field and E its π-adic completion, in the Fargues–Fontaine §11.2.5 convention; the coefficient-ring identification is requested from RD.0.
- Frobenius modules have invertible linearisation; this does not imply Frobenius is bijective on an arbitrary integral lattice.
- σ is invertible; d,h integers with the stated strict signs.

**Prerequisites.** [H^0 and H^1 of the twists Γ_an,con(n) and Γ_con[π^{-1}](n)](#target-rd-1-cohomology-of-rank-one-frobenius-modules) (`RD.1/cohomology-of-rank-one-frobenius-modules`), [Numerical membership criterion, intersections and Mayer-Vietoris splitting for Γ_I](#target-rd-0-analytic-ring-membership-and-intersections) (`RD.0/analytic-ring-membership-and-intersections`).

**Sources.**

- [S39](#source-39), Proposition 3.3.7(c), preprint pp. 34–35, n<0 with σ replaced by σ^h. SFR 3.3.7(c) gives H¹=0 for negative n over Γ_con[π⁻¹] (here with σ replaced by σ^h). Its proof splits x into two parts with backward and forward series; for x∈Γ_con[π⁻¹] the forward part is zero and the solution is the backward series used here (p. 36). The published erratum replaces the Teichmüller presentations in this proof by strong semiunit presentations; the bounded case needs only partial valuations of Witt-vector expansions.
- [S51](#source-51), p. 361. The proof of SFR Proposition 3.3.7(c) is repaired with strong semiunit presentations; the statement is unchanged.
- [S27](#source-27), Proposition 11.2.24, proof, p. 378. FF reduce Ext¹(E†(μ),E†(λ))=0 for λ>μ to the vanishing of the cokernel of Id−π^(−d)φ^h on E† for d>0, h≥1.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Backward Frobenius reduces residue-coefficient growth by q^(−hm), while π^(dm) gives a linearly increasing integral valuation. This produces one positive convergence radius for the tail: if r·v_k(x)+k≥C for all k, then each term π^(dm)σ^(−hm)(x) satisfies the same bound with C+dm in place of C.
2. Telescope finite partial sums; their remaining error tends to zero in the analytic and π-adic topologies.
3. This is the FF coefficient/iterate transport of the imported negative-slope rank-one cohomology, not a new claim of Ext vanishing in both slope directions.

**Checks.**

- Verify the sign with x=1: y=−π^d/(1−π^d).
- The map is additive and linear over σ^h-fixed constants; it is not E†-linear.

<a id="target-rd-1-frobenius-germ-extension"></a>

### Frobenius germ and punctured-disc comparison

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/frobenius-germ-extension` · comparison

For the FF analytic coefficient ring R_F=colim_(ρ→0) B_(0,ρ], restriction and Frobenius gluing identify finite projective Frobenius modules with compatible Frobenius bundles on the punctured analytic radius domain. In equal characteristic E=F_q((π)), the coefficient Frobenius fixes π; comparison with Hartl–Pink uses π as their z and coefficientwise q-power σ.

**Hypotheses.**

- F is algebraically closed complete nontrivially valued of characteristic p; coefficient field E is either FF mixed characteristic or F_q((π)).
- The Banach charts, their overlap restrictions and φ-rescaling maps must be supplied by RD.0; equal-characteristic coefficients are Laurent series in π with coefficients in F.

**Prerequisites.** [The Robba ring R_K is Kedlaya's analytic ring Γ^{k((t))}_an,con: naive and true partial valuations agree](#target-rd-0-robba-ring) (`RD.0/robba-ring`), [The extended Robba ring R^alg = Γ^alg_an,con over the completed algebraic closure of k((t))](#target-rd-0-extended-robba-ring) (`RD.0/extended-robba-ring`), [Numerical membership criterion, intersections and Mayer-Vietoris splitting for Γ_I](#target-rd-0-analytic-ring-membership-and-intersections) (`RD.0/analytic-ring-membership-and-intersections`).

**Sources.**

- [S27](#source-27), §11.2.5: Proposition 11.2.20, p. 377, and Corollaire 11.2.22, p. 378; Remarque 11.3.4, p. 382. Restriction to one annulus Y_I with φ(I)∩I≠∅ plus a gluing isomorphism is equivalent to a φ-bundle on Y (11.2.20), and such bundles are free φ-modules of finite rank over R (11.2.22); the slope classification is separate.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Spread a finitely presented module and Frobenius isomorphism to one small annular chart.
2. Translate that chart by Frobenius powers, glue across intersections using the isomorphism and its cocycle, and restrict back to recover the germ.
3. Match the FF norms and HP Laurent convergence conditions chartwise. This match and the mixed-characteristic extension are G3; a mere coincidence of symbols R is not a ring identification.

**Checks.**

- In equal characteristic σ(π)=π, whereas σ acts nontrivially on F coefficients.
- Do not identify R_F with an ordinary Robba ring having t↦t^q without an explicit comparison.

<a id="target-rd-1-equalchar-degree-zero-section-input"></a>

### Equal-characteristic extension section theorem

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/equalchar-degree-zero-section-input` · theorem

Over the Hartl–Pink punctured-disc ring, for every r≥1 and every σ-bundle extension 0→O(−1)→G→F_(1,r)→0 there is a nonzero Frobenius-fixed section of G.

**Hypotheses.**

- F is complete algebraically closed characteristic p with nontrivial norm; σ is coefficientwise q-power, fixes the Laurent variable z.
- HP F_(d,r) has σ^r=z^(−d), geometric degree d and arithmetic slope −d/r.

**Prerequisites.** [Puiseux Newton-polygon root criterion](#target-rd-1-puiseux-root-input) (`RD.1/puiseux-root-input`), [Standard σ-modules M_{c,d} and their tensor products, twists, duals, H^0, H^1, Hom and Ext](#target-rd-1-standard-frobenius-modules) (`RD.1/standard-frobenius-modules`), [H^0 and H^1 of the twists Γ_an,con(n) and Γ_con[π^{-1}](n)](#target-rd-1-cohomology-of-rank-one-frobenius-modules) (`RD.1/cohomology-of-rank-one-frobenius-modules`).

**Sources.**

- [S52](#source-52), Proposition 9.1, p. 705; Lemmas 9.3–9.4 and the reduction to Proposition 9.5, pp. 706–708; §10.1–Lemma 10.17, pp. 708–713. The public analytic key calculation is independent of the classification it proves.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Write the extension matrix [[z,b],[0,A_(1,r)]]. A section of the quotient has coordinates v_t=Σᵢ∈ℤz^(−i)w^(q^(ir−t)) for 0<|w|<1; the first coordinate u must solve u=zσ(u)+bσ(v).
2. Its forced coefficients are u_i=Σⱼ≥0 f_(i−j)^(q^j). The negative-power tail always converges; the positive tail is controlled by a fractional q-polynomial condition (HP Lemmas 9.3–9.4).
3. Reduce to HP Proposition 9.5. Discard residue-norm ≤1 coefficients and shift so m=Σ_l m_l z^l has only positive exponents, with log|m_l|≤cl. For n=r+1 form F_i(w)=Σ_(0<j<ni)F_(i,j)w^(q^(−j)), where F_(i,j)=Σ_(j/n<k≤i)m_(nk−j)^(q^(−k)). Their logarithmic profiles φ_(i,j)=log|F_(i,j)| satisfy φ_(i+l,j+nl)=q^(−l)φ_(i,j); the actual coefficient differences satisfy log|F_(i′,j)−F_(i,j)|≤cn i q^(−i) for i′≥i≥2.
4. If every limiting φ_j≤0, any sufficiently small nonzero w works. Otherwise choose a corner ρ≥cn of max_j(φ_j−q^(−j)ρ), with positive maximum at two j. Newton polygons yield roots w_i of norm exp(−ρ).
5. Use the ball-image criterion for additive fractional q-polynomials to choose compatible roots with log|w_(i+1)−w_i|≤−c′q^((n−1)i/2). Their limit w retains nonzero norm; splitting j at ni/2 gives limsup log|F_i(w)|≤0 and the required positive-tail convergence.

**Checks.**

- Do not cite HP Theorem 4.3 as input: the source derives it from classification. Use Theorem 4.1 for global generation.
- Maintain the logarithm in the root-difference estimate; a negative upper bound on an absolute value is impossible.

<a id="target-rd-1-equal-characteristic-classification"></a>

### Equal-characteristic Frobenius classification

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/equal-characteristic-classification` · theorem

For algebraically closed perfectoid F and E=F_q((π)), every finite projective Frobenius module over R_F is a direct sum of standard blocks with coprime integer pair (c,r), r>0, satisfying φ^r=π^c. The multiset of pairs is unique, and its arithmetic slope is c/r. With c=−d these are the Hartl–Pink blocks F_(d,r). Together with the imported mixed-characteristic classification, this covers the two coefficient characteristics in FF Remark 11.3.4, subject to the explicit ring comparison G3.

**Hypotheses.**

- The precise coefficient category is the one in frobenius-germ-extension, not a completion-only bounded category.
- Do not assume finite projective underlying modules on a nonspherically complete punctured disc are free before σ-bundle classification.

**Prerequisites.** [Frobenius germ and punctured-disc comparison](#target-rd-1-frobenius-germ-extension) (`RD.1/frobenius-germ-extension`), [Equal-characteristic extension section theorem](#target-rd-1-equalchar-degree-zero-section-input) (`RD.1/equalchar-degree-zero-section-input`), [Standard σ-modules M_{c,d} and their tensor products, twists, duals, H^0, H^1, Hom and Ext](#target-rd-1-standard-frobenius-modules) (`RD.1/standard-frobenius-modules`), [Semistable and stable σ-modules, HN filtrations, HN polygons and descent of subobjects](#target-rd-1-semistability-and-harder-narasimhan-filtration) (`RD.1/semistability-and-harder-narasimhan-filtration`), [Newton polygons of extensions; splitting criteria over R^alg](#target-rd-1-splitting-of-exact-sequences-by-polygons) (`RD.1/splitting-of-exact-sequences-by-polygons`), [Dieudonné-Manin decomposition of σ-modules over the extended Robba ring R^alg (Kedlaya)](#target-rd-1-dieudonne-manin-over-extended-robba-ring) (`RD.1/dieudonne-manin-over-extended-robba-ring`).

**Sources.**

- [S52](#source-52), Theorem 11.1, Lemmas 11.2–11.4, pp. 713–714; Corollary 11.8 p. 715; §8 pp. 703–705. The classification adds equal-characteristic coefficients without rebuilding the already planned standard-block notion.
- [S27](#source-27), Théorème 11.3.2 and the paragraph after it, pp. 381–382; Remarque 11.3.4, p. 382. Remarque 11.3.4 says that classifying φ-modules over R_F cannot avoid Théorème 11.3.2; FF's coefficient field is a local field of either characteristic, and for E=F_q((π)) the book attributes 11.3.2 to Hartl–Pink Theorem 4.3, which HP derive from their classification.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Use HP Theorem 4.1 to find a line subbundle of maximal degree; saturation and the degree bound make its quotient a σ-bundle. Rank-one classification and slope-ordered splitting are the imported standard/HN inputs transported to this coefficient category (G3).
2. Induct simultaneously: every degree-zero bundle has a section; every bundle splits into standard blocks; every nonnegative-degree bundle has a section. The nonsplit degree-zero obstruction is equalchar-degree-zero-section-input.
3. For rank r and degree d, pull back under [r] and twist by −d to obtain degree zero. A section yields a map from [r]_*O(d). If full rank, use saturation/degree and gcd(d,r); otherwise split off a standard summand by the slope inequality and induct.
4. HP Corollary 11.8 gives uniqueness. Transport through the germ comparison, preserving the sign c=−d and arithmetic slope convention.

**Checks.**

- F_(1,r) has arithmetic slope −1/r, not +1/r.
- Direct-sum classification here does not imply direct-sum classification over bounded E†.

<a id="target-rd-1-reverse-algebraic-filtration-comparison"></a>

### de Jong reverse slope filtration

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/reverse-algebraic-filtration-comparison` · comparison

For M† over E†_alg, write the completed increasing slope filtration 0=S₀⊂S₁⊂…⊂Sₘ=M. There is a unique reverse filtration 0=Srev₀⊂…⊂Srevₘ=M† whose i-th graded piece completes to S_(m+1−i)/S_(m−i), for 1≤i≤m. If M† is isoclinic of slope s/r then, after possibly replacing (s,r) by (ks,kr) for a positive integer k, M†[p^(1/r)] has a Frobenius eigenbasis with eigenvalue p^(s/r); this applies to each isoclinic grade.

**Hypotheses.**

- E†_alg is the fraction field of the subring of W(k(t)^alg) of Teichmüller series Σ[fᵢ]pⁱ whose t-adic valuations v(fᵢ) are bounded below by a linear function of i (D'Addezio Definition 4.2.5); k is perfect, the residue field k(t)^alg is algebraically closed but not complete, and E_alg is the p-adic completion. Slope indices begin at 0.
- s∈ℤ, r>0; negative s is allowed; the coefficient extension and Frobenius lift fix the chosen scalar eigenvalue.

**Prerequisites.** [Descending bounded generic slope filtration](#target-rd-1-descending-generic-filtration) (`RD.1/descending-generic-filtration`), [Isoclinic completion comparison](#target-rd-1-isoclinic-completion-comparison) (`RD.1/isoclinic-completion-comparison`), [Dieudonné-Manin classification over a complete discretely valued field with algebraically closed residue field](#target-rd-1-dieudonne-manin-classical) (`RD.1/dieudonne-manin-classical`).

**Sources.**

- [S28](#source-28), Definition 4.2.5 and Theorem 4.2.6 with proof, pp. 14–15; Lemma 4.2.7 proof, p. 15. De Jong's reverse filtration and eigenbasis over E†_alg, with the quotient-index correction of E303; the proof of Lemma 4.2.7 confirms that the first reverse step carries the maximal slope.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Apply the descending generic filtration over the completed extended ring (SFR Proposition 5.4.3, as in descending-generic-filtration) and intersect back to E†_alg using O_(E^alg)[p^(1/b)]∩Γ_(2,b,c)=O†_(E^alg)[p^(1/b)] (D'Addezio, proof of Theorem 4.2.6, p. 15); this ring comparison is part of G3. Compare its graded completions with the ascending filtration in reverse order.
2. Uniqueness identifies the grade as S_(m+1−i)/S_(m−i). The printed shifted indices in D’Addezio are corrected; at i=m the quotient is S₁/S₀.
3. For one isoclinic grade apply classical standard-block classification and fixed-slope full faithfulness after the finite scalar extension to transport the Frobenius eigenbasis.

**Checks.**

- For m=2 the grades complete to S₂/S₁ and S₁/S₀.
- This RD.1 ownership replaces the stray VB0 target; no VB0 dependency.

<a id="target-rd-1-residue-duality-pairing"></a>

### Robba kernel–cokernel residue pairing

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/residue-duality-pairing` · definition

For a finite free differential Robba module M over L with coordinate T and connection operator ∂ for δ=(1+T)d/dT, define H¹_∂(M)=coker ∂ and H⁰_∂(M∨)=ker ∂∨. The pairing sends ([m],ℓ) to Res_T(⟨m,ℓ⟩ dT/(1+T)). For δ=d/dT the one-form is dT instead. The dual connection is determined by δ⟨m,ℓ⟩=⟨∂m,ℓ⟩+⟨m,∂∨ℓ⟩.

**Hypotheses.**

- L is a complete characteristic-zero nonarchimedean coefficient field; the Robba derivative has zero residue on exact one-forms.
- For the Dospinescu–Le Bras convention ∇=t(1+T)d/dT on coefficients and ∂=t⁻¹∇, t=log(1+T).
- The dual is the differential-module dual. For N_rig(V̌), V̌=V*⊗χ_cyc, choose the horizontal generator t⁻¹e_χ of N_rig(L(1)) to identify it with this dual.

**Prerequisites.** [Differential (∇-)modules over annuli, the Robba ring and differential fields](#target-rd-1-differential-module) (`RD.1/differential-module`), [(σ,∇)-modules (φ,∇)-modules over R, R^bd, R^int, E and dagger algebras; Frobenius structures](#target-rd-1-frobenius-differential-module) (`RD.1/frobenius-differential-module`), [The derivation d/dt on annulus rings, R, R^bd, R^int, O_E and E, its norm bounds and Ω^1 = R dt](#target-rd-0-derivation-on-robba-ring) (`RD.0/derivation-on-robba-ring`), [The Robba ring R_K is Kedlaya's analytic ring Γ^{k((t))}_an,con: naive and true partial valuations agree](#target-rd-0-robba-ring) (`RD.0/robba-ring`).

**Sources.**

- [S29](#source-29), §§6.1–6.4, printed pp. 355–357; Proposition 6.4 proof p. 357. The derivative and cyclotomic-dual conventions explain which residue pairing the cokernel argument uses.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- Dospinescu–Le Bras Proposition 6.4: Convert vanishing of horizontal sections of N_rig(V̌) into surjectivity of ∂ on N_rig(V).
- RD.1 Robba duality target: Identify the finite-dimensional cokernel with the dual of the horizontal kernel.

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `robbaResiduePairing` |  | For a finite free differential Robba module M over L with coordinate T and connection operator ∂ for δ=(1+T)d/dT, define H¹_∂(M)=coker ∂ and H⁰_∂(M∨)=ker ∂∨. The pairing sends ([m],ℓ) to Res_T(⟨m,ℓ⟩ dT/(1+T)). For δ=d/dT the one-form is dT instead. The dual connection is determined by δ⟨m,ℓ⟩=⟨∂m,ℓ⟩+⟨m,∂∨ℓ⟩. |
| `dualConnection_leibniz` |  | δ of the evaluation pairing is the sum of the two connection evaluations. |
| `residue_exact` |  | The residue of dg is zero for every convergent Robba Laurent series g. |
| `residuePairing_representative` |  | Evaluation on a quotient class equals the chosen representative formula. |
| `residuePairing_bilinear` |  | The descended pairing is L-bilinear. |
| `residuePairing_coordinate` |  | Under an analytic invertible parameter change, the one-form residue and pairing agree. |
| `residuePairing_tate_generator` |  | Using t⁻¹e_χ identifies the Cartier differential dual with M∨ for the DLB ∂ convention. |

**Unit tests.**

- `trivial_dT` (computation): For the trivial module and δ=d/dT, pairing [T⁻¹] with 1 is 1.
- `exact` (degenerate): For any m and horizontal ℓ, pairing [∂m] with ℓ is zero.
- `cyclotomic_form` (computation): For the trivial δ=(1+T)d/dT line, pairing [(1+T)/T] with 1 is 1.
- `wrong_form` (non-example): For g=T⁻², Res(g dT)=0 but Res(g dT/(1+T))=−1; using dT for δ=(1+T)d/dT is wrong.
- `integer_residue_line` (compatibility): For ∂=d/dT+a/T with a∈ℤ, the horizontal dual section T^a pairs [T^(−a−1)] to 1.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Use the imported Robba Laurent coefficient and derivative to define residue as the coefficient of T⁻¹ in the one-form coefficient.
2. For horizontal ℓ the value on ∂m is the residue of δ⟨m,ℓ⟩ dT/(1+T)=d⟨m,ℓ⟩, hence zero. Descend to the additive/L-linear cokernel.
3. Export the pairing of quotient classes; changes of coordinate act on the differential form, not just on the scalar coefficient. The cyclotomic twist is fixed by the horizontal generator, without an extra claim of φ/Γ-equivariance.

**Checks.**

- The scalar residue for ∂=(1+T)d/dT is the coefficient of T⁻¹ in g/(1+T), not in g.
- Well-definedness follows from integration by parts and horizontality, independently of perfectness.

<a id="target-rd-1-christol-mebkhout-local-index"></a>

### Christol–Mebkhout local index theorems on the Robba ring

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/christol-mebkhout-local-index` · theorem

Let K be complete for a discrete valuation, of characteristic 0, with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, let R be the Robba ring over K in the variable x (germs at the boundary |x| = 1 of analytic functions on annuli 1 − ε < |x| < 1), A the ring of analytic functions on the open unit disc and, for small ε, A(I_ε) = A ⊕ H_ε the functions on the annulus I_ε = ]1 − ε, 1[ split into the parts with nonnegative and negative powers of x. Let M be a finite free differential module over R that is solvable at the boundary (generic radius tending to 1) and whose exponent is non-Liouville in the sense of Christol–Mebkhout (Définitions 10.2–10.9, 13.1). Write the derivation on a basis of a model M_ε over A(I_ε) as D − G. Then: (a) for ε small enough the operator x(D − G) has a generalized index (Robba's notion: the composite of the operator with the projection to the A-part, resp. the H_ε-part, has finite-dimensional kernel and cokernel) and χ(M, A) = −χ(M, H_ε) equals the height of the differential Newton polygon of M, i.e. the irregularity Irr(M), which is the differential Swan conductor of RD.1/differential-swan-conductor; (b) ∇ acting on M itself has finite-dimensional kernel and cokernel, and χ(M, R) := dim ker ∇ − dim coker ∇ = 0. Every solvable module with a Frobenius structure has non-Liouville exponent, so (a) and (b) hold for every (σ, ∇)-module over R.

**Hypotheses.**

- K complete discretely valued of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field of characteristic p.
- M finite free over R, solvable at the boundary, with non-Liouville exponent (automatic in the presence of a Frobenius structure).
- Indices in (a) are generalized indices in the sense of Christol–Mebkhout Définition 14.1; in (b) the index is the ordinary one on R.

**Prerequisites.** [Break multiset and differential Swan conductor of a solvable ∇-module](#target-rd-1-differential-swan-conductor) (`RD.1/differential-swan-conductor`), [Break decomposition of a solvable ∇-module near the boundary (Christol-Mebkhout)](#target-rd-1-break-decomposition) (`RD.1/break-decomposition`), [∇-modules solvable at the boundary (overconvergent, 'soluble en 1')](#target-rd-1-solvable-at-boundary) (`RD.1/solvable-at-boundary`), [A Frobenius structure forces generic radius 1 at the boundary (Dwork; Christol-Mebkhout)](#target-rd-1-frobenius-structure-forces-solvability) (`RD.1/frobenius-structure-forces-solvability`), [Highest break b(E) of a solvable ∇-module (differential irregularity)](#target-rd-1-highest-break) (`RD.1/highest-break`).

**Sources.**

- [S84](#source-84), Définition 14.1, Proposition 14.6, Proposition 14.10, pp. 170-172. Robba's generalized index of an operator on the annulus split into its disc and outer parts, its additivity and its relation with the ordinary index on the annulus.
- [S84](#source-84), Théorème 14.11, p. 172. A solvable module with non-Liouville exponent has a generalized index on the disc part and on the outer part; the two are opposite and equal the height of the Newton polygon of the module.
- [S84](#source-84), Théorème 14.13, p. 173. Such a module has an index on the Robba ring, equal to 0.
- [S84](#source-84), Introduction to Chapter I and Corollaire 11.9, pp. 126-127 and 165. A slope-zero module with Frobenius structure is quasi-unipotent with rational exponents, hence non-Liouville.
- [S91](#source-91), Corollary 2.4.3 and (2.98), p. 39. The de Rham cohomology over the Robba ring is the colimit of that over thin annuli at the boundary germ, finite when the annulus indices stabilise; used as a public cross-check of (b).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Additivity: generalized indices add in short exact sequences of solvable modules (CM Proposition 14.10), so it suffices to treat the graded pieces of the slope (break) decomposition (CM Théorème 9.10 and Corollaire 9.20; RD.1/break-decomposition).
2. Slope-zero pieces: by CM Théorème 12.1 an irreducible solvable module of slope 0 with non-Liouville exponent is x^a·R with a non-Liouville; the index is computed directly and is 0 on A, on H_ε and on R.
3. Pieces of slope λ > 0: take a Frobenius antecedent near ρ < 1 with radius below |π|ρ (CM Théorème 7.5, the transfer of RD.1), use the cyclic vector theorem (CM Théorème 6.2) and invariance of the index under small perturbation (CM Théorème 14.3, c-compact perturbation of operators between LF spaces) to reduce to multiplication by a nonzero analytic function on an annulus, whose generalized index counts its zeros (CM Proposition 14.8); pass to the limit ρ → 1 by Mittag-Leffler. The result is λ times the rank, i.e. the height of the slope-λ side of the Newton polygon.
4. (b) is (a) for both halves: χ on A(I_ε) is the sum of the generalized indices on A and H_ε (CM Proposition 14.6), which cancel; independence of ε gives the index on R (CM Théorème 14.13, compare Poineau–Pulita V Corollary 2.4.3 for the colimit over annuli).
5. Frobenius structure ⇒ hypotheses: solvability is RD.1/frobenius-structure-forces-solvability; the slope-zero part of a module with Frobenius structure is quasi-unipotent and its exponent lies in Z_p ∩ Q, which is non-Liouville (CM Corollaire 11.9 and its introduction, p. 127).

**Checks.**

- The Dwork module ∇e = πe dx at ∞ (coordinate t = 1/x): Irr = 1, so the generalized index on the disc part is 1 while H^0 and H^1 over R both vanish (compare Kedlaya Weil II Proposition 4.4.5, where H^0_loc = H^1_loc = 0 for such twists).
- The trivial module R: H^0 = K and H^1 = K·dx/x, index 0, Irr = 0.
- Kummer module x^a·R with a ∈ (q − 1)^{-1}Z − Z: H^0 = H^1 = 0 over R.

<a id="rd2"></a>

## RD.2 — Local monodromy and ramification

Prove Tsuzuki’s theorem through Lang trivialization and the sharp small-matrix estimate. Combine slope descent, finite étale extension and logarithmic solutions to obtain local monodromy. Quasi-constant modules and Matsuda decomposition supply the monodromy representation category, local differential/ramification break comparisons and the quasi-unipotent residue calculation. André’s local group uses these coefficient categories. The general finite-cover duality comparison retains its analytic descent obligation.

**Landmarks.** Isoclinic descent, Slope filtration theorem, Unipotent differential module, Tsuzuki's unit-root monodromy theorem, p-adic local monodromy theorem, Logarithmic form of the local monodromy theorem.

<a id="target-rd-2-finitely-presented-differential-module-is-free"></a>

### A finitely presented module with connection over the Robba ring is free

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/finitely-presented-differential-module-is-free` · lemma

Let M be a finitely presented R_K-module with a connection ∇ : M → M ⊗ Ω^1_{R_K} (Leibniz rule for d/dt). Then M is free of finite rank. The same holds over R^L = Γ^L_an,con for L/k((t)) finite separable.

**Hypotheses.**

- K of characteristic 0 (used to divide by the order of vanishing).

**Prerequisites.** [Finite modules over Bézout domains: unimodular rows, saturated spans, freeness, Galois descent of saturated submodules](#target-rd-0-modules-over-bezout-domains) (`RD.0/modules-over-bezout-domains`), [Γ_r and Γ_I for closed I are principal ideal domains (Lazard)](#target-rd-0-closed-interval-analytic-ring-pid) (`RD.0/closed-interval-analytic-ring-pid`), [The Robba ring R_K is Kedlaya's analytic ring Γ^{k((t))}_an,con: naive and true partial valuations agree](#target-rd-0-robba-ring) (`RD.0/robba-ring`).

**Sources.**

- [S19](#source-19), Proposition 6.1, p. 735. Statement (A the Robba ring; the OCR renders ∇ as V).
- [S17](#source-17), §3.4, p. 10. André records the same fact for finitely presented differential modules.

**Construction or proof.**

1. By RD.0/modules-over-bezout-domains (b) (finite torsion-free modules are free, so M ≅ T ⊕ M/T) it suffices to show that the torsion submodule T is zero; T is ∇-stable.
2. Over a closed-interval ring Γ_I (a PID by RD.0/closed-interval-analytic-ring-pid) let (f) be the annihilator of T: from f m = 0 one gets f' m + f∇m = 0 and f²∇(m) = 0, so ∇(m) ∈ T, f∇(m) = 0, f'm = 0, hence f' ∈ (f); since Γ_I contains Q, (f) is the unit ideal (Crew Proposition 6.1).
3. Pass to R_K via M = lim M ⊗ Γ_I (Crew 4.8(iv)) and the fact that a torsion element is defined on some annulus.

**Checks.**

- R_K/(log(1+t)) admits no connection: it would force (log(1+t))' = 1/(1+t) ∈ (log(1+t)), impossible since log(1+t) has zeros at ζ − 1 for p-power roots of unity ζ.

<a id="target-rd-2-slope-zero-eigenvectors-descend-to-overconvergent"></a>

### Slope-zero eigenvectors over Γ^alg descend to Γ^alg_con (de Jong)

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/slope-zero-eigenvectors-descend-to-overconvergent` · lemma

Let M be a σ-module over Γ^alg_con[π^{-1}] all of whose generic slopes are nonpositive, and v ∈ M ⊗ Γ^alg[π^{-1}] with F v = v. Then v ∈ M.

**Hypotheses.**

- Generalises de Jong [dJ, Proposition 5.8] and Tsuzuki [T, 4.1.1].

**Prerequisites.** [F-stable lattices: nonnegative generic slopes versus integral models](#target-rd-1-frobenius-stable-lattices) (`RD.1/frobenius-stable-lattices`), [Partial valuations v_n, w_r on Witt vectors and the overconvergent Witt vectors W_con](#target-rd-0-witt-partial-valuations) (`RD.0/witt-partial-valuations`).

**Sources.**

- [S2](#source-2), Lemma 5.4.1, p. 57. Statement (hypothesis: generic slopes nonpositive).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Take an F^{-1}-stable Γ^alg_con-lattice (dual of the lattice of RD.1/frobenius-stable-lattices (a) for M^∨) with matrix A of F^{-1} invertible over Γ^alg_r; the equation x_i = Σ A_ij x_j^{σ^{-1}} gives min_{m≤l} v_{m,r}(x_i) ≥ q w_r(A)/(q − 1) for all l, so the coordinates lie in Γ^alg_con (SFR Lemma 5.4.1).

**Checks.**

- For M = Γ^alg_con[π^{-1}](0) this says the σ-fixed elements of Γ^alg[π^{-1}] (constants of O^{σ}[π^{-1}]) are overconvergent.

<a id="target-rd-2-special-polygon-above-generic"></a>

### The special Newton polygon lies above the generic one, with the same endpoint

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/special-polygon-above-generic` · lemma

For a σ-module M over Γ_con[π^{-1}], the special HN polygon (that of M ⊗ Γ^alg_an,con) lies above the generic HN polygon (that of M ⊗ Γ^alg[π^{-1}]), and both have the same endpoint deg(M).

**Hypotheses.**

- Kedlaya's analogue of Grothendieck's specialisation theorem (SFR §7.3).

**Prerequisites.** [Generic HN filtration: slope decomposition over Γ^alg[π^{-1}] and descent to E = Γ[π^{-1}]](#target-rd-1-generic-slope-decomposition-and-descent) (`RD.1/generic-slope-decomposition-and-descent`), [Semistable and stable σ-modules, HN filtrations, HN polygons and descent of subobjects](#target-rd-1-semistability-and-harder-narasimhan-filtration) (`RD.1/semistability-and-harder-narasimhan-filtration`), [Degree, rank and slope μ(M) = deg(M)/rank(M) of a σ-module](#target-rd-1-degree-and-slope) (`RD.1/degree-and-slope`).

**Sources.**

- [S2](#source-2), Proposition 5.5.1, p. 59. Statement.
- [S1](#source-1), Proposition 5.14, p. 68. The original statement with the endpoint.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Tensor up to Γ^alg_con[π^{-1}]; the descended reverse filtration (RD.1/generic-slope-decomposition-and-descent) is a semistable filtration over Γ^alg_an,con with polygon the generic polygon; apply RD.1/semistability-and-harder-narasimhan-filtration (SFR Proposition 5.5.1). Endpoints agree because the rank one case holds (arXiv:math/0110124 Proposition 5.14).

**Checks.**

- SFR §7.3: F v_1 = v_2, F v_2 = p v_1 + u v_2 with u^σ = u^p: generic slopes {0, 1} (Newton polygon of x² − ux − p), special slopes {1/2, 1/2} (Dwork's trick); PARI/GP newtonpoly gives [1, 0] for x² − (1+3y)x − 3 and [1/2, 1/2] for x² − 3.
- Bessel isocrystal (arXiv:math/0110124 §1.5): generic 0, 1; special 1/2, 1/2.

<a id="target-rd-2-coincident-polygons-common-filtration"></a>

### Coincident generic and special polygons give a common filtration over Γ_con[π^{-1}]

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/coincident-polygons-common-filtration` · theorem

Let M be a σ-module over Γ_con[π^{-1}] whose generic and special HN polygons coincide. Then the generic HN filtration of M ⊗ Γ^alg[π^{-1}] and the special HN filtration of M ⊗ Γ^alg_an,con are both base changes of one exhaustive filtration of M by saturated σ-submodules.

**Hypotheses.**

- Notation of RD.2/special-polygon-above-generic.

**Prerequisites.** [The special Newton polygon lies above the generic one, with the same endpoint](#target-rd-2-special-polygon-above-generic) (`RD.2/special-polygon-above-generic`), [Generic HN filtration: slope decomposition over Γ^alg[π^{-1}] and descent to E = Γ[π^{-1}]](#target-rd-1-generic-slope-decomposition-and-descent) (`RD.1/generic-slope-decomposition-and-descent`), [Newton polygons of extensions; splitting criteria over R^alg](#target-rd-1-splitting-of-exact-sequences-by-polygons) (`RD.1/splitting-of-exact-sequences-by-polygons`), [Rank-one σ-modules over Γ^alg_con, Γ^alg_con[π^{-1}] and R^alg are twists A(n)](#target-rd-1-rank-one-frobenius-modules) (`RD.1/rank-one-frobenius-modules`), [Finite modules over Bézout domains: unimodular rows, saturated spans, freeness, Galois descent of saturated submodules](#target-rd-0-modules-over-bezout-domains) (`RD.0/modules-over-bezout-domains`), [Descent of a saturated subobject through its determinant line](#target-rd-1-saturated-subobject-descent-via-exterior-power) (`RD.1/saturated-subobject-descent-via-exterior-power`), [Numerical membership criterion, intersections and Mayer-Vietoris splitting for Γ_I](#target-rd-0-analytic-ring-membership-and-intersections) (`RD.0/analytic-ring-membership-and-intersections`).

**Sources.**

- [S2](#source-2), Theorem 5.5.2, p. 59. Statement.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Reduce to a determinant line using RD.1/saturated-subobject-descent-via-exterior-power. The generic first step descends to Γ[π^{-1}] (RD.1/generic-slope-decomposition-and-descent); the reverse filtration splits over Γ^alg_an,con (RD.1/splitting-of-exact-sequences-by-polygons) and hence over Γ^alg_con[π^{-1}] (injectivity of H^1(Γ_con[π^{-1}](n)) → H^1(Γ_an,con(n)), RD.1/rank-one-frobenius-modules); so the coordinate ratios lie in Γ[π^{-1}] ∩ Γ^alg_con[π^{-1}] = Γ_con[π^{-1}]. The special first step is the maximal submodule of minimal slope and contains, hence equals, the descended generic one (SFR Theorem 5.5.2; arXiv:math/0110124 Proposition 5.16).

**Checks.**

- If M is isoclinic of generic slope s, both filtrations are 0 ⊂ M and the statement is empty; SFR §7.3's example does not satisfy the hypothesis.

<a id="target-rd-2-good-models-of-sigma-modules"></a>

### Good models: every σ-module over Γ_an,con has, after a finite separable extension, a model with equal polygons

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/good-models-of-sigma-modules` · lemma

(a) (Matrix lemma) Let Γ = Γ^E have enough r0-units with r0 > qr, D invertible over Γ_[r,r], h = −w_r(D) − w_r(D^{-1}), and A with w_r(AD^{-1} − I) > h/(q − 1). Then there is U invertible over Γ_[r,qr] with U^{-1}AU^σD^{-1} − I having entries in πΓ_r and w_r(U^{-1}AU^σD^{-1} − I) > 0; if A and D are invertible over Γ_an,r then U is invertible over Γ_an,qr. (b) For a σ-module M over Γ^K_an,con (K = k((t))) there is a finite separable extension L/K and a σ-module N over Γ^L_con[π^{-1}] with N ⊗ Γ^L_an,con ≅ M ⊗ Γ^L_an,con and equal generic and special HN polygons.

**Hypotheses.**

- Whether the finite extension L in (b) can be avoided is not known (SFR Remark 6.2.3).

**Prerequisites.** [Dieudonné-Manin decomposition of σ-modules over the extended Robba ring R^alg (Kedlaya)](#target-rd-1-dieudonne-manin-over-extended-robba-ring) (`RD.1/dieudonne-manin-over-extended-robba-ring`), [Finite separable extensions: Γ^L_con finite étale over Γ^ℓ_con and Γ^L_an,con = Γ^ℓ_an,con ⊗ Γ^L_con](#target-rd-0-finite-separable-extensions-of-analytic-rings) (`RD.0/finite-separable-extensions-of-analytic-rings`), [F-stable lattices: nonnegative generic slopes versus integral models](#target-rd-1-frobenius-stable-lattices) (`RD.1/frobenius-stable-lattices`), [Semiunit presentations of elements of Γ_I](#target-rd-0-semiunit-presentation) (`RD.0/semiunit-presentation`), [Restriction and induction of Frobenius ([a]_*, [a]^*) and Frobenius pullback](#target-rd-1-frobenius-restriction-and-pullback) (`RD.1/frobenius-restriction-and-pullback`), [Reading the generic polygon from a cyclic vector or from a diagonally dominant Frobenius matrix](#target-rd-1-generic-newton-polygon-from-cyclic-vector) (`RD.1/generic-newton-polygon-from-cyclic-vector`).

**Sources.**

- [S2](#source-2), Proposition 6.2.2, p. 63. Part (b).
- [S2](#source-2), Lemma 6.1.1, p. 62. Part (a).

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a) Iterate U_{l+1} = U_l(I + X_l), X_l the nonpositive-index part of a semiunit presentation of A_lD^{-1} − I; the error in nonpositive indices improves by c_0 each step (SFR Lemma 6.1.1), invertibility over Γ_an,qr by propagating along Γ_[r/q^i, qr] (Lemma 6.2.1).
2. (b) Apply [a]_* to make slopes integral; by RD.1/dieudonne-manin-over-extended-robba-ring write U^{-1}AU^σ = D over Γ^alg_an,con with D diagonal of powers of π; approximate U over Γ^L_[r,qr] for pseudo-finite separable L (RD.0/finite-separable-extensions-of-analytic-rings), apply (a), and read the generic slopes from the resulting matrix via RD.1/generic-newton-polygon-from-cyclic-vector (b) (SFR Proposition 6.2.2; arXiv:math/0110124 Propositions 6.8, 6.9).

**Checks.**

- If M already comes from Γ_con[π^{-1}] with equal polygons, one may take L = K and N = the given model.

<a id="target-rd-2-isoclinic-descent-to-bounded-robba-ring"></a>

### Isoclinic σ-modules descend uniquely from the Robba ring to the bounded Robba ring

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/isoclinic-descent-to-bounded-robba-ring` · theorem

(a) For a unit-root σ-module M over Γ_con[π^{-1}], H^0(M) = H^0(M ⊗ Γ[π^{-1}]) = H^0(M ⊗ Γ_an,con); if K is algebraically closed M has a basis of eigenvectors. (b) Base change from isoclinic σ-modules of slope s over Γ_con[π^{-1}] to isoclinic σ-modules over Γ[π^{-1}] is fully faithful. (c) Base change from isoclinic σ-modules of slope s over Γ_con[π^{-1}] to isoclinic σ-modules of slope s over Γ_an,con is an EQUIVALENCE of categories. (d) A σ-module M over Γ_an,con is isoclinic of slope c/d iff it admits a Γ_con-lattice N on which π^{-c}F^d maps some (any) basis to a basis.

**Hypotheses.**

- The functor in (b) is not essentially surjective in general (ramification breaks of the Galois representation grow too fast; SFR Remark 6.3.4).
- Isoclinic over Γ_con[π^{-1}] means isoclinic generic slope (RD.1/isoclinic-frobenius-module), which implies isoclinic special slope.

**Prerequisites.** [Slope-zero eigenvectors over Γ^alg descend to Γ^alg_con (de Jong)](#target-rd-2-slope-zero-eigenvectors-descend-to-overconvergent) (`RD.2/slope-zero-eigenvectors-descend-to-overconvergent`), [Good models: every σ-module over Γ_an,con has, after a finite separable extension, a model with equal polygons](#target-rd-2-good-models-of-sigma-modules) (`RD.2/good-models-of-sigma-modules`), [Rank-one σ-modules over Γ^alg_con, Γ^alg_con[π^{-1}] and R^alg are twists A(n)](#target-rd-1-rank-one-frobenius-modules) (`RD.1/rank-one-frobenius-modules`), [F-stable lattices: nonnegative generic slopes versus integral models](#target-rd-1-frobenius-stable-lattices) (`RD.1/frobenius-stable-lattices`), [Pure (isoclinic) and unit-root σ-modules over R, R^bd and E](#target-rd-1-isoclinic-frobenius-module) (`RD.1/isoclinic-frobenius-module`), [Finite separable extensions: Γ^L_con finite étale over Γ^ℓ_con and Γ^L_an,con = Γ^ℓ_an,con ⊗ Γ^L_con](#target-rd-0-finite-separable-extensions-of-analytic-rings) (`RD.0/finite-separable-extensions-of-analytic-rings`), [Restriction and induction of Frobenius ([a]_*, [a]^*) and Frobenius pullback](#target-rd-1-frobenius-restriction-and-pullback) (`RD.1/frobenius-restriction-and-pullback`).

**Sources.**

- [S2](#source-2), Theorem 6.3.3(b), p. 64. Part (c).
- [S2](#source-2), Proposition 6.3.5, p. 65. Part (d).

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a) Reduce to K algebraically closed (Corollary 2.5.8); slope-0 eigenvectors over Γ^alg lie in M (RD.2/slope-zero-eigenvectors-descend-to-overconvergent), so M ≅ M_{0,1}^{⊕n}; compare H^0 by RD.1/rank-one-frobenius-modules (SFR Proposition 6.3.2).
2. (b),(c) full faithfulness: Hom(M, N) = H^0(M^∨ ⊗ N) with M^∨ ⊗ N unit-root; essential surjectivity: RD.2/good-models-of-sigma-modules gives a model over Γ^L_con[π^{-1}] (L/K Galois), unique by full faithfulness, hence Gal(L/K)-stable, and it descends by Galois descent (SFR Theorem 6.3.3).
3. (d) Apply RD.1/frobenius-stable-lattices to ([d]_*M)(−c) and its model (SFR Proposition 6.3.5).

**Checks.**

- Unit-root example: M = R_K·e with F e = e is the base change of R^bd·e; the rank one σ-module R_K(c) is isoclinic of slope c and descends to R^bd(c).
- The special-but-not-generic isoclinic case: SFR §7.3's M is isoclinic of special slope 1/2 over Γ_an,con, so by (c) M ⊗ Γ_an,con has a model over Γ_con[π^{-1}] that is isoclinic of GENERIC slope 1/2 — necessarily different from the given model (generic slopes 0, 1).
- For perfect k, K=W(k)[1/p], q=p and standard σ(t)=t^p, identify this target with FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory §§R07.4.7–R07.4.8, including its coefficient carriers, degree convention, standard blocks and increasing slope filtration where applicable. This roadmap supplies the stated general coefficient/Frobenius version and its compatibility with that imported special case, rather than a second implementation of the special case.

<a id="target-rd-2-slope-filtration-for-frobenius-modules-statement"></a>

### Slope filtration theorem for σ-modules over the Robba ring (Kedlaya; Theorem 1.2 / 6.10 of arXiv:math/0110124, Theorem 6.4.1 of SFR)

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/slope-filtration-for-frobenius-modules-statement` · theorem

Let M be a σ-module over Γ_an,con = Γ^E_an,con with E = k((t)) (i.e. over the Robba ring R_K with a Frobenius lift φ, RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring), or more generally over Γ^E_an,con for E complete with enough units. Then there is a UNIQUE filtration 0 = M_0 ⊂ M_1 ⊂ ... ⊂ M_l = M by saturated σ-submodules such that (a) each M_i/M_{i−1} is isoclinic of some slope s_i and (b) s_1 < ... < s_l; it is the HN filtration of M. Moreover: (c) its formation commutes with base change to Γ^{E'}_an,con for any complete extension E' of E with enough units (in particular to Γ^alg_an,con, so absolute HN slopes are the HN slopes); (d) M is semistable iff it is isoclinic; (e) (precise form, arXiv:math/0110124 Theorem 6.10) each M_i/M_{i−1} contains a unique F-stable Γ_con[π^{-1}]-submodule N_i of the same rank spanning it over Γ_an,con, all of whose generic slopes equal s_i; conditions (a),(b) determine the filtration uniquely. In the notation of arXiv:math/0110124 (Theorem 1.2): M_i/M_{i−1} ≅ N_i ⊗ Γ_an,con with N_i defined over Γ_con[1/p] and all slopes of N_i equal to s_i.

**Hypotheses.**

- k any field of characteristic p (not necessarily perfect), O finite totally ramified over a Cohen ring C(k); σ any Frobenius lift in the sense of SFR (an endomorphism lifting the q-power Frobenius, carrying O into itself), which includes Kedlaya's 2004 Frobenius (a composition power of a p-power lift).
- σ-modules are finite locally free, hence free over the Bézout ring R_K (RD.0/modules-over-bezout-domains), with F an isomorphism after inverting π (automatic over R_K since π is a unit).
- Special slopes (over Γ^alg_an,con) and generic slopes (over Γ^alg[π^{-1}], RD.1/frobenius-slopes) differ in general; N_i has generic slopes = special slopes = s_i.
- Slopes: SFR normalises w(π) = 1; this statement is normalisation-independent up to the factor e(K).

**Prerequisites.** [Isoclinic σ-modules descend uniquely from the Robba ring to the bounded Robba ring](#target-rd-2-isoclinic-descent-to-bounded-robba-ring) (`RD.2/isoclinic-descent-to-bounded-robba-ring`), [Dieudonné-Manin decomposition of σ-modules over the extended Robba ring R^alg (Kedlaya)](#target-rd-1-dieudonne-manin-over-extended-robba-ring) (`RD.1/dieudonne-manin-over-extended-robba-ring`), [Existence of eigenvectors and of embeddings of twists over R^alg](#target-rd-1-eigenvectors-over-extended-robba-ring) (`RD.1/eigenvectors-over-extended-robba-ring`), [Semistable and stable σ-modules, HN filtrations, HN polygons and descent of subobjects](#target-rd-1-semistability-and-harder-narasimhan-filtration) (`RD.1/semistability-and-harder-narasimhan-filtration`), [Finite modules over Bézout domains: unimodular rows, saturated spans, freeness, Galois descent of saturated submodules](#target-rd-0-modules-over-bezout-domains) (`RD.0/modules-over-bezout-domains`), [Good models: every σ-module over Γ_an,con has, after a finite separable extension, a model with equal polygons](#target-rd-2-good-models-of-sigma-modules) (`RD.2/good-models-of-sigma-modules`), [Coincident generic and special polygons give a common filtration over Γ_con[π^{-1}]](#target-rd-2-coincident-polygons-common-filtration) (`RD.2/coincident-polygons-common-filtration`), [Finite separable extensions: Γ^L_con finite étale over Γ^ℓ_con and Γ^L_an,con = Γ^ℓ_an,con ⊗ Γ^L_con](#target-rd-0-finite-separable-extensions-of-analytic-rings) (`RD.0/finite-separable-extensions-of-analytic-rings`), [Pure (isoclinic) and unit-root σ-modules over R, R^bd and E](#target-rd-1-isoclinic-frobenius-module) (`RD.1/isoclinic-frobenius-module`), [The Robba ring R_K is Kedlaya's analytic ring Γ^{k((t))}_an,con: naive and true partial valuations agree](#target-rd-0-robba-ring) (`RD.0/robba-ring`), [Weakly continuous Frobenius lifts on the integral Amice ring](#target-rd-0-frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring) (`RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring`), [Frobenius slopes and Newton (HN) polygons of σ-modules: generic slopes over E and R^bd, special slopes over R](#target-rd-1-frobenius-slopes) (`RD.1/frobenius-slopes`), [Every σ-module over Γ_an,con has a Harder-Narasimhan filtration](#target-rd-1-harder-narasimhan-filtration-exists) (`RD.1/harder-narasimhan-filtration-exists`), [Descent of a saturated subobject through its determinant line](#target-rd-1-saturated-subobject-descent-via-exterior-power) (`RD.1/saturated-subobject-descent-via-exterior-power`).

**Sources.**

- [S2](#source-2), Theorem 6.4.1, p. 65. Statement of the slope filtration theorem (conditions (a) isoclinic quotients, (b) increasing slopes).
- [S2](#source-2), Corollary 6.4.2, p. 66. Part (c).
- [S1](#source-1), Section 1.2, Theorem 1.2, p. 5 (extraction lines 199-206). Kedlaya's original formulation (the decomposition's verified locator).
- [S1](#source-1), Section 6.3, Theorem 6.10 and proof, pp. 77-78 (lines 4048-4137). The precise form (e).
- [S14](#source-14), Theorem 1.2, Ann. of Math. 160 (2004), p. 97. The version of record adds 'nontrivial'.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Uniqueness: isoclinic σ-modules are semistable (RD.2/isoclinic-descent-to-bounded-robba-ring with RD.1/dieudonne-manin-over-extended-robba-ring), so any filtration with (a),(b) is an HN filtration, unique by RD.1/semistability-and-harder-narasimhan-filtration.
2. Existence: the HN filtration of M ⊗ Γ^alg_an,con (RD.1/harder-narasimhan-filtration-exists and RD.1/dieudonne-manin-over-extended-robba-ring) must be descended; by RD.1/saturated-subobject-descent-via-exterior-power reduce to descent of the determinant line of the first step.
3. By RD.2/good-models-of-sigma-modules choose a finite Galois L/K and a model N over Γ^L_con[π^{-1}] with equal polygons; by RD.2/coincident-polygons-common-filtration M'_1 descends to M_1 ⊆ M ⊗ Γ^L_an,con.
4. With a generator v = Σ a_i e_i of M_1, the ratios a_i/a_j are Gal(L/K)-invariant elements of Frac Γ^L_an,con, hence lie in Frac Γ^K_an,con (RD.0/finite-separable-extensions-of-analytic-rings (Galois invariants)); clearing denominators gives a nonzero element of M_1 ∩ M, so M_1 descends (SFR Theorem 6.4.1).
5. (c) The characterisation by (a),(b) is stable under base change (SFR Corollary 6.4.2); (d) SFR Corollary 6.4.3.
6. (e) Apply RD.2/isoclinic-descent-to-bounded-robba-ring (c) to each (twisted, [d]_*-rescaled) graded piece: the unique isoclinic model over Γ_con[π^{-1}] is N_i (compare the original argument of arXiv:math/0110124 Theorem 6.10 via Propositions 6.9, 5.16, 4.4, 4.5, 5.11 and Corollary 3.16).

**Checks.**

- Unit-root case (l = 1, s_1 = 0): M ≅ N ⊗ Γ_an,con with N étale over Γ_con[π^{-1}]; this is the input to Tsuzuki's theorem (RD.2/tsuzuki-unit-root-finite-monodromy).
- Bessel isocrystal (arXiv:math/0110124 §1.5): l = 1, s_1 = 1/2 (v_p normalisation): N_1 has generic slopes 1/2, 1/2 although the given model over Γ_con has generic slopes 0 and 1; any implementation must distinguish generic from special slopes.
- SFR §7.3 example (F v_1 = v_2, F v_2 = p v_1 + u v_2, u^σ = u^p): the slope filtration of M ⊗ R_K is 0 ⊂ M ⊗ R_K (isoclinic of slope 1/2), while the generic slope filtration over Γ[π^{-1}] has two steps.
- R(0) ⊕ R(1): M_1 = R(0), s_1 = 0 < s_2 = 1; the filtration is not required to split over R_K and does not in general (RD.1/splitting-of-exact-sequences-by-polygons).
- For perfect k, K=W(k)[1/p], q=p and standard σ(t)=t^p, identify this target with FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory §§R07.4.7–R07.4.8, including its coefficient carriers, degree convention, standard blocks and increasing slope filtration where applicable. <a id="target-rd-2-differentials-have-positive-slopes"></a>

### The Frobenius on differentials has positive generic slopes

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/differentials-have-positive-slopes` · lemma

View Ω^1_{Γ_con/O} = Γ_con du (derivation d(Σ c_i u^i) = Σ i c_i u^{i−1} du) as a σ-module via dσ : Ω^1 → Ω^1, dσ(f du) = f^σ d(u^σ). Then dσ(ω) ≡ 0 mod π for every ω, so the generic slopes of Ω^1_{Γ_con/O} are all positive, and the special slopes of Ω^1_{Γ_an,con/O} are nonnegative. The same holds for Γ^L_con, Γ^L_an,con with L/k((t)) finite separable.

**Hypotheses.**

- σ lifts the q-power Frobenius, so u^σ ≡ u^q mod π and d(u^σ)/du ≡ q u^{q−1} ≡ 0 mod π.

**Prerequisites.** [F-stable lattices: nonnegative generic slopes versus integral models](#target-rd-1-frobenius-stable-lattices) (`RD.1/frobenius-stable-lattices`), [The special Newton polygon lies above the generic one, with the same endpoint](#target-rd-2-special-polygon-above-generic) (`RD.2/special-polygon-above-generic`), [Differential (∇-)modules over annuli, the Robba ring and differential fields](#target-rd-1-differential-module) (`RD.1/differential-module`).

**Sources.**

- [S2](#source-2), Remark 7.1.4, p. 67. Statement.

**Construction or proof.**

1. dσ(du) = (du^σ/du) du with du^σ/du ∈ πΓ_con; RD.1/frobenius-stable-lattices (b) gives positive generic slopes (the Frobenius on the lattice Γ_con du is divisible by π), and RD.2/special-polygon-above-generic gives special slopes ≥ 0 (SFR Remark 7.1.4).

**Checks.**

- For the standard lift u^σ = u^q: dσ(du) = q u^{q−1} du, so the rank one σ-module Ω^1 has generic and special slope w(q) = e(K)·a > 0.

<a id="target-rd-2-slope-filtration-is-horizontal"></a>

### Each step of the slope filtration of a (σ,∇)-module is ∇-stable

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/slope-filtration-is-horizontal` · lemma

Let M be a (σ,∇)-module over Γ_an,con (over R_K: a (φ,∇)-module, RD.1/frobenius-differential-module). Then every step M_i of the slope filtration (RD.2/slope-filtration-for-frobenius-modules-statement) is a (σ,∇)-submodule (arXiv:math/0110124 Theorem 6.12(d)).

**Hypotheses.**

- The Frobenius and connection are compatible: ∇ ∘ F = (F ⊗ dσ) ∘ ∇.

**Prerequisites.** [Slope filtration theorem for σ-modules over the Robba ring (Kedlaya; Theorem 1.2 / 6.10 of arXiv:math/0110124, Theorem 6.4.1 of SFR)](#target-rd-2-slope-filtration-for-frobenius-modules-statement) (`RD.2/slope-filtration-for-frobenius-modules-statement`), [The Frobenius on differentials has positive generic slopes](#target-rd-2-differentials-have-positive-slopes) (`RD.2/differentials-have-positive-slopes`), [Pure (isoclinic) and unit-root σ-modules over R, R^bd and E](#target-rd-1-isoclinic-frobenius-module) (`RD.1/isoclinic-frobenius-module`), [(σ,∇)-modules (φ,∇)-modules over R, R^bd, R^int, E and dagger algebras; Frobenius structures](#target-rd-1-frobenius-differential-module) (`RD.1/frobenius-differential-module`).

**Sources.**

- [S2](#source-2), Proposition 7.1.6, p. 67. Statement.
- [S14](#source-14), Theorem 6.12(d), p. 180. Kedlaya's original formulation.

**Construction or proof.**

1. It suffices to treat the first step M_1 (isoclinic of slope s_1). The Kodaira-Spencer map M_1 → (M/M_1) ⊗ Ω^1 induced by ∇ is Γ_an,con-linear and F-equivariant (compatibility of F and ∇).
2. All slopes of (M/M_1) ⊗ Ω^1 are > s_1: slopes of M/M_1 exceed s_1 and those of Ω^1 are ≥ 0 (RD.2/differentials-have-positive-slopes) and slopes add under ⊗ (RD.1/isoclinic-frobenius-module).
3. Hom vanishing (RD.1/isoclinic-frobenius-module, SFR Proposition 4.6.4) forces the map to vanish, so ∇(M_1) ⊆ M_1 ⊗ Ω^1 (SFR Proposition 7.1.6). Kedlaya's original proof solves a matrix σ-equation with Proposition 3.19(c) (arXiv:math/0110124 p. 81).

**Checks.**

- SFR Example 7.2.6 (corrected): M_1 = span(e_1) of slope 0 is ∇-stable (∇e_1 = 0).

<a id="target-rd-2-isoclinic-model-inherits-connection"></a>

### The isoclinic model over R^bd inherits the connection

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/isoclinic-model-inherits-connection` · lemma

Let M be an isoclinic σ-module over Γ_con[π^{-1}] (= R^bd) such that M ⊗ Γ_an,con carries a (σ,∇)-module structure. Then ∇ preserves M, so M is a (σ,∇)-module over Γ_con[π^{-1}]. In particular each N_i of the slope filtration of a (σ,∇)-module is ∇-stable (arXiv:math/0110124 Theorem 6.12(e); Berger, Lemme V.14).

**Hypotheses.**

- Notation of RD.2/slope-filtration-for-frobenius-modules-statement (e).

**Prerequisites.** [The Frobenius on differentials has positive generic slopes](#target-rd-2-differentials-have-positive-slopes) (`RD.2/differentials-have-positive-slopes`), [Dieudonné-Manin decomposition of σ-modules over the extended Robba ring R^alg (Kedlaya)](#target-rd-1-dieudonne-manin-over-extended-robba-ring) (`RD.1/dieudonne-manin-over-extended-robba-ring`), [Rank-one σ-modules over Γ^alg_con, Γ^alg_con[π^{-1}] and R^alg are twists A(n)](#target-rd-1-rank-one-frobenius-modules) (`RD.1/rank-one-frobenius-modules`), [Pure (isoclinic) and unit-root σ-modules over R, R^bd and E](#target-rd-1-isoclinic-frobenius-module) (`RD.1/isoclinic-frobenius-module`).

**Sources.**

- [S2](#source-2), Proposition 7.1.7, p. 67. Statement (hypothesis: M isoclinic over Γcon[π^{-1}] with M ⊗ Γan,con a (σ,∇)-module).
- [S14](#source-14), Theorem 6.12(e) proof, p. 181. Attribution to Berger.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Choose a basis of M and let f(Σ c_i e_i) = Σ e_i ⊗ dc_i; then ∇ − f is Γ_an,con-linear, i.e. an element v of M^∨ ⊗ M ⊗ Ω^1 ⊗ Γ_an,con with F v − v = w ∈ M^∨ ⊗ M ⊗ Ω^1.
2. M^∨ ⊗ M is unit-root, so M^∨ ⊗ M ⊗ Ω^1 has positive generic and special slopes (RD.2/differentials-have-positive-slopes); by RD.1/dieudonne-manin-over-extended-robba-ring and injectivity of H^1(Γ_con[π^{-1}](n)) → H^1(Γ_an,con(n)) for n ≥ 0 (RD.1/rank-one-frobenius-modules) v is defined over Γ_con[π^{-1}] (SFR Proposition 7.1.7).

**Checks.**

- For the trivial (σ,∇)-module R_K with d, the model R^bd is d-stable.

<a id="target-rd-2-finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring"></a>

### Finite étale extensions of R^int and the Robba rings R^L of finite separable extensions of k((t))

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring` · construction

(a) R^int is a henselian discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal πR^int and residue field k((t)) (K discretely valued). Hence for every finite separable extension L of k((t)) there is a finite étale R^int-algebra R^int_L, unique up to unique isomorphism inducing the specified residue identification R^int_L/π ≅ L; L ↦ R^int_L is an equivalence from finite separable extensions of k((t)) to finite étale local R^int-algebras ('formally étale covers' of a thin annulus). (b) R^L := R_K ⊗_{R^int} R^int_L and R^{bd}_L := R^bd ⊗ R^int_L; they coincide with Kedlaya's Γ^L_an,con and Γ^L_con[π^{-1}]. The Frobenius lift φ and the derivation d/dt extend uniquely to R^int_L, R^{bd}_L, R^L; for L/k((t)) Galois, Gal(L/k((t))) acts on R^L commuting with φ and d, with fixed ring R_K. (c) If the residue field k_L of L is separable over k (always if k is perfect), choosing u ∈ R^int_L lifting a uniformiser of L gives a continuous isomorphism R^L ≅ R_{K'} (Robba ring over K' = the unramified extension of K with residue field k_L, in the variable u); the isomorphism depends on u but the conclusions drawn from it do not. (d) (Nearly separable extensions, needed when k is imperfect) form the direct limit of K →_{σ_K} K →_{σ_K} ⋯ and let K^{(m)} be its m-th copy, containing the original K through σ_K^m and having residue extension k^{q^{-m}}. A nearly finite separable extension is a finite separable extension of k^{q^{-m}}((t)), and its Robba ring is formed over R_{K^{(m)}} ⊇ R_K via φ^m.

**Hypotheses.**

- K is discretely valued (Kedlaya's overview Remark 3.5.3: otherwise R^int is not a valuation ring).
- Separable L/k((t)) may have inseparable residue field extension when k is imperfect (arXiv:math/0110124 §2.2, example k((t))[x]/(x^p − x − ct^{-p}) with c ∉ k^p); then (c) needs the nearly separable replacement (d).

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/LocalMonodromy/Monodromy`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [W_con(ℓ, O) is a henselian discrete valuation ring](#target-rd-0-overconvergent-witt-vectors-henselian) (`RD.0/overconvergent-witt-vectors-henselian`), [Finite separable extensions: Γ^L_con finite étale over Γ^ℓ_con and Γ^L_an,con = Γ^ℓ_an,con ⊗ Γ^L_con](#target-rd-0-finite-separable-extensions-of-analytic-rings) (`RD.0/finite-separable-extensions-of-analytic-rings`), [Kedlaya's analytic rings Γ^ℓ_I, Γ^ℓ_an,r and Γ^ℓ_an,con](#target-rd-0-analytic-ring) (`RD.0/analytic-ring`), [The Robba ring R_K is Kedlaya's analytic ring Γ^{k((t))}_an,con: naive and true partial valuations agree](#target-rd-0-robba-ring) (`RD.0/robba-ring`), [The bounded Robba ring R^bd is a henselian discretely valued field with residue field k((t)); R^bd = R ∩ E](#target-rd-0-bounded-robba-ring) (`RD.0/bounded-robba-ring`), [Weakly continuous Frobenius lifts on the integral Amice ring](#target-rd-0-frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring) (`RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring`), `mathlib:HenselianLocalRing`, `mathlib:Algebra.Etale`, `mathlib:Algebra.IsSeparable`, `mathlib:IsGalois`.

**Sources.**

- [S8](#source-8), Proposition 3.5.5, p. 15. Part (a).
- [S8](#source-8), Definition 3.5.6, p. 16. Formally étale covers = finite étale extensions of R^int.
- [S4](#source-4), Theorem 5.1.2 and proof, pp. 29-30. Part (c).

**Uses and API requirements.**

- RD.2/quasi-unipotent-differential-module: the extensions allowed in the definition of quasi-unipotence
- Kedlaya, Finiteness, Theorem 5.1.2: the form of the local monodromy theorem consumed by RD.5
- PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3 / Berger Théorème 5.20: the extension R_L = B†_rig,L attached to a finite extension L/K via the field of norms
- RD.3/full-faithfulness-overconvergent-to-convergent: local full faithfulness is proved after finite separable extensions

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `RobbaExtension.intAlg` |  | R^int_L, the finite étale R^int-algebra with residue field L. |
| `RobbaExtension.robba` |  | R^L = R_K ⊗_{R^int} R^int_L. |
| `RobbaExtension.bounded` |  | R^{bd}_L = R^bd ⊗_{R^int} R^int_L. |
| `RobbaExtension.frobenius` |  | The unique extension φ_L of φ to R^int_L, R^{bd}_L, R^L. |
| `RobbaExtension.derivation` |  | The unique extension of d/dt to R^L, with Ω^1_{R^L} = R^L ⊗ Ω^1_{R_K}. |
| `RobbaExtension.galoisAction` |  | For L/k((t)) Galois, Gal(L/k((t))) acts on R^L commuting with φ_L and d, with fixed ring R_K. |
| `RobbaExtension.equivOfResidue` |  | L ↦ R^int_L is an equivalence of categories onto finite étale local R^int-algebras. |
| `RobbaExtension.isoRobbaOfUniformizer` |  | If k_L/k is separable, a lift u of a uniformiser gives R^L ≅ R_{K'} (Robba ring over K' in u). |
| `RobbaExtension.isBezout` |  | R^L is a Bézout domain (RD.0/analytic-ring-bezout). |
| `RobbaExtension.trans` |  | R^{L'} = R^L ⊗_{R^int_L} R^int_{L'} for k((t)) ⊆ L ⊆ L', compatible with φ, d and Galois actions. |

**Unit tests.**

- `RobbaExtension.trivial` (degenerate): For L = k((t)), R^int_L = R^int and R^L = R_K.
- `RobbaExtension.kummer` (computation): For p ∤ n and L = k((t))(t^{1/n}), R^L = R_K[v]/(v^n − t), and d/dt(v) = v/(n t).
- `RobbaExtension.artinSchreier` (computation): For L = k((t))[ȳ]/(ȳ^p − ȳ − t^{-1}), R^int_L = R^int[y]/(y^p − y − t^{-1}) is finite étale of degree p (the derivative p y^{p−1} − 1 is a unit).
- `RobbaExtension.galois_fixed` (characterisation): For L/k((t)) Galois with group G, (R^L)^G = R_K.
- `RobbaExtension.not_etale_purely_inseparable` (non-example): L = k((t^{1/p})) is not separable: R^int[y]/(y^p − t) is not étale over R^int (its reduction k((t))[y]/(y^p − t) is inseparable); this extension is reached instead through the Frobenius lift φ (pseudo-finite separable extensions).

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a) R^int is local with residue field k((t)) (overview Lemma 3.5.2) and henselian by Newton iteration convergent on annuli (overview Proposition 3.5.5; arXiv:math/0110124 Lemma 3.9; RD.0/overconvergent-witt-vectors-henselian); a henselian local ring has the stated equivalence of finite étale algebras (EGA IV 18.5.15; lift a monic separable minimal polynomial of a primitive element, SFR Proposition 2.2.15).
2. (b) is RD.0/finite-separable-extensions-of-analytic-rings for E = k((t)); φ extends by étaleness (unique lift of the q-power Frobenius of L, SFR Definition 2.2.8) and d/dt extends uniquely to an étale extension (Kähler differentials of an étale algebra).
3. (c) Cohen structure theorem L ≅ k_L((ū)); lifting ū to u ∈ R^int_L and the unramified K'/K gives R^int_{K',u} → R^int_L, an isomorphism by uniqueness in (a); complete (Kedlaya, Finiteness, proof of Theorem 5.1.2; overview Remark 3.5.7).
4. (d) arXiv:math/0110124 §2.2 (nearly separable valued fields; Annals: 'nearly finite separable'), Kedlaya, Finiteness, Theorem 5.1.2 (K_0 = K^{σ^{-m}}).

**Checks.**

- Kummer: for p ∤ n, L = k((t))[v]/(v^n − t) gives R^L = R_K[v]/(v^n − t), the Robba ring in v.
- Artin-Schreier: L = k((t))[ȳ]/(ȳ^p − ȳ − t^{-1}) (wild, Swan conductor 1) lifts to R^int_L = R^int[y]/(y^p − y − t^{-1}); the Dwork module trivialises over it (RD.2/dwork-exponential-artin-schreier-example).

<a id="target-rd-2-constant-and-quasi-constant-differential-module"></a>

### Constant and quasi-constant ∇-modules over the Robba ring

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/constant-and-quasi-constant-differential-module` · definition

A ∇-module M over R_K (RD.1/differential-module: finite free with connection ∇ : M → M ⊗ Ω^1) is constant if it is spanned by ker ∇, equivalently isomorphic to a direct sum of copies of the trivial ∇-module (R_K, d). It is quasi-constant (étale) if M ⊗ R^L is constant for some finite separable L/k((t)) (RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring; nearly finite separable if k is imperfect). A (σ,∇)-module is (quasi-)constant if its underlying ∇-module is.

**Hypotheses.**

- The notion does not involve the Frobenius structure (SFR Definition 7.2.2).

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/LocalMonodromy/Monodromy`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Differential (∇-)modules over annuli, the Robba ring and differential fields](#target-rd-1-differential-module) (`RD.1/differential-module`), [Finite étale extensions of R^int and the Robba rings R^L of finite separable extensions of k((t))](#target-rd-2-finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring) (`RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring`).

**Sources.**

- [S2](#source-2), Definition 7.2.2, p. 68. Constant.
- [S8](#source-8), Definition 4.3.1, p. 20. Quasi-constant.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- RD.2/quasi-unipotent-differential-module: graded pieces of a quasi-unipotent module are quasi-constant
- Tsuzuki's theorem (RD.2/tsuzuki-unit-root-finite-monodromy): unit-root (σ,∇)-modules are quasi-constant
- Kedlaya overview §5.4, Crew §10: Swan conductors and irregularity of quasi-constant modules

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DifferentialModule.IsConstant` |  | M is spanned over R_K by ker ∇. |
| `DifferentialModule.IsQuasiConstant` |  | M ⊗ R^L is constant for some finite separable L. |
| `DifferentialModule.isConstant_iff_trivial_sum` |  | Constant ⇔ ≅ (R_K, d)^{⊕n}. |
| `DifferentialModule.H0_isConstant` |  | M constant ⇔ dim_K H^0(M) = rank M, and then H^0(M) ⊗_K R_K ≅ M. |
| `DifferentialModule.quasiConstantEquivGaloisRep` |  | Quasi-constant modules becoming constant over R^L ≃ semilinear Gal(L/k((t)))-representations over K' (overview Lemma 4.3.2). |
| `DifferentialModule.isQuasiConstant_tensor` |  | Quasi-constant modules are closed under ⊗, duals, subquotients. |

**Unit tests.**

- `DifferentialModule.trivial_isConstant` (degenerate): (R_K, d)^{⊕n} is constant.
- `DifferentialModule.kummer_quasiConstant` (computation): For p odd, R_K e with ∇e = (1/2)e ⊗ dt/t becomes constant over R_K[v]/(v² − t) (horizontal section v^{-1}e) but is not constant over R_K (the only candidate horizontal sections c t^{-1/2} e are not in R_K).
- `DifferentialModule.constant_iff_H0` (characterisation): M is constant iff dim_K ker ∇ = rank M.
- `DifferentialModule.exp_not_quasiConstant` (non-example): R_K e with ∇e = e ⊗ dt is not quasi-constant (RD.2/frobenius-hypothesis-is-necessary).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Representation-theoretic description: for L/k((t)) finite Galois with R^L ≅ R_{K'}, E ↦ H^0(M ⊗ R^L) is an equivalence from ∇-modules becoming constant over R^L to semilinear representations of Gal(L/k((t))) on finite-dimensional K'-vector spaces (Kedlaya overview Lemma 4.3.2, via Hilbert 90-type semilinear Maschke and Schur lemmas, overview §4.2).
2. Closure: quasi-constant modules are stable under ⊕, ⊗, duals, subobjects and quotients but not extensions (overview Definition 4.3.1).

**Checks.**

- (R_K, d) is constant; R_K·e with ∇e = (1/2) e ⊗ dt/t (p odd) is quasi-constant (constant over R_K[v]/(v² − t), horizontal section v^{-1}e) but not constant.

<a id="target-rd-2-unipotent-differential-module"></a>

### Unipotent ∇-modules over the Robba ring

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/unipotent-differential-module` · definition

A ∇-module M over R_K (more generally over R^L) is unipotent if it admits an exhaustive filtration 0 = M_0 ⊂ ... ⊂ M_n = M by ∇-submodules whose successive quotients are constant (RD.2/constant-and-quasi-constant-differential-module); equivalently (Kedlaya, Finiteness, Definition 5.1.1) M has a unipotent basis v_1, ..., v_n with ∇v_i ∈ (R_K v_1 + ... + R_K v_{i−1}) ⊗ dt/t; equivalently (Crew §6.6) M is a successive extension of copies of the trivial rank one object (R_K, d). A (σ,∇)-module is unipotent if its underlying ∇-module is. A strongly unipotent basis is one with t∇_{d/dt} v_i ∈ K v_1 + ... + K v_{i−1}.

**Hypotheses.**

- The definition does not refer to the Frobenius structure and is invariant under continuous automorphisms of R_K (change of the series parameter) (Kedlaya, Finiteness, after Definition 5.1.1).
- Every ∇-submodule of a ∇-module is saturated (overview Remark 4.1.5), so the filtration is automatically by saturated submodules and the quotients are free.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/LocalMonodromy/Monodromy`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Constant and quasi-constant ∇-modules over the Robba ring](#target-rd-2-constant-and-quasi-constant-differential-module) (`RD.2/constant-and-quasi-constant-differential-module`), [Differential (∇-)modules over annuli, the Robba ring and differential fields](#target-rd-1-differential-module) (`RD.1/differential-module`), [Finite modules over Bézout domains: unimodular rows, saturated spans, freeness, Galois descent of saturated submodules](#target-rd-0-modules-over-bezout-domains) (`RD.0/modules-over-bezout-domains`).

**Sources.**

- [S2](#source-2), Definition 7.2.4, p. 68. The definition (with SFR's repeated 'is said to be').
- [S4](#source-4), Definition 5.1.1, p. 29. Unipotent basis form (dt/t is rendered 'dtt' by the extraction).
- [S19](#source-19), §6.6, p. 737. Crew's formulation (OCR renders ∇ as V).

**Uses and API requirements.**

- RD.2/quasi-unipotence-and-local-monodromy-statement: the conclusion of the local monodromy theorem after a finite étale extension
- Kedlaya, Finiteness, §§5-6 (RD.5): unipotent bases and their relative versions over dagger algebras
- RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue: unipotent modules correspond to nilpotent residues
- Crew §§6, 10: unipotent local monodromy of isocrystals on curves; strictness (finite cohomology)

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DifferentialModule.IsUnipotent` |  | M admits a filtration by ∇-submodules with constant quotients. |
| `DifferentialModule.UnipotentBasis` |  | A basis with ∇v_i ∈ (Σ_{j<i} R v_j) ⊗ dt/t. |
| `DifferentialModule.isUnipotent_iff_exists_unipotentBasis` |  | Unipotent ⇔ has a unipotent basis. |
| `DifferentialModule.StronglyUnipotentBasis` |  | A basis with t d/dt acting on it by a strictly upper triangular matrix over K. |
| `DifferentialModule.exists_stronglyUnipotentBasis` |  | A unipotent module has a strongly unipotent basis; the K-span of such a basis is independent of choices. |
| `DifferentialModule.isUnipotent_closure` |  | Unipotent modules are closed under ⊕, ⊗, duals, subquotients and extensions (overview Definition 4.5.1). |
| `DifferentialModule.isUnipotent_comap` |  | Unipotence is preserved by pullback along continuous automorphisms of R_K and along R_K → R^L. |
| `DifferentialModule.isConstant.isUnipotent` |  | Constant ⇒ unipotent. |

**Unit tests.**

- `DifferentialModule.trivial_isUnipotent` (degenerate): (R_K, d)^{⊕n} is unipotent (the zero filtration step suffices).
- `DifferentialModule.log_isUnipotent` (computation): M = R_K e_1 ⊕ R_K e_2 with ∇e_1 = 0, ∇e_2 = e_1 ⊗ dt/t is unipotent (unipotent basis e_1, e_2) but not constant: ker ∇ = K e_1 (the would-be horizontal section e_2 − log(t) e_1 is not in M).
- `DifferentialModule.isUnipotent_iff_basis` (characterisation): M is unipotent iff it has a basis on which t∇_{d/dt} acts by a strictly upper triangular matrix over K.
- `DifferentialModule.kummer_not_unipotent` (non-example): For p odd, R_K e with ∇e = (1/2)e ⊗ dt/t is not unipotent (its only rank one quotient is itself and ker ∇ = 0), though it is quasi-constant.
- `DifferentialModule.exp_not_unipotent` (non-example): R_K e with ∇e = e ⊗ dt is not unipotent, nor unipotent over any R^L (RD.2/frobenius-hypothesis-is-necessary).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Equivalence of the three formulations: a filtration with constant quotients refines to one with rank one trivial quotients; choosing lifts of horizontal bases gives a unipotent basis (Ω^1 = R_K dt/t since t is a unit of R_K); conversely the spans of v_1..v_i are ∇-stable with trivial quotients.
2. Every unipotent M has a strongly unipotent basis and the K-span of any strongly unipotent basis is canonical (Kedlaya, Finiteness, Proposition 5.2.6, Lemma 5.2.4, Corollary 5.2.5), which leads to RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue.

**Checks.**

- SFR Example 7.2.6 (with u^σ = u^q): unipotent, not quasi-constant.

<a id="target-rd-2-quasi-unipotent-differential-module"></a>

### Quasi-unipotent ∇-modules and (σ,∇)-modules

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/quasi-unipotent-differential-module` · definition

A ∇-module M over R_K is quasi-unipotent if M ⊗ R^L is unipotent (RD.2/unipotent-differential-module) for some finite separable extension L of k((t)) when k is perfect, and for some nearly finite separable L in general (RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring (d)). Equivalently, M admits a filtration over R_K by ∇-submodules whose successive quotients are quasi-constant. A (σ,∇)-module over R_K is quasi-unipotent if its underlying ∇-module is; Kedlaya's 2004 definition (after tensoring with a finite extension of Γ_con, a filtration by (σ,∇)-submodules whose successive quotients have bases in ker ∇) is equivalent for (σ,∇)-modules because the filtration can be chosen canonical (first step spanned by the full kernel of ∇), hence F-stable.

**Hypotheses.**

- The finite extension is an extension of the bounded Robba ring R^int (a finite cover of the thin annulus), not only a coefficient extension of K; if k is perfect it may be required residually separable (arXiv:math/0110124 §1.1).

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/LocalMonodromy/Monodromy`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Unipotent ∇-modules over the Robba ring](#target-rd-2-unipotent-differential-module) (`RD.2/unipotent-differential-module`), [Constant and quasi-constant ∇-modules over the Robba ring](#target-rd-2-constant-and-quasi-constant-differential-module) (`RD.2/constant-and-quasi-constant-differential-module`), [Finite étale extensions of R^int and the Robba rings R^L of finite separable extensions of k((t))](#target-rd-2-finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring) (`RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring`), [Finite modules over Bézout domains: unimodular rows, saturated spans, freeness, Galois descent of saturated submodules](#target-rd-0-modules-over-bezout-domains) (`RD.0/modules-over-bezout-domains`), [(σ,∇)-modules (φ,∇)-modules over R, R^bd, R^int, E and dagger algebras; Frobenius structures](#target-rd-1-frobenius-differential-module) (`RD.1/frobenius-differential-module`).

**Sources.**
