- [S1](#source-1), Section 1.1, pp. 3-4 (lines 130-135). Kedlaya's definition (the decomposition's verified locator).
- [S8](#source-8), Remark 4.6.2, p. 24. Canonical filtration; equivalence of definitions.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- arXiv:math/0110124 Theorem 1.1: the conclusion of the local monodromy theorem
- Crew §10.1: quasi-unipotent isocrystals on curves and finiteness
- Kedlaya, Finiteness (RD.5): local monodromy at the boundary of a curve fibration
- PadicHodgeTheory:R06.3: Berger: V potentially semistable ⇔ N_dR(V) quasi-unipotent

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DifferentialModule.IsQuasiUnipotent` |  | M ⊗ R^L is unipotent for some allowed L. |
| `DifferentialModule.isQuasiUnipotent_iff_filtration` |  | Quasi-unipotent ⇔ filtration over R_K with quasi-constant quotients. |
| `DifferentialModule.canonicalUnipotentFiltration` |  | The shortest unipotent filtration over R^L (first step spanned by ker ∇, ...), unique and Galois-stable. |
| `DifferentialModule.isQuasiUnipotent_closure` |  | Closed under ⊕, ⊗, duals, subquotients, extensions. |
| `DifferentialModule.isQuasiUnipotent_of_isUnipotent` |  | Unipotent ⇒ quasi-unipotent; quasi-constant ⇒ quasi-unipotent. |
| `DifferentialModule.isQuasiUnipotent_baseChange` |  | M quasi-unipotent ⇔ M ⊗ R^L quasi-unipotent for any finite separable L. |

**Unit tests.**

- `DifferentialModule.isQuasiUnipotent_trivial` (degenerate): (R_K, d) is quasi-unipotent with L = k((t)).
- `DifferentialModule.kummer_isQuasiUnipotent` (computation): R_K e, ∇e = (1/2)e dt/t (p odd) is quasi-unipotent with L = k((t^{1/2})) but not unipotent.
- `DifferentialModule.isQuasiUnipotent_iff_filtration_test` (characterisation): The Kummer module above has the one-step filtration 0 ⊂ M with quasi-constant quotient.
- `DifferentialModule.exp_not_isQuasiUnipotent` (non-example): R_K e with ∇e = e ⊗ dt is not quasi-unipotent.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Equivalence of the two formulations: if M ⊗ R^L has a unipotent filtration, the shortest one (first step = span of ker ∇ over R^L, etc.) is unique, Gal(L/k((t)))-stable and descends by Galois descent (RD.0/modules-over-bezout-domains); its descended quotients are quasi-constant (overview Remark 4.6.2). The same canonicity shows the filtration is F-stable for a (σ,∇)-module.
2. Closure properties: quasi-unipotent modules are closed under ⊕, ⊗, duals, subquotients and extensions (overview Definition 4.6.1).

**Checks.**

- Every unipotent and every quasi-constant module is quasi-unipotent; the exponential module R_K e, ∇e = e dt is not (RD.2/frobenius-hypothesis-is-necessary).

<a id="target-rd-2-robba-ring-antiderivative"></a>

### Residues and antiderivatives on the Robba ring

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/robba-ring-antiderivative` · lemma

Let R = R^L ≅ R_{K'} in a variable u (RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring (c)). (a) For f = Σ_n a_n u^n ∈ R, the series Σ_{n≠−1} a_n u^{n+1}/(n+1) converges at every interior radius of each open annulus on which f converges, so f du = a_{−1} du/u + dg with g ∈ R; the residue res(f du) = a_{−1} is well defined and f du is exact in R iff a_{−1} = 0; ker(d : R → R) = K'.

**Hypotheses.**

- K' of characteristic 0. The estimate |1/(n+1)|_p ≤ |n+1|_ordinary for n ≠ −1 (including negative n) keeps the radius of convergence.

**Prerequisites.** [Finite étale extensions of R^int and the Robba rings R^L of finite separable extensions of k((t))](#target-rd-2-finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring) (`RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring`), [The Robba ring R_K is Kedlaya's analytic ring Γ^{k((t))}_an,con: naive and true partial valuations agree](#target-rd-0-robba-ring) (`RD.0/robba-ring`).

**Sources.**

- [S8](#source-8), Example 4.1.11, p. 18. Part (a): H^0 and H^1 of the trivial ∇-module on the Robba ring.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a) For n ≠ −1, |a_n/(n+1)|ρ^{n+1} ≤ |a_n|ρ^n·(|n|+1)ρ, and polynomial factors do not change convergence on open annuli, so the primitive converges where f does; uniqueness up to constants since d(Σ c_n u^n) = 0 forces c_n = 0 for n ≠ 0.

**Checks.**

- res(du/u) = 1, so du/u is not exact in R (its primitive log u lives only in the logarithmic extension, RD.2/log-robba-ring).
- Contrast with the closed disc: ω = Σ_{k≥0} p^k x^{p^k−1} dx has coefficients tending to 0, so it lies in K⟨x⟩dx, but its only formal primitives Σ_k x^{p^k} + c do not lie in K⟨x⟩; on the Robba ring, by (a), every f with a_{−1} = 0 has a primitive in R (the closed-disc example is RD.0/completion-versus-overconvergence (b); it is used in RD.3/punctured-curve-boundary-acceptance).

<a id="target-rd-2-unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue"></a>

### Unipotent ∇-modules are the modules V ⊗ R with nilpotent residue

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue` · theorem

The following categories are equivalent: (a) finite-dimensional K-vector spaces V with a nilpotent endomorphism N; (b) log-∇-modules on the open unit disc A[0,1) with nilpotent residue whose restriction to A(0,1) is overconvergent; (c) unipotent ∇-modules over R_K (or over the ring of any aligned open annulus). The functor (a)→(c) sends (V,N) to V ⊗_K R_K with ∇ = d + N ⊗ dt/t; a quasi-inverse is M ↦ (V = ∪_{n≥0} ker D^n, N = D|_V) with D = t∇_{d/dt}. Moreover Hom and Ext^1 between F(V,N), F(V',N') are the kernel and cokernel of the induced nilpotent endomorphism of V^∨ ⊗ V', and H^0(F(V,N)) ≅ ker N, H^1(F(V,N)) ≅ coker N. For the tame base change t = s^e (p ∤ e), the pullback of F(V,N) is F(V, eN) up to isomorphism.

**Hypotheses.**

- Crew states (a)≃(c) for his Robba ring A (Proposition 6.7); Kedlaya's overview adds (b) (Proposition 4.5.3).

**Prerequisites.** [Unipotent ∇-modules over the Robba ring](#target-rd-2-unipotent-differential-module) (`RD.2/unipotent-differential-module`), [Residues and antiderivatives on the Robba ring](#target-rd-2-robba-ring-antiderivative) (`RD.2/robba-ring-antiderivative`), [Finite modules over Bézout domains: unimodular rows, saturated spans, freeness, Galois descent of saturated submodules](#target-rd-0-modules-over-bezout-domains) (`RD.0/modules-over-bezout-domains`), `mathlib:IsNilpotent`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Equivalence`.

**Sources.**

- [S8](#source-8), Proposition 4.5.3, pp. 21-22. Part (b).
- [S19](#source-19), Proposition 6.7, p. 737. Crew's equivalence (a)≃(c).

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a)→(c): V ⊗ R_K is a successive extension of trivial modules since N is nilpotent (Crew 6.6.3).
2. Full faithfulness and essential surjectivity by induction on length, comparing Ext groups: in (c) they are computed by the de Rham complex and Ext^1((R_K,d),(R_K,d)) = H^1(R_K) = K dt/t, the cokernel of t d/dt on R_K being K·1 (overview Example 4.1.11; RD.2/robba-ring-antiderivative) (Crew Proposition 6.7).
3. (b)↔(c): construct horizontal sections on discs by the operators Q_i(D) built from binomial polynomials, using overconvergence to control convergence (overview Proposition 4.5.3); descending from (b) to (c) is restriction.
4. Tame base change: find g with dg = (residue correction) and set C = exp(gN) (Crew Proposition 6.9).

**Checks.**

- For N = 0, F(V, 0) = V ⊗ (R_K, d) is constant; for V = K² and N = [[0,1],[0,0]], F(V,N) is SFR's Example 7.2.6 (∇e_2 = e_1 dt/t).

<a id="target-rd-2-quasi-unipotent-implies-overconvergent"></a>

### Quasi-unipotent ∇-modules are overconvergent

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/quasi-unipotent-implies-overconvergent` · lemma

Every quasi-unipotent ∇-module over R_K is overconvergent (solvable at the boundary).

**Hypotheses.**

- Overconvergent ∇-modules form an abelian subcategory stable under extensions (overview Definition 4.1.7, and the proof of Proposition 4.5.3).

**Prerequisites.** [Quasi-unipotent ∇-modules and (σ,∇)-modules](#target-rd-2-quasi-unipotent-differential-module) (`RD.2/quasi-unipotent-differential-module`), [A Frobenius structure forces generic radius 1 at the boundary (Dwork; Christol-Mebkhout)](#target-rd-1-frobenius-structure-forces-solvability) (`RD.1/frobenius-structure-forces-solvability`), [Finite étale extensions of R^int and the Robba rings R^L of finite separable extensions of k((t))](#target-rd-2-finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring) (`RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring`), [Constant and quasi-constant ∇-modules over the Robba ring](#target-rd-2-constant-and-quasi-constant-differential-module) (`RD.2/constant-and-quasi-constant-differential-module`).

**Sources.**

- [S8](#source-8), Remark 4.6.7, p. 26. Statement.

**Construction or proof.**

1. By RD.2/quasi-unipotent-differential-module, M has a filtration with quasi-constant quotients, so by stability under extensions it suffices to treat M quasi-constant.
2. A quasi-constant M becoming constant over a formally étale cover f : X → A[r,1) is a direct summand of a sum of copies of f_*O_X (overview Lemma 4.3.2 and proof of Proposition 4.4.3).
3. The Frobenius lift pulls back to X (overview Definition 6.1.1: 'a Frobenius lift pulls back to a Frobenius lift on any formally étale cover'), so f_*O_X carries a Frobenius structure and is overconvergent by RD.1/frobenius-structure-forces-solvability; direct summands of overconvergent modules are overconvergent (overview Remark 4.6.7).

**Checks.**

- Unipotent modules are overconvergent: the trivial module is, and overconvergence is stable under extensions.

<a id="target-rd-2-unramified-extensions-of-amice-rings"></a>

### Unramified extensions E_L, E†_L and the completed maximal unramified extension Ẽ of the Amice ring

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/unramified-extensions-of-amice-rings` · construction

Fix a separable closure k((t))^sep of k((t)) and put G = Gal(k((t))^sep/k((t))). (a) For each finite separable extension L ⊆ k((t))^sep of k((t)) there is a finite étale O_E-algebra O_{E_L}, unique up to unique isomorphism, with O_{E_L}/π ≅ L; E_L = O_{E_L}[1/π] is a complete discretely valued field with residue field L. Its integral elements overconvergent over R^int form the finite étale R^int-algebra R^int_L of RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring, and E†_L := R^int_L[1/π] = R^bd_L is the unique finite unramified extension of the henselian field E† with residue field L; moreover E_L = E ⊗_{E†} E†_L and E†_L is the integral closure of E† in E_L. (b) E^unr = ∪_L E_L and E^{†,unr} = ∪_L E†_L (union over finite separable L ⊆ k((t))^sep), and Ẽ is the π-adic completion of E^unr: a complete discretely valued field with residue field k((t))^sep. The Frobenius lift σ and the derivation d extend uniquely to O_{E_L}, R^int_L, E_L, E†_L, E^unr, E^{†,unr} and (by continuity) Ẽ, and G acts on all of them by continuous ring automorphisms commuting with σ and d, with fixed rings (E^unr)^{G_L} = E_L, (E^{†,unr})^{G_L} = E†_L, Ẽ^G = E and (E^{†,unr})^G = E†, where G_L = Gal(k((t))^sep/L). (c) Constants: the kernel of d on E†_L is the integral closure K_L of K in E†_L (a finite unramified extension of K whose residue field is the algebraic closure of k in L), and the kernel of d on Ẽ is the completion K̃ of the maximal unramified extension of K in Ẽ. (d) Frobenius invariants: if σ_K is absolute (it acts on k by x ↦ x^q) and its fixed field K_0 = K^{σ_K = 1} has residue field F_q and the same value group as K, then Ẽ^{σ=1} = K_0.

**Hypotheses.**

- K complete discretely valued of characteristic 0; L ranges over finite separable extensions of k((t)) inside one fixed separable closure. No perfectness of k is needed for (a)-(c); a purely inseparable residue extension k((t^{1/p}))/k((t)) has no étale lift.
- In (d) the hypotheses are those of Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, Proposition 19.1.5; without them Ẽ^{σ=1} can be smaller than K^{σ_K=1}·(unramified constants) and the coefficient field of the Fontaine-Katz equivalence changes.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/LocalMonodromy/AmiceUnramified`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Finite étale extensions of R^int and the Robba rings R^L of finite separable extensions of k((t))](#target-rd-2-finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring) (`RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring`), [The bounded Robba ring R^bd is a henselian discretely valued field with residue field k((t)); R^bd = R ∩ E](#target-rd-0-bounded-robba-ring) (`RD.0/bounded-robba-ring`), [The derivation d/dt on annulus rings, R, R^bd, R^int, O_E and E, its norm bounds and Ω^1 = R dt](#target-rd-0-derivation-on-robba-ring) (`RD.0/derivation-on-robba-ring`), [Weakly continuous Frobenius lifts on the integral Amice ring](#target-rd-0-frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring) (`RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring`), `mathlib:Field.absoluteGaloisGroup`, `mathlib:Algebra.Etale`, `mathlib:HenselianLocalRing`, `mathlib:IsGalois`.

**Sources.**

- [S57](#source-57), Definition 19.1.1, p. 314; Definition 19.2.1, p. 316; Lemma 15.1.3, p. 263. Defines E_L as the unramified extension of E with residue field L, Ẽ as the completion of the maximal unramified extension with its Galois action and fixed field E, and E†_L via the henselian property of E† (Lemma 15.1.3), with E_L = E ⊗_{E†} E†_L.
- [S57](#source-57), Chapter 19, Exercises (1) and (3), p. 325. Asks to prove Ẽ^{φ=1} = K_0 under the stated hypotheses on K_0, and that the kernel of d on Ẽ is K̃ and on E†_L the integral closure of K.
- [S8](#source-8), Proposition 3.5.5 and Definition 3.5.6, pp. 15-16. Finite étale covers of the thin annulus correspond to finite separable extensions of k((t)) by henselianity of R^int.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, Definition 19.1.2 and Definition 19.2.2: the rings in which a Galois representation is tensored before taking invariants
- RD.2/lang-trivialisation-of-unit-root-modules: Ẽ is the ring over which a unit-root Frobenius module acquires a basis of fixed vectors
- RD.2/tsuzuki-equivalence-finite-local-monodromy: E†_L is the ring over which a unit-root (σ,∇)-module becomes trivial
- RD.2/galois-representation-to-differential-module: the Galois action on E^{†,unr} and Ẽ produces D†(V) and D(V)

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AmiceRing.unramifiedExt` |  | E_L for a finite separable L/k((t)), with its integral ring O_{E_L} finite étale over O_E and residue field L. |
| `AmiceRing.boundedUnramifiedExt` |  | E†_L = R^bd_L, the finite unramified extension of E† with residue field L; E_L = E ⊗_{E†} E†_L. |
| `AmiceRing.completedMaxUnramified` |  | Ẽ, the π-adic completion of E^unr = ∪_L E_L, with residue field k((t))^sep. |
| `AmiceRing.frobeniusExt` |  | The unique extension of σ to E_L, E†_L and Ẽ; it commutes with the Galois action. |
| `AmiceRing.derivationExt` |  | The unique extension of d = d/dt to E_L, E†_L and Ẽ; it commutes with the Galois action. |
| `AmiceRing.galoisAction` |  | The continuous action of G = Gal(k((t))^sep/k((t))) on E^unr, E^{†,unr} and Ẽ by ring automorphisms. |
| `AmiceRing.fixedPoints` |  | Ẽ^G = E, (E^{†,unr})^G = E†, and E_L, E†_L are the fixed fields of G_L in E^unr, E^{†,unr}. |
| `AmiceRing.ker_derivation` |  | ker(d on E†_L) = K_L (integral closure of K) and ker(d on Ẽ) = K̃. |
| `AmiceRing.frobenius_invariants` |  | Under the hypotheses of (d), Ẽ^{σ=1} = K_0. |
| `AmiceRing.boundedUnramifiedExt_tensor_robba` |  | E†_L ⊗_{E†} R ≅ R^L compatibly with σ, d and the Galois action. |

**Unit tests.**

- `AmiceUnramifiedExt.self` (degenerate): For L = k((t)), E_L = E and E†_L = E†, and the Galois group of L/k((t)) is trivial.
- `AmiceUnramifiedExt.constant_field` (computation): For L = k'((t)) with k'/k finite separable of degree f, ker(d on E†_L) = K' with [K':K] = f and K'/K unramified.
- `AmiceUnramifiedExt.artinSchreier` (computation): With π_0^{p−1} = −p, the ring E†[u]/((1+π_0 u)^p − 1 − pπ_0 t^{−1}) is a field, unramified over E† of degree p, with residue field the Artin-Schreier extension ū^p − ū = −t^{−1}.
- `AmiceUnramifiedExt.compat_robba` (compatibility): E†_L ⊗_{E†} R = R^L, the Robba-ring extension of RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring, compatibly with σ and d.
- `AmiceUnramifiedExt.not_inseparable` (non-example): The purely inseparable extension k((t^{1/p}))/k((t)) is not of the form O_{E_L}/π: the reduction of a finite étale O_E-algebra is a finite étale, hence separable, k((t))-algebra.
- `AmiceUnramifiedExt.frob_invariants` (compatibility): For K = Q_q = W(F_q)[1/p] with σ_K the q-power Witt-vector Frobenius (the identity of Q_q) and σ(t) = t^q, Ẽ^{σ=1} = Q_q = K_0; for K = Q_q with σ_K the p-power Witt-vector Frobenius (q = p), Ẽ^{σ=1} = Q_p = K_0.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a) O_E is a complete discrete valuation ring with residue field k((t)) and R^int is henselian with the same residue field (RD.0/bounded-robba-ring (a)), so finite separable extensions of the residue field lift uniquely to finite étale algebras of either (Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, Lemma 15.1.3 and Definition 19.2.1); O_{E_L} is the π-adic completion of R^int_L, which gives E_L = E ⊗_{E†} E†_L, and the integral closure statement follows because R^int_L is normal and finite over R^int.
2. (b) Unique extension of σ and d: an étale algebra over a ring with an endomorphism or derivation carries a unique compatible extension (the residue map of σ is the q-power map, which extends to L because L/k((t)) is separable). G acts on E^unr by transport of structure through the equivalence between finite separable extensions of k((t)) and finite étale algebras, and continuously on the completion; fixed rings by Galois theory for finite étale algebras (Kedlaya, Definition 19.1.1, p. 314).
3. (c) A d-constant x of E†_L is integral over K: reduce to a field extension and use that d has kernel K on E† (power series with i·c_i = 0 for i ≠ 0, RD.0/derivation-on-robba-ring) and that d commutes with the trace of E†_L/E†; the kernel on Ẽ is Kedlaya, Exercise 19.3, p. 325.
4. (d) Kedlaya, Exercise 19.1, p. 325: reduce to residue fields, where the fixed field of the q-power map on k((t))^sep is F_q; the value-group hypothesis gives a uniformiser of K fixed by σ, so σ-invariant elements can be expanded π-adically with σ-invariant digits.

**Checks.**

- For L = k((t)): E_L = E, E†_L = E† and the Galois action is trivial.
- For an unramified L = k'((t)) with k'/k finite separable: E†_L = E† ⊗_K K' with K'/K unramified of residue field k', and ker(d) = K'.
- Artin-Schreier: if K contains π_0 with π_0^{p−1} = −p, then E†[u]/((1 + π_0 u)^p − 1 − pπ_0 t^{−1}) is the unramified extension E†_L for L = k((t))[ū]/(ū^p − ū + t^{−1}) (expand (1 + π_0 u)^p and divide by pπ_0; compare Kedlaya overview, proof of Lemma 5.4.7).

<a id="target-rd-2-c-constant-unit-root-module"></a>

### c-constant unit-root (σ,∇)-modules

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/c-constant-unit-root-module` · definition

For c ∈ (0, 1), a finite free differential module M over E† (or over E, or over E†_L for a finite separable L/k((t))) equipped with a unit-root Frobenius structure F relative to σ is c-constant if M has a basis on which F acts by a matrix A with entries in the integral ring and |A − I|_1 ≤ c, where |·|_1 is the 1-Gauss norm (the π-adic norm on E). Such a basis is a c-constant basis. Properties: (i) the property does not depend on the Frobenius lift: if σ_1, σ_2 are Frobenius lifts that agree on K, the Frobenius structure transported along the Taylor isomorphism of RD.1/change-of-frobenius-for-frobenius-structures is c-constant for σ_2 iff the original one is c-constant for σ_1; (ii) c-constancy is preserved by base change E† → E†_L → E_L, by tensor products and by duals, and c-constant implies c'-constant for c ≤ c' < 1; (iii) if σ is absolute and K_0 = K^{σ_K=1} satisfies the hypotheses of RD.2/unramified-extensions-of-amice-rings (d), then D(V) (RD.2/galois-representation-to-differential-module) is c-constant iff V_0 has a G-stable O_{K_0}-lattice whose supremum norm satisfies |τ(g)x − x| ≤ c|x| for all g ∈ G.

**Hypotheses.**

- The Frobenius structure is unit-root: there is a basis on which F acts by A ∈ GL_n(O_{E†}) (RD.1/frobenius-stable-lattices (a)).
- c is measured in the normalised absolute value of K extended to E by the 1-Gauss norm.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/LocalMonodromy/UnitRoot`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [(σ,∇)-modules (φ,∇)-modules over R, R^bd, R^int, E and dagger algebras; Frobenius structures](#target-rd-1-frobenius-differential-module) (`RD.1/frobenius-differential-module`), [Pure (isoclinic) and unit-root σ-modules over R, R^bd and E](#target-rd-1-isoclinic-frobenius-module) (`RD.1/isoclinic-frobenius-module`), [F-stable lattices: nonnegative generic slopes versus integral models](#target-rd-1-frobenius-stable-lattices) (`RD.1/frobenius-stable-lattices`), [Independence of the Frobenius lift: the Taylor isomorphism σ_1^*E ≅ σ_2^*E](#target-rd-1-change-of-frobenius-for-frobenius-structures) (`RD.1/change-of-frobenius-for-frobenius-structures`), [Unramified extensions E_L, E†_L and the completed maximal unramified extension Ẽ of the Amice ring](#target-rd-2-unramified-extensions-of-amice-rings) (`RD.2/unramified-extensions-of-amice-rings`), [The rank-one exponential connection (Dwork's exponential): radius, highest break 1, Swan conductor 1, unit-root Frobenius structure](#target-rd-1-dwork-exponential-module) (`RD.1/dwork-exponential-module`), [Dwork splitting-function overconvergence](#target-rd-1-dwork-overconvergence-proof) (`RD.1/dwork-overconvergence-proof`).

**Sources.**

- [S57](#source-57), Definition 19.3.2, p. 319. Defines c-constant modules and bases by |A − I|_1 ≤ c, notes invariance under change of absolute Frobenius lift via Corollary 17.3.2 and Proposition 19.1.5, and the characterisation through Galois representations.
- [S57](#source-57), Lemma 17.3.4 and Proposition 17.3.5, p. 297; Chapter 19, Exercise (5), p. 325. Integral lattices of unit-root modules are stable under D^i/i! (Lemma 17.3.4); Proposition 17.3.5 shows that purity survives a change of Frobenius lift, and Definition 19.3.2 says that imitating its proof gives the invariance of c-constancy for arbitrary lifts; the exercise asks for that invariance, through the Taylor formula (17.3.1.1).
- [S57](#source-57), Example 17.1.4 and Definition 17.1.3, p. 292. Dwork's module M_f with its Frobenius structure exp(π f − π φ(f)) and the Dwork exponential series of radius p^{(p−1)/p²}; that Frobenius structure fits the connection D(v) = −π(df/dt)v, not the printed D(v) = π(df/dt)v (source issue E-RD2-12).

**Uses and API requirements.**

- Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, Lemma 19.3.4: the hypothesis of the key lemma: c-constant with c < p^{−1/(p−1)} forces triviality
- RD.2/lang-trivialisation-of-unit-root-modules: the conclusion: every unit-root module becomes c-constant after a finite separable extension
- Kedlaya, A p-adic local monodromy theorem, Proposition 6.11: the condition v_p(A − I) > 1/(p − 1) on a Frobenius matrix is c-constancy with c < p^{−1/(p−1)}

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `IsCConstant` |  | The predicate: M has a basis with Frobenius matrix A integral and \|A − I\|_1 ≤ c. |
| `IsCConstant.mono` |  | c-constant ⇒ c'-constant for c ≤ c' < 1. |
| `IsCConstant.baseChange` |  | Preserved by E† → E†_L and E† → E. |
| `IsCConstant.tensor` |  | Preserved by tensor products. |
| `IsCConstant.dual` |  | Preserved by duals. |
| `IsCConstant.changeFrobenius` |  | Invariant under the change-of-Frobenius equivalence of RD.1/change-of-frobenius-for-frobenius-structures. |
| `IsCConstant.iff_galois` |  | Under the hypotheses of RD.2/unramified-extensions-of-amice-rings (d): D(V) is c-constant iff V_0 has a G-stable lattice on which G acts within c of the identity. |

**Unit tests.**

- `IsCConstant.trivial` (degenerate): The trivial (σ,∇)-module (E†, d, σ) is c-constant for every c ∈ (0,1).
- `IsCConstant.rankOne_const` (computation): The rank-one module E† e with F(e) = (1 + π^m) e and ∇e = 0 is |π|^m-constant.
- `IsCConstant.dwork_threshold` (non-example): Dwork's module M_f (f = t^{−1}, K = Q_p(π_0), σ(t) = t^p) is p^{−1/(p−1)}-constant but not c-constant for any c < p^{−1/(p−1)}.
- `IsCConstant.tensor` (characterisation): If M and M' are c-constant then so are M ⊗ M' and M^∨.
- `IsCConstant.frobenius_change` (compatibility): For σ_1(t) = t^q and σ_2(t) = t^q(1 + πt^{−1}), M is c-constant for σ_1 iff the transported structure is c-constant for σ_2.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (i) Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, Definition 19.3.2 and Exercise (5) of Chapter 19: in Lemma 17.3.4, the integral lattice M_0 spanned by a basis on which F acts integrally is stable under D^i/i!, and if D/i acts with norm at most c on a suitable basis so does D^i/i!; inserting this into the Taylor formula (17.3.1.1) for the transported Frobenius structure gives a matrix A' with |A' − I|_1 ≤ c (|σ_2(t) − σ_1(t)|_1 < 1).
2. (ii) Base change keeps the same basis; for tensor products A ⊗ B − I = (A − I) ⊗ B + I ⊗ (B − I) and for duals (A^T)^{-1} − I = −(A^T)^{-1}(A − I)^T, with |A^{-1}|_1 = 1.
3. (iii) Kedlaya, Definition 19.3.2: through the Fontaine-Katz equivalence (RD.2/fontaine-katz-unit-root-equivalence), a c-constant basis of D(V) corresponds to a G-stable lattice of V_0 on which G acts by matrices congruent to I to within c.

**Checks.**

- The trivial module (E†, d) with F = σ is c-constant for every c: A = (1).
- Rank one: M = E† e with F(e) = a e, ∇e = 0 and a ∈ 1 + π^m O_K is |π|^m-constant (the compatibility N a + t da/dt = q a σ(N) holds with N = 0 because a is constant).
- Dwork's module (K = Q_p(π_0), π_0^{p−1} = −p, σ_K = id, σ(t) = t^p): M_f = E† v with ∇v = −π_0 (df/dt) v ⊗ dt, f = t^{−1}, and F(v) = E(t^{−1}) v with E(z) = exp(π_0(z − z^p)) = Σ λ_n z^n the Dwork exponential (this sign of the connection is the one that matches F; Kedlaya's Example 17.1.4 prints +π_0, source issue E-RD2-12; the dual module is E_π of RD.1/dwork-exponential-module, with F = E(t^{−1})^{−1}); since λ_n ∈ Z_p[π_0] with λ_1 = π_0 and ord_p λ_n ≥ n(p − 1)/p² > 0 for n ≥ 1 (RD.1/dwork-overconvergence-proof, RD.1/dwork-exponential-module), E(t^{−1}) ≡ 1 (mod π_0) and |E(t^{−1}) − 1|_1 = |π_0| = p^{−1/(p−1)}, so M_f is p^{−1/(p−1)}-constant; it is not trivial over E† (its horizontal section exp(π_0 t^{−1})v does not converge near |t| = 1), hence by RD.2/small-constant-unit-root-module-is-trivial it is not c-constant for any c < p^{−1/(p−1)}: the threshold is sharp.

<a id="target-rd-2-lang-trivialisation-of-unit-root-modules"></a>

### Unit-root Frobenius modules are trivialised over Ẽ, and become c-constant over a finite separable extension

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/lang-trivialisation-of-unit-root-modules` · lemma

Setting of RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring: K is complete for a discrete valuation, of characteristic 0, with ring of integers O_K, uniformiser π and residue field k of characteristic p; σ is a Frobenius lift on R^int (a ring endomorphism extending a q-power Frobenius lift σ_K of K and reducing to the absolute q-power map x ↦ x^q of k((t))), q = p^a; E = O_E[1/π] is the Amice ring and E† = R^bd the bounded Robba ring, both with d = d/dt. Let M_0 be a finite free R^int-module (or O_E-module) of rank n with a σ-semilinear F whose linearisation σ^*M_0 → M_0 is an isomorphism (an étale lattice of a unit-root σ-module). Then: (a) M_0 ⊗ O_Ẽ has a basis of F-fixed vectors, and (M_0 ⊗ O_Ẽ)^{F=1} is a free module of rank n over O_Ẽ^{σ=1}; (b) for each m ≥ 1 the set of F-fixed vectors of M_0 ⊗ O_Ẽ/π^m is finite, and each of them is fixed by an open subgroup of G; (c) consequently, for each m ≥ 1 there is a finite Galois extension L of k((t)) such that M_0 ⊗ R^int_L has a basis on which F acts by a matrix A ≡ I (mod π^m). In particular every unit-root (σ,∇)-module M over E† becomes c-constant (RD.2/c-constant-unit-root-module) over E†_L for any prescribed c ∈ (0,1) and a suitable finite separable L/k((t)) depending on c.

**Hypotheses.**

- Only the residual behaviour of σ is used: its reduction is the q-power map of k((t)), which extends to the q-power map of the separably closed field k((t))^sep. No perfectness of k and no condition on σ_K are needed.
- A unit-root σ-module over E† has an étale R^int-lattice (RD.1/frobenius-stable-lattices (a)).

**Prerequisites.** [Unramified extensions E_L, E†_L and the completed maximal unramified extension Ẽ of the Amice ring](#target-rd-2-unramified-extensions-of-amice-rings) (`RD.2/unramified-extensions-of-amice-rings`), [c-constant unit-root (σ,∇)-modules](#target-rd-2-c-constant-unit-root-module) (`RD.2/c-constant-unit-root-module`), [F-stable lattices: nonnegative generic slopes versus integral models](#target-rd-1-frobenius-stable-lattices) (`RD.1/frobenius-stable-lattices`), [Pure (isoclinic) and unit-root σ-modules over R, R^bd and E](#target-rd-1-isoclinic-frobenius-module) (`RD.1/isoclinic-frobenius-module`), `FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4/etale-phi-modules-cohen-ring`.

**Sources.**

- [S57](#source-57), Proposition 19.1.5 and its proof, pp. 315-316; Theorem 14.6.3 (first part of the proof), p. 256. Over Ẽ a unit-root difference module is trivial because the residue field of Ẽ is separably closed, hence weakly difference-closed for absolute Frobenius lifts; this gives the inverse functor (D ⊗ Ẽ)^{φ=1}.
- [S57](#source-57), Proof of Theorem 19.3.1, p. 321. Uses Proposition 19.1.5 to choose a finite separable L over which M becomes c-constant for some c < p^{−1/(p−1)}.
- [S1](#source-1), Proposition 6.11, statement, p. 79 (arXiv v4). Tsuzuki's conclusion is stated for any finite extension on which the Frobenius matrix satisfies v_p(A − I) > 1/(p − 1), and the statement adds that such an extension can be chosen separable (k perfect) or nearly separable (k imperfect); the proof shows only that the horizontal sections descend to a (nearly) separable extension and never constructs an extension with v_p(A − I) > 1/(p − 1). This lemma supplies one.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Modulo π: M_0/π is an étale q-power Frobenius module over k((t)); over k((t))^sep its F-fixed vectors span and form an F_q-space of dimension n (Lang's theorem; the p-power, Z_p-coefficient case is FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4/etale-phi-modules-cohen-ring (i), and the q-power case is the same argument applied to F, whose fixed-point equations X^{(q)} = A^{−1}X are étale of degree q^n).
2. Lifting: if v is F-fixed modulo π^j, write F v − v = π^j w; a correction v + π^j y is F-fixed modulo π^{j+1} iff ȳ − ū^j·F̄(ȳ) = w̄ modulo π, where σ(π) = uπ (indeed F(v + π^j y) − v − π^j y = π^j(w + u^j F(y) − y)); in coordinates this is a system x − c·x^{(q)} = b over k((t))^sep, separable (derivative 1) and solvable with finitely many solutions. Completeness of O_Ẽ gives F-fixed lifts and Nakayama's lemma gives a basis (a); this is Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, proof of Proposition 19.1.5 (via the first part of Theorem 14.6.3, the residue field of Ẽ being separably closed).
3. (b) Each level is cut out by finitely many étale polynomial equations, so the solutions are finite in number and algebraic and separable over k((t)); hence each is fixed by an open subgroup of G.
4. (c) Let L be the Galois closure of the field generated by the coordinates of an F-fixed basis modulo π^m. Since R^int_L/π^m = O_{E_L}/π^m (RD.2/unramified-extensions-of-amice-rings (a)), the basis lifts to a basis of M_0 ⊗ R^int_L, on which F acts by A ≡ I (mod π^m). Choose m with |π|^m ≤ c (Kedlaya, proof of Theorem 19.3.1, p. 321, where L is chosen to make M c-constant).

**Checks.**

- Rank one: for M_0 = R^int e with F(e) = a e, a ∈ (R^int)^×, a fixed vector b e needs b^{−1}σ(b) = a^{−1}; modulo π this is b̄^{q−1} = ā^{−1}, solvable over the finite separable extension k((t))(b̄) (the polynomial x^{q−1} − ā^{−1} is separable).
- Dwork's module M_f (f = t^{−1}, K = Q_p(π_0), π_0^{p−1} = −p) is p^{−1/(p−1)}-constant over E† itself and becomes trivial, hence c-constant for every c, over E†_L for the Artin-Schreier extension L of z^p − z = t^{−1} (RD.2/dwork-exponential-artin-schreier-example).

<a id="target-rd-2-unit-root-matrix-normal-form"></a>

### Normal form of the matrices of a unit-root (σ,∇)-module for a standard Frobenius lift

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/unit-root-matrix-normal-form` · lemma

Let σ be a standard Frobenius lift on E† (σ(t) = t^q; σ_K arbitrary) and M a finite free differential module over E† with a unit-root Frobenius structure. Then there is an integer m ≥ 1 prime to p such that M ⊗_{E†} E†[t^{1/m}] has a basis on which the matrices A, A^{−1} of F and N of t·d/dt have entries in E†[t^{1/m}] ∩ O_K⟦t^{−1/m}⟧ (power series in t^{−1/m} with integral coefficients and no positive powers of t). If M is c-constant for some c < 1 (RD.2/c-constant-unit-root-module), one may take m = 1 and keep |A − I|_1 ≤ c.

**Hypotheses.**

- σ standard: σ(t) = t^q and σ extends σ_K on K; the Frobenius structure is unit-root (a basis with A ∈ GL_n(O_{E†}) exists).
- E†[t^{1/m}] is the bounded Robba ring in the variable t^{1/m}, a tamely ramified extension of E†.

**Prerequisites.** [c-constant unit-root (σ,∇)-modules](#target-rd-2-c-constant-unit-root-module) (`RD.2/c-constant-unit-root-module`), [F-stable lattices: nonnegative generic slopes versus integral models](#target-rd-1-frobenius-stable-lattices) (`RD.1/frobenius-stable-lattices`), [(σ,∇)-modules (φ,∇)-modules over R, R^bd, R^int, E and dagger algebras; Frobenius structures](#target-rd-1-frobenius-differential-module) (`RD.1/frobenius-differential-module`), [The bounded Robba ring R^bd is a henselian discretely valued field with residue field k((t)); R^bd = R ∩ E](#target-rd-0-bounded-robba-ring) (`RD.0/bounded-robba-ring`).

**Sources.**

- [S57](#source-57), Lemma 19.3.3 and proof, pp. 319-320. Normal form of A, A^{−1}, N with entries in E†[t^{1/m}] ∩ o_K⟦t^{−1/m}⟧, and m = 1 with |A − I|_1 ≤ c in the c-constant case.
- [S57](#source-57), Remark 17.1.2, (17.1.2.1), p. 292. The compatibility N A + t dA/dt = (t/φ(t))(dφ(t)/dt) A φ(N) for the derivation t d/dt.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Choose a basis on which A ∈ GL_n(O_{E†}) (RD.1/frobenius-stable-lattices (a)); reorder so that the minimum t-adic valuation of the reduction of the entries occurs in position (1,1), adjoin t^{1/(q−1)} and rescale to make it 0, then eliminate the rest of the first column; proceeding inductively makes A upper triangular and invertible over k⟦t^{1/m}⟧ modulo π (Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, Lemma 19.3.3, first paragraph of the proof).
2. Write A = Σ_i A_i t^{i/m}; repeatedly replace A by U^{−1} A σ(U) with U = I + A_0^{−1} Σ_{i>0} A_i t^{i/m}; the U converge to the identity in the (t^{1/m}, m_K)-adic topology, removing positive powers of t (if M is c-constant start here with m = 1, which preserves |A − I|_1 ≤ c).
3. The compatibility N A + t dA/dt = q A σ(N) (Kedlaya (17.1.2.1) for σ(t) = t^q), i.e. N − q A σ(N) A^{−1} = −t (dA/dt) A^{−1} (the proof of Lemma 19.3.3 prints the right side without its minus sign, source issue E-RD2-10), then forces N to have only nonpositive powers of t: first modulo q, then modulo q^2, q^3, and so on.

**Checks.**

- The trivial module: m = 1, A = I, N = 0.
- Dwork's module M_f, f = t^{−1}: A = E(t^{−1}) and N = π_0 t^{−1} (t·d/dt acts by π_0 t^{−1} for ∇v = π_0 t^{−2} v ⊗ dt, the sign of E-RD2-12) already lie in E† ∩ O_K⟦t^{−1}⟧ with m = 1.

<a id="target-rd-2-dwork-transfer-to-the-centre-of-a-disc"></a>

### Dwork's transfer theorem: the radius of convergence at the centre of a disc is at least the generic radius

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/dwork-transfer-to-the-centre-of-a-disc` · theorem

Let K be complete nonarchimedean of characteristic 0 with residue characteristic p, β > 0, and M a nonzero finite free differential module (for d/dt) over the ring K⟨t/β⟩ of power series converging on the closed disc |t| ≤ β, or over the ring of functions on the open disc |t| < β. Let R(M ⊗ F_β) be the generic radius of convergence of M at radius β (RD.1/generic-radius). Then for every λ < min{β, R(M ⊗ F_β)}, M ⊗ K⟨t/λ⟩ has a basis of horizontal sections; equivalently the fundamental solution matrix at t = 0 and its inverse converge on the open disc of radius min{β, R(M ⊗ F_β)}: the radius of convergence of M at 0 is at least its generic radius.

**Hypotheses.**

- Characteristic 0 is needed to form the Taylor series Σ (−t)^i/i! D^i(x).
- For the open disc one applies the statement to the restrictions to closed discs of radius β' < β and lets β' → β, using continuity of the generic radius (RD.1/generic-radius-basic-properties (d)).

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/DifferentialModules/Transfer`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Generic radius of convergence R(E, ρ), intrinsic radius T(E, ρ) and subsidiary radii](#target-rd-1-generic-radius) (`RD.1/generic-radius`), [Spectral norm of ∂ on a differential module over a complete nonarchimedean differential field](#target-rd-1-spectral-norm-of-differential-module) (`RD.1/spectral-norm-of-differential-module`), [The generic radius is the radius of convergence of horizontal sections at a generic point (Dwork transfer)](#target-rd-1-dwork-transfer-generic-disc) (`RD.1/dwork-transfer-generic-disc`), [Basic properties of generic radii: exact sequences, duals, tensor products, log-concavity, continuity, invariance](#target-rd-1-generic-radius-basic-properties) (`RD.1/generic-radius-basic-properties`), [Differential (∇-)modules over annuli, the Robba ring and differential fields](#target-rd-1-differential-module) (`RD.1/differential-module`).

**Sources.**

- [S57](#source-57), Theorem 9.6.1 and proof, pp. 158-159. Dwork's transfer theorem: R(M) ≥ R(M ⊗ F_β) for a nonzero finite differential module over the closed or open disc of radius β, proved by convergence of the Taylor series of horizontal sections.
- [S57](#source-57), Definition 9.4.4, p. 156. The generic radius R(V) = ω|D|_{sp,V}^{−1} of a nonzero finite differential module over F_ρ or E; the definition sets R = ρ for the zero module, and the trivial module also has R = ρ because |d|_{sp,F_ρ} = ω/ρ.
- [S8](#source-8), Proposition 5.2.3, pp. 29-30. The generic-point form: R(E, ρ) ≥ r iff E has a basis of horizontal sections on discs of radius r around points (or a generic point) of the circle |t| = ρ.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Fix λ < β with λ < ω|D|_{sp,M}^{−1}, ω = p^{−1/(p−1)}, and a supremum norm on M compatible with |·|_λ. Choose ε > 0 with λω^{−1}(|D|_{sp,M} + ε) < 1; there is c > 0 with |D^i(x)| ≤ c(|D|_{sp,M} + ε)^i |x| for all i (Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, Lemma 6.1.8), so the Taylor series y = Σ_i ((−t)^i/i!) D^i(x) converges in M ⊗ K⟨t/λ⟩ since |1/i!| ≤ ω^{−i}.
2. Differentiating term by term gives D(y) = 0. Applied to a basis of M this yields horizontal sections whose reductions modulo t form a basis, hence a horizontal basis of M ⊗ K⟨t/λ⟩ (a finite differential module over the disc is free and a set of sections whose values at 0 are a basis is a basis: Kedlaya, Proposition 9.1.2).
3. The spectral norm |D|_{sp,M} is computed after base change to F_β (RD.1/spectral-norm-of-differential-module), which is the definition of the generic radius R(M ⊗ F_β) = ω|D|_{sp}^{−1} (Kedlaya, Definition 9.4.4).

**Checks.**

- Trivial module: R(M ⊗ F_β) = ω|d|_{sp,F_β}^{−1} = β, since |d|_{sp,F_β} = ω/β (Kedlaya, Definition 9.4.4), and the horizontal sections are constants.
- The exponential module D(v) = v (horizontal section e^{−t}v): R(M ⊗ F_β) = min{β, ω} and e^{−t} converges exactly on |t| < ω = p^{−1/(p−1)}, so the bound is attained.
- Generic-disc form: RD.1/dwork-transfer-generic-disc states the same convergence for discs centred at generic points of the circle |t| = β; this node transfers it to the centre.

<a id="target-rd-2-small-constant-unit-root-module-is-trivial"></a>

### A c-constant unit-root (σ,∇)-module with c < p^{−1/(p−1)} is trivial (the key lemma of Tsuzuki's theorem)

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/small-constant-unit-root-module-is-trivial` · lemma

Let M be a finite free differential module over E† (resp. over E†_L for a finite separable L/k((t)) whose residue field is separable over k, so that E†_L is a bounded Robba ring over the unramified extension K_L of K in a parameter u) with a unit-root Frobenius structure. If M is c-constant (RD.2/c-constant-unit-root-module) for some c < p^{−1/(p−1)}, then M is trivial as a differential module: M has a basis of horizontal sections over E† (resp. E†_L). The space H^0(M) of horizontal sections is F-stable, so it is a unit-root Frobenius module over K (resp. K_L) of dimension rank M.

**Hypotheses.**

- The bound c < p^{−1/(p−1)} is sharp: Dwork's module M_f, f = t^{−1}, is p^{−1/(p−1)}-constant and not trivial over E† (RD.2/c-constant-unit-root-module, acceptance).
- K complete discretely valued of characteristic 0; any Frobenius lift (c-constancy does not depend on it).

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/LocalMonodromy/UnitRoot`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [c-constant unit-root (σ,∇)-modules](#target-rd-2-c-constant-unit-root-module) (`RD.2/c-constant-unit-root-module`), [Normal form of the matrices of a unit-root (σ,∇)-module for a standard Frobenius lift](#target-rd-2-unit-root-matrix-normal-form) (`RD.2/unit-root-matrix-normal-form`), [Dwork's transfer theorem: the radius of convergence at the centre of a disc is at least the generic radius](#target-rd-2-dwork-transfer-to-the-centre-of-a-disc) (`RD.2/dwork-transfer-to-the-centre-of-a-disc`), [Spectral norm of ∂ on a differential module over a complete nonarchimedean differential field](#target-rd-1-spectral-norm-of-differential-module) (`RD.1/spectral-norm-of-differential-module`), [Generic radius of convergence R(E, ρ), intrinsic radius T(E, ρ) and subsidiary radii](#target-rd-1-generic-radius) (`RD.1/generic-radius`), [(σ,∇)-modules (φ,∇)-modules over R, R^bd, R^int, E and dagger algebras; Frobenius structures](#target-rd-1-frobenius-differential-module) (`RD.1/frobenius-differential-module`), [Finite étale extensions of R^int and the Robba rings R^L of finite separable extensions of k((t))](#target-rd-2-finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring) (`RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring`).

**Sources.**

- [S57](#source-57), Lemma 19.3.4 and proof, pp. 320-321. A finite differential module over E† with unit-root Frobenius structure that is c-constant for some c < p^{−1/(p−1)} is trivial; proof by Lemma 19.3.3, the Frobenius descent of Lemma 18.2.3, Proposition 8.2.3, Theorem 6.5.3 and Theorem 9.6.1.
- [S57](#source-57), Lemma 18.2.3 and proof, pp. 303-304. Construction of the matrix V with V_i = 0 for p | i solving N_0 V_i − V_i N_0 + i V_i = −(N_W)_i, which makes the system a function of t^p.
- [S57](#source-57), Proposition 8.2.3, p. 138; Theorem 6.5.3, p. 106. Log-convexity and continuity of ρ ↦ |x|_ρ; the Christol-Dwork formula for the spectral norm of a twisted polynomial (an equality, used here as an upper bound).
- [S1](#source-1), Proposition 6.11, p. 79 (arXiv v4). States the conclusion (kernel of ∇ of full rank and F-stable) under v_p(A − I) > 1/(p − 1), citing Tsuzuki for k algebraically closed and q = p.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Reduce to a standard Frobenius lift σ(t) = t^q (c-constancy is invariant under change of Frobenius, RD.2/c-constant-unit-root-module (i)); by RD.2/unit-root-matrix-normal-form choose a c-constant basis on which F and t·d/dt act by A, N with entries in E† ∩ O_K⟦t^{−1}⟧.
2. The compatibility N A + t dA/dt = q A σ(N) and |A_0| = |A_0^{−1}| = |A|_1 = |A^{−1}|_1 = 1 force N_0 = 0 and |N|_1 ≤ c, so |N|_α ≤ 1 for some α ∈ (0, 1) (A and N then define a module on the region |t^{−1}| ≤ α^{−1}).
3. Frobenius descent of the system (Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, construction in the proof of Lemma 18.2.3): build V with entries in E† ∩ K⟦t^{−1}⟧, |V − I|_1 ≤ c, |V − I|_α ≤ 1, such that A' = V^{−1} A σ(V) and N' = V^{−1} N V + V^{−1} t dV/dt are power series in t^{−p}; substitute t^{−p} ↦ t^{−1} (ψ commutes with the standard σ) and divide N by p: the new pair still satisfies the compatibility, |A'' − I|_1 ≤ c, |N''|_1 ≤ c and |N''|_{α^p} ≤ p.
4. Log-convexity of ρ ↦ |N''|_ρ in log ρ (Hadamard three circles for Gauss norms of matrices over the ring of the annulus, Kedlaya Proposition 8.2.3(c), a routine property of Laurent series) interpolating between |N''|_1 ≤ c and |N''|_{α^p} ≤ p gives |N''|_β ≤ 1 with log β = (p log c/(log c − log p)) log α; since p log c < log c − log p < 0 this improves α by a fixed factor > 1 in −log, so iterating makes α < p^{−1/(p−1)}.
5. Then the module M' on the disc |t^{−1}| < α^{−1} with t^{−1} d/dt^{−1} acting by −N has spectral norm of d/dt^{−1} at most α (RD.1/spectral-norm-of-differential-module, Kedlaya Theorem 6.5.3), hence generic radius at radius α^{−1} at least p^{−1/(p−1)}α^{−1} > 1, so by RD.2/dwork-transfer-to-the-centre-of-a-disc its horizontal sections at t^{−1} = 0 converge on a disc of radius > 1 in t^{−1}; restricting to an annulus near |t| = 1 gives a horizontal basis of M (Kedlaya, Lemma 19.3.4).
6. F-stability of H^0(M): F maps horizontal sections to horizontal sections because ∇∘F = (F ⊗ dσ)∘∇.

**Checks.**

- Kedlaya, Proposition 6.11 (arXiv:math/0110124 v4, p. 79) assumes exactly a basis with v_p(A − I) > 1/(p−1), i.e. c-constancy with c < p^{−1/(p−1)}, and concludes that ker ∇ has full rank: this node is a public proof of that step, replacing the citation of Tsuzuki (Amer. J. Math. 120 (1998), Theorem 5.1.1).
- Rank one with A = 1 + π^m a, a ∈ O_{E†}, |π|^m < p^{−1/(p−1)}: the horizontal generator exists over E† itself.

<a id="target-rd-2-galois-representation-to-differential-module"></a>

### Unit-root differential modules D(V), D†(V) attached to Galois representations; finite local monodromy

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/galois-representation-to-differential-module` · construction

Let V be a finite-dimensional K-vector space and τ : G = Gal(k((t))^sep/k((t))) → GL(V) a continuous homomorphism. (a) (p-adic topology) D(V) := (V ⊗_K Ẽ)^G, with G acting diagonally, is an E-vector space of dimension dim_K V and D(V) ⊗_E Ẽ → V ⊗_K Ẽ is an isomorphism; d acting on the second factor makes D(V) a differential module over E, and any σ_K-semilinear bijection of V commuting with τ (for instance the one fixing a chosen basis) makes it a unit-root (σ,∇)-module for any Frobenius lift σ acting on K by σ_K. (b) (finite image) If τ factors through Gal(L/k((t))) for a finite Galois L, then D†(V) := (V ⊗_K E†_L)^G is an E†-vector space of dimension dim V, canonically independent of L, with D†(V) ⊗ E†_L ≅ V ⊗ E†_L and D†(V) ⊗_{E†} E = D(V); it is a unit-root (σ,∇)-module over E†. (c) τ has finite local monodromy if the image of the inertia subgroup I = Gal(k((t))^sep/k^sep((t))) is finite; then D†(V) is defined by the same formula with E^{†,sep} (the bounded Robba ring over the completion K̂^unr of the maximal unramified extension of K, in the variable t, with its unramified extensions) in place of E†_L, and is again a unit-root (σ,∇)-module over E† of rank dim V. (d) D†(V) is solvable at 1: its generic radius tends to 1 (RD.1/frobenius-structure-forces-solvability). (e) The horizontal sections of D†(V) ⊗_{E†} E†_L are V ⊗_K K_L (K_L = ker d on E†_L), so the differential structure recovers the restriction of V to inertia but not V itself.

**Hypotheses.**

- K complete discretely valued of characteristic 0; V finite-dimensional; τ continuous for the p-adic topology in (a), and with finite image (resp. finite image of inertia) in (b) (resp. (c)).
- The Frobenius structure on D(V) comes from a chosen σ_K-semilinear structure on V; the differential structure needs no choice.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/LocalMonodromy/UnitRoot`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Unramified extensions E_L, E†_L and the completed maximal unramified extension Ẽ of the Amice ring](#target-rd-2-unramified-extensions-of-amice-rings) (`RD.2/unramified-extensions-of-amice-rings`), [(σ,∇)-modules (φ,∇)-modules over R, R^bd, R^int, E and dagger algebras; Frobenius structures](#target-rd-1-frobenius-differential-module) (`RD.1/frobenius-differential-module`), [A Frobenius structure forces generic radius 1 at the boundary (Dwork; Christol-Mebkhout)](#target-rd-1-frobenius-structure-forces-solvability) (`RD.1/frobenius-structure-forces-solvability`), `tauceti:TauCeti.GaloisDescent.span_invariants_eq_top`, `tauceti:TauCeti.GaloisDescent.liftBaseChange_injective_of_invariant`, `mathlib:Field.absoluteGaloisGroup`, `mathlib:Representation`.

**Sources.**

- [S57](#source-57), Definitions 19.1.2 and 19.1.4, Lemma 19.1.3, pp. 314-315. D(V) as Galois invariants of V ⊗ Ẽ, its dimension by Hilbert-Noether and lattices, and the induced differential and Frobenius structures.
- [S57](#source-57), Definitions 19.2.2, 19.2.4 and 19.2.8, Lemma 19.2.3, Proposition 19.2.5, Example 19.2.6, Remark 19.2.7, pp. 317-318. D†(V) for finite image and for finite local monodromy, its solvability at 1, the Artin-Schreier example and the recovery of the inertia restriction from horizontal sections.
- [S3](#source-3), Remark 3.10, p. 7. The local models: unit-root objects over k((t)) correspond to p-adic representations of G_{k((t))}, overconvergent ones to those with finite image of inertia (Tsuzuki).

**Uses and API requirements.**

- RD.2/tsuzuki-equivalence-finite-local-monodromy: D† is the functor of Tsuzuki's equivalence
- RD.2/irregularity-equals-swan-conductor: the generic radius of D†(V) is computed from the upper ramification breaks of V
- Kedlaya, Notes on isocrystals, Theorems 3.7 and 3.9: local model of the Katz-Crew and Tsuzuki correspondences for unit-root F-isocrystals

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unitRootModule` |  | D(V) = (V ⊗ Ẽ)^G, a unit-root (σ,∇)-module over E. |
| `overconvergentUnitRootModule` |  | D†(V) = (V ⊗ E^{†,sep,unr})^G for V with finite local monodromy. |
| `HasFiniteLocalMonodromy` |  | τ(I) is finite. |
| `unitRootModule.finrank` |  | dim D(V) = dim V and D†(V) has rank dim V. |
| `unitRootModule.comparison` |  | D(V) ⊗_E Ẽ ≅ V ⊗_K Ẽ, compatibly with G, d and the Frobenius structures. |
| `overconvergentUnitRootModule.baseChange` |  | D†(V) ⊗_{E†} E ≅ D(V). |
| `unitRootModule.map` |  | D and D† are exact K-linear tensor functors. |
| `overconvergentUnitRootModule.solvable` |  | D†(V) is solvable at 1. |
| `overconvergentUnitRootModule.horizontalSections` |  | H^0(D†(V) ⊗ E†_L) = V ⊗_K K_L for L trivialising τ on inertia. |

**Unit tests.**

- `unitRootModule.trivial` (degenerate): For the trivial one-dimensional representation, D(V) = E and D†(V) = E† with F = σ and ∇ = d.
- `unitRootModule.finrank` (characterisation): dim_E D(V) = dim_K V and D(V) ⊗_E Ẽ ≅ V ⊗_K Ẽ.
- `unitRootModule.artinSchreier` (computation): For the Artin-Schreier character of z^p − z = t^{−1} with value ζ_p on z ↦ z+1, D†(V) ≅ M_f with f = t^{−1}: ∇v = −π_0 (df/dt) v ⊗ dt = π_0 t^{−2} v ⊗ dt. Indeed, with (1 + π_0 u)^p = 1 + pπ_0 t^{−1} and z = −ū, the automorphism z ↦ z + 1 multiplies 1 + π_0 u by ζ_p, so D†(V) is spanned by (1 + π_0 u)^{−1}, whose connection form π_0 t^{−2}(1 + pπ_0 t^{−1})^{−1} dt is isomorphic to π_0 t^{−2} dt near |t| = 1.
- `unitRootModule.horizontal_sections` (compatibility): For τ trivial on Gal(k((t))^sep/L), the horizontal sections of D†(V) ⊗ E†_L form V ⊗_K K_L, of dimension dim V over K_L.
- `unitRootModule.not_overconvergent` (non-example): For p odd let χ: G → Z_p^× be the composite of the Artin-Schreier-Witt Z_p-extension of k((t)) attached to the Witt vector (t^{−1}, 0, 0, …) with x ↦ (1 + p)^x; χ has infinite image of inertia, and D(χ) is not the base change to E of any unit-root (σ,∇)-module over E† (RD.2/tsuzuki-equivalence-finite-local-monodromy).

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a) Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, Lemma 19.1.3: for finite image, Hilbert-Noether descent for the finite Galois extension E_L/E (Tau Ceti's semilinear Galois descent: invariant vectors span, TauCeti.GaloisDescent.span_invariants_eq_top, and stay independent, TauCeti.GaloisDescent.liftBaseChange_injective_of_invariant); in general choose a G-stable O_K-lattice T (compactness), apply the finite case to each T/m^i and pass to the inverse limit.
2. Differential and Frobenius structures: d and σ extend uniquely to Ẽ and commute with G (RD.2/unramified-extensions-of-amice-rings (b)); they preserve invariants; the compatibility ∇∘F = (F ⊗ dσ)∘∇ holds on V ⊗ Ẽ because d kills V and σ is a ring map (Definition 19.1.4).
3. (b) Same descent for E†_L/E† (Lemma 19.2.3); independence of L because enlarging L does not change invariants.
4. (c) Definition 19.2.8, which states the result without proof. Choose a finite Galois L/k((t)) with τ(I ∩ G_L) = 1 (possible because τ(I) is finite), so that τ restricted to G_L is unramified: it factors through G_L/(I ∩ G_L) = Gal(k^sep/k_L), k_L the residue field of L. The group Gal(k^sep/k_L) is infinite, so finite descent does not apply to it; instead the lattice argument of Lemma 19.1.3 for the complete field K̂^unr (a G_L-stable O_K-lattice, Hilbert-Noether descent modulo each power of π, passage to the limit) shows that V' = (V ⊗_K K̂^unr)^{G_L} is a K_L-form of V ⊗_K K̂^unr. Hence (V ⊗ E^{†,sep,unr})^{G_L} = V' ⊗_{K_L} E†_L, using (E^{†,sep,unr})^{G_L} = E†_L (coefficientwise Galois descent), and Hilbert-Noether descent for the finite group Gal(L/k((t))) acting on E†_L, as in (b), gives D†(V) of dimension dim V over E†.
5. (d) Proposition 19.2.5: the Frobenius structure forces generic radius 1 (Theorem 17.2.1 = RD.1/frobenius-structure-forces-solvability).
6. (e) Remark 19.2.7, using ker(d on E†_L) = K_L (RD.2/unramified-extensions-of-amice-rings (c)).

**Checks.**

- Trivial V = K: D(V) = E and D†(V) = E† with F = σ and ∇ = d.
- Artin-Schreier character (Kedlaya Example 19.2.6): with π_0^{p−1} = −p and ζ_p ≡ 1 − π_0 (mod π_0^2), the character of Gal(L/k((t))), L: z^p − z = f, sending z ↦ z + 1 to ζ_p has D†(V) ≅ Dwork's module M_f (∇v = −π_0 (df/dt) v ⊗ dt, with the sign of source issue E-RD2-12).
- An unramified character (finite image of Frobenius only): D†(V) is trivial as a differential module but its Frobenius structure is the twist by the character's value on Frobenius.

<a id="target-rd-2-fontaine-katz-unit-root-equivalence"></a>

### Fontaine-Katz equivalence: unit-root (σ,∇)-modules over E and p-adic representations of G_{k((t))}

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/fontaine-katz-unit-root-equivalence` · theorem

Suppose σ_K is absolute (it acts on k by x ↦ x^q) and its fixed field K_0 = K^{σ_K=1} has residue field F_q and the same value group as K. For a continuous representation V_0 of G = Gal(k((t))^sep/k((t))) on a finite-dimensional K_0-vector space, give V = V_0 ⊗_{K_0} K the σ_K-semilinear Frobenius fixing V_0. Then V_0 ↦ D(V) (RD.2/galois-representation-to-differential-module (a)) is an equivalence, compatible with tensor products and duals, from continuous K_0-representations of G to finite differential modules over E with a unit-root Frobenius structure relative to σ; a quasi-inverse is D ↦ (D ⊗_E Ẽ)^{F=1}. Moreover the differential structure is redundant: a finite free unit-root σ-module over E carries a unique compatible differential structure. For K = Q_q and σ_K the q-power Witt-vector Frobenius (the identity of Q_q) this is an equivalence with continuous Q_q-representations of G_{F_q((t))} (Kedlaya, Corollary 19.1.6).

**Hypotheses.**

- σ is a Frobenius lift on E acting on K by σ_K, with σ_K absolute; the value-group and residue-field hypotheses on K_0 guarantee Ẽ^{σ=1} = K_0 (RD.2/unramified-extensions-of-amice-rings (d)).
- For Z_p-lattices and a p-power Frobenius on a Cohen ring this is FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4/etale-phi-modules-cohen-ring (ii); here the coefficients are O_{K_0} and the Frobenius has order q.

**Prerequisites.** [Unit-root differential modules D(V), D†(V) attached to Galois representations; finite local monodromy](#target-rd-2-galois-representation-to-differential-module) (`RD.2/galois-representation-to-differential-module`), [Unit-root Frobenius modules are trivialised over Ẽ, and become c-constant over a finite separable extension](#target-rd-2-lang-trivialisation-of-unit-root-modules) (`RD.2/lang-trivialisation-of-unit-root-modules`), [Unramified extensions E_L, E†_L and the completed maximal unramified extension Ẽ of the Amice ring](#target-rd-2-unramified-extensions-of-amice-rings) (`RD.2/unramified-extensions-of-amice-rings`), [The derivation d/dt on annulus rings, R, R^bd, R^int, O_E and E, its norm bounds and Ω^1 = R dt](#target-rd-0-derivation-on-robba-ring) (`RD.0/derivation-on-robba-ring`), `FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4/etale-phi-modules-cohen-ring`, [(σ,∇)-modules (φ,∇)-modules over R, R^bd, R^int, E and dagger algebras; Frobenius structures](#target-rd-1-frobenius-differential-module) (`RD.1/frobenius-differential-module`), [Pure (isoclinic) and unit-root σ-modules over R, R^bd and E](#target-rd-1-isoclinic-frobenius-module) (`RD.1/isoclinic-frobenius-module`).

**Sources.**

- [S57](#source-57), Proposition 19.1.5 and Corollary 19.1.6, pp. 315-316. The equivalence between continuous K_0-representations and finite differential modules over E with unit-root Frobenius structure, with inverse (D ⊗ Ẽ)^{φ=1}, under the stated hypotheses on K_0.
- [S57](#source-57), Remark 19.1.7 and Remark 19.1.8, p. 316; Exercises (1) and (2), p. 325. The differential structure is not needed (unique compatible differential structure); for non-absolute lifts the proposition fails because the residue field of Ẽ need not be weakly difference-closed.
- [S3](#source-3), Theorem 3.7 and Remark 3.10, pp. 6-7. The Katz-Crew equivalence of unit-root convergent F-isocrystals with étale Q_p-local systems, whose local model is this statement.

**Construction or proof.**

1. D(V) is a unit-root (σ,∇)-module (RD.2/galois-representation-to-differential-module (a)).
2. (D(V_0) ⊗ Ẽ)^{F=1} = (V ⊗_K Ẽ)^{F=1} = V_0 ⊗_{K_0} Ẽ^{σ=1} = V_0, using Ẽ^{σ=1} = K_0 (Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, proof of Proposition 19.1.5, and Exercise (1) of Chapter 19).
3. For D unit-root, D ⊗ Ẽ is a trivial difference module: it has a basis of F-fixed vectors (RD.2/lang-trivialisation-of-unit-root-modules (a)); hence V_0(D) := (D ⊗ Ẽ)^{F=1} has K_0-dimension rank D, the natural map V_0(D) ⊗ Ẽ → D ⊗ Ẽ is an isomorphism, G acts continuously on V_0(D) by (b) of that lemma, and D(V_0(D)) = D by taking G-invariants (RD.2/unramified-extensions-of-amice-rings (b)).
4. Uniqueness of the differential structure (Kedlaya, Exercise (2) of Chapter 19 and Remark 19.1.7): under D ⊗ Ẽ ≅ V_0 ⊗ Ẽ any compatible connection kills the F-fixed vectors, because ∇ maps (D ⊗ Ẽ)^{F=1} into the F-fixed part of D ⊗ Ẽ ⊗ Ω^1, which is zero: an F-fixed element Σ v_i ⊗ a_i dt (v_i an F-fixed basis) satisfies a_i = σ(a_i)·dσ(t)/dt, and since σ is isometric on Ẽ and |dσ(t)/dt|_1 ≤ |π| (RD.0/derivation-on-robba-ring) this forces a_i = 0; so ∇ = 1 ⊗ d on V_0 ⊗ Ẽ, and it descends uniquely.
5. Tensor compatibility: F-fixed vectors of a tensor product contain the tensor products of F-fixed vectors, with equal dimensions.

**Checks.**

- V_0 = K_0 trivial ↦ (E, d, σ).
- Corollary 19.1.6: for K = Q_q and σ_K = id (the q-power Witt Frobenius), continuous Q_q-representations of G_{F_q((t))} correspond to unit-root (σ,∇)-modules over E for a Frobenius lift with σ(t) ≡ t^q.
- Unramified characters χ: G → G/I → Z_p^× (through Frobenius of k) ↦ rank-one modules E e with ∇e = 0 and F e = χ(Frob)^{±1} e (up to the normalisation of the arithmetic Frobenius).

<a id="target-rd-2-tsuzuki-equivalence-finite-local-monodromy"></a>

### Tsuzuki's theorem: unit-root (σ,∇)-modules over E† have finite local monodromy, and correspond to representations with finite local monodromy

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/tsuzuki-equivalence-finite-local-monodromy` · theorem

(a) (Trivialisation; K complete discretely valued as throughout, any Frobenius lift σ, any k.) Let M be a unit-root (σ,∇)-module over E† = R^bd. If k is perfect there is a finite separable (Galois) extension L of k((t)) such that M ⊗_{E†} E†_L has a basis of horizontal sections, on which F acts by a matrix in GL_n(K_L); for general k the same holds over E†_{L'} for a nearly finite separable L' (RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring (d)). Consequently M ⊗ R is quasi-constant (RD.2/constant-and-quasi-constant-differential-module), and the kernel of ∇ on M ⊗ E†_L is F-stable of rank n over K_L. This is the statement of RD.2/tsuzuki-unit-root-finite-monodromy. (b) (Equivalence; k perfect.) If σ_K is absolute and K_0 = K^{σ_K=1} has residue field F_q and the same value group as K, then V_0 ↦ D†(V_0 ⊗_{K_0} K) (RD.2/galois-representation-to-differential-module (c)) is an equivalence of tensor categories from continuous representations of G = Gal(k((t))^sep/k((t))) with finite local monodromy on finite-dimensional K_0-vector spaces to finite differential modules over E† with a unit-root Frobenius structure; its composite with base change to E is the Fontaine-Katz equivalence (RD.2/fontaine-katz-unit-root-equivalence). In particular a continuous K_0-representation has finite local monodromy iff its unit-root module D(V) over E descends to E†.

**Hypotheses.**

- (a) needs only that σ reduces to the q-power map of k((t)); (b) needs the hypotheses of the Fontaine-Katz equivalence.
- For imperfect k a separable L/k((t)) may have inseparable residue extension, so E†_L need not be a bounded Robba ring over a coefficient field; the nearly separable L' of RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring (d) repairs this (Kedlaya, arXiv:math/0110124, proof of Proposition 6.11, last paragraph; Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, Section 20.5).

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/LocalMonodromy/UnitRoot`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Unit-root Frobenius modules are trivialised over Ẽ, and become c-constant over a finite separable extension](#target-rd-2-lang-trivialisation-of-unit-root-modules) (`RD.2/lang-trivialisation-of-unit-root-modules`), [A c-constant unit-root (σ,∇)-module with c < p^{−1/(p−1)} is trivial (the key lemma of Tsuzuki's theorem)](#target-rd-2-small-constant-unit-root-module-is-trivial) (`RD.2/small-constant-unit-root-module-is-trivial`), [c-constant unit-root (σ,∇)-modules](#target-rd-2-c-constant-unit-root-module) (`RD.2/c-constant-unit-root-module`), [Unit-root differential modules D(V), D†(V) attached to Galois representations; finite local monodromy](#target-rd-2-galois-representation-to-differential-module) (`RD.2/galois-representation-to-differential-module`), [Fontaine-Katz equivalence: unit-root (σ,∇)-modules over E and p-adic representations of G_{k((t))}](#target-rd-2-fontaine-katz-unit-root-equivalence) (`RD.2/fontaine-katz-unit-root-equivalence`), [Unramified extensions E_L, E†_L and the completed maximal unramified extension Ẽ of the Amice ring](#target-rd-2-unramified-extensions-of-amice-rings) (`RD.2/unramified-extensions-of-amice-rings`), [Finite étale extensions of R^int and the Robba rings R^L of finite separable extensions of k((t))](#target-rd-2-finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring) (`RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring`), [Constant and quasi-constant ∇-modules over the Robba ring](#target-rd-2-constant-and-quasi-constant-differential-module) (`RD.2/constant-and-quasi-constant-differential-module`), [F-stable lattices: nonnegative generic slopes versus integral models](#target-rd-1-frobenius-stable-lattices) (`RD.1/frobenius-stable-lattices`), [Independence of the Frobenius lift: the Taylor isomorphism σ_1^*E ≅ σ_2^*E](#target-rd-1-change-of-frobenius-for-frobenius-structures) (`RD.1/change-of-frobenius-for-frobenius-structures`), [Pure (isoclinic) and unit-root σ-modules over R, R^bd and E](#target-rd-1-isoclinic-frobenius-module) (`RD.1/isoclinic-frobenius-module`).

**Sources.**

- [S57](#source-57), Theorem 19.3.1 and its proof, pp. 318 and 321. Tsuzuki's theorem: for an absolute q-power Frobenius lift with K_0 of residue field F_q and the value group of K, V_0 ↦ D†(V) is an equivalence between representations with finite local monodromy and finite differential modules over E† with unit-root Frobenius structure; the proof chooses L with M ⊗ E†_L c-constant for c < p^{−1/(p−1)} and applies Lemma 19.3.4.
- [S57](#source-57), Notes to Chapter 19, p. 323. Attribution: rank one to Crew, the general case to Tsuzuki (Amer. J. Math. 1998, Theorem 5.1.1), alternative expositions by Christol and Kedlaya; the c-constancy argument handles the change of Frobenius lift.
- [S1](#source-1), Proposition 6.11 and proof, pp. 79-80 (arXiv v4). The reductions from q = p to q = p^f, from k algebraically closed to general k, and the nearly separable choice of the extension when k is imperfect.
- [S3](#source-3), Theorem 3.9 and Remark 3.10, p. 7. Tsuzuki's theorem in the language of overconvergent unit-root F-isocrystals and potentially unramified local systems; the local model is this equivalence.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a), k perfect: choose an étale lattice and, by RD.2/lang-trivialisation-of-unit-root-modules (c), a finite Galois L with M ⊗ E†_L c-constant for some c < p^{−1/(p−1)}; since k is perfect the residue field of L is separable over k and E†_L is a bounded Robba ring over K_L in a lifted uniformiser u (RD.2/finite-etale-extension-of-bounded-robba-ring (c)); RD.2/small-constant-unit-root-module-is-trivial gives a horizontal basis, and H^0 is F-stable (Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, proof of Theorem 19.3.1, p. 321).
2. (a), general k: by the Lang step the finite separable L exists; replace it by the compositum L' of L with k^{q^{−m}}((t)) for m so large that the residue extension of L' over k^{q^{−m}} is separable (arXiv:math/0110124, proof of Proposition 6.11, last paragraph); c-constancy persists under base change, and the key lemma applies over E†_{L'}, a bounded Robba ring over the m-th Frobenius copy K^{(m)} of K.
3. Quasi-constancy of M ⊗ R: M ⊗ R^L = (M ⊗ E†_L) ⊗ R^L is spanned by the horizontal basis (RD.2/constant-and-quasi-constant-differential-module).
4. (b) Full faithfulness: D†(V) ⊗ E = D(V) and the Fontaine-Katz equivalence is fully faithful, while every G-equivariant map induces a map of the D† (Kedlaya, proof of Theorem 19.3.1). Essential surjectivity: by (a) M ⊗ E†_L is trivial for a finite Galois L, so the representation V_0(M ⊗ E) is trivial on the inertia subgroup of G_L, i.e. has finite local monodromy, and M = D†(V_0) by Galois descent from E†_L (RD.2/galois-representation-to-differential-module (b), (c)).
5. Converse: if V has finite local monodromy then D†(V) is a unit-root (σ,∇)-module over E† whose base change is D(V).

**Checks.**

- Dwork's module M_f (f = t^{−1}) becomes trivial over the Artin-Schreier extension L: z^p − z = t^{−1} (RD.2/dwork-exponential-artin-schreier-example), and corresponds to the character of Gal(L/k((t))) with value ζ_p on z ↦ z + 1 (Kedlaya, Example 19.2.6).
- A unit-root (σ,∇)-module over E† that is unipotent over R^L is constant over E†_L (Kedlaya, Remark 20.1.5): the generalisation to all slopes is RD.2/quasi-unipotence-and-local-monodromy-statement.
- Non-example: the rank-one ∇-module E† e with ∇e = e ⊗ dt admits no Frobenius structure (it is not solvable, RD.2/frobenius-hypothesis-is-necessary), so the theorem does not apply to it, and indeed it never becomes trivial over any E†_L.

<a id="target-rd-2-tsuzuki-unit-root-finite-monodromy"></a>

### Tsuzuki's theorem: unit-root (σ,∇)-modules have finite local monodromy

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/tsuzuki-unit-root-finite-monodromy` · theorem

Let M be a unit-root (σ,∇)-module over Γ_con[π^{-1}] = R^bd (isoclinic of slope 0, RD.1/isoclinic-frobenius-module). Then for some finite separable extension L of k((t)) (k perfect; nearly finite separable in general), M ⊗ R^bd_L admits a basis of horizontal sections; in particular M ⊗ R_K is quasi-constant. Precise form (arXiv:math/0110124, Annals version, Proposition 6.11): for a unit-root (σ,∇)-module M of rank n over Γ_con and any nearly finite extension K'/k((t)) such that M ⊗ Γ^{K'}_con has a basis on which F acts by a matrix A with v_p(A − I) > 1/(p−1), the kernel of ∇ on M ⊗ Γ^{K'}_con has rank n over O and is F-stable; such a K' can be chosen separable (k perfect) or nearly separable (k imperfect).

**Hypotheses.**

- Unit-root: an étale lattice exists (RD.1/frobenius-stable-lattices (a)), which is ∇-stable after applying F repeatedly (SFR proof of Proposition 7.2.3).
- Equivalently (Katz, Crew, Tsuzuki; Kedlaya's Notes Theorems 3.7, 3.9, Remark 3.10) the p-adic representation of G_{k((t))} attached to the étale lattice has finite image of inertia.
