**Prerequisites.** [Highest breaks under unipotent twists, tame covers and Artin-Schreier covers](#target-rd-2-highest-break-under-finite-etale-pullback) (`RD.2/highest-break-under-finite-etale-pullback`), [Matsuda's decomposition of quasi-unipotent ∇-modules as ⊕ F_i ⊗ U_i](#target-rd-2-matsuda-decomposition) (`RD.2/matsuda-decomposition`), [Quasi-unipotent ∇-modules are classified by their monodromy representations](#target-rd-2-monodromy-representation-equivalence) (`RD.2/monodromy-representation-equivalence`), [Highest break b(E) of a solvable ∇-module (differential irregularity)](#target-rd-1-highest-break) (`RD.1/highest-break`), `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3/breaks-and-swan-conductor`, `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3/upper-numbering-of-an-open-subgroup`, `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3/artin-schreier-break`, `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3/conductor-of-a-character`, `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3/conductor-tame-base-change`, [Quasi-unipotent ∇-modules are overconvergent](#target-rd-2-quasi-unipotent-implies-overconvergent) (`RD.2/quasi-unipotent-implies-overconvergent`), [Basic properties of generic radii: exact sequences, duals, tensor products, log-concavity, continuity, invariance](#target-rd-1-generic-radius-basic-properties) (`RD.1/generic-radius-basic-properties`), `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3/conductor-unramified-base-change`.

**Sources.**

- [S8](#source-8), Theorem 5.4.10 and proof, pp. 35-36. For k perfect, a quasi-unipotent E whose monodromy representation has highest break β has highest break β; proof by reduction to p-group images and double induction using Lemmas 5.4.4-5.4.9.
- [S8](#source-8), Remark 5.4.13, p. 36. Attribution: for K discretely valued this is Matsuda's Corollary 8.8; related results of Tsuzuki (Theorem 7.2.2) and Crew (Theorem 5.4), and André's Tannakian Complement 7.1.2.
- [S8](#source-8), Proposition 2.3.6, p. 8. Hasse-Arf: breaks of abelian extensions are integers, used for the lowest break of the p-group image.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Enlarge k to an algebraic closure, i.e. replace K by the completion of its maximal unramified extension: the inertia group with its upper ramification filtration does not change, so neither do the Galois breaks (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3/conductor-unramified-base-change records the consequence for the conductor and the Swan conductor), and generic radii and differential breaks are unchanged as well (RD.1/generic-radius-basic-properties (f)). By RD.2/highest-break-under-finite-etale-pullback (c) pass to a tame cover so that the image H of τ is a p-group; by RD.2/matsuda-decomposition and parts (a), (b) of that lemma reduce to E quasi-constant and irreducible (Kedlaya overview, proof of Theorem 5.4.10).
2. Induct on |H| and then on the lowest upper break i of H, an integer by Hasse-Arf for the abelian quotient (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3/conductor-of-a-character). Base case |H| = p: Lemma 5.4.9 = part (d) of RD.2/highest-break-under-finite-etale-pullback with the break of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3/artin-schreier-break.
3. Inductive step: choose a maximal subgroup N ⊇ H^i, normal of index p, fixing an Artin-Schreier extension u^p − u = Σ_{j≤i} c_j t^{−j} (p ∤ j); over it either E becomes constant (break i by part (d)) or the highest break of τ becomes βp − (p − 1)i (Herbrand function, ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3/upper-numbering-of-an-open-subgroup) with a smaller lowest break, so the induction hypothesis gives the break of f^*E and part (e) gives β for E; β = i is excluded because H would then be elementary abelian, hence of order p.

**Checks.**

- Dwork's module M_f, f = t^{−n} (p ∤ n): its monodromy is the Artin-Schreier character of u^p − u = t^{−n}, of upper break n, and its highest break is n.
- A tamely ramified character of order m prime to p (Kummer module ∇v = (a/m) v ⊗ dt/t): break 0 on both sides.
- A representation with highest upper break 1/2 (Artin-Schreier over t^{1/2}, p odd): the module has highest break 1/2 (part (c) with n = 2).

<a id="target-rd-2-irregularity-equals-swan-conductor"></a>

### Break decompositions match ramification: the differential Swan conductor equals the Swan conductor of the monodromy

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/irregularity-equals-swan-conductor` · theorem

Suppose k is perfect and E is a quasi-unipotent ∇-module over R_K (for instance one admitting a Frobenius structure, by RD.2/quasi-unipotence-and-local-monodromy-statement), with monodromy representation V restricted to inertia. (a) The monodromy equivalence (RD.2/monodromy-representation-equivalence) carries the break decomposition E = ⊕_b E_b of RD.1/break-decomposition to the break decomposition V = ⊕_λ V(λ) of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3/breaks-and-swan-conductor: E_b corresponds to V(b). (b) Hence the break multisets agree and the differential Swan conductor (irregularity) equals the Galois Swan conductor: Swan(E) (RD.1/differential-swan-conductor) = Sw(V). In particular Swan(E) is a nonnegative integer (Hasse-Arf, R01.3/hasse-arf-integrality), which recovers RD.1/swan-conductor-integrality for quasi-unipotent modules. (c) For a representation V of G = Gal(k((t))^sep/k((t))) with finite local monodromy and D†(V) as in RD.2/galois-representation-to-differential-module, for ρ < 1 close to 1 the intrinsic generic radius is IR(D†(V) ⊗ F_ρ) = ρ^{b} (equivalently R(D†(V) ⊗ F_ρ) = ρ^{b+1}) where b is the highest upper break of V|_I, and the intrinsic subsidiary radii are ρ^{b_1}, …, ρ^{b_n}, the b_j being the highest breaks of the constituents V_j of V|_I counted with multiplicity dim V_j.

**Hypotheses.**

- k perfect (as in R01.3, tier (P) of which rests on its recorded ramification gap; tier (F) for finite k is supplied by Tau Ceti).
- Normalisation: breaks are Serre's upper numbering (G^0 = inertia, G^{0+} = wild inertia), and IR = R/ρ is the intrinsic radius of RD.1/generic-radius; Kedlaya's book (Theorem 19.4.1, Corollary 19.4.2) prints R = ρ^b with b = max{i ≥ 1 : G^i ⊄ ker τ}, which must be read with IR in place of R and with b allowed in [0, ∞) (source issue recorded here).

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/LocalMonodromy/Breaks`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [The highest break of a quasi-unipotent ∇-module equals the highest ramification break of its monodromy representation](#target-rd-2-matsuda-highest-break-theorem) (`RD.2/matsuda-highest-break-theorem`), [Matsuda's decomposition of quasi-unipotent ∇-modules as ⊕ F_i ⊗ U_i](#target-rd-2-matsuda-decomposition) (`RD.2/matsuda-decomposition`), [Unit-root differential modules D(V), D†(V) attached to Galois representations; finite local monodromy](#target-rd-2-galois-representation-to-differential-module) (`RD.2/galois-representation-to-differential-module`), [Quasi-unipotent ∇-modules are classified by their monodromy representations](#target-rd-2-monodromy-representation-equivalence) (`RD.2/monodromy-representation-equivalence`), [The p-adic local monodromy theorem (Crew's conjecture): (φ,∇)-modules over the Robba ring are quasi-unipotent](#target-rd-2-quasi-unipotence-and-local-monodromy-statement) (`RD.2/quasi-unipotence-and-local-monodromy-statement`), [Break decomposition of a solvable ∇-module near the boundary (Christol-Mebkhout)](#target-rd-1-break-decomposition) (`RD.1/break-decomposition`), [Break multiset and differential Swan conductor of a solvable ∇-module](#target-rd-1-differential-swan-conductor) (`RD.1/differential-swan-conductor`), [Generic radius of convergence R(E, ρ), intrinsic radius T(E, ρ) and subsidiary radii](#target-rd-1-generic-radius) (`RD.1/generic-radius`), `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3/breaks-and-swan-conductor`, `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3/hasse-arf-integrality`, `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3/swan-additive`, [Quasi-unipotent ∇-modules are overconvergent](#target-rd-2-quasi-unipotent-implies-overconvergent) (`RD.2/quasi-unipotent-implies-overconvergent`).

**Sources.**

- [S8](#source-8), Corollary 5.4.11, Remarks 5.4.12-5.4.13, p. 36. The monodromy equivalence commutes with break decompositions; attribution to Matsuda (Corollary 8.8), Tsuzuki (Theorem 7.2.2) and Crew (Theorem 5.4).
- [S57](#source-57), Theorem 19.4.1, Corollary 19.4.2, Remark 19.4.4, pp. 321-322. For finite local monodromy, the generic radius of D†(V) ⊗ F_ρ near 1 is computed from the highest upper break, the subsidiary radii from the constituents, and integrality of the product of subsidiary radii is the Hasse-Arf theorem (stated without proof; the radius must be read as the intrinsic radius).
- [S17](#source-17), Complément 7.1.2 and its proof, p. 24. The isomorphism G^{>0} ≅ P identifies the p-adic slope filtration with the upper ramification filtration (Matsuda-Tsuzuki), proved by comparing Swan conductor and p-adic irregularity on K_0(Rep I) via Artin induction and the rank-one computation.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a) E is solvable at 1 (RD.2/quasi-unipotent-implies-overconvergent), so its break decomposition and Swan conductor are defined. By RD.2/matsuda-decomposition and the Galois-theoretic break decomposition, it suffices to show that an indecomposable E with monodromy of uniform break λ has uniform break λ; apply RD.2/matsuda-highest-break-theorem to E and to all its subquotients, which pins down the generic radii of every Jordan-Hölder constituent (Kedlaya overview Corollary 5.4.11 and Remark 5.4.12).
2. (b) Sum the breaks with multiplicities on both sides; Sw(V) = Σ_λ λ dim V(λ) by definition (R01.3/breaks-and-swan-conductor) and Swan(E) = Σ_b b·rank E_b (RD.1/differential-swan-conductor).
3. (c) D†(V) ⊗ R is quasi-constant with monodromy V|_I (RD.2/galois-representation-to-differential-module (e)); apply (a) and the definition of intrinsic subsidiary radii (RD.1/generic-radius).

**Checks.**

- Dwork's module M_{t^{−1}}: Swan = 1 = Sw of the Artin-Schreier character (R01.3/artin-schreier-swan-conductor: Sw = m for u^p − u = u_0 with v(u_0) = −m); IR = ρ, R = ρ^2 near the boundary (RD.1/dwork-exponential-module).
- A tamely ramified or unramified V: all breaks 0, Swan(E) = Sw(V) = 0, IR(D†(V) ⊗ F_ρ) = 1.
- Integrality: for the induced representation from a ramified Artin-Schreier extension of break 1 over the tame extension t^{1/2} (p odd), V is two-dimensional with upper break 1/2 and Sw(V) = 2·(1/2) = 1, an integer, matching the differential Swan conductor of the rank-two module.

<a id="target-rd-2-quasi-unipotent-modules-admit-frobenius-structures"></a>

### Over algebraic coefficients every quasi-unipotent ∇-module carries a Frobenius structure at a finite level

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/quasi-unipotent-modules-admit-frobenius-structures` · lemma

Let K be complete for a discrete valuation, of characteristic 0, with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, K̄ an algebraic closure with residue field k̄, and R_{K̄} := R_K ⊗_K K̄ = ∪_{K'} R_{K'} (union over finite extensions K'/K inside K̄) with the derivation d = d/dt; I = Gal(k̄((t))^sep/k̄((t))), the inertia group of k((t)), and P ⊆ I its wild inertia. Let K_0 = W(k)[1/p] ⊆ K. Say that an object M of MC(R_{K̄}/K̄) admits a Frobenius structure at finite level if there are a finite extension K_1 of K_0 inside K̄, a Frobenius lift σ_1 of K_1 (a continuous endomorphism lifting x ↦ x^{p^h} on the residue field, for some h ≥ 1), a (σ_1,∇)-module M_1 over R_{K_1} for the standard lift t ↦ t^{p^h} (RD.1/frobenius-differential-module), and an isomorphism M_1 ⊗ R_{K̄} ≅ M of ∇-modules. (a) Every quasi-constant ∇-module M over some R_{K'} (K'/K finite) becomes, over R_{K̄}, isomorphic to M_1 ⊗ R_{K̄} with M_1 a (σ_1,∇)-module over R_{K_1}, where F is a finite extension of Q_p inside K̄, k' the compositum of k and the residue field F_{p^f} of F, K_1 = F·W(k')[1/p] and σ_1 = id_F ⊗ φ_W^h (φ_W the Witt-vector Frobenius, f | h). (b) Every unipotent ∇-module over R_{K̄} is the base change of a module over R_{K_0} in Jordan form, which carries a Frobenius structure for every Frobenius lift of K_0. (c) Hence every quasi-unipotent ∇-module over R_{K̄} admits a Frobenius structure at finite level; in the notation of RD.2/differential-modules-with-algebraic-constants, MC^qu(R_{K̄}/K̄) ⊆ MCF(R_{K̄}/K̄). The existence of such a structure does not depend on the choice of the lift t ↦ t^{p^h} (RD.1/change-of-frobenius-for-frobenius-structures).

**Hypotheses.**

- k perfect, so K is a finite totally ramified extension of K_0 = W(k)[1/p] and K̄ is also an algebraic closure of K_0. With F^ur the maximal unramified subextension of F/Q_p, F^ur ⊆ W(k')[1/p], and F·W(k')[1/p] = F ⊗_{F^ur} W(k')[1/p] is a field (F/F^ur totally ramified, W(k')[1/p]/F^ur unramified); id_F ⊗ φ_W^h is well defined because φ_W^h fixes F^ur when f | h.
- Working at a finite, discretely valued level is what makes the p-adic local monodromy theorem applicable; André's definition (§3.4) asks instead for an isomorphism φ_h^*M ≅ M over R_{K̄} for an automorphism σ of K̄, which contains the present notion (σ_1 extends to such a σ).

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/LocalMonodromy/Tannakian`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [∇-modules that become constant over R^L are semilinear representations of Gal(L/k((t)))](#target-rd-2-quasi-constant-modules-are-semilinear-representations) (`RD.2/quasi-constant-modules-are-semilinear-representations`), [Matsuda's decomposition of quasi-unipotent ∇-modules as ⊕ F_i ⊗ U_i](#target-rd-2-matsuda-decomposition) (`RD.2/matsuda-decomposition`), [Unipotent ∇-modules are the modules V ⊗ R with nilpotent residue](#target-rd-2-unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue) (`RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue`), [Quasi-unipotent ∇-modules and (σ,∇)-modules](#target-rd-2-quasi-unipotent-differential-module) (`RD.2/quasi-unipotent-differential-module`), [(σ,∇)-modules (φ,∇)-modules over R, R^bd, R^int, E and dagger algebras; Frobenius structures](#target-rd-1-frobenius-differential-module) (`RD.1/frobenius-differential-module`), [Independence of the Frobenius lift: the Taylor isomorphism σ_1^*E ≅ σ_2^*E](#target-rd-1-change-of-frobenius-for-frobenius-structures) (`RD.1/change-of-frobenius-for-frobenius-structures`).

**Sources.**

- [S57](#source-57), Proposition 20.1.3 and proof, p. 327. A quasi-unipotent module is solvable at 1: after enlarging K, the horizontal sections over R^L form a representation of a finite group with a stable lattice over a finite extension of Q_p, and declaring it fixed gives a Frobenius structure for an absolute Frobenius lift fixing that field.
- [S17](#source-17), §3.4, p. 11. Defines Frobenius structures of order h on objects of MC(R_K̄/K̄) via φ_h (z ↦ z^{p^h}, σ lifting the p^h-power map) and MCF as the objects admitting one, noting that only existence matters.
- [S8](#source-8), Remark 4.7.7, p. 27. For k algebraically closed the monodromy-representation description of quasi-unipotent modules is essentially André's Théorème 7.1.1, i.e. MCF is described by all permissible representations.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a) After a finite extension of the constants, H^0(M ⊗ R^L) is a linear representation of the finite group Gal(L/k((t))) (RD.2/quasi-constant-modules-are-semilinear-representations), which can be defined over a finite extension F of Q_p inside K̄ with a stable O_F-lattice T (Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, proof of Proposition 20.1.3, p. 327). The equivalence of RD.2/quasi-constant-modules-are-semilinear-representations over K_1 = F·W(k')[1/p] produces M_1 with M_1 ⊗ R_{K̄} ≅ M ⊗ R_{K̄}; declaring T fixed defines a Frobenius structure for σ_1 = id_F ⊗ φ_W^h on M_1 ⊗ R^L, which commutes with the Galois action and descends to M_1.
2. (b) A unipotent M is V ⊗ R with ∇ = d + N dt/t, N nilpotent (RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue); after a change of basis N is a Jordan matrix with entries 0 and 1, so M is defined over R_{K_0}; the pull-back along t ↦ t^{q} (q = p^h) has residue qN, conjugate to N by a diagonal matrix with entries powers of q, which gives the Frobenius structure.
3. (c) By RD.2/matsuda-decomposition a quasi-unipotent M is ⊕ F_i ⊗ U_i; take K_1 the compositum of the fields of (a) for the F_i and h a common multiple of the orders (a structure of order h induces one of every multiple order by iteration); tensor products and direct sums of the structures of (a) and (b) give one on M at the level R_{K_1}.

**Checks.**

- (R_{K_0}, d) with the standard lift: a Frobenius structure for every h.
- The Kummer module ∇v = (1/m) v ⊗ dt/t with p ∤ m: quasi-constant (trivial after t ↦ t^{1/m}); for h with m | p^h − 1, the map 1 ⊗ v ↦ t^{(p^h − 1)/m}·v is a horizontal isomorphism φ_h^*M ≅ M (the pulled-back connection is (p^h/m) dt/t), a Frobenius structure of order h already over R_{Q_p}.
- Dwork's module M_{t^{−1}} is defined over R_{Q_p(π_0)} (π_0^{p−1} = −p) with ∇v = π_0 t^{−2} v ⊗ dt and the Frobenius structure exp(π_0(t^{−1} − t^{−p})) for σ_1 = id; its dual E_π of RD.1/dwork-exponential-module has ∇w = −π_0 t^{−2} w ⊗ dt and Frobenius structure exp(π_0(t^{−p} − t^{−1})) (source issue E-RD2-12).

<a id="target-rd-2-differential-modules-with-algebraic-constants"></a>

### The Tannakian categories MC(R_K̄/K̄) ⊇ MCS ⊇ MCF of differential modules over the Robba ring with algebraic constants

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/differential-modules-with-algebraic-constants` · construction

Let K be complete for a discrete valuation, of characteristic 0, with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, K̄ an algebraic closure with residue field k̄, and R_{K̄} := R_K ⊗_K K̄ = ∪_{K'} R_{K'} (union over finite extensions K'/K inside K̄) with the derivation d = d/dt; I = Gal(k̄((t))^sep/k̄((t))), the inertia group of k((t)), and P ⊆ I its wild inertia. (a) MC(R_{K̄}/K̄) is the category of finitely presented R_{K̄}-modules with a connection ∇ : M → M ⊗ Ω^1 (Leibniz rule for d); every object is finite free and is the base change of an object over R_{K'} for some finite K'/K, and Hom-spaces are the colimits of those over the R_{K'}; with ⊗ over R_{K̄}, duals and the unit (R_{K̄}, d) it is a K̄-linear abelian rigid tensor category with End(1) = K̄. (b) Full subcategories: MC^uni of unipotent objects (successive extensions of the unit), MC^qu of quasi-unipotent objects, MCS of objects solvable at 1 (RD.1/solvable-at-boundary), and MCF of objects admitting a Frobenius structure at finite level (RD.2/quasi-unipotent-modules-admit-frobenius-structures); only the existence of a Frobenius structure is recorded, not the structure itself. (c) MC^uni ≃ Vec^nil_{K̄} (finite-dimensional K̄-spaces with a nilpotent endomorphism) via (V, N) ↦ (V ⊗_{K̄} R_{K̄}, d + N dt/t), so the Tannakian group of MC^uni is G_a. (d) MCF = MC^qu ⊆ MCS, and MCF is a Tannakian subcategory stable under subquotients and extensions. (e) The logarithmic fibre functor ω : MCF → Vec_{K̄}, ω(M) = colim_L H^0(M ⊗ R^L_{K̄,log}) (L finite separable over k̄((t)), R^L_log = R^L[log t] as in RD.2/log-robba-ring), is an exact faithful tensor functor, and ω(M) carries commuting actions of I (through the Galois action on R^L_log, fixing log t) and of G_a (c ∈ K̄ acting by log t ↦ log t + c), with dim ω(M) = rank M.

**Hypotheses.**

- K discretely valued with perfect residue field; the colimit over K' ⊆ K̄ is taken inside a fixed algebraic closure, so R_{K̄} is an integral domain (K is algebraically closed in R_K).
- (d) uses the p-adic local monodromy theorem (RD.2/quasi-unipotence-and-local-monodromy-statement) at the finite level K_1 for MCF ⊆ MC^qu; André obtains the Tannakian property from Christol-Mebkhout's theory instead. With André's definition (an isomorphism φ_h^*M ≅ M over R_{K̄} for an automorphism σ of K̄) the category contains this one, and coincides with it by André's Théorème 7.1.1, which shows that all its objects are quasi-unipotent; that comparison is cited, not planned.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/LocalMonodromy/Tannakian`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Over algebraic coefficients every quasi-unipotent ∇-module carries a Frobenius structure at a finite level](#target-rd-2-quasi-unipotent-modules-admit-frobenius-structures) (`RD.2/quasi-unipotent-modules-admit-frobenius-structures`), [The p-adic local monodromy theorem (Crew's conjecture): (φ,∇)-modules over the Robba ring are quasi-unipotent](#target-rd-2-quasi-unipotence-and-local-monodromy-statement) (`RD.2/quasi-unipotence-and-local-monodromy-statement`), [Unipotent ∇-modules are the modules V ⊗ R with nilpotent residue](#target-rd-2-unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue) (`RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue`), [Quasi-unipotent ∇-modules and (σ,∇)-modules](#target-rd-2-quasi-unipotent-differential-module) (`RD.2/quasi-unipotent-differential-module`), [A finitely presented module with connection over the Robba ring is free](#target-rd-2-finitely-presented-differential-module-is-free) (`RD.2/finitely-presented-differential-module-is-free`), [Residues and antiderivatives on the Robba ring](#target-rd-2-robba-ring-antiderivative) (`RD.2/robba-ring-antiderivative`), [The logarithmic Robba ring R^L_log = R^L[log u] with Frobenius, derivation and monodromy operator](#target-rd-2-log-robba-ring) (`RD.2/log-robba-ring`), [Logarithmic form of the p-adic local monodromy theorem](#target-rd-2-logarithmic-form-of-local-monodromy) (`RD.2/logarithmic-form-of-local-monodromy`), [The (φ, N, Gal)-module of logarithmic solutions (local monodromy representation)](#target-rd-2-solution-space-phi-n-module) (`RD.2/solution-space-phi-n-module`), [∇-modules solvable at the boundary (overconvergent, 'soluble en 1')](#target-rd-1-solvable-at-boundary) (`RD.1/solvable-at-boundary`), [A Frobenius structure forces generic radius 1 at the boundary (Dwork; Christol-Mebkhout)](#target-rd-1-frobenius-structure-forces-solvability) (`RD.1/frobenius-structure-forces-solvability`).

**Sources.**

- [S17](#source-17), §3.4, pp. 10-11. MC(R/K) and MCS(R/K) over a Robba-type ring, base change to K̄, the definition of Frobenius structures of order h and of MCF(R_K̄/K̄) as the objects admitting one, its Tannakian property (Christol-Mebkhout) and MCF ⊆ MCS (Dwork).
- [S32](#source-32), §2.9.1, pp. 23-24. MC(R_K/K), MC(R/K̄) with R = R_K ⊗_K K̄, the unipotent subcategory equivalent to Vec^nil_{K̄} with Tannakian group G_a, and MCF(R/K̄) as the full subcategory of objects admitting a Frobenius structure, with Tannakian group 𝒢.
- [S8](#source-8), Definitions 4.6.1, 4.7.1, 4.7.2, 4.7.5, Lemma 4.7.4, pp. 24-27. Quasi-unipotent modules, the logarithmic sheaf O_log, the dimension of H^0_log and the monodromy representation of G_log = Gal × K.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- André, Filtrations de type Hasse-Arf, Théorème 7.1.1: MCF(R_K̄/K̄) is the Tannakian category whose group is computed as I × G_a
- Xu-Zhu, Bessel F-isocrystals, §2.9 and §4.5: restriction of overconvergent F-isocrystals to a boundary point lands in MCF(R/K̄), and the local monodromy group is read there
- RD.6 (global monodromy of overconvergent F-isocrystals): local monodromy groups at the boundary points of a curve are the Tannakian groups of these local categories

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `RobbaAlgConst` |  | R_{K̄} = R_K ⊗_K K̄ with the derivation d. |
| `DiffModCat` |  | MC(R_{K̄}/K̄), the K̄-linear rigid abelian tensor category of finitely presented R_{K̄}-modules with connection. |
| `DiffModCat.descends` |  | Every object and morphism is defined over R_{K'} for some finite K'/K. |
| `MCS` |  | The full subcategory of objects solvable at 1. |
| `MCF` |  | The full subcategory of objects admitting a Frobenius structure at finite level (a (σ_1,∇)-module over some R_{K_1}, K_1/W(k)[1/p] finite). |
| `MCF.eq_quasiUnipotent` |  | MCF = MC^qu. |
| `MCF.subset_MCS` |  | MCF ⊆ MCS. |
| `MCF.closed` |  | MCF is closed under subquotients, extensions, tensor products and duals. |
| `unipotentEquiv` |  | Vec^nil_{K̄} ≃ MC^uni(R_{K̄}/K̄). |
| `logFiberFunctor` |  | ω : MCF → Vec_{K̄}, ω(M) = colim_L H^0(M ⊗ R^L_{K̄,log}). |
| `logFiberFunctor.monoidal` |  | ω is an exact faithful tensor functor with dim ω(M) = rank M. |
| `logFiberFunctor.action` |  | ω(M) carries commuting actions of I and of G_a, natural in M. |

**Unit tests.**

- `MCF.unit` (degenerate): The unit object (R_{K̄}, d) lies in MCF, with ω(1) = K̄ and End(1) = K̄.
- `MCF.unipotent_equiv` (compatibility): The functor (V, N) ↦ (V ⊗ R_{K̄}, d + N dt/t) is an equivalence Vec^nil_{K̄} ≃ MC^uni(R_{K̄}/K̄), and ω of its image is V with c ∈ G_a acting by exp(cN) up to sign.
- `MCF.eq_quasiUnipotent` (characterisation): An object of MC(R_{K̄}/K̄) lies in MCF iff it is quasi-unipotent.
- `MCF.kummer_mem` (computation): The Kummer module ∇v = (1/m) v ⊗ dt/t (p ∤ m) lies in MCF and ω of it is the character of I through its tame quotient of order m.
- `MCF.not_irrational_exponent` (non-example): For λ ∈ Z_p \ Q the module ∇e = λ e ⊗ dt/t is solvable at 1 (in MCS) but not in MCF.
- `MCF.not_unsolvable` (non-example): The module ∇e = e ⊗ dt is not in MCS, hence not in MCF.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a) Finitely presented modules with connection over a Robba ring are free (RD.2/finitely-presented-differential-module-is-free); a presentation involves finitely many coefficients, hence descends to some R_{K'}; rigidity and End(1) = ker(d on R_{K̄}) = K̄ (RD.2/robba-ring-antiderivative).
2. (c) Base change of RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue to K̄ (André §3.4; Xu-Zhu §2.9.1, p. 23); Vec^nil_{K̄} is the category of representations of G_a (c acting by exp(cN)).
3. (d) MCF ⊆ MC^qu by the p-adic local monodromy theorem applied to M_1 over R_{K_1} (K_1 discretely valued with Frobenius lift σ_1; quasi-unipotence is preserved by base change to R_{K̄}); MC^qu ⊆ MCF by RD.2/quasi-unipotent-modules-admit-frobenius-structures; MC^qu is stable under subquotients, tensor products, duals and extensions (Kedlaya overview Definition 4.6.1); MCF ⊆ MCS by Dwork's argument (RD.1/frobenius-structure-forces-solvability).
4. (e) By the logarithmic form of the local monodromy theorem (RD.2/logarithmic-form-of-local-monodromy) and RD.2/solution-space-phi-n-module, for L large H^0(M ⊗ R^L_log) has dimension rank M over the constants and the transition maps are isomorphisms after extending constants; exactness and the tensor property follow from the comparison isomorphism H^0(M ⊗ R^L_log) ⊗ R^L_log ≅ M ⊗ R^L_log.

**Checks.**

- The unit (R_{K̄}, d) ↦ ω = K̄ with trivial I × G_a action.
- U_2 = (K̄², N = [[0,1],[0,0]]) ↦ ω(U_2) = K̄² with G_a acting by [[1,c],[0,1]] (up to the sign convention for N) and I trivially.
- Non-example for MCS ⊆ MCF: the rank-one module ∇e = λ e ⊗ dt/t with λ ∈ Z_p not in Q (Kedlaya, Example 9.5.2: solvable at 1) is in MCS but not quasi-unipotent, hence not in MCF.
- Non-example for MC ⊆ MCS: ∇e = e ⊗ dt is not solvable (RD.2/frobenius-hypothesis-is-necessary).

<a id="target-rd-2-unipotent-solutions-and-residues"></a>

### Solutions of a unipotent ∇-module on the open unit disc: Sol(M) ≅ (coker N)^∨

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/unipotent-solutions-and-residues` · lemma

Let K{x} be the ring of analytic functions on the open unit disc |x| < 1 (Σ a_n x^n with |a_n| ρ^n → 0 for every ρ < 1), with the logarithmic derivation d : K{x} → Ω^1_{K{x}}(log) = K{x}·dx/x, f ↦ x f'(x) dx/x. Let M be a unipotent ∇-module over R_K corresponding to (V, N) (RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue), extended to the log-∇-module M_log = V ⊗ K{x} with ∇(v) = Nv ⊗ dx/x on the disc. Then the solution space Sol(M) := Hom_{K{x}}((M_log, ∇), (K{x}, d))^{∇=0} of horizontal homomorphisms is canonically isomorphic to (coker N)^∨ = ker(N^∨ on V^∨): every horizontal φ is constant, φ(v) = λ(v) with λ ∈ V^∨ and λ∘N = 0. If ∇ is defined by a differential operator D (M = K{x}[∂]/K{x}[∂]D), Sol(M) is the space of solutions of D in K{x}. If M carries a Frobenius structure extending to the disc, Sol(M) and coker N are (φ, N)-modules with N φ = q φ N, compatibly with the duality.

**Hypotheses.**

- K complete of characteristic 0; the residue N is nilpotent (unipotent M).
- Xu-Zhu (2.9.2.2) print a canonical isomorphism Coker(N) ≅ Sol(M); the solution space is the dual of the cokernel (source issue recorded here). Dimensions agree, which is all that their subsequent argument (proof of Proposition 5.1.3) requires.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/LocalMonodromy/Tannakian`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Unipotent ∇-modules are the modules V ⊗ R with nilpotent residue](#target-rd-2-unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue) (`RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue`), [Unipotent ∇-modules over the Robba ring](#target-rd-2-unipotent-differential-module) (`RD.2/unipotent-differential-module`), [(σ,∇)-modules (φ,∇)-modules over R, R^bd, R^int, E and dagger algebras; Frobenius structures](#target-rd-1-frobenius-differential-module) (`RD.1/frobenius-differential-module`).

**Sources.**

- [S32](#source-32), §2.9.2, (2.9.2.1)-(2.9.2.2), p. 24. The ring K{x}, the log derivation, the log extension of a unipotent object and the identification of its solution space with the cokernel of N (printed without the dual).
- [S8](#source-8), Proposition 4.5.3, pp. 21-23. Unipotent ∇-modules on an annulus are equivalent to log-∇-modules on the open disc with nilpotent residue, overconvergent on the punctured disc, and to (V, N).
- [S57](#source-57), Proposition 17.5.1 and Remark 17.1.2, pp. 292, 299. A Frobenius structure on the restriction to an annulus of a module with nilpotent singularity extends to the disc, and on the residue it gives N_0 A_0 = q A_0 φ(N_0).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Write φ(v) = Σ_{n≥0} φ_n(v) x^n with φ_n ∈ V^∨. Horizontality φ(Nv) = x d/dx φ(v) gives φ_n∘N = n φ_n for every n; for n ≥ 1, N − n is invertible (N nilpotent), so φ_n = 0, and for n = 0 the condition is φ_0∘N = 0 (Xu-Zhu §2.9.2, p. 24, in corrected form).
2. Conversely each λ ∈ V^∨ with λ∘N = 0 defines a horizontal homomorphism; so Sol(M) ≅ (V/NV)^∨.
3. For M = K{x}[∂]/K{x}[∂]D, a horizontal homomorphism is determined by the image y of the class of 1, which satisfies D(y) = 0.
4. Frobenius: a Frobenius structure extending to the disc is constant on a horizontal basis (Kedlaya, p-adic Differential Equations, Proposition 17.5.1), giving φ on V with N φ = q φ N (Remark 17.1.2); it induces the dual structure on Sol(M).

**Checks.**

- M = (R_K, d): V = K, N = 0, Sol(M) = K (the constant functions).
- M = U_2 (N e_2 = e_1, N e_1 = 0): coker N is spanned by the class of e_2, and Sol(M) is spanned by the functional e_1^∨ ↦ 0, e_2^∨-dual: λ(e_1) = 0, λ(e_2) = 1; one-dimensional.
- The operator D = (x d/dx)^2: M ≅ U_2 and its solutions in K{x} are the constants (log x is not in K{x}), one-dimensional = dim coker N.

<a id="target-rd-2-andre-local-monodromy-group"></a>

### André's local monodromy theorem: the Tannakian group of MCF(R_K̄/K̄) is I × G_a, with wild part P

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2/andre-local-monodromy-group` · theorem

Let K be complete for a discrete valuation, of characteristic 0, with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, K̄ an algebraic closure with residue field k̄, and R_{K̄} := R_K ⊗_K K̄ = ∪_{K'} R_{K'} (union over finite extensions K'/K inside K̄) with the derivation d = d/dt; I = Gal(k̄((t))^sep/k̄((t))), the inertia group of k((t)), and P ⊆ I its wild inertia. (a) The logarithmic fibre functor ω of RD.2/differential-modules-with-algebraic-constants (e) is an equivalence of K̄-linear rigid tensor categories from MCF(R_{K̄}/K̄) to the category Rep_{K̄}(I × G_a) of finite-dimensional K̄-vector spaces with a linear action of I whose kernel is open and a commuting nilpotent endomorphism N (c ∈ G_a acting by exp(cN)); equivalently, to the finite-dimensional comodules over the commutative Hopf algebra H = C^lc(I, K̄) ⊗ K̄[x] of locally constant functions on I tensored with the coordinate ring of G_a. (b) Consequently the Tannakian group Aut^⊗(ω) is I × G_a: for every commutative K̄-algebra A, Aut^⊗(ω ⊗ A) ≅ Hom_{K̄-alg}(H, A), naturally in A. (c) Under (a), an object has all p-adic slopes zero (highest break 0, RD.1/highest-break) iff P acts trivially on ω(M); more precisely the break filtration of MCF by p-adic slopes corresponds to the upper ramification filtration of P, so that 𝒢^{>0} ≅ P, and the irregularity of M equals the Swan conductor of ω(M)|_I. (d) The tame factor: for M unipotent with (V, N) as in RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue, ω(M) = V with G_a acting through N (up to sign), H^0(M) = ker N = ω(M)^{I × G_a} and H^1(M) = coker N = the G_a-coinvariants of ω(M); the solution space of RD.2/unipotent-solutions-and-residues is the dual (coker N)^∨. (e) Every indecomposable object is isomorphic to F ⊗ U_m with F coming from an irreducible representation of I with finite image and U_m the m-dimensional indecomposable unipotent object; an object M with End(M)^{𝒢^{>0}} = K̄ (completely irreducible) is absolutely irreducible of rank a power of p.

**Hypotheses.**

- k perfect and K discretely valued (André, §7.1). Over K itself (not K̄) the same functor gives the semilinear form RD.2/monodromy-representation-equivalence.
- Tannakian reconstruction is used only in the form of Tau Ceti's comodule reconstruction (points of a commutative Hopf algebra = tensor automorphisms of scalar extension on its finite-dimensional comodules); no general reconstruction of a neutral Tannakian category is needed, because (a) identifies MCF with a comodule category explicitly.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/LocalMonodromy/Tannakian`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [The Tannakian categories MC(R_K̄/K̄) ⊇ MCS ⊇ MCF of differential modules over the Robba ring with algebraic constants](#target-rd-2-differential-modules-with-algebraic-constants) (`RD.2/differential-modules-with-algebraic-constants`), [Over algebraic coefficients every quasi-unipotent ∇-module carries a Frobenius structure at a finite level](#target-rd-2-quasi-unipotent-modules-admit-frobenius-structures) (`RD.2/quasi-unipotent-modules-admit-frobenius-structures`), [The highest break of a quasi-unipotent ∇-module equals the highest ramification break of its monodromy representation](#target-rd-2-matsuda-highest-break-theorem) (`RD.2/matsuda-highest-break-theorem`), [Break decompositions match ramification: the differential Swan conductor equals the Swan conductor of the monodromy](#target-rd-2-irregularity-equals-swan-conductor) (`RD.2/irregularity-equals-swan-conductor`), [Matsuda's decomposition of quasi-unipotent ∇-modules as ⊕ F_i ⊗ U_i](#target-rd-2-matsuda-decomposition) (`RD.2/matsuda-decomposition`), [Solutions of a unipotent ∇-module on the open unit disc: Sol(M) ≅ (coker N)^∨](#target-rd-2-unipotent-solutions-and-residues) (`RD.2/unipotent-solutions-and-residues`), [Quasi-unipotent ∇-modules are classified by their monodromy representations](#target-rd-2-monodromy-representation-equivalence) (`RD.2/monodromy-representation-equivalence`), [The (φ, N, Gal)-module of logarithmic solutions (local monodromy representation)](#target-rd-2-solution-space-phi-n-module) (`RD.2/solution-space-phi-n-module`), [Unipotent ∇-modules are the modules V ⊗ R with nilpotent residue](#target-rd-2-unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue) (`RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue`), [Highest break b(E) of a solvable ∇-module (differential irregularity)](#target-rd-1-highest-break) (`RD.1/highest-break`), `tauceti:TauCeti.Tannaka.pointsFunctorIsoTensorAutFunctor`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Tannaka.fgPointTensorIsoEquiv`.

**Sources.**

- [S17](#source-17), Théorème 7.1.1, Complément 7.1.2 and proof, Corollaires 7.1.3, 7.1.5-7.1.8, pp. 24-26. MCF(R_K̄/K̄) has Tannakian group I × G_a with 𝒢^{>0} = P; the p-adic slope filtration matches the upper ramification filtration (Matsuda-Tsuzuki); countability for finite k; log solutions after a finite étale extension; indecomposables M ⊗ U_m; completely irreducible objects have p-power rank.
- [S32](#source-32), (2.9.1.1) and the following paragraph, p. 24. Restates André's isomorphisms 𝒢 ≅ I × G_a and 𝒢^{>0} ≅ P, the quasi-unipotence of MCF, finiteness of the action of P, and irregularity = Swan conductor of the I-representation on a fibre.
- [S8](#source-8), Theorem 4.7.6 and Remark 4.7.7, p. 27. The monodromy representation is an equivalence from quasi-unipotent ∇-modules to permissible representations of G_log; for k algebraically closed this is essentially André's Théorème 7.1.1.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a) Over K̄ the coefficient Galois action is trivial (residue field k̄ algebraically closed), so the monodromy representation of RD.2/monodromy-representation-equivalence becomes a linear permissible representation of I × G_a, and that theorem (quasi-unipotent modules ≃ permissible representations, Kedlaya overview Theorem 4.7.6) applied over each R_{K'} and passed to the colimit (for M defined over R_{K'}, restrict its semilinear monodromy representation to I × G_a, which acts K'^unr-linearly because I fixes the coefficients, and extend scalars to K̄; objects, morphisms and representations with open kernel are all defined at some finite level, so full faithfulness and essential surjectivity pass to the colimit) gives the equivalence on MC^qu = MCF (RD.2/differential-modules-with-algebraic-constants (d)); tensor compatibility from the comparison isomorphism of RD.2/solution-space-phi-n-module.
2. Comodules over H: H is a commutative Hopf algebra over K̄, built in this node because Tau Ceti's reconstruction takes the Hopf algebra as given: C^lc(I, K̄) is the colimit, over open normal subgroups U of I, of the function algebras K̄^{I/U} of the finite groups I/U with comultiplication dual to the group law, and K̄[x] has x ↦ x ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ x. A finite-dimensional comodule over C^lc(I, K̄) is a representation of I with open kernel (its coefficients lie in some K̄^{I/U}), and one over K̄[x] is a nilpotent endomorphism (characteristic 0), so Comod_fd(H) = Rep_{K̄}(I × G_a).
3. (b) Tau Ceti's reconstruction TauCeti.Tannaka.pointsFunctorIsoTensorAutFunctor (and its pointwise form TauCeti.Tannaka.fgPointTensorIsoEquiv) identifies Hom_{K̄-alg}(H, A) with the tensor automorphisms of scalar extension to A on finite-dimensional H-comodules; transport along (a).
4. (c) RD.2/matsuda-highest-break-theorem and RD.2/irregularity-equals-swan-conductor: the break decomposition corresponds to the Galois break decomposition, and break 0 means P acts trivially (G^{0+} = P); this is André's Complément 7.1.2.
5. (d) RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue (H^0 = ker N, H^1 = coker N) and the action log t ↦ log t + c on horizontal log-sections (Kedlaya overview Definition 4.7.5).
6. (e) Indecomposable representations of I × G_a with I acting through a finite group are W ⊗ (Jordan block) with W irreducible (André Corollaire 7.1.6; equivalently RD.2/matsuda-decomposition); for completely irreducible M, End of the restriction to 𝒢^{>0} = P is K̄, so M|_P is irreducible and P is a pro-p group acting through a finite p-group, whose irreducible representations have p-power dimension (André Corollaire 7.1.8).

**Checks.**

- The unit object ↦ the trivial representation; U_m ↦ the m-dimensional Jordan block of G_a.
- Dwork's module M_{t^{−1}} ↦ the Artin-Schreier character of I of conductor 2 (Swan conductor 1), nontrivial on P.
- Kummer module ∇v = (1/m) v ⊗ dt/t (p ∤ m) ↦ a tame character of I of order m (trivial on P), irregularity 0.
- André Corollaire 7.1.3: if k is finite, the isomorphism classes of objects of MCF(R_{K̄}/K̄) form a countable set, because I has countably many open subgroups.

### Proof obligations and supplier contracts

**G5: public general Robba-duality proof.** The DLB consumer was read but its general duality citation is Kedlaya book Proposition 20.4.2, which is not cleared and was not read. The alternative RD.2 local-monodromy route needs a full proof that finite-cover normal-form cohomology, residue, trace and duality descend, with the exact one-form and degree factors. Establish those comparisons and convergence of Laurent integration; a proof for a nilpotent constant matrix alone is not the general theorem.

Consumes: [Robba residue duality](#target-rd-1-robba-residue-duality) (`RD.1/robba-residue-duality`).

**Upper ramification filtration over an infinite perfect residue field (inherited from ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.3).** The comparison of differential breaks with ramification breaks uses Serre's upper numbering, the break decomposition and the Swan conductor of representations of Gal(k((t))^sep/k((t))) with finite wild image. ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.3 supplies them for finite k through Tau Ceti's LocalFieldsRamification layers 3-4 (tier (F)) and records a gap for an arbitrary perfect residue field (tier (P)). André's setting (k̄ algebraically closed) and Kedlaya's (k perfect) need tier (P). Kedlaya's own proof is insensitive to this (it works over k̄ throughout), so the gap is in the library interface, not in the mathematics; it closes when R01.3's tier (P) gap is closed.

Consumes: [The highest break of a quasi-unipotent ∇-module equals the highest ramification break of its monodromy representation](#target-rd-2-matsuda-highest-break-theorem) (`RD.2/matsuda-highest-break-theorem`), [Break decompositions match ramification: the differential Swan conductor equals the Swan conductor of the monodromy](#target-rd-2-irregularity-equals-swan-conductor) (`RD.2/irregularity-equals-swan-conductor`), [André's local monodromy theorem: the Tannakian group of MCF(R_K̄/K̄) is I × G_a, with wild part P](#target-rd-2-andre-local-monodromy-group) (`RD.2/andre-local-monodromy-group`).

<a id="rd3"></a>

## RD.3 — Frames and convergent and overconvergent coefficients

Build tubes, strict-neighborhood systems, the j† calculus and coherent gluing, then define overconvergent coefficients by their stratification or Taylor-convergent connection. Prove frame and compactification independence, Frobenius-forced convergence and the affine description. Define ordinary convergent coefficients separately, the unit-root correspondence and étale descent, before the global Newton-vertex and dense-open slope results. Mixed full-faithfulness statements that also need local monodromy are in RD.5.

**Landmarks.** Frame, Tube, Berthelot's j† functor, Independence of the frame, Overconvergent F-isocrystal, Convergent F-isocrystal.

<a id="target-rd-3-frame"></a>

### Frames (X ⊂ Y ⊂ P)

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/frame` · definition

Setting of RD.3: K complete discretely valued of characteristic 0, O = O_K, residue field k of characteristic p (perfect where stated), σ_K a Frobenius lift on K; schemes are separated of finite type over k (Mathlib's AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme with the morphism classes of SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0); formal O-schemes are separated and topologically of finite type, and P_K denotes the generic fibre of a formal scheme P as a rigid analytic space with specialisation map sp : P_K → P (both imported from AdicSpacesPartII:R2). A frame is a triple (X, Y, P) with j : X → Y an open immersion of k-schemes, i : Y → P a closed immersion of Y into the special fibre of a formal O-scheme P, such that P is smooth over Spf O in a neighbourhood of X; put Z = Y \ X. The frame is proper if Y is proper over k, and then P_K, ]Y[_P and all constructions only depend on a neighbourhood of Y. A morphism of frames (X', Y', P') → (X, Y, P) is a triple (w, v, u) of morphisms w : X' → X, v : Y' → Y, u : P' → P with i∘v = u∘i' and j∘w = v∘j'; it is smooth near X' if u is smooth in a neighbourhood of X'.

**Hypotheses.**

- P need not be smooth at the points of Z: for X smooth affine with a smooth lift 𝔛 and Y = X̄ the closure in projective space, P = the formal completion of the closure of 𝔛 is not smooth along Z in general (Berthelot 2.3 remark), which is why only smoothness near X is required.
- Frames exist locally: an affine Y admits a closed immersion into the special fibre of the formal affine space over O, which is smooth; global frames need not exist, and constructions are then glued (Čech), see RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystals-of-a-variety.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Isocrystals/Frames`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/raynaud-generic-fibre`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/generic-fibre-fibre-products`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/tube`.

**Sources.**

- [S20](#source-20), (2.2), p. 17. Berthelot's setting (V = O_K); read from the page image.
- [S4](#source-4), Hypothesis 4.2.1, p. 25. Kedlaya's frame hypothesis (X̄ a compactification of X).

**Uses and API requirements.**

- Berthelot 1986, §§2-4: rigid cohomology and overconvergent isocrystals are defined on frames
- Kedlaya, Finiteness, §4: Hypothesis 4.2.1 and Definitions 4.2.2-4.3.4
- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4: the overconvergent de Rham complex and compact support are computed on frames
- ColemanIntegration:L1 (via RD.4): a smooth affine curve with a smooth proper model gives the frame (Y_k, X_k, X̂)

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Frame` |  | A frame (X, Y, P): open immersion X → Y, closed immersion Y → P_s, P smooth near X. |
| `Frame.IsProper` |  | Y is proper over k. |
| `Frame.Hom` |  | Morphisms of frames (w, v, u) with commuting squares. |
| `Frame.Hom.IsSmoothNear` |  | u is smooth in a neighbourhood of X'. |
| `Frame.boundary` |  | Z = Y \ X, a closed subscheme of Y. |
| `Frame.id_comp` |  | Frames with their morphisms form a category (identity and composition). |
| `Frame.prod` |  | Fibre product of frames over (X, Y): (X, Y, P ×_O P') with the diagonal immersion, used to compare two frames. |
| `Frame.affineSpace` |  | (A^n_k, P^n_k, P̂^n_O) and (A^n_k, (P^1_k)^n, (P̂^1_O)^n). |

**Unit tests.**

- `Frame.affineLine_tube` (computation): For (A^1, P^1, P̂^1): ]A^1[ = {|t| ≤ 1} and ]∞[ = {|t| > 1} ∪ {∞}.
- `Frame.proper_self` (degenerate): For X proper and smooth with smooth formal lift P, (X, X, P) is a proper frame with Z = ∅.
- `Frame.scheme_compat` (compatibility): The underlying open immersion X → Y and closed immersion Y → P_s are Mathlib's IsOpenImmersion and IsClosedImmersion morphisms.
- `Frame.not_frame_nonsmooth` (non-example): (X, Y, P) with P = Spf O[x, y]/(xy − π) and X = Y = the node {x = y = 0} is not a frame: P is not smooth near X.

**Construction or proof.**

1. The data are Mathlib schemes and morphism classes (AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion, IsClosedImmersion, IsProper, Smooth) together with a formal scheme from AdicSpacesPartII:R2; smoothness of P near X is smoothness of the reductions P ⊗ O/π^n near X (Berthelot 1.1).

**Checks.**

- Standard frame of the affine line: (A^1_k, P^1_k, P̂^1_O); the tube of A^1 is the closed unit disc and the tube of ∞ is the open disc |t| > 1 around ∞.

### The tube ]T[_P of a locally closed subscheme

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/tube` · definition

For a formal O-scheme P (separated, topologically of finite type) and a locally closed subscheme T of its special fibre, the tube of T is ]T[_P := sp^{-1}(T), an admissible open of the classical rigid generic fibre P_K. If P = Spf A is affine and T is closed, cut out by π and f_1, ..., f_r ∈ Γ(P, O_P), then ]T[_P = {x ∈ P_K : |f_i(x)| < 1 for all i}; for λ ∈ |K^×|^Q ∩ (0,1) the open tube of radius λ is ]T[_{P,λ} = {x : |f_i(x)| < λ for all i}, independent of the equations when |a| < λ for all a ∈ m_K (discrete valuation), which defines it for non-affine P. This is the classical rigid tube. Its adic counterpart is the interior of λ^−1(T) for closed T, as constructed by AdicSpacesPartII:R2/tube, not the whole inverse image under the continuous adic specialization λ; locally it is the union of |f_i|^m ≤ |π|. Use the rigid–adic comparison to transport the tube into a frame.

**Hypotheses.**

- Tubes are defined for any locally closed T ⊆ P_s, not only for Y; the tube of Y in a frame is ]Y[_P and ]X[_P ⊆ ]Y[_P is admissible open.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Isocrystals/Frames`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/raynaud-generic-fibre`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/generic-fibre-fibre-products`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/tube`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme`.

**Sources.**

- [S20](#source-20), (1.3) Définition, p. 12. The definition (read from the page image).
- [S4](#source-4), Definition 4.1.2, p. 25. Same definition.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- Berthelot 1986 §§1-2: naive cohomology H*(]X[_P, Ω) and the complements U_λ = ]Y[ − ]Z[_λ
- RD.3/strict-neighbourhood: strict neighbourhoods of ]X[ in ]Y[
- ColemanIntegration:L1: residue discs ]x[ are tubes of closed points

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Frame.tube` |  | ]T[_P = sp^{-1}(T) ⊆ P_K. |
| `Frame.tube_eq_of_equations` |  | For P affine and T closed with equations π, f_1..f_r: ]T[_P = {max\|f_i\| < 1}. |
| `Frame.tubeRadius` |  | ]T[_{P,λ} = {max \|f_i\| < λ}, independent of equations for λ > \|π\|. |
| `Frame.tube_mono` |  | T ⊆ T' ⇒ ]T[ ⊆ ]T'[; ]T ∩ T'[ = ]T[ ∩ ]T'[. |
| `Frame.tube_map` |  | u(T') ⊆ T ⇒ u_K(]T'[_{P'}) ⊆ ]T[_P. |
| `Frame.tube_isQuasiStein` |  | For P affine, ]T[_P is quasi-Stein. |
| `Frame.tube_union_radius` |  | ]T[_P = ∪_{λ<1} ]T[_{P,λ} (admissible covering) for T closed. |

**Unit tests.**

- `Frame.tube_point_affineLine` (computation): For T = {0} ⊂ A^1_k ⊂ Â^1_O, ]T[ = {|t| < 1}.
- `Frame.tube_whole` (degenerate): ]P_s[_P = P_K and ]∅[_P = ∅.
- `Frame.tube_closedDisc_notEqual_open` (non-example): The tube of A^1 in P̂^1 is the closed disc |t| ≤ 1, not the open disc: tubes of open subschemes are not tubes of closed ones.
- `Frame.tube_radius_limit` (characterisation): For T closed in P affine, ]T[ is the increasing union of the ]T[_λ, λ → 1.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Import R2/tube and its rigid–adic comparison. For an affine formal scheme and a closed T, use its increasing rational exhaustion to prove the tube is quasi-Stein; for locally closed T choose the corresponding open formal locus first. This does not assert that every arbitrary open subspace is quasi-Stein.
2. Functoriality: a morphism u : P' → P with u(T') ⊆ T maps ]T'[_{P'} into ]T[_P (sp is natural).

**Checks.**

- ]A^1[ in P̂^1 is the closed unit disc; for T = {0} ⊂ A^1_k ⊂ Â^1, ]T[ = open unit disc |t| < 1 (a residue disc).

### Strict neighbourhoods of ]X[ in ]Y[

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/strict-neighbourhood` · definition

Let (X, Y, P) be a frame, Z = Y \ X, and for λ < 1 put U_λ := ]Y[_P \ ]Z[_{P,λ} (for P affine and f_1..f_r ∈ Γ(P, O_P) lifting equations of Z in Y, U'_λ := {x ∈ ]Y[ : max_i |f_i(x)| ≥ λ} may be used instead). An admissible open V ⊆ ]Y[_P is a strict neighbourhood of ]X[_P in ]Y[_P if ]X[_P ⊆ V and for every affinoid W ⊆ ]Y[_P there is λ < 1 with W ∩ U_λ ⊆ W ∩ V. For P non-affine the condition is imposed locally.

**Hypotheses.**

- Strict neighbourhoods form a filtered family stable under finite intersections; each U_λ (|π| < λ < 1) is a strict neighbourhood, and every strict neighbourhood contains W ∩ U_{λ(W)} for each affinoid W ⊆ ]Y[.
- In adic terms (AdicSpacesPartII:F1), a strict neighbourhood is a neighbourhood of the closure of ]X[ in ]Y[; F1 owns the dagger-affinoid version (cofinal systems of strict neighbourhoods of an affinoid in a larger one), RD.3 owns the tube version.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Isocrystals/Frames`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [The tube ]T[_P of a locally closed subscheme](#target-rd-3-tube) (`RD.3/tube`), `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/raynaud-generic-fibre`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/generic-fibre-fibre-products`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/tube`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/quasi-stein-theorems-a-b`.

**Sources.**

- [S20](#source-20), (2.5) Remarques a), p. 19. The definition (read from the page image).
- [S4](#source-4), Definition 4.2.2, p. 26. Kedlaya's version (the second ]X[ is ]X̄[, overline lost in extraction).

**Uses and API requirements.**

- Berthelot 1986 (2.2), (4.2.1): j† and overconvergent isocrystals are defined through strict neighbourhoods
- Kedlaya, Finiteness, Definition 4.2.3: an overconvergent F-isocrystal lives on a strict neighbourhood
- RD.4: rigid cohomology is H*(]Y[, j†Ω) = H*(V, j†Ω) for any strict neighbourhood V

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Frame.IsStrictNbhd` |  | V is a strict neighbourhood of ]X[_P in ]Y[_P. |
| `Frame.complementOfTube` |  | U_λ = ]Y[ \ ]Z[_λ. |
| `Frame.isStrictNbhd_complementOfTube` |  | U_λ is a strict neighbourhood for λ ∈ (\|π\|, 1). |
| `Frame.IsStrictNbhd.inter` |  | Finite intersections of strict neighbourhoods are strict neighbourhoods. |
| `Frame.IsStrictNbhd.preimage` |  | Preimages of strict neighbourhoods under morphisms of frames are strict neighbourhoods. |
| `Frame.IsStrictNbhd.cofinal` |  | Every strict neighbourhood contains, on each affinoid W ⊆ ]Y[, some W ∩ U_λ; the U_λ are cofinal on quasi-compact pieces. |
| `Frame.isStrictNbhd_proper` |  | If X = Y (Z = ∅) then ]Y[ is the only strict neighbourhood of ]X[ = ]Y[. |

**Unit tests.**

- `Frame.strictNbhd_affineLine` (computation): For (A^1, P^1, P̂^1) the open discs {|t| < ρ}, ρ > 1, are strict neighbourhoods of the closed unit disc.
- `Frame.strictNbhd_proper` (degenerate): For Z = ∅ the only strict neighbourhood of ]X[ = ]Y[ is ]Y[ itself.
- `Frame.tube_not_strictNbhd` (non-example): For (A^1, P^1, P̂^1), ]A^1[ = {|t| ≤ 1} is not a strict neighbourhood of itself: for W = {1 ≤ |t| ≤ 2}, W ∩ U_λ ⊄ {|t| ≤ 1} for every λ < 1.
- `Frame.strictNbhd_iff_complement` (characterisation): V ⊇ ]X[ is a strict neighbourhood iff for each affinoid W there is λ < 1 with W ∩ U'_λ ⊆ V.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Replacing U_λ by U'_λ does not change the notion (Berthelot 2.2).
2. Intersections: V_1 ∩ V_2 is a strict neighbourhood (take the larger λ on each W).
3. Pullback along a morphism of frames (w, v, u) with v^{-1}(X) = X' (equivalently v^{-1}(Z) = Z'): u_K^{-1}(V) ∩ ]Y'[ is a strict neighbourhood of ]X'[, since the pullbacks f_i∘u of equations of Z are equations of Z' and |f_i∘u| = |f_i|∘u_K (Berthelot 2.2).

**Checks.**

- For (A^1, P^1, P̂^1): the discs {|t| ≤ ρ} ⊆ ]P^1[ = P^1_K (ρ > 1), together with ∞'s complement, i.e. V_ρ = {|t| < ρ}, form a cofinal family of strict neighbourhoods of the closed unit disc ]A^1[.

<a id="target-rd-3-j-dagger"></a>

### Berthelot's functor j† of overconvergent sections

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/j-dagger` · construction

Let (X, Y, P) be a frame and j_λ : U_λ ↪ ]Y[_P the inclusions of the complements of the tubes of radius λ of Z (RD.3/strict-neighbourhood). For an abelian sheaf E on ]Y[_P put j†E := lim_{λ→1} j_{λ*} j_λ^* E, the sheaf of germs of sections of E in a neighbourhood of ]X[; equivalently j†E = lim_V j_{V*} j_V^* E over strict neighbourhoods V of ]X[ in ]Y[. In particular j†O_{]Y[} is a sheaf of rings on ]Y[_P and j†E is a j†O_{]Y[}-module for E an O_{]Y[}-module. For a morphism of frames u : P' → P there is a canonical map j†E → u_* j'† u^{-1} E.

**Hypotheses.**

- The family U_λ may be replaced by U'_λ = {x ∈ ]Y[ : max |f_i(x)| ≥ λ} for any lifts f_i of equations of Z (Berthelot 2.2).
- j† depends only on a strict neighbourhood: if V is a strict neighbourhood then j†E is determined by E|_V and H*(]Y[, j†E) = H*(V, j†E) (Berthelot 2.5 a)).

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Isocrystals/Frames`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Strict neighbourhoods of ]X[ in ]Y[](#target-rd-3-strict-neighbourhood) (`RD.3/strict-neighbourhood`), [The tube ]T[_P of a locally closed subscheme](#target-rd-3-tube) (`RD.3/tube`), `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/raynaud-generic-fibre`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/generic-fibre-fibre-products`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/tube`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/quasi-stein-theorems-a-b`.

**Sources.**

- [S20](#source-20), (2.2), p. 17. The definition (read from the page image).
- [S4](#source-4), Definition 4.3.1, p. 27. Kedlaya's formulation as a limit over strict neighbourhoods.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- Berthelot 1986 (2.3)-(2.4): rigid cohomology H*(]Y[, j†Ω^•)
- RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal: overconvergent isocrystals are locally free j†O_{]Y[}-modules with stratification
- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4: the overconvergent de Rham complex j†(E ⊗ Ω^•) and compact support Γ_{]Z[}
- Kedlaya, Finiteness, Definitions 4.3.1, 4.3.4: rigid cohomology with and without supports

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Frame.jDagger` |  | j†E = lim_λ j_{λ*} j_λ^* E for an abelian sheaf E on ]Y[_P. |
| `Frame.jDagger_eq_lim_strictNbhd` |  | j†E = lim over strict neighbourhoods V of j_{V*} j_V^* E. |
| `Frame.jDaggerStructureSheaf` |  | j†O_{]Y[}, a sheaf of rings; j†E is a j†O-module for O-modules E. |
| `Frame.jDagger_restrict` |  | j†E depends only on E\|_V for any strict neighbourhood V; H*(]Y[, j†E) = H*(V, j†E). |
| `Frame.jDagger_exact_coherent` |  | j† is exact on coherent sheaves and R^q j_{λ*} vanishes on coherent sheaves for q > 0 (P affine). |
| `Frame.jDagger_tensor` |  | j†E = j†O ⊗_O E for coherent E. |
| `Frame.jDagger_map` |  | For a morphism of frames u, the canonical map j†E → u_* j'† u^{-1} E, compatible with composition. |
| `Frame.jDagger_empty_boundary` |  | If Z = ∅ then j†E = E. |

**Unit tests.**

- `Frame.jDagger_affineLine_global` (computation): For (A^1, P^1, P̂^1), Γ(]P^1[, j†O) = K⟨t⟩† (series Σ a_n t^n converging on some |t| ≤ ρ, ρ > 1).
- `Frame.jDagger_trivial_boundary` (degenerate): If X = Y then j†O = O_{]Y[}.
- `Frame.jDagger_restrict_test` (characterisation): For any strict neighbourhood V, H^0(]Y[, j†O) = H^0(V, j†O).
- `Frame.jDagger_ne_restriction` (non-example): j†O ≠ j_* O_{]X[}: for (A^1, P^1, P̂^1), Γ(]A^1[, O) = K⟨t⟩ (closed disc) strictly contains Γ(j†O) = K⟨t⟩†; e.g. Σ p^n t^{p^n} is convergent but not overconvergent.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Direct limit of sheaves (a sheaf on the G-topology of ]Y[ since the limit is filtered).
2. Module structure and the canonical map from the adjunctions (Berthelot 2.2, construction of (2.2.1)).

**Checks.**

- For X = Y (Z = ∅), U_λ = ]Y[ and j†E = E.
- For (A^1, P^1, P̂^1): Γ(]P^1[, j†O) = lim_{ρ→1^+} O({|t| ≤ ρ}) = K⟨t⟩†, the overconvergent power series (RD.3/overconvergent-sections-of-affine-frame).

<a id="target-rd-3-standard-strict-neighbourhoods"></a>

### Strict neighbourhoods: admissible-covering definition, criterion and standard systems

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/standard-strict-neighbourhoods` · lemma

Let P be a formal O-scheme of finite type, Y ⊆ P_k a closed subscheme, X ⊆ Y open and Z = Y ∖ X. For η ∈ |K^×|^ℚ, η < 1, put U_η = ]Y[_P ∖ ]Z[_{P,η}. (a) An admissible open V ⊆ ]Y[_P containing ]X[_P is a strict neighbourhood of ]X[_P (the covering (V, ]Z[_P) of ]Y[_P is admissible) if and only if for every affinoid W ⊆ ]Y[_P there is η_0 < 1 with W ∩ U_η ⊆ V for all η_0 ≤ η < 1; when P is affine and g_1, …, g_s ∈ Γ(P, O_P) cut out Z inside Y, U_η may be replaced by U′_η = {x ∈ ]Y[_P : max_j |g_j(x)| ≥ η}. (b) For increasing sequences λ_n → 1 and η_n → 1 in |K^×|^ℚ the union V_{λ,η} = ⋃_n ([Y]_{λ_n} ∩ U_{η_n}) is a strict neighbourhood, independent of the chosen equations after discarding finitely many terms, and for fixed λ the V_{λ,η} form a fundamental system; they are pseudo-compact in ]Y[_P. (c) Strict neighbourhoods are stable under finite intersection, are local on P, and pull back to strict neighbourhoods along morphisms of triples (X′, Y′, P′) → (X, Y, P); the complement in ]Y[_P of a closed analytic subspace of P_K missing ]X[_P is a strict neighbourhood. (d) If X is open in a larger closed Y′ ⊇ Y, an open V ⊇ ]X[ of ]Y[ is a strict neighbourhood in ]Y[ if and only if it is one in ]Y′[; for opens X_1, X_2 of Y with strict neighbourhoods V_1, V_2, V_1 ∩ V_2 is a strict neighbourhood of ]X_1 ∩ X_2[ and, when V_1, V_2 are pseudo-compact, V_1 ∪ V_2 is one of ]X_1 ∪ X_2[ with (V_1, V_2) an admissible covering.

**Hypotheses.**

- The covering (]X[, ]Z[) of ]Y[ is not admissible in general, which is why strict neighbourhoods are needed (Berthelot's remark after (1.2.1)).
- Radii are taken in |K^×|^ℚ so that the tubes and the sets U_η are finite unions of rational domains.

**Prerequisites.** [Strict neighbourhoods of ]X[ in ]Y[](#target-rd-3-strict-neighbourhood) (`RD.3/strict-neighbourhood`), [The tube ]T[_P of a locally closed subscheme](#target-rd-3-tube) (`RD.3/tube`), `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-maximum-modulus`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/tube`.

**Sources.**

- [S62](#source-62), (1.2.1)–(1.2.4), (1.2.7), (1.2.9)–(1.2.11), pp. 32–38. Defines strict neighbourhoods by admissibility of the covering (V, ]Z[), proves the affinoid criterion, the standard neighbourhoods V_{λ,η} with their independence of equations, pullback along morphisms of triples, and the behaviour under intersections, unions and enlargement of Y.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a): if V is strict, the admissible covering (V, ]Z[_η)_{η→1} of W has a finite subcovering, so some U_η ∩ W lies in V; conversely, for P affine, for any affinoid h: Spm B → ]Y[ the maximum principle puts the image in some [Y]_λ, and the finitely many special domains [Z]_η and {|g_i| ≥ η} ∩ [Y]_λ refine (V, ]Z[) (Berthelot 96-03 (1.2.2), p. 33). The replacement of U_η by U′_η uses the maximum principle once more on W (1.2.3)(iii).
2. (b): the V_{λ,η} are open with the indicated special covering, and given any strict V′, quasi-compactness of [Y]_{λ_n} and (a) produce η_n with U_{η_n} ∩ [Y]_{λ_n} ⊆ V′ (1.2.4)(i); pseudo-compactness is (1.2.9).
3. (c): intersections and locality are immediate from the admissible-covering definition and (1.2.3)(ii); pullback is (1.2.7), using v^{-1}(Z) ⊆ Z′; complements of closed analytic subspaces are (1.2.4)(ii) by the maximum principle.
4. (d): (1.2.11) uses the admissible covering (]Y[, ]Z′[) of ]Y′[ ((1.1.14)(ii)); the intersection and union statements are (1.2.10).

**Checks.**

- Affine space: for P the formal projective space over O and X = A^n_k ⊂ P^n_k = Y, the sets U_η are the closed balls of radius 1/η around 0, so the closed balls of radius > 1 form a fundamental system of strict neighbourhoods of the closed unit polydisc (Berthelot (1.2.4)(iii)).
- Non-example: for P = Spf O⟨t⟩, Y = A^1_k and Z the origin, ]X[ is the annulus |t| = 1 and ]X[ itself is not a strict neighbourhood: the covering (]X[, ]Z[) of the closed disc is not admissible by the maximum principle.
- If Z = ∅ (X = Y) every admissible open containing ]X[ is a strict neighbourhood, in particular ]X[ itself.

<a id="target-rd-3-j-dagger-exactness-and-functoriality"></a>

### j† is exact, commutes with tensor products, is functorial and localises on X

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/j-dagger-exactness-and-functoriality` · lemma

In the setting of RD.3/j-dagger, let V be a strict neighbourhood of ]X[_P in ]Y[_P and 𝒜 a sheaf of rings on V. (a) For every 𝒜-module E the canonical map E → j†E is an epimorphism, an isomorphism when E is a j†𝒜-module, and E ⊗_𝒜 j†𝒜 → j†E is an isomorphism; j† is exact on 𝒜-modules, its restriction to ]X[ is the identity and its restriction to V ∩ ]Z[ is zero; Γ(]Y[, E) → Γ(V, E) is bijective for j†𝒜-modules E. (b) For a morphism of triples (w, v, u): (X′, Y′, P′) → (X, Y, P) and strict neighbourhoods with u_K(V′) ⊆ V there are canonical maps j†E → u_{K*} j′† u_K^{-1}E and, for modules, j†E → u_{K*} j′† u_K^*E; when X′ = v^{-1}(X) the maps u_K^{-1} j†E → j′† u_K^{-1}E and u_K^* j†E → j′† u_K^* E are isomorphisms. (c) For E coherent on V the map j†E → j_{K*} j_K^* E to the sections on ]X[ is injective. (d) For a finite open covering X = X_1 ∪ … ∪ X_n with inclusions j_{i_0…i_k} of the intersections, the alternating Čech complex 0 → j†E → ⊕ j_{i}†E → ⊕_{i_0<i_1} j_{i_0 i_1}†E → … is exact; equivalently j_1† j_2† ≅ j†_{X_1 ∩ X_2} and the sections supported in ]Z[ satisfy Γ_{]Z_1[} Γ_{]Z_2[} = Γ_{]Z_1 ∩ Z_2[}.

**Hypotheses.**

- No coherence is needed for (a), (b) and (d); (c) needs E coherent on a strict neighbourhood.
- The isomorphism statements in (b) need X′ = v^{-1}(X); without it only the canonical maps exist.

**Prerequisites.** [Berthelot's functor j† of overconvergent sections](#target-rd-3-j-dagger) (`RD.3/j-dagger`), [Strict neighbourhoods of ]X[ in ]Y[](#target-rd-3-strict-neighbourhood) (`RD.3/strict-neighbourhood`), [Strict neighbourhoods: admissible-covering definition, criterion and standard systems](#target-rd-3-standard-strict-neighbourhoods) (`RD.3/standard-strict-neighbourhoods`), `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-maximum-modulus`.

**Sources.**

- [S62](#source-62), (2.1.1)–(2.1.8) with the remark after (2.1.8), pp. 47–56. Defines the sheaf of overconvergent germs, proves exactness, the tensor formula, functoriality for morphisms of triples with the isomorphism criterion X′ = v^{-1}(X), injectivity into sections on the tube for coherent sheaves, and the Čech/Mayer–Vietoris resolution localising j† on X.
- [S24](#source-24), 2.7–2.8 and 2.12.2 Proposition, pp. 80–90. Re-proves these properties of j† for V-triples, with references to Berthelot's numbering.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a): sections of j†E over a quasi-compact W are germs of sections over W ∩ V′, V′ strict; surjectivity of E → j†E is local and follows by covering W by the special domains {|t_i| ≥ η} and [Z]_{η′}, on the latter the germ lifting to zero; injectivity for j†𝒜-modules uses that (U_η, ]Z[) covers V admissibly and that j†-modules vanish on ]Z[; the tensor formula follows from the universal property and exactness from exactness of filtered colimits and the epimorphism (Berthelot 96-03 (2.1.1)–(2.1.3), pp. 47–51).
2. (b): the maps come from pulling back germs of sections along u_K, using that preimages of strict neighbourhoods are strict (standard-strict-neighbourhoods (c)); when X′ = v^{-1}(X) an explicit inverse is constructed on affine charts from the sets U_η and U′_η = u_K^{-1}(U_η) ∩ ]Y′[ ((2.1.4), pp. 51–53).
3. (c): a section killed on ]X[ has support a closed analytic, hence quasi-compact, subset of a quasi-compact W disjoint from ]X[, so it is contained in some [Z]_η and the germ is zero ((2.1.5), p. 53).
4. (d): for two opens, compute the germs over V_1 ∩ V_2 and use that the products g′_i g″_j define Z_1 ∪ Z_2 ((2.1.7)); the general exactness follows by induction on n from the exact sequences 0 → Γ_{]Z[} → id → j† → 0 ((2.1.6), (2.1.8), pp. 53–56).

**Checks.**

- Affine space: for P the formal projective n-space and X = A^n_k, Γ(P_K, j†O) is the ring K⟨t_1, …, t_n⟩† of series with radius of convergence > 1 (Berthelot (2.1.2.3)), while Γ(]X[, j†O) = K⟨t_1, …, t_n⟩, so j† genuinely changes global sections.
- Degenerate case: if Z = ∅ then j†E = E.
- Two-open covering of G_m = A^1 ∖ {0} ⊂ P^1 by A^1 ∖ {0} itself and a second copy: the Čech sequence of (d) reduces to j†E ≅ j†E.

<a id="target-rd-3-j-dagger-properties"></a>

### Exactness of j† on coherent sheaves and the acyclicity of j_{λ*}

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/j-dagger-properties` · lemma

Let (X, Y, P) be a frame with P affine. For a coherent O_{]Y[}-module E: (a) R^q j_{λ*}(j_λ^* E) = 0 for q > 0; (b) H^q(]Y[, j†E) = lim_λ H^q(U_λ, E) and, for Y quasi-compact, j† commutes with cohomology in this sense; (c) j† is exact on coherent sheaves and j†E = j†O ⊗ E.

**Hypotheses.**

- P affine; the input is that j_λ : U_λ → ]Y[ is a quasi-Stein morphism (preimages of affinoids are increasing unions of affinoids with dense transition maps), so that Kiehl's Theorem B (AdicSpacesPartII:R3) applies, as Berthelot indicates.
- For the vanishing R^q j_{λ*} used in the proof, the chosen strict neighbourhood intersects every target affinoid in a quasi-Stein space; cite R3/quasi-stein-direct-image-acyclicity only after checking this condition.

**Prerequisites.** [Berthelot's functor j† of overconvergent sections](#target-rd-3-j-dagger) (`RD.3/j-dagger`), `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/quasi-stein-theorems-a-b`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/quasi-stein-direct-image-acyclicity`, [j† is exact, commutes with tensor products, is functorial and localises on X](#target-rd-3-j-dagger-exactness-and-functoriality) (`RD.3/j-dagger-exactness-and-functoriality`).

**Sources.**

- [S4](#source-4), Proposition 4.1.4, p. 25. Theorem B.
- [S20](#source-20), (2.1), p. 16. Acyclicity (read from the page image).

**Construction or proof.**

1. For each inclusion j_λ of a chosen strict neighbourhood, verify that its intersection with every target affinoid is quasi-Stein; R3/quasi-stein-direct-image-acyclicity then gives the vanishing of higher direct images used in (a). Theorem B on the source alone would not suffice.
2. (b) from (a) and quasi-compactness of ]Y[ pieces (cohomology commutes with filtered direct limits on quasi-compact quasi-separated sites).
3. (c) filtered colimits are exact.
4. Exactness of j† (part (c)) holds on all sheaves of modules on a strict neighbourhood, with no coherence or quasi-Stein hypothesis (Berthelot 96-03 (2.1.3)(iii), p. 50); the tensor formula and the localisation on X are j-dagger-exactness-and-functoriality. Parts (a)–(b) keep their quasi-Stein hypotheses.

**Checks.**

- For (A^1, P^1, P̂^1) and E = O: H^1(]P^1[, j†O) = 0 and H^0 = K⟨t⟩†.

<a id="target-rd-3-overconvergent-sections-of-affine-frame"></a>

### Global overconvergent functions on an affine frame are the dagger algebra

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/overconvergent-sections-of-affine-frame` · lemma

Let X = Spec A_0 be a smooth affine k-scheme, A a smooth O-algebra lifting A_0 with a presentation A = O[t_1..t_n]/I, 𝔛 = Spec A ⊂ A^n_O ⊂ P^n_O, X̄ the closure of X in P^n_k and P the formal completion of the closure of 𝔛 in P^n_O. Then for λ < 1, U_λ = 𝔛_K^an ∩ {closed ball of radius 1/λ}, and Γ(]X̄[_P, j†O) = lim_{λ→1} Γ(U_λ, O) = A† ⊗ K, the weak completion of A tensored with K (the Monsky-Washnitzer dagger algebra). More generally the direct limit of Γ(V, O_V) over strict neighbourhoods V of ]X[ is a dagger algebra of MW type with reduction A_0.

**Hypotheses.**

- The frame (X, X̄, P) has P smooth near X but possibly singular along X̄ \ X (Berthelot 2.3 remark).

**Prerequisites.** [Berthelot's functor j† of overconvergent sections](#target-rd-3-j-dagger) (`RD.3/j-dagger`), [Exactness of j† on coherent sheaves and the acyclicity of j_{λ*}](#target-rd-3-j-dagger-properties) (`RD.3/j-dagger-properties`), `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-algebra`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/fringe-presentation`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/fringe-topology`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-differentials`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-tensor-product`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-rational-localisation`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/raynaud-generic-fibre`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/generic-fibre-fibre-products`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/tube`.

**Sources.**

- [S20](#source-20), (2.1), p. 16. Identification A†⊗K = lim Γ(U_λ, O) (read from the page image).
- [S4](#source-4), Remark 4.2.5, p. 26. General statement.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Identify the tube ]X̄[ with 𝔛_K^an ∩ P^{n,an}_K and ]Z[_λ with the complement of the ball of radius 1/λ by an exercise in projective coordinates (Berthelot 2.1).
2. Γ(U_λ, O) is the ring of functions on the affinoid 𝔛_K^an ∩ B(0, 1/λ); their union is A† ⊗ K by the definition of weak completion (AdicSpacesPartII:F1: dagger algebras as unions over radius-indexed presentations; Kedlaya, Finiteness, §2.2 and Remark 4.2.5).
3. The node's identity Γ = A† ⊗ K is Berthelot 96-03 (2.1.2.4), p. 50; the module-level statement (coherent j†O-modules and overconvergent isocrystals on the Monsky–Washnitzer frame are determined by their global sections over A†_K) is affine-frame-global-sections-equivalence, proved in (2.5.2) without Theorem B for the frame.

**Checks.**

- X = A^1_k, A = O[t]: Γ(]P^1[, j†O) = K⟨t⟩† (RD.3/j-dagger test).
- X = G_m: A† ⊗ K = K⟨t, t^{-1}⟩†, the functions overconverging near |t| = 1 on both sides.

<a id="target-rd-3-etale-tube-isomorphism"></a>

### Étale maps induce isomorphisms of tubes

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/etale-tube-isomorphism` · theorem

Let X be a k-scheme of finite type, i: X → P and i′: X → P′ immersions into formal O-schemes of finite type, and u: P′ → P a morphism with u∘i′ = i which is étale on a neighbourhood of i′(X). Then u_K restricts to an isomorphism of rigid spaces ]X[_{P′} → ]X[_P. Moreover, for every closed tube radius λ ∈ |K^×|^ℚ with λ < 1 sufficiently close to 1, u_K restricts to an isomorphism of the closed tubes [X]_{P′,λ} → [X]_{P,λ}.

**Hypotheses.**

- X need not be smooth; P and P′ need not be smooth; only étaleness of u near X is used.
- The tube depends only on an open formal subscheme containing X, so P and P′ may be shrunk to opens containing X.

**Prerequisites.** [The tube ]T[_P of a locally closed subscheme](#target-rd-3-tube) (`RD.3/tube`), `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/tube`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/raynaud-generic-fibre`, `mathlib:Algebra.FormallyEtale`.

**Sources.**

- [S62](#source-62), (1.3.1) Proposition and its proof, pp. 39–40. States that an étale map compatible with the immersions induces an isomorphism of open tubes and of closed tubes of radius close to 1, proved by reducing to affine formal schemes and comparing the presentations of the closed tubes modulo powers of a.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Replace P and P′ by opens containing X so that X is closed in both, u is étale and P′ ×_P X → X is an isomorphism (an étale map with a section is an open immersion near the section). Since tubes are local on P (the generic fibres of an affine covering form an admissible covering), assume P = Spf A and P′ = Spf A′ affine (Berthelot 96-03, proof of (1.3.1), p. 39).
2. Let f_1, …, f_r ∈ A lift equations of X modulo the maximal ideal of O and a ∈ m_K nonzero. The closed tube of radius λ = |a|^{1/n} is the affinoid with algebra A{T}/(f_i^n − aT_i) ⊗ K, and the same presentation with A′ describes [X]_{P′,λ} (Berthelot (1.1.9)). It therefore suffices that A[T]/(a^m, f_i^n − aT_i) → A′[T]/(a^m, f_i^n − aT_i) is an isomorphism for all m, n.
3. The ideal generated by the f_i in A[T]/(a^m, f_i^n − aT_i) is nilpotent; A′[T] is étale over A[T] and the two rings agree modulo that nilpotent ideal ((A/I)[T] ≅ (A′/IA′)[T]). An étale algebra which becomes an isomorphism modulo a nilpotent ideal is an isomorphism (formal étaleness), so each map is an isomorphism; passing to the limit over m gives the closed-tube statement, and the open tube is the admissible union of the closed tubes as λ → 1.

**Checks.**

- Square root near 1: for p odd, P = P′ = Spf O⟨t, t^{-1}⟩ with u(t) = t² and X = {t = 1}: u is étale and u_K maps the residue disc {|t − 1| < 1} isomorphically onto {|s − 1| < 1}, the inverse being the binomial series of (1 + (s − 1))^{1/2}, whose coefficients are p-integral.
- Non-example: for the projection P × Spf O⟨x⟩ → P with X embedded by the zero section, u is smooth but not étale, and the tube of X upstairs is the product of ]X[_P with an open unit disc, not isomorphic to ]X[_P.
- With P′ = P and u the identity the statement is the identity of ]X[_P (degenerate case).

<a id="target-rd-3-weak-fibration-theorem"></a>

### Weak fibration theorem: tubes along smooth morphisms are open polydisc fibrations

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/weak-fibration-theorem` · lemma

Let X be a k-scheme, i : X ↪ P and i' : X ↪ P' immersions into formal O-schemes and u : P' → P a morphism smooth in a neighbourhood of X with u∘i' = i, of relative dimension n near X. Then u_K : ]X[_{P'} → ]X[_P is a fibration in open unit polydiscs: there is an affine covering (P_i) of P and isomorphisms ]X[_{P'} ∩ u_K^{-1}(P_{i,K}) ≅ (]X[_P ∩ P_{i,K}) × D(0,1^-)^n commuting with the projections. Consequently Ru_{K*} Ω^•_{]X[_{P'}/]X[_P} ≃ O_{]X[_P} (Poincaré lemma on open polydiscs and Theorem B), which gives Berthelot's Proposition 1.

**Hypotheses.**

- u need only be smooth near X; P, P' need not be smooth.

**Prerequisites.** [The tube ]T[_P of a locally closed subscheme](#target-rd-3-tube) (`RD.3/tube`), `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/raynaud-generic-fibre`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/generic-fibre-fibre-products`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/tube`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/quasi-stein-theorems-a-b`, [Étale maps induce isomorphisms of tubes](#target-rd-3-etale-tube-isomorphism) (`RD.3/etale-tube-isomorphism`).

**Sources.**

- [S20](#source-20), (1.4) Lemme 1, p. 13. Statement (read from the page image).
- [S20](#source-20), Introduction, p. 8. Berthelot defers proofs to his preprint [3a] (read from the page image).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Locally on P', choose t_1..t_n ∈ Γ(P', O) vanishing on X whose differentials form a basis of Ω_{P'/P} near X; then P' → P ×_O Â^n_O is étale near X and maps X into the zero section.
2. For an étale morphism inducing an isomorphism on X the tubes are isomorphic (Hensel/infinitesimal lifting on each residue class); the tube of the zero section of Â^n over P is ]X[_P × D(0,1^-)^n.
3. Proved in Berthelot 96-03, Théorème (1.3.2), p. 40 (and the remark after it for closed tubes of radius λ → 1): assume X closed in P and P′, P′ smooth over P, and the conormal sheaf of X in P′ ×_P X free on an affine covering; sections t_1, …, t_d lifting a regular sequence of generators give an étale map from P′ to the relative formal affine space P × Â^d near X, sending X to the zero section; by etale-tube-isomorphism the tube of X in P′ is the tube of the zero section, which is ]X[_P × D(0, 1^−)^d. The Poincaré-lemma consequence stated in the main node follows as there.

**Checks.**

- X = a point x ∈ A^1_k, P = Â^1_O, P' = Â^2_O → P the first projection: ]x[_{P'} = ]x[_P × D(0,1^-) (a residue polydisc).

<a id="target-rd-3-etale-strict-neighbourhood-isomorphism"></a>

### Étale morphisms proper over the closure of X induce isomorphisms of strict neighbourhoods

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/etale-strict-neighbourhood-isomorphism` · theorem

Let X ⊆ Y be an open immersion of k-schemes of finite type, i: Y → P and i′: Y′ → P′ closed immersions into formal O-schemes of finite type, v: Y′ → Y and u: P′ → P morphisms with u∘i′ = i∘v and v restricting to the identity on X ⊆ Y′ (X open in Y′). Let X̄ be the closure of X in P′ ×_P Y. If u is étale on a neighbourhood of X and the restriction of v to X̄ is proper, then u_K induces an isomorphism from a strict neighbourhood of ]X[_{P′} in ]Y′[_{P′} onto a strict neighbourhood of ]X[_P in ]Y[_P.

**Hypotheses.**

- Properness of v on the closure of X is essential: it is used to show that the closure of the relevant analytic domain is finite over P_K.
- The étaleness of u is required only near X; P and P′ may be singular along Y ∖ X and Y′ ∖ X.
