**Prerequisites.** [Étale maps induce isomorphisms of tubes](#target-rd-3-etale-tube-isomorphism) (`RD.3/etale-tube-isomorphism`), [Strict neighbourhoods: admissible-covering definition, criterion and standard systems](#target-rd-3-standard-strict-neighbourhoods) (`RD.3/standard-strict-neighbourhoods`), [Strict neighbourhoods of ]X[ in ]Y[](#target-rd-3-strict-neighbourhood) (`RD.3/strict-neighbourhood`), `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-maximum-modulus`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/jacobian-criterion-closed-subspace`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/formal-rigid-properness-comparison`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/quasi-finite-and-finiteness-criteria`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper`.

**Sources.**

- [S62](#source-62), (1.3.4)–(1.3.5) Théorème and its proof, pp. 41–44. States and proves that an étale morphism of formal schemes, proper on the closure of X, induces an isomorphism between strict neighbourhoods of the tubes of X, by isolating an open and closed analytic domain, proving it étale over P_K by the Jacobian criterion and maximum principle, and finite via Raynaud's properness comparison.
- [S24](#source-24), 2.10.2 Proposition, p. 85. Restates the result in the language of V-triples (étale around Y, proper, isomorphism on X) and deduces that pullback of coherent j†-modules is an equivalence with quasi-inverse the direct image, citing Berthelot's Théorème 1.3.5.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Reduce to v proper with v^{-1}(X) = X by replacing Y′ with X̄ (standard-strict-neighbourhoods (d)); localise on a finite affine covering of P, and on a finite covering of X, so that P = Spf A, X = D(g) ∩ Y, and the standard neighbourhoods are built from U_η = {|g| ≥ η}; after the base change P_1 = Spf A{T}/(f_i^q − aT_i) one may assume [Y]_λ = P_K (Berthelot 96-03, proof of (1.3.5), pp. 42–43).
2. Write P′ ×_P Y = Y′ ⊔ D with X open and closed in P′ ×_P X (u étale with a section over X). Choose μ < 1 with P′_K ∖ ]Y′[ ⊆ [D]_μ and then λ_0 < 1 with P′_K ∖ ]D[_μ ⊆ [Y′]_{λ_0}; by the maximum principle, for each λ ≥ λ_0 there is η < 1 with [Y′]_λ ∩ [D]_μ ∩ U′_η = ∅, so T_K = [Y′]_λ ∩ U′_η is open and closed, hence a closed analytic subspace of U′_η.
3. By the Jacobian criterion the non-smooth and non-étale loci of T_K → P_K are closed analytic subsets missing ]X[_{P′} (where etale-tube-isomorphism applies), so after enlarging η the map T_K → U_η is étale; after one more base change T_K is closed in P′_K, its schematic closure T in P′ has special fibre inside Y′, hence is proper over P because v is proper.
4. By the comparison of formal and rigid properness T_K → P_K is proper, hence finite since it is étale (quasi-finite and proper implies finite), given by a coherent O_{P_K}-algebra 𝓇. The map O_{P_K} → 𝓇 is an isomorphism over ]X[_P, and its kernel and cokernel are supported on closed analytic subsets missing ]X[_P, so it is an isomorphism over U_η for η close to 1; thus T_K ∩ U′_η → U_η is an isomorphism, which gives the required strict neighbourhoods.

**Checks.**

- Degenerate case: Y′ = Y and u = id give the identity on any strict neighbourhood.
- Open immersion: if u is the inclusion of an open formal subscheme P′ ⊆ P containing Y and Y′ = Y, the strict neighbourhoods of ]X[ in ]Y[_{P′} and in ]Y[_P coincide.
- Non-example showing properness is needed: P = Spf O⟨t⟩, Y = A^1_k, X = G_m = Y ∖ {0}, P′ = Spf O⟨t, t^{-1}⟩ the open formal subscheme over X, Y′ = X and v the inclusion, which is not proper. Then ]Y′[_{P′} = {|t| = 1} = ]X[_P, which is not a strict neighbourhood of ]X[_P in the closed unit disc ]Y[_P, because the covering of the closed disc by the annulus |t| = 1 and the open disc |t| < 1 is not admissible.

<a id="target-rd-3-strong-fibration-theorem"></a>

### Strong fibration theorem: strict neighbourhoods along smooth morphisms

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/strong-fibration-theorem` · theorem

Let (X,Y,P) and (X,Y′,P′) be frames, with a smooth formal map u:P′→P near X and a map v:Y′→Y identical on X. Require v restricted to the closure of X in P′×_P Y to be proper. Choose sections t₁,…,t_d of the ideal of Y′ in P′ whose classes form a basis over X of the relative conormal sheaf. The coordinate morphism ψ:P′→P×Â^d is étale near X and induces an isomorphism between cofinal strict-neighbourhood systems. A cofinal system has the form ⋃_n(([Y]_(λ_n)∩U_(η_n))×D(0,λ_n⁺)^d), with λ_n,η_n increasing to one. Over the tube ]X[_P the fibre is the open unit polydisc; this is not a fixed open-disc product over every point of a strict neighbourhood. The resulting pullback gives the overconvergent de Rham and coefficient comparisons.

**Hypotheses.**

- The proper-closure, smoothness and relative conormal-coordinate hypotheses above are required; localise on X to obtain the coordinates.

**Prerequisites.** [Weak fibration theorem: tubes along smooth morphisms are open polydisc fibrations](#target-rd-3-weak-fibration-theorem) (`RD.3/weak-fibration-theorem`), [Strict neighbourhoods of ]X[ in ]Y[](#target-rd-3-strict-neighbourhood) (`RD.3/strict-neighbourhood`), `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/raynaud-generic-fibre`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/generic-fibre-fibre-products`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/tube`, [Étale morphisms proper over the closure of X induce isomorphisms of strict neighbourhoods](#target-rd-3-etale-strict-neighbourhood-isomorphism) (`RD.3/etale-strict-neighbourhood-isomorphism`), [Strict neighbourhoods: admissible-covering definition, criterion and standard systems](#target-rd-3-standard-strict-neighbourhoods) (`RD.3/standard-strict-neighbourhoods`).

**Sources.**

- [S20](#source-20), (2.3), p. 18. Berthelot's description of the needed boundary analysis (read from the page image).
- [S20](#source-20), (2.3) Théorème 1, p. 18. The cohomological consequence (read from the page image).
- [S35](#source-35), Théorème 1.3.7 and Remarque 1.3.8, global pp. 44–45 (I, pp. 20–21). Specifies the relative conormal-coordinate and cofinal strict-neighbourhood version.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Proved in Berthelot 96-03, Théorème (1.3.7) with (1.3.4)–(1.3.5), pp. 41–45. The properness hypothesis is that v restricted to the closure X̄ of X in P′ ×_P Y is proper (for instance v proper); the local hypothesis is that sections t_1, …, t_d of the ideal of Y′ in P′ induce a basis, over X, of the conormal sheaf of Y′ in P′ ×_P Y (Berthelot asks for the basis over X only; the properness condition is the one on X̄), which holds locally by (1.3.8)(i) when P, P′ are affine, Z = Y ∩ V(g) and the conormal sheaf is free. Then the P-morphism ψ: P′ → P × Â^d defined by the t_i is étale near X, and etale-strict-neighbourhood-isomorphism applied to ψ gives the isomorphism of strict neighbourhoods; (1.3.8)(ii) identifies a strict neighbourhood upstairs with ⋃_n ([Y]_{λ_n} ∩ U_{η_n}) × D(0, λ_n^+)^d over the standard neighbourhood V_{λ,η} = ⋃_n ([Y]_{λ_n} ∩ U_{η_n}): a union of products whose polydisc radius λ_n tends to 1. Over a point of the tube ]X[_P the fibre is the open polydisc D(0, 1^−)^d, but over a point of V_{λ,η} outside the tube it is a closed polydisc of radius < 1; the main node's isomorphism "V′ ≅ V × D(0,1^−)^n over V" is to be read in this sense, which is what Berthelot proves and what its consequences (sections over strict neighbourhoods, the cohomology and isocrystal comparisons) use.

**Checks.**

- For a formal projection with zero section, the cofinal neighbourhood is a union of products with closed-polydisc radii tending to one. At a point of ]X[ its fibre is the open unit polydisc; at a boundary point the radius can be strictly less than one.

<a id="target-rd-3-overconvergent-isocrystal"></a>

### Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal` · definition

Let (X, Y, P) be a frame, p_1, p_2 : ]Y[_{P×P} → ]Y[_P the projections (Y embedded diagonally) and j† the functors on ]Y[_{P^m}. An isocrystal on X overconvergent along Z = Y \ X (relative to K, realised on P) is a j†O_{]Y[_P}-module E, locally free of finite rank, with an isomorphism ε : p_2^*E ≅ p_1^*E of j†O_{]Y[_{P²}}-modules satisfying the usual cocycle condition on ]Y[_{P³} (and ε restricting to the identity on the diagonal). Morphisms are j†O-linear maps compatible with ε. Equivalently (RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal-connection-form) it is a locally free module M with integrable connection ∇ on some strict neighbourhood V of ]X[_P in ]Y[_P whose Taylor series is induced by an analytic isomorphism p_2^*M ≅ p_1^*M on a strict neighbourhood of ]X[_{P²} in ]Y[_{P²}, two such data being identified when they agree on a smaller strict neighbourhood. The category is denoted Isoc(X, Y, P/K) (Isoc†(X ⊂ Y/K) after RD.3/independence-of-frame).

**Hypotheses.**

- The convergence condition on the Taylor isomorphism is real extra data without Frobenius (Kedlaya, Notes Remark 2.12); with a Frobenius structure it is automatic (Berthelot 96-03 Théorème 2.5.7, quoted by Kedlaya).
- Coherent j†O-modules with such a stratification are automatically locally free (a coherent module with a connection on a smooth rigid space is locally free, Kedlaya Notes Remark 2.3; Kedlaya Finiteness Lemma 3.3.4 for dagger algebras).

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Isocrystals/Overconvergent`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Berthelot's functor j† of overconvergent sections](#target-rd-3-j-dagger) (`RD.3/j-dagger`), [Frames (X ⊂ Y ⊂ P)](#target-rd-3-frame) (`RD.3/frame`), [Strict neighbourhoods of ]X[ in ]Y[](#target-rd-3-strict-neighbourhood) (`RD.3/strict-neighbourhood`), `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/raynaud-generic-fibre`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/generic-fibre-fibre-products`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/tube`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/quasi-stein-theorems-a-b`.

**Sources.**

- [S20](#source-20), (4.2.1), p. 27. The definition (read from the page image).
- [S3](#source-3), Definition 2.4, p. 3. Kedlaya's formulation (with Frobenius).

**Uses and API requirements.**

- Berthelot 1986 (4.2.4): rigid cohomology H*(]X̄[, E ⊗ Ω^•) with coefficients
- Kedlaya, Finiteness, Definition 4.2.3: coefficients of RD.4-RD.5
- RD.3/overconvergent-f-isocrystal: add a Frobenius structure
- RD.2 (local theory): restricting to a boundary annulus gives a ∇-module over the Robba ring, whose Frobenius structure makes it a (φ,∇)-module (Kedlaya Notes Remark 2.11, 4.12)

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OverconvergentIsocrystal` |  | (E, ε): locally free j†O_{]Y[_P}-module with overconvergent stratification ε : p_2^*E ≅ p_1^*E satisfying the cocycle condition. |
| `OverconvergentIsocrystal.connection` |  | The integrable connection ∇ induced by ε on a strict neighbourhood. |
| `OverconvergentIsocrystal.taylorIso` |  | The Taylor isomorphism p_2^*M ≅ p_1^*M on a strict neighbourhood of ]X[_{P²}. |
| `OverconvergentIsocrystal.Hom` |  | Morphisms: germs of horizontal maps on strict neighbourhoods. |
| `OverconvergentIsocrystal.tensor` |  | Tensor products, duals, internal Hom; the category is abelian, K-linear, rigid monoidal. |
| `OverconvergentIsocrystal.unit` |  | The unit object j†O_{]Y[} with the canonical stratification. |
| `OverconvergentIsocrystal.restrictStrictNbhd` |  | Restriction from V to a smaller strict neighbourhood V' is an isomorphism in the category. |
| `OverconvergentIsocrystal.pullback` |  | Pullback along morphisms of frames (RD.3/frame-pullback-functor), with id^* = id and (uu')^* ≅ u'^*u^*. |
| `OverconvergentIsocrystal.isLocallyFree_of_coherent` |  | A coherent j†O-module with overconvergent stratification is locally free. |

**Unit tests.**

- `OverconvergentIsocrystal.dwork_taylor` (computation): For L_π on (A^1, P^1, P̂^1), the Taylor isomorphism of the section 1 is exp π(t' − t), which converges on {|t − t'| < 1}, a strict neighbourhood of ]A^1[ in ]P^1[_{P̂^1×P̂^1} (Berthelot 4.2.3 b).
- `OverconvergentIsocrystal.unit_proper` (degenerate): If X = Y (Z = ∅), overconvergent isocrystals are convergent isocrystals on X realised on ]X[_P = P_K (Berthelot 4.2.2: the category depends only on X).
- `OverconvergentIsocrystal.restriction_iso` (characterisation): Two data on strict neighbourhoods V ⊇ V' agreeing on V' define the same object.
- `OverconvergentIsocrystal.convergent_not_overconvergent` (non-example): On (A^1, P^1, P̂^1), the rank two module with ∇e_1 = 0, ∇e_2 = e_1 ⊗ Σ_k p^k t^{p^k − 1} dt on the closed disc is a convergent isocrystal (even with Frobenius F e_2 = e_2 − t e_1 for t ↦ t^p) but is not isomorphic to the restriction of any overconvergent isocrystal (RD.3/punctured-curve-boundary-acceptance).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Well-defined as a category: the cocycle condition is the usual one for stratifications; morphisms are germs on strict neighbourhoods (RD.3/strict-neighbourhood intersections).
2. Local freeness of coherent j†O-modules with connection is Berthelot 96-03 (2.2.3)(ii); uniqueness of ε and the cocycle condition are (2.2.7)(i) (overconvergence-is-a-property). The automatic convergence with Frobenius is Théorème (2.5.7) of the 96-03 preprint (circulated since 1991 and publicly available), cited by Kedlaya as [Be4]; it is frobenius-structure-forces-overconvergence (affine case).

**Checks.**

- The constant object j†O with ε = canonical identification; the Dwork isocrystal L_π on (A^1, P^1, P̂^1) (Berthelot 4.2.3): M = O_V with ∇(1) = π dt, Taylor isomorphism ε(1) = exp π(t' − t), converging on the diagonal tube {|t − t'| < 1}; the difference-variable disc is not asserted to be larger.

<a id="target-rd-3-coherent-j-dagger-modules"></a>

### Coherent j†O-modules are germs of coherent modules on strict neighbourhoods

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/coherent-j-dagger-modules` · theorem

In the setting of RD.3/j-dagger: (a) j†O_{]Y[} is a coherent sheaf of rings, and coherent j†O_{]Y[}-modules form an abelian subcategory of all j†O_{]Y[}-modules stable under ⊗ and internal Hom. (b) Every coherent j†O_{]Y[}-module is isomorphic to j†𝓮 for a coherent O_V-module 𝓮 on some strict neighbourhood V, and for coherent 𝓮, 𝓯 on V, Hom(j†𝓮, j†𝓯) = colim_{V′ ⊆ V} Hom_{O_{V′}}(𝓮|_{V′}, 𝓯|_{V′}); thus the category of coherent j†O-modules is the 2-colimit over strict neighbourhoods of the categories of coherent modules, and E is locally free of finite rank if and only if it is j†𝓮 for a locally free 𝓮. (c) The restriction functor from coherent j†O_{]Y[}-modules to coherent O_{]X[}-modules is exact and faithful.

**Hypotheses.**

- The 2-colimit in (b) is over the filtered set of strict neighbourhoods; two coherent modules on strict neighbourhoods define the same germ if they become isomorphic on a smaller strict neighbourhood.

**Prerequisites.** [Berthelot's functor j† of overconvergent sections](#target-rd-3-j-dagger) (`RD.3/j-dagger`), [j† is exact, commutes with tensor products, is functorial and localises on X](#target-rd-3-j-dagger-exactness-and-functoriality) (`RD.3/j-dagger-exactness-and-functoriality`), [Strict neighbourhoods: admissible-covering definition, criterion and standard systems](#target-rd-3-standard-strict-neighbourhoods) (`RD.3/standard-strict-neighbourhoods`), `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid`.

**Sources.**

- [S62](#source-62), (2.1.9)–(2.1.11) with the remark after (2.1.10), pp. 56–57. Proves coherence of j†O, the description of coherent j†O-modules (and of locally free ones) as germs of coherent modules on strict neighbourhoods with the colimit formula for Hom, and faithfulness of restriction to the tube.
- [S24](#source-24), 2.9.1 Lemma, p. 84. Records exactness and faithfulness of restriction to the tube for coherent j†-modules, citing Berthelot (2.1.11).

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a): finite generation of kernels of maps (j†O)^n → j†O is checked on an admissible affinoid covering; on W ∩ ]Z[ the kernel vanishes and on W ∩ V it is j† of the kernel of a map of coherent O-modules, by exactness of j† (j-dagger-exactness-and-functoriality (a)) (Berthelot 96-03 (2.1.9), p. 56).
2. (b): first, for each λ < 1, find η and coherent models on V_λ = U_η ∩ [Y]_λ, using that [Y]_λ is quasi-compact and that on affinoids with finite presentations the statement reduces to E = j†O (formula (2.1.1.5)); then build compatible models on ⋃_{n' ≤ n} V_{n'} by induction along sequences λ_n, η_n → 1 and glue on the standard strict neighbourhood V_{λ,η}, which the V_n cover admissibly; the Hom statement is proved the same way ((2.1.10), pp. 56–57, and the remark after it).
3. (c): a morphism f = j†(g) vanishing on ]X[ has image supported on a closed analytic subset missing ]X[, which a smaller strict neighbourhood avoids ((2.1.11), p. 57); exactness is that of restriction to an open.

**Checks.**

- Affine space: the coherent j†O-modules on P^n_K for X = A^n_k correspond to finitely generated K⟨t⟩†-modules (Berthelot (2.5.2)(i) with A = O[t]).
- Faithful but not full: on the frame (A^1_k, P^1_k, P̂^1), the injection K⟨t⟩† → K⟨t⟩ is the restriction functor on global sections of the free rank-one module; the element Σ p^{⌊√n⌋} t^n of K⟨t⟩ shows Hom(j†O, j†O) = K⟨t⟩† is a proper subspace of Hom(O_{]X[}, O_{]X[}) = K⟨t⟩.
- Degenerate case: if Z = ∅, coherent j†O-modules are coherent O_{]Y[}-modules.

<a id="target-rd-3-coherent-j-dagger-gluing"></a>

### Coherent j†O-modules glue along finite open coverings of X

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/coherent-j-dagger-gluing` · theorem

Let X = X_1 ∪ … ∪ X_n be a finite open covering, j_i: X_i → Y the inclusions and j_i† the corresponding functors on ]Y[_P. (a) Given coherent (respectively locally free of finite rank) j_i†O_{]Y[}-modules E_i and isomorphisms j_{i′}†E_i ≅ j_i†E_{i′} satisfying the cocycle condition, there is a coherent (respectively locally free) j†O_{]Y[}-module E, unique up to unique isomorphism, with isomorphisms j_i†E ≅ E_i compatible with the given ones. (b) Given coherent E, F and maps φ_i: j_i†E → j_i†F with j_{i′}†φ_i = j_i†φ_{i′}, there is a unique φ: E → F with j_i†φ = φ_i. Hence X′ ↦ {coherent j_{X′}†O_{]Y[}-modules} is a stack for the Zariski topology on X (Y and P fixed).

**Hypotheses.**

- The covering is finite; for a general Zariski covering of a quasi-compact X refine to a finite one.

**Prerequisites.** [Coherent j†O-modules are germs of coherent modules on strict neighbourhoods](#target-rd-3-coherent-j-dagger-modules) (`RD.3/coherent-j-dagger-modules`), [j† is exact, commutes with tensor products, is functorial and localises on X](#target-rd-3-j-dagger-exactness-and-functoriality) (`RD.3/j-dagger-exactness-and-functoriality`), [Strict neighbourhoods: admissible-covering definition, criterion and standard systems](#target-rd-3-standard-strict-neighbourhoods) (`RD.3/standard-strict-neighbourhoods`).

**Sources.**

- [S62](#source-62), (2.1.12) Proposition, p. 58. Proves that coherent and locally free j†O-modules, and their morphisms, glue along finite open coverings of X, so that they form a stack on Y in the X variable.

**Construction or proof.**

1. By coherent-j-dagger-modules (b) each E_i is j_i†𝓮_i for a coherent 𝓮_i on a strict neighbourhood V_i of ]X_i[, and the gluing isomorphisms come from isomorphisms of models on strict neighbourhoods of ]X_i ∩ X_{i′}[ (Berthelot 96-03 (2.1.12), p. 58).
2. Shrink the V_i to standard neighbourhoods V^i_{λ,η} for a common pair of sequences; their union is the standard neighbourhood of ]X[ and they form an admissible covering of it (standard-strict-neighbourhoods (b), (d)); after shrinking once more the isomorphisms satisfy the cocycle condition on triple overlaps, so the 𝓮_i glue to a coherent 𝓮 on V and E = j†𝓮 works; uniqueness and (b) follow from the Hom formula and the Čech sequence of j-dagger-exactness-and-functoriality (d).

**Checks.**

- Covering G_m ⊂ P^1 by the two opens obtained by removing 1 and −1 (p odd): a locally free module given on each piece and agreeing on the overlap glues to a locally free j†O-module.
- Degenerate case n = 1: the gluing datum is a single module and E = E_1.
- Morphisms: the identity maps on the pieces glue to the identity of E (uniqueness in (b)).

<a id="target-rd-3-overconvergence-is-a-property"></a>

### Overconvergence of a connection is a property, local on P and on X, stable under subquotients

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/overconvergence-is-a-property` · theorem

Let (X, Y, P) be as in RD.3/j-dagger with a morphism P → S of formal O-schemes smooth on a neighbourhood of X, and let E be a coherent j†O_{]Y[}-module with an integrable connection ∇ relative to S_K. (a) (E, ∇) ≅ j†(𝓮, ∇_0) for a coherent O_V-module 𝓮 with integrable connection on some strict neighbourhood V; if S = Spf O then E is locally free of finite rank. (b) ∇ is overconvergent along Z = Y ∖ X — there is an isomorphism ε: p_2^*E ≅ p_1^*E of j†O_{]Y[_{P×_S P}}-modules inducing the Taylor isomorphisms ε_n modulo the (n+1)-st power of the diagonal ideal for all n — if and only if there is an isomorphism ε′: p_2^*𝓮 ≅ p_1^*𝓮 on a strict neighbourhood of ]X[_{P×P} in ]Y[_{P×P} inducing the Taylor isomorphisms of ∇_0. (c) If ∇ is overconvergent, ε is unique, is determined by its restriction to ]X[_{P×P}, and satisfies the cocycle condition on ]Y[_{P×P×P}; a j†O-linear map h: E → F between overconvergent modules is compatible with the ε if and only if h|_{]X[} is horizontal; a section s satisfies ε(p_2^*s) = p_1^*s if and only if s|_{]X[} is horizontal; coherent sub-j†O-modules stable under ∇ and the corresponding quotients are again overconvergent. (d) Overconvergence can be tested on an open covering of P and on a finite open covering of X. (e) Coherent j†O-modules with integrable overconvergent connection form an abelian category with ⊗ and internal Hom, the forgetful functor to coherent j†O-modules is exact, the category is a full subcategory of coherent j†O-modules with integrable connection, and restriction to ]X[ is an exact faithful functor to coherent O_{]X[}-modules with convergent integrable connection.

**Hypotheses.**

- K has characteristic 0 (needed for (a) and for the description of connections by divided-power Taylor series).
- P → S is smooth only near X; by RD.3/j-dagger and the Jacobian criterion the smooth locus of P_K → S_K is a strict neighbourhood of ]X[.

**Prerequisites.** [Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-isocrystal) (`RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal`), [Weak fibration theorem: tubes along smooth morphisms are open polydisc fibrations](#target-rd-3-weak-fibration-theorem) (`RD.3/weak-fibration-theorem`), [Coherent j†O-modules are germs of coherent modules on strict neighbourhoods](#target-rd-3-coherent-j-dagger-modules) (`RD.3/coherent-j-dagger-modules`), [Coherent j†O-modules glue along finite open coverings of X](#target-rd-3-coherent-j-dagger-gluing) (`RD.3/coherent-j-dagger-gluing`), [j† is exact, commutes with tensor products, is functorial and localises on X](#target-rd-3-j-dagger-exactness-and-functoriality) (`RD.3/j-dagger-exactness-and-functoriality`), `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-maximum-modulus`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/jacobian-criterion-closed-subspace`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.1/integrable-connection`.

**Sources.**

- [S62](#source-62), (2.2.1)–(2.2.11) with the remark after (2.2.11), pp. 58–64. Defines overconvergent connections by the existence of the global Taylor isomorphism on the tube of Y in P×P, shows it is a property (unique, determined on the tube of X), local on P and on X, inherited by sub- and quotient objects, and that the category is abelian with ⊗ and internal Hom and a full subcategory of modules with connection.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a): apply coherent-j-dagger-modules (b) to E and to the Taylor isomorphisms on the first-order neighbourhoods in the double and triple products; local freeness of a coherent module with connection in characteristic 0 is the classical argument (Berthelot 96-03 (2.2.3), p. 60).
2. (b): if ε′ exists, ε = j′†(ε′) using that j† commutes with the projections and the diagonal (j-dagger-exactness-and-functoriality (b)); conversely write ε = j′†(ε′) on a standard strict neighbourhood and show that ε′ induces the Taylor isomorphisms after shrinking: the kernel of restriction to ]X[ of sections of 𝓮 has support a closed analytic subset missing ]X[, avoided by U_η for η near 1 ((2.2.6), pp. 61–62).
3. (c): by faithfulness of restriction to the tube (coherent-j-dagger-modules (c)) reduce to Y = X; cover the closed tubes [X]_{P²,λ} by products W × D(0, λ^+)^m (weak fibration theorem, RD.3/weak-fibration-theorem), and use injectivity of M ⊗_A A{τ} → M ⊗_A A[[τ]] to see that ε is determined by its Taylor expansion; subobjects use flatness of the projections on the smooth locus, a strict neighbourhood ((2.2.1), pp. 58–59; (2.2.7), pp. 62–63).
4. (d): ε's obtained on an open covering of P glue by uniqueness ((2.2.8), p. 63); for a finite covering of X apply coherent-j-dagger-gluing (b) to the maps p_2^*E → p_1^*E ((2.2.11), pp. 63–64). (e) follows from (c), coherent-j-dagger-modules (a) and (c) ((2.2.9), (2.2.10), p. 63).

**Checks.**

- Dwork: on (A^1_k, P^1_k, P̂^1_O) with K = ℚ_p(π), π^{p−1} = −p, the module j†O with ∇(1) = −π dt is overconvergent: its Taylor isomorphism is multiplication by exp(−π(t′ − t)), analytic on the strict neighbourhood |t′ − t| < 1 of the diagonal tube (Berthelot (2.2.15)(ii)(a), (1.2.4)(iv)).
- Non-example: j†O with ∇(1) = −dt on the same frame is not overconvergent, not even convergent: its Taylor series exp(−(t′ − t)) converges only for |t′ − t| < p^{−1/(p−1)} < 1.
- Subobjects: the image of a horizontal map between overconvergent modules is overconvergent by (c), so the category is abelian.

<a id="target-rd-3-taylor-series-convergence-criterion"></a>

### The coordinate criterion for convergence and overconvergence of a connection

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/taylor-series-convergence-criterion` · theorem

Assume P and S affine, Z = Y ∩ V(g) for one g ∈ Γ(P, O_P), and t_1, …, t_m ∈ Γ(P, O_P) such that dt_1, …, dt_m is a basis of Ω^1_{P/S} near X; on a strict neighbourhood of ]X[ these give a basis of Ω^1_{P_K/S_K} with dual derivations ∂_1, …, ∂_m. Let (𝓮, ∇_0) be a coherent module with integrable connection on a strict neighbourhood V and (E, ∇) = j†(𝓮, ∇_0); write ∂^{[k]} = ∂^k / k! for multi-indices k, and U_η = {x ∈ P_K : |g(x)| ≥ η}. Then ∇ is overconvergent if and only if for every λ < 1 in |K^×|^ℚ there is η < 1 in |K^×|^ℚ with [Y]_λ ∩ U_η ⊆ V such that ‖∂^{[k]} e‖ λ^{|k|} → 0 as |k| → ∞ for every e ∈ Γ([Y]_λ ∩ U_η, 𝓮), for a (any) Banach norm on this finite module over an affinoid algebra. When Z = ∅ (X closed in P), a connection on a coherent O_{]X[}-module is convergent if and only if ‖∂^{[k]} e‖ λ^{|k|} → 0 for every λ < 1 and every e ∈ Γ([X]_λ, 𝓮).

**Hypotheses.**

- Divided powers ∂^k/k! need characteristic 0.
- The criterion is coordinate-dependent in form but the conclusion is not; any other étale coordinates give the same answer (Guo–Reinecke, Remark 2.13).

**Prerequisites.** [Overconvergence of a connection is a property, local on P and on X, stable under subquotients](#target-rd-3-overconvergence-is-a-property) (`RD.3/overconvergence-is-a-property`), [Strong fibration theorem: strict neighbourhoods along smooth morphisms](#target-rd-3-strong-fibration-theorem) (`RD.3/strong-fibration-theorem`), [Strict neighbourhoods: admissible-covering definition, criterion and standard systems](#target-rd-3-standard-strict-neighbourhoods) (`RD.3/standard-strict-neighbourhoods`), `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid`.

**Sources.**

- [S62](#source-62), (2.2.12)–(2.2.14) and Exemples (2.2.15), pp. 64–67. Proves that, in coordinates, overconvergence is equivalent to the decay of the divided-power derivatives of sections on the sets [Y]_λ ∩ U_η, and convergence to the same decay on the closed tubes [X]_λ; gives the Dwork and Kummer examples.
- [S64](#source-64), Definition 2.12 and Remark 2.13, p. 15. Uses the convergent case of the criterion (cited to Berthelot's Corollary 2.2.14) as the definition of a convergent connection on the generic fibre of an affine smooth formal scheme over W(k), and notes its independence of the coordinates.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Necessity: by overconvergence-is-a-property (b), ε = j′†(ε′) on a strict neighbourhood V′ ⊇ V_{λη} := [Y]_{P²,λ} ∩ p_1^{-1}(U_η); on [Y]_{P²,λ} the conditions |1 ⊗ g| ≥ η and |g ⊗ 1| ≥ η agree for η > λ. By Berthelot's remark (1.3.8)(ii) (strong fibration theorem applied to p_1), V_{λη} ≅ ([Y]_λ ∩ U_η) × D(0, λ^+)^m with coordinates τ_i = 1 ⊗ t_i − t_i ⊗ 1 (Berthelot 96-03 (2.2.13), pp. 64–65).
2. Expanding θ(e) = ε′(p_2^*e) = Σ_k θ_k(e) ⊗ τ^k with ‖θ_k(e)‖ λ^{|k|} → 0 (Lemma (2.2.12): finite modules over A{τ} expand uniquely in τ-series), compatibility of ε′ with the Taylor isomorphisms modulo the powers of the diagonal forces θ_k(e) = ∂^{[k]} e ((2.2.4.1)).
3. Sufficiency: for a sequence λ_i → 1 and corresponding η_i, define θ(e) = Σ_k ∂^{[k]} e ⊗ τ^k on V_{λ_i η_i}; it is semilinear, so gives a linear map p_2^*𝓮 → p_1^*𝓮 inducing the Taylor isomorphisms, with inverse Σ_k (−1)^{|k|} τ^k ⊗ ∂^{[k]} e; these glue by the uniqueness argument of overconvergence-is-a-property (c) to an isomorphism on the standard strict neighbourhood V_{λ,η} ((2.2.13)(ii), p. 66). The case Z = ∅ is (2.2.14).

**Checks.**

- Dwork: for ∇(1) = −π dt on A^1 ⊂ P^1 (K = ℚ_p(π), π^{p−1} = −p), on the chart Spf O⟨t⟩, where Z is empty, ∂^{[k]}1 = (−π)^k/k! has absolute value p^{−s_p(k)/(p−1)} ≤ 1 (s_p the digit sum), so the connection is convergent there. Overconvergence along ∞ is checked on the chart Spf O⟨s⟩, s = 1/t, with g = s and U_η ∩ [Y]_λ = {η ≤ |s| ≤ 1}: there ∇(1) = π s^{−2} ds, the Taylor series of 1 is exp(π τ/(s(s + τ))) with τ = s′ − s, and expanding π τ/(s(s + τ)) = (π/s²) Σ_{j≥0} (−1)^j τ^{j+1}/s^j and using |π^n/n!| ≤ 1 gives ‖∂_s^{[k]}1‖ ≤ η^{−2k} on that annulus; so ‖∂_s^{[k]}1‖ λ^k → 0 once η² > λ, and the connection is overconvergent. Computing only on the chart at 0, where Z is empty, would test convergence and not overconvergence.
- Kummer: for ∇(1) = a dt/t on G_m ⊂ P^1 with a ∈ ℤ_p, ∂^{[k]}1 = binom(a, k) t^{−k} with |binom(a, k)| ≤ 1, so on {η ≤ |t| ≤ 1/η} the norms are ≤ η^{−k} and λ^k η^{−k} → 0 for η > λ: overconvergent.
- Non-examples: for ∇(1) = −dt, ‖∂^{[k]}1‖ = |1/k!| = p^{v_p(k!)} and λ^k p^{v_p(k!)} → ∞ for λ > p^{−1/(p−1)}; for a = 1/p in the Kummer example |binom(1/p, k)| = p^{k + v_p(k!)} is unbounded, so neither is even convergent.

<a id="target-rd-3-overconvergent-isocrystal-connection-form"></a>

### Stratifications versus connections with overconvergent Taylor series

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal-connection-form` · lemma

For a frame (X, Y, P), the functor (E, ε) ↦ (E|_V, ∇) is an equivalence between overconvergent isocrystals in the stratification form (RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal) and locally free modules with integrable connection on strict neighbourhoods V of ]X[_P in ]Y[_P whose formal Taylor isomorphism ε(1 ⊗ m) = Σ_q (1/q!) ∇(D)^q(m) ⊗ τ^q (τ_i = 1 ⊗ t_i − t_i ⊗ 1 for local coordinates t_i on P near X) is induced by an analytic isomorphism p_2^*M ≅ p_1^*M on a strict neighbourhood of ]X[_{P²} in ]Y[_{P²}.

**Hypotheses.**

- P smooth near X with local coordinates t_1..t_n; the diagonal P → P × P is then a closed immersion with ]X[_P → ]X[_{P²} a fibration in open unit polydiscs (RD.3/weak-fibration-theorem).

**Prerequisites.** [Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-isocrystal) (`RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal`), [Weak fibration theorem: tubes along smooth morphisms are open polydisc fibrations](#target-rd-3-weak-fibration-theorem) (`RD.3/weak-fibration-theorem`), [Strict neighbourhoods of ]X[ in ]Y[](#target-rd-3-strict-neighbourhood) (`RD.3/strict-neighbourhood`), [Overconvergence of a connection is a property, local on P and on X, stable under subquotients](#target-rd-3-overconvergence-is-a-property) (`RD.3/overconvergence-is-a-property`), [The coordinate criterion for convergence and overconvergence of a connection](#target-rd-3-taylor-series-convergence-criterion) (`RD.3/taylor-series-convergence-criterion`).

**Sources.**

- [S20](#source-20), (4.2.1), p. 27. Statement (read from the page image).
- [S20](#source-20), (4.1), p. 25. The convergent (non-overconvergent) analogue (read from the page image).

**Construction or proof.**

1. ε ↦ ∇: restrict ε to the first-order infinitesimal neighbourhood of the diagonal (Berthelot 4.1).
2. ∇ ↦ ε: the Taylor series defines ε on the formal completion of the diagonal; the convergence hypothesis says it is induced by an analytic isomorphism on a strict neighbourhood; the cocycle condition holds formally, hence analytically since the tube of the diagonal is a polydisc fibration over ]X[ (RD.3/weak-fibration-theorem) and analytic functions on open polydiscs are determined by their Taylor expansion along the centre section (Berthelot 4.1, 4.2.1).
3. Berthelot 96-03 (2.2.6) (overconvergence via an isomorphism on a strict neighbourhood of the diagonal tube) and (2.2.13) (the coordinate criterion) prove this lemma; see overconvergence-is-a-property (b) and taylor-series-convergence-criterion.

**Checks.**

- Dwork: ∇(1) = π dt gives Σ_q (1/q!) π^q (t' − t)^q = exp π(t' − t) (Berthelot 4.2.3).

<a id="target-rd-3-frame-pullback-functor"></a>

### Pullback of overconvergent isocrystals along morphisms of frames

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/frame-pullback-functor` · construction

For a morphism of frames (w, v, u) : (X', Y', P') → (X, Y, P) the pullback u^* : Isoc(X, Y, P/K) → Isoc(X', Y', P'/K) sends (E, ε) to (j'†u_K^* E, (u×u)^*ε), using that u_K maps strict neighbourhoods of ]X'[ into strict neighbourhoods of ]X[ (RD.3/strict-neighbourhood); in connection form it is the usual pullback of modules with connection. It is compatible with composition up to canonical isomorphism, with ⊗ and duals, and (for Frobenius structures) with Frobenius pullbacks.

**Hypotheses.**

- The functor depends on (w, v, u); RD.3/taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks shows that for fixed (w, v) it is independent of u up to canonical isomorphism.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Isocrystals/Overconvergent`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-isocrystal) (`RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal`), [Strict neighbourhoods of ]X[ in ]Y[](#target-rd-3-strict-neighbourhood) (`RD.3/strict-neighbourhood`), [Berthelot's functor j† of overconvergent sections](#target-rd-3-j-dagger) (`RD.3/j-dagger`), [Frames (X ⊂ Y ⊂ P)](#target-rd-3-frame) (`RD.3/frame`).

**Sources.**

- [S20](#source-20), (4.2.1), p. 27. Functoriality in the frame (read from the page image).

**Uses and API requirements.**

- RD.3/independence-of-frame: equivalences are pullbacks along smooth frame morphisms
- RD.3/overconvergent-f-isocrystal: Frobenius pullback F^* is a pullback along a lift of Frobenius
- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4: functoriality of rigid cohomology

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OverconvergentIsocrystal.pullbackFunctor` |  | u^* for a morphism of frames. |
| `OverconvergentIsocrystal.pullback_id` |  | id^* ≅ id. |
| `OverconvergentIsocrystal.pullback_comp` |  | (u∘u')^* ≅ u'^* ∘ u^* canonically, satisfying the associativity coherence. |
| `OverconvergentIsocrystal.pullback_tensor` |  | u^*(E ⊗ F) ≅ u^*E ⊗ u^*F; u^* preserves duals and the unit. |
| `OverconvergentIsocrystal.pullback_connection` |  | In connection form u^* is the pullback of modules with connection on strict neighbourhoods. |

**Unit tests.**

- `OverconvergentIsocrystal.pullback_unit` (degenerate): u^*(j†O_{]Y[_P}) ≅ j'†O_{]Y'[_{P'}}.
- `OverconvergentIsocrystal.pullback_dwork` (computation): For the Frobenius lift t ↦ t^p of P̂^1, the pullback of L_π has ∇(1) = πp t^{p−1} dt (Berthelot 4.2.3 c).
- `OverconvergentIsocrystal.pullback_comp_test` (characterisation): For composable frame morphisms the canonical isomorphism (uu')^* ≅ u'^*u^* is the identity on underlying modules with connection.
- `OverconvergentIsocrystal.pullback_not_equiv_nonsmooth` (non-example): Pullback along the frame morphism ({0}, {0}, Spf O) → (A^1, P^1, P̂^1), which is not smooth, is not an equivalence: L_π and the unit object both pull back to the unit object on the point, but L_π ≇ O since its only candidate horizontal sections c·exp(−πt) converge only on |t| < 1, not on a strict neighbourhood.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Pullback of stratifications along u × u : ]Y'[_{P'²} → ]Y[_{P²}; strictness of neighbourhoods by RD.3/strict-neighbourhood (pullback API); locally free modules pull back to locally free modules.

**Checks.**

- Pullback along the identity is the identity; pullback of the unit object is the unit object.

<a id="target-rd-3-taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks"></a>

### Canonical isomorphisms between pullbacks along frame morphisms with the same reduction

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks` · lemma

Let f, g : (X', Y', P') → (X, Y, P) be two morphisms of frames inducing the same morphisms X' → X and Y' → Y. For an overconvergent isocrystal (E, ε) on (X, Y, P), the pullback of ε along (f, g) : ]Y'[_{P'} → ]Y[_{P×P} defines an isomorphism χ_{f,g} : g^*E ≅ f^*E of overconvergent isocrystals; χ_{f,f} = id and χ_{f,g}∘χ_{g,h} = χ_{f,h}.

**Hypotheses.**

- (f, g) maps X' into the diagonal image of X, hence ]X'[_{P'} into ]X[_{P×P}, and strict neighbourhoods into strict neighbourhoods (RD.3/strict-neighbourhood).

**Prerequisites.** [Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-isocrystal) (`RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal`), [Pullback of overconvergent isocrystals along morphisms of frames](#target-rd-3-frame-pullback-functor) (`RD.3/frame-pullback-functor`), [Strict neighbourhoods of ]X[ in ]Y[](#target-rd-3-strict-neighbourhood) (`RD.3/strict-neighbourhood`), [The tube ]T[_P of a locally closed subscheme](#target-rd-3-tube) (`RD.3/tube`), [Overconvergence of a connection is a property, local on P and on X, stable under subquotients](#target-rd-3-overconvergence-is-a-property) (`RD.3/overconvergence-is-a-property`).

**Sources.**

- [S8](#source-8), Remark 4.1.9, p. 17. Local analogue on annuli.
- [S4](#source-4), Definition 4.2.3, p. 26. The role of the convergence condition in comparing pullbacks.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Pull back the stratification along (f, g); the cocycle identity for ε on ]Y[_{P³} pulled back along (f, g, h) gives the transitivity (standard crystal formalism; local analogue: Kedlaya overview Remark 4.1.9 for annuli).
2. Berthelot 96-03 (2.2.17), pp. 67–68: the isomorphism χ is h_K^*(ε) for h = (u, u′): P′ → P ×_S P, horizontal, with the transitivity (2.2.17.3) from the cocycle condition on the triple product; uniqueness of ε (overconvergence-is-a-property (c)) makes it canonical.

**Checks.**

- For f = g the isomorphism is the identity; for two Frobenius lifts f, g of P̂^1 inducing t ↦ t^p mod π, χ_{f,g} on L_π is multiplication by exp π(g(t) − f(t)).

<a id="target-rd-3-independence-of-frame"></a>

### Independence of the frame: canonical equivalences between categories of overconvergent isocrystals

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/independence-of-frame` · theorem

(a) If (id_X, id_Y, u) : (X, Y, P') → (X, Y, P) is a morphism of frames with u smooth in a neighbourhood of X, then u^* : Isoc(X, Y, P/K) → Isoc(X, Y, P'/K) is an equivalence of categories. (b) For two frames (X, Y, P_1), (X, Y, P_2) with the same (X, Y), the projections from the diagonal frame (X, Y, P_1 ×_O P_2) are smooth near X, and the composite equivalences E_{12} := (p_2^*)^{-1}∘p_1^* are canonical: independent of choices up to unique isomorphism and satisfying E_{23}∘E_{12} ≅ E_{13}. Hence Isoc†(X ⊂ Y/K) := Isoc(X, Y, P/K) depends only on (X ⊂ Y) up to canonical equivalence, is local on Y, and is functorial in (X ⊂ Y). The same holds with Frobenius structures (RD.3/overconvergent-f-isocrystal).

**Hypotheses.**

- P, P_i smooth near X; no hypothesis at the points of Z (Berthelot 2.3 remark).
- For Y without a global embedding into a formal scheme smooth near X, the category is defined by gluing along a Čech covering by frames (RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystals-of-a-variety).

**Prerequisites.** [Canonical isomorphisms between pullbacks along frame morphisms with the same reduction](#target-rd-3-taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks) (`RD.3/taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks`), [Strong fibration theorem: strict neighbourhoods along smooth morphisms](#target-rd-3-strong-fibration-theorem) (`RD.3/strong-fibration-theorem`), [Pullback of overconvergent isocrystals along morphisms of frames](#target-rd-3-frame-pullback-functor) (`RD.3/frame-pullback-functor`), [Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-isocrystal) (`RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal`), [Frames (X ⊂ Y ⊂ P)](#target-rd-3-frame) (`RD.3/frame`), [Étale morphisms proper over the closure of X induce isomorphisms of strict neighbourhoods](#target-rd-3-etale-strict-neighbourhood-isomorphism) (`RD.3/etale-strict-neighbourhood-isomorphism`), [Overconvergence of a connection is a property, local on P and on X, stable under subquotients](#target-rd-3-overconvergence-is-a-property) (`RD.3/overconvergence-is-a-property`), [Coherent j†O-modules glue along finite open coverings of X](#target-rd-3-coherent-j-dagger-gluing) (`RD.3/coherent-j-dagger-gluing`).

**Sources.**

- [S20](#source-20), (4.2.1), p. 27. Statement (read from the page image).
- [S4](#source-4), Remark 4.2.4, p. 26. Nature of the equivalences.

**Construction or proof.**

1. If u has a section s : P → P' over (X, Y), then s^* and u^* are quasi-inverse: s^*u^* = (us)^* = id and u^*s^* = (su)^* ≅ id^* by RD.3/taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks (su and id_{P'} induce the same maps on X, Y).
2. In general, by RD.3/strong-fibration-theorem, locally on P there are strict neighbourhoods V' ≅ V × D(0,1^-)^n, so sections exist locally over strict neighbourhoods; the local quasi-inverses are compatible on overlaps by RD.3/taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks and glue (descent of overconvergent isocrystals along admissible coverings of strict neighbourhoods, a stack property).
3. (b) The diagonal immersion Y → P_1 × P_2 is a closed immersion and the projections are smooth near X since P_i are; canonicity and the cocycle from RD.3/taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks ('méthode du plongement diagonal', Berthelot 1.5).
4. Part (a) is Berthelot 96-03 Théorème (2.3.1), pp. 68–69: localise on P and on X (overconvergence-is-a-property (d), coherent-j-dagger-gluing), reduce by the strong fibration theorem (etale-strict-neighbourhood-isomorphism applied to ψ: P′ → P × Â^d) to P′ = P × Â^d with the zero section s; s_K^* is a left quasi-inverse and u_K^* s_K^* ≅ id by RD.3/taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks because s ∘ u and id agree on Y. Part (b) is (2.3.2)(i), p. 69, by the diagonal embedding; the case without a global embedding is isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames.

**Checks.**

- Two embeddings of affine space: (A^n, P^n, P̂^n) and (A^n, P^n, P̂^n ×_O P̂^n) (diagonal) give canonically equivalent categories; see RD.3/affine-space-two-embeddings-acceptance for two different compactifications.
- For X smooth affine with lift A and two choices of presentation, the equivalence transports the (σ,∇)-module over A† ⊗ K realised in one presentation to the other by the Taylor isomorphism (Kedlaya Finiteness Remark 4.2.4: 'homotopy equivalences').

<a id="target-rd-3-isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames"></a>

### Overconvergent isocrystals without a global frame: gluing, realisations and pullback

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames` · construction

Let X ⊆ Y be an open immersion of k-schemes of finite type over a formal O-scheme S of finite type. Choose a finite open covering (Y_α) of Y and closed immersions Y_α → P_α into formal S-schemes smooth near X_α = X ∩ Y_α; put Y_{αβ} = Y_α ∩ Y_β embedded diagonally in P_{αβ} = P_α ×_S P_β, with projections p_{αβ}, q_{αβ}. The category Isoc(X, Y/S) consists of families (E_α, φ_{αβ}) with E_α a coherent j†O_{]Y_α[}-module with integrable overconvergent connection and φ_{αβ}: p_{αβ,K}^* E_α ≅ q_{αβ,K}^* E_β horizontal isomorphisms on ]Y_{αβ}[_{P_{αβ}} satisfying the cocycle condition on ]Y_{αβγ}[_{P_α×P_β×P_γ}; morphisms are compatible families. (a) Up to canonical equivalence it does not depend on the covering or on the P_α, and equals Isoc(X, Y, P/S) when a global P exists. (b) For any immersion of an open U ⊆ Y into a formal S-scheme T (not necessarily smooth), each E has a realisation E_T on ]U[_T: locally E_T = u_K^* E_P for an S-morphism u: T → P to a smooth embedding of U restricting to the identity on U, independent of P and u up to canonical isomorphism, with canonical horizontal transition isomorphisms u_K^* E_T ≅ E_{T′} for S-morphisms u: T′ → T, satisfying transitivity. (c) For a commutative diagram (X′ ⊆ Y′ over S′) → (X ⊆ Y over S) given by v: Y′ → Y over S′ → S, there is a pullback functor v^*: Isoc(X, Y/S) → Isoc(X′, Y′/S′), realised by u_K^* for any lift u of v between embeddings, independent of u up to canonical isomorphism, with (v ∘ v′)^* ≅ v′^* ∘ v^* canonically.

**Hypotheses.**

- Frames exist locally: every affine open of Y embeds as a closed subscheme of a formal affine space over S, which is smooth.
- In (b) for O a discrete valuation ring, T may be any formal S-scheme in which U is defined by an ideal of definition (Berthelot (2.3.2)(ii), last paragraph): the lift u: T → P is built successively on the thickenings Spec O_T/𝓲^{i+1} by formal smoothness of P.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Isocrystals/Overconvergent`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Independence of the frame: canonical equivalences between categories of overconvergent isocrystals](#target-rd-3-independence-of-frame) (`RD.3/independence-of-frame`), [Canonical isomorphisms between pullbacks along frame morphisms with the same reduction](#target-rd-3-taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks) (`RD.3/taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks`), [Pullback of overconvergent isocrystals along morphisms of frames](#target-rd-3-frame-pullback-functor) (`RD.3/frame-pullback-functor`), [Overconvergence of a connection is a property, local on P and on X, stable under subquotients](#target-rd-3-overconvergence-is-a-property) (`RD.3/overconvergence-is-a-property`), [Coherent j†O-modules glue along finite open coverings of X](#target-rd-3-coherent-j-dagger-gluing) (`RD.3/coherent-j-dagger-gluing`), [Frames (X ⊂ Y ⊂ P)](#target-rd-3-frame) (`RD.3/frame`).

**Sources.**

- [S62](#source-62), (2.3.2)(i)–(iv) and (2.2.17), pp. 67–72. Defines Isoc(X, Y/S) via a smooth embedding, the realisations E_T on arbitrary embeddings with transition isomorphisms, the gluing definition when no global embedding exists (independence of choices left to the reader), and the pullback functors with their compatibility with composition.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystals-of-a-variety: defines Isoc†(X ⊂ Y/K) when Y has no global embedding, by gluing along local frames
- Étesse 2002, proof of Théorème 1, pp. 593–595: the étale descent theorem glues local overconvergent F-isocrystals built on charts with no global embedding, citing Berthelot (2.3.2)(iii)
- Kedlaya, Notes on isocrystals, Definitions 2.4 and 2.7, pp. 3–4: extends the affine construction to arbitrary open immersions X → Y using the stack property
- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4: rigid cohomology with coefficients is computed from realisations on local frames and Čech gluing

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `IsocDagger.ofGluingData` |  | An object of Isoc(X, Y/S) from overconvergent modules E_α on local frames and horizontal transition isomorphisms φ_{αβ} satisfying the cocycle condition. |
| `IsocDagger.realisation` |  | The realisation E_T, a coherent j†O_{]U[_T}-module with integrable connection, for an immersion of an open U ⊆ Y into a formal S-scheme T. |
| `IsocDagger.realisation_transition` |  | For u: T′ → T compatible with the immersions, a horizontal isomorphism u_K^* E_T ≅ E_{T′}, transitive for composable u. |
| `IsocDagger.gluing_equivalence` |  | Changing the covering or the local embeddings gives a canonical equivalence of gluing categories, compatible with realisations. |
| `IsocDagger.ofFrame_equivalence` |  | When a global frame (X, Y, P) exists, the gluing category is canonically equivalent to Isoc(X, Y, P/S) of RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal. |
| `IsocDagger.pullback` |  | The pullback v^* along v: (X′ ⊆ Y′/S′) → (X ⊆ Y/S), realised by u_K^* for any lift u. |
| `IsocDagger.pullback_comp` |  | Canonical isomorphisms (v ∘ v′)^* ≅ v′^* ∘ v^* and id^* ≅ id, satisfying the usual coherence. |
| `IsocDagger.horizontalSections` |  | The module Γ((X, Y)/S, E) of horizontal sections, independent of the realisation used to compute it. |

**Unit tests.**

- `IsocDagger.gluing_globalFrame` (compatibility): For Y = P^1_k with its two standard affine charts and X = G_m, the gluing category is equivalent to Isoc(G_m, P^1_k, P̂^1_O/K).
- `IsocDagger.gluing_single` (degenerate): For the covering of Y by Y itself with one embedding P, the forgetful functor (E, φ) ↦ E is an isomorphism of categories onto Isoc(X, Y, P/S): the cocycle condition forces φ to restrict to the identity on the diagonal, and a horizontal isomorphism with that restriction is the Taylor isomorphism ε (overconvergence-is-a-property (c)); a datum with φ ≠ ε does not exist.
- `IsocDagger.realisation_product` (computation): For T = P ×_O Spf O⟨s⟩ with U = Y embedded by s = 0 and the projection u: T → P, the realisation E_T is u_K^* E_P, the pullback to the product with the open unit disc.
- `IsocDagger.gluing_cocycle_needed` (non-example): On a covering by three opens, constant rank-one transition scalars c_{αβ} with c_{αβ} c_{βγ} c_{γα} ≠ 1 on the triple overlap do not form a gluing datum.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Independence of P on a fixed covering: two choices P_α, P′_α are compared through the diagonal embedding into P_α ×_S P′_α and the equivalences of RD.3/independence-of-frame along the two projections; the transition data match because the canonical isomorphisms of RD.3/taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks satisfy the transitivity relation (Berthelot 96-03 (2.2.17.3), (2.3.2)(i), pp. 67–70).
2. Independence of the covering (left to the reader by Berthelot, (2.3.2)(iii), p. 71; supplied here): given two coverings with embeddings, pass to the common refinement Y_α ∩ Y′_β embedded in P_α ×_S P′_β; restriction along the two projections gives equivalences from each gluing category to the refined one, because on each piece they are the equivalences of RD.3/independence-of-frame, and the cocycle data correspond since the Taylor isomorphism of an overconvergent module is unique (overconvergence-is-a-property (c)) and the comparison isomorphisms are transitive. Refining twice gives the compatibility needed for a canonical equivalence.
3. Realisations: choose locally a closed immersion of U into a smooth formal S-scheme P and lift U → P to u: T → P by formal smoothness on the nilpotent thickenings; set E_T = u_K^* E_P; two choices (P, u), (P′, u′) are compared through P ×_S P′ and RD.3/taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks, which yields independence and the transition isomorphisms ((2.3.2)(ii), (2.3.2.1), pp. 70–71).
4. Pullback: if v extends to u: P′ → P use u_K^*; otherwise replace P′ by P ×_S P′ with the graph embedding, whose projection to P extends v; canonicity again comes from RD.3/taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks ((2.3.2)(iv), pp. 71–72).

**Checks.**

- Global frame: for Y = P^1_k covered by its two standard affine lines embedded in Â^1_O, and X = G_m, the gluing category is canonically equivalent to Isoc(G_m, P^1, P̂^1/K) defined with the global frame.
- Cocycle condition matters: on a covering of Y by three opens, rank-one data with constant transition scalars c_{αβ} ∈ K^× whose product c_{αβ} c_{βγ} c_{γα} on the triple overlap is ≠ 1 do not define an object.

<a id="target-rd-3-independence-of-compactification"></a>

### Independence of the compactification

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/independence-of-compactification` · theorem

Let j : X ↪ Y and j' : X ↪ Y' be open immersions and v : Y' → Y a PROPER morphism with v∘j' = j and v^{-1}(X) = j'(X) (Kedlaya's formulation: f^{-1}(X) → X an isomorphism). Then v^* : Isoc†(X ⊂ Y/K) → Isoc†(X ⊂ Y'/K) is an equivalence of categories, compatible with Frobenius structures. Consequently, for a proper Y containing X as an open subscheme, Isoc†(X ⊂ Y/K) is independent of Y up to canonical equivalence (two compactifications are dominated by the closure of X in their product).

**Hypotheses.**

- Proper compactifications exist for separated finite type X by Nagata's theorem (request to AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L2/nagata-factorisation-as-used-in-27-4); for quasi-projective X one may take a projective closure.

**Prerequisites.** [Independence of the frame: canonical equivalences between categories of overconvergent isocrystals](#target-rd-3-independence-of-frame) (`RD.3/independence-of-frame`), [Pullback of overconvergent isocrystals along morphisms of frames](#target-rd-3-frame-pullback-functor) (`RD.3/frame-pullback-functor`), [Frames (X ⊂ Y ⊂ P)](#target-rd-3-frame) (`RD.3/frame`), `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper`, [Étale morphisms proper over the closure of X induce isomorphisms of strict neighbourhoods](#target-rd-3-etale-strict-neighbourhood-isomorphism) (`RD.3/etale-strict-neighbourhood-isomorphism`), [Strict neighbourhoods: admissible-covering definition, criterion and standard systems](#target-rd-3-standard-strict-neighbourhoods) (`RD.3/standard-strict-neighbourhoods`), [Overconvergent isocrystals without a global frame: gluing, realisations and pullback](#target-rd-3-isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames) (`RD.3/isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames`), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/modification-domination`.

**Sources.**

- [S20](#source-20), (4.2.2), p. 27. Statement (read from the page image).
- [S3](#source-3), Lemma 2.6, p. 3. Kedlaya's statement with Frobenius.
- [S3](#source-3), Lemma 2.6 proof, p. 3. The proofs are in unavailable sources.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Choose frames Y ⊂ P and Y' ⊂ P' with a morphism u : P' → P lifting v (possible locally); after dévissage and base changes on P inducing an admissible covering of a strict neighbourhood of ]X[_P, reduce to the case where a section P → P' extends the section X → P' ×_P X given by j'; then replace Y' by the image of Y in P' and apply RD.3/independence-of-frame (Berthelot, sketch of the proof of Théorème 2 in 2.4, applied to isocrystals in 4.2.2).
2. Berthelot 96-03 Théorème (2.3.5), pp. 73–74. Reduction to v projective: Berthelot uses Raynaud–Gruson I, Corollaire 5.7.14 (p. 52: an X-admissible blow-up Y″ → Y′ with Y″ → Y quasi-projective, hence projective); equivalently apply SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/modification-domination twice (X-admissible blow-ups Y″ → Y through Y′ and Y‴ → Y′ through Y″) and use that equivalences of categories satisfy the two-out-of-six property. Projective case: the statement is local on Y (gluing, isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames), so Y is affine with a closed immersion into P smooth near X; embed Y′ in P^N_P, localise on X so that X = Y′ ∩ D(s) and the ideal of X in D(s) is generated by a regular sequence lifted to sections t_i of O(md); the zero scheme T of the t_i is étale over P at X and contains the closure of X, and etale-strict-neighbourhood-isomorphism for T → P and T² → P² gives the equivalence.

**Checks.**

- X = A^2, Y = P^2 and Y' = the blow-up of P^2 at a point of the line at infinity: v^* is an equivalence although the boundaries Z = P^1 and Z' (two rational curves) differ.
- X = A^1, Y = P^1, Y' = the closure of the diagonal in P^1 × P^1 with v a projection: v is an isomorphism and v^* is the identity up to canonical isomorphism.

<a id="target-rd-3-overconvergent-isocrystals-of-a-variety"></a>

### The category Isoc†(X/K) of a separated finite type k-scheme

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystals-of-a-variety` · definition

For an open immersion X ⊂ Y of separated finite type k-schemes, Isoc†(X ⊂ Y/K) is defined, when Y embeds into a formal O-scheme P smooth near X, as Isoc(X, Y, P/K) (independent of P by RD.3/independence-of-frame), and in general by gluing along a Zariski covering of Y by opens Y_i admitting such embeddings (a Čech/stack construction, local on Y). For X separated of finite type over k, Isoc†(X/K) := Isoc†(X ⊂ Y/K) for some open immersion into a PROPER k-scheme Y (a compactification), independent of Y up to canonical equivalence by RD.3/independence-of-compactification. If X is proper, Isoc†(X/K) is the category of convergent isocrystals on X.

**Hypotheses.**

- Compactifications exist by Nagata's theorem (requested from AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L2/nagata-factorisation-as-used-in-27-4); frames exist Zariski-locally on Y (affine opens embed in formal affine spaces).
- Isoc†(−/K) is a stack for the Zariski and étale topologies on X (Kedlaya, Notes Definition 2.4, Definition 2.7), which is what makes the gluing well defined.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Isocrystals/Overconvergent`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Independence of the frame: canonical equivalences between categories of overconvergent isocrystals](#target-rd-3-independence-of-frame) (`RD.3/independence-of-frame`), [Independence of the compactification](#target-rd-3-independence-of-compactification) (`RD.3/independence-of-compactification`), [Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-isocrystal) (`RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal`), `AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L2/nagata-factorisation-as-used-in-27-4`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType`, [Overconvergent isocrystals without a global frame: gluing, realisations and pullback](#target-rd-3-isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames) (`RD.3/isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames`).

**Sources.**

- [S3](#source-3), Definition 2.7, pp. 3-4. Definition via a compactification.
- [S20](#source-20), (4.2.2), p. 27. Berthelot's definition (read from the page image).

**Uses and API requirements.**

- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4: coefficients of rigid cohomology H^i_rig(X/K, E) and H^i_{c,rig}
- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.5: finiteness for overconvergent F-isocrystals
- Kedlaya, Notes §§2-9: the p-adic analogue of lisse sheaves

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `IsocDagger` |  | Isoc†(X/K), defined through a compactification and Čech gluing of frames. |
| `IsocDagger.ofFrame` |  | For a proper frame (X, Y, P), Isoc†(X/K) ≃ Isoc(X, Y, P/K) canonically. |
| `IsocDagger.pullback` |  | f^* : Isoc†(X/K) → Isoc†(X'/K) for any morphism f : X' → X of k-schemes, with id^* ≅ id and (fg)^* ≅ g^*f^*. |
| `IsocDagger.isStack` |  | Isoc† is a stack for the Zariski topology. For smooth X, overconvergent F-isocrystals additionally satisfy the étale descent of RD.3/etale-descent-of-overconvergent-f-isocrystals. |
| `IsocDagger.monoidal` |  | K-linear abelian rigid monoidal category with unit O_X^†. |
| `IsocDagger.proper_eq_convergent` |  | If X is proper, Isoc†(X/K) ≃ convergent isocrystals on X. |

**Unit tests.**

- `IsocDagger.affineLine` (computation): The Dwork isocrystal L_π defines an object of Isoc†(A^1_{F_p}/Q_p(π)) (Berthelot 4.2.3).
- `IsocDagger.point` (degenerate): Isoc†(Spec k/K) is the category of finite-dimensional K-vector spaces.
- `IsocDagger.proper_convergent` (characterisation): For X proper, the restriction functor to convergent isocrystals is an equivalence.
- `IsocDagger.not_convergent_affine` (non-example): For X = A^1 the restriction functor Isoc†(A^1/K) → Isoc(A^1/K) (convergent) is not essentially surjective: the extension of RD.3/punctured-curve-boundary-acceptance is not in the image.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Choose a covering of Y by affine opens Y_i with frames (X_i, Y_i, P_i); objects are families of overconvergent isocrystals on the frames of the Y_i together with gluing isomorphisms on the frames of Y_i ∩ Y_j (diagonal embeddings into P_i × P_j), satisfying the cocycle condition; independence of the covering by refinement and RD.3/independence-of-frame (Berthelot §1.5, p. 14, by gluing local frame categories).
2. The gluing construction and its independence of choices are isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames (Berthelot 96-03 (2.3.2)(iii), with the step Berthelot leaves to the reader supplied there); the Zariski stack property is zariski-stack-of-overconvergent-isocrystals. Étale descent is established only with Frobenius structures on smooth X (etale-descent-of-overconvergent-f-isocrystals); the API item IsocDagger.isStack is to be read for the Zariski topology, the étale statement holding for F-isocrystals on smooth X.

**Checks.**

- X = A^n: Isoc†(A^n/K) is equivalent to the category of finite projective K⟨t_1..t_n⟩†-modules with integrable connection satisfying the overconvergence condition (RD.3/affine-smooth-description-of-overconvergent-f-isocrystals).
- X proper: Isoc†(X/K) = convergent isocrystals (Kedlaya, Notes Definition 2.7).

<a id="target-rd-3-overconvergent-f-isocrystal"></a>

### Overconvergent F-isocrystals

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/overconvergent-f-isocrystal` · definition

Let σ_K be a Frobenius lift on K lifting the q-power map of k (q = p^a). The Frobenius pullback F^* on Isoc†(X ⊂ Y/K) is the composite of extension of scalars along σ_K and pullback along the relative q-power Frobenius of (X, Y) over k (realised on a frame by a lift σ : P → P of the q-power Frobenius compatible with σ_K, where such a lift exists, the result being independent of the lift by RD.3/taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks). An overconvergent F-isocrystal on X is an object E ∈ Isoc†(X/K) with an isomorphism Φ : F^*E ≅ E; morphisms commute with Φ. The category is F-Isoc†(X/K) (F^a-Isoc† when the power a is to be recorded). Concretely on a frame with Frobenius lift σ (Kedlaya, Finiteness, Definition 4.2.3): a finite locally free O_V-module E on a strict neighbourhood V of ]X[, with integrable connection satisfying the overconvergence condition, and an isomorphism F : σ^*E ≅ E of modules with connection.

**Hypotheses.**

- The Frobenius structure forces the overconvergence condition on the Taylor isomorphism (Berthelot 96-03 Théorème 2.5.7, cited by Kedlaya), which is why Kedlaya's Definition 4.2.3 can leave it implicit; the condition is not automatic without Frobenius (Kedlaya, Notes Remark 2.12).

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Isocrystals/Overconvergent`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [The category Isoc†(X/K) of a separated finite type k-scheme](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-isocrystals-of-a-variety) (`RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystals-of-a-variety`), [Pullback of overconvergent isocrystals along morphisms of frames](#target-rd-3-frame-pullback-functor) (`RD.3/frame-pullback-functor`), [Canonical isomorphisms between pullbacks along frame morphisms with the same reduction](#target-rd-3-taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks) (`RD.3/taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks`), [Existence of Frobenius lifts on the weak completion of a smooth O_K-algebra (van der Put; Arabia)](#target-rd-0-frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra) (`RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra`), [Overconvergent isocrystals without a global frame: gluing, realisations and pullback](#target-rd-3-isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames) (`RD.3/isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames`).

**Sources.**

- [S4](#source-4), Definition 4.2.3, p. 26. The definition on a frame with Frobenius lift.
- [S20](#source-20), (4.1), p. 26. Frobenius structures (convergent case; the overconvergent case is 'définie comme plus haut', 4.2.2) (read from the page image).

**Uses and API requirements.**

- Kedlaya, Finiteness Theorems 1.2.1-1.2.4 (RD.5): finiteness, Poincaré duality and Künneth for overconvergent F-isocrystals
- Kedlaya, Weil II (RD.6): weights of overconvergent F-isocrystals over finite fields
- RD.3/full-faithfulness-overconvergent-to-convergent: restriction to convergent F-isocrystals
- RD.2/quasi-unipotence-and-local-monodromy-statement: local monodromy at boundary points (Crew's conjecture for curves)
- ColemanIntegration:L1 (via RD.4): constant F-isocrystal and the Frobenius on H^1_rig of affine curves

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FIsocDagger` |  | F-Isoc†(X/K): objects (E, Φ : F^*E ≅ E). |
| `FIsocDagger.frobeniusPullback` |  | F^* = (relative q-Frobenius)^* ∘ σ_K-extension of scalars on Isoc†(X/K). |
| `FIsocDagger.forget` |  | The forgetful functor F-Isoc†(X/K) → Isoc†(X/K). |
| `FIsocDagger.tensor` |  | Tensor products, duals, internal Hom and Tate twists E(n) (Frobenius multiplied by q^{-n}); abelian K_0-linear rigid monoidal (K_0 = K^{σ_K}). |
| `FIsocDagger.pullback` |  | f^* for morphisms of k-schemes, commuting with F^*. |
| `FIsocDagger.independent_of_lift` |  | On a frame, the category defined with a Frobenius lift σ does not depend on σ up to canonical equivalence. |
| `FIsocDagger.pointFiber` |  | For X = Spec F_q and K = W(F_q)[1/p], q-power Frobenius uses σ_K = id and gives finite-dimensional K-spaces with linear automorphism. Choosing p-power Frobenius instead uses the Witt Frobenius and gives Mathlib WittVector.Isocrystal p F_q; its carrier requires perfect residue field, while rank-one classification additionally requires algebraic closure. |
| `FIsocDagger.localAtBoundary` |  | For a smooth curve X ⊂ X̄ and x ∈ X̄ \ X, restriction to the boundary annulus gives a (φ,∇)-module over the Robba ring R_{K} in a local parameter at x (the local monodromy of E at x, RD.2). |

**Unit tests.**

- `FIsocDagger.dwork` (computation): L_π with Φ(1) = exp π(t^p − t) is an overconvergent F-isocrystal on A^1_{F_p}; exp π(t^p − t) converges on |t| < p^{(p−1)/p²} (PARI/GP check of coefficient valuations).
- `FIsocDagger.unit` (degenerate): (O^†_X, id) is the unit object; End(O^†_X) = K^{σ_K} for X geometrically connected.
- `FIsocDagger.point_compat` (compatibility): For X = Spec k with k algebraically closed, O = W(k), q = p: F-Isoc†(X/K) ≃ WittVector.Isocrystal p k (Mathlib), and rank one objects are classified by Mathlib's isocrystal_classification.
- `FIsocDagger.twist` (characterisation): The Tate twist K(n) on Spec F_q has Frobenius q^{-n}; it is not isomorphic to K(0) for n ≠ 0 (slopes −n vs 0).
- `FIsocDagger.no_frobenius_example` (non-example): The isocrystal O·e on A^1 with ∇e = e dt admits no Frobenius structure: its restriction to the boundary annulus at ∞ is not solvable (RD.2/frobenius-hypothesis-is-necessary, in the local parameter 1/t).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Existence of Frobenius lifts on frames: locally, for smooth affine pieces, by the lifting theorem for weakly complete algebras (RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra); globally F^* is defined by functoriality of Isoc† in (X ⊂ Y) (Berthelot 4.1-4.2).
2. Independence of the lift: RD.3/taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks.

**Checks.**

- The unit F-isocrystal O_X^† with Φ = id; the Dwork F-isocrystal L_π on A^1_{F_p} over K = Q_p(π) with σ_K = id, Φ(1) = exp π(t^p − t) (Berthelot 4.2.3 c).

<a id="target-rd-3-rigid-quillen-suslin"></a>

### Rigid-analytic Quillen-Suslin: finite projective modules over K⟨t_1..t_n⟩† are free

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/rigid-quillen-suslin` · theorem

Every finite projective module over K⟨t_1, ..., t_n⟩† (overconvergent power series) is free; the same holds over O⟨t_1, ..., t_n⟩† when K is discretely valued. More precisely, for K complete with nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value and ρ = (ρ_i) with some power of each ρ_i in |K^×|, every finite projective module over the ring K⟨t⟩_ρ of series converging on the closed polydisc of polyradius ρ is free.

**Hypotheses.**

- For the integral O-version restrict K to be complete and discretely valued, so Lemma6.3 applies. The public preprint’s proof of the broader K-version invokes the discrete-valuation Lemma6.2; extending that lemma to a complete rank-one valued field is an explicit proof gap, not supplied by the inaccessible inherited erratum.

**Prerequisites.** `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-algebra`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/fringe-presentation`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/fringe-topology`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-differentials`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-tensor-product`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-rational-localisation`, `mathlib:Module.Projective`, `mathlib:Module.Free`, `mathlib:IsPrincipalIdealRing`.

**Sources.**

- [S16](#source-16), Theorem 6.7, p. 15. Statement (the extraction renders ⟨ ⟩ as h i).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Weierstrass preparation over o⟨t⟩_ρ (Kedlaya, Full faithfulness, Lemma 6.1) and Noether-normalisation changes of variables T_j (Lemmas 6.2, 6.3) reduce unimodular rows over K⟨t⟩_ρ to rows over polynomial rings in one variable over K⟨t'⟩_{ρ'}; Lang's Algebra Theorem XXI.3.4 and induction give the unimodular extension property (Proposition 6.4).
2. Finite free resolutions by induction (Proposition 6.5), so finite projective modules are stably free and hence free (Proposition 6.6); pass to the direct limit over ρ > 1 (Theorem 6.7).
3. PROOF GAP: source-close the rank-one-valued-field Noether-normalisation extension and the projective-module/free-resolution algebra used in Propositions6.4–6.6; do not treat the author-erratum attribution as checked evidence.

**Checks.**

- n = 1: for fixed ρ the ring K⟨t⟩_ρ is a principal ideal domain (Weierstrass preparation), so finite projective modules over it are free before passing to the limit over ρ > 1.

<a id="target-rd-3-sigma-nabla-module-over-dagger-algebra"></a>

### (σ,∇)-modules over a dagger algebra of Monsky–Washnitzer type

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/sigma-nabla-module-over-dagger-algebra` · definition

Let A be a dagger algebra of MW-type over K (a quotient of K⟨x_1,…,x_n⟩† that is regular and whose reduction A^int/πA^int is a smooth k-algebra), with its module of continuous differentials Ω^1_{A/K} (finite projective) and exterior powers Ω^i_{A/K} = ∧^i Ω^1_{A/K}, and let σ: A → A be a Frobenius lift (σ_K-semilinear, acting as the q-power map on the reduction). A (σ,∇)-module over A is a finite locally free A-module M together with (a) an integrable connection ∇: M → M ⊗_A Ω^1_{A/K}: a K-linear map with ∇(am) = a∇(m) + m ⊗ da and ∇_1 ∘ ∇ = 0, where ∇_i: M ⊗ Ω^i → M ⊗ Ω^{i+1} is the induced map; and (b) a Frobenius structure: an additive σ-semilinear map F: M → M (F(am) = σ(a)F(m)) whose linearisation σ^*M → M is an isomorphism; subject to ∇ ∘ F = (F ⊗ dσ) ∘ ∇, i.e. the linearisation is horizontal. Morphisms are A-linear maps commuting with ∇ and F. The trivial object is (A, d, σ). A finite module with integrable connection over a weak completion of a smooth V-algebra, equipped with a horizontal invertible Frobenius pullback map lifting residue Frobenius, has the required overconvergent Taylor isomorphism. Integrability without such Frobenius is not enough.

**Hypotheses.**

- A is a dagger algebra of MW-type; the regularity of A is part of the definition (Kedlaya's errata to Definition 3.2.1).
- σ is a Frobenius lift in the sense of Kedlaya, Definition 3.2.3; its existence is RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra.
- Over a regular A, a finitely generated A-module with connection is automatically locally free (Kedlaya, Lemma 3.3.4), so local freeness may be dropped from the input.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/MonskyWashnitzer`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-algebra`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/fringe-presentation`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/fringe-topology`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-differentials`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-tensor-product`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-rational-localisation`, [Existence of Frobenius lifts on the weak completion of a smooth O_K-algebra (van der Put; Arabia)](#target-rd-0-frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra) (`RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra`), `mathlib:TensorProduct`, `mathlib:Derivation`.

**Sources.**

- [S4](#source-4), Definition 3.3.1, p. 22. The definition used here, with R a dagger algebra and A = K.
- [S4](#source-4), Remark 3.3.3, p. 22. Horizontality of the linearised Frobenius.
- [S4](#source-4), Lemma 3.3.4, p. 22. Local freeness is automatic.
- [S5](#source-5), Section 2.4, p. 15. The trivial object.
- [S35](#source-35), Théorème 2.5.7 and proof, global pp. 86–89 (II, pp. 40–43); §2.5.8, p. 89. The invertible horizontal Frobenius forces Taylor overconvergence and yields the affine coefficient equivalence.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- Kedlaya, Finiteness, Remark 4.2.5: overconvergent F-isocrystals on a smooth affine X are (σ,∇)-modules over the dagger algebra of X
- Kedlaya, Finiteness, Chapters 6–9: all finiteness computations are made on (σ,∇)-modules over dagger algebras and their Robba rings
- ColemanIntegration:L1/frobenius-h1-datum: the constant module A† with a Frobenius lift φ gives the Frobenius on H^1_dR+(Y)
- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.6 (Kedlaya, Weil II, Sections 2.4 and 5): coefficient objects in the trace formula and the Fourier transform computations

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SigmaNablaModule` |  | The type of (σ,∇)-modules over (A, σ): a finite projective A-module M with connection ∇ and σ-semilinear F as above. |
| `SigmaNablaModule.trivial` |  | The trivial module (A, d, σ). |
| `SigmaNablaModule.tensor` |  | M ⊗_A N with ∇(m⊗n) = ∇m⊗n + m⊗∇n and F(m⊗n) = F(m)⊗F(n); the category is symmetric monoidal with unit the trivial module. |
| `SigmaNablaModule.dual` |  | Hom_A(M, A) with the dual connection and the inverse-transpose Frobenius; M ⊗ M^∨ → A is a morphism. |
| `SigmaNablaModule.pullback` |  | For f: A → B a morphism of MW-type dagger algebras with f ∘ σ_A = σ_B ∘ f, the module f^*M = M ⊗_A B with the induced structures (Kedlaya, Definition 3.4.2); pullback along id is id and pullbacks compose. |
| `SigmaNablaModule.pushforward` |  | For f: B → A injective with A finite étale over B, the module f_*M = M viewed over B with the same ∇ and F (Kedlaya, Definition 3.4.2). |
| `SigmaNablaModule.locallyFree_of_connection` |  | Over a regular A, a finitely generated module with connection is locally free (Kedlaya, Lemma 3.3.4). |
| `SigmaNablaModule.isDirectSummand_of_sub` |  | A (σ,∇)-submodule N ⊆ M is an A-direct summand and M/N is again a (σ,∇)-module (Kedlaya, Weil II, Section 2.4). |
| `SigmaNablaModule.changeOfFrobenius` |  | For two Frobenius lifts σ, σ' on A the categories of (σ,∇)- and (σ',∇)-modules are canonically equivalent, compatibly with ∇ and tensor products (Kedlaya, Weil II, Section 2.4, and Kedlaya, Finiteness, proof of Theorem 5.1.2). |

**Unit tests.**

- `SigmaNablaModule.trivial_dual` (degenerate): The dual of the trivial module is isomorphic to the trivial module, and the evaluation map M ⊗ M^∨ → A is an isomorphism when M is trivial.
- `SigmaNablaModule.kummer_frobenius_iff` (characterisation): Over A = K⟨x,x^{-1}⟩† with σ(x) = x^q, the rank-one module K_a (∇e = a·e ⊗ dx/x) has a Frobenius structure e ↦ c·x^m·e (c ∈ K^×) if and only if m = q·σ_K(a) − a (equal to (q−1)a when σ_K(a) = a); if σ_K(a) = a, this is equivalent to a ∈ (q−1)^{-1}ℤ.
- `SigmaNablaModule.point_eq_isocrystal` (compatibility): For A = K (the point) a (σ,∇)-module is a finite-dimensional K-vector space with a σ_K-semilinear F with invertible linearisation (bijective if σ_K is an automorphism); for K = FractionRing(W(k)), q = p and σ_K the Witt vector Frobenius this is Mathlib's WittVector.Isocrystal.
- `SigmaNablaModule.kummer_liouville_nonexample` (non-example): For a ∈ ℤ_p a p-adic Liouville number, K_a is a module with integrable connection over K⟨x,x^{-1}⟩† carrying no Frobenius structure (by kummer_frobenius_iff and a ∉ ℚ); its H^1 is infinite dimensional (RD.5/no-finiteness-without-frobenius).

**Construction or proof.**

1. The dagger algebra, its differentials Ω^i_{A/K} and the exterior derivative d are supplied by AdicSpacesPartII:F1; tensor products are Mathlib's TensorProduct over A.
2. Leibniz and integrability are conditions on the data (∇, F); they are checked on the generators dx_j of Ω^1 for A a quotient of K⟨x_1,…,x_n⟩†.
3. Horizontality of the linearisation σ^*M → M is equivalent to ∇ ∘ F = (F ⊗ dσ) ∘ ∇ (Kedlaya, Remark 3.3.3).
4. Local freeness from a connection (Kedlaya, Lemma 3.3.4): at a maximal ideal a, a minimal nontrivial relation Σ c_i v_i = 0 among lifts of a basis of M/aM is differentiated along a vector field ∂_j with ∂_j c_1 of smaller order, producing a relation of smaller minimal order, a contradiction.
5. Choose local differential coordinates and a Frobenius-stable integral lattice. The derivative of a Frobenius lift is π-divisible, so iterating its horizontal isomorphism makes the connection matrices integral. On a Banach radius near one the normalized iterated derivatives converge for a small Taylor radius. Frobenius extends that radius by η_(n+1)=min(η_n^(1/p),η_n/c), |π|<c<1, so η_n tends to one; shrink the coefficient radius at each stage. Horizontality makes the expansions agree, giving the overconvergent diagonal stratification.

**Checks.**

- The trivial module (A, d, σ) satisfies the axioms; its dual and tensor square are trivial.
- The rank-one module over K⟨x,x^{-1}⟩† with basis e, ∇e = a·e ⊗ dx/x and the standard Frobenius x ↦ x^q admits a Frobenius structure of the form e ↦ c·x^m·e exactly when q·σ_K(a) − a ∈ ℤ, and then m = q·σ_K(a) − a (equal to (q−1)a when σ_K(a) = a).

<a id="target-rd-3-affine-frame-global-sections-equivalence"></a>

### On the Monsky–Washnitzer frame of a smooth affine, global sections give an equivalence with A†_K-modules

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/affine-frame-global-sections-equivalence` · theorem

Let X = Spec A_0 be a smooth affine k-scheme, A a smooth O-algebra lifting A_0 with a presentation A ≅ O[t_1, …, t_n]/I, 𝔛 = Spec A, P the formal completion of the closure of 𝔛 in P^n_O and Y its special fibre. Then ]Y[_P = P_K, the intersections U_η of 𝔛_K^an with the closed balls of radius 1/η > 1 form a fundamental system of affinoid strict neighbourhoods of ]X[_P, and Γ(P_K, j†O) = colim_η Γ(U_η, O) ≅ A† ⊗_O K =: A†_K, the generic fibre of the weak completion. The functor Γ(𝔛_K^an, −) = Γ(P_K, −) induces equivalences (i) from coherent j†O_{P_K}-modules to finitely generated A†_K-modules, locally free ones corresponding to projective ones; (ii) from coherent j†O-modules with integrable connection to finitely generated projective A†_K-modules M with integrable connection M → M ⊗_{A†_K} Ω^1_{A†_K} (Ω^1 in the sense of Monsky–Washnitzer); and (iii) from Isoc†(X/K) to those (M, ∇) whose Taylor series converges on a strict neighbourhood of the tube of the diagonal in 𝔛_K^an × 𝔛_K^an, for instance inside {|t_{2,i} − t_{1,i}| < 1 for all i}.

**Hypotheses.**

- A smooth lift A exists (Elkik) and its weak completion is a dagger algebra of Monsky–Washnitzer type (AdicSpacesPartII:F1/mw-lift-existence-uniqueness).
- Without Frobenius, the convergence condition in (iii) is genuine extra data (see the non-example).
