**Prerequisites.** [Global overconvergent functions on an affine frame are the dagger algebra](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-sections-of-affine-frame) (`RD.3/overconvergent-sections-of-affine-frame`), [Coherent j†O-modules are germs of coherent modules on strict neighbourhoods](#target-rd-3-coherent-j-dagger-modules) (`RD.3/coherent-j-dagger-modules`), [Overconvergence of a connection is a property, local on P and on X, stable under subquotients](#target-rd-3-overconvergence-is-a-property) (`RD.3/overconvergence-is-a-property`), [Strict neighbourhoods: admissible-covering definition, criterion and standard systems](#target-rd-3-standard-strict-neighbourhoods) (`RD.3/standard-strict-neighbourhoods`), `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/weak-completion`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/weak-completion-generic-fibre`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/mw-type-dagger-algebra`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/mw-lift-existence-uniqueness`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-differentials`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid`.

**Sources.**

- [S62](#source-62), (2.1.2), (2.1.2.4), pp. 49–50; (2.5.1)–(2.5.2) with the remark after it, pp. 81–83. Identifies the overconvergent functions on the Monsky–Washnitzer frame with the weak completion, and proves that global sections give equivalences from coherent j†O-modules, modules with connection and overconvergent isocrystals to finitely generated (projective) A†_K-modules, with connection, whose Taylor series converges on a strict neighbourhood of the diagonal.
- [S4](#source-4), Remark 4.2.5, p. 26. States the resulting equivalence between overconvergent F-isocrystals on a smooth affine and (σ,∇)-modules over the dagger algebra, attributing the automatic convergence to Berthelot's Théorème 2.5.7 (cited there as [Be4]).

**Construction or proof.**

1. The strict neighbourhoods: Berthelot 96-03 (1.2.4)(iii)–(iv) shows that in projective space the sets U_η = {x ∈ ]Y[ : |t_i(x)| ≤ 1/η} form a fundamental system; the restriction map from Γ(U_η, O) to Γ(]X[, O) = Â ⊗ K lands in A† ⊗ K by the growth description of A† (Berthelot (2.1.2.2)), and the colimit is A†_K ((2.1.2), (2.1.2.4), pp. 49–50).
2. (i): by coherent-j-dagger-modules (b) a coherent j†O-module is j†𝓮 with 𝓮 coherent on an affinoid U_η, i.e. a finite Γ(U_η, O)-module (Kiehl), and passing to the colimit gives a finite A†_K-module M = Γ(P_K, E) = Γ(U_η, E); locally free corresponds to projective ((2.5.2), pp. 82–83).
3. (ii): Γ(P_K, j†Ω^1) = colim Γ(U_η, Ω^1) = Ω^1_{A†} ⊗ K, so connections correspond, using overconvergence-is-a-property (a) for local freeness; (iii): overconvergence-is-a-property (b) with the explicit strict neighbourhood of the diagonal tube from (1.2.4)(iv) (remark after (2.5.2), p. 83).

**Checks.**

- Affine space: for A = O[t_1, …, t_n], A†_K = K⟨t_1, …, t_n⟩†; the rank-one module with ∇(1) = −π dt_1 (Dwork) satisfies (iii).
- Non-example: the A†_K-module A†_K with ∇(1) = −dt on A^1 is a projective module with integrable connection, so an object of (ii), but not of (iii): its Taylor series does not converge on |t_2 − t_1| < 1.
- Degenerate case n = 0: X = Spec k, A†_K = K and both sides are finite-dimensional K-vector spaces.

<a id="target-rd-3-mw-pullback-realises-frame-pullback"></a>

### Pullback along a lift of a morphism of smooth affines realises the pullback of overconvergent isocrystals

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/mw-pullback-realises-frame-pullback` · theorem

Let w: X′ = Spec A′_0 → X = Spec A_0 be a morphism of smooth affine k-schemes, A, A′ smooth O-algebras lifting A_0, A′_0, and ψ: A† → A′† an O-algebra map between weak completions lifting w (it exists). Under the equivalences of affine-frame-global-sections-equivalence, the base-change functor ψ_K^* from A†_K-modules with integrable connection to A′†_K-modules with integrable connection preserves the convergence condition (iii), and its restriction to Isoc†(X/K) is canonically isomorphic to w^*: Isoc†(X/K) → Isoc†(X′/K). In particular two lifts ψ, ψ′ of w give canonically isomorphic functors, and the identification is compatible with composition. More generally, for immersions X → T, X′ → T′ into separated O-schemes of finite type smooth near X, X′, any morphism u′ from a strict neighbourhood of ]X′[_{T′} to T_K^an extending the map of tubes induced by a formal lift of w realises w^* on overconvergent isocrystals.

**Hypotheses.**

- The lift ψ exists by the lifting property of weak completions (van der Put, Theorem 2.4.4; AdicSpacesPartII:F1/mw-morphism-lifting); it is not unique.

**Prerequisites.** [On the Monsky–Washnitzer frame of a smooth affine, global sections give an equivalence with A†_K-modules](#target-rd-3-affine-frame-global-sections-equivalence) (`RD.3/affine-frame-global-sections-equivalence`), [Overconvergent isocrystals without a global frame: gluing, realisations and pullback](#target-rd-3-isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames) (`RD.3/isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames`), [Independence of the compactification](#target-rd-3-independence-of-compactification) (`RD.3/independence-of-compactification`), [Strict neighbourhoods: admissible-covering definition, criterion and standard systems](#target-rd-3-standard-strict-neighbourhoods) (`RD.3/standard-strict-neighbourhoods`), `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/mw-morphism-lifting`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-maximum-modulus`.

**Sources.**

- [S62](#source-62), (2.5.3)–(2.5.6), pp. 83–86. Proves the norm estimates for elements of weak completions, the extension of morphisms to strict neighbourhoods, and that the base change along a lift of a morphism of smooth affines preserves overconvergence and is canonically isomorphic to the pullback of overconvergent isocrystals.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Bounds: for f ∈ A† and ρ > 1 there is η > 1 such that f extends to the affinoid U_η with sup norm ≤ ρ; hence ψ extends to morphisms U′_{η′} → U_η of strict neighbourhoods (Berthelot 96-03 (2.5.3), pp. 83–84).
2. A morphism u′ from a strict neighbourhood extending a map of tubes sends some strict neighbourhood into ]Y[ and pulls strict neighbourhoods back to strict neighbourhoods, by the maximum principle ((2.5.4), pp. 84–85).
3. Compare u′^* with w^* using the graph embedding X′ → P′ × P: u′ gives a section of the projection on a strict neighbourhood, and the projection induces an equivalence by RD.3/independence-of-compactification; composing shows that u′^* preserves overconvergence and is canonically isomorphic to w^* ((2.5.5)–(2.5.6), pp. 85–86).

**Checks.**

- Frobenius: for a Frobenius lift F: A† → A† over σ, F_K^* realises the Frobenius pullback F^* on Isoc†(X/K); two Frobenius lifts give canonically isomorphic functors through the Taylor series of RD.0/change-of-frobenius-lift-taylor-formula.
- Identity: ψ = id gives the identity functor (degenerate case).
- Translation on A^1: ψ(t) = t + 1 lifts translation by 1 on A^1_k; it carries the Dwork module (K⟨t⟩†, ∇(1) = −π dt) to itself, because d(t + 1) = dt, so translation preserves the Dwork isocrystal.

<a id="target-rd-3-frobenius-structure-forces-overconvergence"></a>

### Dwork–Berthelot: a Frobenius structure forces overconvergence

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/frobenius-structure-forces-overconvergence` · theorem

In the setting of affine-frame-global-sections-equivalence, let σ be an automorphism of O lifting a power of the Frobenius of k, F: A† → A† a lift of the corresponding Frobenius of A_0 over σ, and (M, ∇) a finitely generated A†_K-module with integrable connection admitting a horizontal isomorphism Φ: (F^*M, F^*∇) ≅ (M, ∇). Then the coherent j†O-module with connection corresponding to (M, ∇) is overconvergent. Consequently (Berthelot's Corollary 2.5.8) the category of overconvergent F-isocrystals on X is equivalent to the category of finitely generated (necessarily projective) A†_K-modules with integrable connection and horizontal Frobenius isomorphism, i.e. (σ, ∇)-modules over A†_K, and the equivalence is functorial in A by mw-pullback-realises-frame-pullback.

**Hypotheses.**

- Frobenius is an isomorphism Φ: F^*M → M; a mere horizontal map would not suffice for the radius-extension argument.
- No condition on ∇ beyond integrability is assumed: convergence near the diagonal and then overconvergence are both consequences.

**Prerequisites.** [On the Monsky–Washnitzer frame of a smooth affine, global sections give an equivalence with A†_K-modules](#target-rd-3-affine-frame-global-sections-equivalence) (`RD.3/affine-frame-global-sections-equivalence`), [The coordinate criterion for convergence and overconvergence of a connection](#target-rd-3-taylor-series-convergence-criterion) (`RD.3/taylor-series-convergence-criterion`), [Overconvergence of a connection is a property, local on P and on X, stable under subquotients](#target-rd-3-overconvergence-is-a-property) (`RD.3/overconvergence-is-a-property`), [Pullback along a lift of a morphism of smooth affines realises the pullback of overconvergent isocrystals](#target-rd-3-mw-pullback-realises-frame-pullback) (`RD.3/mw-pullback-realises-frame-pullback`), [Strict neighbourhoods: admissible-covering definition, criterion and standard systems](#target-rd-3-standard-strict-neighbourhoods) (`RD.3/standard-strict-neighbourhoods`), [Existence of Frobenius lifts on the weak completion of a smooth O_K-algebra (van der Put; Arabia)](#target-rd-0-frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra) (`RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra`), [(σ,∇)-modules over a dagger algebra of Monsky–Washnitzer type](#target-rd-3-sigma-nabla-module-over-dagger-algebra) (`RD.3/sigma-nabla-module-over-dagger-algebra`), `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/weak-completion`.

**Sources.**

- [S62](#source-62), (2.5.7) Théorème with its proof and (2.5.8) Corollaire, pp. 86–89. Proves that a horizontal Frobenius isomorphism on a module with connection over the weak completion forces the overconvergence of the connection, by first making the connection matrices integral and then extending the Taylor isomorphism outward with Dwork's Frobenius trick, and deduces the Monsky–Washnitzer description of overconvergent F-isocrystals on a smooth affine.
- [S62](#source-62), (2.3.8)(ii)–(iii), pp. 76–77. Gives the Dwork F-isocrystal (Frobenius exp π(t − t^p)) and the criterion a = m/(p−1) for a Frobenius structure on the Kummer isocrystal.
- [S4](#source-4), Remark 4.2.5, p. 26. Quotes this theorem as the reason the convergence condition is automatic for (σ,∇)-modules over a dagger algebra of MW type.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Localise on X (overconvergence is local, overconvergence-is-a-property (d)) so that Ω^1_{A†} is free on dz_1, …, dz_m; with F(z_i) = z_i^q + π g_i one has dF(dz_i) ∈ π Ω^1. If the connection matrices on generators have entries in π^{−r} A†, the matrices for the generators 1 ⊗ e_i of F^*M have entries in π^{−r+1} A†; transporting by Φ and iterating gives generators whose connection matrices have entries in A† (Berthelot 96-03, proof of (2.5.7), pp. 86–87).
2. With integral connection matrices, for every ρ > 1 there is η_0 > 1 with ‖∂^k e‖_{η_0} ≤ ρ^{|k|} ‖e‖_{η_0} (norm estimates of mw-pullback-realises-frame-pullback); choosing λ_0′ < p^{−1/(p−1)}/ρ gives convergence of the Taylor series on V_{λ_0 η_0} = {|τ_j| ≤ λ_0} ∩ U′_{η_0} (taylor-series-convergence-criterion).
3. Dwork's trick: with |π| < ϱ < 1 set λ_{n+1} = min(λ_n^{1/q}, λ_n/ϱ) → 1; choose η_{n+1} so that F × F maps V_{λ_{n+1} η_{n+1}} into V_{λ_n η_n} (using F(t_j) = t_j^q + π a_j and (F ⊗ F)(τ_j) = τ_j^q + π γ_j with γ_j in the diagonal ideal); extend ε inductively by p_1^*(Φ) ∘ (F×F)^*(ε) ∘ p_2^*(Φ)^{−1}, the extensions agreeing on overlaps because Φ is horizontal. The union of the V_{λ_n η_n} is a strict neighbourhood of the diagonal tube ((2.5.7), pp. 87–89).
4. The corollary combines this with affine-frame-global-sections-equivalence (iii) and the functoriality of mw-pullback-realises-frame-pullback ((2.5.8), p. 89).

**Checks.**

- Dwork F-isocrystal: on A^1 with K = ℚ_p(π), σ = id, F(t) = t^p, the module (K⟨t⟩†, ∇(1) = −π dt) with Φ = multiplication by exp π(t − t^p) (a series of radius p^{(p−1)/p²} > 1) is a (σ,∇)-module, hence an overconvergent F-isocrystal (Berthelot (2.3.8)(ii)).
- Kummer: on G_m with F(t) = t^p, the rank-one module with ∇(1) = a dt/t has a Frobenius structure if and only if a = m/(p − 1) with m ∈ ℤ, given by multiplication by t^m (Berthelot (2.3.8)(iii)); it is overconvergent for every a ∈ ℤ_p, so Frobenius is sufficient but not necessary for overconvergence.
- Non-example: (K⟨t⟩†, ∇(1) = −dt) admits no Frobenius structure, consistently with its failure to be even convergent.

<a id="target-rd-3-affine-smooth-description-of-overconvergent-f-isocrystals"></a>

### Overconvergent F-isocrystals on a smooth affine variety are (σ,∇)-modules over its dagger algebra

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/affine-smooth-description-of-overconvergent-f-isocrystals` · theorem

Let X be a smooth affine k-scheme, A a dagger algebra of MW-type with special fibre X (it exists and is unique up to non-canonical isomorphism), and σ a Frobenius lift on A. Choose the compatible Monsky–Washnitzer affine lifting and its projective frame, with cofinal affinoid strict neighbourhoods V realizing that chosen dagger presentation. Then A ≅ colim_V Γ(V, O_V) over the strict neighbourhoods V of ]X[_P in ]Y[_P, and E ↦ M_E := colim_V Γ(V, E_V) is an equivalence between F-Isoc†(X/K) and the category of (σ,∇)-modules over A, compatible with tensor products, duals and pullbacks. For overconvergent isocrystals carrying a Frobenius structure, the convergence (Taylor) condition in the definition is automatic. A finite module with integrable connection over a weak completion of a smooth V-algebra, equipped with a horizontal invertible Frobenius pullback map lifting residue Frobenius, has the required overconvergent Taylor isomorphism. Integrability without such Frobenius is not enough.

**Hypotheses.**

- X smooth affine over k; A of MW-type with A^int/πA^int ≅ O(X).
- The equivalence depends on σ only through the canonical change-of-Frobenius equivalence (RD.3/sigma-nabla-module-over-dagger-algebra, API changeOfFrobenius).
- The colimit identity is asserted for the compatible affine lifting frame, not for arbitrary smooth frames with unrelated rings of global functions.

**Prerequisites.** [Global overconvergent functions on an affine frame are the dagger algebra](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-sections-of-affine-frame) (`RD.3/overconvergent-sections-of-affine-frame`), [Overconvergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-f-isocrystal) (`RD.3/overconvergent-f-isocrystal`), [Rigid-analytic Quillen-Suslin: finite projective modules over K⟨t_1..t_n⟩† are free](#target-rd-3-rigid-quillen-suslin) (`RD.3/rigid-quillen-suslin`), [Existence of Frobenius lifts on the weak completion of a smooth O_K-algebra (van der Put; Arabia)](#target-rd-0-frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra) (`RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra`), `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-algebra`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/fringe-presentation`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/fringe-topology`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-differentials`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-tensor-product`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-rational-localisation`, [Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-isocrystal) (`RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal`), [Frames (X ⊂ Y ⊂ P)](#target-rd-3-frame) (`RD.3/frame`), [The tube ]T[_P of a locally closed subscheme](#target-rd-3-tube) (`RD.3/tube`), [Strict neighbourhoods of ]X[ in ]Y[](#target-rd-3-strict-neighbourhood) (`RD.3/strict-neighbourhood`), [(σ,∇)-modules over a dagger algebra of Monsky–Washnitzer type](#target-rd-3-sigma-nabla-module-over-dagger-algebra) (`RD.3/sigma-nabla-module-over-dagger-algebra`), `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/raynaud-generic-fibre`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/generic-fibre-fibre-products`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/tube`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/quasi-stein-theorems-a-b`, [On the Monsky–Washnitzer frame of a smooth affine, global sections give an equivalence with A†_K-modules](#target-rd-3-affine-frame-global-sections-equivalence) (`RD.3/affine-frame-global-sections-equivalence`), [Pullback along a lift of a morphism of smooth affines realises the pullback of overconvergent isocrystals](#target-rd-3-mw-pullback-realises-frame-pullback) (`RD.3/mw-pullback-realises-frame-pullback`), [Dwork–Berthelot: a Frobenius structure forces overconvergence](#target-rd-3-frobenius-structure-forces-overconvergence) (`RD.3/frobenius-structure-forces-overconvergence`).

**Sources.**

- [S20](#source-20), (4.2.2), pp. 27-28. Berthelot's description (read from the page image).
- [S4](#source-4), Remark 4.2.5, p. 26. Automatic convergence.
- [S4](#source-4), Remark 4.2.5, p. 26. The dagger algebra as overconvergent functions.
- [S20](#source-20), (4.2.2), p. 27. Berthelot's description of overconvergent F-crystals on smooth affines.
- [S7](#source-7), Theorem 2.4.4, p. 37. Existence and uniqueness of the dagger algebra.
- [S35](#source-35), Théorème 2.5.7 and proof, global pp. 86–89 (II, pp. 40–43); §2.5.8, p. 89. The invertible horizontal Frobenius forces Taylor overconvergence and yields the affine coefficient equivalence.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Existence and uniqueness of A: van der Put, Theorem 2.4.4 (i), via Elkik's smooth lift and Artin approximation.
2. Identification of A with overconvergent functions: Berthelot (2.1) (the ring A† ⊗ K is the colimit of Γ(U_λ, O) over the affinoid neighbourhoods U_λ of the tube, which are strict neighbourhoods by (2.5) b)); with frames via RD.3/frame and RD.3/strict-neighbourhood.
3. Coherent sheaves on the affinoids U_λ correspond to finite Γ(U_λ)-modules (AdicSpacesPartII:R3), so a j†O-module locally free of finite rank gives a finite projective A-module M_E, and the connection gives ∇ on M_E.
4. The Frobenius structure F: σ^*E ≅ E gives the σ-semilinear F on M_E.
5. Essential surjectivity follows from RD.3/frobenius-structure-forces-overconvergence, using the finite-module Taylor criterion of Berthelot 96-03 Théorème 2.5.7. The horizontal invertible Frobenius and smooth weak-lift hypotheses are essential.
6. Full faithfulness: horizontal maps between overconvergent modules on V extend uniquely across the colimit.
7. This is Berthelot 96-03 Corollaire (2.5.8), p. 89: combine affine-frame-global-sections-equivalence ((2.5.2)), the functoriality in the lift mw-pullback-realises-frame-pullback ((2.5.6)) and frobenius-structure-forces-overconvergence ((2.5.7)).
8. Choose local differential coordinates and a Frobenius-stable integral lattice. The derivative of a Frobenius lift is π-divisible, so iterating its horizontal isomorphism makes the connection matrices integral. On a Banach radius near one the normalized iterated derivatives converge for a small Taylor radius. Frobenius extends that radius by η_(n+1)=min(η_n^(1/p),η_n/c), |π|<c<1, so η_n tends to one; shrink the coefficient radius at each stage. Horizontality makes the expansions agree, giving the overconvergent diagonal stratification.

**Checks.**

- X = A^1, A† = O⟨t⟩†: L_π corresponds to K⟨t⟩† with ∇(1) = π dt and Frobenius Φ(1) = exp π(t^p − t) for σ(t) = t^p.
- For X = A^1 the equivalence sends the constant object to (K⟨x⟩†, d, σ) and Berthelot's Dwork F-isocrystal L_π to (K⟨t⟩†, ∇1 = π dt, Φ(1) = exp π(t^p − t)) with K = ℚ_p(π), π^{p−1} = −p.

<a id="target-rd-3-convergent-isocrystal"></a>

### Convergent isocrystals Isoc(X/K)

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/convergent-isocrystal` · definition

Let X be a k-scheme of finite type. The category Isoc(X/K) of convergent isocrystals is the case Y = X of Isoc(X, Y/K) (isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames): when X is a closed subscheme of a formal O-scheme P smooth near X, its objects are coherent O_{]X[_P}-modules E with an integrable connection ∇ that is convergent, i.e. the Taylor isomorphisms extend to an isomorphism ε: p_2^*E ≅ p_1^*E on the whole tube ]X[_{P×P}; in general it is obtained by gluing. Equivalently (taylor-series-convergence-criterion with Z = ∅), for P affine with coordinates t_1, …, t_m near X, ‖∂^{[k]} e‖ λ^{|k|} → 0 for every λ < 1 and every section e over the closed tube [X]_λ. For X smooth affine with a smooth formal lift 𝔛 = Spf R over O (so ]X[_𝔛 = 𝔛_K), the objects are vector bundles on 𝔛_K with integrable connection such that lim_{|α|→∞} ‖θ^α(e)/α!‖ η^{|α|} = 0 for all 0 ≤ η < 1 and all sections e, θ_i being the components of ∇ in a framing. The category does not depend on P up to canonical equivalence, its objects are locally free, and for X proper over k it coincides with Isoc†(X/K).

**Hypotheses.**

- K is complete discretely valued of characteristic 0 with residue field k of characteristic p; no Frobenius structure is assumed.
- The convergence condition is on the whole tube ]X[_{P×P}, not on a strict neighbourhood of it; there is no boundary condition.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Isocrystals/Convergent`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-isocrystal) (`RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal`), [Overconvergence of a connection is a property, local on P and on X, stable under subquotients](#target-rd-3-overconvergence-is-a-property) (`RD.3/overconvergence-is-a-property`), [The coordinate criterion for convergence and overconvergence of a connection](#target-rd-3-taylor-series-convergence-criterion) (`RD.3/taylor-series-convergence-criterion`), [Overconvergent isocrystals without a global frame: gluing, realisations and pullback](#target-rd-3-isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames) (`RD.3/isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames`), [Independence of the frame: canonical equivalences between categories of overconvergent isocrystals](#target-rd-3-independence-of-frame) (`RD.3/independence-of-frame`), [The tube ]T[_P of a locally closed subscheme](#target-rd-3-tube) (`RD.3/tube`), `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/tube`.

**Sources.**

- [S62](#source-62), (2.2.5), (2.2.14), (2.3.2), (2.3.4), (2.3.9), pp. 61, 66, 69–73, 77. Defines convergent connections as those whose Taylor isomorphism extends to the whole tube of the diagonal, gives the coordinate criterion, defines the category of convergent isocrystals as the case of empty overconvergence locus, compares it with Ogus's definition, and notes that it equals the overconvergent category for proper X.
- [S64](#source-64), Construction 2.11, Definition 2.12, Remark 2.13, p. 15. Describes isocrystals on an affine smooth formal lift as modules with connection over R[1/p] and defines convergent connections by the decay condition on θ^α(e)/α! for every η < 1.
- [S3](#source-3), Definition 2.1, Remarks 2.3 and 2.12, pp. 2–5. Defines convergent F-isocrystals on a smooth affine through a smooth formal lift, notes that coherent modules with connection are locally free, and that without Frobenius an extra convergence condition on the Taylor isomorphism must be imposed.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/restriction-to-convergent: the target category of restriction from overconvergent (F-)isocrystals
- Guo–Reinecke, Theorem 2.14 and Proposition 2.17, pp. 15–16: F-isocrystals are identified with vector bundles with convergent connection and Frobenius, and convergent isocrystals have an underlying bundle with connection
- D’Addezio, §2.2 and footnote 2, p. 6: F^n-isocrystals on the crystalline site are convergent, and the paper works with the convergent category Isoc(X)
- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/rigid-crystalline-comparison: for X proper the coefficient objects of the crystalline comparison are convergent isocrystals

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ConvIsoc` |  | Isoc(X/K): coherent O_{]X[_P}-modules with integrable convergent connection on a frame (X, X, P), glued in general. |
| `ConvIsoc.ofFormalLift` |  | On a smooth affine with formal lift 𝔛 = Spf R: vector bundles on 𝔛_K with integrable connection satisfying lim ‖θ^α(e)/α!‖ η^{\|α\|} = 0 for all η < 1. |
| `ConvIsoc.realisation` |  | The realisation E_P on ]X[_P for any closed immersion of X into a formal O-scheme P, with transition isomorphisms. |
| `ConvIsoc.independent_of_frame` |  | Canonical equivalences between the categories defined with two embeddings, compatible with composition. |
| `ConvIsoc.isLocallyFree` |  | Every object is locally free of finite rank on ]X[_P. |
| `ConvIsoc.monoidal` |  | Abelian rigid ⊗-category with unit (O_{]X[}, d), internal Hom and exact forgetful functor to coherent modules. |
| `ConvIsoc.pullback` |  | Pullback along morphisms X′ → X of k-schemes of finite type, with (w ∘ w′)^* ≅ w′^* ∘ w^*. |
| `ConvIsoc.isStack` |  | X ↦ Isoc(X/K) is a Zariski stack. |
| `ConvIsoc.ofOverconvergent` |  | The restriction functor Isoc†(X/K) → Isoc(X/K), restriction from a strict neighbourhood to the tube, exact and faithful. |
| `ConvIsoc.proper_eq` |  | For X proper over k the restriction functor Isoc†(X/K) → Isoc(X/K) is the identity. |

**Unit tests.**

- `ConvIsoc.dwork_convergent` (computation): On A^1_k with P = Spf O⟨t⟩ and K = ℚ_p(π), π^{p−1} = −p: (K⟨t⟩, ∇(1) = −π dt) is convergent, since |π^k/k!| = p^{−s_p(k)/(p−1)} ≤ 1.
- `ConvIsoc.exp_not_convergent` (non-example): (K⟨t⟩, ∇(1) = −dt) is an integrable connection on the closed disc that is not convergent: |1/k!| λ^k → ∞ for λ > p^{−1/(p−1)}.
- `ConvIsoc.point` (degenerate): For X = Spec k, Isoc(X/K) is the category of finite-dimensional K-vector spaces (the tube is a point and connections are zero).
- `ConvIsoc.proper_overconvergent` (compatibility): For X proper over k, Isoc(X/K) = Isoc†(X/K) = Isoc(X, X/K).
- `ConvIsoc.criterion` (characterisation): On an affine frame with coordinates, ∇ is convergent iff ‖∂^{[k]} e‖ λ^{|k|} → 0 for all λ < 1 and e over [X]_λ.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Independence of P is RD.3/independence-of-frame with Y = X (Berthelot 96-03 (2.3.1)–(2.3.2), pp. 68–70); the gluing and the Zariski stack property are isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames and zariski-stack-of-overconvergent-isocrystals (b).
2. The coordinate description is taylor-series-convergence-criterion with Z = ∅ ((2.2.14), p. 66); it agrees with Guo–Reinecke's Definition 2.12 on affine smooth formal lifts, and with Ogus's convergent isocrystals by Berthelot (2.3.4) (the tubes [X]_{P, p^{1/n}} are the generic fibres of Ogus's formal models T_{P,n}(X)).

**Checks.**

- Dwork on A^1: (K⟨t⟩, ∇(1) = −π dt) is convergent (|π^k/k!| ≤ 1); (K⟨t⟩, ∇(1) = −dt) is not.
- For X proper, Isoc(X/K) = Isoc†(X/K) by definition (Berthelot (2.3.9)).

<a id="target-rd-3-convergent-f-isocrystal"></a>

### Convergent F-isocrystals F^a-Isoc(X/K)

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/convergent-f-isocrystal` · definition

Fix an automorphism σ of K lifting the p^a-power Frobenius of k (a ≥ 1, q = p^a). For E ∈ Isoc(X/K) let F_σ^*E be the pullback along σ followed by the pullback along the q-power Frobenius of X (Berthelot (2.3.7)). A convergent F^a-isocrystal on X is a pair (E, Φ) with E ∈ Isoc(X/K) and Φ: F_σ^*E ≅ E an isomorphism in Isoc(X/K); morphisms are morphisms of isocrystals commuting with Φ. The category F^a-Isoc(X/K) is abelian with ⊗ and internal Hom (Φ_{Hom}(F^*f) = Φ_F ∘ F^*(f) ∘ Φ_E^{−1}), linear over the fixed field K^{σ}. The Tate twist E(n) multiplies Φ by q^{−n}. For X smooth affine with a smooth formal lift P = Spf R and a Frobenius lift σ_P over σ, F^a-Isoc(X/K) is equivalent to the category of vector bundles E on P_K with integrable connection and a horizontal isomorphism σ_P^*E ≅ E; the convergence of ∇ is then automatic. For a perfect point η: Spec Ω → X, the fibre functor η^* takes values in F^a-isocrystals over Ω: finite-dimensional K(Ω)-vector spaces with a σ^a-semilinear bijection, where K(Ω) = W(Ω)[1/p] ⊗ K over the Witt vectors of the residue field; for a = 1 and K = W(k)[1/p] these are the isocrystals of Mathlib's WittVector.Isocrystal over the perfect field Ω.

**Hypotheses.**

- σ lifts the q-power Frobenius of k; the case a = 1, K = W(k)[1/p] with k perfect and σ the Witt-vector Frobenius is the one compared with Mathlib's point isocrystals.
- For F^a-isocrystals the natural Tate twist uses q^{−1} = p^{−a}; Berthelot's (2.3.8)(i) is the case a = 1, multiplying Φ by p^{−1}.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Isocrystals/Convergent`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Convergent isocrystals Isoc(X/K)](#target-rd-3-convergent-isocrystal) (`RD.3/convergent-isocrystal`), [Overconvergent isocrystals without a global frame: gluing, realisations and pullback](#target-rd-3-isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames) (`RD.3/isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames`), [Dwork–Berthelot: a Frobenius structure forces overconvergence](#target-rd-3-frobenius-structure-forces-overconvergence) (`RD.3/frobenius-structure-forces-overconvergence`), [Overconvergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-f-isocrystal) (`RD.3/overconvergent-f-isocrystal`), `mathlib:WittVector.Isocrystal`, `mathlib:WittVector.StandardOneDimIsocrystal`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/isocrystal-slope-decomposition`.

**Sources.**

- [S62](#source-62), (2.3.7)–(2.3.8), pp. 75–77. Defines the Frobenius pullback on isocrystals overconvergent along Y − X as base change along σ followed by pullback along Frobenius, F-isocrystals (convergent when Y = X) with their internal Hom and Tate twists, and gives the Dwork and Kummer examples.
- [S3](#source-3), Definition 2.1, Remark 2.10, Remark 2.12, pp. 2–5. Gives the local description of convergent F-isocrystals through a smooth formal lift with Frobenius lift, the fibre functors at points, and the role of Frobenius in forcing convergence.
- [S28](#source-28), §2.2, p. 6. Fixes the conventions F^n-Isoc(X), F^n-Isoc†(X) with Frobenius structures (F^n)^*M ≅ M, powers of Frobenius structures, fibre functors at perfect points and slope filtrations.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/restriction-to-convergent: target category of the restriction functor with Frobenius
- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/full-faithfulness-overconvergent-to-convergent: Kedlaya's theorem compares F-Isoc† with this category
- D’Addezio, Proposition 3.3.4 and its proof, p. 11: unit-root F^n-isocrystals are compared with lisse ℚ_{p^n}-sheaves
- Étesse 2002, §5.1, pp. 590–591: the categories F^a-Isoc(X/K) and their unit-root subcategories, used for descent and full faithfulness
- Guo–Reinecke, Theorem 2.14, p. 15: F-isocrystals as vector bundles with convergent connection and Frobenius on an affine smooth formal lift

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ConvFIsoc` |  | Pairs (E, Φ) with E ∈ Isoc(X/K) and Φ: F_σ^*E ≅ E. |
| `ConvFIsoc.frobeniusPullback` |  | The functor F_σ^* on Isoc(X/K). |
| `ConvFIsoc.forget` |  | The exact faithful forgetful functor to Isoc(X/K). |
| `ConvFIsoc.monoidal` |  | Abelian rigid ⊗-category with internal Hom; Hom-spaces are vector spaces over K^{σ}. |
| `ConvFIsoc.tate` |  | The Tate objects O(n): the unit with Φ multiplied by q^{−n}; E(n) = E ⊗ O(n). |
| `ConvFIsoc.pullback` |  | Pullback along morphisms of k-schemes of finite type, commuting with F_σ^*. |
| `ConvFIsoc.fibre` |  | The fibre functor at a perfect point η: Spec Ω → X, to F^a-isocrystals over K(Ω). |
| `ConvFIsoc.fibre_isocrystal` |  | For a = 1, K = W(k)[1/p], the fibre at a perfect point Ω ⊇ k is an object of Mathlib's WittVector.Isocrystal p Ω (with Frobenius the given semilinear bijection). |
| `ConvFIsoc.slopes` |  | The slope multiset at each point, defined through the fibre at a perfect point and the Dieudonné–Manin decomposition. |
| `ConvFIsoc.ofFrobeniusLift` |  | On a smooth affine with formal lift and Frobenius lift σ_P: vector bundles with integrable connection and horizontal σ_P^*E ≅ E; convergence is automatic. |
| `ConvFIsoc.restrictFromOverconvergent` |  | Restriction from F^a-Isoc†(X/K), compatible with Φ (RD.3/restriction-to-convergent). |

**Unit tests.**

- `ConvFIsoc.tate_fibre` (computation): Over F_p with K = ℚ_p: the fibre of O(1) at the point is the isocrystal ℚ_p with Φ = p^{−1}·id, i.e. StandardOneDimIsocrystal p 𝔽_p (−1).
- `ConvFIsoc.point_isocrystal` (compatibility): For X = Spec k, k perfect, a = 1, K = W(k)[1/p]: F-Isoc(X/K) is equivalent to the category of Mathlib isocrystals over k (finite-dimensional).
- `ConvFIsoc.unit` (degenerate): The unit (O_{]X[}, d, Φ = id) is an object, and End(unit) = K^{σ}.
- `ConvFIsoc.dwork` (characterisation): On A^1 with σ_P(t) = t^p, K = ℚ_p(π) and σ = id: Φ = exp π(t − t^p) is a horizontal isomorphism from the Frobenius pullback of (K⟨t⟩, ∇(1) = −π dt) to itself.
- `ConvFIsoc.no_frobenius_on_exp` (non-example): (K⟨t⟩, ∇(1) = −dt) admits no Frobenius structure: it is not even convergent, while every module with Frobenius structure is.

**Construction or proof.**

1. F_σ^* is the composite of the base change along σ (a functor Isoc(X, Y/K) → Isoc(X^{(σ)}, Y^{(σ)}/K)) and the pullback along the relative Frobenius (X, Y) → (X^{(σ)}, Y^{(σ)}), using isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames (c) (Berthelot 96-03 (2.3.7), pp. 75–76).
2. The local description with a Frobenius lift is Kedlaya, Notes, Definition 2.1, and Guo–Reinecke's Remark 2.16; the convergence of the connection follows from the Frobenius structure by Dwork's trick (the convergent analogue of frobenius-structure-forces-overconvergence; Kedlaya, Notes, Remark 2.12; Guo–Reinecke, Construction 2.11 and the paragraph before Definition 2.12).
3. Fibres at perfect points: pull back along η and use that Isoc(Spec Ω/K(Ω)) is the category of K(Ω)-vector spaces (convergent-isocrystal, test point); the Frobenius becomes a σ^a-semilinear bijection (Kedlaya, Notes, Remark 2.10; D’Addezio §2.2).

**Checks.**

- Tate object over F_p (K = ℚ_p, a = 1): O(1) is the unit with Φ = p^{−1}; its fibre at the point is the one-dimensional isocrystal with Φ x = p^{−1} σ(x), Mathlib's StandardOneDimIsocrystal of slope −1.
- Dwork: (K⟨t⟩, ∇(1) = −π dt, Φ = exp π(t − t^p)) on A^1 with σ_P(t) = t^p is a convergent F-isocrystal (it is even overconvergent).

<a id="target-rd-3-f-crystal-to-convergent-f-isocrystal"></a>

### Dwork's construction: the convergent F-isocrystal M^an of an F-crystal

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/f-crystal-to-convergent-f-isocrystal` · construction

Assume O is a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic with ramification index e ≤ p − 1 and a Frobenius lift σ. Let X be a k-scheme of finite type and (M, Φ) a non-degenerate F-crystal on X/(O, σ) (a crystal of finite type with Φ: F^*M → M and V: M → F^*M, V∘Φ = p^n, Φ∘V = p^n for some n). Then there is a convergent F-isocrystal M^an on X/(K, σ), functorial in (M, Φ) and in X, constructed in two steps: (i) for a closed immersion X → P = Spf A into a smooth formal scheme, the completed divided-power envelope D̂ of the ideal of X maps to the algebra of the affinoid [X]_{P,|π|} by f^{[q]} ↦ π^{|q|} T^q/q!, which is bounded because e ≤ p − 1; this turns M into a coherent module M_P on [X]_{P,|π|} with a Taylor isomorphism on [X]_{P²,|π|} (an isocrystal convergent of radius |π|); (ii) a Frobenius lift F on P maps [X]_{P,λ_{n+1}} into [X]_{P,λ_n} for λ_n = |π|^{p^{−n}}, and the isomorphisms (F_K^*)^n(Φ ⊗ K) extend M_P and its Taylor isomorphism successively to ]X[_P = ⋃ [X]_{P,λ_n} and ]X[_{P²}.

**Hypotheses.**

- e ≤ p − 1 is needed in step (i): the elements π^{|q|}/q! must be p-adic integers.
- Non-degeneracy (existence of V) makes Φ ⊗ K an isomorphism, which step (ii) needs.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Isocrystals/Convergent`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** `CrystallineCohomology:CR.1/isocrystal`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.1/crystal`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.1/taylor-equivalence`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0/completed-envelope`, [Convergent F-isocrystals F^a-Isoc(X/K)](#target-rd-3-convergent-f-isocrystal) (`RD.3/convergent-f-isocrystal`), [Convergent isocrystals Isoc(X/K)](#target-rd-3-convergent-isocrystal) (`RD.3/convergent-isocrystal`), [The tube ]T[_P of a locally closed subscheme](#target-rd-3-tube) (`RD.3/tube`).

**Sources.**

- [S62](#source-62), (2.4) introduction and (2.4.1), pp. 78–79. Under e ≤ p − 1, associates with a crystal an isocrystal convergent of radius |π| via the divided-power envelope, and with a non-degenerate F-crystal a convergent F-isocrystal by extending with Frobenius (Dwork's method), functorially.
- [S64](#source-64), footnote 3, p. 15. Notes that the boundedness of p^n/n! uses the ramification bound and fails when the ramification index is at least p.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/convergent-f-isocrystals-are-crystalline: the comparison theorem is about this functor
- Étesse 2002, proof of Théorème 7, p. 599: R^i f_cris*(O) of an abelian scheme is turned into a convergent F-isocrystal by this construction, using e ≤ p − 1
- Kedlaya, Notes, Theorem 2.2, p. 2: the functor from crystals to convergent F-isocrystals in Ogus's comparison

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FCrystal.toConvergent` |  | The functor (M, Φ) ↦ M^an from non-degenerate F-crystals on X/(O, σ) to F-Isoc(X/K), for e ≤ p − 1. |
| `FCrystal.toConvergent_map` |  | Functoriality in (M, Φ) and compatibility with pullback along morphisms X′ → X. |
| `FCrystal.toConvergent_tensor` |  | (M ⊗ N)^an ≅ M^an ⊗ N^an and (unit)^an = unit. |
| `FCrystal.toConvergent_isogeny` |  | The functor sends p-isogenies to isomorphisms, hence factors through F-crystals up to isogeny (Hom ⊗ ℚ). |
| `FCrystal.toConvergent_twist` |  | (M, p^m Φ)^an ≅ M^an(−m): multiplying Φ by p^m is the inverse Tate twist. |
| `FCrystal.toConvergent_radius` |  | Before Frobenius extension, a crystal gives only an isocrystal convergent on the tube of radius \|π\| (step (i)). |

**Unit tests.**

- `FCrystal.toConvergent_unit` (degenerate): The unit F-crystal (O_{X/O}, id) goes to the unit convergent F-isocrystal.
- `FCrystal.toConvergent_point_slope` (computation): For X = Spec k, O = W(k) and m ≥ 0: (W(k), p^m σ) goes to the one-dimensional isocrystal with Φ = p^m σ, of slope m (Mathlib StandardOneDimIsocrystal p k m). For m < 0 the map p^m σ does not preserve W(k), so negative slopes arise only as Tate twists M^an(n).
- `FCrystal.toConvergent_degenerate_excluded` (non-example): The F-crystal (W(k), Φ = 0) is degenerate (no V with VΦ = p^n) and has no associated F-isocrystal, since Φ ⊗ K is not an isomorphism.
- `FCrystal.toConvergent_twist_test` (compatibility): (O_{X/W}, pσ)^an ≅ O(−1): its fibre at a point has slope 1.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Glue from affine P (the construction is functorial); identify M with a separated complete D̂-module with stratification (Berthelot 96-03 (2.4.1), pp. 78–79).
2. Step (i): the composite D → A ⊗ K → (A ⊗ K){T}/(f_i − πT_i) is continuous for the π-adic topology since π^{q_1+…+q_r}/q_1!⋯q_r! ∈ ℤ_p when e ≤ p − 1, so it extends to D̂; base change gives M_P and, from the stratification, its Taylor isomorphism ((2.4.1.1)–(2.4.1.2)).
3. Step (ii): F_K maps [X]_{λ_{n+1}} into [X]_{λ_n} because F^*(f_i) = f_i^p + π g_i ((2.4.1.3)); setting M_n = (F_K^*)^n M_0 on [X]_{λ_n}, the maps (F_K^*)^n(Φ) identify M_n with the restriction of M_{n+1}, and the compatibility of Φ with the stratification extends the Taylor isomorphism to ]X[_{P²}.

**Checks.**

- The unit crystal O_{X/O} with Φ = id gives the unit object (O_{]X[}, d, id).
- Point: X = Spec k (k perfect, O = W(k)): an F-crystal is a Dieudonné-type module (W(k)^r, Φ) and M^an is (K^r, Φ ⊗ K); for (W(k), p^m σ) with m ≥ 0 one gets Mathlib's StandardOneDimIsocrystal of slope m.

<a id="target-rd-3-convergent-f-isocrystals-are-crystalline"></a>

### Convergent F-isocrystals are F-crystals up to isogeny and twist (Berthelot, Ogus)

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/convergent-f-isocrystals-are-crystalline` · theorem

Let O be a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic with e ≤ p − 1 and Frobenius lift σ, and X a k-scheme of finite type. (a) The functor M ↦ M^an of f-crystal-to-convergent-f-isocrystal is fully faithful on non-degenerate F-crystals up to isogeny: Hom(M, N) ⊗ ℚ ≅ Hom(M^an, N^an). (b) If X is smooth over k, every convergent F-isocrystal N is isomorphic to M^an(n) for a non-degenerate F-crystal M (which may be taken p-torsion free) and an integer n ≥ 0. (c) Hence, for k perfect, O = W(k) and X smooth, the category F^a-Isoc(X/K) is equivalent to the category of pairs (E, Φ) with E an object of Isoc(X/W) = Crys(X/W) ⊗ ℚ (crystals of finite type up to isogeny) and Φ: (F^a)^*E ≅ E. (d) Locally, for 𝔛 = Spf R affine smooth over W(k) with special fibre 𝔛_s and a Frobenius lift F, the functor E ↦ E(𝔛)[1/p] = lim_r E(𝔛_s, 𝔛 ⊗ W_r)[1/p] is an equivalence from F-isocrystals on 𝔛_s/W(k) (crystalline) to vector bundles on 𝔛_η with flat convergent connection and horizontal Frobenius F^*E ≅ E. (e) The F-isocrystals on 𝔛_s for the crystalline site, on the crystalline site of 𝔛 ⊗ O_K/p, and on Ogus's convergent site of 𝔛 ⊗ O_K/p over W(k) are equivalent for a smooth formal O_K-scheme 𝔛 (any ramification), the inverses being restrictions.

**Hypotheses.**

- (b) needs X smooth; the twist n is needed (the Tate object O(1) is not of the form M^an).
- (c)–(e) use the unramified base W(k); the ramified case is reached through (e) and underlying-bundle-of-convergent-isocrystal.
- Kedlaya states Theorem 2.2 for the absolute Frobenius (a = 1, k perfect, K = W(k)[1/p], X smooth); D’Addezio (§2.2) uses the equivalence for F^n-structures. Berthelot's argument in (2.4.1)–(2.4.2) applies with F replaced by F^a: the radii |π|^{q^{−n}}, q = p^a, still tend to 1, and Ogus's input in (b) does not involve the Frobenius.

**Prerequisites.** [Dwork's construction: the convergent F-isocrystal M^an of an F-crystal](#target-rd-3-f-crystal-to-convergent-f-isocrystal) (`RD.3/f-crystal-to-convergent-f-isocrystal`), [Convergent F-isocrystals F^a-Isoc(X/K)](#target-rd-3-convergent-f-isocrystal) (`RD.3/convergent-f-isocrystal`), [Convergent isocrystals Isoc(X/K)](#target-rd-3-convergent-isocrystal) (`RD.3/convergent-isocrystal`), [The coordinate criterion for convergence and overconvergence of a connection](#target-rd-3-taylor-series-convergence-criterion) (`RD.3/taylor-series-convergence-criterion`), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.1/isocrystal`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.1/taylor-equivalence`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.1/crystal`, `mathlib:WittVector.Isocrystal`.

**Sources.**

- [S62](#source-62), (2.4.2) Théorème and its proof, pp. 79–81. Proves full faithfulness of M ↦ M^an on non-degenerate F-crystals up to isogeny and, for X smooth, that every convergent F-isocrystal is a Tate twist M^an(n), using a result of Ogus for the existence of the crystal.
- [S3](#source-3), Theorem 2.2 with its proof, p. 2. States that convergent F-isocrystals are the F-objects of the isogeny category of crystals of finite type, with references to Ogus 1984 for full faithfulness and Berthelot's (2.4.2) for essential surjectivity.
- [S64](#source-64), Construction 2.11, Theorem 2.14, Remarks 2.15–2.16, pp. 15–16. Gives the local description of F-isocrystals on an affine smooth formal W(k)-scheme with Frobenius lift as vector bundles with convergent connection and Frobenius, and the equivalence of crystalline and convergent-site F-isocrystals (Ogus).
- [S28](#source-28), §2.2 and footnote 2, p. 6. Uses the equivalence of F^n-isocrystals on the crystalline site (Isoc(X) = Crys(X)[1/p]) with convergent F^n-isocrystals, citing Kedlaya's Theorem 2.2.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a): by internal Hom, compare Frobenius-invariant horizontal sections; locally with a Frobenius lift, sections of M^an on ]X[ are compatible families over the tubes [X]_{λ_n}, and the map B_1 → D̂ ⊗ ℚ sending T_i to (π^{−1} p!) f_i^{[p]} produces an inverse to the natural map from (M ⊗ ℚ)^{∇=0, Φ=1} (Berthelot 96-03 (2.4.2), first part, pp. 79–81).
2. (b): by (a) the statement is local, so assume X affine with a smooth lift; Ogus's Proposition 7.3 in 'The convergent topos in characteristic p' gives a crystal M, p-torsion free, with N ≅ M ⊗ ℚ compatibly with the Taylor isomorphisms, and p^n Φ is then an F-crystal structure ((2.4.2), second part, p. 81) — Ogus's proposition is an imported, unread input (gap).
3. (c) is (a) and (b) together, as stated by Kedlaya (Notes, Theorem 2.2, attributing full faithfulness to Ogus 1984 and essential surjectivity to Berthelot's (2.4.2)) and used by D’Addezio (§2.2, footnote 2).
4. (d) is the local form (Guo–Reinecke, Theorem 2.14, citing Berthelot's (2.4.2); Construction 2.11 identifies crystals with modules with quasi-nilpotent connection, CrystallineCohomology:CR.1/taylor-equivalence); (e) is Guo–Reinecke's Remark 2.15, citing Ogus 1984 (Example 2.7.3, Proposition 2.18) for the extension along the convergent site by Dwork's trick (imported, unread input).

**Checks.**

- Point: for X = Spec k with k perfect, (c) says that F-isocrystals are Dieudonné modules up to isogeny, i.e. Mathlib's isocrystals over k.
- Twist needed: O(1) (Φ = p^{−1}) is not M^an for any F-crystal M, because Φ would have to map a lattice into itself; it is M^an(1) for M the unit F-crystal.
- Without Frobenius a crystal yields only an isocrystal convergent on the tube of radius |π| (Berthelot (2.4.1)(i)); the full convergence in (d) uses Frobenius.

<a id="target-rd-3-restriction-to-convergent"></a>

### Restriction from overconvergent to convergent F-isocrystals

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/restriction-to-convergent` · construction

For a frame (X, Y, P) (X smooth), restriction along ]X[_P ⊆ V (V a strict neighbourhood) defines a functor j^* : Isoc†(X ⊂ Y/K) → Isoc(X/K), (E, ε) ↦ (E|_{]X[_P}, ε|_{]X[_{P²}}): the restricted Taylor isomorphism converges on ]X[_{P²}, so the connection on ]X[_P is convergent in Berthelot's sense (4.1). With Frobenius structures it gives j^* : F-Isoc†(X/K) → F-Isoc(X/K), landing in the analytic convergent category of RD.3; coherent crystals up to p-isogeny with an invertible Frobenius structure give an equivalent coefficient model, using the early crystalline input from CR.3. This equivalence is only asserted with Frobenius, not for all bare crystals. j^* is compatible with ⊗, duals, pullbacks and Frobenius, and is independent of the frame up to canonical isomorphism.

**Hypotheses.**

- The target category (convergent F-isocrystals, realised as O_{]X[_P}-modules with convergent integrable connection and Frobenius, or as isocrystals on the crystalline site) is imported from CrystallineCohomology:CR.3 by request; CR.3's text warns not to equate convergent and overconvergent F-isocrystals, which this functor keeps apart.
- For X proper (Y = X) j^* is an equivalence (both categories are convergent isocrystals).

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Isocrystals/Overconvergent`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Overconvergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-f-isocrystal) (`RD.3/overconvergent-f-isocrystal`), [Stratifications versus connections with overconvergent Taylor series](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-isocrystal-connection-form) (`RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal-connection-form`), [Independence of the frame: canonical equivalences between categories of overconvergent isocrystals](#target-rd-3-independence-of-frame) (`RD.3/independence-of-frame`), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.3`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.1/isocrystal`, [Convergent isocrystals Isoc(X/K)](#target-rd-3-convergent-isocrystal) (`RD.3/convergent-isocrystal`), [Convergent F-isocrystals F^a-Isoc(X/K)](#target-rd-3-convergent-f-isocrystal) (`RD.3/convergent-f-isocrystal`), [Convergent F-isocrystals are F-crystals up to isogeny and twist (Berthelot, Ogus)](#target-rd-3-convergent-f-isocrystals-are-crystalline) (`RD.3/convergent-f-isocrystals-are-crystalline`).

**Sources.**

- [S20](#source-20), (4.2), p. 26. Convergence is too weak in the nonproper case (read from the page image).
- [S16](#source-16), Introduction, p. 2. The restriction functor.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- RD.3/full-faithfulness-overconvergent-to-convergent: the theorem is about this functor
- Kedlaya, Notes §5: restriction functors F-Isoc(X,Y) → F-Isoc(U,W)
- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7: the rigid-crystalline comparison for proper smooth X (where j^* is an equivalence)

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FIsocDagger.restrictConvergent` |  | j^* : F-Isoc†(X/K) → F-Isoc(X/K). |
| `FIsocDagger.restrictConvergent_tensor` |  | j^* is a K^{σ_K}-linear exact tensor functor commuting with duals and Frobenius. |
| `FIsocDagger.restrictConvergent_pullback` |  | j^* commutes with pullback along morphisms of smooth k-schemes. |
| `FIsocDagger.restrictConvergent_faithful` |  | j^* is faithful (and fully faithful by RD.3/full-faithfulness-overconvergent-to-convergent). |
| `FIsocDagger.restrictConvergent_proper` |  | If X is proper, j^* is an equivalence. |
| `FIsocDagger.restrictConvergent_CR3` |  | The target is CR.3's convergent F-isocrystals; composed with Ogus's comparison it sends the unit to the isogeny class of the structure F-crystal. |

**Unit tests.**

- `FIsocDagger.restrict_unit` (degenerate): j^*(O^†) = O_{]X[}, the unit convergent F-isocrystal.
- `FIsocDagger.restrict_dwork` (computation): j^*(L_π) = (O_{|t|≤1}, ∇(1) = π dt, Φ(1) = exp π(t^p − t)).
- `FIsocDagger.restrict_proper_equiv` (characterisation): For X = P^1 the functor j^* is an equivalence.
- `FIsocDagger.restrict_not_essSurj` (non-example): For X = A^1, j^* is not essentially surjective: the convergent F-isocrystal extension with ∇e_2 = e_1 Σ_k p^k t^{p^k−1} dt, F e_2 = e_2 − t e_1 is not in the essential image (RD.3/punctured-curve-boundary-acceptance).
- `FIsocDagger.restrict_ordinary_locus` (non-example): On the ordinary locus U of the modular curve X(N), the unit-root rank one subobject of the convergent F-isocrystal j^*(R^1f_*O) is not in the essential image of j^* (Kedlaya Notes Example 4.6, Remark 5.12).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Restriction of a module with overconvergent Taylor isomorphism to the tube ]X[ ⊆ V; the Taylor isomorphism defined on a strict neighbourhood of ]X[_{P²} restricts to ]X[_{P²} (Berthelot 4.1-4.2.1).
2. Independence of the frame: restriction commutes with the canonical equivalences of RD.3/independence-of-frame (both are pullbacks).
3. The target is the RD.3-owned convergent category convergent-f-isocrystal (Berthelot 96-03 (2.3.2), (2.3.7)); restriction is exact and faithful ((2.2.9), (2.3.9)(i)). The comparison with crystals up to isogeny carrying an invertible Frobenius is convergent-f-isocrystals-are-crystalline, which uses the existing CrystallineCohomology:CR.1/isocrystal, CR.1/crystal and CR.1/taylor-equivalence nodes; nothing further is needed from CR.3 for this node.

**Checks.**

- j^*(L_π) is the convergent F-isocrystal O_{closed disc} with ∇(1) = π dt; its horizontal sections still do not exist globally (exp(−πt) diverges at |t| = 1).

<a id="target-rd-3-weak-completion-henselian-descent"></a>

### Monsky–Washnitzer algebras are henselian along π; lifting of étale algebras and descent of projective modules

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/weak-completion-henselian-descent` · lemma

Let A be a finitely generated O-algebra (O a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformiser π) with weak completion A†, π-adic completion Â, and A_0 = A/πA. (1) (Spec A†, Spec A_0) is a henselian pair, and A† → Â is faithfully flat and formally étale for the π-adic topology. (2) Every smooth (respectively étale, finite étale) A_0-algebra B_0 lifts to a smooth (respectively étale, finite étale) A†-algebra B, and sections lift. (3) Every finitely generated projective Â_K-module (Â_K = Â ⊗ K) is isomorphic to M ⊗_{A†_K} Â_K for a finitely generated projective A†_K-module M, and two such M with isomorphic base changes are isomorphic.

**Hypotheses.**

- A† is weakly complete of finite type (always the case for the weak completion of a finitely generated algebra); A is Noetherian.

**Prerequisites.** `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/weak-completion`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/weak-completion-universal-property`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-completion-comparison`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0/henselian-pair-characterisations`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0/henselian-smooth-lifting`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/elkik-noetherian-henselian-approximation`.

**Sources.**

- [S68](#source-68), Proposition 2 and Théorème 3, pp. 113–115; Théorème 4, pp. 116–117. Proves that weakly complete finitely generated algebras form henselian pairs with their reductions, with faithful flatness and formal étaleness of the completion, and lifts smooth, étale and finite étale algebras.
- [S69](#source-69), Théorème 3, p. 569; Corollaire 1 and Lemme, p. 573; Théorème 6, p. 580. Descends finitely generated modules over the completion of a henselian pair, locally free outside the closed subset, to the pair itself, and shows uniqueness of locally free modules on the complement. Théorème 6 lifts smooth algebras over the reduction of a noetherian henselian pair to smooth algebras over the pair.
- [S63](#source-63), Proposition 6 and Corollaires 1–2, p. 586. Applies Elkik's theorem to descend finitely generated projective Â_K-modules and their direct sum decompositions to A†_K.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): A† is Noetherian with π in its radical and A† → Â is faithfully flat (Monsky–Washnitzer); A†/π^n = Â/π^n gives formal étaleness; for a finite A†-algebra B, idempotents of B/πB lift to B because they lift to B̂ and B → B̂ is faithfully flat with B weakly complete (Monsky–Washnitzer, Theorem 3.8), which is the henselian property (Étesse, Padova 2002, Proposition 2 and Théorème 3, pp. 113–115).
2. (2): Elkik, Théorème 6, p. 580: over a noetherian henselian pair (A, J) every smooth A/J-algebra lifts to a smooth A-algebra; the proof reduces to relative complete intersections through the symmetric algebra of the conormal module and lifts sections over the henselian pair (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0/henselian-smooth-lifting). Applied to (A†, πA†), which is noetherian and henselian by (1), it gives the smooth case; the étale and finite étale refinements and the lifting of sections are Étesse, Padova 2002, Théorème 4, pp. 116–117, whose proof cites Elkik's Théorème 6 (finite étale algebras also follow from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0/henselian-finite-etale-equivalence).
3. (3): Elkik's Théorème 3 (p. 569): over a henselian pair (A, J), a finitely generated Â-module locally free outside V(J) comes from a finitely generated A-module locally free outside V(J); Corollaire 1 and the following Lemme (p. 573) give the statement for locally free modules on Spec Â ∖ V(J) and uniqueness of isomorphism classes. With J = πA† this is (3) (Étesse 2002, Proposition 6 and Corollaire 1, p. 586).

**Checks.**

- A = O[t]: A† = O⟨t⟩†, and a projective K⟨t⟩-module of rank one (necessarily free, K⟨t⟩ being a principal ideal domain) descends to the free module of rank one over K⟨t⟩†.
- Henselian property on a finite étale algebra: for p odd, the idempotents of O⟨t⟩†[s]/(s² − (1 + πt)) modulo π (where the algebra splits as k[t] × k[t]) lift to idempotents, since 1 + πt has a square root in O⟨t⟩† given by the binomial series.
- Non-example: the polynomial ring O[t] itself is not henselian along π: 1 + πt has no square root in O[t].

<a id="target-rd-3-finite-etale-lifting-of-mw-algebras"></a>

### Étale maps of smooth affines lift uniquely to weak completions, with Frobenius and differentials

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/finite-etale-lifting-of-mw-algebras` · lemma

Let A_0 be a smooth k-algebra with a smooth lift A and weak completion A†, and A_0 → B_0 an étale morphism. (a) There is an étale A†-algebra B lifting B_0, unique up to unique isomorphism, whose weak completion B† is flat and formally étale over A† for the π-adic topology, with Ω^1_{A†} ⊗_{A†} B† ≅ Ω^1_{B†} and Ω^1_{A†} ⊗ B̂ ≅ Ω^1_{B̂}. (b) A Frobenius lift F_{A†} over σ extends uniquely to a Frobenius lift F_{B†} compatible with it: the relative Frobenius B_0 ⊗_{A_0, F} A_0 → B_0 is an isomorphism and lifts uniquely to B† ⊗_{A†, F} A† ≅ B†. (c) If A_0 → B_0 is finite étale of constant degree d, then A†_K → B†_K is finite étale, B†_K is a projective A†_K-module of rank d with a trace map Tr: B†_K → A†_K satisfying Tr ∘ (inclusion) = d, and B†_K ⊗ Ω^i_{A†_K} ≅ Ω^i_{B†_K} for all i.

**Hypotheses.**

- Étale lifts are unique by topological invariance of the étale site along the π-adic filtration; the lift of a Frobenius is unique only once F_{A†} is fixed.

**Prerequisites.** [Monsky–Washnitzer algebras are henselian along π; lifting of étale algebras and descent of projective modules](#target-rd-3-weak-completion-henselian-descent) (`RD.3/weak-completion-henselian-descent`), `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/mw-morphism-lifting`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/mw-lift-existence-uniqueness`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-finite-extension`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-differentials`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-finite-etale-trace`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-completion-comparison`, [Existence of Frobenius lifts on the weak completion of a smooth O_K-algebra (van der Put; Arabia)](#target-rd-0-frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra) (`RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra`), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0/henselian-finite-etale-equivalence`, `mathlib:Algebra.Etale`.

**Sources.**

- [S63](#source-63), (1.2.1)–(1.2.2) and Proposition 1, pp. 578–580. Lifts an étale A_0-algebra to an étale A†-algebra, extends the Frobenius lift uniquely through the relative Frobenius isomorphism, and proves the flatness and the isomorphisms of Monsky–Washnitzer differentials.
- [S4](#source-4), Definition 3.4.2, p. 23, and the proof of Proposition 3.4.5, p. 24. Defines pushforward of (σ,∇)-modules along finite étale maps of dagger algebras as restriction of scalars (Definition 3.4.2), and, in the proof of Proposition 3.4.5, uses the canonical isomorphism S ⊗_R Ω^i_R ≅ Ω^i_S for a finite étale extension of dagger algebras.
- [S68](#source-68), Théorème 4 (2)–(3), pp. 116–117. Lifts étale and finite étale algebras over the reduction to étale and finite étale algebras over the weak completion.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a): lift B_0 to an étale A†-algebra (weak-completion-henselian-descent (2); Étesse 2002, (1.2.2), citing his Padova paper, Théorème 4) and take its weak completion; flatness and the differential isomorphisms are Étesse's Proposition 1 (ii)(1)–(4), pp. 579–580, using formal étaleness and faithful flatness of A† → Â.
2. (b): the relative Frobenius of an étale morphism in characteristic p is an isomorphism; it lifts uniquely along the henselian pair by uniqueness of étale lifts, and F_{B†} is 1_{B†} ⊗ F_{A†} composed with that isomorphism (Étesse (1.2.2), pp. 578–579).
3. (c): for B_0 finite étale over A_0 the lift is finite étale over A†, hence B†_K is finite projective over A†_K with the trace of a finite étale algebra; the differential isomorphism in all degrees is Kedlaya, Finiteness, Proposition 3.4.5.

**Checks.**

- Kummer cover: for p ∤ N, A_0 = k[t, t^{−1}] → B_0 = k[s, s^{−1}], t ↦ s^N, lifts to O[t, t^{−1}]† → O[s, s^{−1}]†, of degree N; the Frobenius t ↦ t^p extends to s ↦ s^p.
- Degenerate case: B_0 = A_0 gives B† = A†.
- Artin–Schreier: for the finite étale cover s^p − s = t of A^1_k, O[t]†[s]/(s^p − s − t) is an étale lift (the derivative p s^{p−1} − 1 is a unit), and by uniqueness every étale lift is isomorphic to it over O[t]†.
- Non-example: for p odd the ramified cover t ↦ s² of A^1_k is not étale, and its lift O[t]†[s]/(s² − t) is not étale at s = 0; the lemma needs A_0 → B_0 étale.

<a id="target-rd-3-zariski-stack-of-overconvergent-isocrystals"></a>

### Overconvergent and convergent (F-)isocrystals form Zariski stacks

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/zariski-stack-of-overconvergent-isocrystals` · theorem

(a) For fixed Y over S, the assignment of Isoc(X, Y/S) to each open X ⊆ Y, with restriction given by pullback, is a stack for the Zariski topology: for a finite open covering X = ⋃ X_i, objects of Isoc(X, Y/S) are equivalent to objects of the Isoc(X_i, Y/S) with gluing isomorphisms on the X_i ∩ X_j satisfying the cocycle condition, and morphisms glue uniquely. (b) The assignment X ↦ Isoc(X/S) of convergent isocrystals is a Zariski stack on X. (c) With a Frobenius lift σ on K, the same holds for the categories of overconvergent and convergent F^a-isocrystals. (d) Realisations, ⊗, internal Hom and pullback commute with restriction to opens.

**Hypotheses.**

- Coverings are finite (Y quasi-compact); Zariski, not étale: étale descent is etale-descent-of-overconvergent-f-isocrystals and needs X smooth and Frobenius structures.

**Prerequisites.** [Coherent j†O-modules glue along finite open coverings of X](#target-rd-3-coherent-j-dagger-gluing) (`RD.3/coherent-j-dagger-gluing`), [Overconvergence of a connection is a property, local on P and on X, stable under subquotients](#target-rd-3-overconvergence-is-a-property) (`RD.3/overconvergence-is-a-property`), [Overconvergent isocrystals without a global frame: gluing, realisations and pullback](#target-rd-3-isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames) (`RD.3/isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames`), [Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-isocrystal) (`RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal`), [Overconvergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-f-isocrystal) (`RD.3/overconvergent-f-isocrystal`), `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/tube`.

**Sources.**

- [S62](#source-62), (2.2.11) with its remark, p. 64; (2.3.3)(i), p. 72. States that coherent j†O-modules with integrable overconvergent connection, and isocrystals overconvergent along Y − X, form a stack on Y in the variable X, and that convergent isocrystals form a stack because the tubes of an open covering form an admissible covering.
- [S63](#source-63), Part II, introductory paragraph, p. 592. Records that F^a-Isoc†(X/K) is local for the Zariski topology on X, citing Berthelot (2.1.12), (2.2.11), (2.3.7).

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a): overconvergence is local on X (overconvergence-is-a-property (d)) and coherent j†O-modules with their morphisms glue along finite coverings of X (coherent-j-dagger-gluing); apply this to the module and to the maps p_2^*E → p_1^*E (Berthelot 96-03, remark after (2.2.11), p. 64, and (2.3.3)(i), p. 72).
2. (b): for an open covering (X_α) of X the tubes ]X_α[ form an admissible covering of ]X[, so coherent modules with convergent connection glue ((2.3.3)(i)).
3. (c): Frobenius structures are isomorphisms in the stack and glue with the objects; Étesse uses this as the Zariski locality of F^a-Isoc†(X/K), citing Berthelot (2.1.12), (2.2.11), (2.3.7).

**Checks.**

- Two opens: an overconvergent isocrystal on G_m ⊂ P^1 is the same as isocrystals on G_m ∖ {1} and G_m ∖ {−1} (p odd) with a gluing isomorphism on G_m ∖ {±1}.
- Degenerate case: the trivial covering gives back Isoc(X, Y/S).
- Boundary: the stack is in the X-variable with Y fixed; changing Y is governed by RD.3/independence-of-compactification.

<a id="target-rd-3-finite-etale-pushforward-of-isocrystals"></a>

### Pushforward of (overconvergent) F-isocrystals along finite étale morphisms

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/finite-etale-pushforward-of-isocrystals` · construction

For a finite étale morphism f : X' → X of constant degree d of smooth k-schemes (extending to finite flat Y' → Y on compactifications), there are pushforward functors f_* : F-Isoc†(X'/K) → F-Isoc†(X/K) and f_* : F-Isoc(X'/K) → F-Isoc(X/K), compatible with j^*, multiplying ranks by d, right adjoint to f^* up to the trace, with H^0_F(X, f_*E) = H^0_F(X', E) (Frobenius-invariant horizontal sections). On dagger algebras: if A → B is finite étale, a (σ,∇)-module over B is viewed as a module over A. The functor f_* on F-Isoc†(X′/K) is exact and also left adjoint to f^*; the trace gives a splitting O_X → f_*O_{X′} → O_X whose composite is multiplication by the degree, and f_*O_{X′} is self-dual through the trace pairing (Kedlaya, Finiteness, Definition 3.4.2).

**Hypotheses.**

- X' → X finite étale; the construction on frames uses a finite flat extension of formal models (Kedlaya, Notes Remark 2.8).

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Isocrystals/Overconvergent`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Overconvergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-f-isocrystal) (`RD.3/overconvergent-f-isocrystal`), [Restriction from overconvergent to convergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-3-restriction-to-convergent) (`RD.3/restriction-to-convergent`), [Existence of Frobenius lifts on the weak completion of a smooth O_K-algebra (van der Put; Arabia)](#target-rd-0-frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra) (`RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra`), [(σ,∇)-modules over a dagger algebra of Monsky–Washnitzer type](#target-rd-3-sigma-nabla-module-over-dagger-algebra) (`RD.3/sigma-nabla-module-over-dagger-algebra`), [Overconvergent F-isocrystals on a smooth affine variety are (σ,∇)-modules over its dagger algebra](#target-rd-3-affine-smooth-description-of-overconvergent-f-isocrystals) (`RD.3/affine-smooth-description-of-overconvergent-f-isocrystals`), [Independence of the frame: canonical equivalences between categories of overconvergent isocrystals](#target-rd-3-independence-of-frame) (`RD.3/independence-of-frame`), `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/quasi-stein-theorems-a-b`, [Étale maps of smooth affines lift uniquely to weak completions, with Frobenius and differentials](#target-rd-3-finite-etale-lifting-of-mw-algebras) (`RD.3/finite-etale-lifting-of-mw-algebras`), [Dwork–Berthelot: a Frobenius structure forces overconvergence](#target-rd-3-frobenius-structure-forces-overconvergence) (`RD.3/frobenius-structure-forces-overconvergence`), [Pullback along a lift of a morphism of smooth affines realises the pullback of overconvergent isocrystals](#target-rd-3-mw-pullback-realises-frame-pullback) (`RD.3/mw-pullback-realises-frame-pullback`), [Overconvergent and convergent (F-)isocrystals form Zariski stacks](#target-rd-3-zariski-stack-of-overconvergent-isocrystals) (`RD.3/zariski-stack-of-overconvergent-isocrystals`), [Convergent F-isocrystals F^a-Isoc(X/K)](#target-rd-3-convergent-f-isocrystal) (`RD.3/convergent-f-isocrystal`).

**Sources.**

- [S3](#source-3), Remark 2.8, p. 4. The construction.
- [S16](#source-16), Section 7, p. 16. Use in the full faithfulness proof.
- [S4](#source-4), Definition 3.4.2, p. 23. MW-level definition.
- [S5](#source-5), Section 2.1, p. 10. Global pushforward.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- Kedlaya, Full faithfulness §7: reduce full faithfulness to affine space via finite étale covers
- Kedlaya, Finiteness Proposition 4.4.2 (RD.4/RD.5): cohomology of f_*E equals that of E
- Kedlaya, Notes Remark 2.9: finite étale maps to A^n cover smooth loci
- Kedlaya, Finiteness, proof of Proposition 9.1.1 (reduction (iii)): replace (X, E) by (A^n, f_*E) along a finite étale map to affine space
- Kedlaya, Finiteness, proof of Lemma 9.3.2: E^∨ ≅ E via the trace from U to A^n
- Kedlaya, Weil II, Section 2.1: reduction of weight statements to affine space

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FIsocDagger.pushforward` |  | f_* for f finite étale. |
| `FIsocDagger.pushforward_rank` |  | rank(f_*E) = d · rank(E). |
| `FIsocDagger.pushforward_H0` |  | H^0_F(X, f_*E) = H^0_F(X', E) in both the convergent and overconvergent categories. |
| `FIsocDagger.pushforward_restrict` |  | j^* ∘ f_* ≅ f_* ∘ j^*. |
| `FIsocDagger.pushforward_adjoint` |  | Hom(f^*E, E') ≅ Hom(E, f_*E') (f_* right adjoint to f^*), and the trace f_*f^* → id splits the unit up to d. |
| `FIsocDagger.pushforward_trace` |  | The trace f_*O_X → O_Y, with trace ∘ unit = deg(f). |
| `FIsocDagger.pushforward_dual` |  | (f_*E)^∨ ≅ f_*(E^∨) via the trace pairing; in particular f_*O_X is self-dual. |
| `FIsocDagger.pushforward_comp` |  | (g ∘ f)_* ≅ g_* ∘ f_* and (id)_* ≅ id. |

**Unit tests.**

- `FIsocDagger.pushforward_id` (degenerate): For f = id, f_* = id.
- `FIsocDagger.pushforward_rank_test` (computation): For the Artin-Schreier cover of degree p, f_*O^† has rank p.
- `FIsocDagger.pushforward_H0_test` (characterisation): H^0_F(A^1, f_*O^†) = H^0_F(X', O^†) = K^{σ_K} for X' geometrically connected.
- `FIsocDagger.pushforward_not_for_ramified` (non-example): For f : A^1 → A^1, t ↦ t^p (finite, radicial, not étale) the construction does not apply: f is not étale.
- `FIsocDagger.pushforward_kummer` (computation): For f: G_m → G_m, x ↦ x^N (p ∤ N), as differential modules, f_*O_{G_m} ≅ ⊕_{a=0}^{N−1} K_{a/N}; Frobenius permutes the summands by a ↦ qa modulo N, and the splitting is by F-isocrystals when q ≡ 1 mod N, where K_b has basis e with ∇e = b·e ⊗ dx/x.
- `FIsocDagger.pushforward_mw` (compatibility): On smooth affines, f_*M is the MW-level pushforward of Kedlaya, Definition 3.4.2, and H^i of it equals H^i(M) (RD.4/finite-etale-pushforward-de-rham).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Locally: a finite étale A_0 → B_0 lifts to finite étale A† → B†, and the Frobenius lift extends (unique lifting for étale algebras); M ↦ M viewed over A† with the same ∇ (Ω_{B†} = B† ⊗ Ω_{A†}) and Frobenius (Kedlaya, Finiteness, Definition 3.4.2).
2. H^0 statement: horizontal Frobenius-invariant sections are the same set (Kedlaya, Full faithfulness §7, citing Tsuzuki [T2, Proposition 5.1.2]); compatibility with cohomology is Kedlaya Finiteness Proposition 4.4.2 (RD.4/RD.5).
3. Construction from public sources: on a smooth affine X with lift A and Frobenius lift, a finite étale X′ → X lifts to a finite étale A† → B† with compatible Frobenius (finite-etale-lifting-of-mw-algebras); for a (σ,∇)-module M over B†_K, f_*M is M viewed over A†_K (Kedlaya, Finiteness, Definition 3.4.2) with the connection through Ω^1_{B†_K} ≅ B†_K ⊗ Ω^1_{A†_K} and the Frobenius of B†; it is a (σ,∇)-module, hence an overconvergent F-isocrystal (frobenius-structure-forces-overconvergence), independent of the lifts up to canonical isomorphism (mw-pullback-realises-frame-pullback), and these local pushforwards glue in the Zariski stack (zariski-stack-of-overconvergent-isocrystals). The convergent version is the same over Â_K with Kedlaya's Definition 2.1 (convergent-f-isocrystal). Restriction of scalars is right adjoint to f^* and, B†_K being finite étale, also left adjoint through the trace; H^0_F(X, f_*E) = Hom(O_X, f_*E) = Hom(f^*O_X, E) = H^0_F(X′, E); ranks multiply by the degree d since B†_K is projective of rank d over A†_K.

**Checks.**

- f = the Artin-Schreier cover y^p − y = t of A^1_{F_p} (Galois with group Z/p): f_*O^† has rank p, and if K contains the p-th roots of unity it splits under the Z/p-action into p rank one eigen-summands, one of them the unit object.
- For f: G_m → G_m, x ↦ x^N with p ∤ N, f_*O decomposes as differential modules into ⊕_{a=0}^{N−1} K_{a/N} (∇e = (a/N)e dx/x). Frobenius permutes these lines; an individual line has the displayed Frobenius when q ≡ 1 mod N.

<a id="target-rd-3-affine-space-two-embeddings-acceptance"></a>

### Acceptance: the frames A^n ⊂ P^n and A^n ⊂ (P^1)^n give equivalent categories

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/affine-space-two-embeddings-acceptance` · application

Let X = A^n_k with the two compactifications Y_1 = P^n_k and Y_2 = (P^1_k)^n and frames (X, Y_1, P̂^n_O), (X, Y_2, (P̂^1_O)^n). (a) In both frames the tube ]X[ is the closed unit polydisc {|t_i| ≤ 1}, and the polydiscs V_λ = {|t_i| ≤ λ^{-1} for all i} (λ < 1, λ → 1) form a cofinal family of strict neighbourhoods, so Γ(]Y_i[, j†O) = K⟨t_1, ..., t_n⟩† in both cases. (b) The equivalence Isoc†(A^n ⊂ P^n/K) ≃ Isoc†(A^n ⊂ (P^1)^n/K) of RD.3/independence-of-compactification is realised through the closure Y_3 of the diagonal of A^n in P^n × (P^1)^n, whose projections to Y_1 and Y_2 are proper and are isomorphisms over A^n, with the frame (X, Y_3, P̂^n × (P̂^1)^n) mapping to both frames; on the pullback of the Dwork isocrystal along the first coordinate it sends (K⟨t_1..t_n⟩†, ∇(1) = π dt_1) to itself.

**Hypotheses.**

- n ≥ 1; for n = 1 the two compactifications coincide and the statement is the identity.

**Prerequisites.** [Independence of the frame: canonical equivalences between categories of overconvergent isocrystals](#target-rd-3-independence-of-frame) (`RD.3/independence-of-frame`), [Independence of the compactification](#target-rd-3-independence-of-compactification) (`RD.3/independence-of-compactification`), [Global overconvergent functions on an affine frame are the dagger algebra](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-sections-of-affine-frame) (`RD.3/overconvergent-sections-of-affine-frame`), [Strict neighbourhoods of ]X[ in ]Y[](#target-rd-3-strict-neighbourhood) (`RD.3/strict-neighbourhood`), [Frames (X ⊂ Y ⊂ P)](#target-rd-3-frame) (`RD.3/frame`).

**Sources.**

- [S20](#source-20), (2.1), p. 16. The tube of the divisor at infinity of P^n with radius λ (read from the page image).
- [S20](#source-20), (4.2.2), p. 27. Independence of the compactification (read from the page image).

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a) In P^n with homogeneous coordinates x_0..x_n and Z = {x_0 = 0}: ]Z[_λ = {|x_0| < λ max_i |x_i|}, whose complement is {|t_i| ≤ λ^{-1}}, t_i = x_i/x_0 (Berthelot §2.1, p. 16, using the projective-coordinate inequalities). In (P^1)^n, Z = ∪_i {t_i = ∞} is cut out near a boundary point by the product of the coordinates s_i = 1/t_i with |t_i| ≥ 1, so the complement W_λ of ]Z[_λ is {|t_i| ≤ λ^{-1} for all i, and |Π_{i∈I} t_i| ≤ λ^{-1} for the set I of indices with |t_i| ≥ 1}; hence W_λ ⊆ V_λ ⊆ W_{λ^n}, and the two families are cofinal. Global sections: RD.3/overconvergent-sections-of-affine-frame.
2. (b) The graph closure Y_3 ⊆ Y_1 × Y_2 contains X as an open subscheme with v_i^{-1}(X) = X for both projections v_i (both are isomorphisms over A^n), so RD.3/independence-of-compactification applies to v_1 and v_2; the diagonal frame is smooth over O (RD.3/independence-of-frame (b)).
3. Computation: under both identifications the pullback of the Dwork isocrystal along the first coordinate t_1 is the free rank one K⟨t_1..t_n⟩†-module with ∇(1) = π dt_1, and its Taylor isomorphism exp π(t'_1 − t_1) converges on the diagonal tube {|t_1 − t'_1| < 1}; the larger strict neighbourhood concerns the base frame coordinates in either frame (Berthelot 4.2.3 b for n = 1).

**Checks.**

- Test: strict neighbourhoods agree: for λ < 1 the complement of ]Z_1[_λ in (P^n)^an is exactly the polydisc V_λ = {|t_i| ≤ λ^{-1}}, and the complement W_λ of ]Z_2[_λ in ((P^1)^n)^an satisfies W_λ ⊆ V_λ ⊆ W_{λ^n} (for n = 2 and |t_1|, |t_2| ≥ 1, W_λ is {|t_1 t_2| ≤ λ^{-1}}, strictly smaller than V_λ).
- Test: global sections of j†O in both frames equal K⟨t_1..t_n⟩† (the union over λ of the Tate algebras of the polydiscs of radius λ^{-1}).

<a id="target-rd-1-common-vertex-global-subobject"></a>

### Common Newton-vertex subisocrystal

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/common-vertex-global-subobject` · theorem

Let X be a smooth variety over a perfect field k of characteristic p, with an F^n-bearing convergent isocrystal E and a common Newton-polygon vertex of horizontal coordinate a at every geometric point. Then there is a unique convergent Frobenius subisocrystal of rank a whose slopes are the smallest a slopes at each point.

**Hypotheses.**

- Finite coefficient field, fixed n≥1 and a fixed common break; use the convergent category, not merely a differential module or an arbitrary overconvergent subobject.

**Prerequisites.** [Restriction from overconvergent to convergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-3-restriction-to-convergent) (`RD.3/restriction-to-convergent`), [Dieudonné-Manin classification over a complete discretely valued field with algebraically closed residue field](#target-rd-1-dieudonne-manin-classical) (`RD.1/dieudonne-manin-classical`), [Calculus of slopes: direct sums, tensor products, exterior powers, restriction of Frobenius, twists, Hom vanishing](#target-rd-1-calculus-of-slopes) (`RD.1/calculus-of-slopes`).

**Sources.**

- [S56](#source-56), Theorem 4.1, Corollary 4.2 and Remark 4.5, PDF pp. 8–9. A common vertex is the global extension input for a constant-Newton-polygon slope filtration.

**Construction or proof.**

1. At the generic point use classical Dieudonné–Manin to select the initial slope block.
2. Extend the corresponding subobject across the base by the common-vertex theorem; this uses the curve/Katz purity arguments named in Notes Theorem 4.1, not just generic linear algebra (G4).
3. A connection respects the block because its second fundamental map goes from lower slopes to higher slopes and the relevant Frobenius Hom is zero (Notes Remark 4.5). Uniqueness follows from the same slope separation.

**Checks.**

- The subobject is connection-stable, not only Frobenius-stable at generic points.
- Neither this theorem nor its application asserts that the filtration lies in the overconvergent category.

<a id="target-rd-1-dense-open-global-slopes"></a>

### Dense-open global slope filtration

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/dense-open-global-slopes` · theorem

For an F^n-bearing convergent isocrystal on a smooth variety X over perfect k, there is a dense open U whose complement is a divisor such that on each connected component of U the Newton polygon is constant and the isocrystal has a unique filtration with isoclinic graded pieces of strictly increasing slopes.

**Hypotheses.**

- X is smooth of finite type; coefficients and F^n are fixed as in common-vertex-global-subobject.
- An empty divisor is allowed; disconnected components are treated separately.

**Prerequisites.** [Common Newton-vertex subisocrystal](#target-rd-1-common-vertex-global-subobject) (`RD.1/common-vertex-global-subobject`), [Restriction from overconvergent to convergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-3-restriction-to-convergent) (`RD.3/restriction-to-convergent`).

**Sources.**

- [S28](#source-28), §2.2, p. 6. A divisor may be removed to obtain the global increasing slope filtration.
- [S32](#source-32), Appendix A §A.2, PDF p. 64. Constant-Newton-polygon convergent F-isocrystals admit the ascending filtration.
- [S56](#source-56), Theorem 3.12 and Corollary 4.2, PDF pp. 7–8. Purity and common-vertex extension provide the geometric prerequisite chain.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Upper semicontinuity and purity of the Newton-jumping locus give a dense open constant-polygon locus with complement of pure codimension one (Notes Theorem 3.12). On regular X this is the support of a divisor. The proof of this purity supplier is G4.
2. For each successive vertex use the common-vertex theorem, then pass to its quotient.
3. The first graded piece has the smallest slope. Frobenius-Hom vanishing gives compatibility and uniqueness; the result is global on U and distinct from the local Robba slope filtration of RD.2.

**Checks.**

- A constant slope-zero object permits U=X.
- A bare connection without Frobenius does not have this Newton filtration.

<a id="target-rd-3-underlying-bundle-of-convergent-isocrystal"></a>

### The underlying vector bundle with connection of a convergent isocrystal on a smooth formal O_K-scheme

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/underlying-bundle-of-convergent-isocrystal` · construction

Let 𝔛 be a smooth formal scheme over Spf O_K, O_K possibly ramified over W(k), with special fibre 𝔛_s and rigid generic fibre 𝔛_η, and let E be a convergent isocrystal on 𝔛_s/K_0, K_0 = W(k)[1/p].
