(i) E has an underlying vector bundle with flat connection (E, ∇) on 𝔛_η: the realisation of E on the (not necessarily W(k)-smooth) formal scheme 𝔛, in which 𝔛_s is defined by an ideal of definition (isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames (b)); the connection is relative to K_0, equivalently to K. (ii) If E underlies a crystalline F-isocrystal on 𝔛_s/W(k), then for every W(k)-model Ũ of an affine open U ⊆ 𝔛 (Ũ ⊗_{W(k)} O_K ≅ U; such models exist for framed affines), (E, ∇)|_{U_η} ≅ (E(Ũ), ∇_Ũ) ⊗_{K_0} K, the right side being given by convergent-f-isocrystals-are-crystalline (d). The construction is exact, compatible with ⊗, duals and pullback along morphisms of smooth formal O_K-schemes.

**Hypotheses.**

- Over a ramified base 𝔛 has no Frobenius lift compatible with a lift of Frobenius on O_K in general; Frobenius structures are carried by E on the special fibre, not by the bundle.
- Framings (étale maps to Spf O_K⟨x_1^{±1}, …, x_d^{±1}⟩) exist on a basis of affine opens (Guo–Reinecke, Lemma 2.10).
- Guo–Reinecke state (i) for convergent isocrystals on Ogus's convergent site of 𝔛_{p=0}; by Berthelot (2.3.4) these are the convergent isocrystals defined by tubes, and tubes depend only on the reduced subscheme, so a convergent isocrystal on 𝔛_s is the same datum.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Isocrystals/Convergent`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Overconvergent isocrystals without a global frame: gluing, realisations and pullback](#target-rd-3-isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames) (`RD.3/isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames`), [Convergent isocrystals Isoc(X/K)](#target-rd-3-convergent-isocrystal) (`RD.3/convergent-isocrystal`), [Convergent F-isocrystals are F-crystals up to isogeny and twist (Berthelot, Ogus)](#target-rd-3-convergent-f-isocrystals-are-crystalline) (`RD.3/convergent-f-isocrystals-are-crystalline`), `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/raynaud-generic-fibre`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/smooth-lifting-from-level-zero`.

**Sources.**

- [S64](#source-64), Lemmas 2.9–2.10 and Proposition 2.17, pp. 14 and 16. Constructs the W(k)-model of a framed affine smooth formal O_K-scheme and states that a convergent isocrystal has an underlying vector bundle with flat connection on the generic fibre, locally given by the bundle of the F-isocrystal on any W(k)-model, citing Ogus.
- [S62](#source-62), (2.3.2)(ii), pp. 70–71. Defines the realisation of an isocrystal on an arbitrary formal scheme containing an open of Y, including formal schemes over a discrete valuation ring in which the subscheme is defined by an ideal of definition.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- Guo–Reinecke, Definition 2.18, p. 16: filtered F-isocrystals are F-isocrystals with a Griffiths-transversal filtration on the underlying bundle
- Guo–Reinecke, proof of Theorem 6.13, pp. 60–61: the comparison of crystalline pushforwards with convergent F-isocrystals uses the underlying bundles
- PadicHodgeTheory (consumer): crystalline local systems on the generic fibre are compared with filtered F-isocrystals through their underlying bundles

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ConvIsoc.underlyingBundle` |  | The vector bundle E on 𝔛_η underlying a convergent isocrystal on 𝔛_s, for 𝔛 smooth over Spf O_K. |
| `ConvIsoc.underlyingConnection` |  | Its flat connection relative to K. |
| `ConvIsoc.underlyingBundle_localModel` |  | For a W(k)-model Ũ of an affine open U: (E, ∇)\|_{U_η} ≅ (E(Ũ), ∇_Ũ) ⊗_{K_0} K. |
| `ConvIsoc.underlyingBundle_monoidal` |  | Exact, compatible with ⊗, duals and the unit. |
| `ConvIsoc.underlyingBundle_pullback` |  | Compatible with pullback along morphisms of smooth formal O_K-schemes. |

**Unit tests.**

- `ConvIsoc.underlyingBundle_unit` (degenerate): The unit isocrystal has underlying bundle (O_{𝔛_η}, d).
- `ConvIsoc.underlyingBundle_unramified` (compatibility): For O_K = W(k) and 𝔛 = Spf R with a Frobenius lift, the underlying bundle of an F-isocrystal is E(𝔛)[1/p], the bundle of convergent-f-isocrystals-are-crystalline (d).
- `ConvIsoc.underlyingBundle_baseChange` (computation): For 𝔛 = Ũ ⊗_{W(k)} O_K, the underlying bundle is the base change (E(Ũ)[1/p], ∇) ⊗_{K_0} K.
- `ConvIsoc.underlyingBundle_forgets_frobenius` (non-example): The unit object O and the Tate object O(1) have the same underlying bundle with connection (O_{𝔛_η}, d) but are not isomorphic as F-isocrystals: the bundle does not determine Φ.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Realisation: for an affine open U with a closed immersion of U_s into a smooth formal W(k)-scheme P, lift U_s → P to u: U → P by formal smoothness along the ideal of definition, and put E_U = u_K^* E_P on U_η = ]U_s[_U; independence and gluing are isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames (b) (Berthelot 96-03 (2.3.2)(ii), last paragraph, pp. 70–71).
2. (ii): for a framed affine U, the unique W(k)-model Ũ with lifted framing (Guo–Reinecke, Lemma 2.9) gives u: U = Ũ ⊗ O_K → Ũ, so E_U = (E(Ũ)[1/p]) ⊗_{K_0} K with its connection (Guo–Reinecke, Proposition 2.17, citing Ogus 1984, Remark 2.8.1, Theorem 2.15, Proposition 2.21).

**Checks.**

- Unit: the underlying bundle of the unit isocrystal is (O_{𝔛_η}, d).
- Unramified case: O_K = W(k) and 𝔛 = Ũ give E(𝔛)[1/p] itself.

<a id="target-rd-3-unit-root-f-isocrystal"></a>

### Unit-root F-isocrystals

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/unit-root-f-isocrystal` · definition

Let E be a convergent or overconvergent F^a-isocrystal on X. E is unit-root if for every geometric point x̄ of X all Frobenius slopes of the fibre x̄^*E are zero, i.e. the fibre has a basis e_1, …, e_r with Φ(e_i ⊗ 1) = e_i (Étesse §5.1); equivalently the fibre at every perfect point is isoclinic of slope 0. Unit-root objects form a full subcategory F^a-Isoc(X/K)^0 (respectively F^a-Isoc†(X/K)^0) stable under ⊗, duals, subquotients and extensions, with no non-zero morphisms to or from isoclinic objects of non-zero slope. At a perfect point with a = 1 and K = W(k)[1/p], unit-root means that the Mathlib isocrystal has a W-lattice L with Φ(L) = L, equivalently a basis in which the matrix of Φ lies in GL_r(W).

**Hypotheses.**

- Slopes are computed after pulling back to a perfect (or algebraically closed) point, where the Dieudonné–Manin classification applies.
- For overconvergent objects the condition is on the image in the convergent category; it is the same pointwise condition.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Isocrystals/UnitRoot`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Convergent F-isocrystals F^a-Isoc(X/K)](#target-rd-3-convergent-f-isocrystal) (`RD.3/convergent-f-isocrystal`), [Overconvergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-f-isocrystal) (`RD.3/overconvergent-f-isocrystal`), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/isocrystal-slope-decomposition`, `mathlib:WittVector.Isocrystal`, `mathlib:WittVector.isocrystal_classification`.

**Sources.**

- [S63](#source-63), §5.1, p. 590. Defines unit F^a-isocrystals (convergent or overconvergent) as those whose Frobenius has all slopes zero at every geometric point, i.e. has a fixed basis of the fibre.
- [S3](#source-3), Definition 3.3 and the following paragraph, p. 6. Defines slope multisets at points via perfect closures, isoclinic and unit-root (étale) objects, their stability under subquotients and extensions, and the vanishing of morphisms between isoclinic objects of distinct slopes.
- [S28](#source-28), Definition 3.3.3, p. 11. Considers the Tannakian subcategory of isoclinic F^∞-isocrystals and its relation to lisse sheaves.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/crew-unit-root-correspondence: unit-root objects are the essential image of lisse ℚ_q-sheaves
- Étesse 2002, Théorème 5, p. 597: full faithfulness F^a-Isoc†(X/K)^0 → F^a-Isoc(X/K)^0 for unit-root objects
- D’Addezio, Proposition 3.3.4, p. 11: isoclinic F^∞-isocrystals as twists of unit-root ones, compared with lisse sheaves
- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/punctured-curve-boundary-acceptance: the unit-root subobject of H^1 of the universal elliptic curve on the ordinary locus is convergent but not overconvergent

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FIsoc.IsUnitRoot` |  | The predicate: every fibre at a geometric point has all Frobenius slopes 0. |
| `FIsoc.isUnitRoot_iff_fibre` |  | E is unit-root iff each fibre at a perfect point admits a lattice stable under Φ on which Φ is bijective. |
| `FIsoc.IsUnitRoot.tensor` |  | Unit-root objects are stable under ⊗, duals and internal Hom, and contain the unit. |
| `FIsoc.IsUnitRoot.subquotient` |  | Subobjects and quotients of unit-root objects are unit-root. |
| `FIsoc.IsUnitRoot.extension` |  | Extensions of unit-root objects are unit-root. |
| `FIsoc.IsUnitRoot.pullback` |  | Pullback along any morphism preserves being unit-root. |
| `FIsoc.hom_eq_zero_of_slopes_ne` |  | There are no non-zero morphisms between isoclinic objects of distinct slopes; in particular from unit-root objects to O(n), n ≠ 0. |

**Unit tests.**

- `FIsoc.isUnitRoot_slopeZero_point` (computation): At a perfect point, Mathlib's StandardOneDimIsocrystal p k 0 (Φ = σ) is unit-root: the lattice W(k) is Φ-stable with Φ bijective.
- `FIsoc.not_isUnitRoot_slopeOne` (non-example): StandardOneDimIsocrystal p k 1 (Φ = pσ) is not unit-root: every lattice L satisfies Φ(L) = pL ≠ L.
- `FIsoc.isUnitRoot_unit` (degenerate): The unit object (Φ = id) is unit-root, and so is the zero object.
- `FIsoc.dwork_isUnitRoot` (computation): The Dwork F-isocrystal on A^1 is unit-root: it has rank one and its Frobenius at the point 0 is θ(0) = 1. At the point 1 its Frobenius is θ(1) = ζ_p, a primitive p-th root of unity and so a unit but not 1; a test asserting Φ = 1 at every Teichmüller point would be wrong.
- `FIsoc.tate_not_unitRoot` (non-example): O(1) is isoclinic of slope −1 and not unit-root, although it has rank one.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Fibres at perfect points are F^a-isocrystals over K(Ω) (convergent-f-isocrystal); over an algebraically closed point Dieudonné–Manin (CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/isocrystal-slope-decomposition; Mathlib's isocrystal_classification in rank one) decomposes them by slope, and slope 0 means a Φ-fixed basis (Étesse 2002 §5.1, p. 590; Kedlaya, Notes, Definition 3.3, p. 6).
2. Stability under subquotients and extensions and the vanishing of Hom between distinct slopes are Kedlaya, Notes, Definition 3.3 and the remark after it (slopes are additive in exact sequences); the lattice characterisation at a point follows from Dieudonné–Manin.

**Checks.**

- The Dwork F-isocrystal L_π (∇(1) = −π dt, Φ = θ(t) := exp π(t − t^p), σ = id) is unit-root: it has rank one, hence is isoclinic (Kedlaya, Notes, Remark 3.5), and at the point 0 its Frobenius is θ(0) = 1. At the other F_p-points the Frobenius is not 1: by Dwork's theorem θ(1) = ζ_p is a primitive p-th root of unity (ζ_p ≡ 1 + π mod π²) and θ(x̂) = ζ_p^x for the Teichmüller lift x̂ of x ∈ F_p, a unit, consistently with slope 0. The tempting substitution x̂^p = x̂ inside exp π(t − t^p) is not legitimate: exp(πt) and exp(−πt^p) diverge on |t| = 1, and only their product θ converges there.
- The Tate object O(1) is isoclinic of slope −1, hence not unit-root.

<a id="target-rd-3-crew-unit-root-correspondence"></a>

### Katz–Crew: unit-root F-isocrystals are lisse p-adic sheaves

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/crew-unit-root-correspondence` · theorem

Let k be a perfect field containing F_q (q = p^a), K = W(k)[1/p] with σ the Witt-vector Frobenius, and X a smooth separated k-scheme of finite type. Let ℚ_q = W(F_q)[1/p] ⊆ K. The functor V ↦ (V ⊗_{ℚ_q} O_{X/K}, 1 ⊗ σ^a) is an exact fully faithful ⊗-functor from the category of étale ℚ_q-local systems on X to F^a-Isoc(X/K), with essential image the unit-root convergent F^a-isocrystals; a quasi-inverse sends E to the étale sheaf of Φ-fixed horizontal sections. If X is connected with a geometric point x̄, unit-root convergent F^a-isocrystals are thus equivalent to continuous representations of π_1^ét(X, x̄) on finite-dimensional ℚ_q-vector spaces. For a = 1 this is the equivalence of Kedlaya, Notes, Theorem 3.7; the version with ℚ_q-coefficients and F^a-structures is the one used in D’Addezio, proof of Proposition 3.3.4.

**Hypotheses.**

- X smooth; the field k perfect and containing F_q so that the F^a-isocrystal category is ℚ_q-linear.
- Local systems are étale ℚ_q-local systems: the étale stackification of the isogeny category of ℤ_q-local systems (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.0/adic-local-systems, with W(F_q)-coefficients).

**Prerequisites.** [Unit-root F-isocrystals](#target-rd-3-unit-root-f-isocrystal) (`RD.3/unit-root-f-isocrystal`), [Convergent F-isocrystals F^a-Isoc(X/K)](#target-rd-3-convergent-f-isocrystal) (`RD.3/convergent-f-isocrystal`), [Convergent F-isocrystals are F-crystals up to isogeny and twist (Berthelot, Ogus)](#target-rd-3-convergent-f-isocrystals-are-crystalline) (`RD.3/convergent-f-isocrystals-are-crystalline`), `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.0/adic-local-systems`, `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.0/etale-fundamental-group`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.1/isocrystal`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/isocrystal-slope-decomposition`, `mathlib:WittVector.Isocrystal`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Etale`.

**Sources.**

- [S3](#source-3), Theorem 3.7, p. 6, and Remark 3.10, p. 7. States that unit-root objects of F-Isoc(X) are equivalent to étale ℚ_p-local systems, hence to continuous representations of the étale fundamental group for connected X, with the local model over k((t)), citing Crew 1987, Theorem 2.1.
- [S28](#source-28), Proposition 3.3.4 and its proof, p. 11. Uses Crew's theorem in the form: for every n, a fully faithful ℚ_{p^n}-linear ⊗-functor from lisse ℚ_{p^n}-sheaves to F^n-isocrystals with essential image the unit-root objects.
- [S3](#source-3), Remark 2.3, p. 3. Notes that unit-root convergent F-isocrystals, unlike general ones, come from crystals of locally free modules.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Lattices: a unit-root convergent F^a-isocrystal is, locally on X, M ⊗ ℚ for a crystal M of finite locally free modules with Φ: (F^a)^*M ≅ M an isomorphism (Kedlaya, Notes, Remark 2.3 records that unit-root objects come from crystals of locally free modules; for the convergent/crystalline translation use convergent-f-isocrystals-are-crystalline (c)).
2. Katz's construction (the proof in Crew 1987, Theorem 2.1, and Katz's Proposition 4.1.1 are not publicly accessible; this outline is supplied here): on M/p^m the equation Φ(v) = v is solved étale-locally, because the Lang map g ↦ g^{−1} σ^a(g) on GL_r(W_m(k′)) is finite étale and surjective; the solutions form a locally constant sheaf T_m of free W_m(F_q)-modules of rank r, and T = lim T_m is a ℤ_q-local system with M ≅ T ⊗ O_crys compatibly with Φ = 1 ⊗ σ^a.
3. Conversely T ↦ T ⊗ O_crys with Φ = 1 ⊗ σ^a is a unit-root F^a-crystal; on Hom-spaces both constructions identify Hom(V, V′) with the Φ-fixed horizontal sections of the internal Hom, which gives full faithfulness; pass to isogeny categories and stackify on both sides (rational local systems are étale-locally of the form T[1/p]), using that convergent F^a-isocrystals on smooth X form an étale stack (Kedlaya, Notes, Definition 2.1 and the remark after it).
4. For X connected, the étale ℚ_q-local systems are continuous ℚ_q-representations of π_1^ét(X, x̄) (IG.0/adic-local-systems with IG.0/etale-fundamental-group).

**Checks.**

- Point over F_p: the F-isocrystal (ℚ_p, Φ = u) with u ∈ ℤ_p^× is unit-root and corresponds to the character of Gal(F̄_p/F_p) sending the arithmetic Frobenius to u^{−1}: a Φ-fixed vector v of K̂^{ur} satisfies u σ(v) = v, so σ(v) = u^{−1} v.
- Non-example: (ℚ_p, Φ = p) over F_p has no non-zero Φ-fixed vector over K̂^{ur} (v_p(p σ(v)) = 1 + v_p(v)), consistently with its slope 1.
- Over an algebraically closed point the theorem is Dieudonné–Manin: unit-root F-isocrystals are ℚ_p-vector spaces tensored with K.

<a id="target-rd-3-direct-summands-of-overconvergent-f-isocrystals"></a>

### Étesse: convergent direct summands of overconvergent F-isocrystals are overconvergent

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/direct-summands-of-overconvergent-f-isocrystals` · theorem

Let X be a smooth separated k-scheme of finite type. (1) If E ∈ F^a-Isoc†(X/K) and its image Ê ∈ F^a-Isoc(X/K) decomposes as Ê ≅ E_1 ⊕ E_2, then there are E_1†, E_2† ∈ F^a-Isoc†(X/K), unique up to isomorphism, with Ê_i† ≅ E_i and E ≅ E_1† ⊕ E_2†. (2) If E ≅ E_1† ⊕ E_2† and E′ ≅ E′_1† ⊕ E′_2† are two such objects and g: E → E′ is a morphism whose image ĝ is diagonal, ĝ = φ ⊕ ψ, then there are unique f_i: E_i† → E′_i† with g = f_1 ⊕ f_2 and ĝ = f̂_1 ⊕ f̂_2.

**Hypotheses.**

- X smooth; Frobenius structures are part of the data (the proof uses the Monsky–Washnitzer description of frobenius-structure-forces-overconvergence).

**Prerequisites.** [Dwork–Berthelot: a Frobenius structure forces overconvergence](#target-rd-3-frobenius-structure-forces-overconvergence) (`RD.3/frobenius-structure-forces-overconvergence`), [Overconvergent and convergent (F-)isocrystals form Zariski stacks](#target-rd-3-zariski-stack-of-overconvergent-isocrystals) (`RD.3/zariski-stack-of-overconvergent-isocrystals`), [On the Monsky–Washnitzer frame of a smooth affine, global sections give an equivalence with A†_K-modules](#target-rd-3-affine-frame-global-sections-equivalence) (`RD.3/affine-frame-global-sections-equivalence`), [Convergent F-isocrystals F^a-Isoc(X/K)](#target-rd-3-convergent-f-isocrystal) (`RD.3/convergent-f-isocrystal`), [Overconvergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-f-isocrystal) (`RD.3/overconvergent-f-isocrystal`), [Monsky–Washnitzer algebras are henselian along π; lifting of étale algebras and descent of projective modules](#target-rd-3-weak-completion-henselian-descent) (`RD.3/weak-completion-henselian-descent`), `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-completion-comparison`.

**Sources.**

- [S63](#source-63), Théorème 6 and its proof, p. 598; Proposition 6 with Corollaries 1–2, p. 586; Propositions 9′ and 10′, pp. 590–592. Proves that a direct summand, in the convergent category, of an overconvergent F^a-isocrystal on a smooth variety is overconvergent, uniquely, with the corresponding statement for morphisms, through the henselian property of Monsky–Washnitzer algebras and descent of projective modules and connections along A†_K ⊂ Â_K.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Localise on X (Zariski stack, zariski-stack-of-overconvergent-isocrystals), so X = Spec A_0 smooth affine with lift A and Frobenius lift F on A†; by frobenius-structure-forces-overconvergence, E is a (σ,∇)-module N over A†_K and Ê corresponds to N ⊗ Â_K (Étesse 2002, §5.2, pp. 591–592).
2. Since (A†, πA†) is a henselian pair and A† is a Zariski ring (weak-completion-henselian-descent), finitely generated projective Â_K-modules descend uniquely to A†_K and summands of N ⊗ Â_K lift to summands M, P of N (Étesse, Proposition 6 and Corollaries 1–2, p. 586, by Elkik's approximation theorem); the decomposition is identified as M = M̂ ∩ N inside N ⊗ Â_K using A†_K = Â_K ∩ B for suitable faithfully flat extensions (Proposition 2 and its corollary, pp. 580–583).
3. The connection and Frobenius of N restrict to M because Ω^1 and the Frobenius pullbacks are compatible with these intersections (Corollary 2 (2)(iii)–(iv) and Propositions 9′ and 10′, pp. 590–592); this gives the affine case of (1) and (2), and the pieces glue by the Zariski stack property (Théorème 6 and its proof, p. 598).

**Checks.**

- Degenerate splitting: Ê = Ê ⊕ 0 lifts to E ⊕ 0.
- Kummer pair (p odd, X = G_m): the direct sum of the Kummer F-isocrystals with a = 0 and a = 1/(p−1) is overconvergent, and its convergent decomposition lifts to the overconvergent decomposition.
- Non-example: a convergent subobject that is not a direct summand need not be overconvergent — the unit-root subobject of H^1 of the universal elliptic curve on the ordinary locus (RD.3/punctured-curve-boundary-acceptance; Berthelot (2.3.9)(iii)).

<a id="target-rd-3-etale-descent-of-overconvergent-f-isocrystals"></a>

### Étesse: étale descent for overconvergent F-isocrystals

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/etale-descent-of-overconvergent-f-isocrystals` · theorem

Let X be a smooth separated k-scheme of finite type. (1) Every étale surjective morphism f: Y → X satisfies descent for overconvergent F^a-isocrystals: f^* induces an equivalence from F^a-Isoc†(X/K) to the category of objects of F^a-Isoc†(Y/K) with descent data relative to f (isomorphisms p_2^*E ≅ p_1^*E on Y ×_X Y satisfying the cocycle condition on Y ×_X Y ×_X Y). (2) If f: Y → X is étale, dominant and separated, F^a-Isoc†(X/K) is the 2-fibre product of F^a-Isoc(X/K) and F^a-Isoc†(Y/K) over F^a-Isoc(Y/K): a convergent F^a-isocrystal on X whose pullback to Y is overconvergent is overconvergent, uniquely, and similarly for morphisms. (3) The analogous fibre-product statements hold for an extension of the base field k ⊆ k′ (with K ⊆ K′ as in Étesse 1.1) and for the combination of both. (4) A proper surjective generically étale morphism f: Y → X also satisfies descent for overconvergent F^a-isocrystals.

**Hypotheses.**

- X smooth and Frobenius structures present; the convergent descent results of Ogus (1984, Theorems 4.5 and 4.6) are used over a perfect closure of k.

**Prerequisites.** [Étale maps of smooth affines lift uniquely to weak completions, with Frobenius and differentials](#target-rd-3-finite-etale-lifting-of-mw-algebras) (`RD.3/finite-etale-lifting-of-mw-algebras`), [Dwork–Berthelot: a Frobenius structure forces overconvergence](#target-rd-3-frobenius-structure-forces-overconvergence) (`RD.3/frobenius-structure-forces-overconvergence`), [On the Monsky–Washnitzer frame of a smooth affine, global sections give an equivalence with A†_K-modules](#target-rd-3-affine-frame-global-sections-equivalence) (`RD.3/affine-frame-global-sections-equivalence`), [Overconvergent and convergent (F-)isocrystals form Zariski stacks](#target-rd-3-zariski-stack-of-overconvergent-isocrystals) (`RD.3/zariski-stack-of-overconvergent-isocrystals`), [Overconvergent isocrystals without a global frame: gluing, realisations and pullback](#target-rd-3-isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames) (`RD.3/isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames`), [Coherent j†O-modules glue along finite open coverings of X](#target-rd-3-coherent-j-dagger-gluing) (`RD.3/coherent-j-dagger-gluing`), [Convergent F-isocrystals F^a-Isoc(X/K)](#target-rd-3-convergent-f-isocrystal) (`RD.3/convergent-f-isocrystal`), [Independence of the compactification](#target-rd-3-independence-of-compactification) (`RD.3/independence-of-compactification`), [Overconvergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-f-isocrystal) (`RD.3/overconvergent-f-isocrystal`), `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-completion-comparison`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Etale`.

**Sources.**

- [S63](#source-63), Théorèmes 1, 2, 2′, 2″, 3 and their proofs, pp. 592–596; Proposition 10, pp. 591–592. Proves étale descent, the fibre-product description along étale dominant morphisms and base field extensions, and descent along proper surjective generically étale morphisms for overconvergent F^a-isocrystals on smooth separated varieties, from Ogus's convergent descent and a Monsky–Washnitzer intersection argument.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Base change to an algebraic closure k′ of k: by Ogus's theorem the convergent F^a-isocrystal descends along f′ (imported, unread input) (Étesse 2002, proof of Théorème 1, p. 593).
2. On a dense affine open U = Spec A_0 ⊆ X with an affine open V = Spec B_0 of Y étale dominant over it, lift to A† → B† (finite-etale-lifting-of-mw-algebras) and use the intersection description A†_K = Â′_{K′} ∩ B†_K: a module over Â′_{K′} with connection and Frobenius whose base change to B̂′ comes from a (σ,∇)-module over B†_K comes from a unique (σ,∇)-module over A†_K (Étesse, Proposition 10, pp. 591–592, built on Propositions 2–9).
3. Glue the affine pieces: with a global frame through the equivalences of RD.3/independence-of-compactification and the gluing of coherent j†-modules (coherent-j-dagger-gluing); without one, along local frames (isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames, Berthelot (2.3.2)(iii)); Frobenius structures glue by the same uniqueness (pp. 593–595).
4. (2), (3) are proved the same way (Théorèmes 2, 2′, 2″, pp. 595–596); (4) combines Ogus's proper descent with (2) over a dense open where f is étale (Théorème 3, p. 596).

**Checks.**

- Kummer descent (p odd, K ⊇ μ_{p−1}): along the finite étale Galois cover G_m → G_m, s ↦ s^{p−1} = t, with group μ_{p−1}, descent data on the unit object of G_m correspond to characters of μ_{p−1}, and descend to the Kummer F-isocrystals on G_m with ∇(1) = (m/(p−1)) dt/t and Frobenius t^m.
- Trivial cover: for f = id descent data are the identity and (1) is the identity functor.
- Zariski coverings are a special case, already covered by zariski-stack-of-overconvergent-isocrystals without smoothness or Frobenius.

<a id="target-rd-3-kummer-isocrystal"></a>

### Kummer isocrystals K_a on G_m

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/kummer-isocrystal` · construction

On the frame (G_m, P^1_k, P̂^1_O) with coordinate t, for a ∈ ℤ_p let K_a be the free j†O_{P^1_K}-module of rank one on a generator e with ∇(e) = a e ⊗ dt/t. Global sections of j†O are the Laurent series Σ_{n∈ℤ} c_n t^n converging on some annulus ρ < |t| < 1/ρ, ρ < 1 (written K⟨t, t^{−1}⟩†), and the sections on the tube ]G_m[ = {|t| = 1} form K⟨t, t^{−1}⟩. Then: K_a is an overconvergent isocrystal on G_m; K_a ⊗ K_b ≅ K_{a+b} and K_a^∨ ≅ K_{−a}; K_a ≅ K_b if and only if a − b ∈ ℤ (an isomorphism K_b → K_a is e_b ↦ t^{b−a} e_a); the horizontal sections of K_a, over the tube or over a strict neighbourhood, are K·t^{−a} e if a ∈ ℤ and 0 otherwise; the pullback along t ↦ t^N is K_{Na}; and, for the Frobenius lift t ↦ t^p with σ = id on K, K_a admits a Frobenius structure if and only if (p − 1)a ∈ ℤ, the structure being multiplication by t^{(p−1)a}.

**Hypotheses.**

- a ∈ ℤ_p is needed for convergence: for a ∉ ℤ_p the binomial coefficients binom(a, k) are unbounded and the connection is not even convergent.
- Frobenius structures are taken with σ = id on K (K ⊇ ℚ_p arbitrary) and the lift t ↦ t^p.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Isocrystals/Overconvergent`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [The coordinate criterion for convergence and overconvergence of a connection](#target-rd-3-taylor-series-convergence-criterion) (`RD.3/taylor-series-convergence-criterion`), [Overconvergence of a connection is a property, local on P and on X, stable under subquotients](#target-rd-3-overconvergence-is-a-property) (`RD.3/overconvergence-is-a-property`), [Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-isocrystal) (`RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal`), [Frames (X ⊂ Y ⊂ P)](#target-rd-3-frame) (`RD.3/frame`), `mathlib:PadicInt`.

**Sources.**

- [S62](#source-62), (2.2.15)(ii)(b), p. 67; (2.3.8)(iii), p. 76. Introduces the overconvergent module with ∇(1) = a t^{−1} dt on G_m ⊂ P^1 for a ∈ ℤ_p and proves that it carries a Frobenius structure iff a = m/(p − 1), m ∈ ℤ, given by multiplication by t^m.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- Berthelot 96-03, (2.2.15)(ii)(b) and (2.3.8)(iii): basic examples of overconvergent isocrystals and of Kummer F-isocrystals, direct factors of the cohomology of Kummer coverings
- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/liouville-extension-counterexample: K_λ with λ a p-adic Liouville-type exponent is the sub-object of the counterexample to full faithfulness without Frobenius
- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/etale-descent-of-overconvergent-f-isocrystals: Kummer F-isocrystals arise by descent along the Kummer cover t = s^{p−1}
- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2: constant ∇-modules with exponent a over the Robba ring are the local models at 0 and ∞

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Kummer.isoc` |  | For a ∈ ℤ_p, the rank-one overconvergent isocrystal K_a on G_m with ∇(e) = a e dt/t. |
| `Kummer.tensor` |  | K_a ⊗ K_b ≅ K_{a+b}, K_0 ≅ unit, K_a^∨ ≅ K_{−a}. |
| `Kummer.iso_iff` |  | K_a ≅ K_b iff a − b ∈ ℤ. |
| `Kummer.horizontalSections` |  | Γ(K_a)^{∇=0} is one-dimensional (spanned by t^{−a} e) if a ∈ ℤ and zero otherwise, over the tube and over strict neighbourhoods. |
| `Kummer.pullback_pow` |  | The pullback along t ↦ t^N is K_{Na}. |
| `Kummer.frobenius_iff` |  | With the Frobenius lift t ↦ t^p and σ = id, K_a has a Frobenius structure iff (p − 1)a ∈ ℤ, namely multiplication by t^{(p−1)a}. |

**Unit tests.**

- `Kummer.zero_eq_unit` (degenerate): K_0 is the unit object (j†O, d).
- `Kummer.one_iso_unit` (computation): K_1 ≅ K_0 via e ↦ t e, so isomorphism classes depend on a modulo ℤ.
- `Kummer.half_frobenius` (computation): For p odd, K_{1/2} has the Frobenius structure given by multiplication by t^{(p−1)/2}.
- `Kummer.no_sections_nonintegral` (characterisation): For a ∈ ℤ_p ∖ ℤ, K_a has no non-zero horizontal section even on the tube {|t| = 1}.
- `Kummer.not_convergent_outside_Zp` (non-example): For a = 1/p the formula ∇(e) = a e dt/t defines a module with connection on the annulus that is not convergent: |binom(1/p, k)| is unbounded.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Overconvergence: by taylor-series-convergence-criterion on the two affine charts (overconvergence is local on P, overconvergence-is-a-property (d)), ∂^{[k]} e = binom(a, k) t^{−k} e with |binom(a, k)| ≤ 1, so on {η ≤ |t| ≤ 1/η} the decay ‖∂^{[k]}e‖ λ^k ≤ (λ/η)^k → 0 holds for η > λ; the chart at ∞ is the same with −a.
2. Tensor, dual and pullback are computed on generators; an isomorphism K_b → K_a sends e_b to g e_a with t g′ = (b − a) g, so g = c t^{b−a}, a unit of K⟨t, t^{−1}⟩† exactly when a − b ∈ ℤ; horizontal sections are the case b = 0, where the Laurent coefficients satisfy (n + a) g_n = 0.
3. Frobenius: a horizontal Φ: F^*K_a → K_a, F^*K_a having ∇(1) = pa dt/t, is multiplication by some h with t h′ = a(p − 1) h, so h = c t^{a(p−1)}, analytic and invertible on annuli near |t| = 1 iff a(p − 1) ∈ ℤ (Berthelot 96-03 (2.3.8)(iii)).

**Checks.**

- K_0 is the unit; K_1 ≅ K_0 through e ↦ t e.
- For p odd, K_{1/2} carries the Frobenius structure t^{(p−1)/2} (Kummer F-isocrystal of the double cover).

<a id="target-rd-3-liouville-exponent-sequence"></a>

### A p-adic Liouville-type exponent: p^n/(n + λ) tends to 0 but not geometrically

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/liouville-exponent-sequence` · lemma

There is λ ∈ ℤ_p ∖ ℤ such that the sequence f_n = p^n/(n + λ), n ≥ 1, satisfies |f_n| → 0 while for no ρ > 1 does |f_n| ρ^n → 0 (equivalently limsup |f_n|^{1/n} = 1). Explicitly one may take λ = −Σ_{k≥1} p^{m_k} with m_1 = 2, N_k = Σ_{j≤k} p^{m_j} and m_{k+1} = N_k − k; this λ is not rational. Consequently the power series Σ_{n≥1} f_n t^n lies in the Tate algebra K⟨t⟩ of the closed unit disc but not in its overconvergent subring K⟨t⟩† (nor in K⟨t, t^{−1}⟩†).

**Hypotheses.**

- Any p ≥ 2; the choice of m_k only needs v_p(N_k + λ) − N_k → −∞ slowly enough that N_k ↦ v_p(N_k + λ)/N_k tends to 1.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:PadicInt`, `mathlib:Padic`, [A function converging only on the closed unit disc separates completion from overconvergence](#target-rd-0-completion-versus-overconvergence) (`RD.0/completion-versus-overconvergence`).

**Sources.**

- [S3](#source-3), Remark 5.6, p. 13. States that without Frobenius structures the restriction functor from overconvergent to convergent isocrystals is not fully faithful, the failure being related to p-adic Liouville numbers (p-adic integers overly well approximated by ordinary integers), citing Abe (IMRN 2011) for a counterexample.
- [S62](#source-62), (2.1.2.2), p. 49. Characterises elements of the weak completion (hence of K⟨t⟩†) by coefficients bounded by c r^{|k|} with r < 1, which is the overconvergence condition violated here.

**Construction or proof.**

1. The m_k increase strictly (m_2 = p² − 1 ≥ 3 and m_{k+1} ≥ p^{m_k} − k), and −λ has infinitely many non-zero and infinitely many zero p-adic digits, so λ ∉ ℤ and n + λ ≠ 0 for all n; since the gaps m_{k+1} − m_k tend to infinity, the digit expansion of −λ is not eventually periodic, so λ ∉ ℚ.
2. For n = N_k: N_k + λ = −Σ_{j>k} p^{m_j} has valuation m_{k+1} = N_k − k, so |f_{N_k}| = p^{−k} → 0 but |f_{N_k}| ρ^{N_k} = p^{−k} ρ^{N_k} → ∞ for every ρ > 1.
3. For N_k < n < N_{k+1} (with N_0 = 0): n + λ = (n − N_k) + (N_k + λ) with 0 < n − N_k < p^{m_{k+1}} ≤ p^{v_p(N_k+λ)}, so v_p(n + λ) = v_p(n − N_k) ≤ log_p n and |f_n| ≤ n p^{−n} → 0. This construction is supplied here; it realises the p-adic Liouville phenomenon referred to by Kedlaya (Notes, Remark 5.6).

**Checks.**

- For p = 2: m_1 = 2, N_1 = 4, m_2 = 3, N_2 = 12, m_3 = 10: |f_4| = 2^{−1}, |f_{12}| = 2^{−2}, while 4 + λ ≡ 0 mod 2^3 and 12 + λ ≡ 0 mod 2^{10}.
- Contrast: for λ = −1/2 (p odd), v_p(n − 1/2) = v_p(2n − 1) ≤ log_p(2n), so |f_n| ≤ 2n p^{−n} and Σ f_n t^n converges for |t| < p: it is overconvergent. The numbers n − 1/2 are not all units (p divides 2n − 1 for n = (p + 1)/2); what matters is that v_p(n + λ) grows only logarithmically. In general Σ f_n t^n is overconvergent if and only if limsup_n v_p(n + λ)/n < 1, and no λ ∈ ℤ_p ∖ ℤ has |n + λ| bounded below, because ℕ is dense in ℤ_p.
- Contrast: for λ ∈ ℤ the sequence is undefined at n = −λ, which is why λ ∉ ℤ is required.

<a id="target-rd-3-liouville-extension-counterexample"></a>

### Acceptance: without Frobenius, restriction from overconvergent to convergent isocrystals is not full

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/liouville-extension-counterexample` · application

Let λ ∈ ℤ_p ∖ ℤ be as in liouville-exponent-sequence and h = Σ_{n≥1} p^n t^n ∈ K⟨t⟩†. On (G_m, P^1_k, P̂^1_O) let M be the free j†O-module on e_1, e_2 with ∇e_2 = λ e_2 ⊗ dt/t and ∇e_1 = h e_2 ⊗ dt/t, an extension 0 → K_λ → M → O → 0 of the unit object by the Kummer isocrystal K_λ. Then M is an overconvergent isocrystal on G_m, Hom_{Isoc†(G_m/K)}(O, M) = 0, and Hom_{Isoc(G_m/K)}(O, M) = K·(e_1 + f e_2) with f = −Σ_{n≥1} p^n t^n/(n + λ). Hence the restriction functor Isoc†(G_m/K) → Isoc(G_m/K), which is faithful, is not full, and the extension M splits in Isoc(G_m/K) but not in Isoc†(G_m/K). No Frobenius structure exists on M (Kedlaya's full faithfulness theorem with Frobenius would forbid this behaviour).

**Hypotheses.**

- The exponent λ must be a p-adic integer, so that M is overconvergent, and not an integer, so that the homogeneous equation has no solution; its Liouville property makes the particular solution f convergent but not overconvergent.

**Prerequisites.** [A p-adic Liouville-type exponent: p^n/(n + λ) tends to 0 but not geometrically](#target-rd-3-liouville-exponent-sequence) (`RD.3/liouville-exponent-sequence`), [Kummer isocrystals K_a on G_m](#target-rd-3-kummer-isocrystal) (`RD.3/kummer-isocrystal`), [The coordinate criterion for convergence and overconvergence of a connection](#target-rd-3-taylor-series-convergence-criterion) (`RD.3/taylor-series-convergence-criterion`), [Overconvergence of a connection is a property, local on P and on X, stable under subquotients](#target-rd-3-overconvergence-is-a-property) (`RD.3/overconvergence-is-a-property`), [Coherent j†O-modules are germs of coherent modules on strict neighbourhoods](#target-rd-3-coherent-j-dagger-modules) (`RD.3/coherent-j-dagger-modules`), [Convergent isocrystals Isoc(X/K)](#target-rd-3-convergent-isocrystal) (`RD.3/convergent-isocrystal`), [Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-isocrystal) (`RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal`), [Restriction from overconvergent to convergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-3-restriction-to-convergent) (`RD.3/restriction-to-convergent`).

**Sources.**

- [S3](#source-3), Remark 5.6, p. 13. Asserts that, without Frobenius structures, full faithfulness of restriction from overconvergent to convergent isocrystals fails, in connection with p-adic Liouville numbers (citing Abe); the explicit extension here is an instance.
- [S62](#source-62), (2.3.9)(i)–(ii), p. 77. Records that the restriction functor Isoc†(X/S) → Isoc(X/S) is faithful, reduces fullness to extending horizontal sections from the tube to a strict neighbourhood, and states that the general case was open (with the rank-one curve case known by Dwork–Robba and Crew).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Overconvergence of M: on the chart at 0, ∂^{[k]}e_2 = binom(λ, k) t^{−k} e_2 and ∂^{[k]}e_1 = a_k e_2 with a_k = (1/k) Σ_{n≥1} p^n binom(n + λ − 1, k − 1) t^{n−k}, whose sup norm on {η ≤ |t| ≤ 1} is ≤ k η^{−k} because binom(n + λ − 1, k − 1) ∈ ℤ_p; so ‖∂^{[k]}e‖ λ_0^k → 0 for η > λ_0 and taylor-series-convergence-criterion applies; the chart at ∞ (s = 1/t, where h(1/s) = Σ p^n s^{−n} is bounded by 1 on |s| ≥ 1/p) is the same, and overconvergence is local on P (overconvergence-is-a-property (d)). The connection is defined on the strict neighbourhood {1/p < |t| < p}.
2. Horizontal sections: s = c e_1 + g e_2 is horizontal iff c is constant and t g′ + λ g = −c h, i.e. (n + λ) g_n = −c h_n for all n ∈ ℤ; as λ ∉ ℤ this forces g = c f.
3. Over the tube {|t| = 1} sections are Laurent series with coefficients tending to 0, and f qualifies (liouville-exponent-sequence), so Hom_{Isoc}(O, M) = K(e_1 + f e_2); over strict neighbourhoods sections are overconvergent Laurent series and f does not qualify, so c = 0 and Hom_{Isoc†}(O, M) = 0. Faithfulness of restriction is coherent-j-dagger-modules (c).
4. A Frobenius structure on M would induce one on the sub-object K_λ, which needs (p − 1)λ ∈ ℤ (kummer-isocrystal), impossible since λ ∉ ℚ (liouville-exponent-sequence); the counterexample is constructed here, Abe's published counterexample (IMRN 2011) not being publicly accessible.

**Checks.**

- The map Hom_{Isoc†}(O, M) = 0 → Hom_{Isoc}(O, M) = K is injective (faithfulness) but not surjective.
- Replacing λ by an exponent with v_p(n + λ) = O(log n) (for instance λ = −1/2 with p odd, or any λ ∈ (ℚ ∩ ℤ_p) ∖ ℤ) makes f overconvergent and the two Hom-spaces agree; here limsup_n v_p(n + λ)/n = 1, so the failure is a Liouville phenomenon. No λ ∈ ℤ_p ∖ ℤ keeps |n + λ| bounded below, so the relevant condition is the growth of v_p(n + λ), not a lower bound.
- In the convergent category M ≅ O ⊕ K_λ, while in the overconvergent category the extension class of M is non-zero.

<a id="rd4"></a>

## RD.4 — Rigid cohomology, support and comparison constructions

Construct ordinary, compact-support and closed-support cohomology before any finiteness assertion. State no-F ordinary coefficient comparisons with Taylor convergence; Frobenius compatibility is extra structure. Develop relative Poincaré and de Rham descent, Gysin, fixed-model dagger and log proper-support comparisons. The constant rigid–crystalline map and quasi-isomorphism lie here and are available to RD.5 trace compatibility; their stable IDs retain the RD.7 prefix. The coefficient theorem with linear q-Frobenius is in RD.7.

**Landmarks.** Rigid cohomology, Rigid cohomology with compact supports, Frobenius on rigid cohomology, Rigid Gysin isomorphism, Log rigid cohomology with proper support, Dagger–rigid cohomology comparison.

### Worked checks

The trivial coefficient on A¹ has ordinary cohomology K in degree zero. Compact support gives K(−1) in degree two. With the closed point Z={0}, the ordinary support triangle and H¹(G_m)=K(−1) give H²_Z(A¹)=K(−1), while H⁰_Z(A¹)=0. This separates the three support conventions and fixes the Gysin twist sign. For q-Frobenius x↦x^q, the form dx/x pulls back to q·dx/x; this verifies Frobenius on H¹(G_m) and the codimension-one purity class.

For a smooth proper special fibre X and open U=A¹ inside X=P¹, the log proper-support group agrees with H_c,rig(A¹): its nonzero class is in degree two. Its map to H²(P¹) is an isomorphism. When U=X, every support kernel is the identity; when U is empty it is zero. For the standard log point the relative log complex has only K₀ in degree zero, while the absolute complex retains dlog t. These are tests of the complexes, including their grading, rather than assumptions on the spectral sequence.

In the log spectral sequence the intersection order is h=2j+k+1. For a single smooth component h>1 terms vanish, so only k=j=0 remains. For two components meeting transversely, the order-two term uses their intersection once. Projection to the positive complex retains j=0 and gives h=k+1; negative k disappears. The high-degree comparison at k=0,q=2d−1 retains only j≥1. Its j=0 exception prevents an unjustified claim about all degree-2d−1 cohomology.

The abstract theta presentation uses the existing quotient W/im θ. A zero operator leaves W unchanged and a surjective operator makes the quotient zero. Every θ(v) has zero class. These checks determine the quotient interface; identifying the actual modular differential with the Igusa coefficient de Rham differential is the additional geometric theorem G3. A direct limit of finite-dimensional finite-level quotients need not be finite-dimensional.


<a id="target-rd-4-monsky-washnitzer-cohomology"></a>

### Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology of a (σ,∇)-module

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4/monsky-washnitzer-cohomology` · definition

For a (σ,∇)-module M over a dagger algebra A of MW-type, the Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology H^i(M) is the i-th cohomology of the de Rham complex 0 → M → M ⊗ Ω^1_{A/K} → M ⊗ Ω^2_{A/K} → ⋯ with differentials ∇_i. The Frobenius F ⊗ ∧^i dσ on M ⊗ Ω^i commutes with the differentials and induces a σ_K-semilinear endomorphism F of each H^i(M) (K-linear when σ_K = id). H^0(M) = ker ∇ is the space of horizontal sections. When the special fibre of A has dimension one, Ω^2_{A/K} = 0 and H^0(M) = ker ∇, H^1(M) = coker(∇: M → M ⊗ Ω^1), H^i(M) = 0 for i ≥ 2. For M = A this is the cohomology H^i(A; K) of Monsky–Washnitzer and van der Put.

**Hypotheses.**

- The output is a K-vector space with a semilinear endomorphism; no finite-dimensionality is built into the definition (it is RD.5/finiteness-for-affine-curves-constant-coefficients, RD.5/finiteness-for-affine-curves and RD.5/finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology).

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/MonskyWashnitzer`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [(σ,∇)-modules over a dagger algebra of Monsky–Washnitzer type](#target-rd-3-sigma-nabla-module-over-dagger-algebra) (`RD.3/sigma-nabla-module-over-dagger-algebra`), `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-algebra`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/fringe-presentation`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/fringe-topology`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-differentials`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-tensor-product`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-rational-localisation`, `mathlib:HomologicalComplex.homology`, `mathlib:CochainComplex`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-de-rham-complex`.

**Sources.**

- [S4](#source-4), Definition 3.4.1, p. 23. The de Rham complex of a (σ,∇)-module.
- [S7](#source-7), Section 2.3, p. 36. Constant coefficients: van der Put's definition.
- [S6](#source-6), Section 2, p. 3. The same definition, used for point counting.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- Kedlaya, Finiteness, Remark 4.3.3: H^i_rig(X/K, E) is computed as H^i(M) on smooth affine X
- Kedlaya, Counting points (math/0105031), Sections 2–4: the Frobenius matrix on H^1(A; K) of an affine hyperelliptic curve computes its zeta function
- ColemanIntegration:L1/frobenius-h1-datum: H^1_dR+(Y) = Ω+(Y)/dA+(Y) with its Frobenius is this cohomology for the constant module
- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.6: the trace formula on smooth affine varieties is proved on this complex (Kedlaya, Weil II, Chapter 5)

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SigmaNablaModule.mwH0` |  | H^0(M) = ker ∇ as a K-vector space (in general H^i(M) for i ∈ ℕ). |
| `SigmaNablaModule.mwH1` |  | H^1(M) = coker(∇: M → M ⊗ Ω^1) for curves (in general the i-th cohomology of the de Rham complex). |
| `SigmaNablaModule.mwH1Frobenius` |  | The σ_K-semilinear endomorphism of H^i(M) induced by F ⊗ ∧^i dσ (on H^1 of a curve: m ⊗ ω ↦ F(m) ⊗ μω). |
| `mwCohomology.map` |  | Morphisms of (σ,∇)-modules and pullbacks along Frobenius-compatible morphisms of dagger algebras induce maps on H^i; map_id and map_comp hold and the maps commute with F. |
| `SigmaNablaModule.mwCohomology_zero` |  | H^0(M) = ker ∇, the horizontal sections. |
| `mwCohomology_of_dim_one` |  | If the special fibre of A has dimension one then H^1(M) = coker(∇: M → M ⊗ Ω^1) and H^i(M) = 0 for i ≥ 2. |
| `mwCohomology.frobenius_injective` |  | F is injective on each H^i(M) (Kedlaya, Remark 3.4.4; RD.4/finite-flat-pullback-injective). |
| `mwCohomology_trivial_zero` |  | If Spec(A^int/πA^int) is geometrically connected then H^0(A) = K with F = σ_K (Kedlaya, proof of Lemma 9.3.2, citing Monsky–Washnitzer, Theorem 7.1). |

**Unit tests.**

- `mwH1_multiplicativeGroup` (computation): For A = K⟨x,x^{-1}⟩† and M = A: the residue map Σ a_n x^n dx/x ↦ a_0 induces an isomorphism H^1(M) ≅ K, and the standard Frobenius σ(x) = x^q acts on H^1(M) by multiplication by q.
- `mwH_affineLine` (computation): For A = K⟨x⟩† and M = A: H^0(M) = K (the constants) and H^1(M) = 0.
- `mwH_point` (degenerate): For A = K (special fibre a point): H^0(M) = M and H^i(M) = 0 for i ≥ 1.
- `mwH1_tateAlgebra_nonexample` (non-example): With the Tate algebra K⟨x⟩ in place of K⟨x⟩† the cokernel of d is infinite dimensional: Σ_n p^n x^{p^n − 1} dx is a limit of exact forms but not exact; so the overconvergence in the definition cannot be dropped.

**Construction or proof.**

1. The de Rham complex is a cochain complex of K-vector spaces because ∇_{i+1} ∘ ∇_i = 0 (integrability); its cohomology is Mathlib's HomologicalComplex.homology of this complex.
2. The Frobenius of M and ∧^i dσ give a morphism of complexes σ^*(M ⊗ Ω^•) → M ⊗ Ω^• by horizontality of F, hence the semilinear F on H^i(M).
3. In dimension one the complex has two terms, so H^0 and H^1 are the kernel and cokernel of ∇.

**Checks.**

- For A = K⟨x,x^{-1}⟩† and M = A, H^1(M) is one-dimensional, spanned by dx/x, and the standard Frobenius x ↦ x^q acts by q.
- For A = K⟨x⟩† and M = A, H^0(M) = K and H^1(M) = 0.

<a id="target-rd-4-de-rham-trace"></a>

### The trace map on de Rham complexes for a finite flat morphism of dagger algebras

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4/de-rham-trace` · construction

Let f: R → S be an injective morphism of dagger algebras of MW-type with S finite and locally free of constant degree n over R. There is an R-linear morphism of complexes Tr: Ω^•_{S/K} → Ω^•_{R/K} with Tr ∘ f = n·id and Tr(ω ∧ η) = ω ∧ Tr(η) for ω ∈ Ω^•_{R/K}, η ∈ Ω^•_{S/K}; in degree 0 it is the algebra trace S → R.

**Hypotheses.**

- R and S are dagger algebras of MW-type (Monsky–Washnitzer's proof uses that dagger algebras are noetherian; Kedlaya, Remark 3.2.7).
- S is finite and locally free over R of constant rank n.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/MonskyWashnitzer`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-algebra`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/fringe-presentation`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/fringe-topology`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-differentials`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-tensor-product`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-rational-localisation`, `mathlib:Algebra.trace`.

**Sources.**

- [S4](#source-4), Proposition 3.2.6, p. 21. The statement.
- [S7](#source-7), Proposition 3.1, p. 38. Van der Put's construction and proof.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- Kedlaya, Finiteness, Proposition 3.4.3: splits H^i(M) off H^i(f^*M), giving the reductions to finite extensions
- Van der Put, (3.2): the operator ψ = Tr ∘ φ_* with ψ ∘ F = q^n used in the Lefschetz formula
- Kedlaya, Finiteness, Section 8.4: morphisms admitting a trace are strict with closed image

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `deRhamTrace` |  | The R-linear morphism of complexes Tr: Ω^•_{S/K} → Ω^•_{R/K}. |
| `deRhamTrace_comp_map` |  | Tr ∘ f = n·id on Ω^•_{R/K}. |
| `deRhamTrace_wedge` |  | Tr(ω ∧ η) = ω ∧ Tr(η) (projection formula). |
| `deRhamTrace_zero` |  | In degree 0, Tr is Mathlib's Algebra.trace R S. |
| `deRhamTrace_frobenius` |  | For an étale morphism of the smooth reductions, compatible lifts give a cartesian relative Frobenius square, and trace commutes with Frobenius through finite-projective base change. Compatibility alone for a finite flat map does not suffice. |

**Unit tests.**

- `deRhamTrace_degree_one` (degenerate): For f = id, Tr is the identity.
- `deRhamTrace_frobenius_power` (computation): For S = K⟨x,x^{-1}⟩† over R = K⟨y,y^{-1}⟩† (y = x^q): Tr(1) = q, Tr(dx/x) = dy/y, and Tr(x^m dx/x) = 0 if q ∤ m.
- `deRhamTrace_algebraTrace` (compatibility): In degree 0 the map agrees with Mathlib's Algebra.trace for the finite free extension.
- `deRhamTrace_not_retraction` (non-example): Tr ∘ f is multiplication by n, not the identity, when n > 1; dividing by n is what makes H^i(M) a direct summand of H^i(f^*M).
- `deRhamTrace_frobenius_compatibility_nonexample` (non-example): For y = x^q, σ_R(y) = y^q and σ_S(x) = x^q, Tr(σ_S(x)) = qy but σ_R(Tr(x)) = 0 for q > 1. The generic-fibre map is finite étale on G_m, but its reduction is radicial, so compatibility alone does not make trace commute with Frobenius.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Over the fraction fields, Ω^1_{S/K} ⊗ Frac(S) = Ω^1_{R/K} ⊗ Frac(S) because Frac(S)/Frac(R) is finite separable (characteristic 0); define Tr on Ω^i ⊗ Frac(S) as the field trace Frac(S) → Frac(R) tensored with Ω^i_{R/K} (van der Put, Proposition 3.1).
2. Show Tr maps Ω^i_{S/K} into Ω^i_{R/K}: since Ω^i_{R/K} is projective and R normal, it suffices to check at height-one primes, where it follows from the discriminant description of differentials (van der Put, proof of Proposition 3.1, citing R. Berger).
3. Tr commutes with d because the field trace commutes with the derivation of the separable extension; Tr ∘ f = n and the projection formula hold by construction.

**Checks.**

- For S = K⟨x,x^{-1}⟩† over R = K⟨y,y^{-1}⟩† with y = x^q: Tr(dx/x) = dy/y and Tr(1) = q.
- On the affine disc with y = x^q, Tr(dx) = 0 for q > 1 and Tr(x^{q−1}dx) = dy; dx/x is not a regular form there.

<a id="target-rd-4-finite-flat-pullback-injective"></a>

### Cohomology injects under finite flat pullback, and Frobenius is injective on cohomology

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4/finite-flat-pullback-injective` · lemma

Let f: R → S be an injective morphism of dagger algebras of MW-type with S finite projective over R, and σ a Frobenius lift on S preserving R. For every (σ,∇)-module M over R, the map H^i(M) → H^i(f^*M) is injective and its image is the image of the canonical projector (1/n)·f ∘ Tr on H^i(f^*M), n = deg(S/R). In particular (applying trace to the relative Frobenius linearisation A ⊗_{K,σ_K} K → A, which is finite flat over the smooth reduction) the Frobenius F is injective on each H^i(M).

**Hypotheses.**

- R, S of MW-type (or one of the two Robba-ring situations of Kedlaya, Remark 3.2.7).
- Characteristic 0, so n is invertible in K.

**Prerequisites.** [The trace map on de Rham complexes for a finite flat morphism of dagger algebras](#target-rd-4-de-rham-trace) (`RD.4/de-rham-trace`), [Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology of a (σ,∇)-module](#target-rd-4-monsky-washnitzer-cohomology) (`RD.4/monsky-washnitzer-cohomology`), [Existence of Frobenius lifts on the weak completion of a smooth O_K-algebra (van der Put; Arabia)](#target-rd-0-frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra) (`RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra`).

**Sources.**

- [S4](#source-4), Proposition 3.4.3, p. 24. The statement.
- [S4](#source-4), Remark 3.4.4, p. 24. Injectivity of Frobenius.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Tensor the trace Tr: Ω^•_S → Ω^•_R (RD.4/de-rham-trace) with M to get H^i(f^*M) → H^i(M) whose composite with H^i(M) → H^i(f^*M) is multiplication by n.
2. Since n ≠ 0 in K, the first map is injective and (1/n) f ∘ Tr is a projector onto its image.
3. Factor Frobenius into coefficient extension along σ_K, which is faithfully flat, followed by the finite-flat relative Frobenius lift of RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra. Trace gives injection for the latter, and the Frobenius structure identifies the pullback module with M. This does not assert that absolute Frobenius is finite over an arbitrary imperfect k.

**Checks.**

- For S = K⟨x⟩† over R = K⟨x^q⟩†, H^1(R) = 0 = H^1(S), and on K⟨x,x^{-1}⟩† the Frobenius q on H^1 is injective.

<a id="target-rd-4-finite-etale-pushforward-de-rham"></a>

### Finite étale pushforward preserves Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4/finite-etale-pushforward-de-rham` · lemma

Let f: R → S be a finite étale morphism of dagger algebras and M a (σ,∇)-module over S. Then H^i(M) ≅ H^i(f_*M) canonically for all i, where f_*M is M viewed as an R-module. Retain both ordinary and compact-support finite étale coefficient pushforward comparisons, with the inherited hypotheses. The underlying finite étale coefficient maps are also required for E∈Isoc† without Frobenius; their support-preserving global identification remains G1.

**Hypotheses.**

- f is finite étale.

**Prerequisites.** [Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology of a (σ,∇)-module](#target-rd-4-monsky-washnitzer-cohomology) (`RD.4/monsky-washnitzer-cohomology`), `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-algebra`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/fringe-presentation`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/fringe-topology`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-differentials`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-tensor-product`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-rational-localisation`.

**Sources.**

- [S4](#source-4), Proposition 3.4.5, p. 24. The statement and proof.
- [S36](#source-36), §§7.3–7.4, pp. 148–152, and Theorem 9.1.1, p. 168. Supplies coherent étale descent and its passage to de Rham descent; this is not claimed to replace the unread compact-support pushforward proof.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Because f is étale, S ⊗_R Ω^i_{R/K} ≅ Ω^i_{S/K}; tensoring with M gives an equality of de Rham complexes M ⊗_S Ω^•_{S/K} = M ⊗_R Ω^•_{R/K}.
2. The Frobenius structures agree, so the identification is F-equivariant.
3. Étale base change of differential modules uses Mathlib’s tensorKaehlerEquivOfFormallyEtale and TauCeti’s basis transport; finite pushforward is coherent and exact on the analytic radius pieces. Global support and proper-compactification compatibility still require the general proof recorded in G1; the algebraic differential identity alone does not discharge it.

**Checks.**

- Pushing the trivial module forward along x ↦ x^N on K⟨x,x^{-1}⟩† (N prime to p, étale on G_m) gives a rank-N module with H^1 one-dimensional.

<a id="target-rd-4-overconvergent-de-rham-complex"></a>

### Berthelot's functor j† and the overconvergent de Rham complex of a frame

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4/overconvergent-de-rham-complex` · construction

Use the functor j† of RD.3/j-dagger and its strict-neighbourhood implementation of RD.3/j-dagger-properties. For E ∈ Isoc†(X,Y/K) realised by E_V with integrable connection on a strict neighbourhood V of ]X[_P, define DR†(E) = j†(E_V ⊗ Ω^•_V). Its hypercohomology on ]Y[_P is the frame cohomology H^i((X,Y,P)/K,E). For a morphism of frames u, pullback of coefficients and differential forms gives a canonical derived morphism DR†_P(E) → Ru_*DR†_{P′}(u^*E), compatible with composition.

**Hypotheses.**

- Strict neighbourhoods in Berthelot's sense (RD.3/strict-neighbourhood); the colimit may be taken over any cofinal system, for instance the U'_λ = {x ∈ ]Y[ : some |f_i(x)| ≥ λ}, f_i lifting equations of Z, λ → 1^-.
- The frame need not have Y proper for DR†(E) and frame cohomology; properness of Y is imposed in RD.4/rigid-cohomology.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/OverconvergentDeRham`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Frames (X ⊂ Y ⊂ P)](#target-rd-3-frame) (`RD.3/frame`), [The tube ]T[_P of a locally closed subscheme](#target-rd-3-tube) (`RD.3/tube`), [Strict neighbourhoods of ]X[ in ]Y[](#target-rd-3-strict-neighbourhood) (`RD.3/strict-neighbourhood`), [Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-isocrystal) (`RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal`), `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-algebra`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/fringe-presentation`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/fringe-topology`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-differentials`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-tensor-product`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-rational-localisation`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/raynaud-generic-fibre`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/generic-fibre-fibre-products`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/tube`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Sheaf`, `mathlib:DerivedCategory`, [Berthelot's functor j† of overconvergent sections](#target-rd-3-j-dagger) (`RD.3/j-dagger`), [Exactness of j† on coherent sheaves and the acyclicity of j_{λ*}](#target-rd-3-j-dagger-properties) (`RD.3/j-dagger-properties`).

**Sources.**

- [S20](#source-20), (2.2), p. 17. Definition of j†.
- [S20](#source-20), (2.5) a), p. 19. Dependence on a strict neighbourhood only.
- [S4](#source-4), Definition 4.3.1, p. 27. The same construction with coefficients.
- [S5](#source-5), Section 2.2, p. 12. Global sections of j†O on the affine line.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- Berthelot, (2.3) and (4.2.4): rigid cohomology is the hypercohomology of this complex
- Kedlaya, Finiteness, Definition 4.3.1: definition of H^i_rig(X/K, E)
- AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:AG2.4: the overconvergent logarithmic de Rham complex with compact-support boundary ideal on ordinary loci is a variant of this complex
- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7: for X proper this is the convergent de Rham complex compared with crystalline cohomology

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cohomology_jDagger` |  | H^*(]Y[, j†F) = H^*(V, j†F) for any strict neighbourhood V (Berthelot (2.5) a)). |
| `overconvergentDeRham` |  | The complex DR†(E) = j†(E_V ⊗ Ω^•_V) of sheaves of K-vector spaces on ]Y[_P. |
| `frameCohomology` |  | H^i((X,Y,P)/K, E) := H^i(]Y[_P, DR†(E)), the hypercohomology. |
| `overconvergentDeRham.map` |  | For a morphism of frames u, the canonical morphism DR†_P(E) → Ru_*DR†_{P'}(u^*E) of (2.2.1); compatible with composition of frame morphisms. |
| `overconvergentDeRham_affine` |  | If Y is the closure of a smooth affine X with a smooth lift, the global sections of DR†(E) form the de Rham complex M_E ⊗ Ω^•_A of the dagger algebra (RD.3/affine-smooth-description-of-overconvergent-f-isocrystals). |

**Unit tests.**

- `jDagger_of_proper` (degenerate): If X = Y then j†F = F for every sheaf F, and DR†(E) = E ⊗ Ω^•_{]X[_P}.
- `jDagger_affineLine_sections` (computation): For the frame (A^1_k, P^1_k, P̂^1_{O_K}): Γ(]P^1[, j†O) is the ring K⟨x⟩† of power series converging on some disc |x| ≤ ρ with ρ > 1.
- `jDagger_restrict_tube` (compatibility): For every sheaf F on ]Y[_P, (j†F)|]X[_P = F|]X[_P, and the natural map F → j†F is the unit of the restriction to strict neighbourhoods.
- `convergent_deRham_affineLine_nonexample` (non-example): Without j†, the de Rham complex of the closed unit disc ]A^1[ = Sp K⟨x⟩ has infinite-dimensional H^1 (Berthelot (1.5), Remarque), so DR† cannot be replaced by the de Rham complex of the tube.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Define j†F as the colimit of j_{V*}j_V^{-1}F; since the strict neighbourhoods form a filtered system, j† is an exact functor on sheaves of abelian groups (Chiarellotto–Tsuzuki, Proposition 2.7.2).
2. j†F depends only on the restriction of F to any strict neighbourhood V, and H^*(]Y[, j†F) = H^*(V, j†F) (Berthelot (2.5) a)).
3. For E realised on V with connection ∇ (RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal), E_V ⊗ Ω^•_V is a complex of sheaves on V (differential forms on the rigid space V, supplied by AdicSpacesPartII:F1); apply j†.
4. For a morphism of frames u, the canonical maps j†F → u_*j'†u^{-1}F composed with u^{-1}Ω^•_{]Y[_P} → Ω^•_{]Y'[_{P'}} and an injective resolution give (2.2.1).

**Checks.**

- If X = Y (Z empty) then j† = id and DR†(E) = E ⊗ Ω^•_{]X[_P}.
- For X = A^1_k ⊂ Y = P^1_k ⊂ P = P̂^1: Γ(]Y[, j†O) = K⟨x⟩†, series converging on some disc |x| ≤ ρ with ρ > 1.

<a id="target-rd-4-relative-overconvergent-poincare"></a>

### Relative overconvergent Poincaré lemma

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4/relative-overconvergent-poincare` · theorem

For a separated morphism u of frames inducing an isomorphism on the open scheme, proper on the compactification, and smooth on the formal ambient space near the open scheme, a coherent j†-module E on the target satisfies E ≃ Ru_* DR†_relative(u†E). The relative differential is the canonical one on the pullback; E need not carry an absolute connection for this assertion.

**Hypotheses.**

- Complete mixed-characteristic DVR V, fraction field K; finite-type separated frames; smoothness is required only near the open scheme.
- Use strict neighbourhoods and coherent modules; the completed closed unit disc is not a substitute for the open-disc system.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti.RigidCohomology.RD4`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Declaration.** `relativeOverconvergentPoincare`

**Prerequisites.** [Frames (X ⊂ Y ⊂ P)](#target-rd-3-frame) (`RD.3/frame`), [Berthelot's functor j† of overconvergent sections](#target-rd-3-j-dagger) (`RD.3/j-dagger`), [Strong fibration theorem: strict neighbourhoods along smooth morphisms](#target-rd-3-strong-fibration-theorem) (`RD.3/strong-fibration-theorem`), `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/open-polydisc-coherent-acyclicity`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4`.

**Sources.**

- [S36](#source-36), Proposition 8.3.5 and Proposition 8.3.4, pp. 156–162; Lemmas 2.6.3–2.6.8, pp. 76–79. The relative de Rham augmentation is an equivalence under these frame hypotheses; radius refinement is part of the proof.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Use strong fibration to obtain étale local coordinates and a cofinal system of products with discs, retaining the compactification hypotheses.
2. On one variable, primitive coefficients a_l/(l+1) converge after shrinking the disc radius: for 0<r<1, |1/(l+1)| r^l tends to zero. The differential has constants as kernel. Iterate in the relative coordinates.
3. Coherent acyclicity on the radius pieces and the cofinality lemmas identify derived direct images with these calculations. Totalize the finite Čech diagram; the augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism.

**Checks.**

- A zero-dimensional relative coordinate gives the identity.
- Integration is checked on every radius piece; no bounded inverse to differentiation on the closed unit disc is asserted.

<a id="target-rd-4-etale-proper-de-rham-descent"></a>

### Étale-proper de Rham descent

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4/etale-proper-de-rham-descent` · theorem

An étale-proper hypercover of frames is universally of cohomological descent for overconvergent de Rham complexes with overconvergent isocrystal coefficients. For its augmentation ε, the target complex is equivalent to Rε_* of the total simplicial de Rham realization, and the associated first-quadrant spectral sequence computes rigid cohomology.

**Hypotheses.**

- Open schemes form an étale hypercover; compactifications form the proper part of the frame hypercover.
- The coefficient objects have compatible descent data; all totalizations use the cohomological grading convention.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti.RigidCohomology.RD4`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Declaration.** `etaleProperDeRhamDescent`

**Prerequisites.** [Relative overconvergent Poincaré lemma](#target-rd-4-relative-overconvergent-poincare) (`RD.4/relative-overconvergent-poincare`), [Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-isocrystal) (`RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal`), `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4`.

**Sources.**

- [S36](#source-36), Theorem 9.1.1 and Corollary 9.1.2, p. 168; §§6.4, 7.3–7.4, pp. 136–139, 148–152; §4.2, pp. 112–115. Coherent descent and the relative Poincaré lemma yield de Rham descent for étale-proper hypercovers.

**Construction or proof.**

1. First obtain coherent descent from smooth-proper covers and the standard étale polynomial covers, using local monic-polynomial presentations and their diagonal factorization.
2. Apply the relative Poincaré equivalence levelwise; filtered relative forms identify the de Rham totalization with the descended coefficient realization.
3. Use injective resolutions of diagrams and the homotopy uniqueness of their comparison maps to make the augmentation and spectral sequence functorial.

**Checks.**

- The constant hypercover yields the identity augmentation.
- Replacing a cover by a common refinement gives the same comparison in the derived category.

<a id="target-rd-4-independence-of-embedding"></a>

### Independence of rigid cohomology from the smooth formal embedding (Berthelot, Théorème 1)

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4/independence-of-embedding` · theorem

Let X ⊂ Y be an open immersion of k-schemes, i: Y → P and i': Y → P' closed immersions into formal O_K-schemes, and u: P' → P a morphism with u ∘ i' = i which is smooth in a neighbourhood of X. Then for every E ∈ Isoc†(X, Y/K) the canonical morphism DR†_P(E) → Ru_*DR†_{P'}(E) of (2.2.1) is an isomorphism; hence H^i((X,Y,P)/K, E) ≅ H^i((X,Y,P')/K, E). Given two embeddings Y → P_1, Y → P_2 smooth near X, applying this to the projections of P_1 × P_2 (diagonal embedding) gives a canonical isomorphism, and these isomorphisms are compatible. Ordinary cohomology is independent of the compactification and smooth frame through the canonical common-refinement comparisons.

**Hypotheses.**

- u smooth in a neighbourhood of X; no hypothesis on u at the points of Z = Y \ X (Berthelot's remark after Théorème 1).

**Prerequisites.** [Berthelot's functor j† and the overconvergent de Rham complex of a frame](#target-rd-4-overconvergent-de-rham-complex) (`RD.4/overconvergent-de-rham-complex`), [Independence of the frame: canonical equivalences between categories of overconvergent isocrystals](#target-rd-3-independence-of-frame) (`RD.3/independence-of-frame`), [Frames (X ⊂ Y ⊂ P)](#target-rd-3-frame) (`RD.3/frame`), `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/quasi-stein-theorems-a-b`, [Relative overconvergent Poincaré lemma](#target-rd-4-relative-overconvergent-poincare) (`RD.4/relative-overconvergent-poincare`), [Étale-proper de Rham descent](#target-rd-4-etale-proper-de-rham-descent) (`RD.4/etale-proper-de-rham-descent`).

**Sources.**

- [S20](#source-20), (2.3) Théorème 1, p. 18. The statement.
- [S20](#source-20), (2.3), p. 18. The boundary study not given in the source.
- [S20](#source-20), (1.4) Proposition 1, p. 14. The relative Poincaré lemma used in the proof.
- [S36](#source-36), Proposition 10.5.3, pp. 187–188; Corollaries 10.5.4–10.5.5, pp. 188–189. Descent and relative Poincaré give the ordinary independence comparisons.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Weak fibration (Berthelot, Lemme 1): if u is smooth near X, then u^{an} makes ]X[_{P'} locally (over an affine cover of P) isomorphic to ]X[_P × D(0,1^-)^d, a fibration in open unit polydiscs; this is the geometric input of RD.3/independence-of-frame.
2. Relative Poincaré lemma (Berthelot, Proposition 1): on an open polydisc fibration, Ω^•_{]X[_P} → Ru'_*Ω^•_{]X[_{P'}} is a quasi-isomorphism and R^q u'_* of the relative forms vanish for q ≥ 1, using global primitives on open discs and Theorem B (AdicSpacesPartII:R3).
3. Strong fibration theorem: the polydisc fibration extends over a cofinal system of strict neighbourhoods of ]X[, giving the statement for DR† (Berthelot’s analysis near the boundary, §2.3, p. 18). The public sources state this step without proof; it is recorded as a gap.
4. Compatibility of the isomorphisms for three embeddings follows from functoriality of (2.2.1) in the triple product.
5. Compare two compactifications via the closure of the diagonal, and two formal embeddings via their product. Apply the relative Poincaré comparison on a common frame. The diagram-resolution homotopy comparison makes the induced equivalence independent of further refinement.

**Checks.**

- For X = A^1 embedded in P̂^1 and in P̂^2 (via the diagonal of P^1 × P^1 composed with a linear embedding), both frame cohomologies are K in degree 0 and 0 otherwise.

<a id="target-rd-4-independence-of-compactification"></a>

### Independence of rigid cohomology from the compactification (Berthelot, Théorème 2)

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4/independence-of-compactification` · theorem

Let j: X → Y and j': X → Y' be open immersions and v: Y' → Y a proper morphism with v ∘ j' = j. Then v^*: H^i((X ⊂ Y)/K, E) → H^i((X ⊂ Y')/K, v^*E) is an isomorphism for all i and all E ∈ Isoc†(X, Y/K) (frame cohomology computed with any embeddings smooth near X, by RD.4/independence-of-embedding). Ordinary cohomology is independent of the compactification and smooth frame through the canonical common-refinement comparisons.

**Hypotheses.**

- v proper; frames exist for Y and Y' (for instance Y, Y' projective), or use the hypercovering construction of Chiarellotto–Tsuzuki, Section 10.

**Prerequisites.** [Independence of rigid cohomology from the smooth formal embedding (Berthelot, Théorème 1)](#target-rd-4-independence-of-embedding) (`RD.4/independence-of-embedding`), [Berthelot's functor j† and the overconvergent de Rham complex of a frame](#target-rd-4-overconvergent-de-rham-complex) (`RD.4/overconvergent-de-rham-complex`), [Frames (X ⊂ Y ⊂ P)](#target-rd-3-frame) (`RD.3/frame`), [Étale-proper de Rham descent](#target-rd-4-etale-proper-de-rham-descent) (`RD.4/etale-proper-de-rham-descent`).

**Sources.**

- [S20](#source-20), (2.4) Théorème 2, p. 18. The statement.
- [S24](#source-24), Corollary 10.5.4, p. 188. The relative form in Chiarellotto–Tsuzuki.
- [S36](#source-36), Proposition 10.5.3, pp. 187–188; Corollaries 10.5.4–10.5.5, pp. 188–189. Descent and relative Poincaré give the ordinary independence comparisons.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Berthelot's sketch: compute v^* with embeddings Y → P, Y' → P' and a morphism u: P' → P; by dévissage and base changes of P inducing admissible covers of a strict neighbourhood, reduce to the case of a section P → P' extending the section X → P' ×_P X given by j'; then replace Y' by the image of Y in P' and apply Théorème 1.
2. Compare two compactifications via the closure of the diagonal, and two formal embeddings via their product. Apply the relative Poincaré comparison on a common frame. The diagram-resolution homotopy comparison makes the induced equivalence independent of further refinement.

**Checks.**

- For X = A^1, the compactifications P^1 and P^1 blown up at a point of the boundary give the same cohomology.

<a id="target-rd-4-rigid-cohomology"></a>

### Rigid cohomology H^i_rig(X/K, E)

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4/rigid-cohomology` · definition

Let X be a separated k-scheme of finite type and E an overconvergent (F-)isocrystal on X/K. Choose a compactification X ⊂ Y (Y proper over k; Nagata) and a closed immersion Y → P into a formal O_K-scheme P smooth in a neighbourhood of X (such a frame exists when X is quasi-projective: take Y the closure of X in P^n_k and P = P̂^n_{O_K}). The rigid cohomology complex is RΓ_rig(X/K, E) := RΓ(]Y[_P, DR†(E)) in the derived category of K-vector spaces and H^i_rig(X/K, E) := H^i(]Y[_P, j†(E ⊗ Ω^•)). By RD.4/independence-of-embedding and RD.4/independence-of-compactification this is independent of (Y, P) up to canonical, compatible isomorphisms. For X admitting no global frame the definition is made with universally de Rham descendable hypercoverings (Chiarellotto–Tsuzuki, Section 10), which agrees with the frame definition whenever a frame exists (their Theorem 10.6.1). Each H^i_rig(X/K, E) is a K-vector space; finite dimensionality is a theorem (RD.5/finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology), not part of the output type.

**Hypotheses.**

- X separated of finite type over k; K complete discretely valued of characteristic 0 with residue field k.
- No finite-dimensional output type: the construction produces K-vector spaces and complexes.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Basic`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Berthelot's functor j† and the overconvergent de Rham complex of a frame](#target-rd-4-overconvergent-de-rham-complex) (`RD.4/overconvergent-de-rham-complex`), [Independence of rigid cohomology from the smooth formal embedding (Berthelot, Théorème 1)](#target-rd-4-independence-of-embedding) (`RD.4/independence-of-embedding`), [Independence of rigid cohomology from the compactification (Berthelot, Théorème 2)](#target-rd-4-independence-of-compactification) (`RD.4/independence-of-compactification`), [Frames (X ⊂ Y ⊂ P)](#target-rd-3-frame) (`RD.3/frame`), [Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-isocrystal) (`RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal`), `AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L2/nagata-factorisation-as-used-in-27-4`, `mathlib:DerivedCategory`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType`.

**Sources.**

- [S4](#source-4), Definition 4.3.1, p. 27. Kedlaya's definition with coefficients.
- [S20](#source-20), (2.4), p. 19. Existence of compactifications.
- [S20](#source-20), (4.2.4), p. 29. Coefficients.
- [S24](#source-24), Section 10.6, p. 189. The hypercovering definition for general X agrees with Berthelot's.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- Kedlaya, Finiteness, Theorem 1.2.1: the object whose finite dimensionality is proved
- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.6 (Kedlaya, Weil II, Section 2.1): Poincaré duality partner of compact-support cohomology in the trace formula and weight arguments
- ColemanIntegration:L1/good-reduction-datum-exists: H^1_rig(Y_k/K) of a smooth affine curve, with its Frobenius
- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7: for smooth proper X, compared with crystalline cohomology to export Weil factors to WeilConjectures:WC.6
- AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:AG2.4: ordinary-locus rigid cohomology of Shimura varieties is computed by the overconvergent (logarithmic) de Rham complex

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rigidCohomology` |  | H^i_rig(X/K, E) as a K-vector space, for X separated of finite type over k and E ∈ Isoc†(X/K). |
| `rigidCohomologyComplex` |  | RΓ_rig(X/K, E) as an object of the derived category of K-vector spaces, with H^i of it equal to rigidCohomology. |
| `rigidCohomology.frameIso` |  | For any frame (X, Y, P) with Y proper and P smooth near X, the canonical isomorphism with frame cohomology H^i((X,Y,P)/K, E). |
| `rigidCohomology_point` |  | For X = Spec k', H^0 is the underlying K-vector space of the fibre and H^i = 0 for i ≠ 0. |
| `rigidCohomology_eq_mw` |  | For X smooth affine with dagger algebra A, the Monsky–Washnitzer comparison (RD.4/monsky-washnitzer-comparison). |
| `rigidCohomology_of_reduced` |  | H^i_rig(X_red/K, E) = H^i_rig(X/K, E): rigid cohomology does not see nilpotents (Kedlaya, Weil II, Section 2.1). |

**Unit tests.**

- `rigidCohomology_point_test` (degenerate): For X = Spec k and E the constant object: H^0_rig(X/K) = K and H^i_rig(X/K) = 0 for i ≥ 1.
- `rigidCohomology_affineLine` (computation): H^0_rig(A^1_k/K) = K and H^1_rig(A^1_k/K) = 0.
- `rigidCohomology_convergent_nonexample` (non-example): The cohomology of the de Rham complex of the closed disc ]A^1_k[ (no overconvergence) has infinite-dimensional H^1, so it is not H^1_rig(A^1_k/K) = 0.
- `rigidCohomology_dwork_vanishes` (computation): For K = ℚ_p(π) with π^{p−1} = −p and Berthelot's Dwork F-isocrystal L_π on A^1_{F_p}: H^i_rig(A^1/K, L_π) = 0 for all i (Berthelot (4.2.4), Exercice).
- `rigidCohomology_point_isocrystal` (compatibility): For K = FractionRing(W(k)), q = p and X = Spec k, H^0_rig(X/K, E) with its Frobenius is a WittVector.Isocrystal in Mathlib's sense, namely the fibre of E.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Choose a frame with Y proper: Nagata compactification (AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L2) and, for quasi-projective X, the projective embedding; form DR†(E) (RD.4/overconvergent-de-rham-complex) and take hypercohomology (Mathlib's derived category of sheaves of K-vector spaces on the G-topology of ]Y[_P).
2. Independence: the category of frames for X with Y proper is connected by products and proper maps; RD.4/independence-of-embedding and RD.4/independence-of-compactification give canonical isomorphisms, and their compatibility for three frames makes the resulting object well defined up to unique isomorphism.
3. General X: Chiarellotto–Tsuzuki construct universally de Rham descendable hypercoverings (Proposition 10.1.4), define rigid cohomology as the derived Čech complex (10.4) independent of choices, and prove agreement with Berthelot's definition (Theorem 10.6.1).

**Checks.**

- H^0_rig(Spec k/K, E) is the underlying K-space of the fibre E, and H^i_rig(Spec k/K, E) = 0 for i > 0.
- H^i_rig(A^n_k/K) = K for i = 0 and 0 otherwise (RD.4/cohomology-of-affine-space).

<a id="target-rd-4-functoriality-of-rigid-cohomology"></a>

### Functoriality of rigid cohomology in the variety and the coefficient

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4/functoriality-of-rigid-cohomology` · construction

For a morphism f: X' → X of separated k-schemes of finite type and E ∈ Isoc†(X/K) there are K-linear maps f^*: H^i_rig(X/K, E) → H^i_rig(X'/K, f^*E) with (id)^* = id and (g ∘ f)^* = f^* ∘ g^* (under f^*g^*E ≅ (gf)^*E), and a morphism h: E_1 → E_2 of overconvergent isocrystals induces h_*: H^i_rig(X/K, E_1) → H^i_rig(X/K, E_2), functorially and compatibly with f^*. Constructed on frames: choose frames (X, Y, P), (X', Y', P') and replace P' by P' × P with Y' the closure of the graph (diagonal embedding method); the morphism of frames gives (2.2.1), and independence makes the result canonical.

**Hypotheses.**

- X, X' separated of finite type over k.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Basic`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Rigid cohomology H^i_rig(X/K, E)](#target-rd-4-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.4/rigid-cohomology`), [Independence of rigid cohomology from the smooth formal embedding (Berthelot, Théorème 1)](#target-rd-4-independence-of-embedding) (`RD.4/independence-of-embedding`), [Independence of rigid cohomology from the compactification (Berthelot, Théorème 2)](#target-rd-4-independence-of-compactification) (`RD.4/independence-of-compactification`).

**Sources.**

- [S20](#source-20), (2.3), p. 18. Functoriality for morphisms of pairs.
- [S20](#source-20), (2.4), p. 19. Functoriality in X.
- [S5](#source-5), Section 2.1, p. 10. The functoriality used in the trace formula.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- Kedlaya, Weil II, Section 2.1: pullback to fibres and along finite étale maps in the trace formula
- Chiarellotto–Tsuzuki, Section 12.2: the Frobenius on rigid cohomology is defined through functoriality for the relative Frobenius
- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7: functoriality of the comparison with crystalline cohomology

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rigidCohomology.map` |  | f^*: H^i_rig(X/K, E) → H^i_rig(X'/K, f^*E). |
| `rigidCohomology.map_id` |  | (id)^* = id. |
| `rigidCohomology.map_comp` |  | (g ∘ f)^* = f^* ∘ g^* up to the canonical isomorphism f^*g^*E ≅ (gf)^*E. |
