**Prerequisites.** [The tube ]T[_P of a locally closed subscheme](#target-rd-3-tube) (`RD.3/tube`), [Restriction from overconvergent to convergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-3-restriction-to-convergent) (`RD.3/restriction-to-convergent`), [For proper X, rigid cohomology is the de Rham cohomology of the tube](#target-rd-4-proper-rigid-equals-convergent) (`RD.4/proper-rigid-equals-convergent`), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0/pd-envelope`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0/completed-envelope`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.1/crystal`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.1/taylor-equivalence`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2/smooth-ambient-comparison`.

**Sources.**

- [S94](#source-94), Proposition 1.9, proof, pp. 14–15 of the author's 1997 preprint. Constructs the map from functions on the tube, through the closed tube of radius p^{-1/p}, to the rationalised completed PD envelope by sending T_i to (p − 1)! times the p-th divided power of f_i, and shows it is unique, glues, commutes with derivations and is functorial without any properness hypothesis.
- [S66](#source-66), §2, Proposition 2.35 (the functor Φ) and the paragraph before Theorem 2.36, pp. 29–31 (arXiv v2). Constructs the functor Φ from locally free isocrystals on the log convergent site to isocrystals on the log crystalline site, through maps from completed log PD envelopes to universal enlargements, and gives the corresponding morphism from the log de Rham complex of a convergent isocrystal E on the tube to the log de Rham complex of Φ(E) on the p-adically completed log PD envelope, by the method of his earlier paper.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- Berthelot, Finitude et pureté, Proposition 1.9: the map (1.9.2) whose hypercohomology is the comparison map H^*_rig(X/K) → H^*_crys(X/W) ⊗ K
- Shiho, Relative log convergent cohomology I, Theorem 2.36: the coefficient and log version whose quasi-isomorphism property is the convergent–crystalline comparison
- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/comparison-map-quasi-isomorphism: the map shown to be a quasi-isomorphism for smooth X
- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/crystalline-rigid-comparison-with-coefficients: the coefficient version, giving Ogus's comparison for proper smooth X
- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/rigid-crystalline-comparison: supplies the comparison map whose isomorphism property the inherited theorem asserts

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `RigidCohomology.tubeToEnvelope` |  | The morphism of sheaves of O_P-algebras c_{X,P} : sp_* O_{]X[_P} → D̂_P(X) ⊗ Q. |
| `RigidCohomology.tubeToEnvelope_affine` |  | On U = Spf A with 𝔦 = (p, f_1, …, f_r): c_{X,P} factors through A{T}/(f_j^p − pT_j) ⊗ Q and sends T_j to (p − 1)!·f_j^{[p]}. |
| `RigidCohomology.tubeToEnvelope_unique` |  | c_{X,P} is the only morphism of A ⊗ Q-algebras sp_*O_{]X[_P}(U) → D̂(U) ⊗ Q that is continuous for the natural topologies. |
| `RigidCohomology.tubeToEnvelope_comm_deriv` |  | c_{X,P} commutes with the derivations of O_P, and so induces a map of complexes sp_*Ω^•_{]X[_P} → D̂ ⊗ Ω^•_{P/W} ⊗ Q. |
| `RigidCohomology.tubeToEnvelope_naturality` |  | For a morphism u : P' → P with u ∘ i' = i, the two maps c_{X,P} and c_{X,P'} commute with the pullbacks of tubes and of PD envelopes along u; c is compatible with restriction to open formal subschemes of P. |
| `RigidCohomology.tubeToEnvelope_lift` |  | If P is a smooth formal lift of X (so 𝔦 = pO_P), then D̂ = O_P, the tube is P_K and c_{X,P} is the identity. |
| `RigidCohomology.tubeToEnvelope_coeff` |  | For a locally free convergent isocrystal E with associated crystalline isocrystal Φ(E) (value Φ(E)_D on D̂): a morphism of complexes sp_*(E ⊗ Ω^•) → Φ(E)_D ⊗ Ω^•, natural in E and equal to c_{X,P} for E = O. |
| `RigidCohomology.tubeToEnvelope_cohomology` |  | For X proper, the map induced on hypercohomology over X goes from H^*_rig(X/K_0, E) (RD.4/proper-rigid-equals-convergent) to the crystalline cohomology of Φ(E), which is H^*_crys(X/W, M) ⊗ K_0 when Φ(E) = M ⊗ Q for a crystal M (CrystallineCohomology:CR.2/smooth-ambient-comparison). |

**Unit tests.**

- `RigidCohomology.tubeToEnvelope_point_in_disc` (computation): For X = Spec k ⊂ P = Spf W⟨t⟩, c sends t^n to n!·t^{[n]}, hence Σ b_n t^n (convergent on |t| < 1) to Σ b_n n!·t^{[n]}; the coefficients b_n n! tend to 0 because v_p(n!) = (n − s_p(n))/(p − 1), with s_p the sum of the p-adic digits.
- `RigidCohomology.tubeToEnvelope_lift_eq_id` (degenerate): For X = Spec k[t] with the lift P = Spf W⟨t⟩, the map is the identity of W⟨t⟩ ⊗ Q.
- `RigidCohomology.tubeToEnvelope_not_surjective` (non-example): For X = Spec k ⊂ Spf W⟨t⟩ the element Σ_k p^k t^{[p^k]} of D̂ is not in the image: as a power series it is Σ_k (p^k/(p^k)!) t^{p^k}, which diverges at points with |p|^{1/(p−1)} < |t| < 1, so the map is a quasi-isomorphism of de Rham complexes (for smooth X), not an isomorphism of rings.
- `RigidCohomology.tubeToEnvelope_compat_crystalline` (compatibility): For X = P^1_k embedded as the special fibre of the formal completion of P^1_W (a lift), the induced map H^*_rig(P^1/K_0) → H^*_crys(P^1/W) ⊗ K_0 is the identity of H^*_dR(P^1_{K_0}), an isomorphism K_0 → K_0 in degrees 0 and 2 and 0 → 0 in degree 1.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Affine description: on U = Spf A with 𝔦 = (p, f_1, …, f_r) the tube is the rigid subspace |f_j| < 1, and its functions restrict to the closed sub-tube |f_j| ≤ |p|^{1/p}, whose affinoid algebra is A{T}/(f_j^p − pT_j) ⊗ Q (Berthelot, Finitude, proof of Proposition 1.9).
2. Since f_j^p = p!·f_j^{[p]} in D, the assignment T_j ↦ (p − 1)!·f_j^{[p]} kills f_j^p − pT_j and defines an A-algebra map A[T]/(f_j^p − pT_j) → D; it extends to the p-adic completions and, after inverting p, to the stated map; uniqueness: it is the only continuous A ⊗ Q-algebra map between these rings (CrystallineCohomology:CR.0/pd-envelope, CR.0/completed-envelope). Berthelot states uniqueness on the closed tube; it holds on sp_*O_{]X[_P}(U) too, because A ⊗ Q is dense there: on each closed tube |f_j|^n ≤ |p|^m of an exhausting family the coordinate f_j^n/p^m already lies in A ⊗ Q, so A ⊗ Q is dense in each affinoid algebra and hence in their inverse limit.
3. The local maps agree on overlaps by uniqueness, so they glue to c_{X,P}; continuity gives compatibility with derivations, hence a map of de Rham complexes, and functoriality in (X, P) follows from uniqueness.
4. Coefficients: a locally free convergent isocrystal E is realised on ]X[_P as a module with integrable connection whose Taylor series converge on the tube of the diagonal; Shiho's functor Φ pulls it back along the canonical maps from the completed PD envelopes of X in P, P × P and P × P × P to the corresponding enlargements, and the value Φ(E)_D, a module with integrable connection on D̂ ⊗ Q (CrystallineCohomology:CR.1/taylor-equivalence), receives the module version of the same map, compatibly with the connections (Shiho, Relative log convergent cohomology I, §2, Proposition 2.35 and p. 31, constructs Φ and the log and relative version of the map 'by the same method' as his earlier paper). For an F-crystal M the convergent F-isocrystal E is supplied by RD.3/restriction-to-convergent, and Φ(E) = M ⊗ Q.

**Checks.**

- For X = Spec k inside P = Spf W⟨t⟩ (𝔦 = (p, t)), the map sends a function Σ b_n t^n on the open unit disc to Σ b_n n!·t^{[n]}.
- For a smooth affine X with a smooth formal lift P (𝔦 = pO_P), D̂ = O_P, ]X[_P = P_K and c_{X,P} is the identity of O_P ⊗ Q.

<a id="target-rd-7-comparison-map-quasi-isomorphism"></a>

### Berthelot's comparison morphism is a quasi-isomorphism for smooth X

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/comparison-map-quasi-isomorphism` · theorem

In the situation of RD.7/tube-to-envelope-comparison-map, assume X smooth over k. Then c_{X,P} : sp_*Ω^•_{]X[_P} → D̂ ⊗_{O_P} Ω^•_{P/W} ⊗ Q is a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of sheaves of K_0-vector spaces on X, and so is its version c_{X,P}(E) with coefficients in a locally free convergent isocrystal E, whose target is the de Rham complex of the crystalline isocrystal Φ(E) on D̂ (Shiho, Theorem 2.36). The induced isomorphism in the derived category does not depend on the embedding P, and is compatible with the canonical isomorphisms between two embeddings on each side. If X is in addition proper, taking hypercohomology on X gives the canonical isomorphism H^i_rig(X/K_0) ≅ H^i_crys(X/W) ⊗_W K_0 of RD.7/rigid-crystalline-comparison, now with its proof.

**Hypotheses.**

- X smooth separated of finite type over the perfect field k.
- i : X → P closed immersion into a p-adic formal W-scheme smooth near X.

**Prerequisites.** [Berthelot's comparison morphism from the tube to the completed PD envelope](#target-rd-7-tube-to-envelope-comparison-map) (`RD.7/tube-to-envelope-comparison-map`), [Weak fibration theorem: tubes along smooth morphisms are open polydisc fibrations](#target-rd-3-weak-fibration-theorem) (`RD.3/weak-fibration-theorem`), [Independence of rigid cohomology from the smooth formal embedding (Berthelot, Théorème 1)](#target-rd-4-independence-of-embedding) (`RD.4/independence-of-embedding`), [For proper X, rigid cohomology is the de Rham cohomology of the tube](#target-rd-4-proper-rigid-equals-convergent) (`RD.4/proper-rigid-equals-convergent`), [Rigid cohomology H^i_rig(X/K, E)](#target-rd-4-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.4/rigid-cohomology`), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2/smooth-ambient-comparison`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2/embedding-independence`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0/completed-envelope`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.3/crystalline-descent`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/deformations-of-smooth-schemes`.

**Sources.**

- [S94](#source-94), Proposition 1.9 and its proof, pp. 14–15 of the author's 1997 preprint. States the canonical isomorphism between rigid and crystalline cohomology for proper smooth X over k with a Cohen ring W, and proves it by reducing to the case of a smooth affine lift, using that both sides are independent of the embedding and that the map is functorial in it.
- [S66](#source-66), Theorem 2.36 and its proof, p. 31 (arXiv v2). The convergent–crystalline comparison for log smooth X with a locally free convergent isocrystal is proved by the same reduction: independence of the embedding on both sides, then the case where the embedding is a lift, where the two complexes coincide.
- [S3](#source-3), Definition 2.1, p. 2. Smooth affine varieties admit smooth affine formal lifts over W(k) (Elkik, Arabia), which the notes use to describe convergent F-isocrystals.

**Construction or proof.**

1. The assertion is local on X and on P, so P = Spf A may be taken affine and X = Spec A/𝔦 affine and smooth.
2. Independence of the embedding on both sides, compatibly with c: for two embeddings X → P and X → P' compare both with the diagonal embedding in P × P'. On the tube side the projection ]X[_{P×P'} → ]X[_P is locally a fibration in open polydiscs (RD.3/weak-fibration-theorem) and the de Rham complex of an open polydisc is a resolution, which is the content of RD.4/independence-of-embedding; on the PD side, CrystallineCohomology:CR.2/smooth-ambient-comparison and CR.2/embedding-independence give the canonical quasi-isomorphisms at each finite level W_n, and the p-adic version is their derived limit, which equals D̂ ⊗ Ω^• because on affines the transition maps are surjective (CR.0/completed-envelope). Naturality of c in the embedding (API tubeToEnvelope_naturality) makes the squares commute.
3. Choose a smooth formal lift P' of the smooth affine X: lifts exist at every finite level because the obstructions lie in H^2(X, T_X) ⊗ I = 0 on an affine (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/deformations-of-smooth-schemes), and the compatible system defines a smooth affine formal scheme (Elkik's theorem is the usual citation; Kedlaya, Notes on isocrystals, Definition 2.1).
4. For the lift, 𝔦' = pO_{P'}, the PD envelope is O_{P'} itself (p has divided powers in W), the tube is P'_K, and c is the identity (API tubeToEnvelope_lift). By the previous two steps c_{X,P} is a quasi-isomorphism (Berthelot, Finitude, end of the proof of Proposition 1.9).
5. Coefficients: the same three steps apply with Φ(E)_D ⊗ Ω^• on the PD side (CrystallineCohomology:CR.2/smooth-ambient-comparison, applied to a crystal M of finite type with M ⊗ Q = Φ(E), for instance an F-crystal; Shiho's proof treats Φ(E) directly) and E ⊗ Ω^• on the tube side (RD.4/independence-of-embedding for the coefficient E); this is Shiho's proof of Theorem 2.36 with trivial log structures and base Spf W.
6. For X proper: RΓ_rig(X/K_0) = RΓ(X, sp_*Ω^•_{]X[_P}) because the strict neighbourhoods are the whole tube and R^q sp_* vanishes for q > 0 on the quasi-Stein inverse images of affines (RD.4/proper-rigid-equals-convergent; Berthelot, Finitude, proof of 1.9), and RΓ_crys(X/W) ⊗ Q = RΓ(X, D̂ ⊗ Ω^•) ⊗ Q because X is quasi-compact; take hypercohomology of the quasi-isomorphism. A non-embeddable proper X is handled by a finite Zariski cover by embeddable opens and Čech descent on both sides (CrystallineCohomology:CR.3/crystalline-descent; RD.4/rigid-cohomology).

**Checks.**

- X = A^1_k with the lift P = Spf W⟨t⟩: c is the identity and both sides compute the de Rham cohomology of the Tate algebra K_0⟨t⟩, whose H^1 is infinite-dimensional (the form Σ_k p^k t^{p^{2k}−1}dt has formal primitive with coefficients p^{−k}, so it is not exact); this is why the rigid form of the comparison needs X proper.
- X = P^1_k: H^0 = K_0, H^1 = 0, H^2 = K_0 on both sides; with the embedding of P^1_k as the special fibre of the formal completion of P^1_W the map c is the identity, so the comparison is the identity of H^*_dR(P^1_{K_0}) (unit test tubeToEnvelope_compat_crystalline).
- The map is a quasi-isomorphism without being an isomorphism of complexes: for X = Spec k ⊂ Spf W⟨t⟩ the degree-zero terms differ (API test tubeToEnvelope_not_surjective), yet both complexes resolve K_0.

<a id="target-rd-7-rigid-crystalline-comparison"></a>

### The rational rigid–crystalline comparison for smooth proper varieties

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/rigid-crystalline-comparison` · theorem

Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], and X a smooth proper k-scheme. There is a canonical isomorphism H^i_rig(X/K_0) ≅ H^i_crys(X/W) ⊗_W K_0 for every i, functorial in X, and compatible with finite extension of scalars: H^i_rig(X/K) = H^i_rig(X/K_0) ⊗_{K_0} K for K/K_0 finite. Here H^i_crys(X/W) is the crystalline cohomology of CrystallineCohomology:CR.3 (finitely generated over W; only its tensor product with K_0 is used). With coefficients: for an F-crystal M of finite locally free modules with associated convergent (= overconvergent, X proper) F-isocrystal E, H^i(X_crys, M) ⊗ Q ≅ H^i_rig(X, E) (Ogus).

**Hypotheses.**

- k perfect; X smooth and proper over k; W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p].

**Prerequisites.** [Rigid cohomology H^i_rig(X/K, E)](#target-rd-4-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.4/rigid-cohomology`), [Independence of the frame: canonical equivalences between categories of overconvergent isocrystals](#target-rd-3-independence-of-frame) (`RD.3/independence-of-frame`), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2/embedding-computation`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2/pd-poincare`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.3`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.3/proper-perfectness`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.3/frobenius-map`, [Berthelot's comparison morphism is a quasi-isomorphism for smooth X](#target-rd-7-comparison-map-quasi-isomorphism) (`RD.7/comparison-map-quasi-isomorphism`), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2/smooth-ambient-comparison`.

**Sources.**

- [S20](#source-20), Proposition 2, p. 14 (text checked on the page image). The comparison with crystalline cohomology.
- [S20](#source-20), (2.4), p. 19 (text checked on the page image). Rigid equals naive cohomology for proper X (the base field in the proper-variety clause is the residue field k; see sourceIssues).
- [S3](#source-3), Theorem 8.3 (Ogus), p. 20. Statement with coefficients (proof cited to Ogus, not read).

**Construction or proof.**

1. X proper: the compactification is X itself, so strict neighbourhoods are trivial and rigid cohomology equals Berthelot's naive cohomology H^i(]X[_P, Ω^•) for a closed embedding X ↪ P into a formal W-scheme smooth near X (Berthelot (2.4); RD.4/rigid-cohomology; independence of P, RD.3/independence-of-frame). For non-embeddable X use a Čech covering by embeddable opens (Berthelot (1.5)).
2. Crystalline cohomology is computed by the p-adically completed de Rham complex of the PD envelope of X in P (CrystallineCohomology:CR.2), with independence of the embedding.
3. Apply RD.7/tube-to-envelope-comparison-map and comparison-map-quasi-isomorphism, using the global p-adic formal embedding and descent comparison in CrystallineCohomology:CR.2/smooth-ambient-comparison. Čech descent gives the comparison for a non-embeddable smooth proper variety. The later coefficient and linear q-Frobenius comparison is RD.7/crystalline-rigid-comparison-with-coefficients.
4. Functoriality in X and base change in K follow from functoriality of both constructions in the embedding.

**Checks.**

- P^1: H^0 = K_0, H^1 = 0, H^2 = K_0 on both sides; H^2_crys(P^1/W) = W with Frobenius aη ↦ p·σ(a)η, matching H^2_rig = K_0(−1) for q = p.
- Elliptic curve E/F_p: both H^1 are 2-dimensional, with the same characteristic polynomial T^2 − a_p T + p of Frobenius (RD.7/frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison).

<a id="target-rd-4-coefficient-long-exact-sequence"></a>

### Exact sequences in rigid coefficients

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4/coefficient-long-exact-sequence` · theorem

For a short exact sequence 0 → E′ → E → E″ → 0 of overconvergent isocrystals on X/K, rigid cohomology has its natural long exact coefficient sequence. The same holds with a fixed closed support Z and with compact support; if the sequence has Frobenius structures, every map is Frobenius compatible.

**Hypotheses.**

- X is separated of finite type over k; support and compactification conventions are those of the inherited RD.4 complexes.
- Use the no-F coefficient refinements of the imported support/localization, MW and finite scalar-extension contracts here; do not obtain arbitrary E∈Isoc† merely by forgetting Frobenius on an F-isocrystal.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti.RigidCohomology.RD4`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Declaration.** `rigidCoefficientLongExactSequence`

**Prerequisites.** [Rigid cohomology H^i_rig(X/K, E)](#target-rd-4-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.4/rigid-cohomology`), [Rigid cohomology with supports in a closed subscheme H^i_{Z,rig}(X/K, E)](#target-rd-4-rigid-cohomology-with-supports) (`RD.4/rigid-cohomology-with-supports`), [Rigid cohomology with compact supports H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E)](#target-rd-4-compactly-supported-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.4/compactly-supported-rigid-cohomology`), [Étale-proper de Rham descent](#target-rd-4-etale-proper-de-rham-descent) (`RD.4/etale-proper-de-rham-descent`), `mathlib:DerivedCategory`, [Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-isocrystal) (`RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal`).

**Sources.**

- [S36](#source-36), Proposition 10.5.1, pp. 185–186; Proposition 2.7.2, pp. 79–81. Coefficient exactness gives the ordinary cohomology triangle.
- [S37](#source-37), §1.2, pp. 6–7, and §2.1–2.5, pp. 16–19 of author copy. Supported realizations use kernels and their exact localization sequences.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Realize the short exact coefficient sequence as coherent j†-modules on a frame; tensoring with locally free forms is exact.
2. Use exactness of j† and of the supported realization functor before deriving global sections. The short exact sequence of complexes gives a triangle.
3. Glue by de Rham descent, then take cohomology. Use naturality of the boundary map to retain Frobenius.

**Checks.**

- The boundary maps for a split coefficient sequence vanish.
- Closed-support and compact-support coefficient triangles commute with their forget-supports maps.

<a id="target-rd-4-general-rigid-gysin"></a>

### Rigid Gysin isomorphism

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4/general-rigid-gysin` · theorem

If i:Z ↪ X is a closed immersion of smooth separated k-schemes of pure constant codimension c and E is an overconvergent isocrystal on X/K, then RΓ_Z,rig(X/K,E) ≃ RΓ_rig(Z/K,i*E)[−2c]. With compatible q-Frobenius structures this is RΓ_rig(Z/K,i*E)(−c)[−2c]. The comparison is natural for restriction and finite scalar extension. This extends the inherited target restricted to liftable coordinate pairs.

**Hypotheses.**

- k is perfect of characteristic p, and K is a complete characteristic-zero coefficient field with residue field k.
- Mixed codimension components require separate shifts; the Frobenius twist is part of the equivariant statement.
- The global coordinate-independence proof is an explicit gap, G1; this node records the full target.
- Use the no-F coefficient refinements of the imported support/localization, MW and finite scalar-extension contracts here; do not obtain arbitrary E∈Isoc† merely by forgetting Frobenius on an F-isocrystal.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti.RigidCohomology.RD4`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Declaration.** `rigidGysin`

**Prerequisites.** [The Gysin isomorphism for smooth liftable pairs](#target-rd-4-gysin-isomorphism) (`RD.4/gysin-isomorphism`), [Localisation sequences for rigid cohomology with supports](#target-rd-4-localisation-sequence) (`RD.4/localisation-sequence`), [Tate twists of F-spaces](#target-rd-4-tate-twist) (`RD.4/tate-twist`), [Étale-proper de Rham descent](#target-rd-4-etale-proper-de-rham-descent) (`RD.4/etale-proper-de-rham-descent`), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4`, [Overconvergent isocrystals on a frame](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-isocrystal) (`RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystal`).

**Sources.**

- [S70](#source-70), Lemma 4.1.2 and its proof, p. 908; Example 2.2.2, p. 895. Tsuzuki applies the unrestricted smooth-pair Gysin isomorphism and records base-extension compatibility, referring to his 1999 Theorem 4.1.1.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Reduce smooth closed pairs étale locally to coordinate pairs. Refine the inherited liftable calculation to Taylor-overconvergent coefficients without Frobenius; its no-F coordinate residue map and gluing are explicitly part of G1, rather than an import of the parent’s F-only theorem for an arbitrary E.
2. The required gluing checks that the residue generator transforms canonically when normal coordinates change, and that the local maps respect support Čech descent. This is the unclosed step in G1.
3. Use localization for the resulting Gysin sequence; scalar extension is inherited. The divisor example determines the twist sign.

**Checks.**

- For {0} in A¹, the sole supported group is H² = K(−1); the shift is 2.
- For c=0 and Z=X the comparison is the identity.

<a id="target-rd-4-quasi-etale-specialization"></a>

### Quasi-étale specialization to the special fibre

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4/quasi-etale-specialization` · construction

For a finite-type O_K′-scheme Z and a closed subscheme X of its special fibre, define the specialization morphism of sites s_(X,Z): ]X[_Zη,qét → X_ét by composing the tube-to-formal-completion map with the equivalence from the étale site of the completion along X to X_ét. Keep pullback and derived pushforward as part of this interface.

**Hypotheses.**

- K′ is a finite extension of K₀=Frac W(κ), κ finite; Zη is the Berkovich generic fibre of the formal completion.
- The equivalence is between the formal-completion and special-fibre étale sites; the tube site itself is not asserted equivalent to X_ét.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti.RigidCohomology.RD4`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Declaration.** `TubeSpecialization`

**Prerequisites.** `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/raynaud-generic-fibre`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/tube`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1`.

**Sources.**

- [S31](#source-31), Appendix B.1, p. 113. The tube quasi-étale site maps to the special-fibre étale site through the formal completion.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- Disegni–Liu, Appendix B.2: Pushes the tube log de Rham realization to X_ét.
- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4/tube-proper-support-functor: Allows support to be imposed on the tube before specialization.

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TubeSpecialization.pullback` |  | s* is the inverse-image functor of sheaves and respects identities and composition. |
| `TubeSpecialization.derivedPushforward` |  | Rs_* acts on bounded-below complexes of R-module sheaves. |
| `TubeSpecialization.adjunction` |  | s* is left adjoint to s_*, with the induced derived unit/counit where defined. |
| `TubeSpecialization.restrictStratum` |  | Restriction to a closed special-fibre stratum commutes with its tube specialization square. |

**Unit tests.**

- `formal_point` (compatibility): For X=Spec κ′ in Spf O_K′, the intermediate formal étale site identifies with the residue-field étale site; this does not identify all analytic sheaves with residue-field sheaves.
- `empty_tube` (degenerate): X empty gives the empty tube and zero derived pushforward of module sheaves.
- `same_special_fibre` (compatibility): Replacing the formal completion by an infinitesimal thickening leaves its special-fibre étale-site comparison unchanged.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Use the generic-fibre construction and the tube map into the formal completion.
2. Compose with the nilpotent/formal invariance of the étale site.
3. Retain the induced adjunction and the derived pushforward on bounded-below sheaf complexes; restrictions of closed strata give the compatible specialization maps.

**Checks.**

- The construction distinguishes its two maps; étale invariance is used only for formal completion.

<a id="target-rd-4-tube-proper-support-functor"></a>

### Proper support on a tube

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4/tube-proper-support-functor` · construction

For U open in the closed special-fibre subscheme X of Z and g: ]X∖U[_Zη ↪ ]X[_Zη, define f!_(U,X)(F)=ker(F → g_*g*F), the kernel of the unit, on R-module sheaves on the tube quasi-étale site. Here g*, g_* and f! are exact. There is a canonical natural map F!F* Rs_* → Rs_* f! for the open immersion F:U ↪ X; no general isomorphism or commuting special-fibre endofunctor is included.

**Hypotheses.**

- The complement tube is the indicated open analytic subspace; f! is an endofunctor on the tube, not extension by zero from ]U[.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti.RigidCohomology.RD4`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Declaration.** `TubeProperSupport`

**Prerequisites.** [Quasi-étale specialization to the special fibre](#target-rd-4-quasi-etale-specialization) (`RD.4/quasi-etale-specialization`), `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1`, `mathlib:LinearMap.ker`.

**Sources.**

- [S31](#source-31), Definition B.1, Remark B.2 and Lemma B.3, pp. 113–114. The kernel defines an exact tube support functor and a canonical comparison from special-fibre extension by zero.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- Disegni–Liu, (B.2)–(B.3): Creates supported log complexes and their localization triangle.
- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4/log-rigid-proper-support-cohomology: Defines cohomology relative to the pair U⊆X.

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TubeProperSupport.ι` |  | There is a natural inclusion f!F → F whose composite with F → g_*g*F is zero. |
| `TubeProperSupport.lift` |  | A map A → F killed by the unit factors uniquely through f!F. |
| `TubeProperSupport.exact` |  | The functor takes short exact sequences to short exact sequences. |
| `TubeProperSupport.monotone` |  | For U⊆U′⊆X there is a natural map f!_(U,X)F → f!_(U′,X)F compatible with composition. |
| `TubeProperSupport.specializationMap` |  | F!F*Rs_* maps naturally to Rs_*f!; it is not specified to be invertible. |

**Unit tests.**

- `whole` (degenerate): For U=X, g has empty domain, so f! is the identity.
- `empty` (degenerate): For U empty, g is the identity and f! is zero.
- `away_from_complement` (characterisation): If g*F=0, the inclusion f!F → F is an isomorphism.
- `kernel_agreement` (compatibility): On module sections with restriction r:V→W, the support condition is r(v)=0, matching Mathlib LinearMap.ker; using ker of the zero map for all r fails when r=id.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Take the kernel of the adjunction unit objectwise in sheaves. Establish exactness using the open tube restriction and direct-image exactness in this setting.
2. For the natural transformation, factor the unit after Rs_* through the closed special-fibre complement G:X∖U ↪ X. Its restriction after F* vanishes.
3. Use the kernel universal property to obtain the natural map, and exactness to pass to bounded-below derived complexes.

**Checks.**

- The support is imposed before Rs_* in every log complex.

<a id="target-rd-4-log-rigid-realization"></a>

### Log rigid and log convergent realizations

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4/log-rigid-realization` · construction

For a fine κ°-log scheme X admitting a Zariski open cover with exact closed embeddings into log-smooth weak formal W°-schemes, and a finite-rank Zariski locally constant K₀-sheaf E, construct RΓ_log-rig(X/W°,E) from the simplicial dagger tubes of exactifications of the embedding-product diagonals, with coefficient complex sp⁻¹E⊗Ω•_log. The completed-formal/rigid version gives RΓ_log-conv(X/W°,E) and the natural map from the dagger realization. Exactifications and common cover refinements give canonical comparison equivalences. For the strictly semistable class, admissible weak lifts provide the local embedding data.

**Hypotheses.**

- Use the standard log point κ° and its weak formal Witt lift W°, with K₀=Frac W. Fix the cohomological totalization and alternating cover signs.
- Only finite-rank Zariski locally constant coefficients are included in this source realization. A general overconvergent logarithmic connection, including the Sym^k Igusa coefficient, requires the separate G3 realization and cannot use the locally constant coefficient theorem by changing its name.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti.RigidCohomology.RD4`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Declaration.** `LogRigidRealization`

**Prerequisites.** [Relative overconvergent Poincaré lemma](#target-rd-4-relative-overconvergent-poincare) (`RD.4/relative-overconvergent-poincare`), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5/log-exactification`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5/log-de-rham`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-space`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-differentials`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`.

**Sources.**

- [S72](#source-72), Lemma 1.4 and §1.5, pp. 8–9; §5.1, p. 26. Exactifications, relative Poincaré and weak-formal dagger tubes define log rigid cohomology, its comparison with the convergent realization, and semistable embedding data.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4/proper-log-rigid-convergent-comparison: Provides the two source/target cohomology realizations for the proper comparison.
- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4/supported-log-de-rham-complexes: Provides the weak-formal counterpart of the completed admissible-system log complexes.

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `LogRigidRealization.refine` |  | Cover refinement and a change of exactification give canonical quasi-isomorphisms, independent of further common refinement. |
| `LogRigidRealization.pullback` |  | A morphism of admissible log schemes and the induced pullback of E give the contravariant realization map, with identities and composition. |
| `LogRigidRealization.toConvergent` |  | Completing the weak formal embeddings gives a natural map from log rigid to log convergent cohomology. |
| `LogRigidRealization.smoothAgreement` |  | For a smooth scheme with log structure pulled back from the standard base, the relative log form complex is the ordinary form complex, and the realization agrees with the inherited ordinary rigid/coefficient realization whenever those coefficient classes coincide. |
| `LogRigidRealization.coefficientMap` |  | A map of finite-rank Zariski locally constant K₀-sheaves induces a map on both realizations, commuting with refinement, pullback and the completion map. |

**Unit tests.**

- `standard_log_point` (computation): For the standard log point and constant coefficient K₀, relative H⁰=K₀ and H^q=0 for q≠0.
- `two_points` (computation): For two disjoint standard log points with constant coefficient, H⁰=K₀², not a single K₀.
- `duplicate_cover` (compatibility): Covering the standard log point by two copies of itself still gives H⁰=K₀; the cover totalization removes duplicate sections, unlike a direct sum of chart cohomology.
- `smooth_projective_line` (computation): For P¹ with the log structure pulled back from κ°, the constant realization has H⁰=K₀, H²=K₀(−1), and H¹=0, agreeing with ordinary rigid cohomology.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Choose the local exact log embeddings. For each finite intersection take a product embedding and its exactification, then its dagger tube. The specialization pullback of E tensors with the relative log form complex.
2. Use the alternating cover diagram and derived global sections to form the realization. Compare choices through product exactifications of a common refinement; the relevant projections are strict and smooth near the embedded scheme, so relative open-polydisc Poincaré gives their quasi-isomorphisms.
3. Replace weak formal schemes by their completions to obtain the convergent version and the canonical comparison. For a semistable log scheme construct local admissible weak lifts using its normal-crossings embedding and smooth affine lift.

**Checks.**

- The coefficient class is explicit in every signature.
- The completion map respects the de Rham differential and cover refinements.

<a id="target-rd-4-supported-log-de-rham-complexes"></a>

### Log de Rham complexes with proper support

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4/supported-log-de-rham-complexes` · construction

Fix a Zariski-log scheme (X,L) over κ° and an admissible embedding system (X_•,L_•) ↪ (Z_•,N_•) over W[t]°. Put Y_•=(t=0) in Z_•, with induced log structure M_•. Let u:X_•→X be the hypercover augmentation. Form ω_X=Ru_*Rs_*(Ω•_(Y_•,M_•)/W°⊗O_tube) and its supported version ω_(U,X) by applying f!_(U_•,X_•) inside Rs_*. Form tildeω similarly using Ω•_(Z_•,N_•)/Wtriv⊗O_Y_•. Invert p throughout. The short exact sequence of log form complexes with θ=dlog t and degree-q injection β↦(−1)^(q−1)β∧θ=θ∧β from ω[−1] (whose differential is −d) gives ω[−1]→tildeω→ω→ω and its connecting operator N.

**Hypotheses.**

- Admissible means: X_• is a Zariski hypercover with exact closed embeddings into finite-type fine log-smooth (Z_•,N_•) over W[t]°. At level zero, (X_0,L_0)≃(Z_0,N_0)×_(W[t]°)κ°; Z_0 is flat and generically smooth over W[t] and smooth over W; Y_0=(t=0) is a relative strict normal-crossings divisor and N_0 is its divisor log structure. Higher levels are induced from these lifts by the embedding-product construction of DL B.1 and GK05 §§5.1–5.2: blow up the componentwise product centre, remove the strict transforms of the component factors, and take the exceptional divisor and lifted diagonal. Arbitrary compatible higher embeddings are not a replacement for this admissible system.
- This is a realization after choosing a system. RD.4 supplies its analytic common-refinement comparisons through the log rigid realization; CR.5 supplies log charts and exactification, with the weak-formal extensions explicitly requested. A generic ordinary log connection alone does not supply such a system.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti.RigidCohomology.RD4`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Declaration.** `SupportedLogComplex`

**Prerequisites.** [Proper support on a tube](#target-rd-4-tube-proper-support-functor) (`RD.4/tube-proper-support-functor`), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5/log-differentials`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`, [Log rigid and log convergent realizations](#target-rd-4-log-rigid-realization) (`RD.4/log-rigid-realization`).

**Sources.**

- [S31](#source-31), Appendix B.1–B.2, pp. 114–116; (B.1)–(B.2). An admissible log embedding system constructs the absolute/relative complexes and applies proper support before derived specialization.
- [S72](#source-72), §§5.1–5.2, pp. 26–28; §5.4, p. 29. The weak-formal absolute/relative log complexes and the wedge-dlog t sequence supply the dagger counterpart and connecting monodromy.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- Disegni–Liu, Definition B.4 and (B.11): Supplies the pair-dependent proper-support cohomology and its boundary sequence.
- Disegni–Liu, Lemmas B.5–B.6: Supplies the abutments of the supported spectral sequences.

| --- | --- | --- |

**Unit tests.**
