- `kunnethMap_gm_square` (compatibility): For G_m × G_m: H^1 ⊗ H^1 → H^2_rig(G_m^2), [dx/x] ⊗ [dy/y] ↦ [dx/x ∧ dy/y], matching the MW external product of Kedlaya, Section 7.6; the Frobenius eigenvalue is q·q = q^2.
- `kunnethMap_sum_nonexample` (non-example): The coefficient on the product is the external tensor product pr_1^*E_1 ⊗ pr_2^*E_2: with pr_1^*O ⊕ pr_2^*O instead of O on A^1 × A^1, H^4_{c,rig} would be two dimensional, while H^2_{c,rig}(A^1) ⊗ H^2_{c,rig}(A^1) is one dimensional.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Product frame (X_1 × X_2, Y_1 × Y_2, P_1 × P_2): ]Y_1 × Y_2[ = ]Y_1[ × ]Y_2[, and products of strict neighbourhoods are cofinal among strict neighbourhoods of ]X_1 × X_2[; the external wedge product of forms gives pr_1^{-1}j†(E_1 ⊗ Ω^•) ⊗ pr_2^{-1}j†(E_2 ⊗ Ω^•) → j†(E ⊗ Ω^•), and hypercohomology with the Künneth map of tensor products of complexes of K-vector spaces gives the map.
2. Compact supports: the same with Γ_{]X_1[} ⊠ Γ_{]X_2[} → Γ_{]X_1 × X_2[}; supports: with the kernels Γ†_{Z_i}.
3. Smooth affine case: M_1 ⊗ Ω^•_{A_1} ⊗_K M_2 ⊗ Ω^•_{A_2} → (M_1 ⊠ M_2) ⊗ Ω^•_{A_1 ⊗̂ A_2}, with A_1 ⊗̂ A_2 the completed tensor product of dagger algebras (Kedlaya, Definition 2.3.8).
4. Proof input: Remove the hypothesis recording Tsuzuki 1999 Section 6.3 as a gap.

**Checks.**

- A^1 × A^1: [dt_1/t_1] ⊗ [dt_2/t_2] ↦ [dt_1/t_1 ∧ dt_2/t_2] ∈ H^4_{c,rig}(A^2), an isomorphism K(−1) ⊗ K(−1) ≅ K(−2).

<a id="target-rd-5-kunneth-formula-with-supports"></a>

### The Künneth formula with supports for smooth varieties (Kedlaya, (1.2.4.2))

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.5/kunneth-formula-with-supports` · theorem

If X_1 and X_2 are smooth over k and Z_i ⊆ X_i are closed, the Künneth morphism ⊕_{j+l=i} H^j_{Z_1,rig}(X_1, E_1) ⊗ H^l_{Z_2,rig}(X_2, E_2) → H^i_{Z_1×Z_2,rig}(X_1 × X_2, E_1 ⊠ E_2) is an isomorphism; in particular (Z_i = X_i) H^•_rig(X_1 × X_2, E_1 ⊠ E_2) ≅ H^•_rig(X_1, E_1) ⊗ H^•_rig(X_2, E_2).

**Hypotheses.**

- X_1, X_2 smooth over k (the version with supports needs smoothness).

**Prerequisites.** [The Künneth morphisms](#target-rd-5-kunneth-morphism) (`RD.5/kunneth-morphism`), [Open dense affines finite étale over affine space in positive characteristic](#target-rd-3-etale-cover-of-affine-space) (`RD.3/etale-cover-of-affine-space`), [Generic pushforwards are (σ,∇)-modules (Kedlaya, Theorem 7.3.3)](#target-rd-5-generic-pushforward-theorem) (`RD.5/generic-pushforward-theorem`), [The Leray long exact sequence for the projection A⟨x⟩† → A](#target-rd-5-leray-long-exact-sequence) (`RD.5/leray-long-exact-sequence`), [Generic pushforwards commute with external products](#target-rd-5-pushforward-external-product) (`RD.5/pushforward-external-product`), [Finite dimensionality of rigid cohomology with coefficients (Kedlaya, Theorem 1.2.1)](#target-rd-5-finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.5/finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology`), [Localisation sequences for rigid cohomology with supports](#target-rd-4-localisation-sequence) (`RD.4/localisation-sequence`), [Finite étale pushforward preserves Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology](#target-rd-4-finite-etale-pushforward-de-rham) (`RD.4/finite-etale-pushforward-de-rham`).

**Sources.**

- [S4](#source-4), Theorem 1.2.4, p. 4. The statement.
- [S4](#source-4), Proof of Theorem 1.2.4, p. 66. The Leray comparison.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Simultaneous induction on n = dim X: (a)_n for Z_i = X_i, (b)_n for dim Z ≤ n. (b): first Z_2 = X_2, tensoring the localisation triangle for T_1 ⊂ Z_1 ⊂ X_1 with RΓ_{Z_2,rig}(X_2, E_2) and arguing as in RD.5/finiteness-for-smooth-varieties.
2. (a): by RD.3/etale-cover-of-affine-space, excision, (b)_{n−1} and RD.4/finite-etale-pushforward-de-rham, reduce to X_1 = A^m and X_2 = V × A^1 with R^if_*E_2 overconvergent F-isocrystals on V (RD.5/generic-pushforward-theorem); compare the two Leray long exact sequences (RD.5/leray-long-exact-sequence) for X_1 × X_2 → X_1 × V and X_2 → V, identified by RD.5/pushforward-external-product; the Künneth maps for the pushforwards are isomorphisms by (a)_{n−1}; conclude by the five lemma.

**Checks.**

- G_m × G_m: dimensions 1, 2, 1 in degrees 0, 1, 2, with Frobenius 1; q, q; q^2.

<a id="target-rd-5-kunneth-formula"></a>

### The Künneth formula for compact-support rigid cohomology (Kedlaya, (1.2.4.1))

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.5/kunneth-formula` · theorem

For separated k-schemes of finite type X_1, X_2 and E_i ∈ F-Isoc†(X_i/K), the Künneth morphism ⊕_{j+l=i} H^j_{c,rig}(X_1/K, E_1) ⊗_K H^l_{c,rig}(X_2/K, E_2) → H^i_{c,rig}(X_1 ×_k X_2/K, pr_1^*E_1 ⊗ pr_2^*E_2) is an isomorphism of F-spaces for every i. No smoothness is needed.

**Hypotheses.**

- No smoothness hypothesis; the version without supports for singular X is not claimed.

**Prerequisites.** [The Künneth morphisms](#target-rd-5-kunneth-morphism) (`RD.5/kunneth-morphism`), [The Künneth formula with supports for smooth varieties (Kedlaya, (1.2.4.2))](#target-rd-5-kunneth-formula-with-supports) (`RD.5/kunneth-formula-with-supports`), [Poincaré duality for rigid cohomology with coefficients (Kedlaya, Theorem 1.2.3)](#target-rd-5-poincare-duality) (`RD.5/poincare-duality`), [Finite dimensionality of compact-support rigid cohomology (Kedlaya, Theorem 1.2.2)](#target-rd-5-finiteness-of-compactly-supported-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.5/finiteness-of-compactly-supported-rigid-cohomology`), [The excision long exact sequence for compact-support rigid cohomology](#target-rd-4-excision-sequence) (`RD.4/excision-sequence`), [Base change of rigid cohomology along finite extensions of the coefficient field](#target-rd-4-finite-flat-base-change) (`RD.4/finite-flat-base-change`).

**Sources.**

- [S4](#source-4), Theorem 1.2.4, p. 4. The statement.
- [S4](#source-4), Proof of Theorem 1.2.4, p. 67. The dévissage (to be read factorwise).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Induction on dim X_1 + dim X_2. Stratify each X_i into its smooth locus U_i and singular locus Z_i (after base change and reduction); X_1 × X_2 is covered by U_1 × U_2 and the closed pieces Z_1 × X_2, U_1 × Z_2 of smaller dimension. By RD.4/excision-sequence tensored with the Künneth maps (a map of long exact sequences) and the induction hypothesis, reduce to U_1 × U_2. (Kedlaya writes 'the singular locus of X'; the argument needs the singular loci of the two factors; see sourceIssues.)
2. For U_1, U_2 smooth: by RD.5/poincare-duality on U_i and on U_1 × U_2 (pure dimensions add), the compact-support Künneth map is dual to the Künneth map for H_rig of the duals, an isomorphism by RD.5/kunneth-formula-with-supports; Frobenius-compatibility since Φ ⊗ Φ = Φ and the twists add.

**Checks.**

- A^1 × A^1: H^4_{c,rig}(A^2) = K(−2) = H^2_c(A^1) ⊗ H^2_c(A^1), others 0; trace-formula check q^2 = #A^2(F_q).
- G_m × G_m: H^2_c = K (weight 0), H^3_c = K(−1)^2, H^4_c = K(−2); check (q − 1)^2 = q^2 − 2q + 1.

<a id="target-rd-5-no-finiteness-without-frobenius"></a>

### Finite dimensionality fails for overconvergent isocrystals without Frobenius structure

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.5/no-finiteness-without-frobenius` · theorem

Let a ∈ ℤ_p be a p-adic Liouville number that is not an integer: there are r < 1 and infinitely many n ∈ ℤ with |a − n| < r^{|n|}. On G_m over F_p (K = ℚ_p), the rank-one overconvergent isocrystal K_a = (K⟨x,x^{-1}⟩†, ∇ = d + a·dx/x) has infinite-dimensional H^1_rig(G_m/K, K_a) = coker(x d/dx + a). K_a has no Frobenius structure. Hence the finiteness theorems RD.5/finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology and RD.5/finiteness-for-affine-curves do not extend to overconvergent isocrystals without Frobenius. Such a exist, for example a = Σ_{m ≥ 1} p^{e_m} with e_1 = 1, e_{m+1} = p^{e_m}.

**Hypotheses.**

- a ∈ ℤ_p ensures that the Taylor series (x'/x)^{−a} = Σ binom(−a, j)((x' − x)/x)^j converges on |x' − x| < |x|, so K_a is an overconvergent isocrystal (by the same convergence as in Berthelot's Dwork example (4.2.3)).

**Prerequisites.** [Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology of a (σ,∇)-module](#target-rd-4-monsky-washnitzer-cohomology) (`RD.4/monsky-washnitzer-cohomology`), [(σ,∇)-modules over a dagger algebra of Monsky–Washnitzer type](#target-rd-3-sigma-nabla-module-over-dagger-algebra) (`RD.3/sigma-nabla-module-over-dagger-algebra`), [Rigid cohomology of the multiplicative group, with and without compact supports](#target-rd-4-cohomology-of-multiplicative-group) (`RD.4/cohomology-of-multiplicative-group`), [Finite dimensionality of rigid cohomology of an overconvergent F-isocrystal on a smooth affine curve](#target-rd-5-finiteness-for-affine-curves) (`RD.5/finiteness-for-affine-curves`).

**Sources.**

- [S3](#source-3), Remark 8.5, p. 20. The source's reason.
- [S19](#source-19), Section 6, p. 739. Definition of p-adic Liouville numbers.
- [S19](#source-19), 6.10 Proposition, p. 740. The local obstruction.
- [S19](#source-19), Introduction, p. 717. Infinite dimensionality on curves.

**Construction or proof.**

1. On coefficients (Σ c_m x^m) the operator x d/dx + a acts by c_m ↦ (m + a)c_m, injective since a ∉ ℤ; a series Σ b_m x^m is in the image iff Σ b_m/(m + a) x^m is overconvergent.
2. Choose infinitely many integers n_k with |a − n_k| < r^{|n_k|} and put m_k = −n_k, so |m_k + a| < r^{|m_k|}; partition {m_k} into infinitely many infinite subsets S_1, S_2, …; choose a real c > 0 with r < s = |π|^c < 1 and set b_m = π^{⌊c|m|⌋} ∈ K. Put g_j = Σ_{m ∈ S_j} b_m x^m. Since s^{|m|} ≤ |b_m| ≤ |π|^{-1}s^{|m|}, these series are overconvergent.
3. A nonzero finite combination Σ λ_j g_j has preimage coefficients λ_j b_m/(m + a) of absolute value ≥ |λ_j|(s/r)^{|m|} → ∞ along S_j, so it is not overconvergent: the classes of the g_j are linearly independent in H^1, which is infinite dimensional.
4. No Frobenius structure: if K_a carried a Frobenius structure it would be an overconvergent F-isocrystal on G_m, and RD.5/finiteness-for-affine-curves would make H^1 finite dimensional, contradicting the previous step. (For Frobenius structures of the form e ↦ c·x^m·e this is visible directly: (q − 1)a ∈ ℤ would be needed, RD.3/sigma-nabla-module-over-dagger-algebra, test kummer_frobenius_iff.)
5. Local form: Crew, Proposition 6.10: the connection x d/dx − a on the Robba ring is strict iff a is not p-adic Liouville; the global computation above is its analogue on G_m.
6. Existence: for a = Σ p^{e_m}, n_m = Σ_{j ≤ m} p^{e_j} ≤ 2p^{e_m} and v_p(a − n_m) = e_{m+1} = p^{e_m} ≥ n_m/2, so |a − n_m| < (p^{−1/4})^{n_m}; a ∉ ℤ because its base-p digits are 0 or 1, infinitely many 1s, not eventually constant.

**Checks.**

- Checked numerically (PARI/GP): for p = 3, n_1 = 3 with v_3(a − 3) = 3 > 3/4, n_2 = 30 with v_3(a − 30) = 27 > 30/4.

<a id="target-rd-5-affine-curve-duality-acceptance"></a>

### Acceptance: H^2_c, the dual twist and the Euler characteristic on smooth nonproper curves

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.5/affine-curve-duality-acceptance` · application

(1) For U = P^1_{F_q} minus N ≥ 1 rational points: H^0_{c,rig}(U) = 0, H^1_{c,rig}(U) = K^{N−1} (Frobenius 1), H^2_{c,rig}(U) = K(−1); H^0_rig(U) = K, H^1_rig(U) = K(−1)^{N−1}, H^2_rig(U) = 0; the Poincaré pairings H^i_rig × H^{2−i}_{c,rig} → K(−1) are perfect; χ = χ_c = 2 − N. (2) For E an elliptic curve over F_q and U = E \ {O}: H^0_{c,rig}(U) = 0, H^1_{c,rig}(U) ≅ H^1_rig(E) (dimension 2, eigenvalues α, β with αβ = q, α + β = a = q + 1 − #E(F_q)), H^2_{c,rig}(U) = K(−1); H^1_rig(U) has eigenvalues q/α = β and q/β = α; χ = −1. (3) Künneth check: for U_1 × U_2 with U_i as in (1), H^•_{c,rig} is the tensor product and Tr(Φ | H^•_c) counts (q + 1 − N_1)(q + 1 − N_2) points.

**Hypotheses.**

- q = #k; constant coefficients; σ_K = id.

**Prerequisites.** [Poincaré duality for rigid cohomology with coefficients (Kedlaya, Theorem 1.2.3)](#target-rd-5-poincare-duality) (`RD.5/poincare-duality`), [Euler characteristics with and without compact supports agree up to duality](#target-rd-5-euler-characteristic-duality) (`RD.5/euler-characteristic-duality`), [Top-degree compact-support cohomology of a geometrically irreducible variety](#target-rd-5-top-compact-support-cohomology) (`RD.5/top-compact-support-cohomology`), [Van der Put's computation of H^1 of an affine Legendre elliptic curve](#target-rd-5-van-der-put-legendre-computation) (`RD.5/van-der-put-legendre-computation`), [The Künneth formula for compact-support rigid cohomology (Kedlaya, (1.2.4.1))](#target-rd-5-kunneth-formula) (`RD.5/kunneth-formula`), [The excision long exact sequence for compact-support rigid cohomology](#target-rd-4-excision-sequence) (`RD.4/excision-sequence`), [Rigid cohomology of the projective line](#target-rd-4-cohomology-of-projective-line) (`RD.4/cohomology-of-projective-line`).

**Sources.**

- [S19](#source-19), Remark after Corollary 9.6, (9.6.2), p. 755. H^2_c(X, K) = K(−1).
- [S5](#source-5), Section 2.6, (2.6.1), p. 18. The curve exact sequence 0 → H^0 → H^0_loc → H^1_c → H^1 → H^1_loc → H^2_c → 0.
- [S7](#source-7), Remarks 7.4, p. 49. The point count on the affine Legendre curve (N* counts affine points).

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1) Excision (RD.4/excision-sequence) for S ⊂ P^1 with RD.4/cohomology-of-projective-line: 0 → H^0_c(U) → H^0(P^1) = K → H^0(S) = K^N → H^1_c(U) → H^1(P^1) = 0 → 0 → H^2_c(U) → H^2(P^1) = K(−1) → 0, all maps Frobenius-equivariant; then RD.5/poincare-duality for H_rig and RD.5/euler-characteristic-duality.
2. (2) Excision for {O} ⊂ E: H^0(E) = K → H^0(O) = K is an isomorphism, so H^1_c(U) ≅ H^1(E) and H^2_c(U) ≅ H^2(E) = K(−1) (RD.5/top-compact-support-cohomology); H^1(E) is two dimensional by van der Put's computation (RD.5/van-der-put-legendre-computation) for Legendre curves, or by duality and the dimension formula; the eigenvalue relation from the pairing into K(−1).
3. (3) RD.5/kunneth-formula.

**Checks.**

- PARI/GP: for y^2 = x^3 − x over F_5, a_5 = −2, #E = 8, #U = 7 = q − (α + β); hyperellcharpoly (Kedlaya's Monsky–Washnitzer algorithm) gives T^2 + 2T + 5 (αβ = 5). For y^2 = x^3 − x + 1 over all good p ≤ 31, #U(F_p) = p − a_p.
- P^1 minus N points: q + 1 − N = q − (N − 1) = Tr(Φ | H^2_c) − Tr(Φ | H^1_c).

<a id="target-rd-5-rigid-cohomology-base-field-extension"></a>

### Rigid cohomology commutes with arbitrary extension of the base field

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.5/rigid-cohomology-base-field-extension` · theorem

Let k ⊂ k' be an arbitrary extension of fields of characteristic p, with Cohen rings W → W' and K → K' (complete discretely valued, residue fields k, k'). For a separated k-scheme X of finite type, the natural maps H^i_rig(X/K) ⊗_K K' → H^i_rig(X_{k'}/K') and H^i_{c,rig}(X/K) ⊗_K K' → H^i_{c,rig}(X_{k'}/K') are isomorphisms for all i.

**Hypotheses.**

- Constant coefficients, as in Berthelot's remark; for finite extensions and coefficients see RD.4/finite-flat-base-change.
- Both sides are finite dimensional (RD.5/finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology, RD.5/finiteness-of-compactly-supported-rigid-cohomology).

**Prerequisites.** [Localisation sequences for rigid cohomology with supports](#target-rd-4-localisation-sequence) (`RD.4/localisation-sequence`), [The excision long exact sequence for compact-support rigid cohomology](#target-rd-4-excision-sequence) (`RD.4/excision-sequence`), [The Gysin isomorphism for smooth liftable pairs](#target-rd-4-gysin-isomorphism) (`RD.4/gysin-isomorphism`), [Traces along finite étale maps and the averaging projector](#target-rd-5-finite-etale-trace-projector) (`RD.5/finite-etale-trace-projector`), [Poincaré duality for rigid cohomology with coefficients (Kedlaya, Theorem 1.2.3)](#target-rd-5-poincare-duality) (`RD.5/poincare-duality`), [Finite dimensionality of rigid cohomology with coefficients (Kedlaya, Theorem 1.2.1)](#target-rd-5-finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.5/finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology`), [Finite dimensionality of compact-support rigid cohomology (Kedlaya, Theorem 1.2.2)](#target-rd-5-finiteness-of-compactly-supported-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.5/finiteness-of-compactly-supported-rigid-cohomology`), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/de-jong-alteration-theorem`, [Base change of rigid cohomology along finite extensions of the coefficient field](#target-rd-4-finite-flat-base-change) (`RD.4/finite-flat-base-change`), [The rational rigid–crystalline comparison for smooth proper varieties](#target-rd-7-rigid-crystalline-comparison) (`RD.7/rigid-crystalline-comparison`), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.3/derived-base-change`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.3/proper-perfectness`.

**Sources.**

- [S73](#source-73), Remarque after 3.4, p. 6. States that the method of the duality and Künneth inductions proves that rigid cohomology commutes with an arbitrary extension of the base field.
- [S73](#source-73), Théorème 2.4 and its proof, p. 5. The double induction (a)_n, (b)_n with de Jong's theorem and the finite étale projector that the remark refers to.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Double induction on dimension exactly as for duality and Künneth (Berthelot Remarque after 3.4): (a)_n for smooth X of dimension ≤ n, (b)_n for cohomology with supports in Z of dimension ≤ n inside smooth X, using the localisation and excision triangles (RD.4/localisation-sequence, RD.4/excision-sequence), Gysin maps for liftable smooth pairs (RD.4/gysin-isomorphism), the proper smooth case through the crystalline comparison, and de Jong's alterations with the finite étale trace projector to pass from opens of proper smooth schemes to general smooth X (RD.5/finite-etale-trace-projector, SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/de-jong-alteration-theorem).
2. Proper smooth case: use CR.3/derived-base-change (the Noetherian p-complete PD-base form) and CR.3/proper-perfectness for the compatible Cohen-ring PD map W → W′. The present RD.7 comparison supplies the perfect-residue-field case only. Comparison for arbitrary imperfect k is a separate recorded gap, not a consequence of finite-flat base change.
3. Compact supports from the result for H_rig by Poincaré duality on smooth strata and excision.

**Checks.**

- For X = G_m both sides are K' in degrees 0 and 1.
- For X = P^1 the map identifies the classes of the hyperplane in degree 2.

<a id="target-rd-5-unipotent-monodromy-along-boundary"></a>

### Constant and unipotent monodromy along a boundary divisor; docile isocrystals

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.5/unipotent-monodromy-along-boundary` · definition

Let X ⊂ Y be an open immersion of smooth k-varieties with Z = Y \ X, and E an isocrystal on X overconvergent along Z. First, under Kedlaya's Hypothesis 4.3.2 (Y, X affine, Z smooth cut out by f with df a local basis direction, and a small frame), the tube of Z decomposes as ]Z[_Q × A^1_K[0, 1) and E restricts to a ∇-module on ]Z[_Q × A^1_K[λ, 1) for some λ < 1; E has constant (resp. unipotent) monodromy along Z if that restriction is constant (resp. admits an exhaustive filtration with constant quotients) as a log-∇-module relative to ]Z[_Q. In general, E has constant/unipotent monodromy along Z if this holds after every complete extension K'/K (residue field k') for every small frame enclosing an open V ⊂ Y in which V \ X is smooth and principal. When Y is smooth and proper and Z is a strict normal crossings divisor, an isocrystal (or F-isocrystal) on X overconvergent along Z with unipotent monodromy along Z is called docile; Isoc†(X)^doc denotes the full subcategory.

**Hypotheses.**

- Smooth X and Y; for k perfect it suffices to test on a dense open of each component of Z (Kedlaya Remark 4.4.3).
- Monodromy along a divisor is a codimension-one notion: removing a closed subset of codimension ≥ 2 from Y does not change it (Kedlaya Proposition 4.4.4).

**Prerequisites.** [The category Isoc†(X/K) of a separated finite type k-scheme](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-isocrystals-of-a-variety) (`RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystals-of-a-variety`), [Frames (X ⊂ Y ⊂ P)](#target-rd-3-frame) (`RD.3/frame`), [The tube ]T[_P of a locally closed subscheme](#target-rd-3-tube) (`RD.3/tube`), [Strong fibration theorem: strict neighbourhoods along smooth morphisms](#target-rd-3-strong-fibration-theorem) (`RD.3/strong-fibration-theorem`), [Unipotent ∇-modules over the Robba ring](#target-rd-2-unipotent-differential-module) (`RD.2/unipotent-differential-module`), [Unipotent ∇-modules are the modules V ⊗ R with nilpotent residue](#target-rd-2-unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue) (`RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue`), `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-snc-divisor`.

**Sources.**

- [S76](#source-76), Hypothesis 4.3.2, Lemma 4.3.3 and Definition 4.3.4, p. 41. Defines constant and unipotent monodromy along a smooth principal divisor through the tubular decomposition of its tube.
- [S76](#source-76), Definition 4.4.2, Remark 4.4.3 and Proposition 4.4.4, p. 43. Extends the definition to arbitrary boundaries by testing on all small frames after field extension, and shows its codimension-one nature.
- [S76](#source-76), Definitions 3.2.5–3.2.6 and Proposition 3.2.20, pp. 19–20, 24. Constant and unipotent log-∇-modules on products with polyannuli, and stability of unipotence under subquotients and tensor products.
- [S79](#source-79), Definition 4.4.1, p. 19. Calls an overconvergent isocrystal on the complement of a simple normal crossings divisor in a smooth proper variety docile when it has unipotent monodromy along the divisor.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- Kedlaya, Semistable reduction I, Theorem 5.2.1, p. 45: constant monodromy along X \ U is the criterion for extending an isocrystal from U to X
- Kedlaya, Semistable reduction I, Theorem 6.4.5, p. 56: unipotent monodromy along an SNC divisor is the criterion for a convergent log extension with nilpotent residues
- D'Addezio, Theorem 4.4.3 and §4.4.11, pp. 20, 23: docile isocrystals satisfy a Lefschetz theorem; semistable reduction reduces the minimal slope conjecture to the docile case
- RD.5/log-rigid-comparison-for-curves: unipotent monodromy at the cusps gives the log extension used for Igusa curves

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HasUnipotentMonodromy` |  | The predicate on E ∈ Isoc†(X, Y/K) of having unipotent monodromy along Z = Y \ X; HasConstantMonodromy likewise. |
| `HasUnipotentMonodromy.subquotient` |  | Unipotent monodromy is preserved by subobjects, quotients and extensions in Isoc†(X, Y/K). |
| `HasUnipotentMonodromy.tensor_dual` |  | Unipotent monodromy is preserved by ⊗, internal Hom and duals; docile isocrystals form an abelian tensor subcategory Isoc†(X)^doc closed under subquotients. |
| `HasUnipotentMonodromy.zariski_local` |  | E has unipotent monodromy along Z iff its restrictions to the members of an open cover of Y do. |
| `HasUnipotentMonodromy.of_dense_open_boundary` |  | If U ⊂ Y is open with U ∩ Z dense in Z, unipotence along Z is equivalent to unipotence along U ∩ Z. |
| `HasConstantMonodromy.of_convergent_extension` |  | If E extends to a convergent isocrystal on Y, it has constant monodromy along Z. |
| `HasUnipotentMonodromy.baseField` |  | Unipotence is invariant under complete extensions K'/K of the coefficient field. |
| `Docile.rankOne_unramified` |  | A docile rank-one overconvergent isocrystal has zero residues in its canonical nilpotent-residue logarithmic extension (D’Addezio, proof of Corollary 4.4.8). Other logarithmic lattices can shift residues by integers. |

**Unit tests.**

- `docile_constant` (degenerate): O_X is docile along every SNC divisor D.
- `docile_kummer_nonexample` (non-example): The Kummer isocrystal ∇ = d + (1/2)dt/t on G_m (p odd) is not docile along {0, ∞} in P^1, though it is quasi-unipotent.
- `docile_kummer_pullback` (computation): The pullback of ∇ = d + (1/2)dt/t along the cover s ↦ t = s^2 is (O, d + ds/s), in which s^{−1} times the basis vector is horizontal; so the pullback is isomorphic to O_{G_m} and docile. Assume p is odd; the resulting zero residues refer to the canonical logarithmic extension after the horizontal gauge transformation.
- `docile_dwork_nonexample` (non-example): The Dwork isocrystal on A^1 (∇ = d + π dt) is not docile along ∞ ⊂ P^1: its Swan conductor at ∞ is 1 (RD.1/dwork-exponential-module).
- `docile_tensor` (characterisation): If E and E' are docile along D then so are E ⊗ E', E^∨ and every subquotient of E in Isoc†(X).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Local definition: Kedlaya Lemma 4.3.3 (the tubular decomposition ]Z[_P ≅ ]Z[_Q × A^1[0, 1)) and Definition 4.3.4; constancy and unipotence of log-∇-modules on V × A^n_K(I): Kedlaya Definitions 3.2.5–3.2.6 with the structure theorem 3.3.4 (unipotent modules are U_I of a module with commuting nilpotent residues).
2. Global definition by testing on all small frames over all field extensions: Kedlaya Definition 4.4.2; independence of choices and Zariski locality: Kedlaya Remark 4.4.1 and the list before Definition 4.4.2.
3. Docility: D'Addezio Definition 4.4.1 (the same notion for a smooth proper compactification with simple normal crossings boundary).

**Checks.**

- The constant F-isocrystal O_X is docile for every SNC compactification.
- The Kummer isocrystal on G_m given by ∇ = d + a dt/t with a ∈ (q − 1)^{−1}ℤ \ ℤ is not docile along {0, ∞}, but its pullback along t ↦ t^{q−1} is.

<a id="target-rd-5-convergent-log-isocrystal"></a>

### Convergent log-isocrystals on a smooth pair

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.5/convergent-log-isocrystal` · definition

Let (X, Z) be a smooth pair over k (X smooth, Z a strict normal crossings divisor) with log structure M defined by Z, and suppose given a closed immersion i of X into a formal V-scheme P smooth near X with a log structure L defined by a relative normal crossings divisor lifting Z (Kedlaya's Hypothesis 6.1.6). A convergent log-isocrystal on (X, M) is a coherent module E on the log tube ]X[^log_P with an isomorphism ε: π_2^*E ≅ π_1^*E on the log tube of the diagonal ]X[^log_{P(1)} satisfying Δ^*ε = id and the cocycle condition on ]X[^log_{P(2)}. Equivalently it is a coherent module on the tube with a convergent integrable log connection Ω^1(log) (Kedlaya Theorem 6.4.1); the residues along the components of Z are endomorphisms of the restrictions; a log-F-isocrystal adds a Frobenius isomorphism. The category is independent of i and agrees with Shiho's convergent log-isocrystals.

**Hypotheses.**

- Smooth pair (X, Z) with Z strict normal crossings.
- Frobenius structures where stated.

**Prerequisites.** [The tube ]T[_P of a locally closed subscheme](#target-rd-3-tube) (`RD.3/tube`), [Frames (X ⊂ Y ⊂ P)](#target-rd-3-frame) (`RD.3/frame`), [Restriction from overconvergent to convergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-3-restriction-to-convergent) (`RD.3/restriction-to-convergent`), `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/log-de-rham-complex`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-snc-divisor`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5/log-crystal`.

**Sources.**

- [S76](#source-76), Hypothesis 6.1.6, Definitions 6.1.4 and 6.1.7, Remark 6.1.5, p. 51. Defines log tubes and convergent log-isocrystals by a stratification on the log tube of the diagonal, independent of the embedding by Shiho's results.
- [S76](#source-76), Theorem 6.4.1, p. 55. Equivalence between convergent log-isocrystals and convergent log-∇-modules under Hypothesis 6.2.1.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- Kedlaya, Semistable reduction I, Theorem 6.4.5, p. 56: the target category of the log extension of a unipotent isocrystal
- Kedlaya, Semistable reduction IV, Theorem 2.4.4, p. 17: semistable reduction produces a convergent log-F-isocrystal with nilpotent residues after alteration
- RD.5/log-rigid-comparison-for-curves: the log de Rham complex of a convergent log-isocrystal computes log-rigid cohomology

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ConvergentLogIsocrystal` |  | The category of convergent log-isocrystals on a smooth pair (X, Z); with Frobenius, ConvergentLogFIsocrystal. |
| `ConvergentLogIsocrystal.toLogNablaModule` |  | Under Hypothesis 6.2.1 the category is equivalent to convergent log-∇-modules on the tube (Kedlaya Theorem 6.4.1). |
| `ConvergentLogIsocrystal.residue` |  | For each component Z_j of Z, the residue res_j(E) ∈ End(E\|_{]Z_j[}), compatible with restriction and tensor products (res(E ⊗ E') = res E ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ res E'). |
| `ConvergentLogIsocrystal.restrict` |  | Restriction to the complement gives an isocrystal on X \ Z overconvergent along Z. |
| `ConvergentLogIsocrystal.noBoundary` |  | For Z = ∅ the category is that of convergent isocrystals on X. |
| `ConvergentLogIsocrystal.nilpotentResidues` |  | The full subcategory with nilpotent residues is an abelian tensor subcategory; a convergent log-F-isocrystal automatically has nilpotent residues. |
| `ConvergentLogIsocrystal.pullback_id_comp` |  | Pullback along morphisms of smooth log pairs preserves the logarithmic stratification; identity and composition agree via canonical isomorphisms, and commute with restriction to the complement. |
| `ConvergentLogIsocrystal.tensor_unit_dual` |  | The unit has zero connection and residues. Tensor products add residues; duals negate their transposes. These operations preserve convergence and nilpotent residues; morphism equality is detected after forgetting to the coherent module on a covering of tubes. |
| `ConvergentLogIsocrystal.ofStratification` |  | A coherent module on a covering of log tubes with a convergent log-stratification, identity on the diagonal and cocycle on the triple log tube defines a log-isocrystal; compatible morphisms glue uniquely. The log Taylor equivalence constructs this from a convergent integrable log connection. |

**Unit tests.**

- `convergentLogIsocrystal_empty_boundary` (degenerate): For Z = ∅ a convergent log-isocrystal is a convergent isocrystal (no residues).
- `convergentLogIsocrystal_residue_computation` (computation): On (A^1,{0}), for a ∈ Z_p ⊂ K, (O,d + a dt/t) is log-convergent and has residue a; a = 0 gives the unit object. For p odd, a = 1/2 gives a nonzero rank-one residue without Frobenius.
- `convergentLogFIsocrystal_nilpotent` (characterisation): A log-F-isocrystal has nilpotent residues: for q-power Frobenius with coefficient action σ, NΦ = qΦσ(N). The characteristic-polynomial coefficients satisfy c_j = q^jσ(c_j); σ is isometric and |q| < 1, so c_j = 0 for j > 0. Linear conjugacy to qN is the special case σ = id.
- `convergentLogIsocrystal_not_overconvergent_nonexample` (non-example): The restriction of a convergent log-isocrystal to X \ Z need not have unipotent monodromy unless the residues are nilpotent: (O, d + (1/2)dt/t) restricts to a non-docile Kummer isocrystal on G_m. Here p is odd, so 1/2 ∈ Z_p and the log-convergence hypothesis is satisfied.
- `convergentLogIsocrystal_integrable_not_convergent` (non-example): The integral log connection d + (1/p)dt/t is not a convergent log-isocrystal: in (1+u)^{1/p}, the n-th coefficient has valuation −n−v_p(n!), so the convergence radius is p^{−1−1/(p−1)} < 1. Integrability alone is insufficient.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Log tubes and the log diagonal: Kedlaya Definition 6.1.4 (after Shiho §2.2), with Remark 6.1.5 on existence of the embedding data.
2. Definition 6.1.7 with Shiho's Proposition 2.2.7 for independence of choices.
3. Equivalence with convergent log-∇-modules on the tube: Kedlaya Theorem 6.4.1 (via the log Taylor isomorphism).

**Checks.**

- For Z = ∅, convergent log-isocrystals are convergent isocrystals.
- For (A^1,{0}), (O,d + a dt/t) with a ∈ Z_p ⊂ K is a convergent log-isocrystal with residue a: its logarithmic Taylor series is (1+u)^a, convergent for |u| < 1. An arbitrary a ∈ K need not be log-convergent.

<a id="target-rd-5-extension-across-boundary"></a>

### Kedlaya's extension theorem: constant monodromy is the obstruction to extending an overconvergent isocrystal

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.5/extension-across-boundary` · theorem

Let U ⊂ X ⊂ Y be open immersions of k-varieties with X smooth and U dense in Y, and E an isocrystal on U overconvergent along Y \ U. (a) E extends to an isocrystal on X overconvergent along Y \ X iff E has constant monodromy along X \ U; the restriction functor Isoc†(X, Y/K) → Isoc†(U, Y/K) is fully faithful, so the extension is unique. (b) If E is an isocrystal on X overconvergent along Y \ X and F ⊂ E|_U a sub-isocrystal overconvergent along Y \ U, then F is the restriction of a sub-isocrystal of E over X. (c) If X \ U has codimension ≥ 2 in X, restriction Isoc†(X, Y/K) → Isoc†(U, Y/K) is an equivalence.

**Hypotheses.**

- X smooth; for singular X purity fails (Kedlaya Remark 5.3.4: a rank-one connection on the quadric cone).
- No Frobenius structure is needed.

**Prerequisites.** [Constant and unipotent monodromy along a boundary divisor; docile isocrystals](#target-rd-5-unipotent-monodromy-along-boundary) (`RD.5/unipotent-monodromy-along-boundary`), [The category Isoc†(X/K) of a separated finite type k-scheme](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-isocrystals-of-a-variety) (`RD.3/overconvergent-isocrystals-of-a-variety`), [Strong fibration theorem: strict neighbourhoods along smooth morphisms](#target-rd-3-strong-fibration-theorem) (`RD.3/strong-fibration-theorem`), [Unipotent ∇-modules are the modules V ⊗ R with nilpotent residue](#target-rd-2-unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue) (`RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue`), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/modification`.

**Sources.**

- [S76](#source-76), Theorem 5.2.1 and its proof, pp. 45–47. Constant monodromy along X \ U is equivalent to extendability; restriction is fully faithful.
- [S76](#source-76), Proposition 5.3.1, Proposition 5.3.3 and Remark 5.3.4, p. 48. Extension of sub-isocrystals, purity in codimension two, and the smoothness hypothesis.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a) Kedlaya Theorem 5.2.1: if X \ U is a smooth divisor, reduce by blow-ups centred outside X and Zariski localisation to the situation of Lemma 5.1.1, where constancy on V ∩ ]X \ U[ (via the tubular decomposition and Proposition 3.5.3) lets one extend across the tube of X \ U by Theorem 3.3.4; overconvergence of the extension is checked by η-convergence (Proposition 2.5.6). The general case reduces to the smooth divisor case by removing codimension-two loci (Proposition 4.4.4).
2. (b) Kedlaya Proposition 5.3.1: F has constant monodromy along X \ U as a subobject (Proposition 3.2.20), so extends to G; the inclusion G → E extends by full faithfulness.
3. (c) Kedlaya Proposition 5.3.3: constant monodromy along a codimension-two locus is automatic.

**Checks.**

- For U = G_m ⊂ X = A^1 ⊂ Y = P^1 and the overconvergent rank-one connection d + a dt/t with a ∈ Z_p ⊂ K, extension to A^1 overconvergently along ∞ occurs iff a ∈ Z. The overconvergence assumption is essential.
- For p odd, on the cone z² = xy minus its vertex, glue rank-one modules on D(x) and D(y) by v_y = (z/x)v_x, with ∇v_x = v_x dx/(2x) and ∇v_y = v_y dy/(2y). These connections agree on the overlap since 2dz/z = dx/x + dy/y. This is Kedlaya’s nonextendable isocrystal of Remark 5.3.4; the bundle is not presented by one global basis. The vertex has codimension two, so smoothness is needed for purity.

<a id="target-rd-5-log-extension-of-unipotent-isocrystal"></a>

### Logarithmic extension of isocrystals with unipotent monodromy

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.5/log-extension-of-unipotent-isocrystal` · theorem

Let U ⊂ X be an open immersion of smooth k-varieties with Z = X \ U a strict normal crossings divisor, and E an isocrystal on U overconvergent along Z. Then E has unipotent monodromy along Z iff E extends to a convergent log-isocrystal with nilpotent residues on (X, Z). The restriction functor from convergent log-isocrystals with nilpotent residues on (X, Z) to Isoc†(U, X/K) is fully faithful, so the extension is unique; Frobenius structures extend uniquely, so the same holds for F-isocrystals.

**Hypotheses.**

- Strict normal crossings boundary; smooth X.

**Prerequisites.** [Constant and unipotent monodromy along a boundary divisor; docile isocrystals](#target-rd-5-unipotent-monodromy-along-boundary) (`RD.5/unipotent-monodromy-along-boundary`), [Convergent log-isocrystals on a smooth pair](#target-rd-5-convergent-log-isocrystal) (`RD.5/convergent-log-isocrystal`), [Kedlaya's extension theorem: constant monodromy is the obstruction to extending an overconvergent isocrystal](#target-rd-5-extension-across-boundary) (`RD.5/extension-across-boundary`), [Unipotent ∇-modules are the modules V ⊗ R with nilpotent residue](#target-rd-2-unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue) (`RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue`), [Overconvergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-f-isocrystal) (`RD.3/overconvergent-f-isocrystal`).

**Sources.**

- [S76](#source-76), Theorem 6.4.5 and its proof, p. 56. Unipotent monodromy along an SNC divisor is equivalent to the existence of a convergent log-isocrystal extension with nilpotent residues; restriction is fully faithful.
- [S76](#source-76), Theorem 3.3.4, p. 27. The functor U_I from modules on the base with commuting nilpotent residues to unipotent log-∇-modules on the base times a polyannulus is an equivalence, which lets a unipotent module extend across the polydisc.
- [S78](#source-78), Remark 2.4.2, p. 16. Uses Theorem 6.4.5 of part I to log-extend near the centre of a valuation, with unique extension of the Frobenius structure.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Zariski-local on X; under Hypothesis 6.2.1 the claim combines Kedlaya Proposition 6.3.2 (unipotent ∇-modules near Z are unipotent log-∇-modules, extendable across the tube of Z by Theorem 3.3.4) with Theorem 6.4.1 (log-∇-modules versus convergent log-isocrystals) (Kedlaya Theorem 6.4.5).
2. Full faithfulness: a horizontal section of a log-∇-module with nilpotent residues on the punctured tube extends across the tube (Theorem 3.3.4: unipotent objects are U_I of their fibre).
3. Frobenius: the extension of Φ: F^*E ≅ E is the unique extension of a morphism (full faithfulness).

**Checks.**

- For (A^1, {0}) and the unipotent rank-two isocrystal on G_m with ∇ = d + N dt/t, N nilpotent, the extension is the same formula on the disc.
- The Kummer isocrystal (O, d + (1/2)dt/t) on G_m is not unipotent along 0; its natural extension to A^1 has residue 1/2, not nilpotent, matching the 'only if'.

<a id="target-rd-5-log-rigid-comparison-for-curves"></a>

### Log-rigid cohomology of a curve with unipotent monodromy equals rigid cohomology of the complement

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.5/log-rigid-comparison-for-curves` · theorem

Let Y be a smooth curve over a perfect field k, Z ⊂ Y a finite set of k-rational points, and E ∈ F-Isoc†(Y \ Z/K) with unipotent monodromy along Z, with log extension E^log (a convergent log-F-isocrystal on (Y, Z) with nilpotent residues N_z, RD.5/log-extension-of-unipotent-isocrystal). Define the log-rigid cohomology H^i_{log-rig}((Y, Z)/K, E^log) as the hypercohomology of the overconvergent log de Rham complex E^log ⊗ Ω^•(log Z) on the tube of Y. Then the restriction map H^i_{log-rig}((Y, Z)/K, E^log) → H^i_rig(Y \ Z/K, E) is a Frobenius-compatible isomorphism for every i; in particular the log-rigid cohomology is finite dimensional.

**Hypotheses.**

- Unipotent monodromy along Z; without it the log extension with nilpotent residues does not exist, and for residues with nonzero integer eigenvalues the comparison fails.
- Rational points of Z (otherwise pass to a finite extension of k; RD.4/finite-flat-base-change).

**Prerequisites.** [Logarithmic extension of isocrystals with unipotent monodromy](#target-rd-5-log-extension-of-unipotent-isocrystal) (`RD.5/log-extension-of-unipotent-isocrystal`), [Finite dimensionality of rigid cohomology of an overconvergent F-isocrystal on a smooth affine curve](#target-rd-5-finiteness-for-affine-curves) (`RD.5/finiteness-for-affine-curves`), [Finite dimensionality of rigid cohomology with coefficients (Kedlaya, Theorem 1.2.1)](#target-rd-5-finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.5/finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology`), [For a unipotent module over R_K, ∇ is an isomorphism modulo the plus-part lattice](#target-rd-5-unipotent-local-residue-isomorphism) (`RD.5/unipotent-local-residue-isomorphism`), [Unipotent ∇-modules are the modules V ⊗ R with nilpotent residue](#target-rd-2-unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue) (`RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue`), [Residues and antiderivatives on the Robba ring](#target-rd-2-robba-ring-antiderivative) (`RD.2/robba-ring-antiderivative`), [Berthelot's functor j† and the overconvergent de Rham complex of a frame](#target-rd-4-overconvergent-de-rham-complex) (`RD.4/overconvergent-de-rham-complex`), [Base change of rigid cohomology along finite extensions of the coefficient field](#target-rd-4-finite-flat-base-change) (`RD.4/finite-flat-base-change`), `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/log-de-rham-complex`.

**Sources.**

- [S80](#source-80), Proof of Proposition 5.1.7, p. 54. Identifies the Igusa theta-cokernel with log-rigid cohomology of a log F-isocrystal on compactified Igusa curves and deduces finiteness from general finiteness of rigid cohomology.
- [S76](#source-76), Theorem 3.3.4, p. 27. The functor U_I, which equips the pullback of a module on the base with the connection twisted by commuting nilpotent residues N_i dt_i/t_i, is an equivalence onto unipotent log-∇-modules on the base times a polyannulus or polydisc.
- [S76](#source-76), Theorem 6.4.5, p. 56. Unipotent monodromy along a strict normal crossings divisor is equivalent to a convergent log-isocrystal extension with nilpotent residues, and the extension is unique.
- [S4](#source-4), Section 6.4, pp. 41–42. Finite dimensionality on curves via the local unipotent computation at the missing points.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Cover the tube of Y by a strict neighbourhood U_1 of the tube of Y \ Z and the residue discs U_2 = ⊔_z ]z[; U_1 ∩ U_2 is a union of annulus germs at the boundaries of the discs. The Mayer–Vietoris sequence for the log de Rham complex reads … → H^i_{log-rig}(Y) → H^i(U_1, E) ⊕ H^i_log(U_2, E^log) → H^i(U_1 ∩ U_2, E) → …, and H^*(U_1, E) = H^*_rig(Y \ Z, E) (RD.4/overconvergent-de-rham-complex).
2. On a residue disc, E^log is isomorphic to a constant module with log connection d + N_z dt/t (Kedlaya, Semistable reduction I, Theorem 3.3.4, the logarithmic form of RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue); for n ≥ 1 the operator n + N_z is invertible, so H^0_log = ker N_z and H^1_log = coker N_z, coming from the t^0 terms (antiderivatives, RD.2/robba-ring-antiderivative).
3. On an annulus germ (the Robba ring), the same constant form gives H^0 = ker N_z and H^1 = coker N_z, since n + N_z is invertible for every n ≠ 0 (RD.5/unipotent-local-residue-isomorphism); the restriction from the disc is an isomorphism on these t^0 terms.
4. Hence the disc terms cancel the annulus terms in the Mayer–Vietoris sequence, and restriction to U_1 is an isomorphism; finiteness follows from RD.5/finiteness-for-affine-curves (Y \ Z affine) or RD.5/finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology.

**Checks.**

- Y = A^1, Z = {0}, E = O: the log complex K⟨t⟩† → K⟨t⟩† dt/t has H^0 = K and H^1 = K·dt/t, which is H^*_rig(G_m), not H^*_rig(A^1) = (K, 0): log cohomology of (A^1, {0}) is the cohomology of the complement.
- Y = A^1, Z = {0}, E of rank two with ∇ = d + N dt/t, N a nonzero nilpotent 2 × 2 matrix: H^0 = ker N = K and H^1 = coker N = K on both sides.
- Non-example: the rank-one log connection d + dt/t (residue 1, not nilpotent) on (A^1, {0}) has log-rigid cohomology 0 in both degrees (t^n ↦ (n + 1)t^n dt/t is bijective for n ≥ 0), while its restriction to G_m is isomorphic to O via multiplication by t, with cohomology (K, K); residues with integer eigenvalues other than 0 must be excluded.

<a id="target-rd-5-igusa-theta-cokernel-finite"></a>

### Acceptance: finite-level Igusa rigid cohomology with Sym^k coefficients is finite dimensional

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.5/igusa-theta-cokernel-finite` · application

For k ≥ 0, n ≥ 0 and tame level K^p, the space H^1_rig(Ig(K^pΓ(p^n)), Sym^k) of Pan, Definition 5.1.6 (the cokernel of θ^{k+1}: M†_{−k} → M†_{k+2} ⊗ D_0^{−k−1} at level K^pΓ(p^n)), once identified at RD.4 with the log-rigid cohomology of the ordinary locus of the compactified Igusa curves at that level, with log poles at the cusps and coefficients Sym^k of the log-F-isocrystal H^1 of the universal generalised elliptic curve, is finite dimensional. The finite dimension is over Pan’s coefficient field C = C_p; the K-valued rigid complex is extended algebraically to C.

**Hypotheses.**

- The identification of the theta-cokernel with log-rigid cohomology is an RD.4 target (Pan Definition 5.1.6, after Coleman); this node only proves finiteness.
- The overconvergence of R^1f_*O of the universal ordinary elliptic curve along the supersingular points and its unipotent (Tate curve) monodromy at the cusps are RD.3 inputs (Étesse's overconvergence of abelian-scheme direct images).
- Igusa curves at level K^pΓ(p^n) in characteristic p are the Igusa components of ModularCurvesPartII:R13.5/igusa-components.
- Fix both n and K^p. The field C is not a discretely valued coefficient field; use algebraic scalar extension of the finite-dimensional K-cohomology, rather than applying the arbitrary-Cohen-field theorem to C.

**Prerequisites.** [Log-rigid cohomology of a curve with unipotent monodromy equals rigid cohomology of the complement](#target-rd-5-log-rigid-comparison-for-curves) (`RD.5/log-rigid-comparison-for-curves`), [Logarithmic extension of isocrystals with unipotent monodromy](#target-rd-5-log-extension-of-unipotent-isocrystal) (`RD.5/log-extension-of-unipotent-isocrystal`), [Finite dimensionality of rigid cohomology of an overconvergent F-isocrystal on a smooth affine curve](#target-rd-5-finiteness-for-affine-curves) (`RD.5/finiteness-for-affine-curves`), [The dimension of H^1_rig of a smooth affine curve with constant coefficients](#target-rd-5-dimension-of-h1-of-affine-curve) (`RD.5/dimension-of-h1-of-affine-curve`), `ModularCurvesPartII:R13.5/igusa-components`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3`, `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4`.

**Sources.**

- [S80](#source-80), Definition 5.1.6 and Proposition 5.1.7, pp. 53–54. Defines the theta-cokernel spaces at finite level and in the limit, and proves finite dimensionality at finite level by Coleman's log-rigid interpretation and general finiteness.
- [S80](#source-80), Proposition 5.1.8, p. 54. Uses the finiteness to get closed images of θ^{k+1} and to describe the cokernel at infinity.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Sym^k H^1 is an overconvergent F-isocrystal on the ordinary locus minus the cusps with unipotent monodromy at the cusps, hence log-extendable with nilpotent residues (RD.5/log-extension-of-unipotent-isocrystal).
2. By RD.5/log-rigid-comparison-for-curves the log-rigid cohomology is H^1_rig of the ordinary locus minus the cusps, a smooth affine curve, which is finite dimensional (RD.5/finiteness-for-affine-curves).
3. After the RD.4 identification, extend the finite-dimensional K-cohomology algebraically to C (flat scalar extension). This yields the C-finiteness of Pan Proposition 5.1.7; it makes no claim about the dimension of the colimit over n.

**Checks.**

- For k = 0 the space is H^1_rig of the ordinary locus minus the cusps; on a geometrically connected component of genus g with s supersingular and c cuspidal geometric points its dimension is 2g + s + c − 1 (RD.5/dimension-of-h1-of-affine-curve).
- The conclusion is levelwise. Pan Proposition 5.1.8 describes a smooth Borel action on the colimit over n; it supplies neither a uniform dimension bound nor a finiteness/nonfiniteness conclusion for that colimit.

<a id="target-rd-5-finiteness-for-smooth-quasi-projective-models"></a>

### Finite rigid and dagger cohomology for smooth quasi-projective integral models and their boundary strata

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.5/finiteness-for-smooth-quasi-projective-models` · theorem

Let K be a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_K and residue field k, and 𝒴 a smooth quasi-projective O_K-scheme with special fibre Y and dagger tube 𝒴^† (the dagger space structure on the tube ]Y[ inside the analytification of the generic fibre). (a) H^i_rig(Y/K) is finite dimensional for every i, the Frobenius of RD.4 is bijective on it, and, through the comparison H^i_rig(Y/K) ≅ H^i(𝒴^†, Ω^•) of Grosse-Klönne's Theorem 5.1 (an RD.4 target), the dagger de Rham cohomology of the tube is finite dimensional, functorially in morphisms of smooth quasi-projective models. (b) If 𝒳 is smooth quasi-projective over O_K with a relative strict normal crossings divisor 𝒟 whose strata 𝒟^{(j)} (disjoint unions of j-fold intersections) are smooth quasi-projective, then every first-quadrant spectral sequence with E_1^{i,j} = H^i_rig(D^{(j)}/K), Frobenius-compatible with the induced differentials (such as the boundary-stratum sequence of Harris–Lan–Taylor–Thorne, Lemma 6.21), has finite-dimensional abutment on which the abutting Frobenius is bijective.

**Hypotheses.**

- Smooth quasi-projective models: the comparison needs the tube of the special fibre inside the generic fibre of the closure in a projective space, not the whole generic fibre (HLTT Lemma 6.8).
- Constant coefficients, as in the source; coefficients would need the comparison with coefficients.

**Prerequisites.** [Finite dimensionality of rigid cohomology with coefficients (Kedlaya, Theorem 1.2.1)](#target-rd-5-finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.5/finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology`), [Frobenius is bijective on rigid cohomology](#target-rd-5-frobenius-bijective-on-cohomology) (`RD.5/frobenius-bijective-on-cohomology`), `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.4`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-algebra`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F1/compact-support-log-complex`.

**Sources.**

- [S81](#source-81), Lemma 6.8, pp. 189–190. For smooth quasi-projective models identifies rigid cohomology of the special fibre with de Rham cohomology of the dagger tube, functorially, via Grosse-Klönne's Theorem 5.1.
- [S81](#source-81), Lemma 6.21 and Corollary 6.22, p. 207. Computes the boundary-supported dagger cohomology by a spectral sequence from the rigid cohomology of boundary strata and deduces finite dimensionality from Berthelot's finiteness theorem.
- [S82](#source-82), Theorem 5.1, p. 23. For a proper admissible formal scheme and an immersion of Y into its special fibre, compares coherent and de Rham cohomology of the dagger space on the tube with j†-cohomology, hence with rigid cohomology when the formal scheme is smooth along Y.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a) Finiteness of H_rig of the separated finite-type k-scheme Y: RD.5/finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology; bijectivity of Frobenius: RD.5/frobenius-bijective-on-cohomology.
2. The dagger–rigid comparison (Grosse-Klönne Theorem 5.1 (c), applied to the closure of 𝒴 in a projective space, with functoriality as explained in HLTT Lemma 6.8) is planned at RD.4; the finiteness transfers through it.
3. (b) Each E_1 term is finite dimensional by (a) applied to the strata, only finitely many are nonzero in each total degree (D^{(j)} is empty for j > dim, and H^i_rig vanishes for i > 2 dim), so the abutment is finite dimensional; Frobenius acts compatibly on the filtration with bijective graded pieces, hence bijectively (HLTT Corollary 6.22).

**Checks.**

- 𝒴 = A^n_{O_K}: H^0 = K and the dagger tube is the overconvergent closed polydisc with H^i_dR = 0 for i > 0.
- 𝒳 = P^1_{O_K} with 𝒟 = {0, ∞}: E_1 has H^*_rig(P^1) and K^2 in the row j = 1, abutment the compactly supported (toward 𝒟) cohomology of G_m, of total dimension 2.

<a id="target-rd-5-relative-convergent-crystalline-comparison"></a>

### Relative convergent cohomology equals rational relative crystalline cohomology, and is perfect

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.5/relative-convergent-crystalline-comparison` · lemma

Let W be a Cohen ring of k, K = W[1/p], and (B,M_B) a p-adic fine log formal scheme separated and topologically of finite type over Spf W. Work in Shiho’s category of separated topologically finite-type fine log (formal) B-schemes. Let f: (X,M_X) → (Y,M_Y) be a proper, log smooth and integral morphism of fine log B_1-schemes, where B_1 = B ⊗ Z/pZ; let Y → (𝒴,M_𝒴) be an exact closed immersion defined by pO_𝒴 with its canonical PD structure, and let E be a locally free isocrystal on (X/𝒴)^log_conv. If Φ(E) is its associated locally free log crystalline isocrystal, there is a natural quasi-isomorphism Rf_{X/𝒴,conv*}E ≅ Rf_{X/𝒴,crys*}Φ(E), and the convergent complex is perfect over Q ⊗ O_𝒴. For trivial logs and a point base this recovers convergent–rational-crystalline comparison. If an integral crystal F with F[1/p] ≅ Φ(E) is separately given, the right side can be written Rf_crys*F[1/p]; such a lattice is not part of the hypothesis.

**Hypotheses.**

- Proper log smooth integral f, locally free isocrystal coefficients and the Noetherian p-adic fine-log base just specified (Shiho conventions, pp. 3–5).
- A locally free crystalline isocrystal need not arise from a locally free integral crystal (Shiho §1, p. 4); use isocrystal perfectness, not only integral-crystal perfectness. The relative sites and log perfectness are the explicit gap/request below.

**Prerequisites.** `CrystallineCohomology:CR.3/proper-perfectness`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2/crystalline-cohomology`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5/log-crystal`, [Convergent log-isocrystals on a smooth pair](#target-rd-5-convergent-log-isocrystal) (`RD.5/convergent-log-isocrystal`), [Restriction from overconvergent to convergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-3-restriction-to-convergent) (`RD.3/restriction-to-convergent`), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5`.

**Sources.**

- [S66](#source-66), Theorem 2.36 and Corollary 2.37, p. 31. Relative log convergent cohomology of a locally free isocrystal is quasi-isomorphic to rational relative log crystalline cohomology and is a perfect complex.
- [S64](#source-64), Proof of Theorem 6.13, p. 61. Uses Shiho's Theorem 2.36 and Corollary 2.37 (with Ogus's Theorem 0.7.7 over a point) for perfectness and for the comparison on p-torsion-free PD thickenings.
- [S66](#source-66), Conventions, pp. 3–4; diagram (1.1), p. 5; Theorem 1.16, p. 9 (proof ends p. 11). Specifies the Noetherian fine-log bases and the canonical PD immersion; proves proper log crystalline perfectness for locally free isocrystals, without requiring an integral locally free crystal.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Shiho Theorem 2.36: with an embedding into a log smooth formal scheme, both sides are computed by de Rham complexes of the same module, on the log tube and on the p-adically completed log PD envelope; the map is the specialisation map, an isomorphism after reduction to the case where the embedding is an isomorphism; in general use embedding systems.
2. Perfectness follows from Shiho Corollary 2.37 and the log crystalline isocrystal perfectness of Theorem 1.16. CR.3/proper-perfectness supplies the trivial-log integral case only; request the general log isocrystal theorem from CR.5.

**Checks.**

- For f the identity, both sides are E.
- For X → Spec k proper smooth and E = O, this is H^*_conv(X/K) = H^*_crys(X/W)[1/p].

<a id="target-rd-5-convergent-direct-image-smooth-proper"></a>

### Higher direct images of convergent F-isocrystals under smooth proper morphisms (Xu)

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.5/convergent-direct-image-smooth-proper` · theorem

Let k be perfect and g: X → Y a smooth proper morphism of k-schemes locally of finite type. For every convergent isocrystal (resp. F-isocrystal) E on X/W, the higher direct images R^ig_{conv*}E are convergent isocrystals (resp. F-isocrystals) on Y/W; the Frobenius structure of R^ig_*E is induced by the natural isomorphism F_Y^*Rg_*E ≅ Rg_*(F_X^*E) composed with the Frobenius of E.

**Hypotheses.**

- Perfect k; smooth proper g. Neither a lift of Frobenius nor a lift of g is assumed.

**Prerequisites.** [Restriction from overconvergent to convergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-3-restriction-to-convergent) (`RD.3/restriction-to-convergent`), [Relative convergent cohomology equals rational relative crystalline cohomology, and is perfect](#target-rd-5-relative-convergent-crystalline-comparison) (`RD.5/relative-convergent-crystalline-comparison`), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.1/isocrystal`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.3/proper-perfectness`.

**Sources.**

- [S83](#source-83), Theorem 1.9, p. 3 (Corollary 9.3, p. 32, in the body). The higher direct image of a convergent isocrystal or F-isocrystal under a smooth proper morphism of k-schemes is a convergent isocrystal or F-isocrystal.
- [S83](#source-83), Theorem 1.5, Corollaries 1.6 and 1.8, pp. 2–3. Frobenius descent and the de Rham comparison used in the proof.
- [S64](#source-64), Proof of Theorem 6.13 (i), p. 61. Cites Xu's results (published numbering Corollary 8.3, Theorem 3.22) for convergence and the Frobenius structure.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Xu Theorem 1.9 (§9.3): Frobenius descent for convergent isocrystals via an Oyama-type site-theoretic Cartier transform (Theorem 1.5 (6.6), Corollary 1.6 (6.7)), comparison of de Rham complexes (Corollary 1.8 (6.9)), and Ogus's description of the direct image of the structure sheaf by relative crystalline cohomology to obtain coherence and convergence.
2. Frobenius structure: by base change for the Frobenius of Y and the Frobenius of E (Xu Proposition 5.10 and §9.3).

**Checks.**

- For g = id the direct image is E.
- For g: E → B an elliptic curve over an ordinary-locus base and E = O, R^1g_*O is the rank-two convergent F-isocrystal of the family, with the unit-root subobject of RD.5/dense-open-restriction-fully-faithful's second acceptance test.

<a id="target-rd-5-convergent-direct-image-perfect-complexes"></a>

### Smooth proper direct images of crystals in perfect complexes underlying F-isocrystals (Guo–Reinecke)

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.5/convergent-direct-image-perfect-complexes` · theorem

Let f: Z_1 → Z_2 be a smooth proper morphism of smooth O_K/p-schemes, f_s: Z_{1,s} → Z_{2,s} the induced map of reduced special fibres, and E' a crystal in perfect complexes on Z_{1,crys} underlying an F-isocrystal (E'[1/p], φ_{E'}) after inverting p. (i) Rf_{s,crys*}E'[1/p] underlies a convergent F-isocrystal in perfect complexes on Z_{2,crys}. (ii) For every p-complete p-torsion-free divided power thickening (A, A/J) in Z_{2,crys} there is a natural isomorphism Rf_{s,crys*}E'[1/p](A, A/J) ≅ RΓ((Z_{1,A/J}/A)_crys, E')[1/p], where the left side is the value of the associated convergent crystal of complexes.

**Hypotheses.**

- Smooth proper f; E' a crystal in perfect complexes (not only a vector bundle); integrality is used only to bound the crystalline cohomology.
- Absolute finiteness of rigid cohomology does not imply this relative statement; it is a separate input for consumers working over PD thickenings.

**Prerequisites.** [Higher direct images of convergent F-isocrystals under smooth proper morphisms (Xu)](#target-rd-5-convergent-direct-image-smooth-proper) (`RD.5/convergent-direct-image-smooth-proper`), [Relative convergent cohomology equals rational relative crystalline cohomology, and is perfect](#target-rd-5-relative-convergent-crystalline-comparison) (`RD.5/relative-convergent-crystalline-comparison`), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.3/proper-perfectness`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.1/crystal`, [Restriction from overconvergent to convergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-3-restriction-to-convergent) (`RD.3/restriction-to-convergent`), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5`.

**Sources.**

- [S64](#source-64), Theorem 6.13 and its proof, pp. 60–61. States and proves that the rational crystalline direct image of a crystal in perfect complexes underlying an F-isocrystal is a convergent F-isocrystal in perfect complexes whose values on p-torsion-free PD thickenings are rational crystalline cohomology.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (i) Perfectness of the restriction to p-torsion-free thickenings: RD.5/relative-convergent-crystalline-comparison (Shiho), after filtering E'[1/p] by its cohomology isocrystals; convergence and Frobenius structure: RD.5/convergent-direct-image-smooth-proper (Xu), with φ given by base change.
2. (ii) On a p-torsion-free PD thickening, the integral crystalline cohomology of the proper smooth Z_{1,A/J} is bounded (CrystallineCohomology:CR.3/proper-perfectness), so rational crystalline equals convergent cohomology there (RD.5/relative-convergent-crystalline-comparison; Ogus over a point).

**Checks.**

- For f = id and E' = O, both sides are A[1/p].
- For f a smooth proper curve over a smooth base and E' = O, the value at a p-torsion-free thickening is relative crystalline H^*(Z_1/A)[1/p], of ranks 1, 2g, 1.

<a id="target-rd-5-dense-open-restriction-fully-faithful"></a>

### Restriction of F-isocrystals to a dense open is fully faithful, and closed under subquotients in the overconvergent case

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.5/dense-open-restriction-fully-faithful` · theorem

Let X be a smooth variety over a perfect field k and U ⊂ X a dense open. (i) The restriction functor F-Isoc(X) → F-Isoc(U) on convergent F-isocrystals is fully faithful. (ii) The restriction functor F-Isoc†(X) → F-Isoc†(U) on overconvergent F-isocrystals is fully faithful, and its essential image is closed under subquotients: every overconvergent sub-F-isocrystal of E|_U is the restriction of a sub-F-isocrystal of E. (iii) More generally, for U smooth dense in X, the restriction F-Isoc†(U, X/K) → F-Isoc(U/K) from isocrystals partially overconvergent along X \ U to convergent ones is fully faithful.

**Hypotheses.**

- Frobenius structures are needed in (i) and (iii); (ii) holds already without Frobenius (RD.5/extension-across-boundary).
- Perfect k as in D'Addezio; Kedlaya's statements allow any k for (ii).

**Prerequisites.** [Kedlaya's extension theorem: constant monodromy is the obstruction to extending an overconvergent isocrystal](#target-rd-5-extension-across-boundary) (`RD.5/extension-across-boundary`), [Kedlaya's full faithfulness theorem: overconvergent F-isocrystals embed fully faithfully into convergent ones](#target-rd-3-full-faithfulness-overconvergent-to-convergent) (`RD.3/full-faithfulness-overconvergent-to-convergent`), [Local full faithfulness: morphisms of (σ,∇)-modules over Γ_con are determined over Γ](#target-rd-3-local-full-faithfulness) (`RD.3/local-full-faithfulness`), [Restriction from overconvergent to convergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-3-restriction-to-convergent) (`RD.3/restriction-to-convergent`), [Overconvergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-f-isocrystal) (`RD.3/overconvergent-f-isocrystal`), [Pushforward of (overconvergent) F-isocrystals along finite étale morphisms](#target-rd-3-finite-etale-pushforward-of-isocrystals) (`RD.3/finite-etale-pushforward-of-isocrystals`), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/de-jong-alteration-theorem`.

**Sources.**

- [S79](#source-79), Theorem 4.1.6, p. 12. States, after Kedlaya, that restriction to a dense open is fully faithful for convergent F-isocrystals, and fully faithful and closed under subquotients for overconvergent ones.
- [S77](#source-77), Theorem 4.2.1 and its proof, pp. 14–15. Restriction from isocrystals overconvergent along X \ U to convergent isocrystals on U is fully faithful in the presence of Frobenius, first for smooth pairs and in general by a quasi-resolution and finite étale descent.
- [S76](#source-76), Proposition 5.3.1 and Remark 5.3.2, p. 48. Sub-isocrystals extend in the overconvergent category; the Legendre unit-root example shows the convergent analogue fails.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (ii) Full faithfulness and closure under subobjects from RD.5/extension-across-boundary (a), (b), applied to E and to Frobenius pullbacks (Frobenius structures extend by full faithfulness); quotients by duality.
2. (iii) Kedlaya, Semistable reduction II, Theorem 4.2.1: reduce to Hom(O, E), i.e. Frobenius-invariant horizontal sections; for a smooth pair (X, X \ U) this is Kedlaya's full-faithfulness argument made unconditional by the local full faithfulness RD.3/local-full-faithfulness; in general choose a quasi-resolution f: X_1 → X (an alteration making (U_1, X_1) a smooth pair, SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/de-jong-alteration-theorem), lift a section on U_1, descend it over the finite étale locus U' ⊂ U by adjunction for finite étale pushforward (RD.3/finite-etale-pushforward-of-isocrystals), and extend from U' to U by RD.5/extension-across-boundary, checking Frobenius compatibility on U'.
3. (i) The restrictions of convergent F-isocrystals on X are naturally partially overconvergent along X \ U. By (iii), a convergent Frobenius-compatible morphism on U is a morphism of these partially overconvergent objects; it extends to X by RD.5/extension-across-boundary and the constant monodromy supplied by the existing convergent extensions. Absolute overconvergent-to-convergent full faithfulness alone would not give this relative assertion (D’Addezio, proof of Theorem 4.1.6).

**Checks.**

- For X = A^1, U = G_m and the unit object, underlying isocrystal endomorphisms are K on both opens; endomorphisms respecting σ-semilinear Frobenius are the fixed field K^σ. Both restriction maps are isomorphisms.
- On the ordinary locus U of the Legendre family B, R^1f_*O has a unit-root convergent subcrystal on U that is not overconvergent, so the subquotient closure in (ii) fails for the convergent category (Kedlaya, Semistable reduction I, Remark 5.3.2).

<a id="target-rd-5-global-semistable-reduction"></a>

### Kedlaya's semistable reduction theorem for overconvergent F-isocrystals

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.5/global-semistable-reduction` · theorem

Let Z ⊂ X be a closed immersion of k-varieties with X \ Z smooth, and E an F-isocrystal on X \ Z overconvergent along Z. Then, after replacing k by k^{q^{−n}} for some n ≥ 0, there is an alteration f: X_1 → X (separable when k is perfect) such that, with Z_1 = (f^{−1}(Z))_red, (X_1, Z_1) is a smooth pair and f^*E extends to a convergent log-F-isocrystal with nilpotent residues on (X_1, Z_1); equivalently f^*E has unipotent monodromy along Z_1. In particular, for X smooth and E ∈ F-Isoc†(X), there is a generically finite alteration X_1 → X from an open X_1 of a smooth proper variety Ȳ_1 with SNC boundary along which f^*E is docile.

**Hypotheses.**

- Frobenius structure on E (as in the p-adic local monodromy theorem, of which this is the higher-dimensional form).
- Alterations in de Jong's sense (proper, surjective, generically finite) from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4; the alteration depends on E.

**Prerequisites.** [Logarithmic extension of isocrystals with unipotent monodromy](#target-rd-5-log-extension-of-unipotent-isocrystal) (`RD.5/log-extension-of-unipotent-isocrystal`), [Constant and unipotent monodromy along a boundary divisor; docile isocrystals](#target-rd-5-unipotent-monodromy-along-boundary) (`RD.5/unipotent-monodromy-along-boundary`), [Convergent log-isocrystals on a smooth pair](#target-rd-5-convergent-log-isocrystal) (`RD.5/convergent-log-isocrystal`), [The p-adic local monodromy theorem (Crew's conjecture): (φ,∇)-modules over the Robba ring are quasi-unipotent](#target-rd-2-quasi-unipotence-and-local-monodromy-statement) (`RD.2/quasi-unipotence-and-local-monodromy-statement`), [Local monodromy theorem in finite étale form (the form used for finiteness of rigid cohomology)](#target-rd-2-local-monodromy-finite-etale-form) (`RD.2/local-monodromy-finite-etale-form`), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/de-jong-alteration-theorem`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/alteration`.

**Sources.**

- [S78](#source-78), Definition 2.4.1, Theorems 2.4.3–2.4.4, pp. 16–17. Defines local semistable reduction at a valuation and proves local and global semistable reduction for F-isocrystals overconvergent along a closed subscheme.
- [S78](#source-78), Theorem 2.3.9 and Definition 2.3.10, p. 15. De Jong's alteration theorem in the form used, and the Galois closure of an alteration.
- [S79](#source-79), §4.4.11, p. 23. Uses Kedlaya's semistable reduction to reduce to an F-isocrystal docile along an SNC boundary of a smooth projective compactification.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Local semistable reduction at every valuation v of k(X) centred on Z (Kedlaya, Semistable reduction IV, Theorem 2.4.3): reduce to k algebraically closed and v minimal (Semistable reduction III); for transcendence defect 0 (monomial valuations) this is Semistable reduction III, Theorem 6.3.1, built on the p-adic local monodromy theorem over polyannuli (RD.2/quasi-unipotence-and-local-monodromy-statement in relative form); induction on transcendence defect is Semistable reduction IV, Theorem 5.0.1.
2. Global from local: the locus of valuations where a given alteration achieves semistable reduction is open in the Riemann–Zariski space, which is quasi-compact; finitely many local alterations are combined into one via de Jong's theorem and Galois closures (Semistable reduction II, Propositions 3.3.4 and 3.4.5; Semistable reduction IV, Definition 2.3.10 and Theorem 2.4.4).
3. Equivalence with unipotent monodromy: RD.5/log-extension-of-unipotent-isocrystal.

**Checks.**

- For X = P^1, Z = {∞} and E the Dwork isocrystal on A^1, the Artin–Schreier alteration P^1 → P^1, t = y^p − y, makes E constant (RD.2/dwork-exponential-artin-schreier-example), hence docile.
- For the Kummer isocrystal (O, d + a dt/t) on G_m with a ∈ (q − 1)^{−1}ℤ, the Kummer alteration t = s^{q−1} makes it docile.

<a id="target-rd-5-docility-acceptance"></a>

### Acceptance: docility of the Kummer and Dwork isocrystals and their semistable reduction

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.5/docility-acceptance` · application

(1) On G_m ⊂ P^1 over F_q, the Kummer F-isocrystal K_a = (O, d + a dt/t) with a ∈ (q − 1)^{−1}ℤ is docile along {0, ∞} iff a ∈ ℤ; its pullback along the Kummer cover s ↦ s^{q−1} = t is constant, hence docile, and its canonical nilpotent-residue log extension to (P^1, {0, ∞}) after pullback has zero residues. (2) On A^1 ⊂ P^1, the Dwork F-isocrystal L_π is not docile along ∞ (Swan conductor 1), and no tame power cover t = s^m with p ∤ m makes it docile; its pullback along the Artin–Schreier cover y^p − y = t is constant. (3) The restriction to G_m of any docile F-isocrystal on A^1 ⊂ P^1 (docile along ∞) is docile along {0, ∞}, and restriction is fully faithful (RD.5/dense-open-restriction-fully-faithful).

**Hypotheses.**

- Conventions for L_π as in RD.1/dwork-exponential-module (π^{p−1} = −p).
- q = p^f; the Kummer twist uses a ∈ (q − 1)^{−1}ℤ so that a Frobenius structure exists.

**Prerequisites.** [Constant and unipotent monodromy along a boundary divisor; docile isocrystals](#target-rd-5-unipotent-monodromy-along-boundary) (`RD.5/unipotent-monodromy-along-boundary`), [Logarithmic extension of isocrystals with unipotent monodromy](#target-rd-5-log-extension-of-unipotent-isocrystal) (`RD.5/log-extension-of-unipotent-isocrystal`), [Kedlaya's semistable reduction theorem for overconvergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-5-global-semistable-reduction) (`RD.5/global-semistable-reduction`), [Restriction of F-isocrystals to a dense open is fully faithful, and closed under subquotients in the overconvergent case](#target-rd-5-dense-open-restriction-fully-faithful) (`RD.5/dense-open-restriction-fully-faithful`), [The rank-one exponential connection (Dwork's exponential): radius, highest break 1, Swan conductor 1, unit-root Frobenius structure](#target-rd-1-dwork-exponential-module) (`RD.1/dwork-exponential-module`), [Acceptance: the Dwork isocrystal at ∞ is trivialised by an Artin-Schreier extension of the Robba ring](#target-rd-2-dwork-exponential-artin-schreier-example) (`RD.2/dwork-exponential-artin-schreier-example`), [Unipotent ∇-modules are the modules V ⊗ R with nilpotent residue](#target-rd-2-unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue) (`RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue`).

**Sources.**

- [S76](#source-76), Theorem 6.4.5, p. 56. Docility is equivalent to log extension with nilpotent residues, which the residue computations test.
- [S79](#source-79), Definition 4.4.1 and the proof of Corollary 4.4.8, pp. 19, 22. Docile rank-one isocrystals have zero residues, hence are unramified.
- [S78](#source-78), Lemma 3.5.1 and Definition 5.1.9, pp. 29, 47. Computes the generic radius of Dwork-type rank-one modules ∇v = πr v ⊗ dx, and lists Artin–Schreier alterations x̃^p − g^{p−1}x̃ = x + ⋯ beside tame m-th power maps among the operations used for local semistable reduction.
- [S78](#source-78), Lemma 3.1.8, p. 25; Lemma 3.5.1, p. 29. The generic-radius formula under a tame power pullback preserves a positive Dwork break; the Dwork module has positive break at infinity.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1) Residues: K_a has residue a at 0 and −a at ∞; unipotent rank one means constant, i.e. residue in ℤ after gauge transformation by t^n (RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue); pullback along s^{q−1} multiplies the residue by q − 1.
2. (2) The Dwork module has highest break 1 at ∞. For a tame power cover x = y^m in a local parameter at ∞, Kedlaya Semistable reduction IV, Lemma 3.1.8 gives f_i(F,s/m)−s/m = f_i(E,s)−s. For a positive break this rescales its slope by m, so the pullback remains nonunipotent. This checks tame power covers specifically; Artin–Schreier trivialisation is RD.2/dwork-exponential-artin-schreier-example.
3. (3) Unipotence along ∞ is unaffected by removing 0 where the isocrystal is overconvergent and regular (constant monodromy), and RD.5/dense-open-restriction-fully-faithful gives full faithfulness.

**Checks.**

- The residues computed in (1) are ±a and change by integers under gauge transformations.
- The break computed in (2) is 1.

### Proof obligations and supplier contracts

**Compact-support Gysin, excision and finite étale pushforward proof interfaces.** RD.4/general-rigid-gysin supplies ordinary no-F Gysin. ## RD.6 — Traces, conductors, Fourier transform and weights

Construct closed-point Frobenius, Euler products, Dwork operators and the coefficient sign dictionary. The nuclear trace comparison supplies the cohomological trace formula. Local indices and Irr=Swan give the global Euler formula. Rank-one finiteness and neutral Tannakian recognition support determinantal weights; Frobenius-equivariant Fourier comparison, genuine constant weight-normalizing lines and local weight–monodromy supply p-adic Weil II. Kloosterman coefficients and middle cohomology are applications of the same theory.

**Landmarks.** L-function of an overconvergent F-isocrystal, Lefschetz trace formula for Frobenius, ι-weights of overconvergent F-isocrystals, p-adic Fourier transform, Dwork isocrystal, Rigid Weil II.

### Worked checks

- Constant coefficient on P^1: Frobenius eigenvalues 1 and q (first part); the zeta function 1/((1 − t)(1 − qt)) is rational over Q (`RD.6/rational-descent-of-power-series`).
- G_m: H^1_c = K of weight 0 and H^1 = K(−1) of weight 2, so the middle cohomology vanishes and is trivially pure of weight 1 (`RD.6/middle-cohomology-is-pure`); H^1_c has slope 0 (`RD.6/nonnegative-slopes-constant-coefficients-on-curves`).
- Dwork coefficient L_{x^d}, p ∤ d: Irr_∞ = Swan_∞ = d, χ(A^1, L_{x^d}) = 1 − d (`RD.6/christol-mebkhout-global-euler-characteristic`, `RD.6/irregularity-equals-swan`); its trace function is ψ\_π^{-1} ∘ Tr (`RD.6/dwork-kummer-sign-dictionary`).
- Kummer coefficient K_a, a ∉ Z: tame, χ(G_m, K_a) = 0, finite monodromy μ\_m (`RD.6/kummer-isocrystal`, `RD.6/coefficient-category-is-neutral-tannakian`).
- Kloosterman coefficient Kl_2: rank 2, Swan_∞ = 1, χ = −1, Frobenius eigenvalues of absolute value √q, the Weil bound |Kl_2(z; q)| ≤ 2√q and the relation Kl_2(z; q^2) = 2q − Kl_2(z; q)^2 (`RD.6/kloosterman-local-monodromy-and-purity`, `RD.6/kloosterman-f-isocrystal`); H^1_mid(G_m, Kl_2) = 0 (`RD.6/symmetric-power-kloosterman-middle-cohomology`).
- A Tate-curve type degeneration: ker N = im N pure of weight 0 inside a weight-1 coefficient (`RD.6/local-monodromy-weight-purity`).


<a id="target-rd-6-linear-q-frobenius"></a>

### The linear q-power Frobenius on rigid cohomology over F_q

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.6/linear-q-frobenius` · definition

Let q = p^a, k = F_q and let K be a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with residue field F_q (so K is a finite extension of K_0 = W(F_q)[1/p]). Take the Frobenius lift σ_K = id_K, which is allowed because the q-power map is the identity on F_q. For a separated scheme X of finite type over F_q and an overconvergent F-isocrystal E on X relative to (K, σ_K) with its q-power Frobenius structure F : σ*E ≅ E (RD.3), the Frobenius on H^i_rig(X/K, E) and on H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E) (RD.4) is K-linear; this K-linear endomorphism is denoted F and called the linear q-Frobenius. If K = K_0 and E carries a p-power Frobenius structure Φ relative to the Witt-vector Frobenius σ_0 of K_0, its q-power Frobenius structure is the a-fold composite Φ ∘ σ_0^*Φ ∘ ⋯ ∘ (σ_0^{a−1})^*Φ, which is σ_0^a = id-semilinear, and the linear q-Frobenius on cohomology is the a-th iterate of the σ_0-semilinear p-Frobenius. Throughout RD.6 and RD.7, 'Frobenius' means this linear q-Frobenius F.

**Hypotheses.**

- k = F_q with q = p^a; K complete discretely valued of characteristic 0 with residue field F_q; σ_K = id_K.
- E an overconvergent F-isocrystal on a separated finite-type F_q-scheme X (RD.3/overconvergent-f-isocrystal).

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/Frobenius`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [The Frobenius on rigid cohomology](#target-rd-4-frobenius-on-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.4/frobenius-on-rigid-cohomology`), [Rigid cohomology H^i_rig(X/K, E)](#target-rd-4-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.4/rigid-cohomology`), [Rigid cohomology with compact supports H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E)](#target-rd-4-compactly-supported-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.4/compactly-supported-rigid-cohomology`), [Overconvergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-f-isocrystal) (`RD.3/overconvergent-f-isocrystal`), `mathlib:WittVector.frobenius`.

**Sources.**

- [S5](#source-5), §2, opening paragraph, p. 9. Pins σ_K = id when k = F_q.
- [S5](#source-5), §2, opening paragraph, p. 9. The q-power Frobenius lift is a power of the Witt vector Frobenius.
- [S5](#source-5), §5 opening, p. 36. Linearity of F over K when σ_K = id.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- Kedlaya, Weil II §5 (Theorem 5.3.2): the traces Trace(F, H^i_c) in the trace formula are traces of this linear map
- RD.7/frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison: the q-Frobenius is matched with the f-th iterate of the semilinear crystalline Frobenius
- ColemanIntegration:L1/good-reduction-datum-exists: the F_q-linear Frobenius on H^1_rig(Y_k/K) whose eigenvalues are required to be Weil numbers

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `linearFrobenius` |  | The K-linear endomorphism F of H^i_rig(X/K, E) and of H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E) induced by the q-power Frobenius structure, for k = F_q and σ_K = id_K. |
| `linearFrobenius_eq_pow` |  | If K = K_0 and E has a p-power Frobenius structure Φ, then linearFrobenius = (Φ_*)^a on cohomology, a = log_p q. |
| `linearFrobenius_natural` |  | linearFrobenius commutes with pullback along morphisms of F_q-schemes, with maps induced by morphisms of F-isocrystals and with the maps of the excision sequence (RD.4/excision-sequence). |
| `linearFrobenius_tateTwist` |  | On E(n) (RD.6/tate-twist-of-f-isocrystals) the linear Frobenius is q^{−n} times that of E. |
| `linearFrobenius_baseChange` |  | After base change to F_{q^r} and K_r, the linear q^r-Frobenius is F^r ⊗ 1 (RD.6/base-change-to-finite-extension-of-fq). |

**Unit tests.**
