The hypothesis 'ι-realizable' holds whenever E is a successive extension of ι-pure objects of integer weights (the global notion of the notes, Definition 10.2); real weights require the scalar-normalisation qualification of RD.6/iota-real-and-realizable, in particular for constant coefficients, for every ι.

**Hypotheses.**

- X separated of finite type over F_q (smooth in (b)); E ι-realizable; ι arbitrary.

**Prerequisites.** [Rigid Weil II on the affine line](#target-rd-6-weil-ii-on-affine-line) (`RD.6/weil-ii-on-affine-line`), [ι-real and ι-realizable overconvergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-6-iota-real-and-realizable) (`RD.6/iota-real-and-realizable`), [Pointwise ι-weights of overconvergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-6-pointwise-iota-weights) (`RD.6/pointwise-iota-weights`), [The rigid Lefschetz trace formula for Frobenius](#target-rd-6-lefschetz-trace-formula) (`RD.6/lefschetz-trace-formula`), [Poincaré duality for rigid cohomology with coefficients (Kedlaya, Theorem 1.2.3)](#target-rd-5-poincare-duality) (`RD.5/poincare-duality`), [The excision long exact sequence for compact-support rigid cohomology](#target-rd-4-excision-sequence) (`RD.4/excision-sequence`), [Rigid cohomology H^i_rig(X/K, E)](#target-rd-4-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.4/rigid-cohomology`), [Rigid cohomology with compact supports H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E)](#target-rd-4-compactly-supported-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.4/compactly-supported-rigid-cohomology`), [Open dense affines finite étale over affine space in positive characteristic](#target-rd-3-etale-cover-of-affine-space) (`RD.3/etale-cover-of-affine-space`), [Generic pushforwards are (σ,∇)-modules (Kedlaya, Theorem 7.3.3)](#target-rd-5-generic-pushforward-theorem) (`RD.5/generic-pushforward-theorem`), [The Leray long exact sequence for the projection A⟨x⟩† → A](#target-rd-5-leray-long-exact-sequence) (`RD.5/leray-long-exact-sequence`), [Compatibility of the Poincaré pairing with the two excision sequences](#target-rd-5-excision-duality-compatibility) (`RD.5/excision-duality-compatibility`), [Normalising an ι-pure coefficient to weight zero](#target-rd-6-weight-normalising-constant-line) (`RD.6/weight-normalising-constant-line`).

**Sources.**

- [S5](#source-5), Theorem 6.6.2, p. 50. Hypotheses.
- [S5](#source-5), Theorem 6.6.2 (b), p. 50. Part (b).
- [S3](#source-3), Theorem 10.3, p. 27. Statement in the notes (global mixedness; cites the published numbering Theorem 5.3.2).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Induction on n = dim X, then on rank E, for all q simultaneously.
2. (b) ⇒ (a) by Poincaré duality (RD.5/poincare-duality); by excision (RD.4/excision-sequence) and induction, (a) reduces to X smooth affine of pure dimension n, and by duality again to (b) for X or any open dense subset.
3. Enlarge K and twist to w = 0; by the geometric lemma (RD.5) an open dense affine U is finite étale over A^n, and H^i(U, E) = H^i(A^n, f_*E) (finite étale pushforward, RD.4), so X = A^n; reduce to E irreducible by the long exact sequence.
4. Write A^n = A^1 × A^{n−1}, f the projection; over an open dense W ⊂ A^{n−1} the kernel F_0 and cokernel F_1 of the vertical connection are overconvergent F-isocrystals (generic pushforward theorem, RD.5); if F_0 ≠ 0 then E = f^*F_0 and induction applies; else F_0 = 0.
5. ι-realizability of F_1: choose E' with E ⊕ E' ι-real and semisimple; by the trace formula (RD.6/lefschetz-trace-formula) the fibre traces of F_1 ⊕ F_1' minus those of F_0' are ι-real, so F_1 is ι-realizable.
6. By RD.6/weil-ii-on-affine-line on the fibres, F_1 is ι-mixed of weight ≥ 1; by induction H^{i−1}_rig(W, F_1) is mixed ≥ i; since F_0 = 0 the Leray sequence (Kedlaya Finiteness Proposition 7.4.1, RD.5) gives a Frobenius-equivariant injection H^i_rig(X/K, E) ↪ H^{i−1}_rig(W/K, F_1), which gives (b) on X (Kedlaya prints f_*E^∨ in place of E here; see sourceIssues).

**Checks.**

- G_m, constant coefficients: H^1_c weight 0 ≤ 0 + 1 and H^1 weight 2 ≥ 0 + 1 (RD.6/multiplicative-group-mixed-weights).
- P^1: H^0 weight 0, H^2 weight 2 = 0 + 2 (RD.6/projective-line-frobenius-eigenvalues).

<a id="target-rd-6-purity-smooth-proper"></a>

### Purity of rigid cohomology of smooth proper varieties

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.6/purity-smooth-proper` · theorem

Let X be a smooth proper scheme over F_q and E an ι-realizable overconvergent F-isocrystal that is ι-pure of weight w. Then H^i_rig(X/K, E) is ι-pure of weight w + i for every i. For constant coefficients E = O_X, H^i_rig(X/K) is ι-pure of weight i for every embedding ι : K^alg ↪ C; hence every eigenvalue of F on H^i_rig(X/K) is an algebraic number all of whose complex conjugates have absolute value q^{i/2} (a Weil q-number of weight i).

**Hypotheses.**

- X smooth and proper over F_q; E ι-realizable, ι-pure of weight w (for constant coefficients: any ι).

**Prerequisites.** [Rigid Weil II over a point (Kedlaya)](#target-rd-6-p-adic-weil-ii) (`RD.6/p-adic-weil-ii`), [ι-real and ι-realizable overconvergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-6-iota-real-and-realizable) (`RD.6/iota-real-and-realizable`), [Rigid cohomology with compact supports H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E)](#target-rd-4-compactly-supported-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.4/compactly-supported-rigid-cohomology`), `DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.0/iota-weight`, `DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.0/endomorphism-weights`, `DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.0/weil-number-iff-iota-pure-for-every-iota`.

**Sources.**

- [S5](#source-5), §6.6 (c) and following, p. 51–52. Kedlaya's deduction of the Riemann hypothesis (for every ι).
- [S5](#source-5), §6.6, p. 52. The argument works for any ι.

**Construction or proof.**

1. X proper ⇒ H^i_c = H^i (RD.4/compactly-supported-rigid-cohomology).
2. RD.6/p-adic-weil-ii (a) gives weights ≤ w + i and (b) (X smooth) gives weights ≥ w + i; so every eigenvalue has |ι(α)| = q^{(w+i)/2}.
3. O_X is ι-pure of weight 0 and ι-realizable for every ι (RD.6/iota-real-and-realizable).
4. An element of K^alg that is ι-pure of weight i for every ι is algebraic over Q and a Weil q-number of weight i (DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.0, bridge between ι-weights and Weil numbers).

**Checks.**

- P^1: H^0 weight 0 (eigenvalue 1), H^2 weight 2 (eigenvalue q).
- Ordinary E/F_7: y^2 = x^3 + x + 1 has H^1 eigenvalues the roots of T^2 − 3T + 7, of absolute value √7 (PARI/GP polroots); supersingular y^2 = x^3 + x over F_7: roots of T^2 + 7, absolute value √7.

<a id="target-rd-6-rigid-functional-equation"></a>

### Functional equation of the rigid Weil factors

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.6/rigid-functional-equation` · lemma

Let X be smooth proper of pure dimension n over F_q, P_i(t) := det(1 − tF | H^i_rig(X/K)) and b_i := deg P_i = dim H^i. Then P_{2n−i}(t) = c_i · t^{b_i} · P_i(q^{−n} t^{−1}) with c_i = (−1)^{b_i} q^{n b_i} / det(F | H^i_rig(X/K)). (Kedlaya prints P_{2n−i}(t) = c t^j P_i(t^{−1}), omitting q^{−n}; see sourceIssues.)

**Hypotheses.**

- X smooth proper of pure dimension n over F_q.

**Prerequisites.** [Poincaré duality for rigid cohomology with coefficients (Kedlaya, Theorem 1.2.3)](#target-rd-5-poincare-duality) (`RD.5/poincare-duality`), [Frobenius is bijective on rigid cohomology of a smooth variety](#target-rd-6-frobenius-bijective-on-smooth) (`RD.6/frobenius-bijective-on-smooth`), [Rigid cohomology with compact supports H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E)](#target-rd-4-compactly-supported-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.4/compactly-supported-rigid-cohomology`).

**Sources.**

- [S5](#source-5), §6.6 (b), p. 52. Statement (the displayed formula omits the q^{−n}).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Frobenius-equivariant Poincaré duality H^i × H^{2n−i} → K(−n) (RD.5/poincare-duality; H_c = H for proper X): the eigenvalues of F on H^{2n−i} are q^n/α_j for the eigenvalues α_j on H^i, with multiplicity (F bijective, RD.6/frobenius-bijective-on-smooth).
2. Then P_{2n−i}(t) = ∏_j (1 − q^n t/α_j) = ∏_j (q^n t − α_j) / ∏_j (−α_j), and ∏_j (q^n t − α_j) = (q^n t)^{b_i} P_i(1/(q^n t)); since ∏_j (−α_j) = (−1)^{b_i} det(F | H^i), this is c_i t^{b_i} P_i(q^{−n} t^{−1}).

**Checks.**

- P^1 (n = 1, i = 0): P_2(t) = 1 − qt and c_0 t P_0(1/(qt)) = −q·t·(1 − 1/(qt)) = 1 − qt with c_0 = −q; the printed form c t^j P_0(1/t) = c(t^j − t^{j−1}) is never 1 − qt.

<a id="target-rd-6-gysin-sequence-for-curves"></a>

### The Gysin sequence of a punctured smooth proper curve

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.6/gysin-sequence-for-curves` · lemma

Let X be a smooth proper curve over F_q, D ⊂ X a nonempty reduced finite closed subscheme and Y = X − D. There is a Frobenius-equivariant exact sequence 0 → H^1_rig(X/K) → H^1_rig(Y/K) → ⊕_{x ∈ |D|} H^0_rig(x/K)^∨(−1) → H^2_rig(X/K) → H^2_rig(Y/K) → 0, whose first map is restriction. If D meets every connected component of X (equivalently Y is affine), then H^2_rig(Y/K) = 0.

**Hypotheses.**

- X smooth proper curve over F_q; D reduced, finite, nonempty; Y = X − D.

**Prerequisites.** [The excision long exact sequence for compact-support rigid cohomology](#target-rd-4-excision-sequence) (`RD.4/excision-sequence`), [Poincaré duality for rigid cohomology with coefficients (Kedlaya, Theorem 1.2.3)](#target-rd-5-poincare-duality) (`RD.5/poincare-duality`), [Rigid cohomology of Spec F_{q^d}](#target-rd-6-rigid-cohomology-of-a-finite-field-point) (`RD.6/rigid-cohomology-of-a-finite-field-point`), [Tate twists of overconvergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-6-tate-twist-of-f-isocrystals) (`RD.6/tate-twist-of-f-isocrystals`), [Rigid cohomology H^i_rig(X/K, E)](#target-rd-4-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.4/rigid-cohomology`), [Rigid cohomology with compact supports H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E)](#target-rd-4-compactly-supported-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.4/compactly-supported-rigid-cohomology`), [Compatibility of the Poincaré pairing with the two excision sequences](#target-rd-5-excision-duality-compatibility) (`RD.5/excision-duality-compatibility`).

**Sources.**

- [S5](#source-5), §2.1, (2.1.2), p. 11. Gysin maps relate the two excision sequences.
- [S5](#source-5), §2.6, (2.6.1), p. 18. The curve sequence 0 → H^0 → H^0_loc → H^1_c → H^1 → H^1_loc → H^2_c → 0.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Compact-support excision for D ⊂ X (RD.4/excision-sequence): 0 → H^0_c(Y) → H^0(X) → H^0(D) → H^1_c(Y) → H^1(X) → H^1(D) = 0 → H^2_c(Y) → H^2(X) → 0, Frobenius-equivariant (X proper: H_c = H; D has dimension 0, RD.6/rigid-cohomology-of-a-finite-field-point).
2. Dualise with Frobenius-equivariant Poincaré duality on the smooth curves X and Y (RD.5/poincare-duality): H^j(Y) ≅ H^{2−j}_c(Y)^∨(−1), H^j(X) ≅ H^{2−j}(X)^∨(−1); the dual of H^0(D) → H^1_c(Y) → H^1(X) → 0 twisted by (−1) gives the displayed sequence (duality is natural for restriction/excision).
3. If D meets every component, H^0(X) → H^0(D) is injective (a horizontal section vanishing at a point of a connected component vanishes, RD.6/pointwise-iota-weights h0 embedding), so H^0_c(Y) = 0 and H^2(Y) = 0.

**Checks.**

- X = P^1, D = {0, ∞}: 0 → 0 → H^1(G_m) → K(−1)^2 → K(−1) → 0, so H^1(G_m) ≅ K(−1) (F = q).
- X = E an elliptic curve, D = {O}: H^1(E − O) ≅ H^1(E).

<a id="target-rd-6-nonnegative-slopes-constant-coefficients-on-curves"></a>

### Constant coefficients on affine curves have H^1_c of nonnegative slopes

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.6/nonnegative-slopes-constant-coefficients-on-curves` · lemma

Let C be a smooth affine curve over F_q and V an F-isocrystal over Spec F_q (a finite-dimensional K-space with linear Frobenius) all of whose slopes are ≥ 0, with pullback V_C to C. Then H^1_{c,rig}(C/K, V_C) has all slopes ≥ 0. This replaces the vanishing assertion of Kedlaya's Lemma 6.7.2 for horizontally constant constituents, which fails (O on G_m has H^1_c = K), as the base case of parent RD.6/nonnegative-slopes-of-h1c-on-curves.

**Hypotheses.**

- C smooth affine over F_q with smooth compactification C̄ and boundary D = C̄ − C; V of slopes ≥ 0.

**Prerequisites.** [Closed points, point counts and the zeta function over a finite field](#target-rd-6-closed-points-and-zeta-function) (`RD.6/closed-points-and-zeta-function`), [The rigid Lefschetz trace formula for Frobenius](#target-rd-6-lefschetz-trace-formula) (`RD.6/lefschetz-trace-formula`), [The Gysin sequence of a punctured smooth proper curve](#target-rd-6-gysin-sequence-for-curves) (`RD.6/gysin-sequence-for-curves`), [Rigid cohomology of Spec F_{q^d}](#target-rd-6-rigid-cohomology-of-a-finite-field-point) (`RD.6/rigid-cohomology-of-a-finite-field-point`), [p-adic slopes of Frobenius eigenvalues and slope intervals](#target-rd-6-slope-interval-of-isocrystal) (`RD.6/slope-interval-of-isocrystal`), [The excision long exact sequence for compact-support rigid cohomology](#target-rd-4-excision-sequence) (`RD.4/excision-sequence`), [The Künneth formula with supports for smooth varieties (Kedlaya, (1.2.4.2))](#target-rd-5-kunneth-formula-with-supports) (`RD.5/kunneth-formula-with-supports`), [Poincaré duality for rigid cohomology with coefficients (Kedlaya, Theorem 1.2.3)](#target-rd-5-poincare-duality) (`RD.5/poincare-duality`), `mathlib:Polynomial.reverse`, `DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.0/characteristic-power-series-and-traces`.

**Sources.**

- [S5](#source-5), Lemma 6.7.2 and its proof, p. 52. Claims nonnegative slopes of H^1_c on affine curves for coefficients of nonnegative slopes; its reduction asserts a vanishing of H^1_c for constant constituents, which fails for O on G_m (roadmap source issue).
- [S3](#source-3), Theorem 9.6 and Remark 9.7, p. 22. Trace formula expressing L-functions, hence zeta functions, through characteristic polynomials of Frobenius on compactly supported cohomology.

**Construction or proof.**

1. H^1_{c,rig}(C/K, V_C) ≅ H^1_{c,rig}(C/K) ⊗_K V with Frobenius F ⊗ F_V (constant coefficients; RD.5/kunneth-formula-with-supports with the point), and slopes of a tensor product are sums of slopes (parent RD.6/slope-interval-of-isocrystal), so it suffices to treat V = K.
2. Excision for D ⊂ C̄ gives H^0(C̄) → H^0(D) → H^1_c(C) → H^1(C̄) → 0 (parent RD.6/gysin-sequence-for-curves, RD.4/excision-sequence); the eigenvalues of F on H^0(D) are roots of unity (parent RD.6/rigid-cohomology-of-a-finite-field-point), of slope 0.
3. After a finite extension of F_q make C̄ geometrically connected. Then H^0(C̄) = K with F = 1 and H^2(C̄) ≅ K(−1), so by the trace formula (parent RD.6/lefschetz-trace-formula) Z(C̄, t) = P_1(t)/((1 − t)(1 − qt)) with P_1(t) = det(1 − tF | H^1(C̄)). Since Z(C̄, t) ∈ 1 + tZ[[t]] (RD.6/closed-points-and-zeta-function), P_1 = Z·(1 − t)(1 − qt) has integer coefficients; since det(1 − tF) is the reverse of the characteristic polynomial (mathlib:Polynomial.reverse, DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.0/characteristic-power-series-and-traces (i)), its reciprocal roots are the eigenvalues of F on H^1(C̄), which are therefore algebraic integers, of slope ≥ 0.
4. The slopes of H^1_c(C) are those of the subquotients, hence ≥ 0. No circular use of parent RD.6/slope-bounds-for-rigid-cohomology occurs.

**Checks.**

- C = G_m: H^1_c = K with F = 1, slope 0.
- C = E − {O} for an elliptic curve E/F_7 with a_7 = 3: H^1_c ≅ H^1(E) with slopes 0 and 1.

<a id="target-rd-6-nonnegative-slopes-of-h1c-on-curves"></a>

### H^1_c of an isocrystal with nonnegative slopes on an affine curve has nonnegative slopes

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.6/nonnegative-slopes-of-h1c-on-curves` · lemma

Let C be an affine curve over F_q and E an overconvergent F-isocrystal on C with slopes in [0, ∞). Then H^1_{c,rig}(C/K, E) has slopes in [0, ∞).

**Hypotheses.**

- C affine curve over F_q; E with nonnegative slopes.

**Prerequisites.** [The rigid Lefschetz trace formula for Frobenius](#target-rd-6-lefschetz-trace-formula) (`RD.6/lefschetz-trace-formula`), [p-adic slopes of Frobenius eigenvalues and slope intervals](#target-rd-6-slope-interval-of-isocrystal) (`RD.6/slope-interval-of-isocrystal`), [Poincaré duality for rigid cohomology with coefficients (Kedlaya, Theorem 1.2.3)](#target-rd-5-poincare-duality) (`RD.5/poincare-duality`), [Constant coefficients on affine curves have H^1_c of nonnegative slopes](#target-rd-6-nonnegative-slopes-constant-coefficients-on-curves) (`RD.6/nonnegative-slopes-constant-coefficients-on-curves`).

**Sources.**

- [S5](#source-5), Lemma 6.7.2, p. 52. Conclusion.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Separate the horizontally constant constituents by exact sequences. Their H^1_c does not generally vanish: for O on G_m it is K. Prove its nonnegative slopes using the compactification exact sequence and the nonnegative-slope crystalline lattice of the smooth proper curve, including boundary-point permutation representations. This is an additional input, not the printed vanishing assertion.
2. For an irreducible constituent with H^0(E)=H^0(E^∨)=0, duality gives H^2_c(E)=0 and compact support gives H^0_c(E)=0. The trace formula then makes every power trace on H^1_c p-integral.
3. Power traces p-integral for all powers force all eigenvalues to have nonnegative valuation: the generating rational function Σ Tr(F^n)t^n has integral coefficients and no pole in |t|<1; a negative-valuation eigenvalue would give such a pole, with a nonzero multiplicity in characteristic zero.

**Checks.**

- E = O on G_m: H^1_c = K with F = 1, slope 0.

<a id="target-rd-6-slope-bounds-for-rigid-cohomology"></a>

### Slope bounds for rigid cohomology (p-adic weights)

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.6/slope-bounds-for-rigid-cohomology` · theorem

Let X be a separated F_q-scheme of finite type of dimension n and E an overconvergent F-isocrystal on X with slopes in [r, s]. For 0 ≤ i ≤ 2n, H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E) has slopes in [r + max{0, i − n}, s + min{i, n}]; if X is smooth, H^i_rig(X/K, E) has slopes in the same interval.

**Hypotheses.**

- X separated finite type over F_q of dimension n; E with slopes in [r, s].

**Prerequisites.** [H^1_c of an isocrystal with nonnegative slopes on an affine curve has nonnegative slopes](#target-rd-6-nonnegative-slopes-of-h1c-on-curves) (`RD.6/nonnegative-slopes-of-h1c-on-curves`), [p-adic slopes of Frobenius eigenvalues and slope intervals](#target-rd-6-slope-interval-of-isocrystal) (`RD.6/slope-interval-of-isocrystal`), [Poincaré duality for rigid cohomology with coefficients (Kedlaya, Theorem 1.2.3)](#target-rd-5-poincare-duality) (`RD.5/poincare-duality`), [The excision long exact sequence for compact-support rigid cohomology](#target-rd-4-excision-sequence) (`RD.4/excision-sequence`), [Open dense affines finite étale over affine space in positive characteristic](#target-rd-3-etale-cover-of-affine-space) (`RD.3/etale-cover-of-affine-space`), [Generic pushforwards are (σ,∇)-modules (Kedlaya, Theorem 7.3.3)](#target-rd-5-generic-pushforward-theorem) (`RD.5/generic-pushforward-theorem`), [The Leray long exact sequence for the projection A⟨x⟩† → A](#target-rd-5-leray-long-exact-sequence) (`RD.5/leray-long-exact-sequence`), [The special Newton polygon lies above the generic one, with the same endpoint](#target-rd-2-special-polygon-above-generic) (`RD.2/special-polygon-above-generic`).

**Sources.**

- [S5](#source-5), Theorem 6.7.1, p. 52. Hypotheses.
- [S5](#source-5), §6.7, p. 52. The elliptic-curve example.

**Construction or proof.**

1. X = A^1: i = 0, 2 directly and by duality; for i = 1, RD.6/nonnegative-slopes-of-h1c-on-curves (after twisting) gives H^1_c(M) ⊂ [r, ∞) and H^1_c(M^∨) ⊂ [−s, ∞); Grothendieck specialization (Kedlaya, local monodromy paper, Proposition 5.14: the special Newton polygon lies above the generic one; RD.2) bounds H^0_loc in [r, s] and H^1_loc(M^∨) in [−s + 1, −r + 1]; combine with (2.6.1) and duality.
2. General X: induction on n using excision (RD.4/excision-sequence), the geometric lemma and generic pushforwards along A^1 × W → W (RD.5), and the Leray sequence.

**Checks.**

- Constant coefficients on a smooth proper curve: H^1 slopes in [0, 1] (elliptic curves: {0, 1} or {1/2, 1/2}).

<a id="target-rd-6-weights-of-h1-of-affine-curve"></a>

### Weights 1 and 2 of Frobenius on H^1 of a smooth affine curve

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.6/weights-of-h1-of-affine-curve` · theorem

Let X_k be a smooth proper curve over F_q, D_k ⊂ X_k a nonempty reduced finite closed subscheme meeting every connected component, and Y_k = X_k − D_k (a smooth affine curve). Let F be the F_q-linear (q-power) Frobenius on H^1_rig(Y_k/K). Then every eigenvalue of F is a Weil q-number: those on the image of H^1_rig(X_k/K) (a subspace of dimension 2g, g the genus when X_k is geometrically connected) have weight 1, and those on the quotient, which embeds in the residue part ⊕_{x ∈ |D_k|} H^0_rig(x/K)^∨(−1) ('K(−1)^{(D)}'), are of the form q·ζ with ζ a root of unity (weight 2). In particular no eigenvalue of F is a root of unity, and for every n, m ≥ 1 no product of n eigenvalues has a power equal to 1.

**Hypotheses.**

- X_k smooth proper curve over F_q; D_k nonempty reduced finite, meeting every component; K with residue field F_q, σ_K = id.

**Prerequisites.** [The Gysin sequence of a punctured smooth proper curve](#target-rd-6-gysin-sequence-for-curves) (`RD.6/gysin-sequence-for-curves`), [Purity of rigid cohomology of smooth proper varieties](#target-rd-6-purity-smooth-proper) (`RD.6/purity-smooth-proper`), [Rigid cohomology of Spec F_{q^d}](#target-rd-6-rigid-cohomology-of-a-finite-field-point) (`RD.6/rigid-cohomology-of-a-finite-field-point`), [Tate twists of overconvergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-6-tate-twist-of-f-isocrystals) (`RD.6/tate-twist-of-f-isocrystals`), [Finite dimensionality of rigid cohomology with coefficients (Kedlaya, Theorem 1.2.1)](#target-rd-5-finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.5/finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology`), `DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.0/iota-weight`, `DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.0/endomorphism-weights`.

**Sources.**

- [S5](#source-5), §6.6 (c), p. 52. Weight 1 on H^1 of the smooth proper curve.
- [S5](#source-5), §2.6, p. 18. Frobenius-equivariant duality for curves into H^2_c = K(−1).

**Construction or proof.**

1. RD.6/gysin-sequence-for-curves gives 0 → H^1(X_k) → H^1(Y_k) → ⊕_x H^0(x)^∨(−1), Frobenius-equivariant, so the eigenvalues of F on H^1(Y_k) are those on H^1(X_k) together with some of those on ⊕_x H^0(x)^∨(−1).
2. H^0_rig(x/K) for x of degree d is K_x with F the generator of Gal(K_x/K): eigenvalues the d-th roots of unity (RD.6/rigid-cohomology-of-a-finite-field-point); on the dual they are inverted and the twist (−1) multiplies by q (RD.6/tate-twist-of-f-isocrystals): eigenvalues qζ, Weil numbers of weight 2.
3. H^1(X_k) is ι-pure of weight 1 for every ι (RD.6/purity-smooth-proper), so its eigenvalues are Weil q-numbers of weight 1 (DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.0).
4. A Weil number of weight w ≥ 1 has all conjugates of absolute value q^{w/2} > 1, so no product of positive-weight Weil numbers has a power equal to 1.

**Checks.**

- (P^1, {0, 1, ∞}): H^1 ≅ K(−1)^2 with F = q (Coleman's datum M = pI for q = p), weight 2.
- (E, {O}) for E: y^2 = x^3 + x + 1 over F_7: H^1(E − O) ≅ H^1(E), eigenvalues roots of T^2 − 3T + 7, |·| = √7 (PARI/GP).
- (P^1, {0, ∞} ∪ μ_N) over F_q with p ∤ N: H^1 eigenvalues are q·ζ where ζ runs over roots of unity of orders the degrees of the closed points of μ_N (one eigenvalue q is removed by the map to H^2).

<a id="target-rd-6-middle-cohomology-is-pure"></a>

### Middle rigid cohomology of a pure coefficient is pure

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.6/middle-cohomology-is-pure` · theorem

Let X be a smooth separated F_q-scheme of pure dimension d, ι : K^alg → C a field embedding, and E ∈ F-Isoc†(X/K) ι-realizable and ι-pure of weight w. The middle cohomology H^i_mid(X/K, E) := image of the forget-supports map H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E) → H^i_rig(X/K, E) is ι-pure of weight w + i. If X is a curve and the local invariants H^0_loc(X/K, E) are ι-mixed of weight ≤ w, then H^1_mid(X/K, E) ≅ gr^W_{w+1} H^1_{c,rig}(X/K, E), the quotient of H^1_{c,rig} by its part of weights ≤ w.

**Hypotheses.**

- X smooth of pure dimension d; E ι-realizable and ι-pure of weight w (for the real-weight normalisation see RD.6/weight-normalising-constant-line).
- For the curve statement, the local invariants at the points at infinity are ι-mixed of weight ≤ w (RD.6/local-monodromy-weight-purity gives this for every ι-pure E).

**Prerequisites.** [Rigid Weil II over a point (Kedlaya)](#target-rd-6-p-adic-weil-ii) (`RD.6/p-adic-weil-ii`), [Pointwise ι-weights of overconvergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-6-pointwise-iota-weights) (`RD.6/pointwise-iota-weights`), [The Gysin sequence of a punctured smooth proper curve](#target-rd-6-gysin-sequence-for-curves) (`RD.6/gysin-sequence-for-curves`), [Crew's finiteness and duality theorem on curves, made unconditional by local monodromy](#target-rd-5-crew-finiteness-and-duality-on-curves) (`RD.5/crew-finiteness-and-duality-on-curves`), [The forget-supports map H^i_{c,rig} → H^i_rig, an isomorphism for proper X](#target-rd-4-forget-supports-map) (`RD.4/forget-supports-map`), `DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.0/purity-under-subquotients-and-extensions`, `DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.0/iota-weight`.

**Sources.**

- [S93](#source-93), Section 3.2.1, pp. 23-24. In the ℓ-adic case, the image of compactly supported cohomology in ordinary cohomology of Sym^k Kl is identified with gr^W of compactly supported cohomology, using that the local inertia invariants have weights at most kn.
- [S93](#source-93), Section 3.2.2, (3.14), p. 25. The rigid analogue, using Kedlaya's weight results for rigid cohomology and the local contributions at 0 and ∞.
- [S5](#source-5), Theorem 6.6.2, pp. 50-51. Weights ≤ w + i on compact supports and ≥ w + i on ordinary cohomology of smooth X.

**Construction or proof.**

1. H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E) is ι-mixed of weight ≤ w + i and H^i_rig(X/K, E) is ι-mixed of weight ≥ w + i (parent RD.6/p-adic-weil-ii (a) and (b)).
2. The image of a Frobenius-equivariant map is a quotient of the first and a subobject of the second, hence has all ι-weights both ≤ w + i and ≥ w + i (DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.0/purity-under-subquotients-and-extensions).
3. Curves: the exact sequence H^0_loc(E) → H^1_c(E) → H^1(E) of (2.6.1) (parent RD.6/gysin-sequence-for-curves, RD.5/crew-finiteness-and-duality-on-curves) shows the kernel of H^1_c → H^1 is a quotient of H^0_loc, of weights ≤ w, while H^1_mid is pure of weight w + 1; so the kernel is exactly the part of weight ≤ w and H^1_mid is gr^W_{w+1}.

**Checks.**

- X = G_m, E = O: H^1_c = K (weight 0), H^1 = K(−1) (weight 2), the forget-supports map is zero and H^1_mid = 0, consistent with purity of weight 1.
- X = E − {O} for an elliptic curve E: H^1_mid = H^1(E), pure of weight 1 (parent RD.6/weights-of-h1-of-affine-curve).

<a id="target-rd-6-kloosterman-f-isocrystal"></a>

### The Kloosterman F-isocrystal Kl_{n+1}

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.6/kloosterman-f-isocrystal` · construction

Let p be odd, q a power of p, K = W(F_q)[1/p](π) with π^{p−1} = −p and σ_K = id, and n ≥ 1 with p ∤ n + 1. Let f : G_m^{n+1} → A^1, f(z, x_1, …, x_n) = x_1 + ⋯ + x_n + z/(x_1⋯x_n), and pr : G_m^{n+1} → G_m the projection to z. The Kloosterman F-isocrystal is Kl_{n+1} := R^n pr_{rig,*}(f^*L_π), the relative rigid cohomology in degree n of the Dwork isocrystal L_π (parent RD.6/dwork-isocrystal) pulled back along f, with the Frobenius structure induced by functoriality. It is an overconvergent F-isocrystal of rank n + 1 on G_m, the other relative cohomology groups vanish, and over the dagger algebra K⟨z, z^{-1}⟩† its connection is the Dwork–Sperber hypergeometric connection (Crew 1994 (1.1.5)). Its linear Frobenius at z_0 ∈ F_{q^r}^× has trace (−1)^n Kl_{n+1}(z_0; q^r), where Kl_{n+1}(z_0; q^r) := Σ_{x_1⋯x_{n+1} = z_0} ψ(Tr(x_1 + ⋯ + x_{n+1})) with ψ = ψ_π^{-1} (RD.6/dwork-kummer-sign-dictionary).

**Hypotheses.**

- p odd and p ∤ n + 1 (Crew's hypotheses for the explicit connection); the geometric construction is valid for every p, but this roadmap specifies only the case covered by its sources.
- Relative rigid cohomology along pr is an overconvergent F-isocrystal on all of G_m here, which is more than the generic-pushforward theorem (RD.5/generic-pushforward-theorem) gives; this is Crew 1994 §1.5 (citing Sperber §6 and Berthelot), recorded as an imported input.

**Prerequisites.** [The Dwork (Artin–Schreier) isocrystal L_π](#target-rd-6-dwork-isocrystal) (`RD.6/dwork-isocrystal`), [Dwork's additive character attached to π](#target-rd-6-dwork-additive-character) (`RD.6/dwork-additive-character`), [Sign and direction conventions for Dwork and Kummer F-isocrystals](#target-rd-6-dwork-kummer-sign-dictionary) (`RD.6/dwork-kummer-sign-dictionary`), [The rigid Lefschetz trace formula for Frobenius](#target-rd-6-lefschetz-trace-formula) (`RD.6/lefschetz-trace-formula`), [Generic pushforwards are (σ,∇)-modules (Kedlaya, Theorem 7.3.3)](#target-rd-5-generic-pushforward-theorem) (`RD.5/generic-pushforward-theorem`), [Overconvergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-3-overconvergent-f-isocrystal) (`RD.3/overconvergent-f-isocrystal`), [Rigid cohomology with compact supports H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E)](#target-rd-4-compactly-supported-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.4/compactly-supported-rigid-cohomology`).

**Sources.**

- [S86](#source-86), Section 1.1 and Proposition 1.2, pp. 4-6. The rank-n Kloosterman isocrystal on G_m as the Dwork–Sperber hypergeometric connection, overconvergent for p ∤ n.
- [S86](#source-86), Section 1.5, pp. 10-11. Geometric construction as relative rigid cohomology of the pullback of the Dwork F-isocrystal, Frobenius from functoriality, traces equal to Kloosterman sums; the printed trace formula (1.5.1) needs the sign (−1)^{n−1} and, for the Frobenius structure Crew gives L_ψ, the character ψ^{-1} (see sourceIssues).
- [S93](#source-93), Section 3.2.2, p. 25. Kl_{n+1} = Rπ_rig,* L_ϖ(f)[n] has rank n + 1 and is pure of weight n, citing Crew 1994 §1.5.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, §3.2.2 and §5.1.5: the rigid cohomology of Sym^k Kl_{n+1} and its comparison with p-adic Galois representations
- Crew 1994, Theorem 2.3: the overconvergent monodromy group of Kl(n, ψ)
- RD.6/symmetric-power-kloosterman-middle-cohomology: the coefficient whose symmetric powers carry the moment L-functions

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kloostermanIsocrystal` |  | Kl_{n+1} := R^n pr_{rig,*}(f^*L_π) on G_m, with its Frobenius structure. |
| `kloostermanIsocrystal_rank` |  | rank Kl_{n+1} = n + 1. |
| `kloostermanIsocrystal_trace` |  | Tr(F_{z_0} \| Kl_{n+1}) = (−1)^n Kl_{n+1}(z_0; q^r) for z_0 ∈ F_{q^r}^×. |
| `kloostermanIsocrystal_pure` |  | Kl_{n+1} is ι-pure of weight n for every ι (RD.6/kloosterman-local-monodromy-and-purity). |
| `kloostermanIsocrystal_local` |  | Unipotent at 0 with a single Jordan block; at ∞ all breaks equal 1/(n+1) and Swan_∞ = 1 (RD.6/kloosterman-local-monodromy-and-purity). |
| `kloostermanIsocrystal_one` |  | For n = 0, Kl_1 = L_π restricted to G_m. |

**Unit tests.**

- `kloostermanIsocrystal_rank_two` (computation): Kl_2 has rank 2 and Tr(F_{z_0}) = −Σ_{x∈F_q^×} ψ(x + z_0/x) for z_0 ∈ F_q^×.
- `kloostermanIsocrystal_degenerate` (degenerate): For n = 0 (a boundary case outside the node's n ≥ 1), Kl_1 ≅ L_π|_{G_m} and its trace at z_0 ∈ F_{q^r}^× is ψ(Tr z_0) with ψ = ψ_π^{-1}.
- `kloostermanIsocrystal_euler` (compatibility): χ(G_m, Kl_{n+1}) = −Swan_∞(Kl_{n+1}) = −1, as RD.6/christol-mebkhout-global-euler-characteristic and RD.6/irregularity-equals-swan predict for a coefficient unipotent at 0.
- `kloostermanIsocrystal_not_unipotent_infinity` (non-example): Kl_{n+1} is not unipotent at ∞: its Swan conductor there is 1, so no finite tame base change trivialises the local monodromy.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Sperber's Dwork-theoretic computation identifies the relative cohomology with the free module of rank n + 1 carrying the hypergeometric connection (Crew 1994 §1.5, citing Sperber §6); Crew 1994 Proposition 1.2 shows that connection is overconvergent.
2. The Frobenius structure is induced from that of L_π by functoriality of relative rigid cohomology (Crew 1994 §1.5, citing Berthelot).
3. Traces: the fibre at z_0 is H^n_rig of pr^{-1}(z_0) ≅ G_m^n with coefficient f^*L_π, which agrees with H^n_{c,rig} there, all other degrees vanishing (base change to fibres and this forget-supports isomorphism are part of the imported input); the parent RD.6/lefschetz-trace-formula on the fibre together with the trace function of L_π (RD.6/dwork-kummer-sign-dictionary) then gives the Kloosterman sum with the sign (−1)^n.

**Checks.**

- n = 1: Kl_2 has rank 2, and Tr(F_{z_0}) = −Σ_{x ∈ F_q^×} ψ(x + z_0/x), the classical Kloosterman sum with a sign.
- Trace of the second power at z_0 ∈ F_q^× for n = 1: Tr(F_{z_0}^2) = (Tr F_{z_0})^2 − 2·det F_{z_0} with det F_{z_0} = q (the two eigenvalues are conjugate of weight 1, with product q). Since Tr(F_{z_0}^r) = −Kl_2(z_0; q^r), this is the classical relation Kl_2(z_0; q^2) = 2q − Kl_2(z_0; q)^2, equivalently the Kloosterman L-function 1 + Kl_2(z_0; q)t + qt^2 (Carlitz); checked numerically for q = 3, 5, 7, 11.

<a id="target-rd-6-kloosterman-local-monodromy-and-purity"></a>

### Local monodromy and purity of the Kloosterman F-isocrystal

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.6/kloosterman-local-monodromy-and-purity` · theorem

In the setting of RD.6/kloosterman-f-isocrystal: (a) Kl_{n+1} is unipotent at 0 with nilpotent residue a single Jordan block of size n + 1; (b) at ∞ it is totally wild: its local monodromy is irreducible of rank n + 1 with all breaks equal to 1/(n + 1), so Irr_∞ = Swan_∞ = 1; (c) H^0_rig(G_m, Kl_{n+1}) = 0 and dim H^1_rig(G_m, Kl_{n+1}) = 1; (d) Kl_{n+1} is ι-pure of weight n for every ι : K^alg → C, i.e. every eigenvalue of F_{z_0} is a Weil q^{deg z_0}-number of weight n.

**Hypotheses.**

- p odd, p ∤ n + 1.

**Prerequisites.** [The Kloosterman F-isocrystal Kl_{n+1}](#target-rd-6-kloosterman-f-isocrystal) (`RD.6/kloosterman-f-isocrystal`), [Irregularity equals Swan conductor for overconvergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-6-irregularity-equals-swan) (`RD.6/irregularity-equals-swan`), [Christol–Mebkhout global p-adic Euler–Poincaré formula with irregularities](#target-rd-6-christol-mebkhout-global-euler-characteristic) (`RD.6/christol-mebkhout-global-euler-characteristic`), [Purity of H^1 on the affine line via the Fourier transform](#target-rd-6-purity-via-fourier-on-affine-line) (`RD.6/purity-via-fourier-on-affine-line`), [Pointwise ι-weights of overconvergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-6-pointwise-iota-weights) (`RD.6/pointwise-iota-weights`), [Break multiset and differential Swan conductor of a solvable ∇-module](#target-rd-1-differential-swan-conductor) (`RD.1/differential-swan-conductor`), [Unipotent ∇-modules are the modules V ⊗ R with nilpotent residue](#target-rd-2-unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue) (`RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue`), `DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.0/characteristic-power-series-and-traces`, `DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.0/weil-q-number`.

**Sources.**

- [S86](#source-86), Proposition 1.2 and its proof, pp. 5-8. Local form of the connection at 0 (unipotent, single block) and at ∞ (after pullback by the (n+1)-st power map).
- [S86](#source-86), Section 1.5, p. 11. Eigenvalues of Frobenius on fibres are algebraic integers pure of weight n − 1 for the rank-n isocrystal, by Deligne's ℓ-adic theorem and equality of traces.
- [S93](#source-93), Sections 3.2.1-3.2.2, pp. 23-25. Kl_{n+1} is lisse of rank n + 1 and pure of weight n (Deligne) in the ℓ-adic case; the rigid Kl_{n+1} has rank n + 1 and is pure of weight n.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a) Near 0 the hypergeometric connection is equivalent to (1.2.1) of Crew 1994, a unipotent connection with a single nilpotent block (Crew 1994 proof of Proposition 1.2).
2. (b) After pullback along z ↦ z^{n+1} the connection at ∞ splits into Dwork-type rank-one pieces of break 1 (Crew 1994 proof of Proposition 1.2), so the breaks before pullback are 1/(n + 1) (RD.1/differential-swan-conductor, behaviour under tame pullback); Irr_∞ = 1 and Swan_∞ = 1 by RD.6/irregularity-equals-swan.
3. (c) By RD.6/christol-mebkhout-global-euler-characteristic, χ(G_m, Kl_{n+1}) = (n + 1)·0 − 0 − 1 = −1; H^0 = 0 because the monodromy at ∞ has no invariants.
4. (d) The characteristic polynomial of F_{z_0} is determined by the traces of its powers (DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.0/characteristic-power-series-and-traces (iii)), which are Kloosterman sums over all extensions of F_{q^{deg z_0}}; these coincide with the Frobenius traces of Deligne's ℓ-adic Kloosterman sheaf, which is pure of weight n (Deligne, SGA 4½ Sommes trigonométriques 7.4 and 7.8, as used by Crew 1994 §1.5 and Fresán–Sabbah–Yu §3.2.1). The ℓ-adic theorem is not planned by any roadmap this one may cite (its atlas owner, FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums:FF.2, lies outside them); an intrinsic rigid proof via the Fourier transform (parent RD.6/purity-via-fourier-on-affine-line, applied to the localized Fourier transform description of Fresán–Sabbah–Yu §3.2.2) is the route this roadmap plans, and its verification is recorded as a gap.

**Checks.**

- n = 1: the two Frobenius eigenvalues at z_0 ∈ F_q^× have absolute value √q under every ι, the Weil bound |Kl_2(z_0; q)| ≤ 2√q.
- χ(G_m, Kl_{n+1}) = −1.

<a id="target-rd-6-symmetric-power-kloosterman-middle-cohomology"></a>

### Middle rigid cohomology of symmetric powers of Kloosterman F-isocrystals

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.6/symmetric-power-kloosterman-middle-cohomology` · theorem

In the setting of RD.6/kloosterman-f-isocrystal, let k ≥ 1, f̃_k the function on G_m^{kn+1} attached to Sym^k (Fresán–Sabbah–Yu (3.9) and §3.2.1), 𝒦 ⊂ G_m^{kn} the hypersurface of Fresán–Sabbah–Yu (3.9), and χ_n the character of S_k × μ_{n+1} there. Then: (a) for ? ∈ {∅, c, mid}, H^1_{rig,?}(G_m/K, Sym^k Kl_{n+1}) ≅ H^{kn+1}_{rig,?}(G_m^{kn+1}/K, f̃_k^*L_π)^{S_k × μ_{n+1}, χ_n}; (b) H^1_{rig,mid}(G_m/K, Sym^k Kl_{n+1}) is ι-pure of weight kn + 1 for every ι and ≅ gr^W_{kn+1} H^{kn+1}_{rig,c}(G_m^{kn+1}/K, f̃_k^*L_π)^{S_k × μ_{n+1}, χ_n}; (c) if kn ≥ 2, it is ≅ gr^W_{kn+1}[H^{kn−1}_{rig,c}(𝒦/K)(−1)]^{S_k × μ_{n+1}, χ_n} ≅ gr^W_{kn+1} H^{kn+1}_{rig,𝒦}(G_m^{kn}/K)^{S_k × μ_{n+1}, χ_n}, and when 𝒦 is smooth also ≅ gr^W_{kn+1}[H^{kn−1}_rig(𝒦/K)(−1)]^{S_k × μ_{n+1}, χ_n}. The comparison of this Frobenius module with p-adic Galois representations and its dimension formula belong to RD.7.

**Hypotheses.**

- p odd, p ∤ n + 1, k ≥ 1; (c) needs kn ≥ 2, as in Fresán–Sabbah–Yu Theorems 3.8 and 3.12; the S_k × μ_{n+1}-isotypic parts are taken for the character χ_n of Fresán–Sabbah–Yu.
- Inputs from rigid cohomology used by the source and imported here: the localized Fourier transform description of the pullback of Kl_{n+1} along the (n+1)-st power map, Künneth (RD.5/kunneth-formula-with-supports), localization sequences and Tsuzuki's Gysin isomorphism (RD.4/gysin-isomorphism).

**Prerequisites.** [The Kloosterman F-isocrystal Kl_{n+1}](#target-rd-6-kloosterman-f-isocrystal) (`RD.6/kloosterman-f-isocrystal`), [Local monodromy and purity of the Kloosterman F-isocrystal](#target-rd-6-kloosterman-local-monodromy-and-purity) (`RD.6/kloosterman-local-monodromy-and-purity`), [Middle rigid cohomology of a pure coefficient is pure](#target-rd-6-middle-cohomology-is-pure) (`RD.6/middle-cohomology-is-pure`), [Weight–monodromy purity at the points at infinity of a curve](#target-rd-6-local-monodromy-weight-purity) (`RD.6/local-monodromy-weight-purity`), [The Fourier transform agrees with the geometric Fourier transform](#target-rd-6-fourier-transform-comparison) (`RD.6/fourier-transform-comparison`), [The Dwork (Artin–Schreier) isocrystal L_π](#target-rd-6-dwork-isocrystal) (`RD.6/dwork-isocrystal`), [The Künneth formula with supports for smooth varieties (Kedlaya, (1.2.4.2))](#target-rd-5-kunneth-formula-with-supports) (`RD.5/kunneth-formula-with-supports`), [The Gysin isomorphism for smooth liftable pairs](#target-rd-4-gysin-isomorphism) (`RD.4/gysin-isomorphism`), [The excision long exact sequence for compact-support rigid cohomology](#target-rd-4-excision-sequence) (`RD.4/excision-sequence`).

**Sources.**

- [S93](#source-93), Section 3.2.2, (3.13)-(3.14) and the following isomorphisms, p. 25. Rigid cohomology of Sym^k Kl_{n+1} on G_m equals an isotypic part of the cohomology of the pullback of Dwork's F-isocrystal on a torus; the middle part is gr^W_{kn+1} of compactly supported cohomology and is expressed through the hypersurface 𝒦.
- [S93](#source-93), Section 3.2.1, Theorem 3.12 and the argument before it, pp. 23-25. The ℓ-adic argument the rigid case follows step by step.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a) The pullback of Kl_{n+1} along z ↦ z^{n+1} is the localized Fourier transform of a pushforward of the constant coefficient; Fourier transform exchanges tensor product and additive convolution, so its k-th tensor power is the relative cohomology of f̃_k^*L_π (Fresán–Sabbah–Yu §3.2.1, transported to rigid cohomology in §3.2.2 via parent RD.6/fourier-transform-comparison); taking S_k × μ_{n+1}-isotypic parts gives (3.13).
2. (b) Purity of H^1_mid is RD.6/middle-cohomology-is-pure with Sym^k Kl_{n+1} ι-pure of weight kn (RD.6/kloosterman-local-monodromy-and-purity); the local contributions at 0 and ∞ are mixed of weights ≤ kn (RD.6/local-monodromy-weight-purity), giving (3.14).
3. (c) The localization sequence for A^1 × 𝒦 ⊂ A^1 × G_m^{kn}, the vanishing of the cohomology of L_π on A^1 (parent RD.6/dwork-isocrystal) after the change of variables s = t·g, Künneth and the Gysin isomorphism reduce H^{kn+1}_{rig,c} to H^{kn−1}_{rig,c}(𝒦)(−1) (Fresán–Sabbah–Yu §3.2.2, last paragraph).

**Checks.**

- n = k = 1 (outside (c)): H^1_{c,rig}(G_m, Kl_2) is one-dimensional and is the image of the one-dimensional local invariants at 0, of weight 0 (RD.6/local-monodromy-weight-purity; the local invariants at ∞ vanish), so the forget-supports map is zero and H^1_mid(G_m, Kl_2) = 0, the rigid counterpart of Fresán–Sabbah–Yu Remark 3.7.
- Weights: for n = 1 the middle cohomology is pure of weight k + 1, matching the motives of symmetric power moments of Kloosterman sums.

## RD.7 — Coefficient comparisons and Weil-factor export

Package the smooth proper coefficient comparison with p- and q-Frobenius distinguished. Weight separation and rational-series descent/Fatou give rational, integral individual Weil factors and their étale comparison, followed by abelian-variety and point-counting exports. Hyperelliptic and Tuitman certificates retain denominator and twisted-matrix-order checks. Mieda’s rigid/log-crystalline map is distinct from the period-ring comparisons needed by the Kloosterman Galois applications.

**Landmarks.** Weight separation of Weil factors, Katz–Messing comparison of Weil factors, Weil-factor export, Ogus comparison with coefficients, Tuitman's point-counting algorithm.

### Worked checks

- P^1 over F_q has factors 1 − t, 1 and 1 − qt. Crystalline and rigid H^2 are both K_0, with linear Frobenius q.
- y^2 = x^3 + x + 1 over F_7 is ordinary: a = 3 and P_1 = 1 − 3t + 7t^2, with slopes 0 and 1 and weights 1. y^2 = x^3 + x over F_7 is supersingular: P_1 = 1 + 7t^2 over F_7 and (1 + 7t)^2 over F_49, with slopes 1/2.
- For y^2 = x^5 + x + 3 over F_7, the factor P_1 is 1 + 3t + 7t^2 + 21t^3 + 49t^4. Its coefficients are recovered modulo 7^3 from Tuitman's bound B = 3, and #C(F_7) = 11.
- For Q = x^3 + x + 1 and p = 5, the reduction of y dx needs the factor 5. The bound printed in Kedlaya's Lemma 3 fails here, and so does the errata formula read in that lemma's indexing.


<a id="target-rd-7-frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison"></a>

### The comparison matches the q-Frobenius with the f-th iterate of crystalline Frobenius

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison` · lemma

Let k = F_q with q = p^f, W = W(F_q), K_0 = W[1/p], X smooth proper over F_q, and φ the σ-semilinear crystalline Frobenius on H^i_crys(X/W) induced by the absolute Frobenius of X and the Witt vector Frobenius σ (CrystallineCohomology:CR.3). Under RD.7/rigid-crystalline-comparison, the linear q-Frobenius F on H^i_rig(X/K_0) (RD.6/linear-q-frobenius) corresponds to φ^f ⊗ 1. Since σ^f = id on W(F_q), φ^f is W-linear, and det(1 − tF | H^i_rig(X/K_0)) = det(1 − tφ^f | H^i_crys(X/W) ⊗ K_0).

**Hypotheses.**

- k = F_q, q = p^f; X smooth proper over F_q.

**Prerequisites.** [The rational rigid–crystalline comparison for smooth proper varieties](#target-rd-7-rigid-crystalline-comparison) (`RD.7/rigid-crystalline-comparison`), [The linear q-power Frobenius on rigid cohomology over F_q](#target-rd-6-linear-q-frobenius) (`RD.6/linear-q-frobenius`), [The Frobenius on rigid cohomology](#target-rd-4-frobenius-on-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.4/frobenius-on-rigid-cohomology`), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.3`.

**Sources.**

- [S5](#source-5), §2 opening, p. 9. The q-power Frobenius lift is a power of the Witt vector Frobenius.
- [S3](#source-3), Definition 8.1, p. 20. Rigid cohomology carries the Frobenius structure by functoriality.
- [S6](#source-6), §4, Step 3, p. 8. In computations the q-Frobenius is the product M M^σ ⋯ M^{σ^{n−1}} of σ-conjugates of the p-power Frobenius matrix.

**Construction or proof.**

1. The comparison of RD.7/rigid-crystalline-comparison is natural for morphisms of pairs (X/k over W) lying over ring endomorphisms of W; apply it to (Fr_X, σ), the absolute Frobenius over the Witt vector Frobenius.
2. The q-Frobenius on rigid cohomology is induced by Fr_X^f over σ^f = id (independence of the Frobenius lift, RD.4/frobenius-on-rigid-cohomology; RD.6/linear-q-frobenius), and φ^f is induced by the same pair on crystalline cohomology (functoriality in CR.3), so the two agree.
3. φ^f is σ^f-semilinear, and σ^f is the identity of W(F_q), so φ^f is linear.

**Checks.**

- P^1: with η the generator of H^2_crys(P^1/W), φ(aη) = p·σ(a)η, so φ^f(aη) = q·aη and the linear q-Frobenius is q.
- Non-example: for f ≥ 2, φ itself is not W-linear, and the characteristic polynomial of its matrix depends on the basis; only φ^f has a well-defined characteristic polynomial.

<a id="target-rd-7-weil-factor"></a>

### The Weil factors P_i of a smooth proper variety over F_q

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/weil-factor` · definition

For X smooth proper over F_q and 0 ≤ i ≤ 2 dim X, the i-th Weil factor is P_i(X, t) := det(1 − tF | H^i_rig(X/K)) ∈ 1 + tK[t], F the linear q-Frobenius; by RD.7/frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison it equals det(1 − tφ^f | H^i_crys(X/W) ⊗ K_0) and in particular lies in 1 + tK_0[t], independent of K. Its degree is b_i := dim H^i_rig(X/K) (F is bijective).

**Hypotheses.**

- X smooth proper over F_q, q = p^f.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/CrystallineComparison`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [The comparison matches the q-Frobenius with the f-th iterate of crystalline Frobenius](#target-rd-7-frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison) (`RD.7/frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison`), [Finite dimensionality of rigid cohomology with coefficients (Kedlaya, Theorem 1.2.1)](#target-rd-5-finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.5/finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology`), [Frobenius is bijective on rigid cohomology of a smooth variety](#target-rd-6-frobenius-bijective-on-smooth) (`RD.6/frobenius-bijective-on-smooth`), [The linear q-power Frobenius on rigid cohomology over F_q](#target-rd-6-linear-q-frobenius) (`RD.6/linear-q-frobenius`).

**Sources.**

- [S5](#source-5), §6.6, p. 52. Kedlaya's choice of the factors P_i.
- [S7](#source-7), §1, (1.3), p. 34 (text checked on the page image). The factors in the Monsky–Washnitzer normalisation (dual to P_i of compactly supported cohomology).

**Uses and API requirements.**

- WeilConjectures:WC.6: the crystalline Frobenius characteristic polynomials exported with their integrality and ℓ-adic comparison
- Kedlaya, point counting §3: the characteristic polynomial of F on H^1(A; K)^− of a hyperelliptic curve is its Weil polynomial
- Katz–Messing (as cited by Kedlaya, Weil II §1.1): crystalline Weil conjectures

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `weilFactor` |  | P_i(X, t) = det(1 − tF \| H^i_rig(X/K)) ∈ K[t]. |
| `weilFactor_constantCoeff` |  | P_i(X, 0) = 1. |
| `weilFactor_natDegree` |  | deg P_i = b_i = dim H^i_rig(X/K). |
| `weilFactor_eq_crys` |  | P_i(X, t) = det(1 − tφ^f \| H^i_crys(X/W) ⊗ K_0). |
| `weilFactor_zeta` |  | Z(X, t) = ∏_i P_i(X, t)^{(−1)^{i+1}} (RD.7/rigid-zeta-expression). |
| `weilFactor_functionalEquation` |  | P_{2n−i}(t) = c_i t^{b_i} P_i(q^{−n} t^{−1}) (RD.6/rigid-functional-equation). |
| `weilFactor_mem_int` |  | P_i(X, t) ∈ 1 + tZ[t] with reciprocal roots Weil q-numbers of weight i (RD.7/weil-factors-rational-and-integral). |
| `weilFactor_baseChange` |  | P_i(X_{F_{q^r}}, t^r) = ∏_{ζ^r = 1} P_i(X, ζt). |
| `weilFactor_eq_ellAdic` |  | P_i(X, t) = det(1 − t Frob_q \| H^i(X_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ)) for ℓ ≠ p (RD.7/ell-adic-comparison-smooth-projective, -proper). |

**Unit tests.**

- `weilFactor_projectiveLine` (computation): P_0(P^1) = 1 − t, P_1(P^1) = 1, P_2(P^1) = 1 − qt.
- `weilFactor_ellipticOrdinary` (computation): For E: y^2 = x^3 + x + 1 over F_7, P_1(E, t) = 1 − 3t + 7t^2 (a_7 = 3, #E(F_7) = 5).
- `weilFactor_point` (degenerate): For X = Spec F_q, P_0 = 1 − t and all other P_i = 1.
- `weilFactor_semilinear_basis` (non-example): On a one-dimensional K_0-space with φ(e) = u·e (q = p^2), replacing e by c·e changes the matrix of φ to u·σ(c)/c, so 'det(1 − tφ)' is not basis independent; the invariant is φ^2 with eigenvalue u·σ(u).
- `weilFactor_crys_compat` (compatibility): For X = P^1 over F_p, the matrix of φ on H^2_crys(P^1/Z_p) = Z_p is (p), so det(1 − tφ) = 1 − pt = P_2(P^1).

**Construction or proof.**

1. Finite dimensionality (RD.5/finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology) and bijectivity of F (RD.6/frobenius-bijective-on-smooth) give a polynomial of degree b_i with constant term 1.
2. Independence of K: H^i_rig(X/K) = H^i_rig(X/K_0) ⊗ K compatibly with F (RD.7/rigid-crystalline-comparison).

**Checks.**

- P_0(P^1) = 1 − t, P_1(P^1) = 1, P_2(P^1) = 1 − qt.

<a id="target-rd-7-rigid-zeta-expression"></a>

### The rigid and crystalline zeta expressions for every finite extension

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/rigid-zeta-expression` · lemma

Let X be smooth proper over F_q. For every r ≥ 1, #X(F_{q^r}) = Σ_i (−1)^i Tr(F^r | H^i_rig(X/K)) = Σ_i (−1)^i Tr(φ^{fr} | H^i_crys(X/W) ⊗ K_0), and Z(X, t) = ∏_i P_i(X, t)^{(−1)^{i+1}} in K[[t]]; for the base change X_{F_{q^r}}, Z(X_{F_{q^r}}, t) = ∏_i det(1 − tF^r | H^i_rig(X/K))^{(−1)^{i+1}}.

**Hypotheses.**

- X smooth proper over F_q.

**Prerequisites.** [The rigid Lefschetz trace formula for Frobenius](#target-rd-6-lefschetz-trace-formula) (`RD.6/lefschetz-trace-formula`), [Base change of rigid cohomology to F_{q^r}](#target-rd-6-base-change-to-finite-extension-of-fq) (`RD.6/base-change-to-finite-extension-of-fq`), [The comparison matches the q-Frobenius with the f-th iterate of crystalline Frobenius](#target-rd-7-frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison) (`RD.7/frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison`), [The Weil factors P_i of a smooth proper variety over F_q](#target-rd-7-weil-factor) (`RD.7/weil-factor`), [Rigid cohomology with compact supports H^i_{c,rig}(X/K, E)](#target-rd-4-compactly-supported-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.4/compactly-supported-rigid-cohomology`), `DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.0/characteristic-power-series-and-traces`.

**Sources.**

- [S5](#source-5), §6.6 (a), p. 51. The rigid zeta expression.
- [S3](#source-3), Remark 9.7, p. 22–23. The compact-support trace formula.

**Construction or proof.**

1. X proper: H^i_c = H^i (RD.4/compactly-supported-rigid-cohomology).
2. The rigid trace formula (RD.6/lefschetz-trace-formula) with constant coefficients, and base change to F_{q^r} (RD.6/base-change-to-finite-extension-of-fq).
3. Crystalline form: RD.7/frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison.
4. The zeta function Z(X, t) = exp(Σ #X(F_{q^r}) t^r/r) and its Euler product are those of RD.6/closed-points-and-zeta-function.

**Checks.**

- P^1: #P^1(F_{q^r}) = 1 + q^r.
- E: y^2 = x^3 + x over F_7: #E(F_7) = 8 = 1 − 0 + 7 and #E(F_49) = 64 = 1 − (−14) + 49 (PARI/GP and brute force), with Tr(F^2 | H^1) = a_7^2 − 2·7 = −14.

<a id="target-rd-7-rational-zeta-descent-and-fatou"></a>

### Rational power series descend to Q and have integral normalised numerator and denominator (Fatou)

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/rational-zeta-descent-and-fatou` · lemma

(a) Descent of rationality. Let k ⊂ L be fields and f ∈ k[[t]]. If there are A, B ∈ L[t] with B(0) ≠ 0 and Bf = A in L[[t]], then there are such A, B in k[t]; that is, k[[t]] ∩ L(t) = k(t) inside L((t)). (b) Local Fatou. Let ℓ be a prime (ℓ = p allowed), f ∈ 1 + tZ_ℓ[[t]], and G, H ∈ Q_ℓ[t] coprime with G(0) = H(0) = 1 and Hf = G. Then G, H ∈ Z_ℓ[t]. (c) Global Fatou. If f ∈ 1 + tZ[[t]] lies in Q(t), there are unique coprime A, B ∈ 1 + tZ[t] with f = A/B; the reciprocal roots of A and of B are algebraic integers. The equality is in Q[[t]], and A, B do not depend on any auxiliary field in which f was first shown to be rational.

**Hypotheses.**

- (a): any field extension k ⊂ L.
- (b): f has ℓ-adically integral coefficients and constant term 1; G, H coprime with constant term 1.
- (c): f has integer coefficients and constant term 1.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:PowerSeries.ext`, `mathlib:IsIntegrallyClosed.eq_map_mul_C_of_dvd`.

**Sources.**

- [S95](#source-95), §1, proof of (1.7) ⇒ (1.6), pp. 276–277. Shows by Hankel determinants that the integral zeta series, rational over Q_ℓ, is rational over Q, and invokes Fatou's lemma to make the coprime integral numerator and denominator have constant term 1.
- [S96](#source-96), Lemma 27.9 and proof, pp. 156–157; Lemma 27.10 and proof, p. 158 (v2.21). Lemma 27.9: rationality over a larger field descends to the smaller field (via Bourbaki's exercise). Lemma 27.10: coprime normalised numerator and denominator of an ℓ-adically integral rational series are ℓ-adically integral.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a) Bf = A with deg A ≤ N, deg B ≤ M is a system of linear equations over k in the coefficients of A and B (the vanishing of the Hankel determinants of order > M of the coefficient sequence of f beyond degree N); a system with coefficients in k that has a nonzero solution over L has one over k, and B(0) ≠ 0 may be arranged after cancelling a power of t (Deligne, Weil I, proof of (1.7) ⇒ (1.6), p. 276; Milne, Lemma 27.9).
2. (b) Work in a finite extension of Q_ℓ splitting H with the extended absolute value. If a reciprocal root α of H had |α| > 1, then α^{−1} lies in the open unit disc, where f converges because its coefficients are bounded by 1, and evaluating Hf = G at α^{−1} gives G(α^{−1}) = 0, contradicting coprimality. So the reciprocal roots of H have absolute value at most 1; since 1/f ∈ 1 + tZ_ℓ[[t]] and (1/f)G = H, the same holds for G. Elementary symmetric functions of elements of absolute value ≤ 1 have absolute value ≤ 1 (Milne, Lemma 27.10, with the non-strict inequality at the boundary).
3. (c) Write f = A/B in lowest terms over Q with A(0) = B(0) = 1 (possible since f(0) = 1 and B(0) ≠ 0 after (a)); apply (b) at every prime ℓ to get A, B ∈ Z_ℓ[t] for all ℓ, hence A, B ∈ Z[t]. Reciprocal roots of a polynomial in 1 + tZ[t] are roots of its reverse, a monic integer polynomial, hence algebraic integers (Deligne, Weil I, p. 276, 'lemme de Fatou').

**Checks.**

- Z(P^1_{F_q}, t) = 1/((1 − t)(1 − qt)): A = 1, B = (1 − t)(1 − qt) ∈ 1 + tZ[t].
- Integrality cannot be dropped: f = 1/(1 − t/2) ∈ 1 + tQ[[t]] is rational with denominator 1 − t/2 ∉ Z[t].
- Coprimality cannot be dropped in (b): G = H = 1 − t/ℓ with f = 1 shows that a non-reduced presentation need not be integral.
- Boundary case: f = 1/(1 − t) ∈ 1 + tZ_ℓ[[t]] has a reciprocal root of absolute value exactly 1, so the bound in (b) is ≤ 1, not < 1.

<a id="target-rd-7-weight-separated-factor-extraction"></a>

### Weight separation: pure factors of a rational zeta function are unique, rational and integral

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/weight-separated-factor-extraction` · theorem

Let q > 1 be an integer and R ∈ 1 + tZ[[t]] ∩ Q(t), written R = A/B with A, B ∈ 1 + tZ[t] coprime (RD.7/rational-zeta-descent-and-fatou). Let L be a field of characteristic 0 with algebraic closure L̄ and P_0, …, P_N ∈ 1 + tL[t] with ∏_{i=0}^{N} P_i^{(−1)^{i+1}} = R in L[[t]], such that every reciprocal root of P_i in L̄ is algebraic over Q and a Weil q-number of weight i (DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.0/weil-q-number). Then: (1) the P_i are pairwise coprime, and A = ∏_{i odd} P_i, B = ∏_{i even} P_i in L[t]; (2) for each i there is a unique Π_i ∈ 1 + tZ[t] whose image in L[t] is P_i, namely Π_i = ∏(1 − αt)^{m(α)}, the product over the reciprocal roots α of A (i odd) or B (i even) that are Weil q-numbers of weight i, with their multiplicities m(α) as roots; (3) the reciprocal roots of Π_i are algebraic integers and deg Π_i = deg P_i; (4) if (P'_i) is a second family over another field L' of characteristic 0 with the same R and the same purity property, then P_i and P'_i are images of the same Π_i. The integrality in (2)–(3) comes from Fatou's lemma and the separation of weights, not from the alternating product alone; without purity, cancellation between degrees can occur and the factors are not determined by R.

**Hypotheses.**

- q > 1 an integer; R ∈ 1 + tZ[[t]] rational.
- L a field of characteristic 0; P_i ∈ 1 + tL[t] with alternating product R.
- Every reciprocal root of P_i is a Weil q-number of weight i (all complex conjugates of absolute value q^{i/2}).

**Prerequisites.** [Rational power series descend to Q and have integral normalised numerator and denominator (Fatou)](#target-rd-7-rational-zeta-descent-and-fatou) (`RD.7/rational-zeta-descent-and-fatou`), `DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.0/weil-q-number`, `DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.0/weil-number-arithmetic`, `mathlib:IsGalois.mem_range_algebraMap_iff_fixed`, `mathlib:IsIntegrallyClosed.eq_map_mul_C_of_dvd`.

**Sources.**

- [S95](#source-95), §1, proof of (1.7) ⇒ (1.6), pp. 276–277. From purity of every eigenvalue the factors P_i are pairwise coprime, so the cohomological product is already reduced; each factor's roots are the roots of the reduced numerator or denominator with the right absolute value, a Galois-stable set, so the factor has rational, then (Gauss, or integrality of the reciprocal roots) integral coefficients independent of the cohomology theory.
- [S96](#source-96), 27.14(c)–(d), p. 159 (v2.21). Summary statement that the factors P_i are integral and independent of ℓ once purity holds.
- [S5](#source-5), §6.6, statement (c) and its proof, pp. 51–52. Deduces from rigid Weil II (Theorem 6.6.2) and Poincaré duality that H^i_rig of a smooth proper variety is ι-pure of weight i for every ι, the purity input that this theorem turns into integral, realisation-independent factors.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Weights separate: a Weil q-number has a unique weight (DWP.0/weil-q-number), so P_i and P_j have no common root for i ≠ j; hence ∏_{i odd} P_i and ∏_{i even} P_i are coprime and their quotient is a reduced presentation of R over L. Comparing with the reduced presentation A/B over Q (both normalised by constant term 1) gives (1).
2. Let K ⊂ L̄ be the splitting field over Q of AB. The set of reciprocal roots of AB of weight i, with multiplicities, is stable under Gal(K/Q), because being a Weil q-number of weight i depends only on the minimal polynomial over Q (DWP.0/weil-q-number). So the coefficients of Π_i are fixed by Gal(K/Q) and lie in Q (mathlib:IsGalois.mem_range_algebraMap_iff_fixed).
3. The reverse of Π_i is a monic factor in Q[T] of the monic integral reverse of A or B, so by Gauss's lemma it has integer coefficients (mathlib:IsIntegrallyClosed.eq_map_mul_C_of_dvd); equivalently its roots are algebraic integers by RD.7/rational-zeta-descent-and-fatou (c).
4. Uniqueness and (4): Π_i is described by R alone, so any second pure family gives the same polynomials (Deligne, Weil I, end of the proof of (1.7) ⇒ (1.6), p. 277).

**Checks.**

- X = P^1_{F_q}: R = 1/((1 − t)(1 − qt)), P_0 = 1 − t (weight 0), P_1 = 1, P_2 = 1 − qt (weight 2).
- Elliptic curve E/F_7, y^2 = x^3 + x + 1: R = (1 − 3t + 7t^2)/((1 − t)(1 − 7t)) and Π_1 = 1 − 3t + 7t^2, whose roots have absolute value 7^{−1/2}.
- Purity is needed: P_0 = 1, P_1 = P_2 = 1 − 2t give the alternating product R = 1, as do P_0 = P_1 = P_2 = 1, so R does not determine the factors; the hypothesis excludes this because 2 cannot be a Weil q-number of weight 1 and of weight 2.
- Genus-two curve y^2 = x^5 + x + 3 over F_7: Π_1 = 1 + 3t + 7t^2 + 21t^3 + 49t^4 (PARI/GP hyperellcharpoly), with all roots of absolute value 7^{−1/2}.

<a id="target-rd-7-weil-factors-rational-and-integral"></a>

### The Weil factors are integral polynomials determined by weights

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/weil-factors-rational-and-integral` · theorem

Let X be smooth proper over F_q. For each i, P_i(X, t) ∈ 1 + tZ[t]; its reciprocal roots are Weil q-numbers of weight i (algebraic integers all of whose complex conjugates have absolute value q^{i/2}); P_i(X, t) = ∏_α (1 − αt)^{m(α)}, where α runs over the reciprocal zeros (i odd) or reciprocal poles (i even) of Z(X, t) of weight i and m(α) is the order; distinct P_i have no common root. Integrality is justified separately from the alternating product: it uses purity for every ι and Fatou's lemma, not the equality of zeta functions alone.

**Hypotheses.**

- X smooth proper over F_q.

**Prerequisites.** [The rigid and crystalline zeta expressions for every finite extension](#target-rd-7-rigid-zeta-expression) (`RD.7/rigid-zeta-expression`), [Purity of rigid cohomology of smooth proper varieties](#target-rd-6-purity-smooth-proper) (`RD.6/purity-smooth-proper`), [Slope bounds for rigid cohomology (p-adic weights)](#target-rd-6-slope-bounds-for-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.6/slope-bounds-for-rigid-cohomology`), [The Weil factors P_i of a smooth proper variety over F_q](#target-rd-7-weil-factor) (`RD.7/weil-factor`), `DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.0/iota-weight`, `DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.0/endomorphism-weights`, `DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.0/weil-number-iff-iota-pure-for-every-iota`, [Rational power series descend to Q and have integral normalised numerator and denominator (Fatou)](#target-rd-7-rational-zeta-descent-and-fatou) (`RD.7/rational-zeta-descent-and-fatou`), [Weight separation: pure factors of a rational zeta function are unique, rational and integral](#target-rd-7-weight-separated-factor-extraction) (`RD.7/weight-separated-factor-extraction`).

**Sources.**

- [S5](#source-5), §6.6 (c), p. 52. The Riemann hypothesis for the rigid factors.
- [S5](#source-5), §1.1, p. 3. Earlier route (Katz–Messing, not read in the inherited source pass) that this node replaces by p-adic purity.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Z(X, t) = ∏ P_i^{(−1)^{i+1}} (RD.7/rigid-zeta-expression) and Z ∈ Q(t) ∩ (1 + tZ[[t]]) (RD.6/closed-points-and-zeta-function).
2. First compute P_i over K_0 = W(F_q)[1/p], using RD.7/weil-factor and its coefficient-independence result. K_0 is a finite extension of Q_p and its algebraic closure has cardinality at most that of C. Purity holds for every embedding K_0^alg → C, so the exact DWP.0 all-embeddings bridge applies to each eigenvalue. Do not run this argument over an arbitrary larger K without the bridge’s cardinality hypothesis.
3. Weights separate degrees: for i ≠ j no root of P_i is a root of P_j, so no cancellation occurs in the alternating product.
4. Weight-separated factor identification (RD.7/weight-separated-factor-extraction): a factorisation of Z into polynomials with pairwise distinct pure weights is unique, each factor is the weight part of Z, is fixed by Gal(Q̄/Q) (weights are conjugation invariant) and so lies in Q[t]; by Fatou's lemma the reduced numerator and denominator of Z lie in 1 + tZ[t], so the reciprocal roots are algebraic integers and each P_i ∈ Z[t].
5. Consistency check: p-adic slopes of the roots lie in [0, i] (RD.6/slope-bounds-for-rigid-cohomology), confirming p-integrality.

**Checks.**

- P^1: P_0 = 1 − t, P_2 = 1 − qt ∈ Z[t].
- E/F_7 ordinary: P_1 = 1 − 3t + 7t^2, roots of modulus 7^{−1/2}; genus-2 curve y^2 = x^5 + x + 3 over F_7: Frobenius polynomial T^4 + 3T^3 + 7T^2 + 21T + 49 (PARI/GP hyperellcharpoly), integral, all roots of modulus √7.

<a id="target-rd-7-ell-adic-comparison-smooth-projective"></a>

### Crystalline, rigid and ℓ-adic Weil factors agree for smooth projective varieties (Katz–Messing)

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/ell-adic-comparison-smooth-projective` · theorem

Let X be smooth projective over F_q, q = p^f, and ℓ ≠ p. For every i, det(1 − tF | H^i_rig(X/K)) = det(1 − tφ^f | H^i_crys(X/W) ⊗ K_0) = det(1 − t·Frob_q | H^i(X_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ)) as elements of 1 + tZ[t] (Frob_q the geometric Frobenius), for every finite extension F_{q^r} as well. In particular b_i^{rig} = b_i^{crys ⊗ Q} = b_i^{ℓ}.

**Hypotheses.**

- X smooth projective over F_q; ℓ ≠ p.

**Prerequisites.** [The Weil factors are integral polynomials determined by weights](#target-rd-7-weil-factors-rational-and-integral) (`RD.7/weil-factors-rational-and-integral`), [The comparison matches the q-Frobenius with the f-th iterate of crystalline Frobenius](#target-rd-7-frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison) (`RD.7/frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison`), `DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.4/smooth-projective-purity`, [Weight separation: pure factors of a rational zeta function are unique, rational and integral](#target-rd-7-weight-separated-factor-extraction) (`RD.7/weight-separated-factor-extraction`).

**Sources.**

- [S5](#source-5), §1.1, p. 3. Public statement that Katz–Messing established the crystalline Weil conjectures (via Deligne).
- [S3](#source-3), abstract, p. 1. Rigid cohomology as the p-adic Weil cohomology.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Étale side: use the Grothendieck–Lefschetz formula for all finite extensions and its determinant/zeta identity, whose supplier interface is CohomologicalPointCounting/TraceFormula Layers 12–13 (the all-power étale trace theorem is a separate supplier obligation). The finite-field zeta arithmetic alone does not prove the étale trace identity. Each degree-i factor is pure of weight i for every complex embedding by DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.4/smooth-projective-purity (Weil I Lemma 1.7).
2. Rigid side: RD.7/weil-factors-rational-and-integral.
3. Both are weight-separated factorisations of the same Z(X, t) ∈ Q(t); by uniqueness (RD.7/weight-separated-factor-extraction) the i-th factors coincide in Q[t].
4. Crystalline equality: RD.7/frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison.

**Checks.**

- P^n: all three give P_{2j} = 1 − q^j t and P_{odd} = 1.
- E/F_7 supersingular (y^2 = x^3 + x): all three give 1 + 7t^2.

<a id="target-rd-7-ell-adic-comparison-smooth-proper"></a>

### Crystalline, rigid and ℓ-adic Weil factors agree for smooth proper varieties

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/ell-adic-comparison-smooth-proper` · theorem

The conclusion of RD.7/ell-adic-comparison-smooth-projective holds for every smooth proper X over F_q (not necessarily projective).

**Hypotheses.**

- X smooth proper over F_q; ℓ ≠ p.

**Prerequisites.** [The Weil factors are integral polynomials determined by weights](#target-rd-7-weil-factors-rational-and-integral) (`RD.7/weil-factors-rational-and-integral`), [The comparison matches the q-Frobenius with the f-th iterate of crystalline Frobenius](#target-rd-7-frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison) (`RD.7/frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison`), `DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.7/hodge-type-triangles-and-proper-smooth-purity-3-3-7-3-3-11`.

**Sources.**

- [S3](#source-3), Theorem 10.3 and proof, p. 27. Rigid purity holds without projectivity (Kedlaya's Weil II).
- [S5](#source-5), §6.6 (c), p. 52. Smooth proper, not projective, suffices on the rigid side.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Identical to the projective case, with ℓ-adic purity of H^i(X_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ) for smooth proper X supplied by Deligne's Weil II (3.3.9) (DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.7) instead of Weil I.
2. The rigid side needs no projectivity: RD.6/purity-smooth-proper holds for all smooth proper X.
3. The all-power étale trace/zeta input is the same CohomologicalPointCounting/TraceFormula Layers 12–13 supplier contract as in the projective case; properness identifies compactly supported with ordinary cohomology. Purity alone does not supply that trace formula.

**Checks.**

- A smooth proper non-projective threefold (Hironaka-type) has P_i^{rig} = P_i^{ℓ}; no explicit example is needed for the statement.

<a id="target-rd-7-weil-factor-export"></a>

### Weil-factor export to WeilConjectures:WC.6

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/weil-factor-export` · theorem

Export (interface RD.7/weil-factor-export). Let X be smooth proper over F_q, q = p^f, of dimension n, and P_i(X, t) := det(1 − tF | H^i_rig(X/K)) = det(1 − tφ^f | H^i_crys(X/W) ⊗ K_0). Then: (1) Z(X, t) = ∏_{i=0}^{2n} P_i(X, t)^{(−1)^{i+1}} as an equality in Q[[t]], hence in Q(t), and likewise for every finite extension F_{q^r}; (2) each P_i ∈ 1 + tZ[t], integrality being justified by purity for every ι and Fatou's lemma rather than by the alternating product; (3) the reciprocal roots of P_i are Weil q-numbers of weight i; (4) P_{2n−i}(t) = c_i t^{b_i} P_i(q^{−n}t^{−1}); (5) for ℓ ≠ p, P_i(X, t) = det(1 − t Frob_q | H^i(X_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ)) (projective X via DWP.4, proper X via DWP.7). No input from WeilConjectures:WC.6 is used.

**Hypotheses.**

- X smooth proper over F_q.

**Prerequisites.** [The rigid and crystalline zeta expressions for every finite extension](#target-rd-7-rigid-zeta-expression) (`RD.7/rigid-zeta-expression`), [The Weil factors are integral polynomials determined by weights](#target-rd-7-weil-factors-rational-and-integral) (`RD.7/weil-factors-rational-and-integral`), [Functional equation of the rigid Weil factors](#target-rd-6-rigid-functional-equation) (`RD.6/rigid-functional-equation`), [Crystalline, rigid and ℓ-adic Weil factors agree for smooth projective varieties (Katz–Messing)](#target-rd-7-ell-adic-comparison-smooth-projective) (`RD.7/ell-adic-comparison-smooth-projective`), [Crystalline, rigid and ℓ-adic Weil factors agree for smooth proper varieties](#target-rd-7-ell-adic-comparison-smooth-proper) (`RD.7/ell-adic-comparison-smooth-proper`), [The comparison matches the q-Frobenius with the f-th iterate of crystalline Frobenius](#target-rd-7-frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison) (`RD.7/frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison`).

**Sources.**

- [S5](#source-5), §6.6, p. 51. The rigid Weil conjectures exported here (with the corrections recorded in sourceIssues).
- [S3](#source-3), §10, p. 27. Rigid cohomology as a Weil cohomology.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): RD.7/rigid-zeta-expression; (2), (3): RD.7/weil-factors-rational-and-integral; (4): RD.6/rigid-functional-equation; (5): RD.7/ell-adic-comparison-smooth-projective and RD.7/ell-adic-comparison-smooth-proper.
2. The crystalline form of each factor: RD.7/frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison.

**Checks.**

- P^1: (1 − t)(1 − qt) in the denominator; all three cohomologies agree.
- Ordinary elliptic curve y^2 = x^3 + x + 1 over F_7: P_1 = 1 − 3t + 7t^2; supersingular y^2 = x^3 + x: P_1 = 1 + 7t^2 over F_7 and (1 + 7t)^2 over F_49.
- Hyperelliptic genus-2 curve y^2 = x^5 + x + 3 over F_7: P_1 = 1 + 3t + 7t^2 + 21t^3 + 49t^4 (the reversed Frobenius polynomial T^4 + 3T^3 + 7T^2 + 21T + 49 of PARI/GP hyperellcharpoly), and #C(F_7) = 7 + 1 − (−3) = 11 (brute force).

<a id="target-rd-7-de-rham-lift-insufficient"></a>

### A de Rham comparison over a lift does not give the finite-field Frobenius statement

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/de-rham-lift-insufficient` · comparison

Let X be smooth proper over F_q with a smooth proper formal lift 𝔛 over W. Berthelot's comparison H^i_crys(X/W) ⊗ K_0 ≅ H^i_dR(𝔛/W) ⊗ K_0 identifies the vector spaces but carries no Frobenius by itself: the linear q-Frobenius on H^i_dR(𝔛/W) ⊗ K_0 is only defined by transport from crystalline or rigid cohomology, because 𝔛 in general admits no endomorphism lifting Fr_X (and X in general admits no lift at all). Hence the equality of characteristic polynomials of RD.7/weil-factor-export is a statement about crystalline/rigid Frobenius and cannot be obtained from a de Rham comparison over the lift, nor from a characteristic-zero comparison on the generic fibre alone. Example: for a supersingular elliptic curve E over F_p (p ≥ 5), no lift 𝔈 over Z_p carries an endomorphism lifting Frobenius: its pullback would preserve the Hodge line H^0(𝔈, Ω^1) and act there by a root of T^2 + p in Z_p, which does not exist; for an ordinary E the canonical lift carries one (the unit root of T^2 − a_p T + p lies in Z_p by Hensel).

**Hypotheses.**

- X smooth proper over F_q with a smooth proper lift 𝔛 over W (when it exists).

**Prerequisites.** [The rational rigid–crystalline comparison for smooth proper varieties](#target-rd-7-rigid-crystalline-comparison) (`RD.7/rigid-crystalline-comparison`), [The comparison matches the q-Frobenius with the f-th iterate of crystalline Frobenius](#target-rd-7-frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison) (`RD.7/frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison`), [The Frobenius on rigid cohomology](#target-rd-4-frobenius-on-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.4/frobenius-on-rigid-cohomology`), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2/embedding-computation`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2/pd-poincare`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.3`.

**Sources.**

- [S20](#source-20), §1.2, p. 11 (text checked on the page image). Crystalline cohomology equals de Rham cohomology of a lift, rationally.
- [S20](#source-20), §1.2, p. 12 (text checked on the page image). Lifts need not exist.
- [S6](#source-6), §2, p. 2. Frobenius lifts exist only on completions, not on the lift itself.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Berthelot §1.2: for X smooth with a smooth formal lift, crystalline cohomology is de Rham cohomology of the lift (integrally if e ≤ p − 1, after ⊗K in general); the identification depends only on the lift, not on any Frobenius.
2. Frobenius on crystalline cohomology is induced by the absolute Frobenius of X (CrystallineCohomology:CR.3), and on rigid cohomology by any lift of Frobenius on a frame or dagger algebra (RD.4/frobenius-on-rigid-cohomology); lifts exist on weak completions of affine pieces, not globally on 𝔛 (Kedlaya, point counting §2).
3. Supersingular example: an endomorphism Π of 𝔈 lifting Fr would act on H^1_dR(𝔈) ≅ H^1_crys(E/Z_p) as φ (functoriality of the comparison, RD.7/rigid-crystalline-comparison), with characteristic polynomial T^2 − a_pT + p = T^2 + p, and would preserve the line H^0(Ω^1), whose eigenvalue would be a root of T^2 + p in Z_p; there is none (v_p would be 1/2).

**Checks.**

- Supersingular y^2 = x^3 + x over F_7: T^2 + 7 has no root in Z_7 (Newton slopes 1/2, 1/2).
- Ordinary y^2 = x^3 + x + 1 over F_7: T^2 − 3T + 7 has two roots in Z_7 (reduction T(T − 3) has simple roots): a unit root u and 7/u (slopes 0, 1); the canonical-lift Frobenius acts on the Hodge line by 7/u.

<a id="target-rd-7-elliptic-curve-slopes-versus-weights"></a>

### Elliptic curves and P^1: p-adic slopes versus complex weights

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/elliptic-curve-slopes-versus-weights` · application

Let E be an elliptic curve over F_q, q = p^f, and a := q + 1 − #E(F_q). Then P_1(E, t) = 1 − at + qt^2; both reciprocal roots have complex absolute value q^{1/2} (weight 1) for every embedding; their p-adic slopes (valuations normalised by v_p(q)) are {0, 1} if p ∤ a (ordinary) and {1/2, 1/2} if p | a (supersingular). For P^1 the eigenvalues 1 and q have weights 0, 2 and slopes 0, 1. Thus slope = weight/2 fails in general: slopes are not determined by weights, and both are needed to pin down eigenvalues (if the normalised algebraic number β = α/q^{w/2} is a unit at every finite place and has complex absolute value one at every embedding, Kronecker’s theorem makes β a root of unity; a slope condition at just one p-adic place is insufficient).

**Hypotheses.**

- E an elliptic curve over F_q.

**Prerequisites.** [Weil-factor export to WeilConjectures:WC.6](#target-rd-7-weil-factor-export) (`RD.7/weil-factor-export`), [The Weil factors are integral polynomials determined by weights](#target-rd-7-weil-factors-rational-and-integral) (`RD.7/weil-factors-rational-and-integral`), [p-adic slopes of Frobenius eigenvalues and slope intervals](#target-rd-6-slope-interval-of-isocrystal) (`RD.6/slope-interval-of-isocrystal`), [Slope bounds for rigid cohomology (p-adic weights)](#target-rd-6-slope-bounds-for-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.6/slope-bounds-for-rigid-cohomology`), [Frobenius slopes and Newton (HN) polygons of σ-modules: generic slopes over E and R^bd, special slopes over R](#target-rd-1-frobenius-slopes) (`RD.1/frobenius-slopes`).

**Sources.**

- [S5](#source-5), §6.7, p. 52. The slope dichotomy.
- [S5](#source-5), §1.5, p. 7. Eigenvalues with matching archimedean and p-adic sizes.

**Construction or proof.**

1. P_1 from RD.7/weil-factor-export (degree 2 = b_1; P_0, P_2 as for P^1 by Poincaré duality).
2. Weights: RD.7/weil-factors-rational-and-integral (purity for every ι).
3. Slopes: Newton polygon of T^2 − aT + q (RD.1/frobenius-slopes; RD.6/slope-interval-of-isocrystal); v_p(q) = f; p ∤ a gives slopes 0 and 1; For q = p ≥ 5, p | a and the Hasse bound force a = 0, giving valuation 1/2. For general q, the supersingular implication additionally uses the elliptic ordinary/supersingular p-rank dichotomy: p | a detects p-rank zero, whose height-two Newton polygon has both slopes 1/2. Hasse’s archimedean bound alone does not force v_p(a) ≥ f/2 for arbitrary f.
4. Slope bounds [0, 1] on H^1 agree with RD.6/slope-bounds-for-rigid-cohomology.

**Checks.**

- PARI/GP ellap and newtonpoly: y^2 = x^3 + x + 1 over F_7: a = 3, P = x^2 − 3x + 7, slopes (1, 0); over F_5: a = −3, slopes (1, 0); y^2 = x^3 + 2x + 3 over F_13: a = −4, slopes (1, 0); y^2 = x^3 + x over F_7 and F_11: a = 0, slopes (1/2, 1/2); all roots have modulus √p.
- y^2 = x^3 + x over F_49: a = −14, P = (x + 7)^2 (brute-force count #E(F_49) = 64); α = −7 = −q^{1/2} has slope 1/2 and weight 1, and α/q^{1/2} = −1 is a root of unity (Kedlaya §1.5).
- Global-unit negative control: α=(2+i)(1+√(−19))/2 is a weight-one Weil 25-number with polynomial T^4−4T^3+35T^2−100T+625. At p=5 its valuations are 0,1,1,2, so some normalised slopes are 1/2. Nevertheless α/5 is not a root of unity, since it is not integral at all places over 5.

<a id="target-rd-7-kedlaya-reduction-denominators"></a>

### Denominator bounds in the reduction of hyperelliptic differentials (Kedlaya Lemma 2, corrected Lemma 3)

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/kedlaya-reduction-denominators` · lemma

Let p be odd, q = p^n, Z_q = W(F_q), Q ∈ Z_q[x] monic of degree d = 2g + 1 with squarefree reduction, and A† the dagger algebra of the affine curve y^2 = Q(x) with the Weierstrass points removed (y invertible). The minus part H^1(A†)^− of its Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology has basis x^i dx/y, 0 ≤ i ≤ 2g − 1 (Edixhoven, Proposition 4.3.2). (a) (Kedlaya, Lemma 2; Edixhoven, Lemma 4.3.4.) For m ≥ 0 and B ∈ Z_q[x] of degree ≤ 2g, write B dx/y^{2m+1} = b dx/y + dφ with deg b ≤ 2g and φ = Σ_{j=1}^{m} F_j(x)/y^{2j−1}, deg F_j ≤ 2g; then p^{⌊log_p(2m+1)⌋}·b and p^{⌊log_p(2m+1)⌋}·F_j have coefficients in Z_q. (b) (Corrected Lemma 3; Edixhoven, Lemma 4.3.5; Harvey §4.) For m ≥ 0 and B ∈ Z_q[x] of degree ≤ 2g, write B·y^{2m+1} dx = b dx/y + dφ with deg b ≤ 2g and φ = Σ_{j=1}^{m+1} F_j(x)y^{2j−1}; then multiplication by p^{⌊log_p((2g+1)(2m+3) − 2)⌋} makes b and the F_j integral.
