Equivalently, for F(x)y^e dx with e > 0 odd the factor is p^{⌊log_p((2g+1)(e+2) − 2)⌋}. (c) Removing the remaining x^{2g} dx/y with the exact form dy = (Q'/2) dx/y divides by d = 2g + 1 and costs a further factor p^{v_p(2g+1)}. The bound printed as Lemma 3 in the source, p^{⌊log_p(2m+1)⌋}, is false, and so is the errata's replacement read literally in that lemma's indexing (sourceIssues E701).

**Hypotheses.**

- p odd; Q monic of degree 2g + 1 over Z_q with squarefree reduction modulo p.
- B ∈ Z_q[x] of degree at most 2g; m ≥ 0.

**Prerequisites.** [H^1 of the dagger algebra of a smooth affine curve is H^1_rig, with a lift-independent Frobenius](#target-rd-4-mw-comparison-for-affine-curves) (`RD.4/mw-comparison-for-affine-curves`), [The Gysin sequence of a punctured smooth proper curve](#target-rd-6-gysin-sequence-for-curves) (`RD.6/gysin-sequence-for-curves`).

**Sources.**

- [S97](#source-97), Lemma 2 and its proof, Lemma 3 as printed, p. 5 (arXiv v2). Lemma 2 bounds the denominators in reducing A(x)dx/y^{2m+1} by p^{⌊log_p(2m+1)⌋} through expansions at the Weierstrass points; Lemma 3 asserts the same bound for A(x)y^{2m+1}dx without proof.
- [S98](#source-98), list of errata, p. 1–2 (13 October 2003). Replaces 2m + 1 by d(m + 1) − 2 at the journal's page 331, line 8, and records Edixhoven's remark that the Frobenius matrix on the monomial basis is not integral.
- [S99](#source-99), Proposition 4.3.2, p. 12; Lemma 4.3.4, p. 13; Lemma 4.3.5, p. 14; §5.2, p. 17. Proves the basis statement, the negative-power bound p^{⌊log_p(m−1)⌋} for ay^{−m}dx/y (m even) and the positive-power bound p^{⌊log_p(dm+d−2)⌋} for ay^m dx/y (m even) by local expansions at the Weierstrass points and at infinity, and notes the extra division by d in the last step.
- [S100](#source-100), §4, proof of Proposition 2, p. 6 (arXiv v2). States the corrected positive-power multiplier p^{⌊log_p((2g+1)(e+2)−2)⌋} for F_j(x)y^e dx, citing the errata and Edixhoven's Lemma 4.3.5.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Negative powers: the poles of φ lie at the Weierstrass points T_i = (r_i, 0), where y is a uniformiser; expand dφ in y with integral coefficients for negative exponents, integrate termwise, and note that the denominators are the odd exponents of y down to −(2m+1); since the r_i are distinct modulo p, integrality of F_m(r_i) for all i forces integrality of F_m, and descending induction gives the rest (Kedlaya, proof of Lemma 2; Edixhoven, proof of 4.3.4).
2. Positive powers: the only pole is ∞, where v_∞(x) = −2, v_∞(y) = −d and z = x^{(d−1)/2}/y is a uniformiser with ι(z) = −z; expand dφ in z, whose coefficients are integral in exponents ≤ −d, integrate, and bound the denominators j + 1 by |j + 1| ≤ dm' + d − 2 for the even exponent m' = 2m + 2; the valuations v_∞(x^i y^j), 0 ≤ i < d, are distinct, which separates the F_j (Edixhoven, proof of 4.3.5).
3. The last reduction uses dy and divides by the leading coefficient d of Q' (Edixhoven, p. 17).
4. These bounds are what the working precision of the parent's RD.7/kedlaya-point-counting-certification (its items (iv)–(v)) absorbs. That node consumes this one, so it is not a prerequisite here (Harvey, §4, proof of Proposition 2, uses (b) with e = −p(2k + 1) + 2j).

**Checks.**

- Q = x^3 + x + 1, p = 5 (good reduction: disc = −31), m = 0: y dx = Q dx/y reduces to (2/5 x + 3/5) dx/y + d((2/5)xy), so the factor 5 = 5^{⌊log_5 7⌋} of (b) is needed, while the printed Lemma 3 (factor 5^{⌊log_5 1⌋} = 1) and the errata formula with m = 0 (factor 5^{⌊log_5 1⌋} = 1) both fail (exact computation with rational arithmetic).
- m = 0 in (a): B dx/y with deg B ≤ 2g − 1 is already reduced and needs no factor (p^{⌊log_p 1⌋} = 1).
- For p > (2g + 1)(2m + 3) − 2 every factor in (a)–(b) is 1, matching the observation that large p needs no extra precision.

<a id="target-rd-7-crystalline-rigid-comparison-with-coefficients"></a>

### Ogus's comparison: crystalline cohomology of an F-crystal versus rigid cohomology of its isocrystal

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/crystalline-rigid-comparison-with-coefficients` · theorem

Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], X a smooth proper k-scheme and (M, Φ) an F-crystal of finite locally free O_{X/W}-modules relative to the Witt vector Frobenius σ (CrystallineCohomology:CR.1/crystal, CR.3/frobenius-map). Let E be the associated convergent F-isocrystal (RD.3/restriction-to-convergent: F-crystals up to isogeny and convergent F-isocrystals correspond, Kedlaya, Notes, Theorem 2.2); because X is proper it is an overconvergent F-isocrystal. Then there are canonical isomorphisms H^i_crys(X/W, M) ⊗_W K_0 ≅ H^i_rig(X/K_0, E) for every i, functorial in (M, Φ) and in X, compatible with finite extensions K/K_0 (RD.4/finite-flat-base-change), and carrying the σ-semilinear crystalline Frobenius to the Frobenius of RD.4/frobenius-on-rigid-cohomology; for k = F_q, q = p^f, the K_0-linear map φ^f on the left corresponds to the linear q-Frobenius F of RD.6/linear-q-frobenius. For M = O_{X/W} this is RD.7/rigid-crystalline-comparison together with RD.7/frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison. Without Frobenius structures the same isomorphism, functorial in E, holds for a crystal M of finite locally free modules whose isocrystal M ⊗ Q is Φ(E) for a locally free convergent isocrystal E (Shiho, Theorem 2.36, with the identification of convergent and rigid cohomology for proper X); not every crystal is of this form, because the isocrystal of a crystal need not be convergent (acceptance tests). Properness is used only to identify the convergent cohomology of E with its rigid cohomology; the crystalline–convergent isomorphism itself holds for smooth X (Ogus; Shiho, Theorem 2.36), while for non-proper X crystalline cohomology is not finite and is not the right comparison object (Kedlaya, Notes on isocrystals, Remark 8.5).

**Hypotheses.**

- k perfect; X smooth and proper over k.
- (M, Φ) an F-crystal of finite locally free O_{X/W}-modules relative to σ; E its convergent (hence overconvergent) F-isocrystal.
- Frobenius-free variant: M a crystal of finite locally free modules with M ⊗ Q = Φ(E) for a locally free convergent isocrystal E; the Frobenius clause is then dropped.

**Prerequisites.** [Berthelot's comparison morphism from the tube to the completed PD envelope](#target-rd-7-tube-to-envelope-comparison-map) (`RD.7/tube-to-envelope-comparison-map`), [Berthelot's comparison morphism is a quasi-isomorphism for smooth X](#target-rd-7-comparison-map-quasi-isomorphism) (`RD.7/comparison-map-quasi-isomorphism`), [The rational rigid–crystalline comparison for smooth proper varieties](#target-rd-7-rigid-crystalline-comparison) (`RD.7/rigid-crystalline-comparison`), [The comparison matches the q-Frobenius with the f-th iterate of crystalline Frobenius](#target-rd-7-frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison) (`RD.7/frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison`), [Restriction from overconvergent to convergent F-isocrystals](#target-rd-3-restriction-to-convergent) (`RD.3/restriction-to-convergent`), [For proper X, rigid cohomology is the de Rham cohomology of the tube](#target-rd-4-proper-rigid-equals-convergent) (`RD.4/proper-rigid-equals-convergent`), [Rigid cohomology H^i_rig(X/K, E)](#target-rd-4-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.4/rigid-cohomology`), [Base change of rigid cohomology along finite extensions of the coefficient field](#target-rd-4-finite-flat-base-change) (`RD.4/finite-flat-base-change`), [The Frobenius on rigid cohomology](#target-rd-4-frobenius-on-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.4/frobenius-on-rigid-cohomology`), [Independence of the Frobenius from the chosen lift](#target-rd-4-frobenius-independent-of-lift) (`RD.4/frobenius-independent-of-lift`), [The linear q-power Frobenius on rigid cohomology over F_q](#target-rd-6-linear-q-frobenius) (`RD.6/linear-q-frobenius`), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.1/crystal`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2/smooth-ambient-comparison`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.3/frobenius-map`.

**Sources.**

- [S3](#source-3), Theorem 8.3, p. 20, with Theorem 2.2, p. 2 and Remark 8.5, p. 20. For X smooth proper and a crystal of finite modules whose isocrystal carries a Frobenius structure, rational crystalline cohomology equals rigid cohomology of the corresponding (over)convergent F-isocrystal; the proof is referred to Ogus's convergent topos paper. Remark 8.5 notes that without properness the convergent statement survives but crystalline cohomology is no longer finite.
- [S66](#source-66), Theorem 2.36 and Corollary 2.37, p. 31 (arXiv v2); Introduction, p. 1. Proves, in the relative log setting, that convergent cohomology of a locally free convergent isocrystal is quasi-isomorphic to crystalline cohomology of the associated crystalline isocrystal, and recalls that Ogus proved the absolute convergent–crystalline comparison for smooth X and the convergent–rigid comparison for proper smooth X.
- [S64](#source-64), Theorem 6.13 and its proof, arXiv v3, PDF p. 60. Uses exactly this comparison (Ogus over a point, Shiho in general) to identify rational crystalline pushforwards with convergent F-isocrystals.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Choose a finite Zariski cover of X by opens admitting closed immersions into p-adic formal W-schemes smooth near them; rigid cohomology of E is computed on the tubes because X is proper (RD.4/proper-rigid-equals-convergent, RD.4/rigid-cohomology), and crystalline cohomology of M by the completed PD envelopes (CrystallineCohomology:CR.2/smooth-ambient-comparison).
2. The coefficient version of Berthelot's morphism (RD.7/tube-to-envelope-comparison-map, API tubeToEnvelope_coeff) is a quasi-isomorphism (RD.7/comparison-map-quasi-isomorphism); glue by Čech descent and take hypercohomology.
3. Functoriality in (M, Φ), or in E for the Frobenius-free variant, is that of the evaluation of crystals and of Φ; base change to K uses RD.4/finite-flat-base-change.
4. Frobenius: the absolute Frobenius of X over σ induces the crystalline Frobenius (CrystallineCohomology:CR.3/frobenius-map) and, through any Frobenius lift on the embeddings, the rigid Frobenius (RD.4/frobenius-on-rigid-cohomology, independent of the lift by RD.4/frobenius-independent-of-lift); naturality of the comparison morphism for morphisms of pairs lying over σ identifies them. Over F_q, σ^f = id on W(F_q), so φ^f is linear and equals F (RD.6/linear-q-frobenius).

**Checks.**

- M = O_{X/W}: the theorem is the inherited rigid–crystalline comparison; for X = P^1 both sides are K_0, 0, K_0 with Frobenius 1, ·, p·σ.
- Rank-one F-crystal on X = Spec F_p: M = W with Φ = p^a gives H^0_crys = Z_p with Frobenius p^a and H^0_rig = Q_p with Frobenius p^a.
- Non-example: for X = A^1_k (not proper) H^1_crys(A^1/W) ⊗ Q is the de Rham H^1 of K_0⟨t⟩, which is infinite-dimensional (the form Σ_k p^k t^{p^{2k}−1}dt is not exact), whereas H^1_rig(A^1/K_0) = 0; properness cannot be dropped from the rigid form.
- Why the coefficient must be convergent: on X = G_m over W = W(F_{p^2}), let μ ∈ W with μ mod p ∉ F_p and a = pμ. The rank-one module W⟨t, t^{−1}⟩ with ∇ = d + a·dt/t is a crystal, since ∇_{d/dt}^n(1) = a(a − 1)⋯(a − n + 1)·t^{−n} tends to 0 p-adically (each multiple of p among 0, …, n − 1 contributes a factor of valuation 1), so the connection is topologically quasi-nilpotent. Its Taylor series Σ_n binom(a, n)(ξ/t)^n converges only for |ξ| < |p|^{1/(p(p−1))}: v_p(binom(a, n)) = 1 + ⌊(n − 1)/p⌋ − v_p(n!), which is about −n/(p(p − 1)). So it does not converge on the whole tube |ξ| < 1 of the diagonal, and the isocrystal of this crystal is not convergent. X is not proper here; the example shows only that crystals do not all give convergent isocrystals, which is why the theorem takes an F-crystal or a convergent isocrystal.

<a id="target-rd-7-hyperelliptic-integral-frobenius-lattice"></a>

### The crystalline lattice in hyperelliptic H^1 and the denominators of the Frobenius matrix

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/hyperelliptic-integral-frobenius-lattice` · theorem

In the situation of RD.7/kedlaya-reduction-denominators let C_Q be the smooth projective model of y^2 = Q(x) over Z_q, M = ⊕_{0 ≤ i ≤ 2g−1} Z_q·x^i dx/y ⊂ H^1(A†)^−, t a uniformiser at ∞ with ι(t) = −t (for example t = x^g/y), and L ⊆ M the submodule of those ω whose principal part at ∞, an element of (t^{−2g}Z_q[[t]]dt)/(t^{−1}Z_q[[t]]dt), is the differential of an element of t^{−2g+1}Z_q[[t]]/Z_q[[t]]. Then: (1) L is the image of H^1_dR(C_Q/Z_q) ≅ H^1_crys(C/Z_q) in H^1(A†)^− = H^1_rig(C/K), so the p-power Frobenius F_p (and every power of it) maps L into L; (2) M/L ≅ ⊕_{i odd, −(2g−1) ≤ i < 0} Z_q/iZ_q, so p^c M ⊆ L ⊆ M with c = ⌊log_p(2g − 1)⌋; (3) consequently the matrix of every power F_p^r on the basis x^i dx/y lies in p^{−c}M_{2g}(Z_q), and if the matrix of F_p is known modulo p^N then the n-fold σ-twisted product computing the q-power Frobenius is known modulo p^{N−(n−1)c}, whereas on a Z_q-basis of L all matrices are integral and the product loses no precision; (4) the matrix of F_p on the monomial basis is in general not integral (computations of Vercauteren; the reduction estimates allow denominators of valuation up to v_p(d) + ⌊log_p(d − 2/p)⌋).

**Hypotheses.**

- p odd; Q ∈ Z_q[x] monic of degree 2g + 1 with squarefree reduction; g ≥ 1.
- F_p a σ-semilinear Frobenius lift on A† with x ↦ x^p (Kedlaya's lift, an instance of RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra), acting on H^1(A†)^−.

**Prerequisites.** [Denominator bounds in the reduction of hyperelliptic differentials (Kedlaya Lemma 2, corrected Lemma 3)](#target-rd-7-kedlaya-reduction-denominators) (`RD.7/kedlaya-reduction-denominators`), [The rational rigid–crystalline comparison for smooth proper varieties](#target-rd-7-rigid-crystalline-comparison) (`RD.7/rigid-crystalline-comparison`), [Ogus's comparison: crystalline cohomology of an F-crystal versus rigid cohomology of its isocrystal](#target-rd-7-crystalline-rigid-comparison-with-coefficients) (`RD.7/crystalline-rigid-comparison-with-coefficients`), [Existence of Frobenius lifts on the weak completion of a smooth O_K-algebra (van der Put; Arabia)](#target-rd-0-frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra) (`RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra`), [H^1 of the dagger algebra of a smooth affine curve is H^1_rig, with a lift-independent Frobenius](#target-rd-4-mw-comparison-for-affine-curves) (`RD.4/mw-comparison-for-affine-curves`), [Independence of the Frobenius from the chosen lift](#target-rd-4-frobenius-independent-of-lift) (`RD.4/frobenius-independent-of-lift`), [The Gysin sequence of a punctured smooth proper curve](#target-rd-6-gysin-sequence-for-curves) (`RD.6/gysin-sequence-for-curves`), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2/formal-and-end0`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.3/smooth-curve-lift`.

**Sources.**

- [S99](#source-99), §5.2, pp. 17–18, and Proposition 5.3.1 with its proof sketch, pp. 18–19. Notes that the reduction estimates do not show integrality of the Frobenius matrix on x^i dx/y and that it often fails, and proves that the submodule of forms with integrable principal part at infinity is the image of integral de Rham (= crystalline) cohomology, stable under Frobenius, with quotient killed by p^{⌊log_p(2g−1)⌋}.
- [S98](#source-98), p. 1. Explains that the Frobenius matrix on the monomial basis is not integral, that the denominators stay bounded, and that the submodule of forms whose expansion at infinity integrates over Z_q is Frobenius-stable and gives integral matrices.
- [S101](#source-101), Definition 4.3, Definition 4.4, Proposition 4.5 and proof, Corollary 4.6, pp. 13–14 (arXiv v2). Proves the lattice inclusions p^{δ_1}Λ ⊂ Λ_cris ⊂ p^{−δ_2}Λ for general curves by the same twisted de Rham complexes, generalising Edixhoven's Proposition 5.3.1.

**Construction or proof.**

1. H^1_dR(C_Q/Z_q) is computed by the complex O(0·∞) → Ω^1(∞); twisting by m·∞ gives complexes C(m) whose quotient C(2g − 1)/C(0) is the principal-part differential in the statement, and the resulting diagram identifies L with the image of H^1(C(0)) = H^1_dR(C_Q/Z_q) and computes M/L (Edixhoven, Proposition 5.3.1 and its sketch; Tuitman, Counting points II, Proposition 4.5, gives the complete argument for general curves, generalising it).
2. H^1_dR(C_Q/Z_q) = H^1_crys(C/Z_q) with its Frobenius (CrystallineCohomology:CR.2/formal-and-end0 for the proper smooth lift, CrystallineCohomology:CR.3/smooth-curve-lift), and it is free over Z_q. The endomorphism F_p of H^1(A†)^− is the rigid Frobenius and does not depend on the lift (RD.4/mw-comparison-for-affine-curves, RD.4/frobenius-independent-of-lift (b)). Its restriction to H^1_rig(C/K) ⊆ H^1_rig(C'/K) (RD.6/gysin-sequence-for-curves) corresponds to the σ-semilinear crystalline Frobenius under the comparison (RD.7/crystalline-rigid-comparison-with-coefficients with M = O, which extends RD.7/rigid-crystalline-comparison). So F_p(L) ⊆ L.
3. Since F_p is σ-semilinear, F_p(M) ⊆ F_p(p^{−c}L) = p^{−c}F_p(L) ⊆ p^{−c}M; the same for F_p^r.
4. Precision: let P_j be the exact product of the first j factors, which is the matrix of a power of Frobenius on M and so lies in p^{−c}M_{2g}(Z_q); an input error in p^N M_{2g}(Z_q) propagates to an error in p^{N−(j−1)c} after j factors by induction on j.

**Checks.**

- g = 1, p ≥ 3: c = ⌊log_p 1⌋ = 0, so L = M and the matrix on dx/y, x dx/y is integral.
- g = 2, p = 3: c = ⌊log_3 3⌋ = 1 and M/L ≅ Z_q/3Z_q (from i = −3), so one extra digit suffices.
- Kedlaya's errata: the denominators on the monomial basis are bounded independently of the extension degree n, which is (3) with c = ⌊log_p(2g − 1)⌋.

<a id="target-rd-7-kedlaya-point-counting-certification"></a>

### Certified point counting by Kedlaya's algorithm: precision and integral reconstruction

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/kedlaya-point-counting-certification` · application

Let p be odd, q = p^n, Q ∈ F_q[x] squarefree of degree 2g + 1, C the smooth projective curve y^2 = Q(x) and A the dagger algebra of C' = C − div(y) with the Frobenius lift σ of Kedlaya (x ↦ x^p, y ↦ y^σ by a binomial series). What the source proves, with corrections: (i) q^i + 1 − #C(F_{q^i}) = Tr(q^i F^{−i} | H^1(A; K)^−) (RD.6/monsky-washnitzer-fixed-point-formula); (ii) the characteristic polynomial T^{2g} + a_1T^{2g−1} + ⋯ + a_{2g} of F on H^1(A; K)^− is the Frobenius polynomial of C, with a_{2g−i} = q^{g−i} a_i (printed 'a_i = a_{2g−i}') and |a_i| ≤ C(2g, i) q^{i/2} for 0 ≤ i ≤ 2g; for 0 ≤ i ≤ g this is at most 2^{2g} q^{g/2} (RD.7/weil-factor-export); (iii) integral reconstruction: a_1, …, a_g ∈ Z are determined by their residues modulo p^{N_1} once p^{N_1} > 2·max_{1≤i≤g} C(2g, i)q^{i/2}, which holds for N_1 ≥ (g/2)n + (2g + 1) log_p 2; (iv) Lemma 2: for m ≥ 0 and integral A(x) of degree ≤ 2g, reduction of A(x) dx/y^{2m+1} becomes integral after multiplying by p^{⌊log_p(2m+1)⌋}; (v) Lemma 3 as printed is incorrect; the corrected statement (Kedlaya's errata, J. Ramanujan Math. Soc. 18 (2003) 417–418, as quoted by Harvey) multiplies by p^{⌊log_p((2g+1)(e+2) − 2)⌋} for integral F_j(x) y^{e} dx, deg F_j ≤ 2g and positive odd e = −p(2k+1) + 2j; (vi) the q-Frobenius matrix is M M^σ ⋯ M^{σ^{n−1}} for the p-Frobenius matrix M. The running time is O(g^{4+ε} n^{3+ε}) with a rational Weierstrass point. The source does not prove that the Frobenius matrix is integral on the basis x^i dx/y; the working precision must absorb the denominators bounded in (iv)–(v).

**Hypotheses.**

- p odd; Q squarefree of degree 2g + 1 over F_q; C with a rational Weierstrass point at infinity.

**Prerequisites.** [The Monsky–Washnitzer fixed point formula](#target-rd-6-monsky-washnitzer-fixed-point-formula) (`RD.6/monsky-washnitzer-fixed-point-formula`), [Weil-factor export to WeilConjectures:WC.6](#target-rd-7-weil-factor-export) (`RD.7/weil-factor-export`), [The Gysin sequence of a punctured smooth proper curve](#target-rd-6-gysin-sequence-for-curves) (`RD.6/gysin-sequence-for-curves`), [The Monsky–Washnitzer comparison: rigid cohomology of a smooth affine is the de Rham cohomology of its dagger algebra](#target-rd-4-monsky-washnitzer-comparison) (`RD.4/monsky-washnitzer-comparison`), [Finite dimensionality of rigid cohomology with coefficients (Kedlaya, Theorem 1.2.1)](#target-rd-5-finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.5/finiteness-of-rigid-cohomology`), [Denominator bounds in the reduction of hyperelliptic differentials (Kedlaya Lemma 2, corrected Lemma 3)](#target-rd-7-kedlaya-reduction-denominators) (`RD.7/kedlaya-reduction-denominators`), [The crystalline lattice in hyperelliptic H^1 and the denominators of the Frobenius matrix](#target-rd-7-hyperelliptic-integral-frobenius-lattice) (`RD.7/hyperelliptic-integral-frobenius-lattice`).

**Sources.**

- [S6](#source-6), §3, p. 6. Precision bound.
- [S6](#source-6), Lemma 2, p. 5. Denominator bound.
- [S26](#source-26), §3, p. 6. Known correction of Lemma 3.
- [S6](#source-6), Abstract, p. 1. Complexity.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (i) from the Monsky–Washnitzer trace formula applied to C' and its quotient by the hyperelliptic involution (the correct count of removed points is #C'(F_{q^i}) = #C(F_{q^i}) − 1 − r_i with r_i the number of roots of Q in F_{q^i}; the printed intermediate counts are corrected in sourceIssues).
2. (ii) from RD.7/weil-factor-export applied to C (integrality, purity, functional equation), transported to H^1(A; K)^− ≅ H^1_rig(C/K) (RD.6/gysin-sequence-for-curves: removing the 2g + 2 points adds only the + part).
3. (iii) an integer a with |a| ≤ B is determined by a mod p^N if p^N > 2B (symmetric residue).
4. For (iv)–(v), use RD.7/kedlaya-reduction-denominators for the negative and positive odd powers separately, and RD.7/hyperelliptic-integral-frobenius-lattice for the crystalline-lattice loss. The corrected positive-power bound uses the exponent of the form, rather than substituting the negative Frobenius-expansion exponent into the positive logarithm.
5. In a Frobenius expansion term with e=−p(2k+1)+2j, use Lemma 2 when e<0 and the corrected Lemma 3 when e>0. Since p is odd, e is odd and never zero. The negative exponents must not be fed into the positive-power logarithm.

**Checks.**

- PARI/GP: C: y^2 = x^5 + x + 3 over F_7 (g = 2): Frobenius polynomial T^4 + 3T^3 + 7T^2 + 21T + 49; a_3 = 21 = 7·a_1 and a_4 = 49 = 7^2 (the corrected relation), while the printed a_1 = a_3 fails; |a_i| ≤ C(4, i)·7^{i/2} for all i; N_1 = ⌈1 + 5 log_7 2⌉ = 3 and 7^3 = 343 > 84 = 2·max C(4, i)7^{i/2}, and a_1, a_2 are recovered from their residues mod 343; #C(F_7) = 11 by brute force = 8 − (−3).
- PARI/GP: for the same curve #C'(F_{7^k}) = #C − 1 − r_k gives 10, 54, 370 for k = 1, 2, 3, while the printed #C − 2g gives 7, 51, 367.

<a id="target-rd-7-abelian-variety-crystalline-frobenius-polynomial"></a>

### The crystalline Frobenius polynomial of an abelian variety is its Weil polynomial

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/abelian-variety-crystalline-frobenius-polynomial` · theorem

Let A be an abelian variety of dimension g over F_q, q = p^f, W = W(F_q), K_0 = W[1/p], π_A ∈ End(A) its q-Frobenius endomorphism (DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.1/frobenius-endomorphism-over-a-finite-field) and P_A(T) = det(T − V_ℓπ_A | V_ℓA) ∈ Z[T] its characteristic polynomial, independent of ℓ ≠ p (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A6/characteristic-polynomial-on-tate-module). Conventions: V_ℓA is the covariant rational Tate module, on which π_A acts as the arithmetic Frobenius x ↦ x^q of Gal(F̄_q/F_q) acts on torsion points; H^1_et(A_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ) = Hom(V_ℓA, Q_ℓ), on which the geometric Frobenius acts as the transpose of V_ℓπ_A; φ is the σ-semilinear crystalline Frobenius on the contravariant H^1_crys(A/W). Then: (1) the K_0-linear map φ^f on H^1_crys(A/W) ⊗ K_0 has characteristic polynomial P_A(T), so P_1(A, t) := det(1 − tφ^f | H^1_crys(A/W) ⊗ K_0) = t^{2g}P_A(1/t) = det(1 − t·Frob_q | H^1_et(A_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ)); (2) for every i, det(1 − tφ^f | H^i_crys ⊗ K_0) = ∏_{|I| = i}(1 − α_I t), where α_1, …, α_{2g} are the roots of P_A and α_I = ∏_{j ∈ I} α_j; (3) for an elliptic curve E given by a Weierstrass model over F_q, P_1(E, t) = 1 − a t + q t^2 with a = q + 1 − #E(F_q) the Frobenius trace (tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.frobeniusTrace). No inversion of the Frobenius and no dualisation changes the characteristic polynomial: transposition preserves it, and the geometric/arithmetic dictionary is absorbed by the contravariance of H^1.

**Hypotheses.**

- A an abelian variety over F_q, q = p^f; ℓ ≠ p.
- Crystalline Frobenius taken relative to the Witt vector Frobenius σ of W(F_q), so φ^f is K_0-linear.

**Prerequisites.** [The rigid and crystalline zeta expressions for every finite extension](#target-rd-7-rigid-zeta-expression) (`RD.7/rigid-zeta-expression`), [The Weil factors are integral polynomials determined by weights](#target-rd-7-weil-factors-rational-and-integral) (`RD.7/weil-factors-rational-and-integral`), [Weight separation: pure factors of a rational zeta function are unique, rational and integral](#target-rd-7-weight-separated-factor-extraction) (`RD.7/weight-separated-factor-extraction`), [The comparison matches the q-Frobenius with the f-th iterate of crystalline Frobenius](#target-rd-7-frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison) (`RD.7/frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison`), `DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.1/frobenius-endomorphism-over-a-finite-field`, `DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.1/weil-estimate-for-abelian-varieties`, `DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.1/point-counts-of-abelian-varieties`, `DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.0/weil-number-arithmetic`, `AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A6/characteristic-polynomial-on-tate-module`, `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6`, `tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.frobeniusTrace`.

**Sources.**

- [S79](#source-79), proof of Theorem 5.1.6, p. 25 (arXiv v4). Uses that the overconvergent F-isocrystal R^1f_crys,*O of an abelian scheme is pure, by the Riemann hypothesis for abelian varieties (the crystalline Frobenius eigenvalues on H^1 of each fibre are Weil numbers of weight 1), and that the linear Frobenius on the crystalline cohomology of a fibre is semisimple because it is central in its endomorphism algebra.
- [S5](#source-5), §1.1, p. 3. Records that Chiarellotto's rigid version of Weil II is not purely p-adic because it rests on Katz and Messing's crystalline version of the Weil conjectures, which in turn rests on Deligne. The node is the degree-one case of that comparison for abelian varieties; here it is obtained from weight separation instead.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Weil numbers: P_A ∈ Z[T] is independent of ℓ (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A6/characteristic-polynomial-on-tate-module) and its roots α_1, …, α_{2g} are Weil q-numbers of weight 1 (DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.1/weil-estimate-for-abelian-varieties); so each α_I is a Weil q-number of weight |I| (DWP.0/weil-number-arithmetic).
2. Zeta function: Z(A, t) = ∏_{r=0}^{2g} P_r(t)^{(−1)^{r+1}} with P_r(t) = ∏_{|I|=r}(1 − α_I t) ∈ 1 + tZ[t] (DWP.1/point-counts-of-abelian-varieties); this is a family over Q whose degree-r factor is pure of weight r.
3. Crystalline side: A is smooth and proper, so Z(A, t) = ∏_i P_i(A, t)^{(−1)^{i+1}} with P_i(A, t) = det(1 − tF | H^i_rig(A/K)) = det(1 − tφ^f | H^i_crys(A/W) ⊗ K_0) (RD.7/rigid-zeta-expression, RD.7/frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison), and the reciprocal roots of P_i(A, t) are Weil q-numbers of weight i (RD.7/weil-factors-rational-and-integral). Weight separation (RD.7/weight-separated-factor-extraction (4)) applied to the two pure families gives P_i(A, t) = P_i for every i. This is (2); for i = 1 it gives P_1(A, t) = ∏_j(1 − α_j t) = t^{2g}P_A(1/t), which is (1) on the crystalline side.
4. ℓ-adic side: H^1_et(A_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ) ≅ Hom(V_ℓA, Q_ℓ) Frobenius-equivariantly, with geometric Frobenius the transpose of V_ℓπ_A (request to ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.6); a transpose has the same characteristic polynomial, so det(1 − t·Frob_q | H^1_et) = t^{2g}P_A(1/t), which completes (1). The equality of crystalline and ℓ-adic factors in every degree is also Katz–Messing's theorem (RD.7/ell-adic-comparison-smooth-projective); this proof does not use it.
5. Elliptic curves: P_A(T) = T^2 − aT + q with a = Tr π_A = q + 1 − deg(1 − π_A) = q + 1 − #E(F_q) (DWP.1/point-counts-of-abelian-varieties), which is Tau Ceti's WeierstrassCurve.frobeniusTrace for an elliptic model (WeierstrassCurve.frobeniusTrace_eq_card_point).

**Checks.**

- y^2 = x^3 + x + 1 over F_7: #E(F_7) = 5, a = 3, P_1 = 1 − 3t + 7t^2; the crystalline polynomial T^2 − 3T + 7 has a unit root in Z_7 (E ordinary).
- y^2 = x^3 + x over F_5: #E(F_5) = 4, a = 2, slopes 0 and 1; y^2 = x^3 − x over F_3: a = 0, φ has characteristic polynomial T^2 + 3 with slopes 1/2, 1/2 (agreeing with CrystallineCohomology:CR.3/elliptic-frobenius).
- Supersingular y^2 = x^3 + x over F_7 and its base change to F_49: P_1 = 1 + 7t^2 and (1 + 7t)^2.
- Degenerate g = 0 (A = Spec F_q): H^0 only, P_0 = 1 − t.

<a id="target-rd-7-tuitman-frobenius-structure-algorithm"></a>

### Tuitman's Frobenius lift and cohomological reduction for curves with a map to P^1

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/tuitman-frobenius-structure-algorithm` · construction

Let X be a smooth projective curve of genus g over F_q, q = p^n, with a finite separable map x : X → P^1 of degree d_x and a rational function y generating the function field, satisfying an irreducible equation Q(x, y) = 0 monic in y of degree d_x; let Q ∈ Z_q[x, y] be a lift with the same support, still monic in y, Δ its discriminant in y, r = Δ/gcd(Δ, dΔ/dx), U = Spec Z_q[x, 1/r, y]/(Q) and R† its weak completion. Assume Tuitman's Assumption 1 in its corrected form: (1) matrices W^0 ∈ GL_{d_x}(Z_q[x, 1/r]) and W^∞ ∈ GL_{d_x}(Z_q[x, 1/x, 1/r]) give integral bases of the function field over Q_q[x] and over Q_q[1/x] whose reductions are integral bases over F_q[x] and F_q[1/x]; (2) the discriminant of r is a unit; (3) the discriminants of the reduced parts (quotients by the nilradicals) of the finite Z_q-algebras R^0/(r) and R^∞/(1/x) are units (June 2020 erratum). Then: (a) U is the complement of a smooth relative divisor D_X in a smooth proper curve X over Z_q with special fibre X (Tuitman, Proposition 2.3); (b) there is a σ-semilinear Frobenius lift F_p on R† with F_p(x) = x^p, computed by Newton iteration modulo p^{2^i} (Theorem 2.6); (c) cohomological reduction at the finite and infinite points produces a basis ω_1, …, ω_κ of H^1_rig(U) from algebraic differentials, whose first 2g elements span H^1_rig(X) (the kernel of the residue map), together with, for every overconvergent 1-form ν on U, its coordinates and an overconvergent primitive: ν = Σ_j c_jω_j + dh; (d) applied to F_p^*ω_i this gives the Frobenius matrix F and overconvergent functions f_i with F_p^*ω_i = Σ_j F_{ij}ω_j + df_i, the q-power Frobenius F^{(n)} = F^{σ^{n−1}}⋯F^{σ}F (row convention: the i-th row of F holds the coordinates of F_p^*ω_i, as in BDMTV and in Tuitman's implementation; in the column convention of Tuitman's Step III the product is taken in the opposite order, F·F^{σ}⋯F^{σ^{n−1}}, sourceIssues E707), and the reverse characteristic polynomial χ(T) = det(1 − F^{(n)}T | H^1_rig(X)), which equals the Weil factor P_1(X, T) of RD.7/weil-factor (so #X(F_{q^r}) = q^r + 1 − Tr(F^{(n)r}|H^1_rig(X))). Consumers apply (c) to further forms, for example to the right-hand sides of the equations for the Frobenius structure of a unipotent connection (Balakrishnan–Dogra–Müller–Tuitman–Vonk, (22)).

**Hypotheses.**

- X smooth projective geometrically connected curve over F_q with a finite separable x : X → P^1 and a plane model Q monic in y.
- Tuitman's Assumption 1 with condition (3) as corrected in June 2020.

**Intended library interface.** `TauCeti/RigidCohomology/PointCounting`, `TauCeti.RigidCohomology`

**Prerequisites.** [Existence of Frobenius lifts on the weak completion of a smooth O_K-algebra (van der Put; Arabia)](#target-rd-0-frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra) (`RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra`), [H^1 of the dagger algebra of a smooth affine curve is H^1_rig, with a lift-independent Frobenius](#target-rd-4-mw-comparison-for-affine-curves) (`RD.4/mw-comparison-for-affine-curves`), [The Gysin sequence of a punctured smooth proper curve](#target-rd-6-gysin-sequence-for-curves) (`RD.6/gysin-sequence-for-curves`), [The Monsky–Washnitzer fixed point formula](#target-rd-6-monsky-washnitzer-fixed-point-formula) (`RD.6/monsky-washnitzer-fixed-point-formula`), [The Weil factors P_i of a smooth proper variety over F_q](#target-rd-7-weil-factor) (`RD.7/weil-factor`), [The comparison matches the q-Frobenius with the f-th iterate of crystalline Frobenius](#target-rd-7-frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison) (`RD.7/frobenius-compatibility-of-comparison`), `mathlib:Matrix.charpolyRev`, `mathlib:Matrix.reverse_charpoly`.

**Sources.**

- [S101](#source-101), Definition 2.1, p. 2; Assumption 1, Remark 2.2 and Proposition 2.3, p. 3; Definition 2.5, Theorem 2.6 and Remark 2.7, p. 5; Theorem 3.11, p. 9; §4.1 Step I, p. 11; §4.3 Step III and §4.4 Step IV, p. 12 (arXiv v2). Sets up the lift of the plane model, the integral-basis assumption, the good compactification it implies, the Frobenius lift with x ↦ x^p obtained by Newton iteration, the residue sequence cutting H^1_rig(X) out of H^1_rig(U), the choice of a basis whose first 2g elements span H^1_rig(X), the Frobenius matrix F (its index convention is E707) and χ(T).
- [S102](#source-102), the single correction (June 2020). Condition (3) of Assumption 1 should require unit discriminants only for the reduced parts of R^0/(r(x)) and R^∞/(1/x); the printed condition is sufficient but far too restrictive.
- [S103](#source-103), §5.2, equations (22)–(23), pp. 25–26 (arXiv v1). Uses Tuitman's algorithms to compute the Frobenius matrix F, the primitives f with φ^*ω = Fω + df, and to solve the further equations for g and h that give the Frobenius structure on the unipotent connection.

**Uses and API requirements.**

- EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6: the Frobenius matrix on H^1_rig, the overconvergent primitives f, and solutions of the further reduction equations for g, h (BDMTV item /95 request)
- Balakrishnan–Dogra–Müller–Tuitman–Vonk, §5.2, (22)–(23): computing the Frobenius structure of the unipotent connection and the Teichmüller-point splitting
- Tuitman, Counting points II, §4.4: the zeta function of X from χ(T)
- PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/tuitman-precision-certification: the precision analysis of the computed matrix

**API.**

| Declaration | Role | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `RigidCohomology.Tuitman.Assumption1` |  | The data (Q, W^0, W^∞) and the three conditions, with condition (3) on the reduced parts of R^0/(r) and R^∞/(1/x). |
| `RigidCohomology.Tuitman.goodCompactification` |  | Under Assumption 1, a smooth proper curve X over Z_q and a smooth relative divisor D_X with U = X − D_X and X ⊗ F_q ≅ X. |
| `RigidCohomology.Tuitman.frobeniusLift` |  | A σ-semilinear ring endomorphism F_p of R† lifting the p-power map with F_p(x) = x^p. |
| `RigidCohomology.Tuitman.reduce` |  | For an overconvergent 1-form ν on U: coordinates c ∈ Q_q^κ and an overconvergent h with ν = Σ c_jω_j + dh. |
| `RigidCohomology.Tuitman.reduce_unique` |  | The coordinates c are unique, and h is unique up to an additive constant. |
| `RigidCohomology.Tuitman.frobeniusMatrix` |  | The matrix F with F_p^*ω_i = Σ_j F_{ij}ω_j + df_i (row i holds the coordinates of F_p^*ω_i), and the primitives f_i. |
| `RigidCohomology.Tuitman.frobeniusMatrix_eq_rigid` |  | F is the matrix of the rigid Frobenius of H^1_rig(U) in the basis ω (independent of the Frobenius lift). |
| `RigidCohomology.Tuitman.charpolyRev_eq_weilFactor` |  | The reverse characteristic polynomial of F^{(n)} = F^{σ^{n−1}}⋯F on H^1_rig(X) is P_1(X, T). |
| `RigidCohomology.Tuitman.hyperelliptic` |  | For Q = y^2 − f(x) with f of odd degree, the construction specialises to Kedlaya's algorithm. |

**Unit tests.**

- `RigidCohomology.Tuitman.hyperelliptic_genus_two` (computation): For y^2 = x^5 + x + 3 over F_7 the computed χ(T) is 1 + 3T + 7T^2 + 21T^3 + 49T^4.
- `RigidCohomology.Tuitman.genus_zero` (degenerate): For Q = y − x (X = P^1, d_x = 1) the basis of H^1_rig(X) is empty and χ(T) = 1.
- `RigidCohomology.Tuitman.assumption_printed_too_strong` (non-example): For Q = y^2 − f(x) the printed condition (3) fails (R^0/(r) is not reduced, discriminant 0) while the corrected condition holds when disc(f) is a unit.
- `RigidCohomology.Tuitman.lift_independent` (compatibility): Replacing F_p by another Frobenius lift of R† changes the primitives f_i but not the matrix F (RD.4/mw-comparison-for-affine-curves).
- `RigidCohomology.Tuitman.frobeniusPower_order` (non-example): The order of the twisted product matters once n ≥ 3. Take n = 3, F_8 = F_2[a]/(a^3 + a + 1) and any lift A ∈ M_2(W(F_8)) of the matrix with rows (0, 1) and (a, a^2). Modulo 2 the trace of A^{σ^2}A^{σ}A is 0 and the trace of A·A^{σ}·A^{σ^2} is 1. In the row convention only the first is the matrix of the cube of the σ-semilinear map with matrix A.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (a): glue Spec R^0 and Spec R^∞ along U; flatness and regularity of both fibres (from the integral bases) give smoothness, and the unit discriminants give étaleness of the boundary (Tuitman, proof of Proposition 2.3).
2. (b): define F_p(1/r) and F_p(y) as limits of the Newton iterations α_{i+1} = α_i(2 − α_i r^σ(x^p)) and the analogous iteration for y with 1/Δ = g(x)/r(x)^m; convergence in R† is the Hensel argument for the étale map U → V (Tuitman, Theorem 2.6). This is an instance of RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-dagger-algebra with a chosen form.
3. (c): reduce poles along r = 0 using the integral basis b^0 and the relation from d of b^0_j/r^ℓ, then poles above ∞ using b^∞; H^1_rig(X) is the kernel of the residue map on H^1_rig(U) (Tuitman, Theorem 3.11, quoted there as well known; here RD.6/gysin-sequence-for-curves), and the basis is chosen with ω_1, …, ω_{2g} spanning that kernel (Tuitman, §4.1, Step I).
4. (d): F is the matrix of the rigid Frobenius on H^1_rig(U) for the basis ω (RD.4/mw-comparison-for-affine-curves: the Frobenius on Ω^1_{R†}/dR† is independent of the lift); its characteristic polynomial on H^1_rig(X) is the Weil factor by RD.7/weil-factor and RD.6/monsky-washnitzer-fixed-point-formula.

**Checks.**

- Hyperelliptic case: Q = y^2 − f(x), d_x = 2, with f squarefree of odd degree 2g + 1 and unit discriminant; Assumption 1 holds with W^0 = 1, and the algorithm recovers Kedlaya's: for y^2 = x^5 + x + 3 over F_7, χ(T) = 1 + 3T + 7T^2 + 21T^3 + 49T^4 and #X(F_7) = 11.
- Genus zero: for x : P^1 → P^1 the identity (Q = y − x), H^1_rig(X) = 0 and χ = 1.
- The printed Assumption 1(3) excludes every hyperelliptic curve: R^0/(r) = (Z_q[x]/(f))[y]/(y^2) is not reduced, so its discriminant is 0, while its reduced part Z_q[x]/(f) has unit discriminant; the corrected condition holds.

<a id="target-rd-7-tuitman-precision-certification"></a>

### Certified precision for Tuitman's algorithm

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/tuitman-precision-certification` · theorem

In the situation of RD.7/tuitman-frobenius-structure-algorithm, write χ(T) = det(1 − F^{(n)}T | H^1_rig(X)) ∈ Z[T]. Let e_0, e_∞ be the maximal ramification indices of x over the zeros of r and over ∞, ord_0(W), ord_∞(W^{−1}) the orders of the change-of-basis matrix W = (W^0)^{−1}W^∞, and put B = max_{1≤i≤g}(⌊log_p binom(4g, i) + ni/2⌋ + 1), δ_1 = ⌊log_p(−(ord_0(W) + 1)e_∞)⌋, δ_2 = ⌊log_p((⌊(2g−2)/d_x⌋ + 1)e_∞)⌋, δ = δ_1 + δ_2, f_1(m) = ⌊log_p(p(m − 1)e_0)⌋ + ⌊log_p(−(ord_∞(W^{−1}) + 1)e_∞)⌋ and f_2 = ⌊log_p(−p(ord_0(W) + 1)e_∞)⌋. Then: (1) χ is determined by its residue modulo p^B; (2) with Λ the Z_q-span of the reduction basis and Λ_cris the image of the log-crystalline H^1_cris(X, D_X), p^{δ_1}Λ ⊆ Λ_cris ⊆ p^{−δ_2}Λ, so ord_p(F) ≥ −δ; (3) knowing F modulo p^{B+δ} suffices to recover χ; (4) it suffices to run the computation at working p-adic precision N such that m − max(f_1(m), f_2) ≥ B + δ for every m ≥ N, and N can be taken in Õ(d_x d_y n). For the hyperelliptic case this recovers RD.7/hyperelliptic-integral-frobenius-lattice.

**Hypotheses.**

- The hypotheses of RD.7/tuitman-frobenius-structure-algorithm (corrected Assumption 1).

**Prerequisites.** [Tuitman's Frobenius lift and cohomological reduction for curves with a map to P^1](#target-rd-7-tuitman-frobenius-structure-algorithm) (`RD.7/tuitman-frobenius-structure-algorithm`), [The crystalline lattice in hyperelliptic H^1 and the denominators of the Frobenius matrix](#target-rd-7-hyperelliptic-integral-frobenius-lattice) (`RD.7/hyperelliptic-integral-frobenius-lattice`), [Weil-factor export to WeilConjectures:WC.6](#target-rd-7-weil-factor-export) (`RD.7/weil-factor-export`), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5/log-poincare`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5/p-adic-log-crystalline`.

**Sources.**

- [S101](#source-101), §4.5: Proposition 4.2, Definitions 4.3–4.4, Proposition 4.5, Corollary 4.6, Proposition 4.7, Definition 4.8 and Proposition 4.9, pp. 13–15 (arXiv v2). Gives the reconstruction precision, the lattices of reduction and of log-crystalline cohomology with their inclusions, the resulting bound on the valuation of the Frobenius matrix, and the working precision that certifies χ.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): the coefficients of χ satisfy the functional equation and the Weil bounds of RD.7/weil-factor-export, so the first g of them are integers of absolute value at most binom(2g, i)q^{i/2} ≤ binom(4g, i)q^{i/2}/2 and are determined by their residues modulo p^B (Tuitman, Proposition 4.2; Kedlaya's reconstruction lemma).
2. (2): compare the log de Rham complex of (X, D_X) twisted by m·D_∞ with the untwisted one, whose H^1 is the log-crystalline H^1_cris(X, D_X) (CrystallineCohomology:CR.5/log-poincare, CR.5/p-adic-log-crystalline); the cokernel is killed by p^{⌊log_p(m e_∞)⌋}; Serre duality kills H^1(O(m_2D_∞)) for m_2 = ⌊(2g − 2)/d_x⌋ + 1 (Tuitman, Proposition 4.5). Since Frobenius preserves Λ_cris, ord_p(F) ≥ −δ (Corollary 4.6).
3. (3): compute χ in a basis of Λ_cris, where no precision is lost, and change basis (Proposition 4.7).
4. (4): track the denominators in reducing F_p(ω_i) at the finite and infinite points, bounded by f_1(m) and f_2 (Definition 4.8, Proposition 4.9).

**Checks.**

- Hyperelliptic genus two over F_7 (y^2 = x^5 + x + 3): B = max(⌊log_7 8 + 1/2⌋ + 1, ⌊log_7 28 + 1⌋ + 1) = max(2, 3) = 3; |a_1| ≤ 4·7^{1/2} < 11 and |a_2| ≤ 6·7 = 42, and 7^3 = 343 > 2·42, so the residues modulo 343 determine a_1 = 3 and a_2 = 7.
- Genus zero: the maximum over 1 ≤ i ≤ g is over the empty set; χ = 1 needs no precision.
- The bound uses binom(4g, i) rather than the sharper 2·binom(2g, i); the certification is valid with either, and Kedlaya's N_1 of RD.7/kedlaya-point-counting-certification is the hyperelliptic instance.

<a id="target-rd-7-mieda-p-adic-picard-lefschetz"></a>

### Mieda's p-adic Picard–Lefschetz map for ordinary quadratic degenerations

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/mieda-p-adic-picard-lefschetz` · theorem

Let p be odd, L = Q_p(√−p) with ring of integers O_L and uniformiser √−p, and 𝒳 a proper flat Z_p-scheme of relative dimension N whose generic fibre is smooth and whose special fibre 𝒳_{F_p} is smooth outside finitely many ordinary quadratic points, each of which over O_L is formally given by an equation Q − u·(√−p)^2 with u a unit and Q a quadratic form defining a smooth quadric in P^N over O_L. Then: (1) the blow-up 𝒳'' of 𝒳 ⊗ O_L at these points is strictly semistable over O_L, with generic fibre 𝒳_L; (2) there is an injective L-linear map β : H^N_rig(𝒳_{F_p}/Q_p) ⊗ L → H^N_dR(𝒳_{Q_p}) ⊗ L, compatible with Frobenius when the right-hand side carries the Hyodo–Kato Frobenius of 𝒳'' (constructed with logarithmic de Rham–Witt complexes), and compatible with the restriction maps to the boundary strata (the commutative square of the Picard–Lefschetz formula); (3) if 𝒳_{F_p} is smooth, β is the rigid–de Rham comparison isomorphism of a smooth proper lift (RD.7/rigid-crystalline-comparison with CrystallineCohomology:CR.2/formal-and-end0).

**Hypotheses.**

- p odd; 𝒳 proper flat over Z_p with smooth generic fibre.
- Special fibre smooth away from finitely many ordinary quadratic points of the stated formal type over O_L = Z_p[√−p].

**Prerequisites.** [The rational rigid–crystalline comparison for smooth proper varieties](#target-rd-7-rigid-crystalline-comparison) (`RD.7/rigid-crystalline-comparison`), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2/formal-and-end0`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.6/log-de-rham-witt-model`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.6/proper-log-rigid-hk`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.6/hk-comparison`, [The Frobenius on rigid cohomology](#target-rd-4-frobenius-on-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.4/frobenius-on-rigid-cohomology`).

**Sources.**

- [S93](#source-93), proof of Proposition 5.23, pp. 49–51 (arXiv v5). Recalls Mieda's p-adic Picard–Lefschetz formula: for ordinary quadratic singularities the blow-up over Z_p[√−p] is semistable, and there is a commutative diagram with an injective Frobenius-compatible map β from rigid cohomology of the special fibre to de Rham cohomology of the generic fibre, built with logarithmic de Rham–Witt complexes; in the smooth case β is the usual comparison isomorphism.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): blowing up an ordinary quadratic point of a family Q = u·π^2 gives two components meeting transversally, the exceptional quadric and the strict transform (Mieda, (2.3), as recalled by Fresán–Sabbah–Yu).
2. (2): the log-crystalline (Hyodo–Kato) cohomology of the special fibre of 𝒳'' carries Frobenius and monodromy (CrystallineCohomology:CR.6/log-de-rham-witt-model, CR.6/proper-log-rigid-hk) and is compared with de Rham cohomology of 𝒳_L by the Hyodo–Kato isomorphism (CrystallineCohomology:CR.6/hk-comparison); β is the composite of the map from rigid cohomology of the singular special fibre into it (Mieda, Theorem 1.1 and Theorem 2.13). Its injectivity and the Picard–Lefschetz square are Mieda's theorem; his paper was not read for this plan (recorded gap).
3. (3): when the special fibre is smooth there is nothing to blow up and the construction reduces to the comparison of rigid cohomology with de Rham cohomology of a lift.

**Checks.**

- Fresán–Sabbah–Yu apply it to the compactification 𝒦̄' of the hypersurface 𝒦 attached to Sym^k Kl_2 (N = k − 1), where Q is the quadratic form Q_{ap} or Q_{bp} of their (5.6), (5.16).
- Degenerate: no singular points, then 𝒳'' = 𝒳 ⊗ O_L is smooth and β is an isomorphism.
- Non-example: without the extension to L = Q_p(√−p) the equation Q − u·p is not of the form Q − u·π^2 with π a uniformiser, and the blow-up over Z_p is not semistable; the ramified base change is necessary.

<a id="target-rd-7-kloosterman-semistable-realization"></a>

### The p-adic realisation of the Kloosterman moments and middle rigid cohomology (Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, Proposition 5.23)

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/kloosterman-semistable-realization` · application

Fix k > 1, a prime p, and a place of Q̄ above p; let V_{k,p} be the p-adic étale realisation of the Kloosterman motive M_k of Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, ϖ ∈ Q̄_p with ϖ^{p−1} = −p, K = Q_p(ϖ), and H^1_{rig,mid}(G_m/K, Sym^k Kl_2) = gr^W_{k+1}H^1_{rig,c}(G_m/K, Sym^k Kl_2) the middle rigid cohomology of the symmetric power of the Kloosterman F-isocrystal (RD.6), of dimension ⌊(k − 1)/2⌋ − δ_{4Z}(k) when p > k for odd k and p > k/2 for even k. Then: (1) V_{k,p} is de Rham as a representation of Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p); (2) if p is odd, V_{k,p} is semistable over Q_p(√−p) and there is an injection of Frobenius modules H^1_{rig,mid}(G_m/K, Sym^k Kl_2) → (V_{k,p} ⊗ B_st)^{Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p(√−p))} ⊗ K; (3) if moreover p > k for odd k (respectively p > k/2 for even k), V_{k,p} is crystalline and the map is an isomorphism with (V_{k,p} ⊗ B_cris)^{Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p)} ⊗ K.

**Hypotheses.**

- k > 1; p prime (odd for (2)–(3)); the bounds on p in (3).
- The period rings and functors of NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties:R11.5 and the p-adic comparison theorems C_dR and C_st (recorded gap).

**Prerequisites.** [Mieda's p-adic Picard–Lefschetz map for ordinary quadratic degenerations](#target-rd-7-mieda-p-adic-picard-lefschetz) (`RD.7/mieda-p-adic-picard-lefschetz`), `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.6`, [The excision long exact sequence for compact-support rigid cohomology](#target-rd-4-excision-sequence) (`RD.4/excision-sequence`), [The Frobenius on rigid cohomology](#target-rd-4-frobenius-on-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.4/frobenius-on-rigid-cohomology`), [Rigid Weil II over a point (Kedlaya)](#target-rd-6-p-adic-weil-ii) (`RD.6/p-adic-weil-ii`), `NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties:R11.5`.

**Sources.**

- [S93](#source-93), §5.1.5, Proposition 5.23 and its proof, pp. 49–51 (arXiv v5). States and proves that the p-adic realisation is de Rham, semistable over Q_p(√−p) with an inclusion of the middle rigid cohomology into its D_st, and crystalline with equality under the bounds on p, using the localisation spectral sequence, Mieda's p-adic Picard–Lefschetz formula and the p-adic comparison theorem.

**Construction or proof.**

1. (1): V_{k,p} is a subquotient of the cohomology of the smooth proper varieties 𝒦̄ or 𝒦̄', which is de Rham by the de Rham comparison theorem (gap), and subquotients of de Rham representations are de Rham.
2. (2), even k: the localisation spectral sequence for compact-support rigid cohomology of 𝒦̄' with its boundary (RD.4/excision-sequence) identifies the middle cohomology with gr^W_{k−1} of the kernel of the restriction α to the boundary; Mieda's injective β (RD.7/mieda-p-adic-picard-lefschetz) embeds that kernel into the kernel of the de Rham restriction over L, which by the semistable comparison theorem for the semistable model 𝒦̄'' (gap) is (V_{k,p}(1) ⊗ B_st)^{Gal(Q̄_p/L)} ⊗ L; β is Frobenius-compatible; extend scalars to K and take χ-isotypic parts.
3. (3): when 𝒦̄' is smooth, β is the comparison isomorphism and the kernel is pure of weight k − 1, giving the crystalline statement.
4. Odd k: the same argument with 𝒦' = 𝒦 (no first resolution).

**Checks.**

- Dimensions from the formula ⌊(k − 1)/2⌋ − δ_{4Z}(k): k = 5, p > 5 gives 2; k = 8, p > 4 gives 3 − 1 = 2.
- Small k: dimension 0 for k = 2 and k = 4 (so (3) is an equality of zero spaces) and 1 for k = 3 with p > 3.

<a id="target-rd-7-kloosterman-newton-above-hodge"></a>

### Newton above Hodge for Kloosterman moments and the valuation of their coefficients (Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, Corollary 5.27)

`PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.7/kloosterman-newton-above-hodge` · application

Let k ≥ 1 and p an odd prime. The Newton polygon of the Frobenius module H^1_{rig,c}(G_m,F_p/K, Sym^k Kl_2) lies on or above the Hodge polygon of H^1_{dR,c}(G_m, Sym^k Kl_2), with the same endpoints when p > k for odd k and 2p > k for even k. Consequently, writing the moment L-function as Z_k(p; T) = Σ_n c_n T^n, one has v_p(c_n) ≥ n(n − 1) for every n and every p ≥ 3.

**Hypotheses.**

- k ≥ 1; p odd.
- RD.7/kloosterman-semistable-realization (with its recorded comparison-theorem gap).

**Prerequisites.** [The p-adic realisation of the Kloosterman moments and middle rigid cohomology (Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, Proposition 5.23)](#target-rd-7-kloosterman-semistable-realization) (`RD.7/kloosterman-semistable-realization`), `FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.3`, [Slope bounds for rigid cohomology (p-adic weights)](#target-rd-6-slope-bounds-for-rigid-cohomology) (`RD.6/slope-bounds-for-rigid-cohomology`), `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.6`.

**Sources.**

- [S93](#source-93), Corollary 5.27 and its proof, Remark 5.28 with (5.29), p. 51 (arXiv v5). Deduces from weak admissibility of D_st and the injection of Proposition 5.23 that the Newton polygon of compactly supported rigid cohomology lies above the Hodge polygon, with equal endpoints under the bounds on p, and that the coefficients of the moment L-function satisfy v_p(c_n) ≥ n(n − 1) for all p ≥ 3.

**Construction or proof.**

1. The filtered (φ, N)-module (V_{k,p} ⊗ B_st)^{Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p(√−p))} of the semistable representation V_{k,p} is weakly admissible (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.3, weak admissibility of D_st(V)): its Newton polygon lies above its Hodge polygon with the same endpoints.
2. Newton and Hodge polygons are additive for direct sums (Minkowski sums of the regions above them); the middle rigid cohomology injects into the Frobenius module of V_{k,p} (RD.7/kloosterman-semistable-realization (2)), so its Newton polygon lies above that of V_{k,p}, which lies above the Hodge polygon of the middle de Rham cohomology; under the bounds on p the two modules are equal and the endpoints agree.
3. Add back the trivial factor: one-dimensional with slopes 0 if k ≢ 0 mod 4, two-dimensional with slopes 0 and k/2 otherwise.
4. The valuation bound: c_n is, up to sign, the n-th elementary symmetric function of the Frobenius eigenvalues, so its valuation is at least the sum of the n smallest Newton slopes, hence at least the sum of the n smallest Hodge slopes; Fresán–Sabbah–Yu read off v_p(c_n) ≥ n(n − 1) from the Hodge numbers of the middle de Rham cohomology computed in their §5 (Remark 5.28). RD.6/slope-bounds-for-rigid-cohomology gives the coarser consistency check that all slopes lie in [0, k + 1].

**Checks.**

- The bound v_p(c_n) ≥ n(n − 1) sharpens Haessig's (1 − 1/(p − 1))n(n − 1) for p ≥ 5 (Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, Remark 5.28).
- Small n: the bound is empty for n = 0, 1 and for n = 2 asserts p^2 | c_2.

### Proof obligations and supplier contracts

**All-power étale trace and arithmetic zeta supplier.** CohomologicalPointCounting/TraceFormula Layers 12–13 is the requested supplier for the following theorem: for every separated finite-type X over F_q and ℓ≠p, #X(F_(q^r))=Σ_i(−1)^i Tr(Frob_q^r | H_c^i(X_Fbar,Q_ℓ)) for every r≥1, with the closed-point Euler product and cohomological determinant expression for its zeta function. The registered SF.2 interface routes this request; it does not prove the trace theorem. For proper X, compactly supported and ordinary cohomology agree. Local finite-field arithmetic and weight separation do not supply this cohomological input.

Consumes: [Crystalline, rigid and ℓ-adic Weil factors agree for smooth projective varieties (Katz–Messing)](#target-rd-7-ell-adic-comparison-smooth-projective) (`RD.7/ell-adic-comparison-smooth-projective`), [Crystalline, rigid and ℓ-adic Weil factors agree for smooth proper varieties](#target-rd-7-ell-adic-comparison-smooth-proper) (`RD.7/ell-adic-comparison-smooth-proper`), [The rigid and crystalline zeta expressions for every finite extension](#target-rd-7-rigid-zeta-expression) (`RD.7/rigid-zeta-expression`).

**Elliptic p-rank dichotomy for nonprime finite fields.** For q = p^f, f > 1, supplement the Newton-polygon computation by the elliptic ordinary/supersingular p-rank theorem. The Hasse bound and p | a alone do not prove v_p(a) ≥ f/2 for a general integer a; this arithmetic assertion needs the fact that a is an elliptic Frobenius trace.

Consumes: [Elliptic curves and P^1: p-adic slopes versus complex weights](#target-rd-7-elliptic-curve-slopes-versus-weights) (`RD.7/elliptic-curve-slopes-versus-weights`).

**Mieda p-adic Picard–Lefschetz comparison obligation.** Develop the semistable-model lemma, injectivity of the rigid/log-crystalline comparison β and its Frobenius compatibility through logarithmic de Rham–Witt complexes. The current route uses Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, proof of Proposition 5.23, pp. 49–51, citing Mieda, Math. Z. 257 (2007), Theorem 1.1, (2.3) and Theorem 2.13. Mieda’s proof is not established by that account alone; the comparison and the semistability of the blow-up remain separate proof obligations.

Consumes: [Mieda's p-adic Picard–Lefschetz map for ordinary quadratic degenerations](#target-rd-7-mieda-p-adic-picard-lefschetz) (`RD.7/mieda-p-adic-picard-lefschetz`), [The p-adic realisation of the Kloosterman moments and middle rigid cohomology (Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, Proposition 5.23)](#target-rd-7-kloosterman-semistable-realization) (`RD.7/kloosterman-semistable-realization`).

**p-adic comparison theorems C_dR and C_st are owned above this tier.** Fresán–Sabbah–Yu, Proposition 5.23, uses that étale cohomology of a smooth proper variety over Q_p is de Rham and that of a proper semistable model over Q_p(√−p) is semistable, with D_st identified with Hyodo–Kato/log-de Rham cohomology (Tsuji's C_st). The atlas plans these comparisons in CohomologyComparisons:CP.4 (proper-rigid-potential-semistable-comparison, semistable-filtered-bdr-agreement) and PadicHodgeTheory, both in higher tiers than this roadmap (tier 12), so they cannot be cited here; moving them down into RD.7 would duplicate the core of p-adic Hodge theory. The two Kloosterman applications therefore rest on this gap; the restructuring proposal below moves them up to the owner of C_st.

In particular, Witt-vector rank-one classification is not arbitrary-rank Dieudonné–Manin, and total convolution does not supply analytic summability or closure.

## Source corrections used by the targets

The formulations above use the following mathematical corrections at the stated source locators. Version-specific corrections do not assert an error in every edition. The register gives the corrected statement and its mathematical reason, rather than source passages.

**E1 — [S2](#source-2), Proposition 4.6.3(b), p. 52 (arXiv v4).** The absolute HN-slopes of M ⊗ M′ are c_i + c′_j. Lemma 4.1.2(a) gives M_{c,d} ⊗ M_{c′,d′} ≅ M_{c′′,d′′}^{⊕} with c/d + c′/d′ = c′′/d′′, and the proof reads the slopes off tensor products of eigenvectors, whose slopes add; for R(1) ⊗ R(1) = R(2) the printed rule would give slope 1.

**E2 — [S2](#source-2), Proof of Proposition 2.6.8, p. 22.** by Proposition 2.6.5, J′ is principal The proof cites the proposition being proved; the principality of Γ_r is Proposition 2.6.5.

**E3 — [S2](#source-2), Remark 3.3.6, p. 34.** ... which as in (c1) above is impossible for n < 0 (indeed for n ≠ 0). The remark concerns n < 0; for x ∈ O[π^{−1}] the equation π^n x^σ = x forces w(x^σ) + n = w(x), impossible for n ≠ 0, so 'n > 0' must read 'n < 0'.

**E4 — [S2](#source-2), Example 7.2.6, p. 69.** u^σ = u^q With u^σ = qu, σ is not a Frobenius lift (it reduces to 0, not to the q-power map), and the commutation ∇∘F = (F ⊗ dσ)∘∇ fails on e_2: ∇(F e_2) = q e_1 ⊗ du/u while (F ⊗ dσ)(∇ e_2) = e_1 ⊗ d(qu)/(qu) = e_1 ⊗ du/u. With u^σ = u^q both sides equal q e_1 ⊗ du/u.

**E5 — [S2](#source-2), Proposition 4.2.4, p. 43.** ... σ-submodules of M ... σ-submodule of M ... No module N is in scope; the proof bounds the slopes of submodules of M.

**E6 — [S8](#source-8), Definition 5.1.3, p. 28 (arXiv v2).** max in place of min With min, the trivial module (D_s = 0 for s ≥ 1) would have |T|_{ρ,sp} = 0 and R(E, ρ) = ∞, and every module would have R(E, ρ) ≥ ρ, contradicting Lemma 5.4.7 (breaks n > 0) and Christol-Dwork's definition ‖δ‖_Sp = max(lim sup T(δ^s, E)^{1/s}, ‖D‖_Sp) (p. 668).

**E7 — [S8](#source-8), Corollary 5.2.4, p. 30.** for ρ ∈ [ρ_0, 1) ∩ Γ∗ ρ_0 is introduced and never used; [ρ, 1) is meaningless as a range for ρ.

**E8 — [S8](#source-8), Lemma 5.3.2, last assertion, p. 31.** the disc |t − t_ρ^{1/p}| < r^{1/p}ρ^{1/p} is carried into the disc |t − t_ρ| < rρ. For r slightly above p^{−p/(p−1)} and z = t_ρ^{1/p}(1 + ε) with |ε| < r, the linear term p·ε dominates (1 + ε)^p − 1, so |z^p − t_ρ| can equal ρ|p||ε| > ρ r^p; with |ε| < r^{1/p} and |ε| > p^{−1/(p−1)} the dominant term is ε^p and |z^p − t_ρ| < rρ.

**E9 — [S9](#source-9), Hypothesis 1.1.1 and Lemma 1.1.5, p. 3 (arXiv v3).** Add the hypothesis that ∂ is not identically zero on F (equivalently F is not equal to its field of constants). If ∂ = 0 on F (allowed by Hypothesis 1.1.1) and V = F^2 with ∂ = 0, then ∂v = 0 for every v, so no v has v, ∂v linearly independent. The paper applies the lemma only to Frac of annulus rings with ∂ = d/dt ≠ 0.

**E10 — [S10](#source-10), Lemma 1.2.4, p. 6 (arXiv v4).** Add the hypothesis that ∂ ≠ 0 on K. Same counterexample as for Swan conductors I Lemma 1.1.5 (K with the zero derivation, V = K^2 with ∂ = 0); the paper uses the lemma for K = F_ρ with ∂ = d/dt.

**E11 — [S9](#source-9), Corollary 2.5.5, p. 10.** There exist b ∈ Q≥0 and ǫ′ ∈ [ǫ, 1) such that T(E, ρ) = ρ^b for all ρ ∈ (ǫ′, 1). Proposition 2.5.4 only gives linearity of r ↦ log T(E, e^{−r}) near r = 0. Counterexample under Hypothesis 2.5.2: the rank-one module D(e) = λt^{−2}e on A_K(ǫ, 1) with 0 < |λ| < |π| (π^{p−1} = −p) and ǫ < |λ|/|π| is solvable at 1 with T(E, ρ) = 1 for ρ ≥ |λ|/|π| (exp(λ/t) converges there) but T(E, ρ) = |π|ρ/|λ| < 1 for ρ < |λ|/|π|. Later uses (Definition 2.8.1) take ρ close to 1.

**E17 — [S16](#source-16), Proof of Proposition 3.3, p. 7 (arXiv v4).** (log u)^σ = q log u + log(u^σ/u^q), since σ = σ_0^f lifts the q-power Frobenius (q = p^f). u^σ ≡ u^q mod π for σ = σ_0^f, so log(u^σ/u^p) is not defined by the logarithm series unless f = 1; with q the series converges and the formula is σ-compatible with d(log u) = du/u.

**E18 — [S16](#source-16), Proof of Theorem 5.1, condition (a) and the ∇-stability argument, p. 11; Section 7, p. 16 (arXiv v4).** φ(F v) = q^ℓ φ(v)^σ (the Tate twist multiplies F by q^ℓ, and F is σ-semilinear); correspondingly Lemma 4.2 is applied with exponent fℓ, the slope of P is fℓ, 'F v = p^ℓ v' reads F v = q^ℓ v, 'u^σ ≡ u^p' reads u^σ ≡ u^q, and in Section 7 the Frobenius lift sends x^I to x^{qI} and horizontal sections satisfy F v = q^ℓ v. The paper defines M(ℓ) with F multiplied by q^ℓ (Section 2) and σ = σ_0^f; Lemma 4.2 (correctly) has φ(F v) = p^ℓ φ(v)^σ, which is the σ-semilinear form. The printed forms agree with the corrected ones only when f = 1.

The applications (proofs of 9.1.1, 9.3.1, 9.3.2, 1.2.3, 1.2.4) can be run componentwise.

(1.2.4.2) is proved only for smooth X_1, X_2, and the induction hypothesis concerns products X_1 × X_2; the singular locus of X_1 × X_2 is a union, not a product, of such.

The relations a_1a_2 = q and a_1 + a_2 = a ∈ ℤ, which are all that is used, hold. For the Legendre curve y^2 = x(x − 1)(x + 1) over F_7 (supersingular), PARI/GP gives a_7 = 0 and characteristic polynomial T^2 + 7, irreducible over ℚ_7 (factorpadic), so ±√−7 ∉ W(F_7)[1/7].

**E55 — [S6](#source-6), Section 2, p. 3 (arXiv v2); journal p. 326, line −4.** The left side should be d(x dy_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ dy_i). The displayed formula defines d.

**E56 — [S6](#source-6), Section 3, p. 6 (arXiv v2); journal p. 331, line 14.** The 2g on the left should be the number of Weierstrass points rational over F_{q^i} (and likewise on the right-hand side of the displayed computation), so they still cancel. C′ removes ∞ and the roots of Q: for y^2 = x^3 − x over F_5, #C = 8, #C′ = 4 ≠ 8 − 2. The final identity q^i + 1 − #C(F_{q^i}) = Tr(q^iF^{−i} | H^1_−) is unaffected. By Kedlaya's Remark 3.2.5 a Frobenius lift does not act on an individual fringe algebra T_{n,ρ} (it maps T_{n,ρ} into T_{n,ρ^{1/q}}), so a (σ,∇)-module over T_{n,ρ} is not defined.

Applied to x (c_{10} = 1) the printed formula returns x instead of ρ(x) = ∂. Normal-ordering ρ(x^i ∂^j) = ∂^i(−x)^j with Lemma 4.1.2 by machine (exact rational arithmetic, all i, j < 5): the printed formula disagrees on 20 of 25 monomials, the corrected one on none.

Kedlaya's own formula F ∘ ψ = q^n on the next page uses |G| = q^n.

**E60 — [S5](#source-5), §5.1, properties of the canonical Dwork operator, p. 38.** ψ ∘ F = q^n on M ⊗ Ω^i_A; F ∘ ψ = q^n holds on cohomology, where G acts trivially. For A = M = K⟨x⟩†, σ(x) = x^q: ψ(x) = 0, so F(ψ(x)) = 0, while ψ(F(x)) = ψ(x^q) = qx.

**E61 — [S5](#source-5), Proof of Theorem 5.3.2, p. 39.** The passage from the de Rham complex to its cohomology needs the additivity of nuclear traces along exact sequences (van der Put, Mém. SMF 23, (1.5)) together with finite dimensionality of H^i(M). ψ acts on infinite-dimensional spaces M ⊗ Ω^i; ordinary linear algebra does not give the equality, and the step is asserted without argument in a section declared to be a brief review.
